nodes.label: Suggested Node platform topics
nodes.rationale: Transactional outbox, outbound side-effects as jobs, time on the server, large payloads and temp files, outbound HTTP client discipline, boot sequence.

nodes.label: Master share 35% vs 25–30% guideline
nodes.rationale: 240 topics: Master 84 (35%), Understand 79, Know 47, When Needed 30. Demotion target roughly 70–75 Master (~30%).

nodes.label: Node.js syllabus consolidated review
nodes.rationale: Historical record of a 2026-08-09 review of 240 topics. Findings applied afterwards; syllabus is now 248 topics at docs/nodejs/syllabus/.

nodes.label: Node syllabus covers the Node layer
nodes.rationale: Strong enough for the Node layer of a fullstack platform. Not the whole backend: Express, PG/Mongo, Redis, Docker/Nginx remain separate.
nodes.norm_label: node syllabus covers the node layer

nodes.label: Node stops before the framework
nodes.rationale: Do not pull pagination, RBAC routes, middleware stacks, or OpenAPI into Node. Express would become empty and Master % balloons.

nodes.label: react.dev You Might Not Need an Effect
nodes.norm_label: react.dev you might not need an effect

nodes.label: FILTERABLE column and operator spec
nodes.rationale: Both the column and the operator come from the map. Letting the client choose ?op=>= is the same identifier hole.

nodes.label: quote_ident and format %I
nodes.rationale: Quoting stops stacked statements but is not authorization. An attacker can still order by any real column, including password_hash. %s is unquoted substitution.

nodes.label: SORTABLE lookup map
nodes.rationale: An allowlist is not validation. Use the request key into an object whose values are SQL you authored. User input never reaches the query. Direction is a ternary, never interpolated.

nodes.label: Concatenated identifier injection
nodes.rationale: No parameter array uses the simple query protocol, which permits stacked statements. ?sort=name; DROP TABLE fs_items CASCADE; -- executed 2 statements and the table was gone. Same payload as $1 left the table intact.

nodes.label: ORDER BY $1 silent no-op
nodes.rationale: The parameter binds as a constant string, so every row sorts by the same value. Sorting by name and by price returned byte-identical output and no error.

nodes.label: base64url cursor encoding
nodes.rationale: base64 + and / are not URL-safe. Keep timestamp precision; keep bigint id as a string. Base64 is not security — sign if the cursor must not be forgeable.

nodes.label: Switch on err.constraint not message
nodes.rationale: Every unique violation is 23505. Only constraint distinguishes email_taken from username_taken. err.message is translated prose.

nodes.label: err.detail leak
nodes.rationale: 23505 detail echoes the submitted key value. 23514 detail is the entire failing row, including columns the client never sent.

nodes.label: bigint arrives as a String
nodes.rationale: pg will not silently lose precision past Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER. id === 2 is false because id is '2'. Treat ids as opaque strings.

nodes.label: toDomain mapper
nodes.rationale: Lives next to the SELECT list. It is an allowlist: a later column does not appear in the API until named here. Missing SELECT returns undefined, not an error.

nodes.label: One-pass predicate and parameter builder
nodes.rationale: Build predicate strings and the parameter array in the same loop so $n numbering cannot drift. Built separately you get a runtime error or an injection hole.

nodes.label: = ANY($1) for variable-length IN
nodes.rationale: One array parameter keeps statement text constant. Generated IN ($1,$2,$3) fills pg_stat_statements; IN () is a syntax error; ANY('{}') matches nothing.

nodes.label: Placeholder from params.length
nodes.rationale: params.length after the push is the 1-based $n. A separate i++ drifts on a branch that increments without pushing.

nodes.label: jsonb_agg empty-children trap
nodes.rationale: LEFT JOIN plus jsonb_agg yields [{sku:null}]. Need FILTER (WHERE child.id IS NOT NULL) and coalesce(..., '[]'::jsonb) because an aggregate over zero rows is NULL.

nodes.label: Flat join grouped in JavaScript
nodes.rationale: Default: one join, Map-group in JS behind the repository mapper. Two queries + JS was 103.3 ms — a wash. Keeps one query serving several response shapes.

nodes.label: jsonb_agg nested shaping
nodes.rationale: Slowest option measured: 284.8 ms vs 90.7 ms JS grouping. 232 ms was server CPU parsing jsonb. json_agg was 131.2 ms. Payload 2.0 MB vs 1.2 MB flat.

nodes.label: Types change through jsonb
nodes.rationale: numeric as a column is the string '11.00'; through jsonb it is the number 11. timestamptz goes Date → string. jsonb also reorders keys.

nodes.label: N+1 one query per parent
nodes.rationale: 298.6 ms for 500 orders; 2986 ms extrapolated to 5000. The one to avoid.

nodes.label: Explicit JS field mapper
nodes.rationale: 31.6 ms over 20000 rows, tied with SQL alias (33.2 ms). An allowlist by construction. Reverse direction is a lookup map, not camelToSnake().

nodes.label: Generic snake-to-camel rewriter
nodes.rationale: 2.3× slower (75.3 ms). Publishes every column like SELECT *. oauth2_token → oauth2Token → oauth_2_token. Rewrites keys inside jsonb payloads.

nodes.label: Unquoted identifiers fold to lower case
nodes.rationale: CREATE TABLE t (fullName text) stores fullname. Quoting forever, miss one quote, 42703. snake_case is the convention where what you type is what you get.
nodes.norm_label: unquoted identifiers fold to lower case

nodes.label: Quoted SQL alias trap
nodes.rationale: ORDER BY customerName after AS "customerName" failed with 42703 column "customername" does not exist. Fine for a fixed SELECT list, awkward for a dynamic one.

nodes.label: Built SET list from client keys
nodes.rationale: Object.entries sees present-and-null. Column names go through an allowlist; only values are parameters. A crafted key was rejected by membership.
nodes.norm_label: built set list from client keys

nodes.label: COALESCE partial-update form
nodes.rationale: A static statement cannot distinguish absent from explicit null. PATCH {nickname: null} left the nickname unchanged.

nodes.label: Phase 8 — Schema and data from Node
nodes.norm_label: phase 8 — schema and data from node

nodes.label: Sorting cannot use the parameter builder
nodes.rationale: ORDER BY needs an identifier. Identifiers cannot be parameters; ORDER BY $1 silently sorts by a constant.
nodes.norm_label: sorting cannot use the parameter builder

nodes.label: Bound parameter cannot become SQL
nodes.rationale: The statement is parsed before the value is bound. apple'; DROP TABLE fs_items; -- as $1 returned 0 rows and left the table intact.

nodes.label: await does not block the thread
nodes.rationale: await suspends the function, not the thread. A hot loop after an await still freezes everything — run-to-completion applies to continuations.
nodes.norm_label: await does not block the thread

nodes.label: Three-pass async ordering method
nodes.rationale: Pass 1 walk the synchronous path to each first await. Pass 2 drain microtasks (re-queue at each await). Pass 3 run one task and repeat.

nodes.label: Two async functions interleave
nodes.rationale: Both run synchronously to their first await, then resume in queue order. Concurrency without parallelism.

nodes.label: await always costs one tick
nodes.rationale: Even an already-fulfilled promise or await null still pauses until the next microtask. No fast path.

nodes.label: Exactly where await suspends
nodes.rationale: Top-level code up to and including the first await runs synchronously. At await, control exits and returns to the caller.

nodes.label: Each chain link costs a microtask
nodes.rationale: Handlers always run asynchronously even when already settled. A hundred-link chain of sync handlers freezes the frame; yield a task to paint.
nodes.norm_label: each chain link costs a microtask

nodes.label: Promise executor is synchronous
nodes.rationale: new Promise(fn) calls fn immediately on the current stack. Wrapping slow work in a promise does not offload it.

nodes.label: Microtasks vs macrotasks
nodes.rationale: Two queues; microtasks have absolute priority. A task runs one job; a microtask drain runs every microtask including ones queued during the drain.

nodes.label: Microtask drain until empty
nodes.rationale: After each task the loop runs all microtasks, including those queued during the drain, until the queue is empty.

nodes.label: Microtask starvation
nodes.rationale: A self-re-arming microtask chain never returns to the task queue — no timers, events, or rendering. A recursive setTimeout yields; a recursive then does not.

nodes.label: Node nextTick and setImmediate
nodes.rationale: process.nextTick drains before the promise microtask queue; setImmediate is a check-phase task. Relative setTimeout(0) vs setImmediate is context-dependent.

nodes.label: 1, 4, 3, 2 ordering
nodes.rationale: Synchronous first, then the entire microtask queue, then one task. Nested timers drain their microtasks before the next timer task.

nodes.label: Tasks vs microtasks
nodes.rationale: Tasks: setTimeout, setInterval, event dispatch, initial script — one per turn. Microtasks: then/catch/finally, await continuations, queueMicrotask, MutationObserver — all of them after the current task.

nodes.label: Run-to-completion
nodes.rationale: Whenever a function runs it cannot be preempted. Explains both why JS needs no locks and why a 200 ms loop freezes everything.

nodes.label: The event loop
nodes.rationale: An agent maintains a heap, a stack of execution contexts, and a queue of jobs. The loop pulls one job, runs it to completion, pulls the next.

nodes.label: Rendering between tasks
nodes.rationale: The browser schedules rendering between tasks after the microtask queue is empty. await null cannot yield to paint; await setTimeout(0) or scheduler.yield() can.

nodes.label: Single-threaded code, concurrent platform
nodes.rationale: Your JavaScript is one thread; fetch, timers, and workers are not. await suspends the function, not the thread.

nodes.label: Deno
nodes.rationale: Secure by default, TypeScript first-class. Deno 2 added npm, package.json and node_modules.

nodes.label: Job idempotency
nodes.rationale: Run twice: 2 emails, or 1 and a rowCount of 0.

nodes.label: FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED job queue
nodes.rationale: 20 jobs, 3 workers, 20 unique claims and no double delivery.
nodes.norm_label: for update skip locked job queue

nodes.label: Transactional outbox
nodes.rationale: The order committed and nothing was ever enqueued. One transaction fixes it.

nodes.label: Node Permission Model
nodes.rationale: Locked down to one readable directory, the process still opened a TCP connection — there is no --allow-net.

nodes.label: Prototype pollution
nodes.rationale: JSON.parse is innocent; the recursive merge is the bug.

nodes.label: Sessions vs JWT
nodes.rationale: The whole trade is revocation against a lookup. Short expiry plus refresh is sessions with extra steps.

nodes.label: SSRF
nodes.rationale: A custom DNS guard is never called for a literal IP.

nodes.label: Contract testing
nodes.rationale: A renamed field caught in 18 ms, in the backend's own suite.

nodes.label: listen(0) for API tests
nodes.rationale: listen(0), or EADDRINUSE with a race deciding which file fails.

nodes.label: node:test runner
nodes.rationale: *.spec.mjs is not discovered — a suite named that way runs 0 tests and exits 0.

nodes.label: --test-rerun-failures false green
nodes.rationale: The state file replays previous passes; a test edited to throw still printed ✔ (passed on attempt 0) and exited 0.

nodes.label: Forgotten await fails the file
nodes.rationale: The test prints ✔ but the runner reports generated asynchronous activity after the test ended, fails the file, and exits 1.

nodes.label: async and await
nodes.rationale: Syntax over promises: async makes a function return a promise and permits await. Adds no new capability.

nodes.label: await inside forEach
nodes.rationale: Array.forEach ignores the returned promise so async work floats. Use for...of or Promise.all(map).

nodes.label: Top-level await
nodes.rationale: ES modules can await outside a function; importers wait. Makes the module impossible to require() from CommonJS.

nodes.label: Promise.all
nodes.rationale: Settles when all fulfil; rejects on first failure with that reason. Waiting primitive, not a concurrency limiter.

nodes.label: Promise.allSettled
nodes.rationale: Waits for every input; never rejects. Returns {status, value|reason} so partial success is inspectable.

nodes.label: Unbounded Promise.all
nodes.rationale: Starts every item immediately. Exhausts FDs, pools, memory, or a remote rate limit on a real dataset.

nodes.label: Custom error class
nodes.rationale: Extend Error, set name and a stable code, carry structured context as properties, forward options so {cause} works.

nodes.label: error.cause
nodes.rationale: Standard wrap that keeps the root error attached. Wrap when adding information; rethrow bare otherwise.

nodes.label: Operational versus programmer errors
nodes.rationale: Operational (timeout, 404, disk full) are handled. Programmer (TypeError) crash and restart — retrying reproduces the bug.

nodes.label: .catch() placement
nodes.rationale: Mid-chain .catch recovers and the chain continues fulfilled. End-of-chain is a final net. Covers only upstream.

nodes.label: try/catch with await
nodes.rationale: A rejected promise throws at the await. Without await the try finishes synchronously and the rejection is unhandled.

nodes.label: Floating promise
nodes.rationale: A promise-returning call nobody awaited or .catch'd. Since Node 15 an unhandled rejection terminates the process.

nodes.label: @typescript-eslint/no-floating-promises
nodes.rationale: Lint that flags discarded promises. Needs TypeScript type information; strongest practical TS argument in Node.

nodes.label: Unhandled rejection is fatal
nodes.rationale: Node 15+ exits with code 1 on unhandledRejection by default. A process handler is a detector, not a fix.

nodes.label: Error codes not messages
nodes.rationale: Messages are prose and get reworded. code is a stable contract (ENOENT, ERR_USER_NOT_FOUND). instanceof can fail if the class module is duplicated.

nodes.label: Catch only what you can handle
nodes.rationale: A giant try cannot say what failed. Recover or add {cause} locally; let the rest propagate to a boundary.
nodes.norm_label: catch only what you can handle

nodes.label: void plus .catch for fire-and-forget
nodes.rationale: Deliberate background work must be explicit and handled. void signals intent; .catch is what makes it safe.

nodes.label: Structural selectors use DOM order
nodes.rationale: display:none and flex/grid visual order do not change :nth-child counts.

nodes.label: :nth-child(An+B)
nodes.rationale: n counts from 0; matches 1-based sibling index. -n+3 is the first-three idiom.

nodes.label: :nth-child vs :nth-of-type
nodes.rationale: :nth-child counts every sibling then checks type; :nth-of-type counts only that type. p:nth-child(2) can miss or pick the wrong p.

nodes.label: :nth-child of S
nodes.rationale: of S changes what is counted. :nth-child(odd of :not([hidden])) stripes after filtering.

nodes.label: Connection leak
nodes.rationale: pool.connect() without release() is invisible until the pool is exhausted hours later. Prefer pool.query(); if you check out, release in finally.

nodes.label: SQLite autocommit vs explicit transaction
nodes.rationale: Each write outside a transaction is its own fsync. 1000 inserts: 66 ms autocommit vs 1 ms in one BEGIN/COMMIT.

nodes.label: Transient database errors
nodes.rationale: Retry ECONNREFUSED/57P01/08006 and 40001/40P01 (serialization/deadlock). Never retry 23505, 42601, 28P01. Retry the whole transaction from BEGIN, never one statement (25P02).

nodes.label: 25P02 aborted transaction
nodes.rationale: A failed statement poisons the Postgres transaction. Further commands return 25P02 until ROLLBACK. Continue only via SAVEPOINT / ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT.

nodes.label: Mongo session.withTransaction
nodes.rationale: Requires a replica set. Every operation must pass {session} or it commits independently. withTransaction retries the callback — it must be idempotent.

nodes.label: pool.query BEGIN bug
nodes.rationale: Each pool.query may use a different connection. Concurrent flows can ROLLBACK each other's transactions. Appears to work when the process is idle.

nodes.label: Backoff and jitter
nodes.rationale: Without jitter all 500 clients retried in one 100 ms bucket.

nodes.label: Thundering herd of retries
nodes.rationale: Correlated failures plus deterministic backoff make every client retry at once, knocking a recovering service over again. Backoff sets rate; jitter breaks sync. A circuit breaker stops calls.

nodes.label: Dead-letter queues
nodes.rationale: BullMQ has no DLQ — the failed set is a holding area.

nodes.label: Dead-letter queue
nodes.rationale: Where poison jobs go when retrying no longer helps. BullMQ's failed set is not a DLQ — it mixes today's transients with last month's poison. Store full payload, error, attempts, correlation id.

nodes.label: UnrecoverableError
nodes.rationale: A 4xx other than 429 should die on the first attempt. Classify the error rather than counting retries. Replay into the original queue with a derived jobId and idempotent handlers.

nodes.label: Timeout budgets
nodes.rationale: fetch has no timeout. A 500 ms budget gave the second call 300 ms, not a fresh 500.

nodes.label: Retry and backoff on transient failures
nodes.norm_label: retry and backoff on transient failures

nodes.label: Idempotent write retry
nodes.rationale: A timeout is not knowing whether the write committed. Retry only reads or writes keyed with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING. Mongo already retries once via retryWrites.

nodes.label: withTransaction helper
nodes.rationale: Checkout one client, BEGIN, run fn(client), COMMIT or ROLLBACK, release in finally. Propagate via explicit executor or AsyncLocalStorage. No HTTP inside a transaction.

nodes.label: Full jitter
nodes.rationale: random(0, backoff) breaks synchronized retry waves. 500 clients no-jitter all landed in one 100 ms bucket; full jitter max bucket 122. Equal jitter when a minimum spacing is required.

nodes.label: Header versioning
nodes.rationale: Cleaner URLs, harder to explore.

nodes.label: Media type versioning
nodes.rationale: Accept: application/vnd.app.v1+json is strict and heavy.

nodes.label: Sunset deprecation headers
nodes.rationale: Deprecate with docs + sunset headers; do not break v1 silently.

nodes.label: URL prefix versioning
nodes.rationale: Clearest default for this stack. Visible, cache-friendly, easy routers. Most common style for REST JSON APIs.

nodes.label: Phase 7 — Layering at the Express edge
nodes.norm_label: phase 7 — layering at the express edge

nodes.label: createApp(deps)
nodes.rationale: Pure function returns app; no listen inside; inject db/redis/queue clients. Production entrypoint only listens after deps are ready.

nodes.label: Part 4 — Edge correctness & ops
nodes.rationale: Phases 8–10: parse input, attach identity, enforce access, harden headers, compose a testable app.

nodes.label: Express vs Node boundary rule
nodes.rationale: Hashing, JWT structure, Helmet ideas, Zod-as-library stay in Node. Express owns the middleware that validates, authenticates, authorizes, sets cookies, and mounts Helmet/CORS/rate-limit.

nodes.label: Execution context and the call stack
nodes.rationale: One thread, one stack. A frame holds arguments, locals, the defining scope, this, and the return address.
nodes.norm_label: execution context and the call stack

nodes.label: Stack limit is bytes, not calls
nodes.rationale: Measured 12524 frames with no locals versus 5442 with six args plus an array local. Never treat about 10000 calls as a budget.
nodes.norm_label: stack limit is bytes, not calls

nodes.label: Closures
nodes.rationale: Closures are what make callbacks and promises hold state.

nodes.label: Default parameters fire only on undefined
nodes.norm_label: default parameters fire only on undefined

nodes.label: == null idiom
nodes.rationale: null and undefined are loosely equal only to each other. value == null is the permitted exception to always-===; ESLint eqeqeq:'smart' allows it.

nodes.label: null (deliberate emptiness)
nodes.rationale: null is absence you chose. Defaults do not fire on it; JSON.stringify keeps it. Use it at the boundary to mean 'explicitly cleared' (PATCH).

nodes.label: undefined (engine absence)
nodes.rationale: undefined is absence the engine produced: unassigned binding, missing property, unpassed argument, no return. Prefer omitting the property rather than assigning undefined.

nodes.label: Automatic semicolon insertion
nodes.rationale: ASI inserts a semicolon only where the code would otherwise be a syntax error. If the next line can continue, it will.

nodes.label: Restricted productions
nodes.rationale: A newline after return/throw/break/continue/yield/postfix ++ forces a semicolon. return\n{a:1} yields undefined.

nodes.label: Always use braces
nodes.rationale: A brace-less body contains only the first statement. Apple's goto-fail TLS bug. Also interacts badly with ASI. Enable ESLint curly.

nodes.label: Object keys are strings or symbols
nodes.rationale: Everything else stringifies, so o[1]===o["1"] and two objects collide on [object Object]. That collision is why Map exists.
nodes.norm_label: object keys are strings or symbols

nodes.label: Duplicate object keys last wins
nodes.rationale: After ES2015 duplicates are legal even in strict mode because computed keys cannot be checked at parse time. Only private class elements must stay unique.

nodes.label: Computed property names
nodes.rationale: Expressions in [] evaluate in source order while the object is built and may have side effects. Only literal form that accepts a symbol key.

nodes.label: Shorthand property names
nodes.rationale: {a} means {a:a}. Cannot rename, so API casing boundaries stay verbose. Pairs with destructuring as the pick-fields idiom.

nodes.label: await in a for loop is sequential
nodes.rationale: Each iteration waits for the previous. Correct when steps depend on each other; a waterfall when independent.
nodes.norm_label: await in a for loop is sequential

nodes.label: A chain is strictly sequential
nodes.rationale: Each link waits for the previous. Independent work belongs in Promise.all and friends. Chaining independent requests is an accidental waterfall.

nodes.label: Sequential for...of vs Promise.all
nodes.rationale: for...of+await when operations depend on each other or the target cannot take parallel load. Promise.all starts every request at once.

nodes.label: Awaited expression runs immediately
nodes.rationale: await fetch(url) starts the request now; only the waiting is deferred. Starting several calls then awaiting them is concurrency.

nodes.label: Web Workers
nodes.rationale: A separate agent with its own thread, heap and event loop. Isolation by structured clone preserves run-to-completion.

nodes.label: CPU-bound work in Node
nodes.rationale: Node's one real weakness; the fix is never async.

nodes.label: diagnostics_channel hasSubscribers
nodes.rationale: Performance gate so the hot path stays cheap when nobody is listening. Keep payloads small and immutable.

nodes.label: TracingChannel
nodes.rationale: Request-shaped helper (tracePromise) around a named channel. Many OTel instrumentations subscribe to diagnostics_channel under the hood.

nodes.label: trace vs span
nodes.rationale: A span is one timed operation with attributes and status. A trace is the tree of spans sharing a trace id.

nodes.label: CSPRNG APIs
nodes.rationale: Math.random is a recoverable PRNG. randomUUID for ids; randomBytes(32) base64url for secrets.

nodes.label: Confused deputy via access token
nodes.rationale: An access token is a bearer API credential, not an assertion addressed to you. Validate an ID token whose aud is your client id.

nodes.label: OAuth 2.0
nodes.rationale: Delegated authorization: issues an access token so an app can act on a user's behalf. Says nothing reliable about who the user is.

nodes.label: PKCE
nodes.rationale: Binds the authorization code to the client that started the flow so an intercepted code cannot be redeemed without the verifier.

nodes.label: OAuth state parameter
nodes.rationale: CSRF protection for the callback; without it an attacker can feed their code and link accounts.

nodes.label: Session fixation
nodes.rationale: Rotate the id on every privilege change so a pre-login id cannot ride the authenticated session.

nodes.label: JWT
nodes.rationale: Valid until expiry because validity is a signature check. A denylist rebuilds sessions with extra steps.

nodes.label: Opaque session
nodes.rationale: Default for a single browser app: revocable instantly because the server holds the truth.

nodes.label: Idle and absolute session timeouts
nodes.rationale: Idle alone lets a daily session live forever; absolute alone logs out active users. Redis TTL cannot express the absolute cap.

nodes.label: Short access JWT plus opaque refresh
nodes.rationale: Accept a revocation window equal to the access token lifetime; choose that window deliberately.
nodes.norm_label: short access jwt plus opaque refresh

nodes.label: Dirent.parentPath
nodes.rationale: Replaced deprecated Dirent.path. Full path is path.join(entry.parentPath, entry.name).

nodes.label: opendir walk
nodes.rationale: Async iterator over one entry at a time for huge trees. Constant memory vs readdir({recursive:true}) materialising the whole array.

nodes.label: readdir order not guaranteed
nodes.rationale: Filesystem-dependent (ext4 vs overlayfs). Sort explicitly or numbered migrations run in the wrong order.

nodes.label: readdir withFileTypes
nodes.rationale: Dirent already knows type, avoiding one stat per entry and thousands of extra thread-pool ops on large directories.

nodes.label: os.availableParallelism
nodes.rationale: Respects CPU affinity masks but still misses CFS quota (--cpus=0.5). Prefer configured WORKER_CONCURRENCY.

nodes.label: node:os
nodes.rationale: Reports what the host looks like. In a container that is a lie for cores and memory.

nodes.label: os.cpus / totalmem container lie
nodes.rationale: A 0.5-CPU / 512 MB pod on a 64-core node still sees 64 CPUs and host RAM. Sizing a WorkerPool from cpus().length is a classic production bug.

nodes.label: process vs os
nodes.rationale: process.memoryUsage / cpuUsage describe this process. os.totalmem / loadavg describe a machine you may be sharing.

nodes.label: closeAllConnections
nodes.rationale: Destroys in-flight responses. Forced-exit backstop, not the strategy.

nodes.label: closeIdleConnections
nodes.rationale: Must be swept on an interval. Connections become idle as in-flight requests finish.

nodes.label: server.close
nodes.rationale: Stops new connections and waits for existing ones. Idle keep-alive sockets never end, so the callback never fires.

nodes.label: TOTP drift window and replay
nodes.rationale: Accept ±1 step. Record the accepted step and reject anything not newer, or the code is reusable for 90s.

nodes.label: Hashed MFA recovery codes
nodes.rationale: Ten single-use codes hashed like passwords. Without them, support becomes a weaker recovery path.

nodes.label: TOTP
nodes.rationale: HMAC of the 30-second time step with a shared secret, dynamically truncated to six digits. RFC 6238.

nodes.label: TOTP is not phishing-resistant
nodes.rationale: A proxy can relay the code in its window. WebAuthn/passkeys are origin-bound and will not sign a lookalike.

nodes.label: Regular expression denial of service
nodes.rationale: A backtracking match runs on the event loop; one request stalls the whole process. Node 24 has no regex timeout.

nodes.label: p99 latency
nodes.rationale: A 45 ms mean can hide a 4 s p99; a page of 100 requests hits the tail every load.

nodes.label: Linter vs formatter
nodes.rationale: A formatter rewrites layout; a linter finds legal but wrong code. They are different jobs.

nodes.label: BYPASSRLS job role
nodes.rationale: Exactly one unfiltered role, named for that purpose; the application must not use it.

nodes.label: char(n) blank-padded
nodes.rationale: Pads to width (51 vs 4 bytes for 'abc' in char(50)); comparison ignores trailing spaces. Avoid except genuinely fixed-width codes.

nodes.label: text type
nodes.rationale: Default string type. Same implementation, size and speed as varchar(n) (13 MB / ~26 ms on 300k rows).

nodes.label: varchar(n)
nodes.rationale: Column insert raises 22001 over length; explicit ::varchar(n) truncates silently. Widening is metadata-only (2.4 ms); narrowing rewrites (305 ms / 200k).

nodes.label: text plus CHECK length
nodes.rationale: Cannot be cast away, visible in \d, and changeable with NOT VALID + VALIDATE without rewriting the table.

nodes.label: LEFT JOIN plus WHERE bug
nodes.rationale: Manufactured NULLs filtered by WHERE turn a LEFT JOIN into an INNER JOIN. Explain from evaluation order.

nodes.label: NOT IN NULL trap
nodes.rationale: EXISTS beats JOIN + DISTINCT. NOT IN over a nullable set returns nothing. Phase 6 repeats the same trap for subqueries.

nodes.label: CTE as optimization fence
nodes.rationale: A name for a subquery — and when it is a fence. Phase gate: say whether a CTE is inlined or fenced.

nodes.label: HAVING vs WHERE
nodes.rationale: Filter groups, not rows. WHERE runs before grouping.

nodes.label: UNSAFE_ lifecycles
nodes.rationale: They run before commit, so an abandoned concurrent render has already executed them. Signal of pre-16.3 code.

nodes.label: Compiler is the stricter static checker
nodes.rationale: It analyses and bails out rather than rewriting impure components. Skipped list is a purity report.
nodes.norm_label: compiler is the stricter static checker

nodes.label: Abandoned concurrent renders cannot roll back side effects
nodes.norm_label: abandoned concurrent renders cannot roll back side effects

nodes.label: Three tiers of impurity cost
nodes.rationale: StrictMode today, next feature or Compiler tomorrow, abandoned concurrent render in production.

nodes.label: node --test file discovery
nodes.rationale: *.spec.mjs is not discovered. A suite named that way runs zero tests and still exits 0.

nodes.label: Test isolation process vs none
nodes.rationale: Default process isolation prevents module state leaking between files. none is a local speed-up, not a CI setting.

nodes.label: --test-rerun-failures
nodes.rationale: Replays recorded passes without executing. A test edited to throw still reported green. Local iteration only — never CI.

nodes.label: --experimental-test-tag-filter
nodes.rationale: Key is tags, plural, array. Singular tag: is silently ignored so a filtered CI job can run zero tests and exit 0.

nodes.label: --test-randomize
nodes.rationale: Finds inter-test coupling. Same three shared-state tests: seed 7 passed entirely, which is why the bug survives in file order.

nodes.label: --test-shard
nodes.rationale: Safest CI speed-up here — unlike rerun-failures or tag filtering it cannot make a broken suite look green.

nodes.label: *.itest.mjs separate suite
nodes.rationale: A filename glob cannot be silently wrong. The runner tag filter is experimental and silently matches nothing on tag: instead of tags.

nodes.label: If mocking removes the risk, do not mock
nodes.rationale: A repository is mostly SQL. Mocking pool.query tests that you can write a mock. Draw the unit/integration boundary at I/O, not at one class.
nodes.norm_label: if mocking removes the risk, do not mock

nodes.label: <Widget /> is not Widget()
nodes.rationale: Direct calls inline the result into the caller. Hooks join the caller's list and break if conditional.

nodes.label: Hooks matched by call order
nodes.rationale: No name, no key, just position on the fiber. Conditional hooks shift every later slot.

nodes.label: React calls it, not you
nodes.rationale: A helper is a function you call. Ownership lets React attach state, effects, position and identity.

nodes.label: A component is a function React calls
nodes.rationale: Who calls the function is the definition that matters: React owns timing, repetition, position and identity.
nodes.norm_label: a component is a function react calls

nodes.label: One props argument
nodes.rationale: Built fresh each render so props identity is always new. defaultProps removed for functions in React 19.

nodes.label: HOC ref forwarding after React 19
nodes.rationale: ref is now an ordinary prop, so spreading props forwards it. Class instance refs and React 18 still need forwardRef.

nodes.label: forwardRef deprecated not removed
nodes.rationale: Still works in 19. Libraries supporting 18 still need it. No announced removal date.

nodes.label: ref is an ordinary function-component prop
nodes.rationale: Spreads, wrappers and HOCs now carry ref because it is in props.
nodes.norm_label: ref is an ordinary function-component prop

nodes.label: Memoization does not stop context updates
nodes.norm_label: memoization does not stop context updates

nodes.label: React assumes purity and never verifies it
nodes.rationale: Same props, state and context produce the same output. Every optimisation is a bet on that.
nodes.norm_label: react assumes purity and never verifies it

nodes.label: memo is last, not first
nodes.rationale: Comparison cost, silent failure on fresh objects, no context stop. Structural fixes survive the Compiler.

nodes.label: Skipping a render is a hint
nodes.rationale: React may re-render anyway. Code that only works because a render was skipped is already broken.
nodes.norm_label: skipping a render is a hint

nodes.label: Module-level mutation during render
nodes.rationale: react.dev Cup example: StrictMode doubling yields 2, 4, 6 instead of 1, 2, 3.

nodes.label: Same inputs, same output
nodes.rationale: Inputs are props, state and context only. Time, Math.random, window and localStorage are untracked.

nodes.label: useSyncExternalStore for external sources
nodes.rationale: Window size, media queries and mutable singletons need a tracked subscription.

nodes.label: Doubling is the test
nodes.rationale: React cannot inspect purity, so it runs the function twice and lets the damage double.

nodes.label: as const object plus derived union
nodes.rationale: const Status = {Pending:'pending'} as const; type Status = (typeof Status)[keyof typeof Status]. Erasable, readable logs, same call sites.
nodes.norm_label: as const object plus derived union

nodes.label: as const for heterogeneous returns
nodes.rationale: return [value, inc] without as const infers (number | (() => void))[]. as const makes readonly [number, () => void]. Most common custom-hook type bug.

nodes.label: Tuple types
nodes.rationale: Fixed length, positional meaning, optional and rest elements, named labels (docs only). Arity is checked.

nodes.label: const object plus derived union
nodes.rationale: Runtime iteration and named constants. Same name for const and type is legal — value and type namespaces are separate.

nodes.label: Cannot set headers after they are sent
nodes.rationale: Something tried to write status/headers/body after the response started. Causes: next() after res.json, error middleware after a handler already responded, fall-through return res paths.
nodes.norm_label: cannot set headers after they are sent

nodes.label: Headers already sent
nodes.rationale: The first write wins. A second res.json / send throws Cannot set headers after they are sent to the client.

nodes.label: res.headersSent guard
nodes.rationale: In error middleware: if (res.headersSent) return next(err); so a second write is not attempted.

nodes.label: Set headers before first stream byte
nodes.rationale: Once the stream writes, status and headers are frozen. A mid-flight failure leaves a truncated 200. Validate and authorise before the pipe starts. The catch only logs; it cannot rescue the response.
nodes.norm_label: set headers before first stream byte

nodes.label: trust proxy
nodes.rationale: Behind a proxy, trust proxy is what makes req.ip the real client IP.

nodes.label: trust proxy true spoofs req.ip
nodes.rationale: trust proxy: true takes the leftmost X-Forwarded-For hop, which the client sent. Combined with IP-keyed rate limits this is a bypass.

nodes.label: trust proxy Master row
nodes.rationale: Correct client IP and protocol behind Nginx; rate limits and secure cookies fail without it.

nodes.label: fetch cannot verify 304
nodes.rationale: Sending If-None-Match through fetch returns 200 with a body; the same request via node:http returns 304 empty. Use node:http or curl.

nodes.label: Express does not enforce If-Match
nodes.rationale: Stale If-Match is ignored; Express generates ETags but never enforces preconditions. Lost-update protection is application code (412/428).

nodes.label: Automatic semicolon insertion
nodes.rationale: Semicolons are not optional. ASI inserts only where the next token would otherwise be a syntax error, so valid continuations are taken even when unintended.

nodes.label: Five dangerous ASI line starts
nodes.rationale: ( [ ` + - and / continue the previous line. + and - produce no error, just a wrong number. Semicolon-free style needs a leading ;.

nodes.label: Restricted productions
nodes.rationale: Newline after return/throw/break/continue/yield/postfix ++/-- forces a semicolon. return\n{a:1} yields undefined.

nodes.label: Always brace if bodies
nodes.rationale: Brace-less bodies caused Apple goto-fail TLS. Interacts badly with ASI. Enable ESLint curly.

nodes.label: RESTRICTIVE RLS plus FORCE
nodes.rationale: RESTRICTIVE so isolation applies regardless of permissive policies. FORCE so the table owner cannot bypass. Connect as a non-owner application role.

nodes.label: set_config LOCAL for app.tenant_id
nodes.rationale: SET LOCAL x = $1 is 42601. Use set_config('app.tenant_id', $1, true) inside a transaction. Plain SET persists across pool handoff (measured in ex54).

nodes.label: tenant_id leads every index
nodes.rationale: Every query is tenant-scoped (explicitly and via RLS). Index (created_at) is nearly useless; (tenant_id, created_at) serves the real filter. Most common shared-schema perf failure.

nodes.label: Tenant isolation test suite
nodes.rationale: A reads B by id → 0 rows; insert/update to B's id rejected; no context → 0 or error; sequential requests on one pooled connection must not inherit tenant.

nodes.label: public CREATE revoked since PG15
nodes.rationale: Since PostgreSQL 15, public no longer grants CREATE to PUBLIC. SECURITY DEFINER functions need an explicit search_path to avoid shadowing.

nodes.label: RLS tenant isolation
nodes.rationale: ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY with USING (tenant_id = current_setting('app.tenant_id')::bigint) so a forgotten WHERE cannot leak another tenant.

nodes.label: Schema as namespace
nodes.rationale: A schema is a namespace inside a database. Identical SELECT FROM items returns different rows under tenant_a vs tenant_b via search_path.

nodes.label: search_path
nodes.rationale: Ordered list of schemas for unqualified names. Default is "$user", public. SET search_path persists on a pooled connection and leaks across requests.

nodes.label: SET LOCAL search_path
nodes.rationale: SET LOCAL inside a transaction reverts on commit/rollback. Schema names cannot be $1; validate against pg_namespace then escapeIdentifier.

nodes.label: Three multi-tenant layouts
nodes.rationale: Shared tables + tenant_id (cheapest, weakest); schema per tenant (catalog multiplies, stops at low thousands); database per tenant (strongest, a pool each).

nodes.label: Temp tables vs connection pooling
nodes.rationale: CREATE on connection A and INSERT on B → 42P01. Hold one checked-out client. ON COMMIT DROP prevents leftover temp data on reused pooled connections.

nodes.label: TEMPORARY tables
nodes.rationale: Private to one session in pg_temp_N, dropped with the session. Shadow permanent names via search_path. Live in temp_buffers (default 8 MB), not shared_buffers.

nodes.label: date_trunc bucketing
nodes.rationale: Correct way to bucket for reports (timestamp, sortable, indexable). Pass a timezone: date_trunc('day', ts, 'Europe/Berlin') or local midnight lands in the previous UTC day.

nodes.label: timestamptz for instants
nodes.rationale: timestamptz stores UTC and renders in TimeZone. timestamp without zone is a wall-clock reading with no recoverable zone. SET TIME ZONE on a pool leaks like search_path.

nodes.label: Shared schema as the tenancy default
nodes.rationale: Only model that scales to thousands of tenants; migrations run once; reporting is ordinary SQL. Weak isolation is bought back with repository + RLS + tests.
nodes.norm_label: shared schema as the tenancy default

nodes.label: tenant_id as future shard key
nodes.rationale: Shared schema shards later because tenant_id is already the partition key. Keep it on every table and avoid cross-tenant FKs.

nodes.label: CTE instead of a temp table
nodes.rationale: If the data is only needed in one statement, WITH staging AS (…) avoids DDL, locks, catalog churn and the pooling problem.
nodes.norm_label: cte instead of a temp table

nodes.label: Function declaration hoisting
nodes.rationale: Name and body exist from the top of the scope, even out of unreachable code. Only form callable before its line.

nodes.label: Function expression TDZ
nodes.rationale: const/let expressions throw ReferenceError: Cannot access before initialization. var f=function(){} hoists as undefined then TypeError: f is not a function.

nodes.label: Parameter-list TDZ
nodes.rationale: Later defaults can read earlier parameters (h=w*2). Forward refs throw at runtime only when that default runs. (a=a) is TDZ too.

nodes.label: Phase 3 — Functions, scope and closures
nodes.rationale: 20 topics. Master 01–08 written 2026-08-13; 09–20 deferred. this, closures, and the scope chain are assumed by later phases.

nodes.label: Direct eval
nodes.rationale: Can introduce bindings into the surrounding scope. Indirect eval (0, eval)(...) runs in global scope instead.

nodes.label: Lexical scope
nodes.rationale: Fixed by where the function appears in the source, not where it is called. Makes closures possible and lets engines resolve names to slot indices.

nodes.label: with is banned in strict mode
nodes.rationale: Injects an object's properties into the scope chain so names cannot be resolved statically.
nodes.norm_label: with is banned in strict mode

nodes.label: Scope is decided where code is written
nodes.rationale: Lexical scoping makes closures possible, makes var and let differ, and lets engines resolve most lookups before the program runs.
nodes.norm_label: scope is decided where code is written

nodes.label: HoistableDeclaration
nodes.rationale: The spec term is not hoisting. HoistableDeclaration covers function declarations only.

nodes.label: Value hoisting
nodes.rationale: Functions (and function*, async function) are usable before their line because the slot holds the finished function.

nodes.label: Function declaration value hoisting
nodes.rationale: The only form that is usefully hoisted: the slot holds the finished function before the first line runs.

nodes.label: var and function name collision
nodes.rationale: At scope entry the function wins regardless of source order. Only an initializer overwrites it at execution time.

nodes.label: Replacement $ patterns
nodes.rationale: $&, $1 and $<name> are interpreted in a replacement string. Use the function form when the replacement is data-derived.

nodes.label: String.prototype.replace
nodes.rationale: A string pattern replaces only the first occurrence — the most common string bug.

nodes.label: String.prototype.replaceAll
nodes.rationale: Throws TypeError if a regex lacks the g flag. Equivalent to replace with a global regex; the difference exists only for string patterns.

nodes.label: Never build a regex from user input
nodes.rationale: A string in replaceAll matches literally. new RegExp(userInput) treats metacharacters as syntax and is a backtracking DoS vector.
nodes.norm_label: never build a regex from user input

nodes.label: Destructuring null or undefined throws
nodes.rationale: Throws even with empty patterns. Guard with ?? {} or a parameter default of = {}.

nodes.label: Destructured parameter = {}
nodes.rationale: function f({ a }) {} throws on f() because the parameter is undefined. Any optional destructured parameter needs = {}.

nodes.label: Destructuring and fn.length
nodes.rationale: A destructured parameter counts as one. A default stops the count, so adding = {} drops arity from 1 to 0.

nodes.label: Options object as named arguments
nodes.rationale: Order-independent, self-documenting, and addable without touching callers. Worth the allocation past two or three parameters.

nodes.label: Spoofed X-Forwarded-For
nodes.rationale: If Node is reachable directly, anyone can send X-Forwarded-For: 1.2.3.4 and break rate limits, redirects, and cookies.

nodes.label: TLS termination at the edge
nodes.rationale: Node often speaks HTTP on a private network. Redirects and Secure cookies must use X-Forwarded-Proto, not req.socket.encrypted.

nodes.label: trust proxy
nodes.rationale: Tell the framework how many hops of forwarded headers to trust when computing IP and protocol. Not blind true without understanding hop count.

nodes.label: X-Forwarded-* headers
nodes.rationale: X-Forwarded-For, Proto, Host, and RFC 7239 Forwarded. Only trust if the socket peer is your proxy.

nodes.label: --max-old-space-size
nodes.rationale: Most common production V8-related flag; heap_size_limit is not always equal to the number passed.

nodes.label: V8 heap limit vs cgroup RSS
nodes.rationale: Heap flag is V8's; cgroup kills on RSS including off-heap. Size them together.
nodes.norm_label: v8 heap limit vs cgroup rss

nodes.label: --trace-gc is diagnostic only
nodes.rationale: Log volume and overhead; not a production default. Random blog flags add unowned risk.

nodes.label: npm day to day
nodes.rationale: The dozen commands you actually run, and two decisions: which list a package belongs in, and whether this machine should resolve ranges.

nodes.label: npm explain
nodes.rationale: Prints the dependency chain that pulled a package in. Do not import a transitive package directly.

nodes.label: npx
nodes.rationale: Resolves a local binary first, then downloads to a cache and executes without installing. A typo'd package name is a real attack vector.

nodes.label: Avoid global npm installs
nodes.rationale: Global packages are unversioned, invisible to the project, and differ per machine. Put the tool in devDependencies or use npx.

nodes.label: Mock (interaction assertion)
nodes.rationale: Canned values plus expectations about calls. Correct when the call itself is the behaviour — payments, emails, webhooks.

nodes.label: Spy
nodes.rationale: Records calls while real behaviour continues. t.mock.method(obj, name) with two arguments spies; a third argument stubs.

nodes.label: Stub
nodes.rationale: Returns canned values; assert on the result of the code under test. Reach for this most often. Nothing is asserted about the stub itself.

nodes.label: Over-mocking as a design smell
nodes.rationale: Seven doubles for one assertion restates implementation. Setup size equals collaborator count. Extract pure functions; leave one thin wiring test.

nodes.label: MySQL strict mode
nodes.rationale: Default since 5.7. Measured MySQL 8.4 rejects out-of-range smallint (1264) and oversized varchar (1406). CHECK enforced since 8.0.16. ONLY_FULL_GROUP_BY in default sql_mode since 5.7.

nodes.label: SQLite STRICT tables
nodes.rationale: SQLite 3.37+ opt-in type enforcement. Use when prototyping on SQLite and deploying on PostgreSQL.

nodes.label: SQLite type affinities
nodes.rationale: Column types are affinities, not constraints. Text sits in an integer column; varchar(3) holds eight characters. Prototype-on-SQLite surprises appear on PostgreSQL.

nodes.label: Real BOOLEAN type
nodes.rationale: Only PostgreSQL has a real boolean and rejects non-booleans. MySQL BOOLEAN is TINYINT(1) and stores 2. SQLite reports integer for true.

nodes.label: Transactional DDL
nodes.rationale: Failed third CREATE rolled back two successful tables. Tracking insert must share the transaction or applied and recorded diverge.

nodes.label: Issuing DDL through the driver
nodes.rationale: CREATE TABLE is client.query. Success is no thrown error; rowCount is null and fields is empty.

nodes.label: DDL locks and the blocking they cause
nodes.rationale: What the same DDL does to a table being read. ACCESS EXCLUSIVE conflicts with everything including SELECT's ACCESS SHARE.
nodes.norm_label: ddl locks and the blocking they cause

nodes.label: Startup races and advisory locks
nodes.rationale: ensureSchema() at boot is a bug. IF NOT EXISTS is idempotent, not concurrency-safe.

nodes.label: Migration tools
nodes.rationale: Every tool implements a tracking table. Choose on workflow assumption, not feature list. Own-runner until CONCURRENTLY or baselining; node-pg-migrate for raw SQL; schema-derived tools only with their client.

nodes.label: Migrations
nodes.rationale: A migration is a numbered file that runs exactly once, inside a transaction, with the fact recorded in the database. Drop any property and the schema is unreproducible.

nodes.label: Writing a minimal migration runner
nodes.rationale: A correct runner is about sixty lines. Write it to learn the mechanism; switch when you need CONCURRENTLY, baselining, dry-run, or JS data migrations.

nodes.label: Schema drift
nodes.rationale: Drift is live schema vs what code assumes. Migrations prevent most of it; a boot-time check turns 42703 into a deploy that refuses to start.

nodes.label: Seeding
nodes.rationale: A seed runs more than once. If twice is not identical to once, it is a data-corruption script.

nodes.label: SQL in .sql files, not template literals
nodes.rationale: SQL in JS strings is invisible to formatters, linters and psql. Files cost a loader and restore tooling, diffs and a boundary against concatenation.
nodes.norm_label: sql in .sql files, not template literals

nodes.label: Wrapping a migration in BEGIN/COMMIT
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL transactional DDL is why a failed migration leaves nothing and why forward-only is practical here unlike MySQL.

nodes.label: Sort and filter allowlists
nodes.rationale: ?sort=price reintroduces injection after everything else is parameterized. Values can be parameters; column names and ASC/DESC cannot.

nodes.label: Keyset (cursor) pagination
nodes.rationale: Remember the last row and ask for what comes after. 1.23 ms vs 295.87 ms OFFSET at the same depth on 500k rows.

nodes.label: list with filtering, sorting and pagination
nodes.rationale: Filters are parameters, sort is an allowlist, pagination is two more parameters plus a tiebreaker. Wrong combination duplicates rows with no error.
nodes.norm_label: list with filtering, sorting and pagination

nodes.label: Migrations as a deploy step
nodes.rationale: Not at app boot. Failure should stop the deploy, app role should lack CREATE/ALTER, and ACCESS EXCLUSIVE must not block old instances still serving traffic.

nodes.label: Forward-only migrations
nodes.rationale: Down migrations are rarely tested and cannot restore DROP COLUMN data. Recovery is a new forward file plus backup restore.

nodes.label: Seeding is not migration
nodes.rationale: Migrations change schema, run once, not edited after shipping. Seeds run every time and are editable. Reference data later migrations depend on belongs in a migration.

nodes.label: jsonb shallow merge ||
nodes.rationale: || replaces the whole top-level key; nested updates need jsonb_set. Every mutation rewrites the document.

nodes.label: No foreign key into a jsonb key
nodes.rationale: CHECK on presence/range works; FOREIGN KEY from a jsonb key is 42601.
nodes.norm_label: no foreign key into a jsonb key

nodes.label: jsonb key-name storage cost
nodes.rationale: Same two facts: 22 MB as jsonb vs 1736 kB as columns (~13x) because key names repeat per row.

nodes.label: Hybrid columns plus jsonb
nodes.rationale: Promote queried keys to columns; keep the varying remainder as jsonb. Generated STORED columns migrate without a write-path change.

nodes.label: HNSW 2000-dimension cap
nodes.rationale: vector column holds up to 16000 dimensions; HNSW indexes cap at 2000 (54000 at 2001). halfvec indexes up to 4000.

nodes.label: vector distance operators
nodes.rationale: <-> L2, <=> cosine, <#> negative inner product. All are distances so ORDER BY ASC is nearest-first. Dimension mismatches raise 22000.

nodes.label: ef_search recall knob
nodes.rationale: On well-separated clusters recall was 10/10 at every setting; raising ef_search only added latency 1.2→4.5 ms. Measure recall on your vectors.

nodes.label: HNSW approximate index
nodes.rationale: 50000 384-dim vectors: exact 88 ms → HNSW 2.1 ms (42×). Build 22.9 s, index 98 MB vs 78 MB table. Results are approximate.

nodes.label: pg_hba auth methods
nodes.rationale: scram-sha-256 is the correct password method. trust authenticates any password. md5 rule can use a SCRAM-stored password; a scram rule cannot use an md5-stored one.

nodes.label: pg_hba_file_rules parsed view
nodes.rationale: Resolves includes and numbers rules. error column names a bad line. Reload keeps old rules; restart with a syntax error takes the server down.

nodes.label: First matching pg_hba rule wins
nodes.rationale: No fall-through. If that method fails the connection fails. Reversing reject and scram inverted the outcome.

nodes.label: hostssl hostnossl enforce TLS on the server
nodes.rationale: Client sslmode is the client's choice. hostnossl reject plus hostssl scram is the only version of require-TLS that survives a misconfigured service.
nodes.norm_label: hostssl hostnossl enforce tls on the server

nodes.label: pg returns bigint as a string
nodes.rationale: bigint and numeric exceed Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER so pg returns strings. count(*) is bigint; cast to int in SQL. Do not parseInt a real bigint.
nodes.norm_label: pg returns bigint as a string

nodes.label: date maps to JS Date at local midnight
nodes.rationale: date 2026-01-01 printed as 2025-12-31T18:30:00Z at UTC+5:30. Return to_char YYYY-MM-DD or setTypeParser on OID 1082. timestamptz is lossless.
nodes.norm_label: date maps to js date at local midnight

nodes.label: pg_advisory_xact_lock
nodes.rationale: Serialises bootstrap; 500 of 500 succeeded. Prefer the _xact_ form so a crash releases the lock at rollback. Session-scoped pg_advisory_lock can wedge migrations.

nodes.label: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS race
nodes.rationale: Catalog check and insert are not atomic. 228 of 500 concurrent attempts failed with 23505 on pg_type_typname_nsp_index.
nodes.norm_label: create table if not exists race

nodes.label: Silent startup seed duplication
nodes.rationale: 20 workers, 20 duplicate admin rows, zero errors. Fix with a unique constraint plus ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING.

nodes.label: Idempotent vs concurrency-safe
nodes.rationale: Idempotent means twice in sequence is the same. Concurrency-safe means twice at the same time is also correct. IF NOT EXISTS buys only the first.

nodes.label: Features that assume calling is free
nodes.rationale: Batching, memo, Compiler, transitions, Suspense, Activity, SSR and offscreen prerendering all assume render has no consequences.
nodes.norm_label: features that assume calling is free

nodes.label: Phase 2 load-bearing pages 01 02 03 05
nodes.rationale: Topics 12–16 are pre-hooks era: read them to read code, not to write it.

nodes.label: Skipping a render is a hint not a contract
nodes.rationale: React may re-render anyway. Returning false does not stop children when their own state changes. Memoization is never a correctness mechanism.
nodes.norm_label: skipping a render is a hint not a contract

nodes.label: Three effect passes per commit
nodes.rationale: useInsertionEffect, then DOM mutation, then useLayoutEffect before paint, then browser paint, then useEffect. Each pass finishes across the whole commit.

nodes.label: useLayoutEffect
nodes.rationale: Same hook as useEffect except it fires before the browser repaints. That difference is the reason to use it and the reason not to.

nodes.label: Effect timing relative to paint is not guaranteed
nodes.rationale: An interaction-caused Effect may run before paint; React may also repaint before processing state updates inside it. useLayoutEffect or setTimeout for a guarantee.
nodes.norm_label: effect timing relative to paint is not guaranteed

nodes.label: Layout state update executes remaining Effects immediately
nodes.rationale: A setState here drags every pending useEffect into the blocking window, including expensive work elsewhere in the tree.
nodes.norm_label: layout state update executes remaining effects immediately

nodes.label: One contextType per class
nodes.rationale: A second context needs a render prop or wrapper. useContext has no such limit.

nodes.label: children as the free slot
nodes.rationale: A wrapper has a hole the parent fills with arbitrary JSX.

nodes.label: Compound components
nodes.rationale: Free-form children plus context so parts share state and can be arranged freely.

nodes.label: Named element props (slots)
nodes.rationale: Community name, not a React API. Name regions, keep primary content in children, do not slice children by index.

nodes.label: Reset uncontrolled state with key
nodes.rationale: A changing key remounts a fresh instance. Lighter than controlling solely to reset.

nodes.label: Four disguises of the nesting bug
nodes.rationale: Local arrows, HOCs in render, inline map values, lazy or memo called during render.
nodes.norm_label: four disguises of the nesting bug

nodes.label: Deliberate remount with key
nodes.rationale: key participates in position. Change it when the record identity changes.

nodes.label: Reconciliation compares type by reference
nodes.rationale: Object.is on the function. Same body evaluated twice is two components. Same type at same position keeps state.

nodes.label: HOC wraps rather than mutates
nodes.rationale: A function that takes a component and returns a new one that renders the original with extra props.

nodes.label: createPortal
nodes.rationale: createPortal(children, domNode, key?) is renderable, not a component or hook. The node must already exist.

nodes.label: Native events follow the DOM
nodes.rationale: Click-outside listeners see portal clicks as coming from body. Compare against the portal node.

nodes.label: Portals follow the React tree
nodes.rationale: Only DOM placement changes. Events, context, state, error boundaries and Suspense follow the React parent.

nodes.label: Render prop pattern
nodes.rationale: A function prop the component calls to decide what to render. children works and reads better.

nodes.label: Composition over configuration
nodes.rationale: A prop that exists only to be rendered should have been the rendered thing. Design decisions stay props.

nodes.label: When configuration is the right answer
nodes.rationale: Keep props for data, owned behaviour, closed variant sets and enforced consistency.
nodes.norm_label: when configuration is the right answer

nodes.label: Never nest component definitions
nodes.rationale: A new function each parent render remounts the subtree: state, refs, effects, DOM, focus and scroll.

nodes.label: Never apply a HOC during render
nodes.rationale: A new enhanced type each render remounts the subtree and wipes state. Apply once at module level.
nodes.norm_label: never apply a hoc during render

nodes.label: Token in remote URL
nodes.rationale: .git/config is plaintext; an embedded credential is easy to leak when sharing a repo or image.

nodes.label: .git directory
nodes.rationale: The whole repository is one directory. Copy it and you copy history; delete it and the working tree becomes untracked files.

nodes.label: Git is not a place for secrets
nodes.norm_label: git is not a place for secrets

nodes.label: Part 3 — Git in a real project
nodes.norm_label: part 3 — git in a real project

nodes.label: One directory removes safety rails
nodes.rationale: Portable, inspectable, offline — and rm -rf .git is irreversible. Mitigations are social: push often.

nodes.label: Permanent history is the feature and the trap
nodes.rationale: Nothing is lost, every clone is complete — which is why a committed secret is an incident and a committed binary is permanent weight.
nodes.norm_label: permanent history is the feature and the trap

nodes.label: AbortError
nodes.rationale: Aborted fetch rejects with a DOMException named AbortError; treating it as failure flashes an error on every keystroke.

nodes.label: AbortController in an effect
nodes.rationale: Cleanup calls abort(); catch must ignore AbortError or cancel becomes a visible error.

nodes.label: ignore flag
nodes.rationale: let ignore = false inside setup so each run has its own flag; cleanup sets it true. Fixes the render, does not cancel the request.

nodes.label: Updater form removes a state dependency
nodes.rationale: setMessages(msgs => [...msgs, received]) does not read messages, so the chat does not reconnect on every message.
nodes.norm_label: updater form removes a state dependency

nodes.label: react-hooks/exhaustive-deps
nodes.rationale: Computes the correct array from the code. Disabling converts a compile-time complaint into a runtime bug months later.

nodes.label: cleanup(old) then setup(new)
nodes.rationale: Cleanup closes over the render that created it, so it disconnects the old room, not the new one.

nodes.label: Three dependency-array forms
nodes.rationale: No array: after every commit. Empty: after initial commit only. Populated: initial plus Object.is change, positionally.

nodes.label: Effect Events
nodes.rationale: Non-reactive pieces of Effect code. Always see latest props and state; calling them does not re-run the surrounding Effect.

nodes.label: Synchronize with an external system
nodes.rationale: If you are not synchronizing with a browser API, widget, network, or non-React component, you probably do not need an Effect.

nodes.label: react.dev You Might Not Need an Effect
nodes.norm_label: react.dev you might not need an effect

nodes.label: Twelve You-Might-Not-Need-an-Effect cases
nodes.rationale: Only fetching data (case 12) survives as an effect, and even there a framework or cache library is preferred.

nodes.label: Phase 4 — Effects and synchronization
nodes.rationale: The most misused hook, almost always because it is understood as run-after-render instead of synchronize-with-something-outside-React.

nodes.label: Phase 3 — State and the render cycle
nodes.norm_label: phase 3 — state and the render cycle

nodes.label: When cleanup is not the answer
nodes.norm_label: when cleanup is not the answer

nodes.label: The dependency array is not a preference
nodes.norm_label: the dependency array is not a preference

nodes.label: You might not need an effect
nodes.norm_label: you might not need an effect

nodes.label: Part 3 — Concurrent React and the server
nodes.norm_label: part 3 — concurrent react and the server

nodes.label: Analytics Effects need no cleanup
nodes.rationale: The double logVisit is development-only and must not skew production metrics. A POST that mutates application state has neither property.

nodes.label: Buying a product is not an Effect
nodes.rationale: No cleanup fixes a purchase that fires because the page rendered. You want to buy when the user clicks Buy. Same POST verb as analytics, opposite answer.
nodes.norm_label: buying a product is not an effect

nodes.label: Start with ignore, abort when the request is the cost
nodes.rationale: ignore is what react.dev documents and works with any promise. AbortController when payloads, search-as-you-type, or mobile bandwidth make the request itself costly.
nodes.norm_label: start with ignore, abort when the request is the cost

nodes.label: Suppressed interval always shows 1
nodes.rationale: eslint-disable with [] keeps the first render's onTick, which always calls setCount(0 + 1). The counter is frozen at first-render arithmetic.

nodes.label: Refs used to hide a dependency
nodes.rationale: Reading ref.current is not tracked, so a ref can smuggle a reactive value past the linter and produce the same stale-forever bug.
nodes.norm_label: refs used to hide a dependency

nodes.label: Omitted deps freeze the first render
nodes.rationale: An empty array means only the first setup ever runs, so the effect keeps that render's roomId forever. No error, quietly wrong.
nodes.norm_label: omitted deps freeze the first render

nodes.label: Do not use useEffectEvent to avoid dependencies
nodes.rationale: Wrapping the whole effect body to reach [] hides real staleness. Only genuinely event-like logic belongs in an Effect Event.
nodes.norm_label: do not use useeffectevent to avoid dependencies

nodes.label: Effects versus events
nodes.rationale: Effects are caused by rendering; events by a particular interaction. Ask why it happens. If the answer names a user action, it is not an effect.

nodes.label: componentDidMount is the wrong model
nodes.rationale: useEffect(fn, []) stays connected to the first room forever. Synchronization with real deps and cleanup handles mount, update, and unmount.

nodes.label: Passive-effect paint timing is unguaranteed
nodes.rationale: Interaction-caused Effects may run before paint; React may also paint before processing state updates inside them. For a guarantee use useLayoutEffect or setTimeout.

nodes.label: Same POST, opposite homes
nodes.rationale: visit_form analytics stays in an Effect because the form was displayed. Registration POST belongs in handleSubmit because the user pressed the button.

nodes.label: Share handler logic with a plain function
nodes.rationale: Hoisting shared follow-up into an Effect fires it on mount and every product change. An ordinary function in the component body is enough.
nodes.norm_label: share handler logic with a plain function

nodes.label: Do not use Effects to transform data or handle events
nodes.rationale: Transform at the top of the component. By the time an Effect runs you do not know what the user did.
nodes.norm_label: do not use effects to transform data or handle events

nodes.label: for...in vs Object.keys
nodes.rationale: for...in enumerates the prototype chain as well. That single difference is why Object.keys should be the default.

nodes.label: Integer-index enumeration order
nodes.rationale: Integer-index keys come out ascending regardless of insertion. {100,2,7} yields 2, 7, 100. Objects keyed by numeric ID are not ordered collections.

nodes.label: Object.keys throws on null and undefined
nodes.rationale: Non-objects are coerced except null and undefined, which throw TypeError. Guard with ?? {}.
nodes.norm_label: object.keys throws on null and undefined

nodes.label: Object.entries
nodes.rationale: Array of [key, value] pairs for own enumerable string-keyed properties. Keys come back as strings.

nodes.label: Object.keys
nodes.rationale: Returns own enumerable string keys. Default over for...in because it does not walk the prototype chain.

nodes.label: Own enumerable string-keyed
nodes.rationale: MDN's phrase for entries/keys/values. Skips inherited, non-enumerable, and symbol keys. Same set JSON.stringify serialises.

nodes.label: Reflect.ownKeys
nodes.rationale: Returns every own property including symbols and non-enumerables. getOwnPropertyNames adds non-enumerable strings only.

nodes.label: Map ↔ Object conversion
nodes.rationale: Object.fromEntries(map) and new Map(Object.entries(obj)). The bridge into real insertion order and non-string keys.

nodes.label: Object.fromEntries
nodes.rationale: Transforms any iterable of key-value pairs into a plain object. Reverse of Object.entries. Does not use this; always a plain object.

nodes.label: entries/fromEntries round-trip losses
nodes.rationale: Drops symbols, non-enumerables, inherited, prototype, accessors (getters invoked), descriptors, and numeric key order. Shallow.

nodes.label: URLSearchParams to object is lossy
nodes.rationale: Repeated keys cannot live on an object. tag=a&tag=b becomes {tag:'b'}. Use getAll or keep URLSearchParams.

nodes.label: Object.keys / values / entries / fromEntries
nodes.rationale: Three methods share one definition: own enumerable string-keyed properties. fromEntries performs the reverse of entries.

nodes.label: 08.1 · What they include and what they skip
nodes.norm_label: 08.1 · what they include and what they skip

nodes.label: entries → map/filter → fromEntries
nodes.rationale: Objects have no map or filter. Convert to pairs, use array methods, convert back. A pick built this way is safer than delete.

nodes.label: Glean client ID (react-p0)
nodes.rationale: Firefox Glean telemetry client_id 1dee9a49-7f70-4d7b-aef9-6845e8b97e82 for the react-p0 .ffprof profile.

nodes.label: Glean client ID (react-p1)
nodes.rationale: Firefox Glean telemetry client_id 57a0dc83-3bf7-433c-87ff-01598547499a for the react-p1 .ffprof profile.

nodes.label: NSS Internal PKCS #11 Module (react-p0)
nodes.rationale: Firefox profile NSS module. configdir is sql:…/sandbox/react-p0/.ffprof. Internal, critical; slot flags include ECC, RSA, DSA, DH, AES, SHA256, SHA512, SSL, TLS.

nodes.label: NSS Internal PKCS #11 Module (react-p1)
nodes.rationale: Firefox profile NSS module. configdir is sql:…/.claude/worktrees/react-phases/sandbox/react-p1/.ffprof, so this profile was created from a worktree path.

nodes.label: require is synchronous
nodes.rationale: require reads and compiles on the main thread, blocking the event loop. Fine at startup; a latency spike inside a request handler. Also why CJS cannot load ESM with top-level await.

nodes.label: CJS ↔ ESM interop
nodes.rationale: Both directions work on Node 24. require(esm) shed its experimental label in v24.15.0. One hard boundary remains: top-level await.

nodes.label: cjs-module-lexer named exports
nodes.rationale: Node statically analyses CJS source to synthesise named exports. Computed keys, loops, and conditionals are invisible. Default-import and destructure.

nodes.label: Dual package hazard
nodes.rationale: Separate CJS and ESM builds can both load in one process. Module-scope state then exists twice.

nodes.label: ERR_REQUIRE_ASYNC_MODULE
nodes.rationale: require cannot load an ESM graph that contains top-level await anywhere in the subtree. Use await import() or --experimental-print-required-tla.

nodes.label: __esModule marker
nodes.rationale: Node sets __esModule: true on the namespace from require(esm) so interop code can distinguish it from a plain CJS export object.

nodes.label: JSON import attribute
nodes.rationale: import data from './x.json' with { type: 'json' }. Mandatory security requirement; the old assert spelling is gone.

nodes.label: require() of an ES module
nodes.rationale: Returns the module namespace object, not the default export. A default is at .default. Unflagged in v23.0.0 / v22.12.0 / v20.19.0.

nodes.label: main vs exports
nodes.rationale: main is the old single entry point. exports takes precedence wherever both exist.

nodes.label: Conditional exports
nodes.rationale: Node picks the first matching condition in written order. types must be first; default must be last.

nodes.label: Dual package hazard
nodes.rationale: Shipping both CJS and ESM builds means an app can load both. Caches, registries and instanceof disagree. Ship ESM only or keep state out of module scope.

nodes.label: ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED
nodes.rationale: Thrown for any path not listed. Adding an exports map is a major version if consumers were deep-importing.

nodes.label: exports map
nodes.rationale: Defines the package public surface and makes everything else unreachable. Turns an open directory into a declared interface.

nodes.label: Subpath exports
nodes.rationale: Left side is the public name, right side is the file. Once exports exists the only valid specifiers are listed keys, including the real path.

nodes.label: Phase 1 gate: dual-consumer exports map
nodes.rationale: A package with type module, an exports map that blocks deep imports, works from import and require, and ships only what files allows.

nodes.label: Phase 1 — Modules and packages
nodes.rationale: Fourteen pages on how code gets into your program. Target runtime Node 24.19.0 with npm 12.0.2.

nodes.label: Ship ESM only by default
nodes.rationale: require(esm) works from Node 22.12 and is stable in 24.15, so CommonJS consumers are served without a second build.

nodes.label: Session cookie flags
nodes.rationale: HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax, Path=/, Max-Age, __Host- prefix. Node sends invalid flags with 200; browsers drop them silently. ~4096-byte cap.

nodes.label: HTTP Strict Transport Security
nodes.rationale: Ignored on plaintext by spec. includeSubDomains makes uncertified hosts unreachable. preload takes months to remove. Ramp max-age from 300.

nodes.label: TLS 1.3 session resumption trap
nodes.rationale: getSession() in the connect callback does not resume on TLS 1.3. Cache the ticket from the session event. Measured 3.82 ms resumed vs 5.58 ms full.

nodes.label: X-Forwarded-Proto trust
nodes.rationale: Client-settable. Trust req.socket.encrypted when Node terminates TLS; trust the header only if a controlled proxy overwrites it and the origin is unreachable.

nodes.label: Account lockout as DoS
nodes.rationale: Hard lock after N failures lets anyone lock any known email. Use exponential per-account delay plus per-IP limit; sit the limiter in front of scrypt.

nodes.label: Rate limiting
nodes.rationale: In-memory Map is per-process (4 workers → 4× limit) and unbounded (200k keys / 31.2 MB). Redis INCR+TTL is the shared store.

nodes.label: Redis INCR then EXPIRE race
nodes.rationale: Death between INCR and EXPIRE leaves ttl -1 and a permanent lock. One Lua script: INCR, PEXPIRE only when n==1.

nodes.label: Fixed window, sliding window, token bucket
nodes.rationale: Fixed window allowed 10 in 80 ms against 5/s. Sliding has no boundary. Token bucket separates burst and refill. Sliding for login; token bucket for APIs.
nodes.norm_label: fixed window, sliding window, token bucket

nodes.label: Content Security Policy
nodes.rationale: script-src 'unsafe-inline' is not a CSP. Per-response nonce; a fixed nonce is a permanent password. Roll out via Report-Only. Second line behind output encoding.

nodes.label: helmet defaults
nodes.rationale: x-xss-protection: 0 is deliberate. Default HSTS includes includeSubDomains. Node sends none of these headers itself.

nodes.label: X-Content-Type-Options nosniff
nodes.rationale: Without it browsers sniff bytes so text/plain containing script can execute. Node sends no Content-Type by default. Pair with a correct type and a separate origin for uploads.

nodes.label: HTTPS, HSTS and cookie flags
nodes.rationale: TLS encrypts; HSTS stops the plaintext first request; cookie flags remain if either fails. Node validates no cookie attribute.

nodes.label: Rate limiting and brute-force protection
nodes.rationale: Takes volume away so timing, stuffing and ReDoS stop being practical. Algorithm, key and store are the three decisions.

nodes.label: Security headers and CSP
nodes.rationale: Browser instructions, not API access control. helmet() is 0.80 µs and 356 bytes; only CSP needs a decision.

nodes.label: Phase 8 — Security
nodes.rationale: All 27 pages written on Node 24.19.0. Node-side concerns; Express owns route authz; data-access owns query hardening.

nodes.label: Limiter fail-open vs fail-closed
nodes.rationale: Open keeps a read API up unprotected; closed keeps login protected while unavailable. Silent fail-open is never acceptable — alert on limiter errors.

nodes.label: CORS is not access control
nodes.rationale: CORS relaxes the browser SOP; curl and server fetch ignore it. Dangerous only with cookie auth plus reflected Origin and Allow-Credentials.

nodes.label: node --test file discovery
nodes.rationale: Picks up *.test.*, *-test.*, and everything in test/. Not *.spec.* — that suite runs zero tests and still exits 0. A directory positional is a module, not a search.

nodes.label: node:test runner
nodes.rationale: A test fails when it throws. test and it are the same function. Hooks may be async; a rejected before fails every test in the suite.

nodes.label: Test process isolation
nodes.rationale: Default --test-isolation=process: one child per file. none is ~2× faster and hides cross-file state. Local loop, not CI.

nodes.label: node:test concurrency
nodes.rationale: Files run in parallel up to core count. Tests in one file are serial unless {concurrency: true}. it.only needs --test-only or it is ignored.

nodes.label: node:assert/strict
nodes.rationale: legacy.equal(1, '1') passes. An assertion that ignores type is worse than none. assert.equal in strict is strictEqual.

nodes.label: deepStrictEqual rules
nodes.rationale: Object.is: NaN equals NaN, 0 ≠ -0. Prototypes compared so a class instance ≠ a literal. Holes ≠ undefined. Explicit undefined keys count. Maps ignore insertion order.

nodes.label: assert.throws matcher
nodes.rationale: Regexp, property subset, or class. A string is the failure message and can raise ERR_AMBIGUOUS_ARGUMENT. Matcher functions must return true. rejects must be awaited.

nodes.label: Ephemeral real server
nodes.rationale: Boot the real app so middleware runs. Bind 127.0.0.1 not localhost (verbatim DNS can yield ::1). Close in after; closeAllConnections if keep-alive hangs.

nodes.label: listen(0) ephemeral port
nodes.rationale: Hardcoded ports plus file-parallelism produce EADDRINUSE as a race. Read server.address().port after listen(0).

nodes.label: supertest
nodes.rationale: Starts the app on an ephemeral port, chained .expect() for status/headers/body. Empty res.body usually means missing Content-Type. Pick fetch or supertest, not both.

nodes.label: assert.rejects shapes
nodes.rationale: Await rejects, return the promise, or await fn().catch(e => e). No default timeout — set --test-timeout in CI. Prefer allSettled so siblings do not outlive the test.

nodes.label: Forgotten await misattribution
nodes.rationale: Test prints ✔; file prints ✖ and exit 1 with 'asynchronous activity after the test ended'. A .catch() swallows the evidence and CI goes green.

nodes.label: node:test — the built-in runner
nodes.rationale: No dependency to test a Node app. describe/it, hooks, mocks, timers, coverage, snapshots, watch. Verified Node 24.19.0, 8 cores.

nodes.label: node:assert — strict mode and deep equality
nodes.rationale: Import node:assert/strict, never the legacy == module. Verified Node 24.19.0.
nodes.norm_label: node:assert — strict mode and deep equality

nodes.label: API testing
nodes.rationale: Make HTTP requests. Do not fake req/res. fetch + listen(0) or supertest 7.2.2 against express 5.2.1.

nodes.label: Async testing done right
nodes.rationale: The runner ends when the test function settles. A missing await moves assertions past that point. Corrects the 'passes silently' folklore on Node 24.19.0.

nodes.label: try/catch rejection test trap
nodes.rationale: If the code stops throwing, catch never runs and the test passes. assert.rejects reports Missing expected rejection.

nodes.label: Express 5.x on Node 24
