nodes.rationale: Target Express 5.2.1 / Node 24.19.0. Thin routing and middleware layer over node:http. 11 phases, 114 topics, 78 pages.

nodes.label: Express request lifecycle
nodes.rationale: Accept → middleware chain → handler → response (or error middleware). Lost if nobody calls next and nobody writes.

nodes.label: Express over node:http
nodes.rationale: Not a second language or full architecture — router + middleware on http.Server.

nodes.label: createApp(deps) factory
nodes.rationale: Pure factory; no listen inside. Production listens only after deps are ready. Supertest covers happy + 403 without a real DB.

nodes.label: Express route ordering
nodes.rationale: Order is load-bearing. Static segments before params or /export becomes an id. Express will not warn.

nodes.label: Express 5 path-to-regexp
nodes.rationale: * and :id? throw on Express 5; path matching was rewritten vs 4.

nodes.label: Middleware contract
nodes.rationale: (req, res, next) => void — continue, finish, or error. The whole framework is a stack.

nodes.label: next() semantics
nodes.rationale: next() vs next(err) vs hang vs double-send. Body parser early; error middleware last.

nodes.label: Body size limits
nodes.rationale: 413 too large is DoS control, not polish. Mount JSON parsing with a hard size limit.

nodes.label: express.json and urlencoded
nodes.rationale: Content-type gated parsers. Malformed bodies become 400 into error middleware.

nodes.label: Phase 10 — Testable app and ops boundary
nodes.norm_label: phase 10 — testable app and ops boundary

nodes.label: DTO mapping at the edge
nodes.rationale: Map API DTOs at the edge; pick feature or layer folders and stay consistent.

nodes.label: Transaction-per-request middleware
nodes.rationale: Thin wrapper only; transaction mechanism stays in Node Phase 6.

nodes.label: HTTP 202 Accepted
nodes.rationale: 202 means accepted for processing, not necessarily completed.

nodes.label: Transactional outbox
nodes.rationale: Persist in a transaction with an outbox when needed; Node Phase 7 owns retries and worker shutdown.

nodes.label: req.validated
nodes.rationale: Put parsed result on req under a clear name — not mixed with raw body.

nodes.label: Idempotency keys
nodes.rationale: Idempotency-Key header, store outcome, replay safe responses for unsafe requests.

nodes.label: Phase 7 — Layering at the Express edge
nodes.rationale: Folders and function boundaries so routes stay thin. Deliverable: handlers under ~20 lines, services unit-testable without req/res.
nodes.norm_label: phase 7 — layering at the express edge

nodes.label: Part 3 — API product
nodes.rationale: Phases 6–7: REST surface clients depend on, then Express-side controller/service/repository wiring only.

nodes.label: Domain vs transport
nodes.rationale: Transport is HTTP; domain is product language. Crossing them freely couples tests to Express.

nodes.label: DTO at the edge
nodes.rationale: Map to a DTO at the HTTP edge so API shapes stay stable when persistence models change.

nodes.label: Fat controllers
nodes.rationale: If a handler needs scrolling, logic leaked upward. Smells: SQL in the route, 200-line try/catch, copy-pasted auth.

nodes.label: Thin handler pipeline
nodes.rationale: Auth middleware then validate middleware then thin handler then service; one use-case per handler.

nodes.label: Background jobs from routes
nodes.rationale: Validate, persist, enqueue, respond. Never await email, webhooks, or PDF generation on the request path.

nodes.label: Private elements are not inherited
nodes.rationale: JavaScript has no protected. Parent and child can reuse the same #name as independent slots.

nodes.label: Class methods are non-enumerable
nodes.rationale: Hand-assigned prototype methods show up in for...in. Class methods do not.

nodes.label: delete on an array leaves a hole
nodes.rationale: length is unchanged. Use splice, filter, or toSpliced. Holes make array methods inconsistent and slower.
nodes.norm_label: delete on an array leaves a hole

nodes.label: delete removes own properties only
nodes.rationale: Does not free memory, remove variables, or touch the prototype. Deleting an own key unshadows the inherited one.

nodes.label: delete return value
nodes.rationale: true does not mean anything was deleted. false (or TypeError in strict) only reports an own non-configurable property.

nodes.label: Map for dynamic keys
nodes.rationale: map.delete is first-class, no HiddenClass cost, any key type. If you delete in a loop you wanted a Map.

nodes.label: Rest destructuring to omit a key
nodes.rationale: const { password, ...safe } = user builds a new stable-shape object. Shallow; nested copies survive.
nodes.norm_label: rest destructuring to omit a key

nodes.label: Four existence checks
nodes.rationale: in, Object.hasOwn, hasOwnProperty, and !== undefined disagree on inherited keys and on keys holding undefined.

nodes.label: Object.fromEntries
nodes.rationale: Reverse of Object.entries. Gives objects the map/filter they do not have via the entries round trip.

nodes.label: Object.keys own enumerable string keys
nodes.rationale: keys/values/entries share one definition. They drop inherited, non-enumerable, and symbol keys. Same set as JSON.stringify.

nodes.label: Integer-index key order
nodes.rationale: Integer-like keys first ascending, then strings by insertion, then symbols. Not the order you wrote.

nodes.label: __proto__ prototype setter
nodes.rationale: { __proto__: x } sets the prototype, not a property. { __proto__ } and { ['__proto__']: p } are different.

nodes.label: Shallow copy
nodes.rationale: spread, Object.assign, slice, Array.from copy one level. Nested references are shared. Usually the right answer for immutable updates.

nodes.label: Prototype chain
nodes.rationale: An object is own properties plus a link. Lookup walks until it finds a name or reaches null. Nothing is copied onto instances.

nodes.label: Existence-check decision table
nodes.rationale: Object.hasOwn by default for data. in for feature detection. !== undefined only when missing and undefined mean the same thing.

nodes.label: async always returns a promise
nodes.rationale: No path out of an async function is not a promise. A return fulfils, a throw rejects, a returned promise is adopted.

nodes.label: async return vs Promise.resolve identity
nodes.rationale: Promise.resolve(p) returns the same native promise. An async function must create its own and resolve it with p, so references differ.

nodes.label: await assimilates thenables
nodes.rationale: await cares about the then shape, not the class. An object with an unrelated then field is assimilated.

nodes.label: once wrapper
nodes.rationale: A called flag that ignores a second invocation. Exactly what a promise provides structurally by settling once.

nodes.label: Default thrower error propagation
nodes.rationale: There is no special skip-to-catch rule. Each then without onRejected uses (x) => { throw x; }, so a rejection walks link by link.

nodes.label: Handling restores the chain
nodes.rationale: After a catch the chain is fulfilled. Later then runs on both success and recovered-failure paths. Re-throw to stop.

nodes.label: .then(f, g) vs .then(f).catch(g)
nodes.rationale: Two-argument then handles only upstream rejections. A throw in f rejects the next promise and is not caught by g. Trailing catch catches both.

nodes.label: finally is a link, not a clause
nodes.rationale: finally attaches to the promise immediately before it. It is transparent and does not mark a rejection handled. A chain ending in finally still reports unhandled rejection.
nodes.norm_label: finally is a link, not a clause

nodes.label: reduce-over-then sequencing
nodes.rationale: [f1,f2,f3].reduce((p,f) => p.then(f), Promise.resolve()) runs an unknown number of dependent steps in order.

nodes.label: then returns a new promise
nodes.rationale: Each link represents the previous step and this handler. Combined with adoption, each result becomes the next argument at the same level.

nodes.label: Promise chaining
nodes.rationale: then returns a new promise representing the previous step and your handler. Flat chains follow from that plus adoption.

nodes.label: Promise
nodes.rationale: A state machine that runs forwards exactly once. An object representing eventual completion or failure; you attach callbacks instead of passing them in.

nodes.label: Promise three states
nodes.rationale: pending / fulfilled / rejected. Transition is one-shot and irreversible. Resolved is not fulfilled — a resolved promise can still be pending.

nodes.label: async/await desugars to then
nodes.rationale: await 1 becomes Promise.resolve(1).then(continuation). Semantics equal a chain; the gain is try/catch, loops, if/else, and locals in one scope.

nodes.label: Promise as the return-value fix
nodes.rationale: A real fix must give the operation a return value representing the eventual result so steps sequence by return rather than by call.

nodes.label: Nest then to scope a catch
nodes.rationale: A nested catch only sees its scope. The pattern for letting optional steps fail while a critical failure still reaches the outer handler.
nodes.norm_label: nest then to scope a catch

nodes.label: setImmediate work chunking
nodes.rationale: Yield between chunks so other callbacks can run; total work slightly slower, process stays responsive.

nodes.label: UV_THREADPOOL_SIZE
nodes.rationale: Default 4, max 1024. Created lazily; size is fixed after first use. Set in the environment before start.

nodes.label: Blocking vs non-blocking
nodes.rationale: Blocking holds the thread until the answer is ready; non-blocking returns immediately.

nodes.label: Password storage
nodes.rationale: ~422,000 MD5 guesses/sec against about 11 scrypt hashes — and 23 logins/sec the thread pool allows.

nodes.label: ReDoS
nodes.rationale: 28 characters bought 3.6 s of CPU, during which a 10 ms interval fired zero times.

nodes.label: Four event-loop blocking fixes
nodes.rationale: Async version; chunk with setImmediate; worker_threads; queue out of the request.

nodes.label: Sync suffix in a request path is a bug
nodes.rationale: Sync is fine at startup before the server listens; in a request handler it stalls everyone.
nodes.norm_label: sync suffix in a request path is a bug

nodes.label: dns.lookup thread-pool trap
nodes.rationale: dns.lookup calls getaddrinfo and uses the pool; outbound HTTP can starve fs. resolve4 is a real DNS query with no threads.

nodes.label: Thread pool vs worker_threads
nodes.rationale: Pool runs C/C++ ops you never see; worker_threads run JS in their own isolate.

nodes.label: await yields lock-free safety
nodes.rationale: No locks between callbacks, but a read-modify-write spanning await can interleave.

nodes.label: Network I/O uses kernel readiness
nodes.rationale: Sockets use epoll/kqueue/IOCP with no extra threads.

nodes.label: require is synchronous
nodes.rationale: Reads and compiles on the main thread. Fine at startup; a latency spike in a handler.

nodes.label: INHERIT and SET ROLE
nodes.rationale: INHERIT (default) activates group privileges automatically. NOINHERIT or WITH INHERIT FALSE leaves membership available until SET ROLE. SET ROLE is not SET SESSION AUTHORIZATION and leaks on a pooled connection until RESET ROLE or DISCARD ALL.

nodes.label: pg_authid cluster-wide roles
nodes.rationale: Roles live in pg_authid and are shared by every database. A pg_dump contains grants but not roles unless pg_dumpall --roles-only ran first.

nodes.label: PostgreSQL role
nodes.rationale: There is no user type. LOGIN is an attribute. CREATE USER is CREATE ROLE … LOGIN. A group is a role nobody logs in as.

nodes.label: MAINTAIN privilege
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL 17+ delegates VACUUM, ANALYZE, REINDEX, CLUSTER and REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW without ownership. VACUUM without MAINTAIN returns OK and only warns, so nightly jobs can succeed while vacuuming nothing.

nodes.label: Ownership outranks privileges
nodes.rationale: REVOKE from the owner succeeds and is not a boundary: ownership carries the right to GRANT it back. There is no GRANT DROP; DDL is an ownership right.

nodes.label: Least privilege model
nodes.rationale: A role is an identity, a privilege is a verb on one object, ownership outranks both, and effective privileges are the union over every inherited role.

nodes.label: log_statement logs bound parameters
nodes.rationale: Parameters stay out of statement text and pg_stat_activity but log_statement=all adds DETAIL: Parameters. log_parameter_max_length defaults to -1 (unlimited).

nodes.label: pg_stat_activity.query text
nodes.rationale: Any superuser or pg_read_all_stats member can read the running statement, including the last statement of an idle session. Bound parameters appear as $1 in the view.

nodes.label: application_name
nodes.rationale: Empty by default. Set it on the pool so pg_stat_activity, pg_stat_statements and the server log attribute work to a service.

nodes.label: Roles are not in pg_dump
nodes.rationale: The GRANT is dumped; CREATE ROLE is not. A complete logical backup is pg_dumpall --roles-only plus pg_dump. Also absent: tablespaces, other databases, postgresql.conf, pg_hba.conf, replication slots.

nodes.label: pg_restore continues after errors
nodes.rationale: relation already exists is reported and the run keeps going. Use --exit-on-error in automation, --clean --if-exists to replace, or restore into a new database and rename.

nodes.label: pg.Pool vs PgBouncer
nodes.rationale: pg.Pool bounds one Node process. PgBouncer bounds total backends across every client. They are complementary, not alternatives.

nodes.label: replicas × pool max
nodes.rationale: pg.Pool max is per process. Ten replicas × 10 is the whole default max_connections before workers and admin sessions. A rolling deploy doubles it.

nodes.label: Protocol-level prepared statements
nodes.rationale: Since PgBouncer 1.21.0, named extended-protocol statements work in transaction mode when max_prepared_statements is non-zero (default 200). SQL-level PREPARE is still unsupported.

nodes.label: server_reset_query unused in transaction mode
nodes.rationale: DISCARD ALL runs in session mode on client disconnect. In transaction pooling it is not used; there is no automatic cleanup between transactions.

nodes.label: Session features broken in transaction mode
nodes.rationale: SET/RESET, LISTEN/NOTIFY, WITH HOLD cursors, SQL PREPARE, temp tables, LOAD and session advisory locks never work. Failures are intermittent because they appear only when the next transaction lands on a different backend.
nodes.norm_label: session features broken in transaction mode

nodes.label: SET LOCAL on a pooled connection
nodes.rationale: Plain SET persists across a pooled handoff; SET LOCAL does not. A leaked tenant id is a cross-tenant exposure. Use pg_advisory_xact_lock, not session advisory locks.
nodes.norm_label: set local on a pooled connection

nodes.label: Transaction pooling
nodes.rationale: Server connection returns when the transaction finishes. Measured: 40 sequential clients used 1 backend; 40 concurrent used exactly default_pool_size=5. Session mode pins a backend for the client lifetime and saves nothing behind pg.Pool.

nodes.label: Idle-in-transaction pool exhaustion
nodes.rationale: In transaction pooling the backend is held for the whole transaction. Five open transactions filled a pool of 5. Set idle_in_transaction_session_timeout and statement_timeout; both default to 0 (disabled).

nodes.label: query_wait_timeout
nodes.rationale: Default 120 s. With pool size 5, two extra clients holding BEGIN waited 120204 ms then 08P01. Upstream timeouts fire first, so the symptom is the service hanging.

nodes.label: client.release() in finally
nodes.rationale: A client never released on the error path is the most common way to produce pool exhaustion.

nodes.label: connectionTimeoutMillis
nodes.rationale: Unset by default, so pool.connect() waits forever on a saturated pool. Set it shorter than the upstream HTTP timeout.

nodes.label: SHOW POOLS
nodes.rationale: cl_waiting and maxwait are the leading indicator of the 120-second failure. Pair with pg_stat_activity state = idle in transaction for the cause.

nodes.label: Read-your-writes
nodes.rationale: A client must see its own committed writes. Async replicas replay after the primary commits, so a post-save read can return the old value with no error. Load-dependent and invisible in development.

nodes.label: remote_apply
nodes.rationale: COMMIT returns once WAL is replayed and visible on the synchronous standby. Apply per transaction with SET LOCAL; a global setting couples write availability to replica health.

nodes.label: replay_lag
nodes.rationale: On an async standby, approximates the delay before recent transactions became visible. now() - pg_last_xact_replay_timestamp() grows without bound on an idle primary; compare receive vs replay LSN for health.

nodes.label: synchronous_commit
nodes.rationale: Per-transaction. on is not synchronous replication unless synchronous_standby_names is set. Only remote_apply waits for replay. A slow synchronous standby stalls commits on the primary.

nodes.label: Four WAL LSN stages
nodes.rationale: sent_lsn, write_lsn, flush_lsn, replay_lsn on pg_stat_replication. The flush-to-replay gap is durability without visibility. Lag columns revert to NULL when caught up and idle.

nodes.label: Sticky-to-primary and LSN wait
nodes.rationale: Sticky window longer than typical replay_lag is simple. Capturing pg_current_wal_lsn() and requiring pg_last_wal_replay_lsn() >= that LSN is exact. Not reading from replicas is often correct.

nodes.label: Read routing hierarchy
nodes.rationale: Same-request and post-write reads, and any read that feeds a write decision, stay on the primary. Lists, search, feeds and analytics may go to a replica.

nodes.label: pg_cancel_backend vs pg_terminate_backend
nodes.rationale: Cancel stops the running query and keeps the session; it does nothing to idle in transaction. Terminate closes the session and rolls back. Prefer cancel first; set idle_in_transaction_session_timeout so humans are the fallback.

nodes.label: idle in transaction
nodes.rationale: BEGIN then the application went away. Holds locks, pins the vacuum horizon, and occupies a pooled backend. query shows the last statement, the clue to the missing COMMIT or release().

nodes.label: pg_blocking_pids
nodes.rationale: Returns pids holding locks the waiter needs. Fix the root of the chain, not the queue. pg_locks is the detail when lock mode and object matter.

nodes.label: pg_stat_activity
nodes.rationale: One row per server process. Filter backend_type = client backend and state <> idle, order by xact_start. xact_age vs query_age distinguishes a slow statement from idle in transaction. Remembers nothing.

nodes.label: Wait events
nodes.rationale: Lock means find the blocker. Client/ClientRead means the application is slow, not the database. IO is disk-bound.

nodes.label: Query normalisation
nodes.rationale: Literals become $n so one shape aggregates. String concatenation fills pg_stat_statements.max (default 5000) and evicts useful rows. queryid is not stable across major versions.

nodes.label: shared_preload_libraries restart
nodes.rationale: The module needs a restart, then CREATE EXTENSION per database. Both halves are required. Enable it before the incident where you first wish you had it.

nodes.label: total_exec_time beats mean time
nodes.rationale: A 4 ms lookup run 500000 times costs far more than an 8 s nightly report. Slow-query logging never shows the cheap-but-constant query.

nodes.label: Cumulative counters need a delta
nodes.rationale: A single snapshot is since last reset, possibly months. Monitoring products sample and report rates. pg_stat_statements_reset() is unrecoverable.

nodes.label: pg_read_all_stats
nodes.rationale: Non-superusers see only their own query text. Granting this role to monitoring is the read-only observability privilege. The same membership can read every session's SQL via pg_stat_activity.

nodes.label: stddev_exec_time
nodes.rationale: Large relative to mean on a high-call statement signals parameter-dependent plans, lock waits or data skew. An average hides it.

nodes.label: Separate owner and app roles
nodes.rationale: Separate roles cost a bootstrap step and a second connection string for migrations. A leaked app credential is then bounded by a readable grant list instead of superuser.

nodes.label: Atomic write pattern
nodes.rationale: Write a unique temp file in the same directory with 'wx', sync(), then rename over the target. rename is atomic within one filesystem.

nodes.label: EXDEV cross-device rename
nodes.rationale: rename across mounts throws EXDEV. In containers /tmp is often a different mount, so write-to-tmpdir-then-move is broken.

nodes.label: mkdtemp
nodes.rationale: Creates a directory atomically with a random suffix so there is no window to pre-create or symlink a predictable temp path.

nodes.label: rm recursive force
nodes.rationale: Modern rm -rf. Replaces deprecated rmdir({recursive}) (DEP0147). force makes a missing path a no-op for finally cleanup.

nodes.label: EMFILE
nodes.rationale: Per-process fd limit. One leaked handle per request exhausts the budget; every later file and socket fails. Invisible on a high-ulimit laptop.

nodes.label: FileHandle.sync
nodes.rationale: fsync — only way to know bytes reached disk rather than the page cache. Required before rename in the atomic-write pattern.

nodes.label: FileHandle
nodes.rationale: open() returns a handle owning an OS descriptor. Close in finally; GC does not reliably reclaim leaked fds.

nodes.label: 'wx' exclusive create
nodes.rationale: Atomic create-if-absent; fails with EEXIST. How you build a lock file without a check-then-create race.

nodes.label: err.code
nodes.rationale: Branch on code (ENOENT, EEXIST, EACCES, ENOSPC, EMFILE, EXDEV), never message text. Swallowing all errors hides EACCES as empty config.

nodes.label: node:fs/promises
nodes.rationale: Default filesystem API. Every operation returns a promise; errors are exceptions with a code; nothing blocks the event loop.

nodes.label: rename atomicity
nodes.rationale: Atomic within one filesystem: readers see old or new, never a partial write. Across devices throws EXDEV.

nodes.label: memfs
nodes.rationale: Full in-memory fs for tests. Fast and isolated, but one device so EXDEV, umask, permissions, and EMFILE never appear.

nodes.label: node:sea getAsset
nodes.rationale: Assets live inside a single executable, not on disk. Branch on isSea(); prefix-only builtin (require('sea') hits npm).

nodes.label: Virtual filesystem
nodes.rationale: An object implementing the fs interface without a disk. Stream constructors accept an fs option so you can substitute without monkey-patching.

nodes.label: Mid-stream upload size limit
nodes.rationale: Count bytes as they arrive and destroy past the limit. Content-Length is client-supplied and absent under chunked encoding.

nodes.label: Inject fs as a dependency
nodes.rationale: Tests pass memfs, production passes fs/promises, no global mock. Leaves the door open for S3 later. Do not mock tests whose subject is the filesystem.

nodes.label: Stale planner statistics
nodes.rationale: A never-analyzed table has reltuples=-1 (unknown). Stale stats after 200× growth estimated 1 row vs 400001 actual and chose a bad index-only scan.

nodes.label: Bitmap heap scan
nodes.rationale: Bitmap Index Scan collects locations, then heap is read in physical order. Recheck Cond / Heap Blocks: lossy= means the bitmap exceeded work_mem.

nodes.label: Index scan
nodes.rationale: Walk the index and fetch each heap row. Chosen for a handful of rows; random I/O but very few of them.

nodes.label: random_page_cost
nodes.rationale: Default 4.0 assumes spinning disks. On SSD ~1.1 makes index scans more attractive. Change this instead of disable_seqscan.

nodes.label: Sequential scan
nodes.rationale: Correct when most of the table qualifies. Forced index scan on 80% of 500k rows was 3× slower with 400358 vs 3712 buffers.

nodes.label: ANALYZE
nodes.rationale: The planner plans against a sample, not live data. Last step of every bulk load. Takes SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE so reads and writes continue.

nodes.label: autovacuum analyze threshold
nodes.rationale: Fires at threshold + scale_factor × reltuples (50 + 10%). Too late on large tables; lower autovacuum_analyze_scale_factor to 0.01.

nodes.label: default_statistics_target
nodes.rationale: Histogram buckets and MCV count. Raise per column with ALTER COLUMN SET STATISTICS, not globally. Target 1000 took 1309 ms ANALYZE.

nodes.label: Extended statistics
nodes.rationale: CREATE STATISTICS (dependencies, ndistinct, mcv) ON correlated columns. Independence assumed otherwise: 33607 estimated vs 100000 actual, corrected to 100990.

nodes.label: pg_stats
nodes.rationale: null_frac, n_distinct, most_common_vals/freqs, correlation. n_distinct -1 means unique per row; negative fraction scales with table size. reltuples=-1 means never analyzed.

nodes.label: Why an index is not being used
nodes.norm_label: why an index is not being used

nodes.label: Seq scan vs index scan vs bitmap heap scan
nodes.norm_label: seq scan vs index scan vs bitmap heap scan

nodes.label: Cast on the indexed side
nodes.rationale: Casting the indexed column casts every row and skips the index. Cast the literal or parameter instead. Hand-added :: is the trap; pg sends untyped text.

nodes.label: Function-wrapped column
nodes.rationale: lower(email) or created_at::date defeats a B-tree on the bare column. Index the expression or rewrite so the column is bare.

nodes.label: Low selectivity
nodes.rationale: When a value matches most of the table the planner correctly ignores the index. Forcing it for 99.89% active rows was slower than seq scan.

nodes.label: merge_action()
nodes.rationale: Returns INSERT, UPDATE, or DELETE per row. Legal only in a MERGE RETURNING list; elsewhere 42601. rowCount is the total only.

nodes.label: MERGE RETURNING
nodes.rationale: Supported since PostgreSQL 17. Widely-repeated advice that MERGE has no RETURNING is obsolete.

nodes.label: MERGE
nodes.rationale: One statement can insert, update, and delete. First matching WHEN branch wins, so specific conditions must precede bare MATCHED.

nodes.label: WHEN NOT MATCHED BY SOURCE
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL 17 delete-half of a reconcile: target rows the source no longer has.

nodes.label: MERGE 21000 source duplicate
nodes.rationale: Two source rows matching one target raise 21000. Deduplicate with DISTINCT ON before merging.

nodes.label: RETURNING into a CTE
nodes.rationale: DELETE … RETURNING can feed an INSERT in one atomic statement. Sibling CTEs share a snapshot and see only RETURNING output.

nodes.label: ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING RETURNING trap
nodes.rationale: A skipped conflict returns no row. DO UPDATE of a harmless column plus xmax = 0 always returns a row.
nodes.norm_label: on conflict do nothing returning trap

nodes.label: RETURNING old. and new.
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL 18 can return both versions of an updated row. On 17 and below this is a syntax error.

nodes.label: RETURNING
nodes.rationale: The only way to read what a write did without a second query that can see a different transaction's data.

nodes.label: UPDATE ... FROM
nodes.rationale: Inner-join a source of new values. Duplicate source keys pick one winner arbitrarily; MERGE raises 21000 instead.

nodes.label: Lost updates from read-modify-write
nodes.rationale: 20 concurrent SELECT-then-UPDATE increments produced 2. SET qty = qty + 1 serialises under a row lock and produced 20.

nodes.label: UPDATE writes a new tuple version
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL never updates in place. Dead versions wait for VACUUM; non-HOT updates also write new index entries.
nodes.norm_label: update writes a new tuple version

nodes.label: PATCH via COALESCE
nodes.rationale: SET col = COALESCE($n, col) leaves unsent fields alone. It cannot set a column to NULL; then build SET from present keys.

nodes.label: UPDATE
nodes.rationale: SET can reference current values. Forget WHERE and every row changes; read-modify-write loses concurrent increments.

nodes.label: MERGE is not index-arbitrated
nodes.rationale: ON CONFLICT uses a unique index as arbiter. Concurrent MERGE can both take NOT MATCHED and raise 23505 or insert duplicates.

nodes.label: RETURNING vs later SELECT
nodes.rationale: Under READ COMMITTED a follow-up SELECT takes a fresh snapshot and can race. RETURNING is the same statement.

nodes.label: Empty sum is NULL
nodes.rationale: sum FILTER that matches no rows is NULL, not 0; wrap with COALESCE when a pivot needs zeros.

nodes.label: avg is sum over count
nodes.rationale: avg(x) is sum(x)/count(x), so NULLs in x do not enter either side.

nodes.label: GROUP BY collapse
nodes.rationale: GROUP BY reduces the input to one row per key; selected expressions must be keys or aggregates.

nodes.label: bigint numeric as JS strings
nodes.rationale: node-postgres returns bigint and numeric as strings so they are not rounded in JS Number.

nodes.label: Aggregates skip NULL
nodes.rationale: Most aggregates skip NULL; count(*) is the exception that still counts the row.

nodes.label: No GROUP BY is one row
nodes.rationale: An aggregate query with no GROUP BY always returns exactly one row, even on an empty table.
nodes.norm_label: no group by is one row

nodes.label: sum of empty set is NULL
nodes.rationale: sum over no rows is NULL, not 0.
nodes.norm_label: sum of empty set is null

nodes.label: HAVING without GROUP BY
nodes.rationale: HAVING on a no-GROUP-BY aggregate can drop the single result row and return zero rows.

nodes.label: WHERE vs HAVING
nodes.rationale: WHERE filters rows before grouping; HAVING filters groups after aggregates exist.

nodes.label: ERROR 42P20
nodes.rationale: Window functions are illegal in WHERE; they run after grouping.

nodes.label: OVER without collapse
nodes.rationale: A window function computes over a partition but keeps every input row; GROUP BY collapses.

nodes.label: WindowAgg
nodes.rationale: The plan node that evaluates OVER; it is not free even when the function looks cheap.

nodes.label: Create React App sunset
nodes.rationale: Announced 14 February 2025. Still on npm 5.1.0, not marked deprecated — why tutorials still show it.

nodes.label: SPA fallback
nodes.rationale: Direct visit to /orders/42 404s in production unless the host rewrites to index.html.

nodes.label: Vite SPA starter
nodes.rationale: npm create vite --template react-ts. Measured hello-world: 193.27 kB / 60.62 kB gzip, built in 306ms.

nodes.label: Vite server.proxy for Express
nodes.rationale: Forward /api to localhost:3000 so development is same-origin and needs no CORS.

nodes.label: Development vs production bundle size
nodes.rationale: Measured: 1,125,752 vs 194,799 bytes. Selected by process.env.NODE_ENV dead-code branch.

nodes.label: Backport patches
nodes.rationale: Same fix lands on 19.2, 19.1 and 19.0 the same day. backport tag points at 19.0.8.

nodes.label: beta dist-tag is stale
nodes.rationale: Still points at 19.0.0-beta from 2024. Dist-tags are not retired when a cycle ends.

nodes.label: React release channels
nodes.rationale: latest for apps; canary for frameworks; experimental for React's team; beta/rc are frozen leftover tags.

nodes.label: React Foundation
nodes.rationale: Moved under the Linux Foundation on 24 February 2026. RFCs still required. Day-to-day team unchanged.

nodes.label: React 19.2.8 / react-dom 19.2.8
nodes.rationale: Target latest dist-tag as of August 2026. Browser experiments in Firefox 153.0; Node 24.19.0.

nodes.label: When not to choose React
nodes.rationale: Embedded widget (Preact), mostly-static site (Astro), or a team already fluent in Vue/Svelte.

nodes.label: Vite vs React Router vs Next.js
nodes.rationale: Choice is about the server, not React. MERN/PERN default is Vite SPA behind an existing Express API.
nodes.norm_label: vite vs react router vs next.js

nodes.label: Canary is for frameworks
nodes.rationale: Server Components land in canary first. Frameworks pin an exact canary build and take responsibility.

nodes.label: Pin react and react-dom exactly
nodes.rationale: Caret ranges can resolve them to different patches of shared internals.

nodes.label: as const is not as T
nodes.norm_label: as const is not as t

nodes.label: Phase 9 Motion and the cost model
nodes.norm_label: phase 9 motion and the cost model

nodes.label: Sass variables vs CSS custom properties
nodes.norm_label: sass variables vs css custom properties

nodes.label: App boot order
nodes.rationale: validate env → connect pool → createApp(deps) → server.listen → signal ready. Production listens only after deps are ready.

nodes.label: Liveness vs readiness
nodes.rationale: Failing readiness stops new traffic; failing liveness restarts the process. Conflating them causes restart storms. Liveness is cheap; readiness checks pool/redis.

nodes.label: Restart storms
nodes.rationale: A readiness failure that is treated as liveness kills and respawns the process in a loop.

nodes.label: SIGTERM graceful shutdown
nodes.rationale: On SIGTERM stop accepting, drain in-flight work, then close pools. Keep the listen() return value to close later.

nodes.label: http.Server.close
nodes.rationale: Call close on the http.Server from listen(), not on the Express app object.

nodes.label: Auth helpers in tests
nodes.rationale: Helpers mint sessions or JWTs for 403-path coverage.

nodes.label: createApp factory
nodes.rationale: Pure factory; no listen inside. Production listens only after deps are ready.

nodes.label: Supertest against createApp
nodes.rationale: Route tests with mocked services; no real listen or DB.

nodes.label: Phase 10 — Testable app and ops boundary
nodes.rationale: Composition root for HTTP. Docker/Nginx depth lives in their syllabi.
nodes.norm_label: phase 10 — testable app and ops boundary

nodes.label: server.js vs app.js
nodes.rationale: server.js listens; app.js exports the factory. Feature flags and serverless-http adapters are When Needed.

nodes.label: Scoped vs global middleware
nodes.rationale: Global middleware is easy and expensive (runs for health checks and static). Scope auth to /api so probes on /health do not break.

nodes.label: Inject deps via factory not req
nodes.rationale: Avoid putting DB clients on req. Lifecycle and testing — inject via app.locals or factory deps instead.
nodes.norm_label: inject deps via factory not req

nodes.label: CTEs (WITH)
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL 12+ inlines CTEs unless MATERIALIZED is specified.

nodes.label: jsonb_agg
nodes.rationale: One query can return a fully shaped API response instead of Node stitching result sets.

nodes.label: INSERT ... ON CONFLICT
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL upsert via DO NOTHING / DO UPDATE / EXCLUDED instead of extra round trips.

nodes.label: RETURNING
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL's way to get a generated id back without a second query.

nodes.label: pool.query() with $1 placeholders
nodes.rationale: The safe path every time, including IN lists via = ANY($1).

nodes.label: Migrations from Node
nodes.rationale: Forward-only, one file per change, applied inside a transaction, recorded in a tracking table.

nodes.label: Phase 8 — Schema and data from Node
nodes.norm_label: phase 8 — schema and data from node

nodes.label: Phase 9 — CRUD patterns for a real API
nodes.norm_label: phase 9 — crud patterns for a real api

nodes.label: pg type parsing
nodes.rationale: bigint and numeric arrive as strings; finding that out in production is a bad day.

nodes.label: EXPLAIN vs EXPLAIN ANALYZE
nodes.rationale: ANALYZE actually runs the query.

nodes.label: Lost update
nodes.rationale: Promoted to Master because every application hits the read-modify-write bug.

nodes.label: MVCC
nodes.rationale: Snapshots and row versions; readers never block writers.

nodes.label: pg_dump and pg_restore
nodes.rationale: Restore once to verify; backups are Master-tier.

nodes.label: Phase 10 — Indexes and the query planner
nodes.norm_label: phase 10 — indexes and the query planner

nodes.label: Part 3 — Node + raw pg
nodes.rationale: Raw-SQL-first on purpose; no ORM writes the queries.

nodes.label: LEFT JOIN + WHERE bug
nodes.rationale: Filtering the right-hand table in WHERE turns a LEFT JOIN back into an inner join.

nodes.label: Logical query processing order
nodes.rationale: FROM → WHERE → GROUP BY → HAVING → SELECT → ORDER BY → LIMIT; a SELECT alias therefore fails in WHERE.

nodes.label: NOT IN NULL trap
nodes.rationale: One of two SQL mistakes most likely to ship silently, alongside the LEFT JOIN + WHERE bug.

nodes.label: Parameterized queries
nodes.rationale: Never string-build values; driver $1 placeholders are the safety mechanism.

nodes.label: Repository module per resource
nodes.rationale: Plain functions taking a client and returning rows; layering rationale lives in Node Phase 6.

nodes.label: Safe dynamic WHERE
nodes.rationale: Build predicates and a parameter array together; identifiers cannot be parameterized so sort/filter need allowlists.

nodes.label: Application role should not own the schema
nodes.norm_label: application role should not own the schema

nodes.label: When a column beats JSON
nodes.rationale: The schema-versus-document decision is made early and lived with for years.

nodes.label: Why an index is not being used
nodes.rationale: Type mismatch, a function wrapping the column, low selectivity, or stale statistics.
nodes.norm_label: why an index is not being used

nodes.label: Double send
nodes.rationale: First body wins; second write throws Cannot set headers after they are sent to the client.

nodes.label: res.headersSent guard
nodes.rationale: Documented custom-handler guard: if (res.headersSent) return next(err). After a write the default error handler closes the connection.

nodes.label: res.redirect
nodes.rationale: Defaults to 302. Overload accepts an explicit code.

nodes.label: res.send
nodes.rationale: Chooses Content-Type from the body: Buffer → octet-stream, String → text/html, Array/Object → JSON. Flexible and easy to misuse.

nodes.label: res.sendStatus
nodes.rationale: Sets the status and sends its string body — a terminal call, not a variant of res.status.

nodes.label: 401 vs 403
nodes.rationale: 401 unauthenticated; 403 authenticated but not allowed.

nodes.label: Express 5 status 100–999
nodes.rationale: Express 5 restricts res.status() to 100–999 and rejects anything outside that range. An Express 4 habit of passing a made-up code now throws.

nodes.label: Always-200 RPC-over-HTTP
nodes.rationale: Always HTTP 200 with {success:false} is an RPC-over-HTTP habit. Use real statuses; keep error body for details.

nodes.label: 204 No Content
nodes.rationale: Success with no response body (e.g. DELETE). Use res.status(204).end().

nodes.label: One terminal response method
nodes.rationale: Pick one terminal method. Mixing json then send is how headers-already-sent starts. Every branch ends with send/json/end/redirect.

nodes.label: Headers fixed once body starts
nodes.rationale: res.set, res.type, and res.vary are only meaningful before the first write. res.headersSent flips once headers go out.

nodes.label: HTTP status as contract
nodes.rationale: Useful APIs pick 201/204/400/401/403/404/409 deliberately — not always 200. Align with OpenAPI and stick to it.

nodes.label: Error middleware arity detection
nodes.rationale: Function length 4: (err, req, res, next). Omit next and Express treats it as normal middleware; errors vanish into the wrong path.

nodes.label: Four-arg error middleware
nodes.rationale: Error middleware has four parameters. Express detects it by arity. Mount it last.

nodes.label: Express 5 async rejection forwarding
nodes.rationale: Rejected promises from async handlers reach error middleware on Express 5. You do not need express-async-errors for that baseline. Express 4 often needed wrappers or next(err).

nodes.label: Error response contract
nodes.rationale: One public JSON shape for errors. Include a stable code. Never send err.stack when NODE_ENV === production.

nodes.label: 401 vs 403
nodes.rationale: 401 = who are you?; 403 = I know who you are and you may not.

nodes.label: HttpError class
nodes.rationale: Thin helper: statusCode, code, message; expose = statusCode < 500. Avoid deep inheritance trees.

nodes.label: Domain-to-HTTP status mapping
nodes.rationale: Carry statusCode on errors you throw. Map domain failures once in error middleware — not with ad-hoc res.status in every catch. 400/422 validation, 401 unauthenticated, 403 forbidden, 404 missing, 409 conflict, 429 rate limit, 503 upstream, 500 bug.

nodes.label: Operational errors
nodes.rationale: Expected at the edge: bad input, not found, 409. Client sees a clear message + code.

nodes.label: Programmer errors
nodes.rationale: Bugs such as Cannot read properties of undefined. Client sees a generic 500. Messages leak paths, schemas, and exploit detail.

nodes.label: 404 as three-arg middleware
nodes.rationale: 404 is normal middleware (3 args) after routes, not error middleware. It always sends 404 when reached. Error middleware mounts after it.

nodes.label: Phase 5 — Error handling
nodes.rationale: One funnel for failures. Express 5 forwards async rejections — you still design the envelope.

nodes.label: Handler-local try/catch for domain mapping
nodes.rationale: Still use try/catch when you convert errors to domain responses inside the handler without wanting the global mapper.

nodes.label: Hide production stacks and 500 messages
nodes.rationale: Stack traces and internal exception messages for unexpected 500s must never appear in production error JSON. Use a generic Internal Server Error when status >= 500 or err.expose === false.

nodes.label: Request-scoped vs process-level errors
nodes.rationale: At the HTTP edge: expose operational, hide programmer, log both. Do not keep the process alive after unknown programmer errors in a bad state. Express error middleware is for request-scoped failures; uncaughtException is Node.

nodes.label: Process crashes are Node topics
nodes.rationale: unhandledRejection / uncaughtException belong to Node Phase 5. Structured logging of errors is Node Phase 10 plus request-id middleware. Request 404/500 envelope stays in Express.

nodes.label: Phase 5 gate — same public envelope
nodes.rationale: Thrown async errors, next(err), and malformed JSON all produce the same public envelope without stack traces when NODE_ENV=production.

nodes.label: Syllabus Phase 0 — How Git stores things
nodes.norm_label: syllabus phase 0 — how git stores things

nodes.label: The commit graph is a DAG
nodes.norm_label: the commit graph is a dag

nodes.label: Never parse porcelain output
nodes.rationale: Porcelain output may change between versions and is affected by aliases and config. Scripts use plumbing or status --porcelain.

nodes.label: Array.prototype.pop
nodes.rationale: Removes the last element; returns it, or undefined if empty. Constant work.

nodes.label: Array.prototype.push
nodes.rationale: Adds at the back; returns the new length, not the array. Cannot be chained.

nodes.label: push(...huge) argument limit
nodes.rationale: Spread turns every element into an argument and can throw RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded. Loop with push, or concat.

nodes.label: Array.prototype.shift
nodes.rationale: Removes the first element and shifts all remaining values left by 1. Work proportional to length.

nodes.label: Array.prototype.unshift
nodes.rationale: Inserts at the front by re-indexing everything. Returns the new length.

nodes.label: Omitted splice deleteCount deletes to the end
nodes.rationale: splice(2) truncates from index 2. splice(2,0) inserts without removing. Most damaging splice mistake.
nodes.norm_label: omitted splice deletecount deletes to the end

nodes.label: Array.prototype.splice
nodes.rationale: Removes, inserts, and replaces in place. Returns the removed elements as an array, not the modified array.

nodes.label: indexOf + splice(-1) trap
nodes.rationale: indexOf miss is -1; splice(-1,1) removes the last element. Guard with i !== -1, or use filter.

nodes.label: Array.prototype.toSpliced
nodes.rationale: Non-mutating counterpart: same arguments, returns the new array. Produces a dense array; splice preserves sparseness.

nodes.label: Adding and removing array elements
nodes.rationale: Adders return a length; removers return an element. The front is fundamentally more expensive. splice with missing deleteCount throws away the tail.

nodes.label: Non-mutating add/remove equivalents
nodes.rationale: push → [...arr,x]; unshift → [x,...arr]; pop → slice(0,-1); shift → slice(1). Default unless the array is local. Identity change is what React detects.

nodes.label: O(n²) queue via shift in a loop
nodes.rationale: n shifts each re-index the remaining array. Fix: index cursor, or reverse once and pop. Specified algorithm, not a measured multiplier.
nodes.norm_label: o(n2) queue via shift in a loop

nodes.label: Never splice inside a forward loop
nodes.rationale: Removing at i shifts later elements down, so i++ skips the next. Iterate backwards, or filter (the default).
nodes.norm_label: never splice inside a forward loop

nodes.label: Mongoose autoIndex
nodes.rationale: Defaults true; every instance of every deploy issues createIndex. Turn off in production; create indexes in a migration.

nodes.label: Mongoose .lean()
nodes.rationale: Plain objects instead of hydrated documents. 5001 docs: 136 ms hydrated vs 57 ms lean. Lose save, virtuals, getters.

nodes.label: MongoDB from Node
nodes.rationale: The official driver is not a thin wrapper around Mongoose — it is the other way round.

nodes.label: Transactions from Node
nodes.rationale: A transaction lives on one connection. Every statement must go through that connection, and nothing else may.

nodes.label: Mongoose schemas, models, middleware
nodes.rationale: Mongoose adds the schema MongoDB does not have. Every convenience has an edge where it does something you did not ask for.

nodes.label: node:sqlite
nodes.rationale: Node ships SQLite 3.53.3. Zero-setup SQL for learning, tests, and local tools — not a networked PostgreSQL replacement.

nodes.label: Phase 6 — Data access
nodes.rationale: Node-side data access only: pooling, parameterization, transactions, N+1, cursors. Planners and MVCC belong to the database sections.

nodes.label: Indexes belong in migrations
nodes.rationale: createIndex at boot in every pod triggers expensive index builds N times during deploy.

nodes.label: An ORM is not a repository
nodes.rationale: A Prisma client in business logic leaks call shapes and error classes just like pool.query leaks rows.
nodes.norm_label: an orm is not a repository

nodes.label: Atomicity and aborted transactions
nodes.rationale: A failed statement aborts the whole transaction. Later commands return 25P02. COMMIT on an aborted transaction is executed as ROLLBACK.

nodes.label: Durability and WAL flush
nodes.rationale: COMMIT does not return until the WAL record is flushed. 112 bytes for one UPDATE. Batching 500 inserts in one transaction (128 ms) beat turning synchronous_commit off (170 ms).

nodes.label: Default isolation READ COMMITTED
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL's default trades isolation for concurrency; the anomalies it allows are the source of most real transaction bugs.

nodes.label: synchronous_commit
nodes.rationale: Off buys 6× write throughput (1042 ms → 170 ms) for a window of lost recent commits. Not corruption — lost commits. Check commit frequency first.

nodes.label: No nested transactions
nodes.rationale: ORMs implement nesting as SAVEPOINT. An inner commit is RELEASE; the outer rollback still discards it.

nodes.label: SAVEPOINT
nodes.rationale: The only way to survive a statement error inside a transaction. Must be taken before the risky statement. Prefer ON CONFLICT when a single statement can express recovery.

nodes.label: Savepoint subtransaction XIDs
nodes.rationale: Each writing savepoint burns a real xid. 2000 inserts 2.3× slower wrapped in SAVEPOINT/RELEASE (599.8 ms → 1362.5 ms). Past 64 subxids the cache overflows and other sessions hit SubtransSLRU.

nodes.label: XID consumption rate
nodes.rationale: One xid per write statement in autocommit (201 for 200 UPDATEs). SELECTs burn zero. Batching 100 writes costs one id. 10000 tx/s exhausts 2^31 in under three days without freezing.

nodes.label: READ COMMITTED and the anomalies it allows
nodes.norm_label: read committed and the anomalies it allows

nodes.label: INNER JOIN matching pairs
nodes.rationale: Output is pairs that satisfy ON. Unmatched left rows vanish; N matches repeat the left row N times. Dee gone, Ann twice.

nodes.label: count(DISTINCT) rescues counts only
nodes.rationale: sum(DISTINCT o.total) collapses different orders that share a total. DISTINCT on the query removes rows, not contributions.

nodes.label: Join fan-out
nodes.rationale: Duplicated parent rows make sum(o.total) 450 against a true 350. The join changes grain; the aggregate is then applied at the wrong grain.

nodes.label: Result grain
nodes.rationale: A join sets grain to the finest side. Aggregates are correct only on columns at that grain.

nodes.label: Pre-aggregate the child then join
nodes.rationale: Reduce the child to one row per parent before joining so no multiplication happens.

nodes.label: LEFT JOIN at-least-once guarantee
nodes.rationale: Every left row appears at least once, not exactly once. Fan-out still applies. Unmatched left rows are NULL-extended.

nodes.label: Fan-out compounds across independent branches
nodes.rationale: 2 tags × 3 comments = 6 rows. Pre-aggregate each child. Diagnose with count(*) vs count(DISTINCT parent.id).

nodes.label: array_agg FILTER plus coalesce
nodes.rationale: FILTER drops the manufactured NULL row; coalesce turns empty-group NULL into {}. They fix two different NULLs.

nodes.label: RIGHT JOIN is LEFT JOIN with operands swapped
nodes.rationale: Prefer LEFT so the preserved table is read first. RIGHT earns its keep when FROM order is not yours to choose.
nodes.norm_label: right join is left join with operands swapped

nodes.label: LATERAL correlated FROM subquery
nodes.rationale: Lets a FROM subquery see tables to its left and run once per driving row, returning many columns and many rows.

nodes.label: LEFT JOIN LATERAL ON true
nodes.rationale: CROSS JOIN LATERAL drops empty driving rows. ON true is required syntax; matching already happened in the subquery WHERE.

nodes.label: LATERAL top-N per group
nodes.rationale: With a real dimension table and an index, 9.3 ms vs 51.8 ms for row_number() on 200k rows — 5.6×. Probe ~1500 rows instead of numbering all 200000.

nodes.label: Migration file checksum
nodes.rationale: Never edit a shipped file. Hash comparison fails the deploy when two environments share a version and differ in schema.

nodes.label: Lexical migration filename order
nodes.rationale: Unpadded sort is 1, 10, 11, 2. Surfaces as 42P01 on a fresh database. Zero-pad or UTC timestamps.

nodes.label: schema_migrations tracking table
nodes.rationale: version PRIMARY KEY, applied_at, checksum. The database records its own version. Second run applies nothing.

nodes.label: INVALID leftover CONCURRENTLY index
nodes.rationale: A failed CONCURRENTLY build is not rolled back. Planner ignores it; writes still maintain it. Find via pg_index WHERE NOT indisvalid.

nodes.label: migrate no-transaction directive
nodes.rationale: Per-file opt-out so CONCURRENTLY can run unwrapped. Honest shape: most DDL should be atomic; non-blocking statements cannot be.

nodes.label: Statements that cannot run in a transaction
nodes.rationale: CREATE/DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY, VACUUM, CREATE/DROP DATABASE fail with 25001 inside BEGIN.
nodes.norm_label: statements that cannot run in a transaction

nodes.label: Minimal migration runner
nodes.rationale: About sixty lines: tracking table, one client, advisory lock after BEGIN, lexical sort, checksum, apply plus record in one transaction.

nodes.label: Baselining an existing database
nodes.rationale: Dump schema as one initial migration and mark it applied without running. History before the baseline is no longer replayable.

nodes.label: drizzle-kit
nodes.rationale: TypeScript schema objects; SQL generated by diff. Same write-vs-derive split as Prisma.

nodes.label: graphile-migrate
nodes.rationale: One idempotent current.sql re-run on every save, then committed as a numbered file. Fits functions, triggers, views, RLS; poor for incremental ALTER TABLE.

nodes.label: Migration tools
nodes.rationale: Every tool implements a tracking table. Choose on workflow assumption: you write SQL, or the tool derives it.

nodes.label: node-pg-migrate
nodes.rationale: SQL or JS files, you own the schema. Natural next step from the hand-written runner for raw SQL and pg.

nodes.label: Prisma Migrate
nodes.rationale: schema.prisma is source of truth; migrations are generated by diff. Do not use without Prisma Client.

nodes.label: Batch vs per-file migration transaction
nodes.rationale: Batch is all-or-nothing and simpler. Per-file resumes, releases locks, and is the only way to opt a CONCURRENTLY file out. Tools default to per-file.

nodes.label: Where sixty lines stops being enough
nodes.rationale: Switch at CONCURRENTLY opt-out, timestamped generator, dry-run/status, baselining, down migrations, or JS backfills.
nodes.norm_label: where sixty lines stops being enough

nodes.label: Write SQL vs derive migrations
nodes.rationale: Writing SQL keeps CONCURRENTLY, exclusion constraints, triggers. Derived tools type for free but escape-hatch anything the schema language cannot express.

nodes.label: Fiber
nodes.rationale: Replaces the call stack with a linked list React owns so rendering can pause, resume, or be abandoned.

nodes.label: StrictMode
nodes.rationale: Development-only detector: double-invokes components and double-mounts effects so impurity fails immediately.

nodes.label: Vite SPA starter
nodes.rationale: Default for this bible's MERN/PERN stack: Express already owns the API, so a second React server is extra deployment cost.

nodes.label: React Compiler
nodes.rationale: Build-step automatic memoization via a per-fiber cache array; stable at babel-plugin-react-compiler 1.0.0.

nodes.label: Profiler API
nodes.rationale: actualDuration vs baseDuration is the memoization signal; onRender is compiled out of production.

nodes.label: Part 3 — Concurrent React and the server
nodes.norm_label: part 3 — concurrent react and the server

nodes.label: Render must be pure
nodes.rationale: Render can run repeatedly and be discarded, so observable work in the body is a bug.

nodes.label: Reconciliation two rules
nodes.rationale: Different types produce different trees; key identifies a child across renders. Comparison unit is (position, type, key).

nodes.label: Type change remounts the subtree
nodes.rationale: Changing a parent div to span, wrapping in a new depth, or defining a component inside another all destroy state.

nodes.label: Fiber double buffering
nodes.rationale: current and work-in-progress trees point at each other through alternate; the DOM pointer is not retargeted each render.

nodes.label: Hook state lives on the fiber
nodes.rationale: A function component has no instance; hooks are a linked list keyed by call order.
nodes.norm_label: hook state lives on the fiber

nodes.label: Framework vs Vite SPA
nodes.rationale: Choose a framework when pages must be indexable, first paint matters, or you specifically want Server Components.

nodes.label: Compiler is not a linter
nodes.rationale: It compiled a component that mutates a prop; eslint-plugin-react-hooks owns Rules of React validation.

nodes.label: useState initial value is read once
nodes.norm_label: usestate initial value is read once

nodes.label: Phase 3 — State and the render cycle
nodes.norm_label: phase 3 — state and the render cycle

nodes.label: State belongs to a tree position
nodes.norm_label: state belongs to a tree position

nodes.label: Lift per-row UI state to the list
nodes.norm_label: lift per-row ui state to the list

nodes.label: Same type and position keep state
nodes.norm_label: same type and position keep state

nodes.label: max_connections
nodes.rationale: Server-wide cap on concurrent backends. Every app, admin session, and tool shares that budget (sandbox default 100).

nodes.label: Node connection pool
nodes.rationale: One global Pool at module scope reuses backends. pool.query borrows a client; it does not fork a new process per query.

nodes.label: Process-per-connection backend
nodes.rationale: Each client connection is a dedicated OS backend that holds session state and can crash without taking down other clients.

nodes.label: Cluster database schema table
nodes.rationale: You connect to a database. Schemas are folders of names inside one database, not separate databases.

nodes.label: search_path
nodes.rationale: Default is "$user", public. Unqualified names resolve in that order. Schema is session state, changeable with SET search_path.

nodes.label: Background workers
nodes.rationale: WAL writer, checkpointer, background writer, autovacuum launcher, I/O workers, logical replication launcher — labeled in pg_stat_activity.backend_type.

nodes.label: Client backend
nodes.rationale: The process that runs SQL for one connection. Client backends scale with connections.

nodes.label: Postmaster
nodes.rationale: Supervisor that accepts connections and starts backends. Managed by the service or container; do not kill random postgres PIDs.

nodes.label: OS page cache
nodes.rationale: Kernel caches file pages the server read or wrote. A shared_buffers miss may still be fast if the OS cache is warm.

nodes.label: shared_buffers
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL's shared 8 KB page cache used by all backends. Alpine default measured at 128MB; production is tuned higher.

nodes.label: CREATE DATABASE copies a template
nodes.rationale: Requires superuser or CREATEDB. App runtime roles must not. Day-to-day apps connect and migrate; CREATE DATABASE is provisioning.

nodes.label: template0
nodes.rationale: Pristine factory image. datallowconn is usually false; use only as TEMPLATE template0 when template1 is dirty.

nodes.label: template1
nodes.rationale: Default source for CREATE DATABASE. Custom encodings or extensions installed here appear in every new database.

nodes.label: Engine folklore that no longer holds
nodes.rationale: MySQL 8 is strict by default (CHECK, ONLY_FULL_GROUP_BY). SQLite has transactional DDL. Sequence gaps happen on every engine.
nodes.norm_label: engine folklore that no longer holds

nodes.label: Differences that survive measurement
nodes.rationale: Isolation default, identifier case folding (createdAt → createdat), RETURNING vs UPDATE…LIMIT, BOOLEAN, concurrency ceiling, JS driver types.

nodes.label: MySQL transactional DDL outlier
nodes.rationale: SQLite sides with PostgreSQL on transactional DDL. MySQL cannot roll back CREATE TABLE — the difference that changes a migration plan.

nodes.label: WAL then heap double write
nodes.rationale: Once to WAL immediately for durability; later to heap/index via dirty shared buffers, checkpoints, and the background writer.

nodes.label: wal_level replica
nodes.rationale: Usual default on PostgreSQL 18.4; supports physical replication. Never delete WAL files by hand.

nodes.label: Write-ahead log
nodes.rationale: Every committed change is recorded in WAL before it is treated as durable. COMMIT succeeds only after the needed WAL is flushed.

nodes.label: Database cluster
nodes.rationale: One data directory on disk that may contain many databases. The server process writes WAL and data files for that cluster.

nodes.label: PostgreSQL object-relational server
nodes.rationale: A long-running program that stores data, enforces rules, and answers SQL over a network protocol — not an embedded library, not SQL syntax alone.

nodes.label: Full-text search tsvector
nodes.rationale: Understand-tier: tsvector. Justified only when search is a real requirement — the phase gate.

nodes.label: jsonb operators
nodes.rationale: Master-tier: arrow accessors and containment.

nodes.label: PgBouncer transaction vs session pool
nodes.rationale: External pooler exists because process-per-connection is expensive. Transaction vs session pool is the decision.

nodes.label: Physical backup and PITR
nodes.rationale: WAL archiving plus a base backup. Phase gate: restore a backup once.

nodes.label: Money never in float
nodes.rationale: Master-tier: numeric vs float. Modelling money covers currency, rounding, allocation.

nodes.label: IDENTITY over serial
nodes.rationale: Master-tier primary keys. Phase gate: 1-N and N-N with identity PKs, FKs, and CHECKs without an ORM.

nodes.label: Transactional DDL
nodes.rationale: Wrap migrations in a transaction. PostgreSQL can roll back CREATE TABLE; MySQL cannot.

nodes.label: INSERT RETURNING
nodes.rationale: Ids without a second query. A surviving difference versus engines that lack RETURNING.

nodes.label: OFFSET degrades
nodes.rationale: Master-tier LIMIT/OFFSET. Keyset pagination in Phase 9 is the replacement.

nodes.label: Parameterized queries
nodes.rationale: Never string-build values. Phase gate: INSERT…RETURNING, UPDATE with WHERE, parameterize every user value.

nodes.label: Pool at module scope
nodes.rationale: Master-tier wiring. Phase gate: open a pool, parameterize, map 23505, never leak clients.

nodes.label: Forward-only migrations
nodes.rationale: Migrate forward-only and seed idempotently without runtime DDL in requests. IF NOT EXISTS is not migrations.

nodes.label: Allowlisted dynamic WHERE
nodes.rationale: Param array plus identifier allowlists. Phase gate: list/filter/sort is allowlisted; transactions use try/catch/finally release.

nodes.label: Connection approximates a process
nodes.rationale: Isolation and simpler memory accounting cost RAM and startup per backend. That cost is why PgBouncer exists (Phase 13).

nodes.label: Qualify names in migrations
nodes.rationale: Always write app.users in migrations and multi-schema apps so a path change cannot silently hit another table.

nodes.label: Pooling does not replace shared buffers
nodes.rationale: Pooling reuses backends; shared buffers cache data pages. Different layers. Too-large shared_buffers fights the OS cache.
nodes.norm_label: pooling does not replace shared buffers

nodes.label: App is a guest with a connection
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL owns durable multi-user truth; the Node process stays a client. You pay an external process to run, back up, and upgrade.
nodes.norm_label: app is a guest with a connection

nodes.label: Columns vs jsonb phase gate
nodes.rationale: Move on when you can choose columns vs jsonb and know when FTS or partitioning is justified.

nodes.label: Default type stack
nodes.rationale: Default to bigint + text + timestamptz + numeric for money. Never write = NULL.

nodes.label: Cheap to animate
nodes.rationale: Only transform and opacity are composite-only; width/height/top/margin force layout every frame.

nodes.label: Container queries
nodes.rationale: Most responsive behaviour should need no breakpoint; the component's own width is the correct input.

nodes.label: oklch() and color-mix()
nodes.rationale: Perceptual lightness plus mixing hover/active/disabled from one brand token.

nodes.label: Stacking contexts
nodes.rationale: z-index, opacity<1, transform, filter, will-change, isolation, contain create contexts a child can never escape.

nodes.label: Sass $var vs CSS custom properties
nodes.rationale: $size is compile-time (can drive @media); --size is inherited runtime (can be themed and set from script).

nodes.label: SCSS practically
nodes.rationale: Teach Sass constructs that remain after native CSS took nesting, variables and colour.

nodes.label: @use and @forward
nodes.rationale: Module system that replaced @import: namespacing, as, with, private members.

nodes.label: CSS rendering pipeline
nodes.rationale: style → layout → paint → composite. Every later performance rule is downstream of which stage a property invalidates.

nodes.label: Custom properties as component API
nodes.rationale: Inherited runtime values in the cascade, not compile-time variables. var(--x, fallback) lets consumers override without extra classes.

nodes.label: Flex automatic minimum size
nodes.rationale: A flex item will not shrink below min-content; min-width: 0 is the fix — the most common flexbox bug.

nodes.label: auto-fit + minmax() card grid
nodes.rationale: Responsive card grid with no media query; highest-leverage modern layout idiom.

nodes.label: minmax(0, 1fr) track fix
nodes.rationale: A 1fr track is minmax(auto, 1fr) and will not shrink below min-content. Same problem as flex min-width: 0.

nodes.label: Express boundary rule
nodes.rationale: Concept → Node (or DB / Redis / Docker / Nginx). Middleware + route surface + HTTP contracts → Express.

nodes.label: HTTP API design half
nodes.rationale: Roughly half of this syllabus is HTTP API design that happens to be mounted on Express. Node refused to absorb REST modeling.

nodes.label: Git scope rule
nodes.rationale: If it still applies when you delete every framework from the repo, it is Git's. Stops at the push event.

nodes.label: Do not start Express before Phase 5
nodes.rationale: Express is a thin layer over node:http. Learning it first means learning the abstraction without the thing it abstracts.
nodes.norm_label: do not start express before phase 5

nodes.label: Call stack
nodes.rationale: Execution contexts and the 12 524-frame ceiling. One half of the event loop; queues are the other half.

nodes.label: Engine, runtime, and spec
nodes.rationale: Why document is not JavaScript, and what actually is.

nodes.label: Phase 0 — How JavaScript runs
nodes.rationale: The engine reads the whole file before it runs any of it. Twelve topics from engine/runtime/spec through reading the spec.

nodes.label: Strict mode
nodes.rationale: Six silent failures turned into errors.

nodes.label: The eight types
nodes.rationale: typeof for every value, and the null bug.

nodes.label: == versus ===
nodes.rationale: null >= 0 is true but null > 0 is false — relational and equality coerce null differently.

nodes.label: Numbers are doubles
nodes.rationale: (1.005).toFixed(2) is "1.00", not "1.01". Cart totals should not be stored as 19.99.

nodes.label: Phase 1 — Values, types and coercion
nodes.rationale: Seventeen topics. References vs copies, coercion, and floating point account for a disproportionate share of shipped bugs.

nodes.label: Strings are UTF-16
nodes.rationale: A three-person family emoji has .length 8, spreads to 5, and is 1 grapheme.

nodes.label: Type coercion
nodes.rationale: [] + {} explained once. sort default string comparison and JSON.stringify omissions are coercion in disguise.

nodes.label: Measured versus documentation-validated
nodes.rationale: Phases 0–2 and Phase 3 topics 01–07 are sandbox-measured on Node 24.19.0. Later pages cite MDN and the spec. No run means no console block.

nodes.label: JavaScript explanations
nodes.rationale: 76 of 337 topics written. Phases 0–2 complete; Master tiers in progress through Phase 7. Claimed by session 01ECVvH5.

nodes.label: 300-line cap is a file-size rule
nodes.rationale: A Master topic may run 900–1400 lines across chunks. Write first, then split. Never trim a gotcha to save lines.

nodes.label: Engine reads the whole file before running
nodes.rationale: Why a SyntaxError on line 90 stops line 1, and why hoisting is a consequence rather than a rule.
nodes.norm_label: engine reads the whole file before running

nodes.label: Primitives are copied, objects are shared
nodes.rationale: Why a value changed. Prerequisite for React immutable state updates.
nodes.norm_label: primitives are copied, objects are shared

nodes.label: Arrow callback this fix
nodes.rationale: An arrow has no this, so the inner obj.method() keeps its receiver. Wrong as the method itself at module scope.

nodes.label: bind identity trap
nodes.rationale: bind returns a new function each call, so removeEventListener never matches. Store the bound function once.

nodes.label: Class field arrow
nodes.rationale: Per-instance own property capturing constructor this. Survives detach; cannot be super-called or stubbed on the prototype.

nodes.label: Lost this
nodes.rationale: Implicit binding is a property of the call site. Assigning, destructuring, or passing a method drops the receiver.

nodes.label: thisArg
nodes.rationale: forEach/map/filter/some/every/find/findIndex/flatMap accept a thisArg. reduce and sort do not.

nodes.label: Default this binding
nodes.rationale: Bare fn() is undefined in strict/module/class code and globalThis in sloppy. Module top-level this is undefined.

nodes.label: Explicit this binding
nodes.rationale: call/apply invoke immediately; bind returns a new function with this fixed. A bound function cannot be re-bound.

nodes.label: Four this binding rules
nodes.rationale: this is a hidden first parameter filled by the call site: new, then explicit, then implicit, then default.

nodes.label: Implicit this binding
nodes.rationale: obj.fn() binds this to whatever is left of the last dot. The rest of the chain is irrelevant.

nodes.label: this precedence
nodes.rationale: new beats bind beats call/apply beats implicit beats default. new on a bound function discards bound this but keeps bound arguments.

nodes.label: Derived field initialization order
nodes.rationale: Base: fields at constructor start. Derived: immediately before super() returns. An overridden method called from the parent constructor sees uninitialised fields.

nodes.label: Instance field vs prototype method
nodes.rationale: A field is an own enumerable property per instance. A method is one shared non-enumerable function. Mutable defaults must be fields.

nodes.label: Method shorthand
nodes.rationale: Not equivalent to prop: function(){}. Not constructable, and super works.

nodes.label: Four this fixes
nodes.rationale: Default to wrapping at the call site. Arrow field for always-callback handlers. bind in the constructor for stable identity.

nodes.label: A method is not attached
nodes.rationale: A method is an ordinary function reachable through an object. The binding is created by the dot and does not travel.

nodes.label: Array holes three states
nodes.rationale: Present value, present undefined, and a hole all read as undefined. Only in/Object.hasOwn distinguish them. map/forEach skip holes; spread and for...of visit them as undefined.

nodes.label: Object method shorthand
nodes.rationale: Not equivalent to prop: function(){}. Methods cannot be constructors (TypeError) and only methods have super via a home object. Arrows in literals capture enclosing this, not the object.

nodes.label: this from the call site
nodes.rationale: obj.f() binds this to obj. Finding an inherited method and resolving properties it reads are two lookups that can land at different levels. Methods are not owned by their object.

nodes.label: Array method thisArg
nodes.rationale: forEach/map/filter/some/every/find/findIndex/flatMap take a thisArg. reduce/reduceRight use the second argument as initialValue; sort has none. Arrows work everywhere.

nodes.label: Array splice and toSpliced
nodes.rationale: Remove, insert, replace. Omitted deleteCount deletes to the end — splice(2) on ten elements drops eight. Beats delete (no hole). Never splice in a forward loop. toSpliced is the non-mutating twin.

nodes.label: Array.from
nodes.rationale: Accepts iterables and array-likes; spread accepts only iterables. mapFn second argument. Array.from({length:n}, fn) is never sparse.

nodes.label: Array length writable property
nodes.rationale: One more than the highest index, not a count of present values. Non-enumerable so Object.keys skips it. arr.length=0 truncates in place; arr=[] replaces the binding.

nodes.label: Array.of
nodes.rationale: Exists because Array(3) is holes while Array(1,2,3) is values. Use Array.of whenever argument count is dynamic.

nodes.label: new Array(n) holes
nodes.rationale: Creates holes, not undefined slots, so new Array(5).map(f) does nothing. Never create holes; then the hole-behaviour table stops mattering.

nodes.label: async forEach trap
nodes.rationale: forEach does not await. Async callbacks return discarded promises; MDN's example prints 0 instead of 14.

nodes.label: every on empty array is true
nodes.rationale: Vacuous truth. [].every(x => x.inStock) is true — a validation bug if emptiness should fail.
nodes.norm_label: every on empty array is true

nodes.label: Array iteration method table
nodes.rationale: Same walk, different return and early-stop. forEach returns undefined and cannot break (MDN names for...of). map always same length; filter ≤ length; find/findIndex/some/every stop early.

nodes.label: map(parseInt) radix bug
nodes.rationale: ["1","2","3"].map(parseInt) is [1, NaN, NaN] because the index arrives as radix.

nodes.label: reduce initialValue
nodes.rationale: Omitted: accumulator is element 0, iteration starts at 1, TypeError on an empty array. Always pass an initial value.

nodes.label: Array.prototype.reduce
nodes.rationale: Four-argument callback, no thisArg. Holes skipped; stored undefined is not. Wins for scalar folds, pipe, promise sequencing. MDN has a when-not-to-use section.

nodes.label: Microtask try/catch gap
nodes.rationale: A surrounding try/catch only guards the synchronous act of scheduling. Handle errors inside the callback.

nodes.label: queueMicrotask
nodes.rationale: Runs after the current JS execution context exits but before event handlers, timeouts, or other callbacks. Prefer it over Promise.resolve().then when you only want scheduling: no promise allocation, and exceptions surface as uncaught errors.

nodes.label: Promise
nodes.rationale: An object representing eventual completion or failure. You attach callbacks to the returned object instead of passing them into a function.

nodes.label: Thenable
nodes.rationale: The language asks whether an object has a callable then, not whether it is a native Promise. An unrelated then field gets assimilated.

nodes.label: Executor throws catch cannot see
nodes.rationale: Only a synchronous throw during the executor becomes a rejection. Async throws and throws after resolve() are not converted.

nodes.label: Phase 18 Building the store front end
nodes.rationale: Framework-free on purpose so a later React break is a named solution, not API surface to memorise.
nodes.norm_label: phase 18 building the store front end

nodes.label: Phase 11 Network, storage and data transfer
nodes.norm_label: phase 11 network, storage and data transfer

nodes.label: Batching within one event-loop turn
nodes.rationale: The length===1 check schedules one queueMicrotask flush; later calls in the same turn join the array. Microtasks run after all synchronous code and before rendering, so the batch is complete and nothing paints twice.

nodes.label: Sometimes-async / Releasing Zalgo
nodes.rationale: A function that is synchronous on a cache hit and asynchronous on a miss fires events before the caller can attach a listener. A function should be always-async or never-async, never sometimes.

nodes.label: Promise state is not readable
nodes.rationale: No promise.state or promise.value. A synchronous isSettled() would reintroduce Zalgo.

nodes.label: One-shot promise state machine
nodes.rationale: The transition happens at most once and is irreversible. That is why a promise cannot model a stream of events.

nodes.label: Active LTS
nodes.rationale: Frozen feature set, actively maintained. Node 24 is Active LTS as of August 2026.

nodes.label: Odd/even LTS rule ending
nodes.rationale: From v27 every annual April major becomes LTS in October. Node 26 is the last odd/even line.

nodes.label: Hidden classes
nodes.rationale: Objects with the same properties in the same order share a shape so V8 can cache offsets.

nodes.label: V8 four-tier compilation
nodes.rationale: Ignition → Sparkplug → Maglev → TurboFan. Fast to start, slow to optimise.

nodes.label: Bun
nodes.rationale: JavaScriptCore + Zig. Runtime, package manager, bundler and test runner in one binary.

nodes.label: NODE_OPTIONS
nodes.rationale: --eval, --print, --test, --env-file are forbidden so an inherited env cannot hijack every process.

nodes.label: Choose Node for production apps
nodes.rationale: Ecosystem completeness and operational maturity beat hello-world throughput. Most apps are bound by the database.

nodes.label: Node flags before the script
nodes.rationale: Everything after the filename is process.argv. A misplaced --watch is silently ignored.

nodes.label: Poll blocking vs blocked event loop
nodes.norm_label: poll blocking vs blocked event loop

nodes.label: Return or it is not chained
nodes.norm_label: return or it is not chained

nodes.label: setImmediate always wins inside I/O callbacks
nodes.norm_label: setimmediate always wins inside i/o callbacks

nodes.label: AsyncLocalStorage request context
nodes.rationale: Preserves reqId across await without threading an extra argument. Does not cross worker threads or child processes; not a security boundary.

nodes.label: x-request-id header
nodes.rationale: Accept a well-formed incoming id, mint UUID when missing, echo on the response, forward on egress, persist on job payloads. Validate length and charset.

nodes.label: captureException on handled errors
nodes.rationale: If you only hook uncaughtException, production's most common failures — the ones you already catch — never reach the tracker.

nodes.label: error tracker release
nodes.rationale: Usually git SHA. Without it, 'new in this deploy' is guesswork. Load-bearing field on SDK init.

nodes.label: Sentry issue grouping
nodes.rationale: Groups the same crash across events, tracks first/last seen per release, pages on new issues. Complementary to logs and OTel — not a replacement.

nodes.label: trace sampling
nodes.rationale: 100% traces at scale melt the backend. Head-based ratio for cost, always sample errors/slow requests, tail sampling in the collector after duration is known.

nodes.label: W3C Trace Context
nodes.rationale: traceparent/tracestate is the standardized inter-service join key — the cousin of x-request-id.

nodes.label: pino child logger
nodes.rationale: Bind reqId/orderId once so every subsequent line carries them. One child per request. base holds process-lifetime facts; children hold per-request facts.

nodes.label: pino err serializer
nodes.rationale: log.error({err}, msg) with stdSerializers.err preserves type, message and stack. log.error(err) often serializes as an empty object.

nodes.label: pino-pretty
nodes.rationale: Development only. Production stdout must be one JSON object per line for shippers and aggregators.

nodes.label: pino redact
nodes.rationale: Strips matching keys before write. Defense in depth, not a substitute for not putting secrets on the object.

nodes.label: Foreign Function Interface (FFI)
nodes.rationale: Call C ABI functions in an existing shared library from JS without a dedicated Node addon.

nodes.label: FFI wrong-type undefined behaviour
nodes.rationale: A wrong argument/return declaration is process-level undefined behaviour and can corrupt memory.

nodes.label: vm constructor-chain breakout
nodes.rationale: this.constructor.constructor("return process")() against createContext({}) returned process.version on Node 24.19.0.
