nodes.label: vm.createContext and runInContext
nodes.rationale: createContext freezes an API object; runInContext evaluates a string against it, optionally with timeout.

nodes.label: node:vm
nodes.rationale: Runs a string of JavaScript in a configured V8 context for soft isolation, tests, and REPLs.

nodes.label: WASI preopens
nodes.rationale: Map guest paths to host directories. Overly broad maps (guest / → host root) leak or overwrite data.

nodes.label: uvwasi
nodes.rationale: Node's WASI implementation; process.versions.uvwasi reports 0.0.23 on Node 24.19.0.

nodes.label: WASI
nodes.rationale: Portable system interface for Wasm modules — host-gated files, clocks, and similar — not a full OS.

nodes.label: WebAssembly.instantiate
nodes.rationale: Load .wasm bytes (or streaming variants) plus host imports; no ambient Node APIs inside the module.

nodes.label: WebAssembly in Node
nodes.rationale: Near-native portable compute for a profiled CPU hotspot without rewriting the app as a C++ addon.

nodes.label: worker_threads
nodes.rationale: Real parallelism on another thread. Spawn is expensive; use a pool (piscina). Data is structured-cloned unless transferred.

nodes.label: FFI versus Node-API addon
nodes.rationale: FFI ships JS plus a vendor lib with runtime types; a Node-API addon ships a compiled .node with compile-time safety and better chatty-API performance.

nodes.label: node:vm is not a security sandbox
nodes.rationale: Node documents vm as not a security mechanism. Hostile code reaches the outer realm; untrusted code needs a process or container.
nodes.norm_label: node:vm is not a security sandbox

nodes.label: WASI is not safe because Wasm
nodes.rationale: The host chooses directories and env the guest sees. Misconfigured preopens are data exposure, same as dangerous Wasm imports.
nodes.norm_label: wasi is not safe because wasm

nodes.label: Wasm versus worker_threads versus N-API
nodes.rationale: Workers give threads at JS speed; Wasm gives portable compute; N-API gives full native power and a build matrix.

nodes.label: t.mock auto-restore
nodes.rationale: t.mock restores everything it touched when the test ends; the top-level mock does not and leaks into later tests. Use t.mock unless you have a reason not to, or call mock.restoreAll() in afterEach.

nodes.label: mock.module()
nodes.rationale: Escape hatch for a dependency you cannot inject. Prefer dependency injection: no flag, no import-order rule, no experimental warning.

nodes.label: node:assert/strict
nodes.rationale: Legacy node:assert uses ==; equal(1, '1') and deepEqual({a:1},{a:'1'}) both pass. An assertion that ignores type is worse than none.

nodes.label: node:test
nodes.rationale: No dependency, no transform, no config. A test fails when it throws — that is the whole contract.

nodes.label: Dependency injection
nodes.rationale: Pass the dependency in. Injection needs no flag, no import-order rule, and makes mocking mostly unnecessary.

nodes.label: Jest
nodes.rationale: Native ESM still needs --experimental-vm-modules plus transform: {}. For a new ESM project in 2026 that is hard to justify.

nodes.label: vi.mock hoisting
nodes.rationale: Vitest's transform hoists vi.mock above imports, so it avoids the import-order trap that mock.module has. Bought with a transform step.

nodes.label: Vitest
nodes.rationale: Earns its place for a shared frontend runner, jsdom, or first-class TypeScript — not because it tests Node backends better.

nodes.label: Vitest and Jest — when they earn their place
nodes.norm_label: vitest and jest — when they earn their place

nodes.label: Module mock import-order trap
nodes.rationale: Mock first, then dynamic-import the module under test. A static import resolves bindings before the mock exists; later await import() returns the cached module.

nodes.label: No DI container in Node
nodes.rationale: A function taking an object already is DI. A container adds indirection and a second language. Wire the graph by hand in main.mjs.

nodes.label: ALTER ROLE PASSWORD plaintext in log
nodes.norm_label: alter role password plaintext in log

nodes.label: auto_explain.log_analyze overhead
nodes.rationale: Instruments every statement, not only slow ones; documented extremely negative performance impact.

nodes.label: Parameters in the log, and auto_explain
nodes.rationale: Parameterised queries do not keep values out of the log. auto_explain.log_analyze instruments every statement.
nodes.norm_label: parameters in the log, and auto_explain

nodes.label: What to log
nodes.rationale: Defaults log almost nothing. Turn on duration, lock waits, temp files; never log_statement=all in production.

nodes.label: Parameters leak into the log
nodes.rationale: pg_stat_activity shows $1 but log_statement=all writes DETAIL Parameters; log_parameter_max_length defaults to -1 (full).

nodes.label: What you give up on managed PostgreSQL
nodes.rationale: No superuser, no filesystem, parameter groups, extension allowlist. Application-side problems remain yours.
nodes.norm_label: what you give up on managed postgresql

nodes.label: pg_stat_statements — finding the expensive query
nodes.rationale: The query killing the database is usually a fast one run constantly. Sort by total_exec_time, not mean.

nodes.label: Reading pg_stat_statements
nodes.rationale: Counters are cumulative. Diff snapshots. High stddev_exec_time flags unstable plans.

nodes.label: Application-side work remains yours
nodes.rationale: Managed hosting removes sysadmin work, not missing indexes, long xacts, connection exhaustion, or locking migrations.

nodes.label: total_exec_time vs mean_exec_time
nodes.rationale: A 4 ms lookup run 500000 times costs far more than an 8 s report; slow-query logs never surface the former.

nodes.label: Largest-remainder allocation
nodes.rationale: 100/3 → 33.33×3 = 99.99. Floor each share, then give leftover pennies to largest remainders so parts sum exactly to the whole.

nodes.label: Store FX rate with the transaction
nodes.rationale: fx_rate numeric(18,8) and fx_rate_at timestamptz are part of the record. Converting at query time makes historical reports change.
nodes.norm_label: store fx rate with the transaction

nodes.label: Append-only ledger
nodes.rationale: Immutable signed entries; derive balance with SUM. Mutable balances lose history, corrupt permanently, and contend. Snapshot periodically if reads get slow.

nodes.label: Always declare numeric scale
nodes.rationale: Bare numeric allows 16383 fractional digits so 19.990000001 ≠ 19.99. Totals numeric(14,2); unit prices more scale; rates numeric(18,8).

nodes.label: ISO 4217 minor units
nodes.rationale: Not every currency has two decimals (JPY 0, some 3). Hard-coded ÷100 is wrong by 10× or 100×. Store minor_units per currency.

nodes.label: numeric plus currency column
nodes.rationale: An amount without a currency is incomplete. Composite FK (invoice_id, currency) can force child rows to match the parent currency.

nodes.label: double precision (float8)
nodes.rationale: Fast approximate binary float. 1000×0.01 stored as 9.999999999999831 so WHERE total = 10 finds nothing. Use for measurements, not money.

nodes.label: numeric half-away-from-zero rounding
nodes.rationale: 2.5::numeric(2,0) → 3; float-to-int uses half-to-even → 2. numeric NaN compares equal to itself so it can be indexed.

nodes.label: Integer cents in bigint
nodes.rationale: Exact and as fast as float8 (27.7 ms vs 76.8 ms numeric on 300k sums). Units become implicit; name columns total_cents.

nodes.label: numeric exact decimal
nodes.rationale: Exact software decimal. numeric(12,2) is 12 digits, 2 after the point. Default for money; 1000×0.01 sums to 10.00.

nodes.label: pg returns numeric as a string
nodes.rationale: Converting to JS Number would discard exactness. Do arithmetic in SQL or use a decimal library; never setTypeParser(1700, parseFloat).
nodes.norm_label: pg returns numeric as a string

nodes.label: numeric field overflow 22003
nodes.rationale: Exceeding declared precision errors; extra scale rounds silently.

nodes.label: Round money once at the end
nodes.rationale: Rounding at each step discards information that compounds. Carry full precision, round at the charging boundary, and store both inputs and rounded outputs.
nodes.norm_label: round money once at the end

nodes.label: Never parseFloat numeric from pg
nodes.rationale: numeric arrives as a string on purpose. Compute in SQL or a decimal library; do not override the type parser.

nodes.label: Do not use the money type
nodes.rationale: Locale-dependent via lc_monetary; dump/restore can misinterpret; no currency identity. Docs warn against it for financial records.
nodes.norm_label: do not use the money type

nodes.label: DISTINCT ON ORDER BY rule
nodes.rationale: DISTINCT ON expressions must be the leading ORDER BY expressions (42P10 otherwise). Omitting ORDER BY is legal and returns an arbitrary row per group.

nodes.label: CASE expression
nodes.rationale: First matching WHEN wins. Implicit ELSE NULL if none match. Short form uses = and cannot express IS NULL. Useful for custom ORDER BY.

nodes.label: COALESCE
nodes.rationale: First non-null argument; short-circuits. NULLIF(a,b) returns NULL when equal — x / NULLIF(y,0) avoids 22012.

nodes.label: || vs concat vs concat_ws
nodes.rationale: || propagates null ('x' || NULL is NULL). concat treats null as empty. concat_ws skips null values but a null separator voids the result.

nodes.label: GREATEST/LEAST skip nulls
nodes.rationale: Opposite of most SQL: GREATEST(NULL, 2) is 2. NULL only if every argument is null. Row-wise, not aggregates.

nodes.label: count(*) vs reltuples vs LIMIT n+1
nodes.rationale: Exact count 25.69 ms on 500k; reltuples 0.49 ms. LIMIT n+1 answers 'is there a next page?' for free. Clamp user-supplied limit.
nodes.norm_label: count(*) vs reltuples vs limit n+1

nodes.label: Keyset pagination
nodes.rationale: WHERE id > $1 ORDER BY id LIMIT 20 seeks the index. Same depth: 0.93 ms and 4 buffers vs 105.85 ms and 5045. Loses random access to page N.

nodes.label: LIMIT without ORDER BY
nodes.rationale: No default order. An UPDATE rewrote a tuple at heap end and changed which five rows came back. Only correct when identity of rows does not matter.

nodes.label: OFFSET cost grows with depth
nodes.rationale: OFFSET is produce-then-discard. 500k rows LIMIT 20: 1.22 ms at 0 vs 105.85 ms at 499980; EXPLAIN shows rows=500000 feeding Limit 20. Index cannot skip counting.

nodes.label: OFFSET pages drift under writes
nodes.rationale: An insert between requests shifts later pages; item 16 served twice. A delete hides a row. Keyset uses a value, not a count.

nodes.label: Unique ORDER BY tiebreaker
nodes.rationale: Non-unique sort: paging 100 rows by 5 gave 54 distinct ids and 46 repeats on a static table. ORDER BY grp, id is a total order.

nodes.label: Select-list alias visibility
nodes.rationale: WHERE total > 10 → 42703 because WHERE runs before SELECT. Same alias works in ORDER BY. Repeat the expression or wrap in a subquery/CTE.

nodes.label: Logical query processing order
nodes.rationale: FROM → WHERE → GROUP BY → HAVING → SELECT → DISTINCT → ORDER BY → LIMIT. Aliases are created at SELECT (seventh). Defines semantics, not execution.

nodes.label: WHERE vs HAVING
nodes.rationale: WHERE filters rows before grouping; HAVING filters groups. Aggregates in WHERE → 42803. Non-aggregate filters belong in WHERE to reduce grouping work.

nodes.label: Logical order is not execution order
nodes.rationale: Planner pushes predicates, uses top-N heapsort, reorders joins. 'Most selective WHERE first' has no effect. Use EXPLAIN for performance.
nodes.norm_label: logical order is not execution order

nodes.label: Calendar spine
nodes.rationale: CROSS JOIN generate_series then LEFT JOIN facts with the date filter in ON. count(*) reports 1 on empty days; count(o.id) reports 0.

nodes.label: Comma FROM accidental product
nodes.rationale: FROM a, b with a missing WHERE produced 20 rows from 4×5 with no error. JOIN … ON makes the same omission a syntax error.

nodes.label: CROSS JOIN
nodes.rationale: Every left row pairs with every right row. Deliberate for spines and grids; accidental via comma FROM with no error.

nodes.label: INNER JOIN
nodes.rationale: One row per matching pair, not per left row. Unmatched rows disappear; multiple matches duplicate and inflate sum().

nodes.label: Join row-count rule
nodes.rationale: Dee has no orders and vanishes; Ann has two and duplicates. The fixture is shared across the joins phase.

nodes.label: LATERAL
nodes.rationale: A FROM subquery may reference tables to its left and run once per driving row. Without LATERAL that reference is 42P01.

nodes.label: LEFT JOIN LATERAL … ON true
nodes.rationale: CROSS JOIN LATERAL drops empty driving rows. LEFT JOIN LATERAL requires ON true because matching already happened in WHERE.

nodes.label: LATERAL top-N per group
nodes.rationale: With a real 500-row group table and an index, LATERAL was 9.3 ms vs 51.8 ms for row_number(). Drive from a dimension table.

nodes.label: LEFT JOIN
nodes.rationale: Keeps every left row and NULL-extends the right. A right-table predicate in WHERE turns it back into an INNER JOIN.

nodes.label: ON vs WHERE on outer joins
nodes.rationale: The single most common SQL bug in application code. count(*) and count(o.id) disagree by the unmatched left rows.
nodes.norm_label: on vs where on outer joins

nodes.label: Compounding join fan-out
nodes.rationale: Two independent one-to-many branches multiply: 2 tags × 3 comments = 6 rows. Pre-aggregate each child first.

nodes.label: array_agg FILTER and coalesce
nodes.rationale: FILTER drops the manufactured NULL row; coalesce turns an empty aggregate into {}. They are not interchangeable.

nodes.label: NATURAL JOIN
nodes.rationale: Infers equality on every same-named column. A shared created_at silently cut two rows to one. Do not write it.

nodes.label: JOIN ON
nodes.rationale: Any boolean condition. The only form that works when FK and PK names differ, the normal customer_id = id case.

nodes.label: JOIN USING
nodes.rationale: Equality on identically named columns, merged into one output column. On FULL OUTER JOIN that column is coalesced.

nodes.label: ReactDOM.render removed
nodes.rationale: Gone in 19, not deprecated: TypeError: ReactDOM.render is not a function. Also hydrate, findDOMNode, unmountComponentAtNode.

nodes.label: actualDuration vs baseDuration
nodes.rationale: actual far below base means memoization is working. Measured: 8 ms vs 21 ms after memo settled.

nodes.label: React DevTools
nodes.rationale: Components and Profiler panels. Highlight updates, hide StrictMode logs, filter host elements.

nodes.label: Performance Tracks
nodes.rationale: React 19.2 console.timeStamp marks: 837 in development, 0 in production. Lanes, phases, component names.

nodes.label: Profiler API
nodes.rationale: onRender(id, phase, actualDuration, baseDuration, …). Inert in production unless react-dom/profiling.

nodes.label: Activity
nodes.rationale: Hide a subtree, keep its state, unmount its effects. Pre-render the next screen without showing it.

nodes.label: Document metadata hoisting
nodes.rationale: title, meta and link hoist to head from anywhere in the tree.

nodes.label: React 19 additions
nodes.rationale: use, useActionState, useOptimistic, cache, form resource hints, useFormStatus. ref is an ordinary prop.

nodes.label: React 19.2 additions
nodes.rationale: useEffectEvent, Activity, cacheSignal, captureOwnerStack, Partial Pre-rendering, Performance Tracks.

nodes.label: useActionState
nodes.rationale: State + action + pending. Replaces deprecated useFormState from react-dom.

nodes.label: ViewTransition is experimental-only
nodes.rationale: Not in 19.2.8 latest despite React Labs posts. Also addTransitionType, startGestureTransition, SuspenseList.

nodes.label: ref as a prop
nodes.rationale: React 19 made ref ordinary and retired forwardRef for function components.

nodes.label: useEffectEvent
nodes.rationale: Latest props and state without a dependency. Stable in React 19.2, not experimental.

nodes.label: Automatic batching
nodes.rationale: Everywhere since React 18. Batching decides how many renders; the snapshot decides the value.

nodes.label: Updater functions
nodes.rationale: Required, not stylistic, in three cases; also removes state from an effect's dependency array.

nodes.label: useState
nodes.rationale: State belongs to a position, and React finds it by counting hook calls.

nodes.label: Phase 4 in progress
nodes.rationale: 12 of 18 topics written; topics 13–18 unwritten.

nodes.label: You might not need an effect
nodes.rationale: Twelve cases; only one survives as an effect.
nodes.norm_label: you might not need an effect

nodes.label: Phase 3 — State and the render cycle
nodes.norm_label: phase 3 — state and the render cycle

nodes.label: Derived state
nodes.rationale: The sync-with-an-effect antipattern costs a visible frame.

nodes.label: Props changed is not a re-render trigger
nodes.rationale: Two reasons to re-render — and 'props changed' is not one.
nodes.norm_label: props changed is not a re-render trigger

nodes.label: State is a snapshot
nodes.rationale: Setting state only changes it for the next render.

nodes.label: The dependency array is not a preference
nodes.rationale: Lying produces an effect that reads one render's values forever. To remove a dep you must prove the linter it is not read.
nodes.norm_label: the dependency array is not a preference

nodes.label: Effect timing relative to paint is not guaranteed
nodes.rationale: An interaction-caused effect may run before paint, and React may repaint before processing state set inside an effect.
nodes.norm_label: effect timing relative to paint is not guaranteed

nodes.label: Effects synchronize with external systems
nodes.rationale: Not a lifecycle callback. An effect is caused by rendering, and setup/cleanup are a pair React may run any number of times.

nodes.label: dependencies vs devDependencies vs peerDependencies
nodes.rationale: dependencies ship to consumers; devDependencies are omitted in production; peerDependencies expect the host to provide the package so plugins do not duplicate a framework.

nodes.label: package.json engines
nodes.rationale: Declaration not enforcement unless engine-strict=true. State a floor not a ceiling so future Node majors are not locked out.

nodes.label: package.json files allowlist
nodes.rationale: Without files, npm publishes almost everything. README, LICENSE and package.json always ship; node_modules never does. Verify with npm pack --dry-run.

nodes.label: main vs exports
nodes.rationale: main is the old single entry; exports takes precedence, supports subpaths and conditions, and blocks unlisted deep imports.

nodes.label: node --run
nodes.rationale: Minimal script runner: no pre/post scripts, no .npmrc, faster startup; use npm run when a script needs npm's environment.

nodes.label: postinstall scripts
nodes.rationale: Run automatically on every install of the package — debugging surprise and supply-chain risk. Prefer an explicit user-run script.

nodes.label: package.json scripts
nodes.rationale: Scripts prepend node_modules/.bin to PATH. Avoid pre/post hooks because they run implicitly; postinstall is a supply-chain risk.

nodes.label: package.json type field
nodes.rationale: Most consequential field: decides how every .js file is parsed. Absent type triggers MODULE_TYPELESS_PACKAGE_JSON and a reparse cost. Set explicitly; type is scoped to the nearest package.json.

nodes.label: Corepack
nodes.rationale: Pins package manager version via packageManager field. Ships with Node but must be enabled once per machine.

nodes.label: node_modules hoisting
nodes.rationale: npm and yarn flatten transitive deps into top-level node_modules so duplicates collapse; that is how undeclared imports can accidentally resolve.

nodes.label: phantom dependencies
nodes.rationale: A package your code imports without declaring it because hoisting put it at top-level. Breaks when the real dependent drops it.

nodes.label: pnpm content-addressable store
nodes.rationale: One copy per version in a global store; node_modules is symlinks exposing only declared deps. Undeclared require fails immediately; disk is shared across projects.

nodes.label: npm workspaces
nodes.rationale: One install and one lockfile; local packages are symlinked. Do not give build orchestration. Root needs private:true to block accidental publish.

nodes.label: npm dist-tags
nodes.rationale: Pre-releases need --tag so they do not become latest. Without it every plain npm install gets the beta.

nodes.label: dual CJS/ESM packages
nodes.rationale: ESM-only is the default now that require(esm) works on Node 22.12+/24.15. Shipping both costs the dual-package hazard of two copies of module state.

nodes.label: npm deprecate
nodes.rationale: Realistic recovery from a bad release: deprecate plus a new version. Treat every publish as permanent.

nodes.label: npm pack dry-run
nodes.rationale: Only way to see the tarball contents before publish. Catch secrets going out and needed files staying home. Then install the tgz as a consumer smoke test.

nodes.label: npm version
nodes.rationale: Edits package.json, commits and tags. Refuses a dirty tree. A published version is permanent; unpublish is 72 hours and unused only.

nodes.label: npm publish --provenance
nodes.rationale: CI-only signed attestation linking the tarball to commit and workflow. Meaningful because no human laptop was involved.

nodes.label: scoped package names
nodes.rationale: Scoped packages default to private (paid). Public publish needs --access public or publishConfig.access. Forgetting this is the common first-publish failure.

nodes.label: caret and tilde ranges
nodes.rationale: ^1.2.3 allows <2.0.0; ~1.2.3 allows <1.3.0. ^ is npm default so package.json does not describe what you are running.

nodes.label: lockfile integrity hash
nodes.rationale: Makes install verifiable not just reproducible. A tampered tarball fails even if the version number matches.

nodes.label: npm ci
nodes.rationale: Installs the lockfile exactly, deletes node_modules first, never writes the lockfile, fails if package.json and lock disagree. Use in CI, Docker, production.

nodes.label: package.json overrides
nodes.rationale: Force a nested dependency version when the parent has not updated. You override the parent's declared compatibility — verify it works.

nodes.label: package-lock.json
nodes.rationale: Records exact version, resolved URL and integrity hash for the whole tree. Commit it always including for libraries; consumers ignore it and use their own lockfile.

nodes.label: semantic versioning
nodes.rationale: MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH records maintainer intent, not a guarantee. A patch that fixes a bug your code depended on is still a break. 0.x anything may break; ^0.3.1 allows only 0.3.x.

nodes.label: erasable TypeScript syntax
nodes.rationale: Annotations, interface, type, generics, import type erase cleanly. enum, runtime namespace, parameter properties must generate JS and throw ERR_UNSUPPORTED_TYPESCRIPT_SYNTAX in strip-only mode.

nodes.label: ERR_UNSUPPORTED_NODE_MODULES_TYPE_STRIPPING
nodes.rationale: Node refuses to strip types inside node_modules so published packages must ship JS plus .d.ts. Bounds startup cost.

nodes.label: TypeScript import specifiers
nodes.rationale: Running .ts directly requires importing ./helper.ts. The tsc convention of importing ./helper.js assumes you compile first. Mixing them fails under one of the two commands.

nodes.label: tsc --noEmit
nodes.rationale: Native .ts execution removes the build, not the check. Dropping tsc --noEmit from CI silently switches to decorative annotations.

nodes.label: Node type stripping
nodes.rationale: Default since v23.6.0, Stability 2 as of v24.12.0. Replaces type annotations with whitespace so stack traces stay correct. Never type-checks.

nodes.label: Automatic batching
nodes.rationale: React waits until all code in the event has run before processing state updates, preventing half-finished renders. React 18 made batching apply everywhere, not only in React event handlers.

nodes.label: await is a batch boundary
nodes.rationale: Updates before and after an await live in different tasks, so they batch separately. Automatic batching is not one render per function.

nodes.label: flushSync
nodes.rationale: The only per-callback opt-out of batching. Uncommon last resort: may force Suspense fallbacks, run pending Effects, and flush unrelated pending work.

nodes.label: Half-finished renders
nodes.rationale: Without batching, each update can paint a frame where one related value has changed and another has not. Batching is a correctness feature, not only a performance one.

nodes.label: Queueing a Series of State Updates (react.dev)
nodes.norm_label: queueing a series of state updates (react.dev)

nodes.label: Stale closure
nodes.rationale: A timeout or interval created in one render reports that render's snapshot, even seconds later. Usually correct for the action as started; a bug only when current value is needed.

nodes.label: State is a snapshot
nodes.rationale: Setting state only changes it for the next render. The variable in a given render is a const; handlers close over that invocation.

nodes.label: The update queue
nodes.rationale: Per state variable, React walks queued updates in order. A plain value replaces the running value; an updater transforms it. Each variable has its own queue.

nodes.label: Three cases where updaters are required
nodes.norm_label: three cases where updaters are required

nodes.label: Updater function
nodes.rationale: setX(x => ...) applies a transformation to pending state in the queue, not the render snapshot. Required for multiple updates, later-running callbacks, and concurrent sources.

nodes.label: Numeric enum IIFE
nodes.rationale: enum becomes an IIFE building a two-way map (Status.Pending=0, Status[0]='Pending'). Real object, resists tree-shaking.

nodes.label: Erasable vs non-erasable syntax
nodes.rationale: Erasable syntax describes values that already exist. Non-erasable syntax creates runtime values: enum, runtime namespace, parameter properties, legacy import=, experimental decorators.

nodes.label: Type erasure
nodes.rationale: Most TS syntax is deleted on the way to JS. 15 lines in, 7 out: interface, type, generics, annotations, satisfies, as vanish. Runtime logic is untouched.

nodes.label: export {} module marker
nodes.rationale: Compiler adds export {} so a file with no imports/exports stays a module instead of a script sharing global scope.

nodes.label: Parameter properties emit assignments
nodes.rationale: constructor(private readonly id: string) becomes field declarations plus this.id = id. private and readonly themselves are erased.

nodes.label: private is compile-time only
nodes.rationale: private is erased; JS can read o.id. #private is the runtime-enforced form.

nodes.label: ERR_UNSUPPORTED_TYPESCRIPT_SYNTAX
nodes.rationale: Load-time SyntaxError for enum, namespace, and parameter properties in strip-only mode. The module never evaluates.

nodes.label: --experimental-transform-types
nodes.rationale: Escape hatch that transforms enums. Experimental, warns every start, reintroduces source maps. Rewriting syntax is cheaper.

nodes.label: Strip-only mode
nodes.rationale: Node runs TS by deleting types, never transforming. Syntax that needs a transform is rejected at parse as SyntaxError, not a catchable exception.

nodes.label: Node 24 type stripping
nodes.rationale: node file.ts strips annotations and runs JS with no flag, no tsconfig, no check. Same lying.ts prints HEAVY and exits 0.

nodes.label: enum vs union vs const object
nodes.rationale: Three ways to model a fixed set. Union and const-object erase; enum emits an IIFE. Default: string-literal union.
nodes.norm_label: enum vs union vs const object

nodes.label: Enums are nominal
nodes.rationale: Two enums with identical members are not interchangeable. Unusual in TS; string-literal unions are structural.

nodes.label: String-literal union
nodes.rationale: type Status = 'pending' | 'shipped'. Zero runtime, readable serialisation, no import. Cannot iterate members at runtime.

nodes.label: Erasure is the load-bearing fact
nodes.rationale: Once 'types are deleted and never checked at runtime' is internalised, enum's reputation, erasableSyntaxOnly, runtime validation, and why a green bundler proves nothing stop being separate facts.

nodes.label: Whitespace type stripping
nodes.rationale: Annotations are replaced with whitespace so every character position is preserved and stack traces match without a source map. That forbids generating an IIFE or inserting this.id = id.

nodes.label: Configurable middleware factory
nodes.rationale: A function that accepts options and returns middleware. Every built-in follows it: express.json({limit}), express.static(root, options), express.urlencoded({extended}).

nodes.label: validate(schema) factory
nodes.rationale: Same pattern powers validation middleware: validate(schema) returns (req, res, next) => …

nodes.label: Content-Type parser gate
nodes.rationale: Wrong type means empty body, not a thrown error — usually not an automatic 415. Body is undefined if no body, type unmatched, or an error occurred.

nodes.label: express.json
nodes.rationale: Defaults: limit 100kb, type application/json, strict true, inflate true. Populates req.body only when Content-Type matches.

nodes.label: Parser limit option
nodes.rationale: Default 100kb on json, urlencoded, raw, and text. Treat limit as a production control. Different routes can use different limits.

nodes.label: 415 unsupported type
nodes.rationale: Odd Content-Type values can skip the parser. Reject unsupported types with 415 if the API is strict.

nodes.label: Multer fileSize defaults to Infinity
nodes.rationale: An uncapped upload is the default. Memory storage plus large or many files can OOM.

nodes.label: Multer 2.x
nodes.rationale: Multer latest 2.2.0 as of 2026-08-14. Pin multer@2 for Express 5. Parse multipart, enforce counts/sizes, memory vs disk.

nodes.label: Object storage for uploads
nodes.rationale: Large files belong in S3-compatible object storage, not the API container writable layer. Cleanup temp paths on failure.

nodes.label: Phase 3 gate
nodes.rationale: Mount JSON parsing with a hard size limit, handle a huge body without hanging, and receive multipart without trusting Content-Type alone.

nodes.label: No module-level middleware options
nodes.rationale: Module-level let options lets tests and concurrent apps clobber each other. Closure over options makes each instance independent.

nodes.label: Per-route body parsers
nodes.rationale: Global express.json() is simple. Per-route parsers avoid parsing huge bodies on routes that never need them.

nodes.label: First matching parser consumes the stream
nodes.rationale: Global JSON before a route-level raw webhook handler leaves an empty or wrong body. Mount raw on /webhooks/* before global JSON.
nodes.norm_label: first matching parser consumes the stream

nodes.label: Never global multer
nodes.rationale: Multer README: never add multer as a global middleware since a malicious user could upload files to a route you did not anticipate.

nodes.label: Untrusted upload originalname and mimetype
nodes.rationale: Multer README has no explicit warning; this bible's advice. Clients lie. Generate your own object keys. Prefer file-signature checks.

nodes.label: Module request waterfall
nodes.rationale: The graph is discovered one level at a time. modulepreload or bundling flattens it; this is why bundlers remain standard despite native ESM.

nodes.label: nomodule two-bundle pattern
nodes.rationale: Module-aware browsers ignore nomodule; older ones ignore type=module. Exactly one of the pair runs. Mostly historical in 2026.

nodes.label: script async
nodes.rationale: Runs the moment it arrives; no order between async scripts. Only for independent third-party code.

nodes.label: script defer
nodes.rationale: Downloads in parallel, runs after HTML is parsed, in document order. Safe default for classic scripts; DOM is complete so no DOMContentLoaded wrapper is needed.

nodes.label: script type=module
nodes.rationale: Deferred automatically and strict; the whole import graph must be fetched and parsed before execute, so deferral is a consequence of modules.

nodes.label: browserslist
nodes.rationale: Single control for Babel and bundlers. Stale IE11 targets force ES5 plus a large core-js for everyone.

nodes.label: Polyfill
nodes.rationale: Adds a missing API at runtime. A missing method fails at call time on one interaction. Patches the global.

nodes.label: Transpiler
nodes.rationale: Rewrites syntax at build time so an older parser can read it. Syntax fails at parse time and takes the whole file down.

nodes.label: useBuiltIns usage
nodes.rationale: Babel injects only the core-js polyfills the source actually references for the browserslist targets. entry pulls a fixed block.

nodes.label: localStorage write probe
nodes.rationale: Safari private mode defines localStorage then throws QuotaExceededError on every write. Existence is not usability.

nodes.label: navigator exists in Node 21+
nodes.rationale: typeof navigator !== 'undefined' is true on Node 21+, so SSR hydrates as if it were a browser. Probe document or the specific API.

nodes.label: User-agent sniffing
nodes.rationale: The UA string is a compatibility fiction. Acceptable only for a documented engine bug with a removal condition, store links, or analytics.

nodes.label: Phase 0 How JavaScript runs
nodes.rationale: The engine reads the whole file before it runs any of it; hoisting and SyntaxError-on-line-90 follow from that.

nodes.label: Feature detection
nodes.rationale: Test the capability, never the browser or environment. Use typeof so an undeclared name does not throw.

nodes.label: Progressive enhancement
nodes.rationale: Ship a version that works everywhere, then add capability-gated improvements. A Load more button beats a dead page.

nodes.label: base64 vs base64url
nodes.rationale: base64url swaps +/ for -_ and drops = padding for JWTs and URL-safe tokens. Node accepts both alphabets; other languages do not.

nodes.label: Buffer encodings
nodes.rationale: An encoding is the rule for turning bytes into text and back. Wrong choice yields mojibake, silent truncation, or a size limit off by 33% — nothing throws.

nodes.label: Invalid UTF-8 becomes U+FFFD
nodes.rationale: Buffer.toString('utf8') substitutes the replacement character and does not throw, so corruption travels into storage.

nodes.label: TextDecoder fatal true
nodes.rationale: Only built-in way to make bad bytes loud: throws TypeError on malformed UTF-8. Use at trust boundaries.

nodes.label: utf8 encoding
nodes.rationale: Default and lossless for all text. 1–4 bytes per character. There is no case where ascii beats utf8.

nodes.label: Per-chunk toString corruption
nodes.rationale: Chunk boundaries fall on bytes, not characters. Decoding each half independently substitutes U+FFFD and the character is lost irreversibly.

nodes.label: DataView endianness API
nodes.rationale: Same ground with per-call littleEndian. Portable to the browser. Use in shared code; Buffer named methods in Node-only parsers.

nodes.label: Endianness
nodes.rationale: BE stores the most significant byte first (network byte order). LE stores the least first. Wrong order yields a valid but wrong number with no error.

nodes.label: Length-prefixed framing
nodes.rationale: Fixed header of type plus payload length, then payload. Buffer remainder on incomplete frames. Validate attacker-controlled length before allocating.

nodes.label: readBigInt64 / readBigUInt64
nodes.rationale: A JS number holds integers exactly only to 2^53−1. Database IDs and Snowflake IDs must stay BigInt.

nodes.label: Buffer typed read and write
nodes.rationale: Uniform family: read/write + type + BE/LE. Named methods throw ERR_BUFFER_OUT_OF_BOUNDS or ERR_OUT_OF_RANGE; index assign wraps modulo 256.

nodes.label: Base64 decode is not validation
nodes.rationale: Node's decoder ignores characters outside the alphabet and tolerates missing padding, so garbage still decodes.

nodes.label: Base64 +33% size cost
nodes.rationale: 3 bytes become 4 ASCII chars. Acceptable for tokens and data URIs; wrong for file payloads — use multipart or raw binary.

nodes.label: latin1 vs ascii
nodes.rationale: latin1 maps every byte 0–255 to the same code point and round-trips bytes. ascii masks the high bit and silently destroys bytes above 127.

nodes.label: Index assign skips validation
nodes.rationale: buf[i] = 256 stores 0 with no throw. writeUInt8 throws ERR_OUT_OF_RANGE, which a parser wants on a malformed frame.

nodes.label: Buffer.alloc
nodes.rationale: Zero-fills and never uses the pool. Default for anything holding user data, secrets, or crossing a response boundary.

nodes.label: Buffer.allocUnsafe
nodes.rationale: Returns recently freed process memory unzeroed — about 20× faster. Must overwrite every byte before anything reads it.

nodes.label: Buffer.allocUnsafeSlow
nodes.rationale: Skips the pool: own exactly-sized ArrayBuffer, byteOffset 0. Still uninitialized; safe to retain long-term.

nodes.label: Buffer pool
nodes.rationale: 64 KB slab (Buffer.poolSize 65536 in Node 24). allocUnsafe below half the pool is carved from the slab. buf.buffer is the whole shared slab.

nodes.label: new Buffer deprecated DEP0005
nodes.rationale: A numeric argument dispatched to allocUnsafe, so new Buffer(req.body.size) was a remote memory disclosure. Split into Buffer.from and Buffer.alloc.

nodes.label: Buffer extends Uint8Array
nodes.rationale: Same memory model plus encoding methods, numeric read/write, and the pool. Why crypto.subtle, fetch, TextDecoder and Web Streams accept a Buffer.

nodes.label: Buffer.from copy vs view overloads
nodes.rationale: Buffer.from(typedArray) and Buffer.from(buffer) copy. Buffer.from(arrayBuffer[, offset, length]) creates a view.

nodes.label: Buffer.slice shares memory
nodes.rationale: Buffer.prototype.slice returns a view; Uint8Array.prototype.slice copies. Use subarray for a view and Buffer.from for a copy.

nodes.label: fetch Response.body
nodes.rationale: A ReadableStream. pipeline(Readable.fromWeb(res.body), createWriteStream) streams a download; res.arrayBuffer buffers the whole file.

nodes.label: Web stream locking and tee
nodes.rationale: Exactly one reader; getReader/for await/pipeTo lock. res.json() then res.text() fails. tee/clone buffers the slower branch.

nodes.label: Readable.toWeb and fromWeb
nodes.rationale: Convert at the boundary. Node chunks are Buffers; web chunks are Uint8Array. Each conversion adds a queue — convert once.

nodes.label: Web Streams
nodes.rationale: WHATWG ReadableStream, WritableStream, TransformStream. Globals in Node since v18. fetch bodies are web streams.

nodes.label: allocUnsafe memory disclosure
nodes.rationale: After 5000 fake request bodies, 44% of subsequent 80-byte allocUnsafe calls contained the password. Mechanism behind CVE-2016-2216-class bugs.

nodes.label: Prefer Uint8Array outside Node
nodes.rationale: Buffer is a Node global. Shared browser/Worker/Deno code should use Uint8Array plus TextEncoder/TextDecoder.

nodes.label: Default to Node streams in Node
nodes.rationale: Node streams have pipeline, object mode and every Node API. Use web streams for edge/browser or when you never leave fetch/Response.
nodes.norm_label: default to node streams in node

nodes.label: Duplex stream
nodes.rationale: Independent read and write halves, e.g. net.Socket. end() sends FIN on write only; stream.finished waits for both.

nodes.label: PassThrough
nodes.rationale: Transform that changes nothing. Used to tap a pipeline, expose a stream before its source exists, or fan out.

nodes.label: Transform stream
nodes.rationale: Duplex where output derives from input. Transform is a Duplex is a Readable, so it can sit anywhere in a pipeline.

nodes.label: Late data handler data-loss window
nodes.rationale: Once flowing, chunks emitted before a handler attaches are gone. One tick after resume received 0 of 3 chunks.

nodes.label: Flowing vs paused mode
nodes.rationale: readableFlowing is null (no consumer), true (pushing via data), or false (paused after flowing). on('data'), pipe, resume switch to flowing.

nodes.label: readable event plus read n
nodes.rationale: Explicit pull API. read(n) returns exactly n bytes or null — the one thing for await cannot do. Do not mix with data.

nodes.label: Transform chunk boundary problem
nodes.rationale: A per-chunk regex misses a token that straddles two chunks. A tok_live_ secret split across chunks was not redacted.

nodes.label: _transform and _flush
nodes.rationale: _transform handles each chunk and emits zero or more outputs. _flush runs after input ends and emits buffered state such as a trailing partial line.

nodes.label: decodeStrings
nodes.rationale: Default true converts written strings to Buffers before _transform. decodeStrings: false passes the original string through.

nodes.label: Transform streams topic
nodes.rationale: Reusable middle of a pipeline. Two methods — _transform and _flush — and the difficulty is that chunk boundaries do not respect data structure.

nodes.label: objectMode
nodes.rationale: Carries arbitrary JS values. High water mark counts items (default 16) not bytes (65536). Writing an object to a byte stream throws ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE synchronously.

nodes.label: One-sided object mode
nodes.rationale: readableObjectMode is bytes in, records out (parser). writableObjectMode is records in, bytes out (serialiser).

nodes.label: push null is end of stream
nodes.rationale: push(null) terminates in every mode. A legitimate null value must be wrapped. undefined is likewise unusable.
nodes.norm_label: push null is end of stream

nodes.label: stream.compose
nodes.rationale: Glues stages into one Duplex so a multi-stage pipeline ships as one value. Stability 1 Experimental. Always consume through pipeline.

nodes.label: Object-mode memory is unmeasured
nodes.rationale: Sixteen 10 MB documents is 160 MB. No coalescing: each object is a separate _write. Lower the mark or batch with _writev.

nodes.label: alg none and HS256-as-RS256
nodes.rationale: A library that trusts the header skips verification for alg:none, or uses the public key as an HMAC secret. Always pass an explicit algorithms allowlist.

nodes.label: Asymmetric JWT signing
nodes.rationale: RS256/EdDSA so verifiers hold only a public key. With HS256 every service holds the signing secret and is a forgery risk.

nodes.label: Short access JWT plus opaque refresh
nodes.rationale: 5–15 minute access JWT plus revocable refresh in an HttpOnly cookie. Accept a revocation window equal to the access lifetime — a deliberate trade.
nodes.norm_label: short access jwt plus opaque refresh

nodes.label: JWT
nodes.rationale: Signed claims, readable by anyone holding the token. No storage to validate. Roles bake in at issue time. Pin algorithms; check iss and aud.

nodes.label: Opaque server-side session
nodes.rationale: Random id in an HttpOnly cookie; server holds the truth. Default for a single browser app. Instant revocation, ~32 bytes on the wire.

nodes.label: HttpOnly cookie credential
nodes.rationale: JavaScript cannot read it. XSS can still act as the user on that page but cannot exfiltrate a portable credential. Flags: httpOnly, secure, sameSite; leave domain unset.

nodes.label: In-memory SPA access token
nodes.rationale: Short-lived JWT in memory; refresh in an HttpOnly cookie scoped to /auth/refresh. Persisting the access token for convenience undoes the design.

nodes.label: localStorage token
nodes.rationale: Readable by any script on the page, including a compromised dependency. sessionStorage is equally readable. Stolen JWTs often cannot be revoked.

nodes.label: Content-Type and nosniff
nodes.rationale: Node sets no Content-Type. The browser sniffs and may parse JSON as HTML. Set the type plus X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff.

nodes.label: Allowlist HTML sanitiser
nodes.rationale: Do not write the sanitiser. Allowlist tags and attributes; sanitise on output as well as storage so a library update improves stored content.

nodes.label: javascript: URL in href
nodes.rationale: JSX escapes interpolation but treats javascript:alert(1) as a valid attribute. Validate scheme against http/https. dangerouslySetInnerHTML is the other hole.

nodes.label: JSON.stringify inside a script tag
nodes.rationale: </script> inside the JSON string terminates the block. Replace < with \u003c; also escape U+2028/U+2029. Or use type=application/json.

nodes.label: idle in transaction
nodes.rationale: BEGIN then silence. wait_event=ClientRead: the server waits on the client. Holds a pool slot, locks, and possibly the horizon until COMMIT/ROLLBACK.

nodes.label: pg pool error event on backend kill
nodes.rationale: Timeouts kill the backend. pg emits an error event, not a rejected promise. Unhandled, it crashes Node. pool.on('error') is mandatory; release(true) to destroy the client.
nodes.norm_label: pg pool error event on backend kill

nodes.label: Leaked transaction costs a pool slot
nodes.norm_label: leaked transaction costs a pool slot

nodes.label: transaction_timeout 25P04
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL 17+. Kills any transaction older than N, busy or idle. Covers the always-active case the idle timeout misses.

nodes.label: Phase 11 gate: prevent lost updates and idle-in-transaction
nodes.norm_label: phase 11 gate: prevent lost updates and idle-in-transaction

nodes.label: The lost update, and four ways to stop it
nodes.norm_label: the lost update, and four ways to stop it

nodes.label: Long-running transactions and the xmin horizon
nodes.norm_label: long-running transactions and the xmin horizon

nodes.label: statement_timeout does not kill idle transactions
nodes.rationale: A session idle 600 ms with statement_timeout=200ms was still alive. No statement is running.
nodes.norm_label: statement_timeout does not kill idle transactions

nodes.label: Window functions forbidden in HAVING
nodes.rationale: 42P20: windows run after HAVING so the value does not exist yet. Compute the window in a subquery and filter outside. rank() OVER (ORDER BY count(*) DESC) is legal because windows run after grouping.

nodes.label: first_value
nodes.rationale: Frame-relative start of the window. Default frame makes it the partition first row. first_value OVER (ORDER BY x DESC) is the preferred last-value spelling — no frame reasoning.

nodes.label: last_value default frame trap
nodes.rationale: ORDER BY implies RANGE BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW, so last_value is the current row. first_value looks correct by accident because the frame starts at UNBOUNDED PRECEDING. Fix: full ROWS frame, or first_value over reversed ORDER BY.

nodes.label: nth_value
nodes.rationale: 1-based, frame-relative. With the default frame, nth_value(x, 2) is NULL on the first row of each partition. No negative form — reverse the ordering. Named windows cannot override ORDER BY.

nodes.label: generate_series date spine for lag
nodes.rationale: lag counts rows, not days. Missing days make day-over-day skip the gap silently. Generate a dense spine and LEFT JOIN; use count(o.id) not count(*) or empty days report 1.

nodes.label: lag
nodes.rationale: Value n rows back (default 1), optional default when the offset falls outside the partition. Frame-independent. Never crosses PARTITION BY. ORDER BY is optional in syntax and always a bug without it. Non-constant offset is accepted and can yield an all-NULL column.

nodes.label: lead
nodes.rationale: Value n rows forward. Same offset/default/partition/ORDER BY rules as lag. First row has no predecessor and last has no successor — both NULL unless a default is supplied.

nodes.label: Hypothetical-set aggregates
nodes.rationale: rank/dense_rank/percent_rank/cume_dist WITHIN GROUP rank a value that is not in the set. Arguments must match ORDER BY columns. Inverse of percentile_cont: value→fraction vs fraction→value. rank(150) measured 66721 / 0.1334.

nodes.label: mode()
nodes.rationale: On a tie, returns the first value in the WITHIN GROUP sort order with no indication of the tie. Four kinds tied at 125000; reversing ORDER BY changed click to view. Ignores NULLs; empty input is NULL.

nodes.label: percentile_cont
nodes.rationale: Interpolates; can return a value not in the data (2.5 from 1,2,3,4). numeric/interval only. Must sort: 178.32 ms vs 57.41 ms for avg on 500k (3.1×). Percentiles do not compose — cannot average hourly p95s.

nodes.label: percentile_disc
nodes.rationale: Returns an actual value from the set. Works on any sortable type. percentile_disc(0.0) is min, percentile_disc(1.0) is max. NULLs ignored like every aggregate.

nodes.label: WITHIN GROUP ordered-set syntax
nodes.rationale: Fraction is the argument; the column lives in WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY ...), separate from the query's ORDER BY. percentile_cont(ARRAY[0.5, 0.9, 0.99]) sorts once and returns an array.

nodes.label: dense_rank
nodes.rationale: Ties share; no gap (1, 1, 2). Use when you want the count of distinct levels rather than sporting position.

nodes.label: ntile
nodes.rationale: Remainder goes to earliest buckets (7 into 3 → 3,2,2). Splits ties across boundaries with no peer notion — unsuitable for grading. Use percentile_cont thresholds instead.

nodes.label: percent_rank and cume_dist
nodes.rationale: percent_rank is (rank-1)/(rows-1), 0 to 1. cume_dist is the proportion at or before this row, starts above 0, ends at 1.

nodes.label: rank
nodes.rationale: Ties share; next value skips (1, 1, 3). max(rank) equals the row count, not the number of distinct values. Sporting convention: two golds, no silver.

nodes.label: row_number
nodes.rationale: Consecutive integers; ties broken arbitrarily. Non-unique ORDER BY is non-deterministic — WHERE rn = 1 can pick a different row after a plan flip. Always add a unique tiebreaker. Ranking functions ignore the frame.

nodes.label: DISTINCT ON top-1
nodes.rationale: Shortest PostgreSQL-only spelling of top-1 per key; one whole consistent row. Cannot do N > 1.

nodes.label: LATERAL LIMIT per group
nodes.rationale: Wins when groups are few and indexed; loses when groups approach a fraction of rows. 5000 groups / 500k rows: timeout without index, 906 ms with index vs 435 ms for row_number. Only form that takes OFFSET per group.

nodes.label: WindowAgg Run Condition
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL 15+ pushes WHERE rn <= N into WindowAgg so each partition stops after N rows. Applies to monotonic windows (row_number, rank, dense_rank, count). The Sort still processes all input rows.

nodes.label: Correlated subquery
nodes.rationale: References an outer column so it cannot be computed once — N+1 inside one statement. count() over empty is 0; sum/avg/min/max are NULL. Fine for a detail endpoint; rewrite as GROUP BY + LEFT JOIN for a list.

nodes.label: SubPlan loops= signature
nodes.rationale: SubPlan with high loops and Index Searches matching the outer row count is per-row work. Measured 5000 probes. If the planner already un-correlated it there is no SubPlan.

nodes.label: 21000 more than one row from scalar subquery
nodes.rationale: Enforced at runtime, not plan time. LIMIT 1 without ORDER BY converts a loud error into a silently arbitrary answer. Prefer an aggregate or a unique-key constraint.
nodes.norm_label: 21000 more than one row from scalar subquery

nodes.label: Scalar subquery
nodes.rationale: Must return one row and one column. Uncorrelated form is evaluated once for the statement. Zero rows is NULL, not an error. Derived tables in FROM need an alias and cannot see siblings without LATERAL.

nodes.label: OVER () whole-result partition
nodes.rationale: Every row is one partition — the canonical way to attach a grand total or percentage without a self-join. Use 100.0 * not 100 * or integer division floors to zero. FILTER goes before OVER.

nodes.label: PARTITION BY does not collapse rows
nodes.rationale: Same sums as GROUP BY, different row count: one row per group vs every input row with the group's value attached. Measured 3 grouped rows vs 5 windowed.
nodes.norm_label: partition by does not collapse rows

nodes.label: ORDER BY inside OVER running total
nodes.rationale: Implies RANGE BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW. Inner ORDER BY changes values; outer ORDER BY only presentation. RANGE includes peers so equal keys share a running total.
nodes.norm_label: order by inside over running total

nodes.label: Compatible windows share one sort
nodes.rationale: Same partition: one Sort, 999 ms. Different partitions: two Sorts, 1518 ms, 3.4× temp I/O. Second WindowAgg is not free even sharing a sort (~470 ms). Align PARTITION BY or split queries.

nodes.label: Window sort dominates cost
nodes.rationale: One window over 500k: 530 ms, 8560 kB disk sort. Plain count(*) is 26.73 ms. Matching btree (PARTITION BY then ORDER BY) dropped it to 283 ms index-only scan, 575 buffers, no temp I/O.

nodes.label: WindowAgg is not parallel-aware
nodes.rationale: No Gather in the plan. Extra cores do not help. Two 530 ms queries overlapped from the app beat one 1518 ms serial dual-window query.

nodes.label: 42P20 window functions not allowed in WHERE/HAVING
nodes.rationale: WHERE deciding which rows exist while the window depends on those rows would be circular. Fix: subquery or CTE, then filter. Planner flattens it and can push rn <= N as Run Condition.
nodes.norm_label: 42p20 window functions not allowed in where/having

nodes.label: Named WINDOW clause
nodes.rationale: Naming convenience between HAVING and ORDER BY; planner already merges identical definitions. Can extend with ORDER BY/frame if the named window has none; cannot override existing ORDER BY or change PARTITION BY.

nodes.label: Window evaluation pipeline
nodes.rationale: FROM → WHERE → GROUP BY → HAVING → SELECT → windows → DISTINCT → ORDER BY → LIMIT. Filter on a window needs another query level. DISTINCT after windows means row_number prevents de-duplication.

nodes.label: Window over an aggregate
nodes.rationale: sum(count(*)) OVER () is legal: GROUP BY produces per-group counts, then the window sums those group rows. Standard percentage-of-total without a self-join.

nodes.label: Non-covering window index backfire
nodes.rationale: Index (user_id, amount DESC) became Index Scan not Index Only Scan because id was not included — 500574 buffers vs 3783, 534 vs 435 ms. INCLUDE selected columns, or accept the sequential scan plus disk sort.

nodes.label: Correlated cost depends on visibility map
nodes.rationale: Best case after VACUUM: 145 vs 65 ms GROUP BY (2.2×). After touching 1 row in 500, Heap Fetches 0→133359 and 414 vs 90 ms (4.6×). GROUP BY barely moved because it reads the heap once.
nodes.norm_label: correlated cost depends on visibility map

nodes.label: A view cannot take a parameter
nodes.rationale: CREATE VIEW ... WHERE customer = $1 raises 42P02. Workaround is LANGUAGE sql STABLE SRF or filter at the call site.
nodes.norm_label: a view cannot take a parameter

nodes.label: LANGUAGE sql inlining vs plpgsql black box
nodes.rationale: sql inlines and sees real statistics (60 rows). plpgsql is a Function Scan with a fixed 1000-row guess that wrecks joins.
nodes.norm_label: language sql inlining vs plpgsql black box

nodes.label: Function volatility IMMUTABLE STABLE VOLATILE
nodes.rationale: VOLATILE is the default and blocks inlining even for LANGUAGE sql. Lying about IMMUTABLE gives wrong answers, not errors. Index expressions need IMMUTABLE (42P17).

nodes.label: DETACH and DROP partition for retention
nodes.rationale: DETACH 5 ms, DROP 103353 rows in 10 ms. The real payoff is cheap bulk deletion, not query speed.
nodes.norm_label: detach and drop partition for retention

nodes.label: Foreign data wrappers — postgres_fdw and dblink
nodes.norm_label: foreign data wrappers — postgres_fdw and dblink

nodes.label: Put SRFs in FROM not SELECT
nodes.rationale: SRFs produce rows. Two SRFs in SELECT run in lockstep with NULL padding. An SRF in WHERE raises 0A000. ROWS FROM makes zipping explicit.
nodes.norm_label: put srfs in from not select

nodes.label: AT TIME ZONE bidirectional conversion
nodes.rationale: timestamptz AT TIME ZONE zone yields timestamp (clock reading there). timestamp AT TIME ZONE zone yields timestamptz (interpret those digits as that zone). Direction depends on input type.

nodes.label: date to JavaScript Date midnight trap
nodes.rationale: pg turns date into a Date at local midnight. In Asia/Calcutta that is 18:30 UTC the previous day, so toISOString prints the day before. Fix with to_char or setTypeParser(1082).
nodes.norm_label: date to javascript date midnight trap

nodes.label: DST: 1 day versus 24 hours
nodes.rationale: Same wall-clock time tomorrow and 24 hours from now differ across a DST boundary in a local zone. On UTC-normalised timestamptz they agree.

nodes.label: now() versus clock_timestamp()
nodes.rationale: now()/CURRENT_TIMESTAMP is frozen at transaction start. clock_timestamp() is wall clock and changes every call. Use now() for created_at so one transaction shares a timestamp.

nodes.label: timestamptz vs timestamp
nodes.rationale: Both 8 bytes; neither stores a zone. timestamptz is a UTC instant converted on input/output. timestamp keeps the digits and means a different instant to every reader.

nodes.label: GROUP BY day depends on session zone
nodes.rationale: Events at 21:00Z and 23:30Z on 15 June bucket to 15 June in UTC and 16 June in Asia/Kolkata. Always name the zone: date_trunc('day', at AT TIME ZONE ...).
nodes.norm_label: group by day depends on session zone

nodes.label: IANA time zone names
nodes.rationale: Abbreviations like IST are ambiguous. Fixed offsets miss DST. Store users' zones as IANA names so history and legislation are applied correctly.

nodes.label: Pin the pg pool to UTC
nodes.rationale: options: '-c timezone=UTC'. Plain SET leaks across pooled release(). SET LOCAL TIME ZONE $1 fails 42601; use set_config(name, value, true) or put AT TIME ZONE in the query.
nodes.norm_label: pin the pg pool to utc

nodes.label: Session TimeZone setting
nodes.rationale: Display and interpretation, not storage. Affects timestamptz printing, bare timestamp literals, current_date, date_trunc, and ::date. Precedence: SET, PGTZ/options, postgresql.conf, OS at initdb. Pin server and database to UTC.

nodes.label: date arithmetic
nodes.rationale: 4 bytes, no time or zone. date - date is an integer day count. date + integer is a date. date + interval is a timestamp. Month arithmetic clamps: 31 Jan + 1 month = 28 Feb, and is not associative.

nodes.label: interval comparison versus addition
nodes.rationale: 16 bytes: months, days, microseconds. interval '1 month' = interval '30 days' is true for comparison, but addition uses the calendar. Compare timestamps (created_at < now() - interval '1 month'), not intervals. age() is a human calendar breakdown; subtraction is an exact duration.

nodes.label: Multirange
nodes.rationale: A plain range must be contiguous; [1,5)+[10,15) is 22000. PostgreSQL 14+ multiranges hold disjoint ranges as one value, for availability windows with gaps.

nodes.label: Range types
nodes.rationale: First-class values with @>, &&, <<, -|-. Half-open [) by default; discrete types canonicalise [1,10] to [1,11). range(x,x) is empty. pg returns the text form '[1,10)'.

nodes.label: Phase 2 — Data types and the relational model
nodes.rationale: Target PostgreSQL 18.4, Node 24, pg. Seventeen topics from integer widths through modelling money.
nodes.norm_label: phase 2 — data types and the relational model

nodes.label: Phase 2 gate — bigint text timestamptz numeric
nodes.rationale: Move on when you default to bigint + text + timestamptz + numeric for money, and you never write = NULL.
nodes.norm_label: phase 2 gate — bigint text timestamptz numeric

nodes.label: = ANY($1::int[]) for IN lists
nodes.rationale: One array parameter instead of N placeholders. Avoids string assembly and the 65535-parameter protocol ceiling.

nodes.label: EXISTS must be correlated
nodes.rationale: Uncorrelated EXISTS is true whenever the inner table has any row. Extra conditions belong inside the subquery. SELECT 1 is convention; the select list is never evaluated.

nodes.label: Parallel Hash Semi Join
nodes.rationale: EXISTS and IN both plan to Parallel Hash Semi Join. The millisecond gap is noise; choosing between them is readability, not performance.

nodes.label: Semi join
nodes.rationale: Short-circuits after the first match. Written as EXISTS or IN. Use EXISTS when correlated, IN/= ANY for independent lists.

nodes.label: Anti join
nodes.rationale: Keeps left rows with no match. Default spelling is NOT EXISTS. Must prove absence, so it cannot short-circuit the way a semi join does.

nodes.label: Anti join needs the child FK index more
nodes.rationale: Absence must be proven for every unmatched left row. Without an index on the correlated child column that is a scan per left row.
nodes.norm_label: anti join needs the child fk index more

nodes.label: EXCEPT is not an anti join
nodes.rationale: EXCEPT compares whole rows, de-duplicates the left side, and plans as HashSetOp. It answers set difference, not 'which left rows have no related row'.
nodes.norm_label: except is not an anti join

nodes.label: Hash Anti Join
nodes.rationale: NOT EXISTS gets Parallel Hash Anti Join. NOT IN gets Seq Scan plus subplan because the planner cannot assume the column is NULL-free.

nodes.label: LEFT JOIN … WHERE pk IS NULL
nodes.rationale: Older idiom that plans as Hash Anti Join. Correctness depends on the tested column being NOT NULL — test the primary key, not a nullable column.
nodes.norm_label: left join ... where pk is null

nodes.label: NOT IN NULL trap
nodes.rationale: x NOT IN (a,b,NULL) expands to AND of inequalities including x <> NULL, which is NULL for any x. WHERE keeps only true, so every row vanishes. Measured: Dee became [].

nodes.label: LEFT JOIN count(*) trap
nodes.rationale: Never count(*) inside a LEFT JOIN. Count a NOT NULL column of the right table — its PK. count(o.total) under-counts real orders that are unpriced. HAVING count(*) > 0 matches everyone.

nodes.label: HAVING count(*) > 0 after LEFT JOIN
nodes.rationale: The NULL-extended row makes count(*) at least 1. Use count(o.id) or EXISTS. 'Customers who have ordered' is a semi-join.

nodes.label: Semi joins: EXISTS and IN
nodes.rationale: A semi join filters the left side by existence, emits the left row at most once, and exposes no right-hand columns — so it cannot fan out.

nodes.label: Anti joins and the NOT IN trap
nodes.rationale: NOT EXISTS implements the anti join correctly. NOT IN returns the empty set the moment the subquery contains one NULL.
nodes.norm_label: anti joins and the not in trap

nodes.label: Semi and anti joins
nodes.rationale: Split at the positive/negative seam: EXISTS/IN are interchangeable, while one anti-join spelling silently loses data.

nodes.label: Default window frame
nodes.rationale: RANGE BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW. Why a running total over a non-unique ORDER BY jumps two rows at once. Hidden in development against unique keys.

nodes.label: RANGE frame
nodes.rationale: Treats equal ORDER BY values as peers sharing one frame. Default. Running total per distinct ordering value. Two same-day rows both showed 30 under RANGE versus 10 then 30 under ROWS.

nodes.label: ROWS frame
nodes.rationale: Counts physical rows. Running total that advances one row at a time. Write ROWS UNBOUNDED PRECEDING even when ORDER BY is unique, because RANGE and ROWS only agree until peers appear.

nodes.label: Window peers
nodes.rationale: Rows with equal ORDER BY values are indistinguishable to a RANGE frame and share one total. Add a unique tiebreaker or write ROWS.

nodes.label: 0A000 RANGE offset unsupported type
nodes.rationale: RANGE offset is not supported for text — no defined subtraction. Hits when ordering by a formatted date string instead of the date.

nodes.label: 42P20 RANGE offset one ORDER BY column
nodes.rationale: RANGE with offset PRECEDING/FOLLOWING requires exactly one ORDER BY column. Collides with the unique-tiebreaker advice. Drop the tiebreaker or use GROUPS.
nodes.norm_label: 42p20 range offset one order by column

nodes.label: EXCLUDE CURRENT ROW
nodes.rationale: Removes this row from the frame. Leave-one-out: others = 210 minus own amount. Shape for compare-to-the-rest.

nodes.label: EXCLUDE GROUP
nodes.rationale: Removes this row and its peers. Compare this day against all other days. GROUP = TIES + CURRENT ROW.

nodes.label: EXCLUDE NO OTHERS
nodes.rationale: Default EXCLUDE. Writing it changes nothing; exists to make the default explicit.

nodes.label: EXCLUDE TIES
nodes.rationale: Removes peers but keeps the current row. Only option that keeps this row while dropping equals. For a row with one peer: 6→5 versus GROUP 6→4; alone: TIES removes nothing.

nodes.label: GROUPS frame
nodes.rationale: Counts distinct ordering values present in the data. Previous two trading days, not last 48 hours. Accepts multi-column ORDER BY — workaround when 42P20 blocks a RANGE offset. Agrees with RANGE on a dense series; diverges on gaps.

nodes.label: RANGE value offset
nodes.rationale: Measures the frame in ORDER BY units, so a missing day narrows the window rather than silently widening it. Only correct frame over a sparse series. Exactly one ORDER BY column (42P20). Type must support subtraction (0A000 on text). '6 days' PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW is 7 inclusive days.

nodes.label: Window frames
nodes.rationale: A window aggregate is computed over a slice of the partition. You get a frame whether or not you write one. Syntax: {ROWS|RANGE|GROUPS} BETWEEN start AND end [EXCLUDE ...]. Omitting BETWEEN implies AND CURRENT ROW.

nodes.label: Partial moving-average window
nodes.rationale: Frame clips at the partition edge rather than returning NULL. First row of a 3-row MA is its own value. Detect with count(*) over the same frame and blank short windows.

nodes.label: Ranking functions ignore the frame
nodes.rationale: row_number, rank, dense_rank, lag, lead are defined over the partition. PostgreSQL accepts a frame clause and silently ignores it — even an absurd frame produced identical output. Worse than a rejection. Aggregates plus first_value/last_value/nth_value do depend on the frame.

nodes.label: application_name
nodes.rationale: Appears in pg_stat_activity so every connection is attributable. Costs nothing. Without it the column is empty strings during an incident.

nodes.label: pg.Pool
nodes.rationale: One Pool, created once at module scope, exported, shared by every request. pg 8.23.0, pure JavaScript, no libpq. Default import then pg.Pool is the form that has never broken.

nodes.label: pg.Client
nodes.rationale: Exactly one connection you own from connect() to end(). Right when a session must outlive a single query and pooling buys nothing. Single-use; connect() twice raises Client has already been connected.

nodes.label: pool.connect()
nodes.rationale: Checks one connection out of the pool. Use for transactions, SET, cursors, advisory locks, named prepared statements — anything session-stateful. release() in finally. Not a bare Client.

nodes.label: waitingCount
nodes.rationale: max is a queue depth, not a speed limit. Fourth query against max:3 raised waitingCount to 1. Persistent waitingCount>0 means the pool is the bottleneck. Unreleased clients exhaust it.

nodes.label: connectionString
nodes.rationale: One of three config sources (URL, object, PG* env). Mixing URL with database/user looks like overrides and is not — the parsed string wins with no warning. Pool-level options (max, idleTimeoutMillis, ssl object) combine safely. Percent-encode passwords.

nodes.label: connection options passthrough
nodes.rationale: options: '-c search_path=app,public -c statement_timeout=5000' applies on every connection the pool opens. SET through pool.query() lands on one arbitrary connection and is lost.

nodes.label: password as function
nodes.rationale: Evaluated when a connection is opened, not per query. Measured called 1× for 2 queries on 1 connection. Makes IAM/RDS tokens work. Keep idleTimeoutMillis below token TTL.

nodes.label: sslmode=require
nodes.rationale: In pg 8.x treated as verify-full — encrypts AND verifies, stricter than libpq. pg 9.0 will adopt libpq semantics so connections that verify today will silently stop verifying. Write sslmode=verify-full now.

nodes.label: sslmode=verify-full
nodes.rationale: Encrypt and verify certificate and hostname. What production should write explicitly. For a private CA pass ssl:{ca:...}; rejectUnauthorized:false is local-dev only.

nodes.label: Lazy pool connection
nodes.rationale: new Pool() performs no I/O. Measured totalCount 0 idleCount 0 after construct, 1 and 1 after first query. Bad host is ECONNREFUSED on first query, not at startup. Add await pool.query('SELECT 1') before listen().

nodes.label: One pool per process
nodes.rationale: Two pools of max 10 are 20 connections against default max_connections 100 shared by every client. Exceptions: replica pool, dedicated Client for LISTEN, short-lived migration pool. Per-request pools defeat pooling.

nodes.label: pool.on('error')
nodes.rationale: Idle pooled connections can be killed server-side. Unhandled 'error' on the pool is an uncaught exception that kills the process. Handler usually just logs; the pool discards the dead connection.

nodes.label: LISTEN needs a dedicated Client
nodes.rationale: LISTEN via pool.query() returns the connection to the pool with no handler; notifications are lost. The real new pg.Client() case. Also honest for one-shot migration/admin scripts.

nodes.label: FATAL errors arrive as events
nodes.rationale: When the server terminates a connection there may be no in-flight query to reject, so pg emits 'error' on the client or pool. Unhandled, the process dies. Reinforces pool.on('error').

nodes.label: Spread precedence is later keys win
nodes.rationale: {...props} type="text" forces the type. type="text" {...props} is an overridable default.
nodes.norm_label: spread precedence is later keys win

nodes.label: Ref cleanup functions
nodes.rationale: A callback may return a detach cleanup. Implicit arrow returns now look like cleanups — use braces.

nodes.label: findDOMNode removed
nodes.rationale: Slow, fragile, first-child only, broke abstraction. Replacement is an ordinary ref on the element you want.

nodes.label: forwardRef is deprecated, not removed
nodes.rationale: Still works in 19. Still required in libraries that support React 18. New app code on 19 should pass ref as a prop.

nodes.label: ref is an ordinary prop in React 19
nodes.rationale: JSX used to strip ref. Now it travels through spreads, wrappers and HOCs. key is still a third argument.
nodes.norm_label: ref is an ordinary prop in react 19

nodes.label: String refs removed
nodes.rationale: ref="input" with this.refs.input no longer works. Class-only; codemod react/19/replace-string-ref.

nodes.label: Naming as a design check
nodes.rationale: And in the name is two components. Wrapper/Inner often means no responsibility. Position names go stale when the design moves.

nodes.label: React v19 blog — ref as a prop
nodes.norm_label: react v19 blog — ref as a prop

nodes.label: Spread the set, not a domain object
nodes.rationale: Right for DOM passthrough and framework props objects. {...user} silently changes the component when the object gains a field.
nodes.norm_label: spread the set, not a domain object

nodes.label: Split by responsibility, not length
nodes.rationale: Thinking in React: one concern, less granular than CSS classes. A 200-line one-thing component is fine.

nodes.label: Colocation
nodes.rationale: Keep a component next to its only caller. Location communicates scope; deleting a feature deletes its parts. Promote on a second caller.

nodes.label: When splitting hurts
nodes.rationale: Hides flow, manufactures a props contract for local variables, invites speculative variants. More than about five local-variable props is a smell.

nodes.label: as const
nodes.rationale: On a literal expression: every property becomes readonly and every literal keeps its type. On an array it produces a readonly tuple. Applies only to literals, not computed values.

nodes.label: Derived union from as const list
nodes.rationale: const STATUSES = [...] as const; type Status = (typeof STATUSES)[number]. One runtime list; the type updates when an entry is added.
nodes.norm_label: derived union from as const list

nodes.label: Literal type
nodes.rationale: A type inhabited by exactly one value — 'pending', 42, true. In a union it is the main modelling tool: autocompletion, typo errors, and narrowing.

nodes.label: satisfies vs as const
nodes.rationale: satisfies checks against a type without replacing the inferred one. An annotation would widen; as const alone would not check. Use it for computed values that as const cannot wrap.

nodes.label: Tuple type
nodes.rationale: Fixed structure: what is in it, in what order, and how many. Named members are documentation only. Optional and rest elements are allowed. Prefer objects past two or three members.

nodes.label: Union common-members rule
nodes.rationale: Accessible members of A | B are the intersection of the branches' members. Anything else requires narrowing.

nodes.label: Union types
nodes.rationale: One of these. Until you prove which, you may only touch members common to every branch — that restriction is the feature.

nodes.label: Private members are nominal
nodes.rationale: Two classes with identically named private fields are not interchangeable. Each private declaration is unique to its class — the one place TypeScript is nominal without a brand.

nodes.label: Non-null assertion !
nodes.rationale: Removes null/undefined with no check. A claim, not a proof. An explicit throw fails at the cause instead of Cannot read properties of null later.

nodes.label: const enum
nodes.rationale: Inlines values at call sites — a whole-program transform. Banned by isolatedModules and breaks under esbuild, swc, and Vite.

nodes.label: const object plus derived union
nodes.rationale: const Status = {...} as const; type Status = (typeof Status)[keyof typeof Status]. Same name in value and type namespaces. Call sites keep Status.Pending. Erases cleanly.

nodes.label: enum
nodes.rationale: Emits an IIFE two-way map. Cannot be stripped (ERR_UNSUPPORTED_TYPESCRIPT_SYNTAX / erasableSyntaxOnly). Resists tree-shaking. Numeric enums log as numbers and are nominally typed.

nodes.label: String literal union
nodes.rationale: Default for a fixed set of values. Zero runtime cost, readable serialisation, no import. Cannot iterate members at runtime.

nodes.label: as const is not as T
nodes.rationale: as const asks for the narrowest inference of something already written and cannot lie. as T asserts a type the compiler cannot verify.
nodes.norm_label: as const is not as t

nodes.label: Hook return as const tuple
nodes.rationale: return [value, inc] without as const infers (number | (() => void))[] so both destructured names become that union. as const makes readonly [number, () => void].

nodes.label: connect-redis session store
nodes.rationale: Session store is integration only; Redis syllabus owns Redis.

nodes.label: Cookie flags
nodes.rationale: res.cookie flags: httpOnly, secure, sameSite. Session vs JWT choice is Node Phase 8.

nodes.label: cookie-parser
nodes.rationale: Mount cookie-parser before session so session libraries read cookies from the parsed object.

nodes.label: Logout and revocation
nodes.rationale: Logout clears cookies / hits revocation; storage is Node/Redis.

nodes.label: Middleware contract
nodes.rationale: (req, res, next) => void. next() vs next(err) vs never calling next: hang, double-send, silent drop.

nodes.label: Phase 1 — Routing and path matching
nodes.rationale: Order is load-bearing; Express will not warn you. A catch-all registered too early steals traffic.

nodes.label: Phase 2 — Middleware architecture
nodes.rationale: The whole framework is a stack of functions. Order, next, and termination are the job.

nodes.label: Body parsers
nodes.rationale: express.json() and express.urlencoded() with content-type gates, empty-body behaviour, and size limits as DoS control.

nodes.label: Part 1 — Foundations
nodes.rationale: Express is a routing and middleware layer on top of http.Server, not a replacement for Node.

nodes.label: Part 2 — HTTP surface
nodes.rationale: How Express packages Node streams and http.Server into req/res and a single error channel.

nodes.label: Express over node:http
nodes.rationale: Express is router + middleware over node:http, not a language and not an application architecture.

nodes.label: call/apply/bind cannot change arrow this
nodes.rationale: They fail silently on this while still passing arguments; bind still returns a function.

nodes.label: Array method borrowing
nodes.rationale: Array methods need only length and integer keys; Array.from replaced most slice.call uses.

nodes.label: Partial application with bind
nodes.rationale: Fills arguments only from the left; hoist bind out of hot loops.

nodes.label: Object.prototype.toString.call type tag
nodes.rationale: typeof cannot tell Array from null; toString.call reads the internal tag but loses to Symbol.toStringTag.

nodes.label: Function.prototype.apply
nodes.rationale: Second argument must be array-like or CreateListFromArrayLike throws.

nodes.label: Function.prototype.bind
nodes.rationale: Returns a new function object every time, so inline bind never matches removeEventListener.

nodes.label: thisArg coercion strict vs sloppy
nodes.rationale: Strict passes thisArg through; sloppy boxes primitives and maps null/undefined to globalThis.

nodes.label: bind and new
nodes.rationale: new discards bound this but keeps bound args; [[Construct]] delegates so instanceof still holds.

nodes.label: Handwritten bind
nodes.rationale: Naive apply misses new; new.target plus prototype linking restores construct, but .name/.length/absent prototype are exotic.

nodes.label: bind permanence
nodes.rationale: Later call/apply/bind cannot change this; further bind still accumulates leading arguments.

nodes.label: Borrowing, partial application and cost
nodes.rationale: call/apply/bind survive as borrowing, type tags, and left-to-right partial application.

nodes.label: The three methods
nodes.rationale: All three set this; only bind defers the call. apply takes an array.

nodes.label: What bind does
nodes.rationale: A bound function is an exotic object: prefixed name, reduced length, no own prototype, permanent this.

nodes.label: console.log can block the event loop
nodes.rationale: console is synchronous on some destinations. When stdout is a pipe a slow consumer can block the loop under a traffic spike.
nodes.norm_label: console.log can block the event loop

nodes.label: Log levels
nodes.rationale: fatal/error, warn, info, debug, trace. Default production to info. Turning on debug fleet-wide fills a disk.

nodes.label: Minimum log schema
nodes.rationale: time, level, msg, service/version, reqId/traceId, and domain ids as dedicated fields — never only buried in msg.

nodes.label: Structured logging
nodes.rationale: A production log line is a searchable record. Every line is one JSON object with a small set of agreed keys.

nodes.label: Logs, traces, and metrics
