nodes.rationale: Logs are discrete events. Metrics are aggregates. Traces connect work across services. None replaces the others.

nodes.label: pino child loggers
nodes.rationale: Bind reqId and orderId once so every subsequent line carries them. One child per request or job. base is process-lifetime facts.

nodes.label: pino
nodes.rationale: A fast JSON logger with the knobs production uses: child bindings, redaction paths, and serializers.

nodes.label: pino redact
nodes.rationale: Redact at the logger, not in every call site. Defense in depth, not a substitute for not putting secrets on the object.

nodes.label: pino serializers
nodes.rationale: stdSerializers.err pulls type, message, and stack. Pass the error under an err field on the merge object.

nodes.label: ALS does not cross threads
nodes.rationale: Worker threads and child processes do not inherit ALS. Pass the id in workerData or the message.

nodes.label: AsyncLocalStorage for request context
nodes.rationale: Preserves the id across await points without threading an extra argument. Enter the context once at the edge.

nodes.label: Correlation and request IDs
nodes.rationale: Generate or accept one id at the edge and thread it through logs, outbound calls, jobs, and errors until the work is done.

nodes.label: Persist request id on job payloads
nodes.rationale: Otherwise background failures are orphaned from the HTTP request that caused them. Re-enter ALS in the worker.
nodes.norm_label: persist request id on job payloads

nodes.label: x-request-id
nodes.rationale: Trust a well-formed incoming header from your own edge, mint a UUID when missing, echo it on the response. Validate length and charset.

nodes.label: Access logs vs app logs
nodes.rationale: Access log: method, path, status, duration, request id. App log: domain events and failures. Duplicating every request as info doubles cost.

nodes.label: Data minimization vs redaction
nodes.rationale: Minimization means not putting sensitive fields on the object. Redaction strips fields that slipped through. Minimization first.

nodes.label: Never log secrets or raw PII
nodes.rationale: Passwords, tokens, full PAN/CVV, government ids, raw address books, private keys. Logs have wider read access than the database.
nodes.norm_label: never log secrets or raw pii

nodes.label: What to log
nodes.rationale: Log decisions and outcomes: authz denies, state transitions, dependency failures, exhausted retries, config fallbacks.

nodes.label: OpenTelemetry
nodes.rationale: Instrument once and export to many backends. Vendor SDKs lock you in; OTel is the portable layer.

nodes.label: Trace sampling
nodes.rationale: Full traces for 100% of traffic melts a backend. Head-based ratio, always-sample errors/slow, or tail sampling at the collector.

nodes.label: Span
nodes.rationale: One unit of work with a start, an end, attributes, and optional status. Manual spans belong on business operations.

nodes.label: Trace
nodes.rationale: A tree of spans sharing a trace id. Answers where a request spent time across services.

nodes.label: W3C Trace Context
nodes.rationale: traceparent / tracestate is the standardized join key across processes. The cousin of x-request-id.

nodes.label: Error tracking
nodes.rationale: Sentry, Bugsnag, GlitchTip group the same crash across thousands of events, show the release that introduced it, and page on rate changes.

nodes.label: Error fingerprinting
nodes.rationale: Groups events into issues by root cause. Unique ids in the message string split one bug into hundreds of issues.

nodes.label: Error tracker release
nodes.rationale: An identifier for the code version, often git SHA. Without it, new in this deploy is guesswork.

nodes.label: diagnostics_channel
nodes.rationale: Zero-dependency in-process pub/sub. Libraries publish named events; observability glue subscribes without monkey-patching private APIs.

nodes.label: hasSubscribers
nodes.rationale: The performance gate. Keep payloads small on hot paths so the path stays cheap when nobody is listening.

nodes.label: TracingChannel
nodes.rationale: Request-shaped helper: tracingChannel('myservice:charge').tracePromise(() => doCharge(orderId), {orderId}).

nodes.label: Node diagnostic report
nodes.rationale: Structured JSON dump of stacks, handles, versions, resource usage on demand or on fatal conditions. Large and may contain env secrets.

nodes.label: --report-on-fatalerror
nodes.rationale: Writes a report when the process dies fatally. Needs a writable --report-directory in the container.

nodes.label: trace_events
nodes.rationale: Low-level V8/node trace categories. Scope to a critical section; leaving global tracing on under traffic collapses latency.

nodes.label: Do not pretty-print in production
nodes.rationale: Aggregators parse JSON. Colourized multi-line output is for humans on a laptop.

nodes.label: Log volume discipline
nodes.rationale: Do not log every SQL query, full bodies, debug fleet-wide, or inside tight loops. Sample high-volume success; always keep errors.

nodes.label: captureException on handled failures
nodes.rationale: If you log and continue without captureException, the tracker never sees production's most common failures — the ones you already catch.

nodes.label: Chunking with setImmediate
nodes.rationale: Split work into ~10–50ms pieces and await setImmediate so the loop can drain I/O. Bounds latency, not throughput.

nodes.label: CPU-bound work
nodes.rationale: Busy compute on the single JS thread. While it runs, no request, timer, or health check is handled.

nodes.label: libuv thread pool crypto APIs
nodes.rationale: crypto.pbkdf2, scrypt, and async bcrypt run off the loop; *Sync variants block it. Cheapest password-hashing fix.

nodes.label: Check phase (setImmediate)
nodes.rationale: Runs setImmediate. After poll in the same tick, so inside an I/O callback setImmediate always beats setTimeout(0).

nodes.label: Event loop phases
nodes.rationale: Fixed order per tick: timers → pending → idle/prepare → poll → check → close. nextTick and microtasks drain between phases.

nodes.label: process.getActiveResourcesInfo
nodes.rationale: Lists handles keeping the process alive. unref() excludes a handle from the exit count without cancelling it.

nodes.label: Poll phase
nodes.rationale: Waits for I/O then runs I/O callbacks. An idle server spends its life blocked here consuming no CPU.

nodes.label: setTimeout(0) versus setImmediate from main
nodes.rationale: From the main module their order is a genuine race. Inside I/O it is always setImmediate first.

nodes.label: Microtasks versus macrotasks
nodes.rationale: Microtasks (then/await/queueMicrotask) drain completely between phases. Macrotasks (timers, setImmediate, I/O) belong to a phase.

nodes.label: process.nextTick
nodes.rationale: Node-only queue drained at a checkpoint before microtasks. Drains to exhaustion including newly queued ticks — starvation risk.

nodes.label: queueMicrotask
nodes.rationale: Web-standard microtask. Prefer over nextTick except when you must run before pending promise continuations.

nodes.label: await yields to microtasks not the event loop
nodes.rationale: Body runs synchronously to the first await; resumption is a microtask. A loop of already-resolved awaits never lets timers or I/O run.
nodes.norm_label: await yields to microtasks not the event loop

nodes.label: async does not stop CPU from blocking
nodes.rationale: async changes the return value, not whether the body blocks. There is no await that yields inside a tight loop.
nodes.norm_label: async does not stop cpu from blocking

nodes.label: nextTick after promises at ESM top level
nodes.rationale: The nextTick-before-promises rule fails at ESM top level because module evaluation is itself a microtask. Inside a timer callback the familiar order returns.
nodes.norm_label: nexttick after promises at esm top level

nodes.label: GIN index
nodes.rationale: GIN indexes the parts of a value — jsonb keys, array elements, lexemes, trigrams — making @>, @@, ? and LIKE '%x%' indexable. Selective needles win; a 16% match was slower than seq scan.

nodes.label: gist_trgm_ops distance ordering
nodes.rationale: ORDER BY col <-> 'text' is nearest-neighbour. GIN cannot do it; gist_trgm_ops can, at a larger index size.

nodes.label: jsonb_ops
nodes.rationale: Default GIN opclass stores keys and values separately. Serves @> and existence operators ? / ?| / ?&.

nodes.label: jsonb_path_ops
nodes.rationale: Hashes whole paths; smaller and faster for @> only. Existence operators fall back to sequential scan.

nodes.label: pg_trgm gin_trgm_ops
nodes.rationale: Trigram GIN makes infix LIKE/ILIKE indexable. Patterns shorter than three characters produce too few distinguishing trigrams and can be slower than a seq scan.

nodes.label: BRIN index
nodes.rationale: Block Range INdex stores min/max per 128-page range. Tiny filter, not a lookup; needs physical correlation near ±1. 24 kB vs 64 MB B-tree on 3M ordered rows.

nodes.label: Exclusion constraint
nodes.rationale: EXCLUDE USING gist (room WITH =, during WITH &&) raises 23P01 on overlap. Needs btree_gist for equality types. Cannot be expressed with UNIQUE or CHECK.

nodes.label: GiST index
nodes.rationale: Framework for overlap, containment and distance on types with no total order: ranges, PostGIS, inet, nearest-neighbour.

nodes.label: Hash index
nodes.rationale: Equality only. Cannot UNIQUE (0A000), range, ORDER BY, INCLUDE, or index-only scans. Crash-safe since PostgreSQL 10. Smaller on wide keys.

nodes.label: Physical correlation
nodes.rationale: pg_stats.correlation near 1 or −1 makes BRIN useful. Shuffled data at 0.0119 caused the planner to ignore the BRIN index entirely.

nodes.label: GIN for jsonb, arrays and full text; pg_trgm for LIKE
nodes.norm_label: gin for jsonb, arrays and full text; pg_trgm for like

nodes.label: GIN pending list
nodes.rationale: GIN buffers inserts in a pending list (gin_pending_list_limit 4MB). Cost is deferred to VACUUM or a query that scans the unmerged list; fastupdate=off pays on insert instead.

nodes.label: Non-indexable predicate shape
nodes.rationale: <> , NOT IN and leading-wildcard LIKE cannot seek a B-tree. OR is fine only if every branch has its own usable index (BitmapOr).

nodes.label: Deadlock 40P01
nodes.rationale: Cycle of lock waits. After deadlock_timeout PostgreSQL aborts the cheaper victim with 40P01. DETAIL names both processes; queries are only in the server log.

nodes.label: deadlock_timeout
nodes.rationale: Default 1s. PostgreSQL does not check for cycles on every wait. Every deadlock costs at least that second. log_lock_waits logs waits past this threshold.

nodes.label: REPEATABLE READ
nodes.rationale: One snapshot for the whole transaction, taken at the first statement not BEGIN. Read-only RR cannot fail with 40001. Writers updating a changed row get 40001 concurrent update.

nodes.label: SERIALIZABLE
nodes.rationale: Outcome equals some serial execution. Tracks read/write dependencies. High-conflict: 135 attempts / 115 retries / 12.4s vs 20 attempts / 71ms for FOR UPDATE in id order.

nodes.label: Serialization failure 40001
nodes.rationale: Retry the whole transaction on 40001/40P01 with bounded attempts, jittered backoff outside the checked-out connection, and no external side effects inside the body.

nodes.label: Write skew
nodes.rationale: Two transactions read an overlapping set then write different rows, breaking an invariant neither saw break. RR allows it; SERIALIZABLE aborts one with 40001 read/write dependencies.

nodes.label: Lost update
nodes.rationale: Read-modify-write under READ COMMITTED: 20 concurrent increments produced qty=2 with no error. Last writer wins with a stale absolute value.

nodes.label: Optimistic version column
nodes.rationale: UPDATE ... WHERE version = $2; rowCount 0 means lost the race. Right for edit forms spanning requests or low contention. Worst on a hot row: 170 retries, 337 ms.

nodes.label: SELECT FOR UPDATE
nodes.rationale: Row lock serialises the read-modify-write so application logic can run. 20/20 correct at 58 ms. Hold the lock only until COMMIT; no I/O in the window.

nodes.label: The lost update, and four ways to stop it
nodes.norm_label: the lost update, and four ways to stop it

nodes.label: Consistent lock order
nodes.rationale: The fix is locking rows in a stable order via SELECT ... ORDER BY id FOR UPDATE, not retry. Opposite order deadlocked in 1155 ms; same order both committed in 326 ms.

nodes.label: SQL arithmetic UPDATE
nodes.rationale: SET qty = qty + 1 is atomic in one statement. Fastest fix (20/20, 37.9 ms) when the new value is expressible in SQL.

nodes.label: Full-text cannot find typos
nodes.rationale: Stemming normalises grammar, not misspellings. router against a document saying routr → 0 rows. That is pg_trgm's job.

nodes.label: GIN index on tsvector
nodes.rationale: 200002 products: 1165ms seq scan → 17.36ms Bitmap Heap Scan (~66×). Query expression must match the indexed expression exactly.

nodes.label: IMMUTABLE to_tsvector trap
nodes.rationale: One-arg to_tsvector(body) reads session default_text_search_config so it is not IMMUTABLE — 42P17. Name the config.

nodes.label: ts_headline
nodes.rationale: Re-reads original text so it cannot use the index. Apply after LIMIT, never before.

nodes.label: english vs simple configurations
nodes.rationale: english for descriptions (stemming); simple for SKUs, tags, codes. Serve both from one config and everyone is slightly wrong.

nodes.label: Prefix query :*
nodes.rationale: Full-text matches whole lexemes. rout → 0 rows; rout:* → 13336. Type-ahead appends :* to the last token.

nodes.label: to_tsquery
nodes.rationale: Parses tsquery syntax, not prose. Two words, an apostrophe, or a quote raise 42601. Never give it a search box.

nodes.label: to_tsvector
nodes.rationale: Configuration is part of the data. Document indexed as english will not match a query parsed as simple.

nodes.label: tsvector
nodes.rationale: Sorted set of lexemes with positions. english stems and drops stop words; simple lowercases and keeps everything.

nodes.label: websearch_to_tsquery
nodes.rationale: Search-engine syntax: quotes=phrase, -=negation, or=|. Never raises; silently discards unparseable tokens.

nodes.label: security_invoker views
nodes.rationale: Default owner privileges bypass caller RLS. PG15+ security_invoker=true uses the caller's privileges.

nodes.label: ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES
nodes.rationale: Stops every migration from needing a manual GRANT. Keyed FOR ROLE the owner, so hand-created tables miss it.

nodes.label: App role should not own the schema
nodes.rationale: DDL is an ownership right with no GRANT form. Injected DROP TABLE is 42501 for a non-owner and a completed migration for an owner.
nodes.norm_label: app role should not own the schema

nodes.label: GRANT USAGE not CREATE
nodes.rationale: CREATE on the schema lets the app create tables it then owns, silently eroding the boundary.

nodes.label: Two connection strings
nodes.rationale: Migrations as owner, request path as app. If both live in the same .env a compromised process reads both.

nodes.label: Direct vs pooled endpoint
nodes.rationale: The most common connection incident. Differ by one token or port; the wrong choice fails only under load. Migrations/DDL/LISTEN need direct.

nodes.label: Managed PostgreSQL
nodes.rationale: Removes sysadmin work and none of the application work. Missing indexes, long transactions, connection exhaustion and locking migrations remain yours.

nodes.label: Connection limits and PgBouncer
nodes.rationale: A PostgreSQL connection is an OS process. 40 clients non-overlapping → 1 backend; 40 concurrent → exactly default_pool_size.

nodes.label: Pool exhaustion 08P01
nodes.rationale: 5 open transactions, pool 5: two clients waited 120204 ms then 08P01. Saturation becomes a hang at the 120s default.

nodes.label: Transaction pooling
nodes.rationale: The answer and a source of intermittent bugs. Session features (prepared statements historically, SET) break.

nodes.label: FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY
nodes.rationale: Table owners bypass RLS by default. An app connecting as schema owner is unprotected and its tests pass.

nodes.label: Row-level security
nodes.rationale: Moves which rows a user may see into the database so a missing WHERE stops being a data breach. Default-deny: enable with no policy and the table looks empty.

nodes.label: SET LOCAL for RLS identity
nodes.rationale: A plain SET persists on a pooled connection into the next request — measured — which is a cross-tenant exposure.

nodes.label: USING vs WITH CHECK
nodes.rationale: UPDATE needs WITH CHECK as well as USING, otherwise a user can modify a row they own into one they should not.

nodes.label: SET LOCAL work_mem on pooled connections
nodes.norm_label: set local work_mem on pooled connections

nodes.label: Session features broken in transaction mode
nodes.norm_label: session features broken in transaction mode

nodes.label: The providers, and connecting correctly
nodes.rationale: Every provider has a direct and a pooled endpoint. Wrong endpoint fails only under load. Migrations need the direct endpoint.

nodes.label: Pool modes
nodes.rationale: Transaction mode multiplexes; session state does not follow the client. SET LOCAL, not SET.

nodes.label: btree_gist extension
nodes.rationale: Required so GiST can mix scalar equality with range overlap in one exclusion constraint.

nodes.label: Exclusion constraint
nodes.rationale: EXCLUDE USING gist (room WITH =, during WITH &&) forbids same-room overlap (23P01). Index-enforced, so concurrent read-then-write cannot both insert.

nodes.label: Half-open range default
nodes.rationale: [1,10) includes 1 excludes 10. Discrete types canonicalise [1,10] to [1,11). Touching intervals do not overlap, so back-to-back bookings are legal.

nodes.label: Named constraints for API mapping
nodes.rationale: err.constraint plus SQLSTATE (23505→409, 23514→422, 23502→422, 23503→409) turns DB errors into field messages. Auto-generated names change on rename.

nodes.label: Circular foreign keys
nodes.rationale: Immediate insert of mutual references fails 23503. Deferral lets both rows exist before the check. Often a modelling smell versus a nullable FK plus flag.

nodes.label: DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED
nodes.rationale: Checked at COMMIT. INITIALLY IMMEDIATE is usually right: fail-fast unless SET CONSTRAINTS … DEFERRED. Applies to UNIQUE, PK, EXCLUDE, FK — not NOT NULL.

nodes.label: Deferrable UNIQUE cannot be ON CONFLICT arbiter
nodes.rationale: Upsert needs an immediate arbiter. Deferring a unique constraint silently removes it as an ON CONFLICT target.
nodes.norm_label: deferrable unique cannot be on conflict arbiter

nodes.label: Defer UNIQUE to swap values
nodes.rationale: Swapping positions 1 and 2 collides midway under immediate UNIQUE. A bare unique index cannot be deferred.

nodes.label: DROP defaults to RESTRICT (2BP01)
nodes.rationale: dependent_objects_still_exist. The error/NOTICE list is the dry-run. Prefer dropping named dependents over blanket CASCADE.

nodes.label: DROP CASCADE is schema not data
nodes.rationale: Drops views and the child's FK constraint; the child table and its rows survive, now orphanable. Opposite of ON DELETE CASCADE.
nodes.norm_label: drop cascade is schema not data

nodes.label: NO ACTION vs RESTRICT
nodes.rationale: Difference is timing: deferred NO ACTION checks at COMMIT; RESTRICT always fires immediately (23001).

nodes.label: ON DELETE actions
nodes.rationale: NO ACTION 23503, RESTRICT 23001, CASCADE deletes children, SET NULL, SET DEFAULT. Map both 23503 and 23001 to HTTP 409.

nodes.label: Rename before drop
nodes.rationale: Rename to old_deprecated_DATE so leftover code fails with 42703 immediately; drop a deploy later. Turns irreversible data loss into a reversible mistake.

nodes.label: Application cannot enforce referential integrity
nodes.rationale: Check-then-insert is not atomic; another transaction can delete the parent between them. Only the database evaluates the constraint as part of the write.

nodes.label: bigint ids as JavaScript strings
nodes.rationale: pg returns bigint as a string because 64-bit exceeds Number.SAFE_INTEGER. Treat ids as opaque strings; user.id + 1 becomes '11'.

nodes.label: bigint identity, not int
nodes.rationale: int stops at 2,147,483,647. Sequences advance on attempts, so failures burn the range faster than row count. Migrating int→bigint rewrites under ACCESS EXCLUSIVE.

nodes.label: GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY
nodes.rationale: SQL-standard identity refuses manual inserts with 428C9. serial accepts them without advancing the sequence, later colliding with 23505.

nodes.label: Natural vs surrogate keys
nodes.rationale: Surrogate keys win because natural keys change. Natural keys fit immutable reference data (ISO codes). A surrogate does not replace UNIQUE on the natural key.

nodes.label: serial is not a type
nodes.rationale: serial creates an integer, a sequence, and a default. The sequence is owned by the column and dropped with the table. Identity is is_identity, not column_default.

nodes.label: UUID primary keys
nodes.rationale: 16 bytes vs 8; v4 UUIDs destroy btree insert locality. Prefer UUIDv7 if client-generated ids are required. Adding uuid DEFAULT gen_random_uuid() rewrites the table.

nodes.label: RETURNING over currval
nodes.rationale: currval is session state and errors 55000 if nextval was never called; lastval() is whichever sequence was touched last. RETURNING is unambiguous and one round trip.

nodes.label: Sequence gaps
nodes.rationale: Sources: rollback, unique failure, CACHE n, crash recovery (last_value WAL-logged periodically). Gapless invoice numbers need a serialised counter row.

nodes.label: Sequences are non-transactional
nodes.rationale: nextval takes a value and releases immediately so concurrent inserters never block. Rollbacks and failed inserts keep their values — gaps are the design.

nodes.label: Sequence OWNED BY
nodes.rationale: serial/identity sequences drop with the table (0 left after DROP). Hand-created sequences survive unless ALTER SEQUENCE … OWNED BY. Ownership does not restrict nextval.

nodes.label: setval sequence repair
nodes.rationale: After explicit ids: setval(seq, max(id)+1, false). is_called false means next nextval returns the given value; true returns the one after.

nodes.label: INSERT RETURNING
nodes.rationale: Only correct way to learn a generated id. A follow-up SELECT can see another transaction's row under concurrency.

nodes.label: Always name INSERT columns
nodes.rationale: INSERT INTO t VALUES binds to current column order; adding a column silently rewires statements. Omit columns that have defaults. Explicit NULL overrides DEFAULT.

nodes.label: Identity consumed before conflict
nodes.rationale: Identity is generated before conflict detection. Three idempotent two-row seeds left last_value at 6. Harmless because sequences are not gapless.

nodes.label: CTE as named subquery
nodes.rationale: WITH names a query so the outer statement can read it like a table.

nodes.label: No forward references
nodes.rationale: A CTE cannot refer to a later sibling unless the WITH is RECURSIVE.

nodes.label: CTE name shadowing
nodes.rationale: A CTE name hides a same-named table in that statement.

nodes.label: WITH on DML
nodes.rationale: WITH can wrap INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE and RETURNING, not only SELECT.

nodes.label: FILTER vs N subqueries
nodes.rationale: One scan with several FILTER aggregates is about 4× cheaper than N correlated subqueries.

nodes.label: CYCLE clause
nodes.rationale: Detects cycles so a graph walk cannot loop forever.

nodes.label: SEARCH clause
nodes.rationale: Declares breadth-first or depth-first walk order without hand-rolled path bookkeeping.

nodes.label: WITH RECURSIVE
nodes.rationale: Anchor term seeds the working table; the recursive term is evaluated until it returns no rows.

nodes.label: Correlated subquery
nodes.rationale: Refers to the outer row and is conceptually re-evaluated per outer row.

nodes.label: Scalar subquery
nodes.rationale: Must return at most one row and one column; more than one row is an error.

nodes.label: NOT IN vs NOT EXISTS
nodes.rationale: NOT IN is UNKNOWN when the set contains NULL, so the anti-join silently returns no rows; NOT EXISTS does not have that trap.

nodes.label: CSS syllabus
nodes.rationale: Critical-path syllabus, not a CSS course. Cut twice: 230 → 119 → 74 topics.

nodes.label: @layer
nodes.rationale: Declare precedence up front; unlayered is the implicit final layer. Load-bearing reason this phase exists.

nodes.label: CSS example policy
nodes.rationale: Measured behaviour comes from the local Firefox render; cross-browser availability comes from web-features. Keep the two apart.

nodes.label: Cascade comparison order
nodes.rationale: Origin and importance, then context, then inline styles, then layers, then specificity, then source order. First criterion that separates two declarations ends the comparison.

nodes.label: CSS two-source verification
nodes.rationale: What does this do? measured in Firefox 153. Is it safe to ship? web-features Baseline.

nodes.label: CSS is resolved, not executed
nodes.rationale: You write constraints and the engine computes the result. Explains silent typos, specificity, and height: 100% doing nothing.

nodes.label: Never invent output
nodes.rationale: Every number, timing and error string comes from a run that actually happened. No run means no console block.

nodes.label: No new sandboxes
nodes.rationale: Validate against official documentation or the web and name the source in the Verified line.

nodes.label: PG dual-half example policy
nodes.rationale: Every page carries both the SQL (or shell) and the Node pg code that issues it.

nodes.label: Handbook writing style
nodes.rationale: Concept → why it exists → runnable code → gotchas → when to use it. Second person, present tense, name the trade-off.

nodes.label: Derived state
nodes.rationale: If a value can be calculated from existing props or state, calculate it during rendering. That removes cascading updates and makes out-of-sync state unrepresentable.

nodes.label: useEffect-that-syncs-state antipattern
nodes.rationale: Storing a derivable value and syncing it with an effect costs an extra render and commits a stale frame to the DOM before the effect runs.

nodes.label: Store selectedId, derive the object
nodes.rationale: A stored selected object goes stale on edit and dangles on delete. find by id reflects edits automatically and yields null when the item is gone.

nodes.label: useMemo for expensive derivation
nodes.rationale: Expensive calculations stay derived via useMemo. State plus an effect creates a second source of truth that only usually agrees.

nodes.label: Shape 2: effect sets its own dependency
nodes.norm_label: shape 2: effect sets its own dependency

nodes.label: Too many re-renders
nodes.rationale: The throw is a guard on consecutive re-renders, not a diagnosis. Effect loops often never throw because each iteration is a separately scheduled update.

nodes.label: Five principles for structuring state
nodes.rationale: Group related state; avoid contradictions; avoid redundant state; avoid duplication; avoid deep nesting. Framed as database normalisation.

nodes.label: Impossible states
nodes.rationale: Two booleans give four combinations, some meaningless. A single status value makes invalid combinations unrepresentable.

nodes.label: Updating state during render
nodes.rationale: Legal only for the currently rendering component, inside a condition that makes itself false. Restarts before children render and before commit, so the stale value never paints.

nodes.label: Priority tiers
nodes.rationale: Tiers allocate effort, not importance: Master, Understand, Know, When Needed — assigned for fullstack application development.

nodes.label: Measured vs Baseline sources
nodes.rationale: What it does is measured in Firefox 153; whether it is safe to ship comes from web-features.

nodes.label: Critical-path CSS syllabus
nodes.rationale: Cut twice on instruction: 230→119 advanced-only, then 119→74 critical-only. Architecture, tokens, CSS Modules and Tailwind dropped; SCSS kept as usage.

nodes.label: CSS example policy
nodes.rationale: Claims checked against a real render: getComputedStyle, getBoundingClientRect, CSS.supports, and Baseline keys.

nodes.label: Single-engine limitation
nodes.rationale: Only Firefox 153.0.3 is installed. Measured behaviour is labelled with the engine; availability comes from web-features.

nodes.label: 300-line file-size cap
nodes.rationale: Caps how much lives in one file, never how much a topic gets explained. Write first, then split on a concept boundary at 301 lines.

nodes.label: Link form .md with numeric prefixes
nodes.rationale: Directory-slug links broke 188 links; every link ends in .md and keeps every numeric prefix.

nodes.label: Verified line policy
nodes.rationale: Every number, timing and error string comes from a run that happened. No run means no console block.

nodes.label: express.static
nodes.rationale: Serves files from a directory as middleware. Put it after API routes if the same app also hosts a SPA. Prefer a CDN or Nginx for heavy static traffic.

nodes.label: Bare star path invalid on Express 5
nodes.rationale: Bare * path tokens are invalid; registration throws. 2020 MERN tutorials crash on Express 5.
nodes.norm_label: bare star path invalid on express 5

nodes.label: Named splat {*splat}
nodes.rationale: On Express 5, app.get('*') throws at boot. Use a named splat.

nodes.label: SPA fallback
nodes.rationale: Client-side routers need index.html on unknown paths. Register the catch-all after API routes.

nodes.label: httpOnly cookie flag
nodes.rationale: Blocks document.cookie. Stops trivial XSS from stealing session tokens via JavaScript.

nodes.label: res.cookie
nodes.rationale: Built in. Flags decide whether browser JS can read the cookie and when it is sent. Reading cookies needs cookie-parser.

nodes.label: SameSite cookie flag
nodes.rationale: CSRF posture for cookie-based sessions. SameSite=None requires secure.

nodes.label: Secure cookie flag
nodes.rationale: HTTPS only. Required with SameSite=None. Typically enabled when NODE_ENV === production.

nodes.label: stream.pipeline over pipe
nodes.rationale: A bare .pipe() leaves the source open when the destination fails or the client disconnects, leaking handles. pipeline destroys every stream in the chain on failure.

nodes.label: Streaming and downloads
nodes.rationale: res.sendFile and res.download stream files with safer path options. For big dynamic bodies, pipe a stream and handle errors mid-flight.

nodes.label: Phase 4 — Responses and static files
nodes.rationale: What leaves the process: status, body shape, files, cookies, SPA fallback. Target Express 5.2.1 on Node 24.19.0.

nodes.label: API then static then splat
nodes.rationale: Catch-all before API makes /api/users return HTML. Correct order: API → static assets → HTML fallback.

nodes.label: Stream vs buffer trade-off
nodes.rationale: Streaming keeps memory flat regardless of payload size. You give up changing status after the first byte. Buffering keeps error handling simple until size makes it untenable.

nodes.label: Phase 4 gate — one response per path
nodes.rationale: Every success and error path ends in exactly one response with a deliberate status and consistent JSON shape; SPA fallback does not steal /api.
nodes.norm_label: phase 4 gate — one response per path

nodes.label: Abstract operations
nodes.rationale: Internal non-callable algorithms in SmallCaps — ToPrimitive, ToNumber, Get — reused so every operator shares one set of rules.

nodes.label: Date Symbol.toPrimitive default-as-string
nodes.rationale: Date overrides default hint to behave as string, so date + '' is a date string while date * 1 is a timestamp.

nodes.label: ToPrimitive
nodes.rationale: Hint string tries toString then valueOf; number and default try valueOf then toString. Symbol.toPrimitive overrides. + uses default; templates use string; arithmetic uses number.

nodes.label: {} + [] statement parse
nodes.rationale: As a statement {} is an empty block, leaving unary +[] which is ToNumber('') = 0. In expression position it is concatenation.

nodes.label: + concatenates if either side is a string
nodes.rationale: After ToPrimitive, if either operand is a string, + concatenates. Every other arithmetic operator ToNumbers both. Form values are always strings.
nodes.norm_label: + concatenates if either side is a string

nodes.label: ToNumber
nodes.rationale: null becomes 0; undefined becomes NaN. A null price silently becomes free; a missing value becomes NaN and poisons later arithmetic.

nodes.label: ToPrimitive coercion
nodes.rationale: Hint string: toString then valueOf. number/default: valueOf then toString. Symbol.toPrimitive overrides.

nodes.label: map(parseInt) radix trap
nodes.rationale: map passes (value, index); index becomes radix so ['1','2','3'].map(parseInt) is [1, NaN, NaN]. Always pass radix 10.

nodes.label: Number versus parseInt
nodes.rationale: Number demands the whole string; Number('42px') is NaN. parseInt reads a prefix. Number('') is 0; parseInt('') is NaN. Use Number plus Number.isFinite.

nodes.label: Symbol implicit string coercion throws
nodes.rationale: '' + sym and template interpolation throw. String(sym) and toString work. Silent stringify would defeat uniqueness.

nodes.label: Symbol.for global registry
nodes.rationale: Process-wide lookup so independent modules share one symbol. Plain Symbol() is always unique.

nodes.label: Symbol unique property key
nodes.rationale: Symbol('id') === Symbol('id') is false. Hidden from keys/for-in/JSON.stringify but copied by spread and Object.assign. Not privacy.

nodes.label: Well-known symbols
nodes.rationale: Symbol.iterator drives for-of and spread. Also asyncIterator, toPrimitive, toStringTag, hasInstance.

nodes.label: Convert at the boundary
nodes.rationale: Form fields, query params, localStorage, dataset and env vars are always strings. Parse and validate once on the way in. Apply ?? before Number because Number(null) is 0.

nodes.label: reduce callback and initial value
nodes.rationale: callback(accumulator, currentValue, currentIndex, array). Second parameter of reduce is initialValue, so there is no thisArg.

nodes.label: Missing return in reduce callback
nodes.rationale: Most common reduce bug. Next accumulator is undefined; failure appears on the second iteration.

nodes.label: reduce without initialValue
nodes.rationale: First element becomes the accumulator; iteration starts at index 1; empty array throws TypeError; single element returns it with no callback call.

nodes.label: reduceRight
nodes.rationale: Same method from the end. Matters only when the operation is not associative (compose, string building).

nodes.label: Object.groupBy / Map.groupBy
nodes.rationale: Prefer Map.groupBy — any key type and insertion order. Replaces the hand-written grouping reduce.

nodes.label: Better-named methods than reduce
nodes.rationale: flat, Object.groupBy/Map.groupBy, flatMap, Array.from(new Set), find/some, filter. Grouping is the most common legitimate-looking misuse.

nodes.label: Array.prototype.reduce
nodes.rationale: Collapses an array into one value. MDN has a section on when not to use it. Mechanism is small; judgement is the hard part.

nodes.label: Always pass a reduce initial value
nodes.rationale: An empty array is the first render, a filtered-to-nothing list, an API with no rows. Initial value also declares the accumulator type.
nodes.norm_label: always pass a reduce initial value

nodes.label: reduce is a for...of loop
nodes.rationale: MDN equivalence: any reduce you cannot immediately rewrite as that loop should have been the loop.

nodes.label: pipe and asyncPipe via reduce
nodes.rationale: Fold over functions, not data. asyncPipe sequences promises with acc.then(fn). Genuine reduce: scalar fold or fold over functions.

nodes.label: Spreading the reduce accumulator is O(N²)
nodes.rationale: MDN anti-pattern: {...allNames, [name]: n} copies the whole object every iteration. Mutate the private accumulator or use for...of.
nodes.norm_label: spreading the reduce accumulator is o(n2)

nodes.label: node:24-alpine musl
nodes.rationale: Smaller, but native prebuilds often target glibc first and fail or rebuild on musl.

nodes.label: node:24-bookworm-slim
nodes.rationale: Default for most fullstack APIs: glibc addon compatibility plus multi-stage and non-root.

nodes.label: process.versions.napi 10
nodes.rationale: Node-API version supported on Node 24.19.0.

nodes.label: node-addon-api
nodes.rationale: C++ wrappers over Node-API for safer, more ergonomic addon code.

nodes.label: Node-API stable ABI
nodes.rationale: Sits between C/C++ and Node/V8 so addons are less tied to V8 churn across majors than NAN.

nodes.label: Native addon prebuilds
nodes.rationale: Users and CI may lack compilers; ship binaries per platform via prebuildify/prebuild.

nodes.label: C++ addon
nodes.rationale: A shared library Node loads into the process via require of a .node file.

nodes.label: Node embedder API
nodes.rationale: Opposite direction: your C++ binary hosts Node/V8. Not the path for typical HTTP services.

nodes.label: Foreign Function Interface
nodes.rationale: Call C ABI functions from JS via a binding library without writing a dedicated addon.

nodes.label: glibc vs musl for native addons
nodes.rationale: Pick slim/distroless/alpine from libc and ops needs, not from a blog title.
nodes.norm_label: glibc vs musl for native addons

nodes.label: Addon segfaults kill the process
nodes.rationale: Native memory corruption and signals abort outside JS try/catch.

nodes.label: FFI type declarations are load-bearing
nodes.rationale: A wrong struct layout or pointer lifetime is undefined behaviour at process level.

nodes.label: FFI vs Node-API addon
nodes.rationale: FFI trades build complexity for runtime binding risk; prefer a real addon for chatty or complex APIs.

nodes.label: Vertical vs horizontal scaling
nodes.rationale: One Node process uses one JS core well for concurrent I/O; extra cores need more processes.

nodes.label: Check phase
nodes.rationale: Runs setImmediate; immediately after poll, so I/O callbacks see setImmediate before the next timers lap.

nodes.label: Close callbacks phase
nodes.rationale: Last phase of a tick — socket/server close events run after check even if destroy was called first.

nodes.label: Event loop phases
nodes.rationale: One thread, six phases in fixed order: timers, pending, idle/prepare, poll, check, close.

nodes.label: setTimeout(0) vs setImmediate race from main
nodes.rationale: From the main module the order depends on startup vs timer threshold; inside an I/O callback setImmediate is first.
nodes.norm_label: settimeout(0) vs setimmediate race from main

nodes.label: Timers phase
nodes.rationale: Runs expired setTimeout/setInterval; delay is a minimum, not a promise.

nodes.label: process.getActiveResourcesInfo and unref
nodes.rationale: The process exits when no phase has work and nothing waits on I/O; unref excludes a handle from that count.

nodes.label: epoll / kqueue / IOCP idle wait
nodes.rationale: Thousands of idle sockets cost file descriptors and almost no CPU because they share one blocking kernel call.

nodes.label: libuv thread pool signals poll
nodes.rationale: File reads, dns.lookup, crypto.pbkdf2 and zlib finish on the pool then wake poll; sockets do not compete for the pool.

nodes.label: Poll phase
nodes.rationale: Run ready I/O callbacks, then decide whether to block and for how long. Where an idle server spends its life.

nodes.label: nextTick and microtasks are not phases
nodes.rationale: Drained between every phase and every individual callback, so phase order alone does not predict output.
nodes.norm_label: nexttick and microtasks are not phases

nodes.label: setTimeout delay is a floor
nodes.rationale: Poll blocks at most until the nearest timer, then the loop must reach the timers phase; slow callbacks push firing later.

nodes.label: Contributing to Node.js core
nodes.rationale: Large C++/JS monorepo with TSC governance and CITGM-scale impact; most product bugs are still in app code.

nodes.label: lib/ JS builtins vs src/ C++
nodes.norm_label: lib/ js builtins vs src/ c++

nodes.label: node:vm — and why it is not a security sandbox
nodes.norm_label: node:vm — and why it is not a security sandbox

nodes.label: WebAssembly in Node — CPU-bound work when it fits
nodes.norm_label: webassembly in node — cpu-bound work when it fits

nodes.label: V8 flags — what they actually control
nodes.norm_label: v8 flags — what they actually control

nodes.label: C++ addons and the embedder API
nodes.norm_label: c++ addons and the embedder api

nodes.label: FFI — calling native libraries without a full addon
nodes.norm_label: ffi — calling native libraries without a full addon

nodes.label: Custom module loaders and resolution hooks
nodes.norm_label: custom module loaders and resolution hooks

nodes.label: Failing test then fix
nodes.rationale: Small PR: failing test first, then fix; explain why; follow existing style.

nodes.label: Promise.allSettled
nodes.rationale: Never rejects. Returns {status, value|reason} per input. Use when partial success is meaningful.

nodes.label: Promise.any
nodes.rationale: Settles with the first to fulfil, ignoring rejections. Rejects only if all reject, with AggregateError.errors. Use for redundant sources.

nodes.label: .catch placement
nodes.rationale: Covers everything upstream, nothing downstream. Mid-chain recovers and the chain continues fulfilled; end-of-chain is a safety net.

nodes.label: error.cause
nodes.rationale: throw new HigherLevelError(msg, { cause: original }) keeps the root attached. Tooling prints the chain.

nodes.label: try/catch with await
nodes.rationale: A rejected promise that you await throws at the await. If there is no await, there is no catch — the try finishes synchronously.

nodes.label: AggregateError
nodes.rationale: Several failures, one reason is not enough. Promise.any throws one; use it for batches where the caller needs every failure.

nodes.label: Custom error class
nodes.rationale: Extend Error, set name and a stable code, carry structured context as properties, forward options so cause works. Keep the hierarchy shallow.

nodes.label: Catch only what you can handle
nodes.rationale: A giant try cannot say what failed. Recover, add context, or let the rest propagate to a boundary. Log-and-rethrow unchanged is usually noise.
nodes.norm_label: catch only what you can handle

nodes.label: Branch on err.code not err.message
nodes.rationale: Messages are prose — reworded, translated, interpolated. code is the contract. Node uses ENOENT. instanceof fails across dual package copies; code survives.

nodes.label: Never leak internals in error responses
nodes.rationale: Return a stable code plus requestId. Log the stack server-side. Never send SQL or stack traces to the client.
nodes.norm_label: never leak internals in error responses

nodes.label: return await inside try is not redundant
nodes.rationale: Without await the promise is returned before it settles, so the enclosing catch never runs. Everywhere else return await just adds microtask ticks.
nodes.norm_label: return await inside try is not redundant

nodes.label: CJS partial exports on cycle
nodes.rationale: Node returns the half-built module.exports. Assigned-before-require is visible; after is undefined.

nodes.label: ESM TDZ on cycle
nodes.rationale: Bindings exist but const/let values are in the TDZ. Loud ReferenceError instead of silent undefined.

nodes.label: cjs-module-lexer named exports
nodes.rationale: Static analysis of CJS source synthesises named exports; computed keys are invisible.

nodes.label: Dual package hazard
nodes.rationale: Separate CJS and ESM builds can load twice; module-scope state exists twice.

nodes.label: JSON import attribute
nodes.rationale: import data from './x.json' with { type: 'json' }. Prevents substituting executable JS.

nodes.label: require() of ESM
nodes.rationale: Stable in Node 24. Returns the namespace object; default is at .default. Fails on TLA.

nodes.label: CommonJS module wrapper
nodes.rationale: Node wraps each file in a function(exports, require, module, __filename, __dirname).

nodes.label: require.cache
nodes.rationale: A module runs once per resolved path. Core modules are not in the cache.

nodes.label: ESM live bindings
nodes.rationale: An import is a view onto the exporter's variable, read-only from the importer.

nodes.label: Top-level await
nodes.rationale: Importers wait for it transitively; it makes the module un-require()-able (ERR_REQUIRE_ASYNC_MODULE).

nodes.label: Conditional exports
nodes.rationale: First matching key wins. types first, default last.

nodes.label: ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED
nodes.rationale: Once exports exists it is exhaustive, including the real file path.

nodes.label: Subpath imports #internal
nodes.rationale: Private aliases inside the package. # prefix cannot collide with npm.

nodes.label: package.json type field
nodes.rationale: Nearest package.json decides .js parse mode. .mjs always ESM, .cjs always CJS.

nodes.label: enableCompileCache
nodes.rationale: Persists V8 compilation to disk. Call first, or set NODE_COMPILE_CACHE. Keyed by Node version and arch.

nodes.label: module.register hooks
nodes.rationale: resolve and load hooks on a separate thread. Register before the target is imported.

nodes.label: Prefix-only builtins
nodes.rationale: node:sea, node:sqlite, node:test, node:test/reporters have no bare alias; require('test') loads npm.

nodes.label: CommonJS require and the module cache
nodes.norm_label: commonjs require and the module cache

nodes.label: Extract shared module to break cycles
nodes.norm_label: extract shared module to break cycles

nodes.label: module.exports vs exports
nodes.rationale: exports is a local alias. Assigning to exports severs the link; require returns module.exports.

nodes.label: ESM requires file extensions
nodes.rationale: ESM does not probe .js / index.js. ./math and ./math.js are different requests.

nodes.label: CJS probes, ESM does not
nodes.rationale: CJS adds .js/.json/.node and index.js; ESM fails with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND or ERR_UNSUPPORTED_DIR_IMPORT.

nodes.label: Command injection
nodes.rationale: exec spawns a shell. Six syntaxes including a bare newline ran id. Escaping is a denylist of someone else's grammar.

nodes.label: execFile / spawn without a shell
nodes.rationale: Argument array, no shell: report.txt; id is one filename. shell:true concatenates and now emits DEP0190.

nodes.label: Identifier allowlist
nodes.rationale: select * from $1 is 42601. Dynamic sort columns must be checked against a Set you wrote, then interpolated.

nodes.label: NoSQL injection
nodes.rationale: Structural, not concatenated. {"password":{"$ne":null}} logged in as admin. Coerce with $eq:String(v) and validate body shape at the boundary.

nodes.label: SQL injection
nodes.rationale: Concatenated email plus x'; drop table sessions; -- dropped the table on the simple protocol. $1 returned 0 rows. Placeholders cannot be identifiers.

nodes.label: Block __proto__, constructor, prototype
nodes.rationale: All three keys, at every nesting level. JSON.parse reviver is a free place. Schema validation that strips unknown keys scales better than remembering each merge.

nodes.label: --disable-proto and freeze
nodes.rationale: --disable-proto=throw aborts the merge. Object.freeze prevents the write but is a silent no-op in sloppy CJS. Neither covers constructor.prototype. structuredClone does not sanitise.

nodes.label: Object.create(null) or Map
nodes.rationale: No prototype to pollute or inherit from. Map treats keys as values so __proto__ is just a string. Strongest structural defence.

nodes.label: Recursive merge pollution
nodes.rationale: Reading target['__proto__'] returns Object.prototype; the recursive write then assigns isAdmin onto it. Process-wide, persists until restart. constructor.prototype is the other door.

nodes.label: Never concatenate code and data
nodes.rationale: Every injection is data read as instructions. The fix is never escaping: send code and data on separate channels so the interpreter is told which is which.

nodes.label: Encode on output, not input
nodes.rationale: The same string is safe in one context and executable in another. Input filters guess every future context, miss one, and corrupt O'Brien.

nodes.label: JSON.parse is not the vulnerability
nodes.rationale: JSON.parse creates __proto__ as an ordinary own property and does not invoke the setter. Damage happens in the merge, config loader, or path-setter that walks it.

nodes.label: SET LOCAL lock_timeout
nodes.rationale: A 3 ms ALTER can outage a table: ACCESS EXCLUSIVE queues behind a long read and everything after queues behind it. 55P03 and retry is the good outcome.

nodes.label: ADD CONSTRAINT NOT VALID
nodes.rationale: Skips the validation scan (3 ms). VALIDATE CONSTRAINT later takes SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE so reads and writes continue.

nodes.label: Transactional DDL
nodes.rationale: CREATE ALTER DROP roll back like any statement. Most engines commit DDL implicitly. A created table vanished after a later 42P07 in the same transaction.

nodes.label: Adding NOT NULL safely
nodes.rationale: The obvious SET NOT NULL holds ACCESS EXCLUSIVE for a full scan. Do the long part under a weaker lock.

nodes.label: DROP CASCADE
nodes.rationale: Drops views, constraints, triggers that cannot exist without the object. Child table survives; only its FK is dropped, then orphans accumulate.

nodes.label: DROP RESTRICT default
nodes.rationale: 2BP01 dependent_objects_still_exist. The error NOTICE list is the cheapest inventory of dependents.

nodes.label: Gapless counter row
nodes.rationale: Invoice numbers cannot use a sequence. UPDATE counters SET n = n + 1 RETURNING n serialises every insert on that counter. Gapless and concurrent are mutually exclusive.

nodes.label: Sequence
nodes.rationale: Separate object whose state is deliberately outside the transaction. Every surprising sequence behaviour follows from that.

nodes.label: Sequence gaps
nodes.rationale: Four attempts produced ids 1 and 4. Required for concurrency: transactional nextval would serialise all inserts. CACHE and crash recovery also leave holes.

nodes.label: Atomic migrations
nodes.rationale: Nothing applied and nothing recorded stay consistent. Makes forward-only migrations practical. Still holds ACCESS EXCLUSIVE until commit.

nodes.label: Batched backfill
nodes.rationale: One UPDATE over millions of rows holds row locks, huge WAL, and VACUUM's cleanup horizon. Batches of a few thousand commit and stay interruptible.

nodes.label: NOT VALID then VALIDATE for NOT NULL
nodes.rationale: ADD CHECK (col IS NOT NULL) NOT VALID 3 ms; VALIDATE 25 ms under SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE. Direct SET NOT NULL 36 ms ACCESS EXCLUSIVE throughout. From PG12 SET NOT NULL can use the validated CHECK as proof.
nodes.norm_label: not valid then validate for not null

nodes.label: DROP CASCADE vs ON DELETE CASCADE
nodes.rationale: Same word, different mechanism. DROP CASCADE acts on schema dependencies; ON DELETE CASCADE acts on row references.
nodes.norm_label: drop cascade vs on delete cascade

nodes.label: RETURNING id over currval
nodes.rationale: currval is session state (55000 if unused). lastval() silently changes if a trigger consumes another sequence. RETURNING is unambiguous and one round trip.

nodes.label: JOIN plus DISTINCT costs 2.5x
nodes.rationale: HashAggregate at 189.98 ms vs Hash Semi Join at ~73–91 ms. The join materialises duplicates the semi join never produces. Gap grows with children per parent.

nodes.label: GROUP BY does not order
nodes.rationale: HashAggregate emits hash order. GroupAggregate happens to emit sorted. A report that ships without ORDER BY reshuffles when the planner switches.

nodes.label: GROUP BY without aggregate is DISTINCT
nodes.rationale: 54.49 ms vs 55.74 ms on 500000 rows, both HashAggregate. DISTINCT cannot HAVING-filter. Combining DISTINCT + GROUP BY is almost always undiagnosed fan-out.
nodes.norm_label: group by without aggregate is distinct

nodes.label: GroupAggregate
nodes.rationale: Sort by the key, then one pass. Needs sorted input. Output is grouped-key order. Over an ordered index scan it uses O(1) memory.

nodes.label: HashAggregate
nodes.rationale: Hash table, one entry per group. Memory scales with group count, not row count. Output is hash order. Chosen when groups fit in work_mem.

nodes.label: GroupAggregate over ordered index scan
nodes.rationale: At 64kB work_mem the index dropped 117.68 ms to 85.19 ms and buffers 3801 to 577. At default work_mem the index changed nothing. Heap Fetches: 0 is a true index-only scan.

nodes.label: Partial and Finalize aggregation
nodes.rationale: Workers produce combinable partials; leader merges. count/sum/min/max/avg combine. count(DISTINCT x) cannot. actual rows=166666.67 is average per loop.

nodes.label: count(1) is not faster than count(*)
nodes.rationale: 26.73 vs 28.35 ms, identical plans, buffers=3783. count(*) is 'no argument'; the executor counts tuples. Scan is the cost.
nodes.norm_label: count(1) is not faster than count(*)

nodes.label: count(DISTINCT) is not combinable
nodes.rationale: Two workers both seeing user 7 cannot combine partial counts without the values. Falls back to a single-threaded external merge sort. 208.87 ms, Disk 5880kB.

nodes.label: DISTINCT-subquery rewrite
nodes.rationale: count(*) FROM (SELECT DISTINCT user_id …) is a parallel HashAggregate. 208.87 ms → 57.61 ms, 3.6×, no spill.

nodes.label: Index flips the rewrite ranking
nodes.rationale: With a btree leading on the counted column, count(DISTINCT) becomes an index-only scan at 63.53 ms / 575 buffers and beats the rewrite's 76.21 ms sequential scan.

nodes.label: HAVING on an aggregate cannot be pushed
nodes.rationale: Filter sits on Finalize HashAggregate. Selectivity does not reduce work: keeping 0 of 5000 groups was no cheaper than keeping all. Same buffers=3783.
nodes.norm_label: having on an aggregate cannot be pushed

nodes.label: FILTER vs four scalar subqueries
nodes.rationale: FILTER 65.45 ms / 3783 buffers; CASE 65.14 ms / 3783; four subqueries 161.21 ms / 15132. Buffer ratio is exactly the number of scans.

nodes.label: Compare Buffers before milliseconds
nodes.rationale: Identical plans, shared hit=3783, 59.57 ms vs 83.22 ms. Clock said 40% worse; buffers said identical work. Scan dominates: 4 groups 58.59 ms vs 5000 groups 59.57 ms.

nodes.label: FILTER before OVER
nodes.rationale: count(*) FILTER (WHERE …) OVER (…). Reverse order is a syntax error. FILTER attaches only to aggregates, not row_number or rank.

nodes.label: PARTITION BY is GROUP BY that does not collapse
nodes.rationale: For each row PostgreSQL finds rows sharing the partition key, computes the aggregate, and attaches it to that row. OVER () is one partition of the whole result.
nodes.norm_label: partition by is group by that does not collapse

nodes.label: Running total via ORDER BY in OVER
nodes.rationale: ORDER BY inside OVER implies RANGE BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW, turning the aggregate cumulative. Inner ORDER BY changes values; outer ORDER BY only presentation.
nodes.norm_label: running total via order by in over

nodes.label: lag
nodes.rationale: lag(expr, offset=1, default=NULL) from a preceding row. Does not cross PARTITION BY. Without ORDER BY, previous means scan order. Non-constant offset is accepted and can yield all NULLs.

nodes.label: lead
nodes.rationale: Same arguments as lag, looking forward. Last row of each partition is NULL unless a default is supplied.

nodes.label: first_value
nodes.rationale: Returns expr from the first row of the frame. Correct under the default frame only because the frame starts at UNBOUNDED PRECEDING. Prefer it over last_value with reversed ORDER BY.

nodes.label: last_value default-frame trap
nodes.rationale: ORDER BY implies RANGE BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW, so last_value is the current row. Fix with ROWS … UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING, or first_value over the reverse order.

nodes.label: nth_value
nodes.rationale: 1-based index into the frame. With the default frame, nth_value(x, 2) is NULL until the frame contains two rows. No negative form — reverse the order.

nodes.label: OVER keeps the rows
nodes.rationale: Same aggregate, same numbers, different row count. GROUP BY collapses; OVER (PARTITION BY) attaches the group value to every original row.

nodes.label: Window functions
nodes.rationale: A window computes an aggregate without collapsing rows. That difference from GROUP BY makes running totals, percentages of total, and rank-within-group expressible.

nodes.label: Ranking functions
nodes.rationale: row_number, rank and dense_rank differ only in ties. ntile has an uneven-division rule that breaks equal-sized quartile claims.

nodes.label: lag and lead
nodes.rationale: Fetch a value a fixed number of rows away. Makes change-since-last-time a column. Counts rows, not days.

nodes.label: lag, lead, first_value, last_value
nodes.rationale: lag/lead count rows relative to the current row and ignore the frame. first_value/last_value/nth_value index the frame — which is why last_value famously returns the current row.

nodes.label: generate_series date spine before lag
nodes.rationale: lag returns the previous row. A missing day silently compares across the gap. Build a dense spine, LEFT JOIN, count(o.id) not count(*). Use nullif(lag(n), 0) for percent change.

nodes.label: Set subquery
nodes.rationale: Used with IN / ANY / EXISTS. Any number of rows. Runs once as a semi join when uncorrelated.

nodes.label: CUBE
nodes.rationale: CUBE (a, b) is every subset: ((a,b), (a), (b), ()). 2^n sets. Three columns is 8, four is 16. Measured 12 rows vs 9 ROLLUP vs 5 plain. Ask for the sets you need instead of reaching for CUBE.

nodes.label: Empty grouping set ()
nodes.rationale: Group by nothing — the grand-total row over the whole filtered table.

nodes.label: MixedAggregate
nodes.rationale: Plan node that maintains several hash tables from one pass. One Hash Key line per grouping set over a single Seq Scan.

nodes.label: ROLLUP
nodes.rationale: ROLLUP (a, b) expands to GROUPING SETS ((a,b), (a), ()) — drop columns from the right. Hierarchy shorthand. n+1 sets. Does not produce per-b totals. ROLLUP (a,b) GROUPING levels are 0, 1 and 3 — never 2.

nodes.label: GROUPING()
nodes.rationale: Returns 1 if that column was rolled up in this row, 0 if it is a real grouping value. Several columns yield a bit mask, MSB first. 42803 if the argument is not a grouping expression. The only reliable discriminator.

nodes.label: GROUPING SETS
nodes.rationale: Ask for several grouping levels in one statement. () is the empty set — the grand total. One scan feeding MixedAggregate, but grouping sets are not parallelised.

nodes.label: SQLSTATE / err.code
nodes.rationale: Branch on the five-character SQLSTATE, never on err.message. Messages are localised and version-dependent. Class 42 is always a bug (500), never a user 400. Socket failures are Node errnos, not SQLSTATEs. Test /^[0-9A-Z]{5}$/.

nodes.label: 23505 unique_violation
nodes.rationale: Map to HTTP 409. Match err.constraint, not just the code — a table can have several unique constraints. Insert-and-catch is the race-free check. 23505 fills constraint, not column; 23502 fills column.

nodes.label: NOT IN versus NOT EXISTS
nodes.rationale: Three spellings of one membership question. Negated IN returns nothing when a NULL appears, because of three-valued logic. NOT EXISTS does not have that trap.

nodes.label: Grouping sets are not parallelised
nodes.rationale: Like-for-like on the same three sets, cached 500k table: GROUPING SETS 293.67 ms vs three separate GROUP BYs 170.22 ms (0.58× — one scan loses). Plain GROUP BY got Gather Merge and two workers. One-pass wins when I/O dominates, not when CPU does.

nodes.label: Subtotal NULL versus data NULL
nodes.rationale: A rolled-up column is NULL; so is a genuine missing value. Measured two country:null rows, n=1 is_subtotal=0 versus n=7 is_subtotal=1. Invisible until a NULL exists in the data — same latent shape as the NOT IN trap. Label with CASE WHEN GROUPING=1 THEN ALL ELSE coalesce(col,'(none)').

nodes.label: err.detail leaks data
nodes.rationale: detail contains the offending value (Key (email)=(a@x.com) already exists). Returning it enables user enumeration. Log detail; return your own message keyed off code and constraint.

nodes.label: Retryable 40001 and 40P01
nodes.rationale: Serialization failure and deadlock are isolation doing its job. Retry the whole transaction with backoff and jitter, not the failed statement. Connection errors retryable for reads; writes only if idempotent.

nodes.label: bigint arrives as string
nodes.rationale: JS number is exact only to 2^53-1. int8 goes to 2^63-1. Auto-convert would silently corrupt. count(*) therefore returns '12'.

nodes.label: date and timestamp read in Node timezone
nodes.rationale: date becomes Date at local midnight; timestamp assumes local offset. Passes UTC CI and is wrong east of UTC. Keep date as a string.
nodes.norm_label: date and timestamp read in node timezone

nodes.label: numeric arrives as string
nodes.rationale: numeric is arbitrary precision; float rounding is unacceptable for money. Keep the string and use a decimal library.

nodes.label: PostgresInterval object
nodes.rationale: Months and days are not fixed durations, so there is no correct millisecond value. Use extract(epoch FROM …) for a number.

nodes.label: timestamptz as instant
nodes.rationale: timestamptz is a genuine instant and converts correctly. Prefer it for every moment in time.

nodes.label: Type OID parser key
nodes.rationale: fields[i].dataTypeID selects the parser. Array OIDs are distinct from element OIDs. Custom types get per-database OIDs.

nodes.label: pg type parsing
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL sends text; pg converts by column type OID. json/jsonb arrive parsed, arrays as arrays, bytea as Buffer, NULL as null.

nodes.label: Array types have their own OIDs
nodes.rationale: Changing 1700 (numeric) does not change 1231 (numeric[]). Override both or aggregated columns surprise you.
nodes.norm_label: array types have their own oids

nodes.label: Custom type OID lookup in pg_type
nodes.rationale: Enums, domains, composites get OIDs at creation. Look them up at startup; never hard-code.
nodes.norm_label: custom type oid lookup in pg_type

nodes.label: pg.types.setTypeParser
nodes.rationale: One process-wide registry. Affects every pool, query, and library using pg. Register once before opening the pool.

nodes.label: TypeOverrides per query
nodes.rationale: Scopes a parser to one query or one pool. Safe form when a single report needs numbers and the rest of the app does not.

nodes.label: Override date OID 1082 to string
nodes.rationale: The almost-always-right global override. A date is a calendar label; Date-at-local-midnight produces off-by-one days.

nodes.label: int8 parser Number vs BigInt
nodes.rationale: Number is silent-lossy above 2^53-1. BigInt is exact but contagious and JSON.stringify throws. Corpus default: cast per query.

nodes.label: SQL casts instead of global parsers
nodes.rationale: No global state, visible at the call site. Overflow raises rather than silently truncating.
nodes.norm_label: sql casts instead of global parsers

nodes.label: list with filtering, sorting and pagination
nodes.norm_label: list with filtering, sorting and pagination

nodes.label: Partial updates COALESCE vs built SET
nodes.norm_label: partial updates coalesce vs built set

nodes.label: SELECT FOR UPDATE inside a request
nodes.norm_label: select for update inside a request

nodes.label: Shaping the response in SQL vs JavaScript
nodes.norm_label: shaping the response in sql vs javascript

nodes.label: created_at and updated_at trigger or application
nodes.norm_label: created_at and updated_at trigger or application

nodes.label: Phase 9 CRUD patterns for a real API
nodes.norm_label: phase 9 crud patterns for a real api

nodes.label: $$typeof / react.transitional.element
nodes.rationale: A symbol so JSON.parse cannot inject a fake element — XSS mitigation.

nodes.label: React element
nodes.rationale: A frozen plain object describing desired UI. Creating one runs nothing.

nodes.label: React.createElement
nodes.rationale: Still exported in 19.2.8; the automatic runtime is a compiler change, not an API removal.

nodes.label: jsx vs jsxs
nodes.rationale: jsxs means children were written literally so React skips the key check; that is why a hand-written sibling list never asks for keys.

nodes.label: key is not a prop
nodes.rationale: key is the third jsx() argument; React 19 leaves a non-enumerable getter that warns and returns undefined.

nodes.label: ref is an ordinary prop
nodes.rationale: forwardRef is no longer needed for function components in React 19.

nodes.label: JSX falsy render rules
nodes.rationale: null, undefined, true and false render nothing; 0 and NaN stringify. That is why {items.length && <X/>} leaves a 0 on screen.

nodes.label: canary channel
nodes.rationale: Every passing commit, intended for frameworks that pin an exact build; applications should install latest.

nodes.label: Activity
nodes.rationale: Hide a subtree, keep its state, unmount its effects.

nodes.label: ViewTransition (experimental only)
nodes.rationale: Still not in the stable 19.2.8 package despite blog posts and talks; pages must never teach it as shippable.

nodes.label: React reading order
nodes.rationale: Do not skip Phase 3; do not start effects before the render cycle is solid; do not start RSC before Suspense.

nodes.label: filter-repo and LFS absent
nodes.rationale: switch, restore, sparse-checkout, worktree, maintenance, replay, backfill, last-modified, bundle, range-diff, filter-branch are builtins; filter-repo and lfs are ABSENT; scalar reports git version 2.55.0.

nodes.label: Blob header plus content hash
nodes.rationale: SHA-1 of blob 6\0hello\n is ce013625030ba8dba906f756967f9e9ca394464a and matches what git reports.

nodes.label: Empty blob hash e69de29
nodes.rationale: hash-object of an empty file is e69de29bb2d1d6434b8b29ae775ad8c2e48c5391; raw object header is blob.

nodes.label: git restore
nodes.rationale: git restore is a builtin; usage is git restore [<options>] [--source=<branch>] <file>...

nodes.label: git switch
nodes.rationale: git switch is a builtin and is no longer advertised as experimental; usage is git switch [<options>] [<branch>].

nodes.label: init.defaultBranch unset uses master
nodes.rationale: With init.defaultBranch unset, git init still names the first branch master and hints that Git 3.0 will change the default to main. HEAD points at refs/heads/master.

nodes.label: Default object hash SHA-1
nodes.rationale: Default object hash is sha1; sha256 is supported as an alternate object format.

nodes.label: Git porcelain surface
nodes.rationale: 46 main commands from git help -a first section; 172 commands on PATH.

nodes.label: Git ref storage backend
nodes.rationale: Default ref format is files; loose-ref layout is heads and tags.

nodes.label: reftable ref format
nodes.rationale: reftable is supported; on-disk tables.list shows a 0x000000000001-0x000000000001-5d9a0b8b.ref table.

nodes.label: Commit is a snapshot
nodes.rationale: A commit is a tree, parents, and metadata. Subdirectories are their own tree objects.

nodes.label: Git config layers and precedence
nodes.rationale: Local .git/config user.email is work@example.com. git -c user.email=once@example.com is scope command and wins for that invocation.

nodes.label: Four Git object types
nodes.rationale: blob, tree, commit, and tag. After the first commit: 3 blob, 1 commit, 2 tree. An annotated tag adds a tag object.

nodes.label: .git directory layout
nodes.rationale: COMMIT_EDITMSG, config, description, HEAD, hooks, index, info, logs, objects, refs. repositoryformatversion 0, filemode true, bare false, logallrefupdates true.

nodes.label: git hash-object
nodes.rationale: Nothing is stored until -w writes. Without -w, cat-file fails with could not get object info. After -w the object lives at .git/objects/ce/013625… and is type blob size 6.

nodes.label: Git index
nodes.rationale: The index is a real file with real blobs. ls-files --stage shows mode, blob SHA, stage, and path. file .git/index reports Git index, version 2.

nodes.label: Loose objects become a packfile
nodes.rationale: Before gc: 51 loose files, 204K. After git gc: 2 non-pack files, 36K, in-pack 51 across 2 packs totaling 6.03 KiB.

nodes.label: Refs and HEAD are plain files
nodes.rationale: .git/HEAD is ref: refs/heads/main. The branch file holds the same 40-character SHA that rev-parse HEAD and symbolic-ref HEAD report.
nodes.norm_label: refs and head are plain files

nodes.label: Staged and modified at once
nodes.rationale: Editing after add leaves the old content staged. Status AM means staged AND modified at the same time.

nodes.label: Git 2.55.0 environment probe
nodes.rationale: Measured porcelain surface, default branch, ref backend, object hash, pull-on-diverge, switch/restore, empty identity, and blob hashing on git 2.55.0.

nodes.label: Git object model probe
nodes.rationale: Walks content-addressed objects, the three trees, commits as snapshots, refs, packfiles, config layers, and plumbing-built commits.

nodes.label: Divergent pull requires reconcile
nodes.rationale: With pull.rebase unset, a bare git pull on diverged branches is fatal: Need to specify how to reconcile divergent branches. Options are pull.rebase false (merge), true (rebase), or pull.ff only.

nodes.label: Empty author identity failure
nodes.rationale: Why every setup guide starts with user.email: commit fails with Author identity unknown / Please tell me who you are until user.email and user.name are set.

nodes.label: Annotated tag object
nodes.rationale: An annotated tag is an object (object, type, tag, tagger, message). Lightweight tags are not objects.

nodes.label: A branch costs 41 bytes
nodes.rationale: git branch feature/pricing writes a 41-byte ref file. Object count is unchanged: a branch is a pointer, not a copy.

nodes.label: Commit graph is parents not timestamps
nodes.rationale: A commit dated 2030 is still the child of its parent. git log --reverse is ancestry order, not date order.
nodes.norm_label: commit graph is parents not timestamps

nodes.label: Content-addressed Git objects
nodes.rationale: An object is content addressed by the hash of header+content. The filename is nowhere in the hash: greeting.txt and copy-of-greeting.txt share ce013625030ba8dba906f756967f9e9ca394464a.

nodes.label: Plumbing vs porcelain commit
nodes.rationale: A commit built only from blob, tree, and commit plumbing is a real commit (45c50f3 Made with plumbing only) even when reachable from no branch.

nodes.label: Working tree, index, and HEAD
nodes.rationale: Git keeps three trees. ?? is working-tree only; A is in the index. git diff is working tree vs index; git diff --staged is index vs HEAD.

nodes.label: Phase 6 — REST surface and API features
nodes.norm_label: phase 6 — rest surface and api features

nodes.label: React Part 4 Building a real app
nodes.norm_label: react part 4 building a real app

nodes.label: ViewTransition still experimental
nodes.rationale: ViewTransition and gesture transitions are all over 2025–26 talks and still not in the stable package.

nodes.label: Event loop split
nodes.rationale: Language half (job queue, microtasks) is JS Phase 7; runtime half (libuv, setImmediate, nextTick) is Node Phase 2.

nodes.label: Do not skip Node Phase 0
nodes.rationale: Every Node is weird complaint traces back to skipping the runtime model.

nodes.label: React computes a UI description
nodes.rationale: A renderer applies it. Why react and react-dom are separate, why RSC can exist, why keys matter, why mutation never works.

nodes.label: Do not skip React Phase 3
nodes.rationale: Every React is weird complaint — stale values, state that didn't update, infinite loops — traces back to the render cycle.

nodes.label: Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty
nodes.rationale: Legacy own-only check looked up on the receiver, so Object.create(null) throws and a JSON hasOwnProperty key can lie.

nodes.label: hasOwnProperty.call fallback
nodes.rationale: Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(obj, prop) bypasses null-prototype and shadowing. Keep only for pre-ES2022 runtimes.

nodes.label: in operator
nodes.rationale: Walks the prototype chain, so user keys like constructor match Object.prototype. Throws TypeError on primitives, null, and undefined — unlike property access, in does not auto-box.

nodes.label: Object.hasOwn
nodes.rationale: ES2022 static own-only check. Works on null-prototype objects, immune to a shadowed hasOwnProperty, and coerces primitives instead of throwing.

nodes.label: Integer-index key definition
nodes.rationale: Only the canonical string of a non-negative integer. "-1", "01", "007", "1.5", and "1e2" sort with ordinary strings.

nodes.label: Three-tier property order
nodes.rationale: Integer indices ascending, then other strings by insertion, then symbols by insertion. Numeric-ID objects silently reorder; JSON.stringify follows the same rule.

nodes.label: Object.create(null) dictionary
nodes.rationale: No inherited keys and no __proto__ accessor to pollute. Cost: no toString/hasOwnProperty — string conversion throws; existence checks need Object.hasOwn. Prefer Map unless a plain-object shape is required.

nodes.label: Map
nodes.rationale: Any key type, insertion order for all keys, size, direct iteration, cheaper add/remove. NaN is a usable key via SameValueZero. JSON.stringify(map) is {}.

nodes.label: SameValueZero Map keys
nodes.rationale: Map key equality treats NaN as equal to NaN, so m.set(NaN,"ok"); m.get(NaN) works. Objects cannot have a NaN key.

nodes.label: Object.groupBy and Map.groupBy
nodes.rationale: Named replacement for the grouping fold. Map.groupBy usually beats Object.groupBy because object key order re-sorts integer-like keys.

nodes.label: reduce spread-accumulator anti-pattern
nodes.rationale: Spreading the accumulator each step is O(N²). The accumulator is private — mutating it is not an immutability violation. Prefer flat, Object.groupBy, Set, filter.

nodes.label: in for behaviour, hasOwn for data
nodes.rationale: Feature detection needs the chain (DOM methods live on prototypes). Dictionary keys from users must be own-only or constructor/toString become true.
nodes.norm_label: in for behaviour, hasown for data

nodes.label: Map when keys are data
nodes.rationale: Use a Map when keys are data; an object when keys are code. Tells: delete in a loop, Object.keys(o).length in a hot path, or Object.create(null) for user keys.

nodes.label: delete vs splice on arrays
nodes.rationale: delete leaves a hole and length unchanged; splice removes, closes the gap, decrements length.

nodes.label: Omitted splice deleteCount
nodes.rationale: splice(i) deletes from i to the end; splice(i, 0) inserts. Omitting deleteCount is not 0.

nodes.label: Array.prototype.splice
nodes.rationale: In-place remove/insert/replace. Returns the removed elements, not the array.

nodes.label: Array length writable property
nodes.rationale: Writable nonnegative integer < 2³². Shrinking truncates; growing creates holes. Not a count of values.

nodes.label: Sparse array holes
nodes.rationale: A hole is an absent index property, not stored undefined. From new Array(n), elision, length grow, or delete.

nodes.label: Three array index states
nodes.rationale: Present value, present undefined, or hole. Reading both last two is undefined; only in/hasOwn distinguish.

nodes.label: Array.of
nodes.rationale: Always treats arguments as elements, unlike new Array(n) which is a length.

nodes.label: Array constructor holes
nodes.rationale: One numeric argument is a length of holes; any other count is elements. new Array(n).map skips holes.

nodes.label: undefined and holes sort last
nodes.rationale: undefined then holes always go to the end; the comparator is never called for them.

nodes.label: String.prototype.substring
nodes.rationale: Negatives become 0; start>end swaps arguments and hides bugs.

nodes.label: for...in
nodes.rationale: Iterates keys including inherited. Almost never for arrays: string indices, non-index keys, skips holes.

nodes.label: splice in a forward loop
nodes.rationale: Removing at i shifts later items down so i++ skips the next. Filter or iterate backwards.

nodes.label: Mutation during iteration
nodes.rationale: Visit range is fixed first. Appends are skipped; removals skip the next item. Do not mutate the array being iterated.

nodes.label: Stream backpressure
nodes.rationale: write() returning false is the whole protocol. pipeline over pipe because pipe leaks descriptors.

nodes.label: Phase 2 Async and the event loop
nodes.norm_label: phase 2 async and the event loop

nodes.label: Log levels as a dial
nodes.rationale: Default production to info; fleet-wide debug fills disks and logging bills.

nodes.label: Structured logging
nodes.rationale: One JSON object per event with stable fields; the library is optional, the schema is not.

nodes.label: X-Forwarded-* headers
nodes.rationale: Only trust forwarded headers if the socket peer is the proxy; otherwise clients forge IPs.

nodes.label: What to log and what never to log
nodes.norm_label: what to log and what never to log

nodes.label: Metric cardinality
nodes.rationale: Never label by userId, orderId, full URL, or exception message; identity belongs in logs and traces.

nodes.label: Autoscale on lag not only CPU
nodes.rationale: CPU-only HPA misses I/O-bound APIs that are slow but idle on CPU.
nodes.norm_label: autoscale on lag not only cpu

nodes.label: High water marks and buffer tuning
nodes.norm_label: high water marks and buffer tuning

nodes.label: Per-chunk toString corruption
nodes.rationale: Chunk boundaries fall on byte offsets, so decoding each chunk independently substitutes U+FFFD for both halves of a multi-byte character.

nodes.label: stream.setEncoding
nodes.rationale: Installs a StringDecoder internally. Prefer this in application code; stay in buffers when bytes matter.

nodes.label: StringDecoder
nodes.rationale: Buffers a trailing incomplete UTF-8 sequence and prepends it to the next write so chunk.toString() cannot permanently replace a split character with U+FFFD.

nodes.label: decodeStrings
nodes.rationale: Default true converts written strings to Buffers before _transform. decodeStrings:false passes the original string through.

nodes.label: Transform is sequential
nodes.rationale: One chunk at a time preserves order and forbids in-transform parallelism. Use readable.map({concurrency}) or a bounded pool instead.

nodes.label: _flush
nodes.rationale: Runs after input ends and before downstream 'end'; the only place buffered tail state can be emitted.

nodes.label: Transform streams
nodes.rationale: Reusable pipeline middle: _transform and _flush. The hard part is that chunk boundaries do not respect data structure.

nodes.label: Transform callback contract
nodes.rationale: Call callback exactly once. Never calling hangs the pipeline; twice throws ERR_MULTIPLE_CALLBACK. callback(null,v) emits one chunk.

nodes.label: Chunk boundary problem
