nodes.rationale: A per-chunk regex misses a token that straddles the 64 KB mark. Verified: tok_live_ split across chunks was not redacted.

nodes.label: SplitLines framing
nodes.rationale: Hold everything after the last newline as a tail, push complete lines, emit remainder in _flush. Frame first, then operate on records.

nodes.label: Character vs token boundaries
nodes.rationale: StringDecoder fixes character boundaries only. A regex still misses a token split across chunks; that needs a framing Transform.

nodes.label: Async generator pipeline stage
nodes.rationale: Same backpressure and error propagation without the callback contract. Write a Transform class only for reuse, _writev, _destroy, or custom HWM.

nodes.label: _flush emits the last record
nodes.rationale: Files without a trailing newline drop the last record if _flush is omitted.

nodes.label: Brotli default quality 11
nodes.rationale: createBrotliCompress() with no options uses quality 11: 75.7 s on 19 MB vs 0.78 s for gzip 6. Intended for pre-compressed static assets.

nodes.label: zlib on libuv thread pool
nodes.rationale: Stream zlib runs on the 4-thread libuv pool shared with fs and dns.lookup. Four concurrent gzips match one; eight double wall time.

nodes.label: maxOutputLength zip-bomb cap
nodes.rationale: A few KB of gzip can expand 1000×+. Cap decompressed size; maxOutputLength throws ERR_BUFFER_TOO_LARGE.

nodes.label: node:zlib streams
nodes.rationale: gzip, deflate, and brotli as Transform streams so compression drops into a pipeline with constant memory.

nodes.label: fs/promises thread pool overlap
nodes.rationale: 200 async reads 45 ms with 23 timer ticks vs 200 sync 86 ms and 0 ticks. Unbounded Promise.all still hits EMFILE.

nodes.label: existsSync
nodes.rationale: Not deprecated (unlike fs.exists DEP0018). Fine at startup/CLI. Never a security check or request-handler guard.

nodes.label: TOCTOU
nodes.rationale: Time-of-check to time-of-use. exists then readFile can lose the file or have it swapped for a symlink. Do the operation and handle ENOENT.

nodes.label: Hidden sync I/O
nodes.rationale: require() inside a handler, existsSync, template engines loading with readFileSync, and console.log to a file are all sync.

nodes.label: Sync fs blocks the event loop
nodes.rationale: 200 readFileSync blocked a 1 ms timer for 86 ms with zero ticks. One thread runs all JS; a sync syscall owns it.
nodes.norm_label: sync fs blocks the event loop

nodes.label: Three fs flavors
nodes.rationale: Promise (default), callback (legacy), sync (startup only). Sync returns inline; promise on a microtask; callback in a later phase.

nodes.label: Compress in nginx or CDN
nodes.rationale: Keep CPU out of the event loop and thread pool. Compress in Node only for files you write, required upstreams, or no-proxy environments.

nodes.label: gzip level trade-off
nodes.rationale: Level 9 is 2.2× CPU of level 6 for 0.8% smaller. Level 1 is usually right for dynamic responses; 9 belongs in a build step.

nodes.label: When sync fs is correct
nodes.rationale: Before listen (config, certs), CLI/build scripts, a dedicated worker_thread, and crash handlers with no future event-loop turn.

nodes.label: SCHED_RR connection round-robin
nodes.rationale: Round-robin distributes accepts, not requests. Keep-alive pins many requests to one worker.

nodes.label: dns.lookup
nodes.rationale: Calls getaddrinfo on the libuv thread pool. Respects /etc/hosts and the OS cache. Used by http, https, net, and fetch.

nodes.label: DNS rebinding SSRF
nodes.rationale: Validate-then-connect resolves twice. Pin the checked address for the connection.

nodes.label: dns.resolve
nodes.rationale: Speaks DNS via c-ares as non-blocking network I/O. Ignores host files and the OS cache. Node itself caches neither.

nodes.label: TCP head-of-line blocking
nodes.rationale: HTTP/2 removes HTTP-layer HOL only. A lost TCP segment stalls every multiplexed stream, which is why HTTP/3 uses QUIC over UDP.

nodes.label: http.Agent
nodes.rationale: keepAlive has defaulted to true since Node 19. maxSockets is a concurrency limit disguised as a pool setting.

nodes.label: global fetch (undici)
nodes.rationale: Does not throw on 4xx/5xx. Rejects only when the exchange fails. Check res.ok. Implemented by bundled undici.

nodes.label: undici Dispatcher
nodes.rationale: Default dispatcher has no per-origin cap. Parallel fetch opens a socket per in-flight request. Node bundles undici but does not export it.

nodes.label: AbortSignal.timeout
nodes.rationale: fetch has no default timeout. The deadline covers the whole exchange including the body stream.

nodes.label: Timeouts shrink down the call graph
nodes.norm_label: timeouts shrink down the call graph

nodes.label: Mocking fetch
nodes.rationale: Fine for unit-testing response mapping. For headers, retries, timeouts or AbortSignal, use a real ephemeral server.

nodes.label: mock.method spy versus stub
nodes.rationale: Two arguments spies (original still runs); a third argument stubs. Spy when the real behaviour is harmless.

nodes.label: mock.timers
nodes.rationale: Mock timers and real I/O do not mix — faked setTimeout also fakes a query's internal timeouts. Enable only the APIs you need.

nodes.label: Fake
nodes.rationale: A second implementation that can drift. Keep it small and back it with one integration test against the real thing.

nodes.label: Mock (interaction double)
nodes.rationale: Assert on the call only when the call is the behaviour — payments, emails, webhooks. Not loggers or metrics.

nodes.label: Stub
nodes.rationale: Returns canned values; assert on the result of the code under test. The double you should reach for most often.

nodes.label: Mocking — mock.fn, mock.method and mock timers
nodes.norm_label: mocking — mock.fn, mock.method and mock timers

nodes.label: Test doubles — stub, spy, mock, fake
nodes.norm_label: test doubles — stub, spy, mock, fake

nodes.label: Over-mocking
nodes.rationale: Number of doubles equals number of collaborators. Seven doubles for one assertion is a design report: extract pure functions.

nodes.label: jsonb -> accessor
nodes.rationale: Returns jsonb so it chains. Use for every step except the last.

nodes.label: jsonb ->> accessor
nodes.rationale: Returns text and terminates the chain. ->> 'tags' renders the whole array as text, not an element.

nodes.label: jsonb #> / #>> path operators
nodes.rationale: Prefer #>> when the path is fixed and more than two levels, or built as a text[] parameter.

nodes.label: jsonb_typeof
nodes.rationale: ->> flattens 1 and "1" to the same text. Type distinction survives only via jsonb_typeof or jsonb comparison.

nodes.label: Missing key vs JSON null
nodes.rationale: ->> returns SQL NULL for both. Distinguish with ? (presence) or jsonb_typeof = 'null'.

nodes.label: jsonb @> containment
nodes.rationale: Asks whether the right-hand document appears inside the left. GIN can serve it; ->> = cannot. Measured 4.5ms Index Cond vs 35.4ms seq scan.

nodes.label: jsonb mutation operators
nodes.rationale: || is shallow; every mutation produces a new document so UPDATE rewrites the whole column.

nodes.label: jsonb_path_ops vs jsonb_ops
nodes.rationale: path_ops is smaller and faster for @> but has no entry for a bare key, so ?/?|/ ?& seq-scan.

nodes.label: jsonpath @? / @@
nodes.rationale: Comparisons and wildcards that containment cannot express. @? asks whether a path matches; @@ evaluates a boolean path.

nodes.label: jsonb ? key exists
nodes.rationale: True even when the value is JSON null. jsonb_path_ops cannot serve existence operators.

nodes.label: jsonb_to_recordset
nodes.rationale: One JSON parameter for any number of rows with types declared in AS. Convenient when the body is already JSON; unnest is generally faster.

nodes.label: GIN cannot serve ->> equality
nodes.rationale: A GIN index on a jsonb column indexes structure. doc->>'tag' = 't42' is a different expression and falls back to a filter.

nodes.label: generate_series
nodes.rationale: Gap filling: endpoints are inclusive (hourly over one day is 25 rows); descending needs a negative step; step 0 raises 22023.

nodes.label: LATERAL unnest
nodes.rationale: Explodes a per-row array by referencing the left-hand row.

nodes.label: ROWS FROM zip
nodes.rationale: Explicit lockstep zip of two SRFs in FROM; same padding as two SRFs in SELECT but readable.

nodes.label: Set-returning functions in FROM
nodes.rationale: An SRF returns rows, so it belongs in FROM where rows enter a query. In SELECT two SRFs lockstep-pad with NULL; in WHERE they raise 0A000.

nodes.label: unnest bulk-insert bridge
nodes.rationale: One array parameter per column keeps the bind count fixed. VALUES hits the 65535 protocol cap at 21845 three-column rows; unnest has no such ceiling.

nodes.label: WITH ORDINALITY
nodes.rationale: The only way to preserve array input order once values become rows. pos is bigint, which pg returns as text.

nodes.label: View predicate pushdown
nodes.rationale: Filter on a GROUP BY key: 0.8ms / 60 rows. Filter on the aggregate: 135.8ms / 300000-row seq scan — 170×. Aggregates, DISTINCT, windows, LIMIT, set ops are fences.

nodes.label: Automatically updatable view
nodes.rationale: One base table, no aggregate/DISTINCT/GROUP BY/window/set op. Otherwise 55000; needs INSTEAD OF.

nodes.label: View hard dependencies
nodes.rationale: 2BP01 on DROP COLUMN/TABLE a view uses. CREATE OR REPLACE can only append columns.

nodes.label: Views cannot take parameters
nodes.rationale: CREATE VIEW ... WHERE customer = $1 raises 42P02. Workaround: LANGUAGE sql STABLE SRF, or filter at the call site.

nodes.label: SQL views
nodes.rationale: A stored query, not stored data. pg_relation_size is 0. Substituted before planning so the planner sees one combined query.

nodes.label: WITH CHECK OPTION
nodes.rationale: Without it a write can insert a row that immediately vanishes from the view. With it: 44000 at insert time.

nodes.label: Backup retention window
nodes.rationale: Choose against how long a problem might go unnoticed. Slow corruption discovered weeks later defeats a 7-day window.

nodes.label: Disaster drill
nodes.rationale: An untested backup is a belief. A drill converts an unknown RTO into a known one.

nodes.label: Disaster runbook
nodes.rationale: Must live outside the systems it describes. Someone who did not write it must be able to follow it.

nodes.label: Point-in-time recovery
nodes.rationale: The most likely disaster is a bad migration or wrong DELETE. Replicas replicate the mistake; only PITR helps.

nodes.label: Recovery Time Objective
nodes.rationale: Measure detection, decision, fetch, restore, verify, repoint. Restore usually dominates — measured 4× dump time.

nodes.label: pg_dump and pg_restore
nodes.rationale: Logical backup from one consistent snapshot. Portable across majors and selective to a table. Restore measured at 4× dump time.

nodes.label: Restore rebuilds indexes
nodes.rationale: Indexes and constraints are separate manifest items. pg_restore -t can restore zero indexes including the PK.

nodes.label: Physical backup and PITR
nodes.rationale: Base backup + every WAL record since = land on any second. The base backup need not be filesystem-consistent; log replay repairs it.

nodes.label: recovery_target_action=pause
nodes.rationale: Default pause. Verify before promoting; timelines mean a wrong attempt can be repeated.

nodes.label: Stale read / read-your-writes
nodes.rationale: Looks like the save button didn't work — no error. Write committed on primary, not yet replayed on replica.

nodes.label: Streaming replication replicas
nodes.rationale: Consumer half only. Managed provider runs it; you get broken by stale reads and recovery conflicts.

nodes.label: sslmode=prefer default
nodes.rationale: libpq default; silently falls back to plaintext when the server stops offering TLS.

nodes.label: sslmode=require
nodes.rationale: Encrypts always but verifies nothing; stops sniffing not an active attacker.

nodes.label: TLS to the database
nodes.rationale: sslmode=require encrypts but verifies nothing. verify-full authenticates the server. Enforce TLS in pg_hba with hostnossl reject + hostssl.

nodes.label: Identifier folding to lower case
nodes.rationale: Unquoted identifiers are lower-cased before lookup; quoted ones are stored verbatim. Creating "UserAccounts" means every future reference must be quoted.

nodes.label: 63-byte identifier limit
nodes.rationale: max_identifier_length is 63 bytes, truncated silently with a notice. Two long names that differ only after byte 63 collide; non-ASCII hits the limit sooner.

nodes.label: Reserved word user
nodes.rationale: SELECT * FROM user resolves to current_user, not a table. Plural users and other plural table names dodge most reserved-word collisions.

nodes.label: snake_case naming convention
nodes.rationale: Use unquoted snake_case because that is what unquoted identifiers become. Plural tables, singular columns; constraint names follow PostgreSQL generated patterns.

nodes.label: First normal form
nodes.rationale: One value per column. Comma-separated product_names cannot be joined, indexed, or counted without parsing; fix with a child table.

nodes.label: Second normal form
nodes.rationale: No partial dependency on part of a composite key. product_name on order_items depends only on product_id, not (order_id, product_id).

nodes.label: Store every fact exactly once
nodes.rationale: Normalization is a checklist for finding duplicated facts. Duplication permits contradiction that concurrent writers can create and the database cannot resolve.

nodes.label: Third normal form
nodes.rationale: No dependency between non-key columns. customer_city belongs on customers, not orders. Test: every non-key column depends on the key, the whole key, and nothing but the key.

nodes.label: Composite primary keys
nodes.rationale: Natural fit for join tables: PRIMARY KEY (post_id, tag_id) is the uniqueness rule. Leading column serves one direction; the other needs its own index.

nodes.label: Composite key serves one direction
nodes.rationale: On 20k join rows, WHERE post_id used Index Only Scan; WHERE tag_id did Seq Scan. Almost always add a second index on the trailing column.

nodes.label: Join table becomes an entity
nodes.rationale: When the relationship carries role, joined_at, quantity it deserves a domain name (memberships). Add a surrogate only if something must reference the relationship.

nodes.label: Many-to-many join table
nodes.rationale: Join table with PRIMARY KEY (a_id, b_id). A surrogate id would permit the duplicate the composite key forbids.

nodes.label: Repository-layer snake_case to camelCase
nodes.rationale: Map once in the repository. Unquoted AS userId folds to userid, so per-query aliases need quotes and drift.

nodes.label: LEFT JOIN count(*) trap
nodes.rationale: count(*) counts the NULL-extended row (5 vs 4). Per group it turns no-orders into 1. Use count(child.pk) and coalesce(sum(...), 0).

nodes.label: Manufactured NULLs
nodes.rationale: Join-created NULLs are indistinguishable from stored ones. Test a NOT NULL column, normally the right table's primary key, to detect unmatched rows.

nodes.label: FROM ON then WHERE pipeline
nodes.rationale: FROM (including JOIN … ON) → WHERE → GROUP BY → HAVING → SELECT → ORDER BY. ON participates in matching; WHERE runs on finished join output. NULL = 'paid' is unknown and WHERE drops it.

nodes.label: count(DISTINCT) cost
nodes.rationale: Measured 3.6× slower than an equivalent rewrite and cannot go parallel. An index can flip which form is faster.

nodes.label: count variants
nodes.rationale: count(*) counts rows, count(col) counts non-NULL, count(DISTINCT col) counts distinct non-NULL. On the fixture 6, 5 and 2 over the same six rows. The wrong one is never a syntax error.

nodes.label: FILTER (WHERE)
nodes.rationale: Restricts the rows one aggregate sees without restricting the query. One scan can answer paid/open/cancelled counts. Not pure CASE sugar: they disagree about the empty set.

nodes.label: agg_orders fixture
nodes.rationale: Six orders and five customers for topics 01–08; ex37 then adds a NULL-FK order and a no-country customer so later topics see 8 orders. Same growing-fixture pattern as phase 5.

nodes.label: GROUP BY
nodes.rationale: Splits rows into groups and emits one row per group. Every select-list column must be a grouping key or an aggregate. HashAggregate vs GroupAggregate can flip 59 ms to 118 ms.

nodes.label: GROUPING()
nodes.rationale: Subtotal rows mark rolled-up columns with NULL, indistinguishable from a data NULL. GROUPING(col) returns 1 for the former and 0 for the latter.

nodes.label: GROUPING SETS
nodes.rationale: Several grouping levels in one statement. Not parallelised: three sets took 293.67 ms in one scan versus 170.22 ms as three parallel GROUP BYs.

nodes.label: ROLLUP and CUBE
nodes.rationale: ROLLUP (a,b) expands to ((a,b),(a),()) — n+1 sets. CUBE expands to every subset — 2^n. () is the grand total.

nodes.label: HAVING
nodes.rationale: Filters groups after aggregation. WHERE filters rows into groups. When the same predicate is legal in both, prefer WHERE; the planner can move some HAVING predicates and not others.

nodes.label: FILTER vs CASE empty set
nodes.rationale: sum(x) FILTER (…) returns NULL when nothing matches; sum(CASE … ELSE 0) returns 0. The empty-set NULL is inherited from ordinary aggregates.

nodes.label: HAVING on grouping columns rewritten to WHERE
nodes.rationale: A HAVING that references only grouping columns is constant per group, so the planner drops the extra grouping key and evaluates the predicate as a scan Filter. Measured plans were identical (55.08 ms vs 57.21 ms). The rewrite needs a non-volatile predicate.
nodes.norm_label: having on grouping columns rewritten to where

nodes.label: HAVING on an aggregate
nodes.rationale: Filter sits on Finalize HashAggregate because the value does not exist until every group row is read. Selectivity cannot reduce work: HAVING count(*) > 100 keeping 0 of 5000 groups was not cheaper than keeping all. Tune the input, not the HAVING.

nodes.label: Exact count capped at a ceiling
nodes.rationale: count(*) FROM (SELECT 1 … LIMIT 1000). Pays only when matches are plentiful (1.46 vs 33.85 ms at 125000). With 120 matches: 3.01 vs 3.02 ms — no saving, the scan still looks everywhere.
nodes.norm_label: exact count capped at a ceiling

nodes.label: Planner Plan Rows estimate
nodes.rationale: EXPLAIN (FORMAT JSON) Plan Rows: 125833 vs actual 125000 (0.7% high), zero row reads. Error is unbounded for correlated columns or stale stats. Label it approximate.

nodes.label: pg_class.reltuples
nodes.rationale: Approximate whole-table row count maintained by VACUUM/ANALYZE. Order of magnitude only; stale between maintenance.

nodes.label: count(*) OVER () plus page
nodes.rationale: WindowAgg must see every matching row before emitting the first, so LIMIT cannot stop early. 152.77 ms vs 48.83 ms for a separate count(*); plan showed WindowAgg actual rows=125000 feeding Limit 20.

nodes.label: Exact count(*) for pagination total
nodes.rationale: 48.83 ms against 2.11 ms for the page (~23×). Scales with matching rows while the page stays bounded by LIMIT. Count once when the filter changes, not on every page.

nodes.label: LIMIT pageSize + 1 has-more
nodes.rationale: 2.10 ms vs 2.11 ms for the plain page — free and exact. Slice the extra row before responding or the last page returns 21 items. Compose with keyset, not OFFSET.

nodes.label: = ANY($1::int[]) list parameter
nodes.rationale: One parameter regardless of list length; empty array matches nothing. Empty IN () is a syntax error. Stable statement text avoids re-planning per list size.

nodes.label: EXISTS / NOT EXISTS
nodes.rationale: Positive IN / = ANY / EXISTS all plan as a semi join and agreed at 4. Target list inside EXISTS is never evaluated — SELECT 1 is convention. Prefer EXISTS for nullable columns and all negations.

nodes.label: NOT IN NULL trap
nodes.rationale: x NOT IN (a, NULL) is x <> a AND x <> NULL. The last comparison is unknown, so every row fails. Measured: 1 row became 0 after one NULL elsewhere. NOT EXISTS is null-safe.

nodes.label: Row constructor comparison
nodes.rationale: (a, b) > (1, 5) is lexicographic: a > 1 OR (a = 1 AND b > 5), not AND of both. Correct spelling for keyset pagination. NULL in any component yields unknown.

nodes.label: HAVING count > 0 rewritten as EXISTS
nodes.rationale: count(...) > 0 forces a full count of every group. EXISTS stops at the first match and can use an index. Does not apply when the threshold is a real count (> 5).

nodes.label: HMAC-SHA256
nodes.rationale: SHA-2 is length-extendable, so hash(secret+message) is not a signature. HMAC's inner/outer construction closes that; compare tags with timingSafeEqual.

nodes.label: --allow-child-process escape
nodes.rationale: The child is a new process with no permission model, so granting it discards every other restriction.

nodes.label: Node Permission Model
nodes.rationale: Blast-radius reduction for your own dependencies, not a sandbox for untrusted code. Policy lives only on the CLI.

nodes.label: Prototype pollution
nodes.rationale: JSON.parse is inert; damage is a recursive merge that reads target['__proto__'] and writes onto Object.prototype.

nodes.label: npm allowScripts
nodes.rationale: npm 12 blocks install scripts unless listed in allowScripts; approval is a reviewable diff.

nodes.label: Login user enumeration
nodes.rationale: Skipping the password hash for unknown emails is an 83 ms oracle. Hash against a dummy with the same parameters.

nodes.label: extractable false CryptoKey
nodes.rationale: Key material can never be read back into JavaScript; node:crypto KeyObject has no equivalent.

nodes.label: KeyObject vs Buffer key
nodes.rationale: A Buffer is converted on every HMAC/cipher call; createSecretKey once at startup.

nodes.label: Resolve then verify containment
nodes.rationale: Compare against root + path.sep, not a bare prefix; startsWith(root) matches sibling uploads-evil.

nodes.label: path.join is not a security boundary
nodes.rationale: join normalises .. faithfully: path.join('/srv/app/uploads', '../../../etc/passwd') returns /etc/passwd.
nodes.norm_label: path.join is not a security boundary

nodes.label: Phase 0 load-bearing pages
nodes.rationale: Pages 01, 03, 04 and 07: What React is; Render/reconcile/commit; Reconciliation; StrictMode.

nodes.label: key among siblings
nodes.rationale: Stable, unique among siblings, derived from data. Index keys shift state onto the wrong items.

nodes.label: Reconciliation
nodes.rationale: O(n) because different types mean different trees and key identifies children. Unit is (position, type, key).

nodes.label: Reset state on purpose with key
nodes.rationale: ProfileEditor key={userId} so drafts do not leak across users.
nodes.norm_label: reset state on purpose with key

nodes.label: Reconcile phase
nodes.rationale: Diffs the new element tree against the current one. Part of render; can be thrown away.

nodes.label: Resetting state with key
nodes.rationale: The supported 'this is a different thing now'.

nodes.label: Confounded memo measurement
nodes.rationale: First render after swapping Cell for MemoCell remounts 400 rows (31 ms). Next update is 8 ms.

nodes.label: Components defined inside components remount
nodes.rationale: New function identity every render => new type => remount every keystroke.

nodes.label: Type change unmounts the subtree
nodes.rationale: Changing a parent div to span resets a grandchild. Extra nesting is also a new position.

nodes.label: Index keys do not remount
nodes.rationale: Measured: React keeps the nodes and rewrites their text. Missing-key warning is suppressed after the first offending list.

nodes.label: Nesting rule is type identity
nodes.rationale: Reconciliation compares component types by reference. HOCs, lazy() and memo() called in render are the same remount bug.

nodes.label: State belongs to a position
nodes.rationale: Together with snapshot and Object.is, this is why lists, keys and remounts behave as they do.

nodes.label: Boolean attributes
nodes.rationale: Known booleans: true emits empty attr, false removes it. disabled="false" is truthy. aria-* and data-* stringify.

nodes.label: className and htmlFor
nodes.rationale: class and for are reserved words. Raw class/for also reach the DOM since React 16, with a dev warning.

nodes.label: Four attribute outcomes
nodes.rationale: Renamed, passed through, dropped, or (in 19) class/for accepted with a warning.

nodes.label: null/undefined remove attributes
nodes.rationale: Idiomatic conditional omit: href={isExternal ? url : undefined}.

nodes.label: style must be an object
nodes.rationale: A string throws. The one attribute where pasted HTML fails loudly.

nodes.label: Unknown host props
nodes.rationale: String/number: lowercased with a warning. Boolean: dropped. on*: dropped as unknown event.

nodes.label: Controlled vs uncontrolled
nodes.rationale: Who owns the value, and why undefined decides it forever.

nodes.label: onclick is silently dropped
nodes.rationale: Unknown on* is parsed as an event and discarded. Production prints nothing. Highest-cost typo on the page.

nodes.label: Bottom-up effect order
nodes.rationale: Effects run children-first so a parent measuring a child finds mounted refs. ref.current is null during render because refs attach at commit.

nodes.label: Cannot update a component while rendering a different component
nodes.norm_label: cannot update a component while rendering a different component

nodes.label: Top-down depth-first render
nodes.rationale: A parent must finish before its children, because React cannot know the children until the parent returns them.

nodes.label: Two render triggers
nodes.rationale: Initial render, or a state update in the component or an ancestor. A prop change is a symptom of the parent rendering, not a trigger.

nodes.label: Cleanup contract
nodes.rationale: React runs setup and cleanup as many times as needed. The only correct effect is one where setup → cleanup → setup is indistinguishable from setup alone.

nodes.label: StrictMode door-lock extra cycle
nodes.rationale: React starts and stops the effect one extra time in development to verify cleanup is the inverse of setup, not to simulate a rare user journey.

nodes.label: One effect per synchronization process
nodes.rationale: One effect has one dependency array. Merging processes unions their deps, so each restarts for the other's reasons.

nodes.label: Reactive values
nodes.rationale: Props, state, and values declared inside the component are reactive. ref.current and location.pathname are not, because they live outside render data flow.

nodes.label: Effect start/stop lifecycle
nodes.rationale: Components mount, update, unmount. Effects only start and stop synchronizing. One mount can contain many start/stop cycles.

nodes.label: An effect has its own lifecycle
nodes.norm_label: an effect has its own lifecycle

nodes.label: void means ignore the return
nodes.rationale: Not undefined and not never. A void function returns undefined at runtime; void says the value is not part of the contract.

nodes.label: Functions returning values assign to void
nodes.rationale: A function returning something is assignable to () => void. Lets forEach(x => list.push(x)) compile. Trap: useEffect(() => fetchData()) returns a Promise as cleanup.
nodes.norm_label: functions returning values assign to void

nodes.label: Call signature
nodes.rationale: Object/interface form can carry properties (Express middleware). Arrow form is callable only. Multiple call signatures are overloads; first match wins.

nodes.label: Hybrid call/construct type
nodes.rationale: Call signature plus construct signature plus properties. Rare in new code; common in .d.ts for older JS (jQuery $).

nodes.label: Contextual typing of callbacks
nodes.rationale: When the target type is known, parameter types are inferred. Remove the annotation and they revert to implicit any (TS7006).

nodes.label: Default vs optional parameters
nodes.rationale: x?: string is string | undefined in the body. x = 'a' is optional for callers and string in the body. Default makes the emitted signature optional.

nodes.label: Fewer parameters is assignable
nodes.rationale: Ignoring an argument is safe; demanding one the caller never sends is not. Makes map(x => …) legal. Reverse: Target signature provides too few arguments.

nodes.label: Function types
nodes.rationale: A contract with a caller. Parameters must be annotated unless contextual; return types inferred but worth writing on exports.

nodes.label: Overload implementation is not callable
nodes.rationale: Only declared overloads are visible. Invalid calls report against the overload list. First matching overload wins; specific first. Prefer union/generic when return type does not depend on args.

nodes.label: TypeScript 13-phase syllabus
nodes.rationale: Phases 0–1 written (30 topics). Next is Phase 2 narrowing. Parts: type system, types at scale, in the stack, rigour and tooling.

nodes.label: TypeScript explanations hub
nodes.rationale: One page per syllabus topic; console blocks from sandbox/ts-p0 and siblings. Verified 2026-08 on TypeScript 7.0.2 and Node 24.19.0.

nodes.label: Phase 0 · How TypeScript runs
nodes.rationale: 13 pages on what the tool is, what it leaves behind, and which of the three programs that accept .ts actually reads types.

nodes.label: Phase 1 · The type vocabulary
nodes.rationale: 17 pages. Inferred types read from emitted .d.ts, not editor tooltips. sandbox/ts-p1/.

nodes.label: checkJs project-wide
nodes.rationale: "checkJs": true checks every .js. // @ts-nocheck opts a stubborn file out. Per-file @ts-check is the adoption path.

nodes.label: JSDoc type annotations
nodes.rationale: @param, @returns, @type, @typedef, @template, import('./x.js').T. Conditional/mapped types get unreadable — convert that file to .ts.

nodes.label: // @ts-check
nodes.rationale: First comment in a .js file turns the checker on. With allowJs, tsc --noEmit --checkJs reports TS2345 in a file Node still runs unchanged.

nodes.label: TypeScript is a checker, not a runtime
nodes.rationale: TypeScript reads code and complains. It is not a language the computer runs. By execution time every annotation is gone, like a comment.
nodes.norm_label: typescript is a checker, not a runtime

nodes.label: Seven flags under strict
nodes.rationale: noImplicitAny, strictNullChecks, strictPropertyInitialization, useUnknownInCatchVariables, strictFunctionTypes, strictBindCallApply, alwaysStrict.

nodes.label: Four sources of types
nodes.rationale: Inference, bundled .d.ts (types/exports), DefinitelyTyped @types/*, or a local ambient .d.ts. Plus lib for the ambient environment.

nodes.label: TS7016 missing declaration file
nodes.rationale: Module resolved; JS found; no description so the import would be any. noImplicitAny turns that silence into TS7016.

nodes.label: any turns checking off
nodes.rationale: Assignable to everything and from everything. Property access, call, and index all allowed and produce any. Spreads through inference with no error. Measured: two any lines produced zero diagnostics.

nodes.label: unknown requires narrowing
nodes.rationale: Everything assignable to unknown; unknown assignable to nothing except unknown and any. TS18046 / TS2322 until you prove what it is.

nodes.label: Types are promises, not runtime checks
nodes.rationale: No runtime type representation or check. An API, JSON.parse, or as can lie. That gap is Phase 9 — types at the boundary.
nodes.norm_label: types are promises, not runtime checks

nodes.label: Annotate boundaries, infer the interior
nodes.rationale: Annotate parameters and exported returns. Interior annotations add noise and can lose information (Record<string,number> drops known keys).

nodes.label: A declaration is a promise, not a check
nodes.rationale: Nothing verifies shout really takes a string. The compiler enforces your assertion. Get it wrong and it confidently enforces the wrong thing.
nodes.norm_label: a declaration is a promise, not a check

nodes.label: unknown at the door, never any
nodes.rationale: Correct type for every input you did not create. fetch JSON as unknown then schema.parse. JSON.parse returns any — assign to unknown and validate.
nodes.norm_label: unknown at the door, never any

nodes.label: Phase 6 Modules, declarations and the build
nodes.norm_label: phase 6 modules, declarations and the build

nodes.label: http.Server
nodes.rationale: Created by http.createServer(app) or app.listen. Owns port, SIGTERM, and server.close. Express does not own process signals.

nodes.label: http.Server, app, and Router object graph
nodes.rationale: http.Server owns the socket. app owns settings and the top-level stack. Router is a portable mountable stack. Only the server listens. Confusing them is how middleware never runs.
nodes.norm_label: http.server, app, and router object graph

nodes.label: Hang if no next and no response
nodes.rationale: If nothing calls next and nothing writes a response, the client hangs. next() after res.json yields Cannot set headers after they are sent.
nodes.norm_label: hang if no next and no response

nodes.label: next()
nodes.rationale: Each middleware sends and stops, calls next() to continue, or next(err) to jump to error middleware. Express will not auto-continue.

nodes.label: One JS thread
nodes.rationale: Express does not process two requests on two threads. Concurrency is async I/O, not multi-threaded handlers.

nodes.label: Express request lifecycle
nodes.rationale: Server accepts → app stack top to bottom → handler or 404 → or four-arg error middleware. No parallel Express event loop; it is Node's loop.

nodes.label: https.createServer(options, app)
nodes.rationale: app.listen is not enough for HTTPS. Prefer explicit createServer in production once TLS or multi-protocol shows up.

nodes.label: Phase 0 gate
nodes.rationale: Draw the object graph, point to where a request is lost if nobody calls next and nobody writes a response, and name what Express 5 broke about app.get('*').

nodes.label: AsyncLocalStorage for request id
nodes.rationale: Carry request id across async hops. Owned conceptually by Node Phase 10.

nodes.label: X-Request-Id middleware
nodes.rationale: Accept inbound x-request-id or crypto.randomUUID(). Set on req and response. Continue with AsyncLocalStorage. Accept inbound IDs for trace continuity across gateways.

nodes.label: app.param
nodes.rationale: Same idea at application scope. Prefer router scope to limit blast radius.

nodes.label: param callback runs once per cycle
nodes.rationale: Documented guarantee: called only once in a request-response cycle even if the parameter matches multiple routes. Load, 404, attach req.item.
nodes.norm_label: param callback runs once per cycle

nodes.label: router.param
nodes.rationale: Runs when a named param is present. Signature (req, res, next, value). Sugar for repeated preload — not an application architecture.

nodes.label: Express 5 async throw forwarding
nodes.rationale: On Express 5, throw inside async handlers and rejections are forwarded like next(err).

nodes.label: next(err)
nodes.rationale: Skips remaining non-error middleware and jumps to error handlers. Mount those last.

nodes.label: Four-argument error middleware
nodes.rationale: You must provide four arguments to identify it as error-handling middleware, even when next goes unused.

nodes.label: 404 handler
nodes.rationale: Goes at the very bottom of the stack below all other functions, just above errors. A 404 is not an error and never reaches the error handler.

nodes.label: entity.too.large
nodes.rationale: Express/body-parser type for an over-limit entity. Map it to a stable error body in error middleware.

nodes.label: entity.parse.failed
nodes.rationale: Typical status 400. Reaches the four-arg handler through next(err). strict:true is why only objects and arrays are accepted at the top level.

nodes.label: HTTP composition root
nodes.rationale: One place wires middleware, routes, and deps. createApp({mocks}) under Supertest covers happy plus 403 paths without a real DB.

nodes.label: Canonical Express skeleton
nodes.rationale: disable x-powered-by, json parser, routes, 404 (3-arg), error handler (4-arg). Keep one composition root instead of ad-hoc app.use across files.

nodes.label: Error middleware last
nodes.rationale: Error-handling middleware is defined last, after other app.use() and routes. If registered before routes, those routes never fall into it.

nodes.label: Body parsers early
nodes.rationale: Handlers and validators read req.body. If they run before express.json(), req.body is empty. Size limits also need to apply before business logic.

nodes.label: Stable parse-error envelope
nodes.rationale: Default handler writes err.stack in development. Map to {code:'BAD_JSON', message:'Invalid JSON body'} and log detail server-side with a request id.

nodes.label: Scope chain lookup
nodes.rationale: Walks outward and stops at the first match. Outer scopes cannot see inner bindings.

nodes.label: Shadowing
nodes.rationale: An inner binding hides an outer one for its scope and does not overwrite it. let cannot redeclare a parameter in the same function scope; var merges.

nodes.label: Behavioral hoisting
nodes.rationale: let/const/class create a dead zone above their line: the binding exists but is uninitialised.

nodes.label: Environment record
nodes.rationale: One per scope, chained to its parent. Hoisting is how that record is populated before its code runs.

nodes.label: Side-effect hoisting
nodes.rationale: import bindings are available early and the imported module's side effects run before the rest of the file.

nodes.label: Declaration closes the TDZ
nodes.rationale: let x; initialises to undefined and ends the zone. const without an initialiser is a parse-time SyntaxError.

nodes.label: Self-referential initializer
nodes.rationale: let x = x throws because the RHS is evaluated before initialisation. var y = y silently assigns undefined.

nodes.label: Temporal dead zone
nodes.rationale: From block entry until the let/const/class declaration initialises the binding. The slot exists but is empty; a read throws ReferenceError.

nodes.label: globalThis feature detect
nodes.rationale: globalThis.SomeGlobal !== undefined cannot hit a dead zone. typeof is only safe for genuinely undeclared names.

nodes.label: typeof throws in the TDZ
nodes.rationale: typeof still reads the binding. The 'undefined' special case applies only to names with no binding at all.

nodes.label: Two-step scope entry
nodes.rationale: Nothing is relocated. Scope entry first creates a binding for every declaration, then code runs. What differs is whether the slot is initialised.

nodes.label: TDZ is a feature
nodes.rationale: Fails at the wrong line instead of later; lets const guarantee one observable value; makes a shadow own its name for the whole block.

nodes.label: Getter and setter properties
nodes.rationale: Accessors look like data from outside but run functions. Spread and Object.assign invoke getters and store values, converting accessors to data.

nodes.label: Object.assign triggers setters
nodes.rationale: Object.assign mutates the target and runs its setters. Spread defines properties on a fresh Object.prototype object. Reach for spread by default.

nodes.label: Object spread own enumerable shallow
nodes.rationale: Spread copies own enumerable properties shallowly, excluding the prototype. Spreading a class instance drops methods. Later spreads win as a replace, not a deep merge.

nodes.label: Shallow copy
nodes.rationale: Top-level properties become independent; nested objects are shared by reference. Spread, Object.assign, slice and Array.from are all shallow.

nodes.label: Spread drops the prototype
nodes.rationale: Spreading a class instance yields fields with no methods. Map, Date, Set and RegExp keep data in internal slots, so { ...new Map(...) } is {}.

nodes.label: structuredClone silent losses
nodes.rationale: Drops the prototype chain, descriptors, getters/setters, private elements and RegExp.lastIndex. A frozen object comes back writable.

nodes.label: structuredClone
nodes.rationale: Built-in deep clone via the structured clone algorithm. Rebuilds cycles to point at the clone. Preserves Map, Set, Date, RegExp and typed arrays.

nodes.label: structuredClone transfer option
nodes.rationale: Moves transferable objects instead of copying them. The original ArrayBuffer is detached and byteLength becomes 0. Only use when nothing still reads the source.

nodes.label: Hand-written deep clone with WeakMap
nodes.rationale: Register the clone in a WeakMap before recursing so cycles terminate and shared identity is preserved. Handle Date, RegExp, Map and Set with their constructors. In production call structuredClone.

nodes.label: JSON round-trip clone
nodes.rationale: JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(x)) is still the most-written deep clone and is lossy in seven documented ways. Acceptable only when data is already JSON-shaped with no cycles.

nodes.label: Shallow vs deep copy
nodes.rationale: Copy is not one operation. Everything convenient is shallow. structuredClone is deep and loses types. JSON is deep and loses seven things. Pick by what you can afford to lose.

nodes.label: Inherited setters intercept writes
nodes.rationale: If the chain has a setter for that key, the setter runs and no own property is created. A read-only inherited property throws TypeError in strict mode instead of shadowing.

nodes.label: Copy the path you are changing
nodes.rationale: Idiomatic React/Redux updates share untouched branches. That identity sharing is what makes prev === next and memoisation work. Deep-cloning state defeats it.
nodes.norm_label: copy the path you are changing

nodes.label: Bearer tokens skip CSRF
nodes.rationale: Authorization Bearer tokens are not sent automatically by the browser, so classic CSRF does not apply.

nodes.label: CSRF on cookie session APIs
nodes.rationale: CSRF is a concern for a JSON API only when auth relies on cookies the browser sends automatically cross-site.

nodes.label: csurf is archived
nodes.rationale: Do not teach csurf as current; prefer double-submit cookie, SameSite, and Node Phase 8 guidance.

nodes.label: Request timeout soft deadline
nodes.rationale: Timeout middleware is a soft deadline at the Express edge; deep budgets stay in Node Phase 7.

nodes.label: 38 sections to 3 parts 9 phases
nodes.rationale: Early 2026-08-10 consolidation of a fragmented 38-section draft; later superseded by the 4-part 11-phase inventory.

nodes.label: Cookie read write asymmetry
nodes.rationale: res.cookie is built in; req.cookies needs cookie-parser. Without it cookies are undefined.

nodes.label: Quality cliff after Phase 3
nodes.rationale: 29 finished pages in Phases 0-3; Phases 6-10 are accurate outlines. Quality degrades monotonically, not bimodally.

nodes.label: Timeouts and secrets at the edge
nodes.norm_label: timeouts and secrets at the edge

nodes.label: Concept to Node middleware to Express
nodes.rationale: Concept lives in Node or DB/Redis/Docker/Nginx. Middleware, route surface, and HTTP contracts live in Express.
nodes.norm_label: concept to node middleware to express

nodes.label: Node vs Express technology boundaries
nodes.rationale: Async, streams, logging, retries stay in Node; drivers/models stay in DB syllabi; Redis owns cache/queues; Nginx/Docker own TLS and containers. Express owns middleware mounts and trust proxy.

nodes.label: Half the syllabus is HTTP API design
nodes.rationale: Node refused REST modeling, pagination, versioning, idempotency and ETags; they live on Express because the framework shapes the routes.
nodes.norm_label: half the syllabus is http api design

nodes.label: Hold Express 8-10 until Node 8
nodes.rationale: Preferred sequencing: write Express 0-7 now (Node Phase 5 only); hold 8-10 until Node Phase 8 validation and headers exist.

nodes.label: Errors signal
nodes.rationale: Rate of failed work (5xx ratio, failed jobs). Error ratio, not absolute count. Often only 5xx plus selected 4xx belong in the SLO.

nodes.label: Latency signal
nodes.rationale: How long successful and failed work takes. Histogram by status class. Average latency hides the long tail.

nodes.label: Traffic signal
nodes.rationale: Demand: requests/sec, jobs enqueued/sec, messages consumed/sec. Alert on sudden drop or spike vs baseline.

nodes.label: Counter, gauge, histogram, summary
nodes.rationale: Counters only go up (requests, errors). Gauges for lag, heap, pool wait. Histograms enable p50/p95/p99. Summaries are less common in modern setups.

nodes.label: Negative cache
nodes.rationale: Caching 'not found' without TTL, or caching 5xx, turns a transient failure into a long outage.

nodes.label: TTL and write-path invalidation
nodes.rationale: TTL bounds how wrong you can be; it is not the only invalidation. Delete or overwrite the key on write when updates must show sooner.

nodes.label: Four golden signals
nodes.rationale: From Google's SRE workbook. Latency, traffic, errors, and saturation tell you whether a service is healthy — everything else is a breakdown or a distraction.

nodes.label: Finding the bottleneck
nodes.rationale: The bottleneck is the resource that is full. Optimizing anything else is a hobby.

nodes.label: Caching strategy
nodes.rationale: A cache is a correctness trade: stale in exchange for not hitting the expensive path. If you cannot name the invalidation rule, you have a future incident.

nodes.label: Benchmarking
nodes.rationale: A benchmark answers a specific question under a specific load shape. A microbenchmark answers a different question with confidence it has not earned.

nodes.label: Startup time
nodes.rationale: Cold-start and deploy latency until readiness. Optimize when you scale to zero or restart often; ignore it on a long-lived API that starts once a week.

nodes.label: Phase 10 Observability and performance
nodes.rationale: Logs, traces, metrics, health, and the performance workflow that turns a 3 a.m. page into a measured change. Target Node 24.19.0.

nodes.label: Measure then change one thing
nodes.rationale: Reproduce with a number, check golden signals and loop lag, time dependencies, profile only if the loop or CPU is hot, change one thing, remeasure.

nodes.label: dependencies vs devDependencies vs peerDependencies
nodes.rationale: Runtime vs build/test vs host-supplied. Production installs with --omit=dev skip devDependencies.

nodes.label: Lockfile integrity hash
nodes.rationale: Makes the install verifiable, not just reproducible. A tampered tarball fails even if the version number matches.

nodes.label: package-lock.json
nodes.rationale: Records exact version, resolved URL and integrity hash for every package. package.json ranges do not describe what you are running.

nodes.label: npm ci
nodes.rationale: Installs the lockfile exactly, never writes it, deletes node_modules first, and fails if package.json and the lockfile disagree. Use in CI, Docker, production.

nodes.label: npm ci --omit=dev
nodes.rationale: What production installs. Getting dependencies vs devDependencies wrong fails only in production.

nodes.label: Erasable vs non-erasable syntax
nodes.rationale: Annotations, interface, generics, import type erase cleanly. enum, runtime namespace, and parameter properties must generate JavaScript.

nodes.label: ERR_UNSUPPORTED_TYPESCRIPT_SYNTAX
nodes.rationale: Thrown for TypeScript enum in strip-only mode. --experimental-transform-types works but drops the stability guarantee.

nodes.label: ERR_UNSUPPORTED_NODE_MODULES_TYPE_STRIPPING
nodes.rationale: Node refuses to strip types inside node_modules. Published packages should ship JavaScript plus .d.ts.

nodes.label: Node is not a type checker
nodes.rationale: Native execution removes the build, not the check. Dropping tsc --noEmit means type errors reach production.
nodes.norm_label: node is not a type checker

nodes.label: tsc --noEmit
nodes.rationale: Type checking stays a separate step in CI, editor, and pre-commit. Required in every situation even when the build is optional.

nodes.label: Type stripping
nodes.rationale: Node replaces type annotations with whitespace and runs the result. Enabled by default since v23.6.0; Stability 2 as of v24.12.0.

nodes.label: require(esm) stable in v24.15.0
nodes.rationale: Advice written before 2025 says CommonJS cannot load ES modules. On Node 24 it can.

nodes.label: Commit the lockfile
nodes.rationale: Always, including for libraries. It governs your CI; consumers' own lockfiles govern them. There is no downside and a real supply-chain upside.

nodes.label: stream.setEncoding
nodes.rationale: Installs a StringDecoder internally. After string mode you cannot recover exact bytes; size limits become character counts.

nodes.label: StringDecoder
nodes.rationale: Holds a partial trailing byte sequence and prepends it to the next write so multi-byte characters split on chunk boundaries survive.

nodes.label: A chunk is not a line
nodes.rationale: Default high water mark is 64 KB (raised from 16 KB in Node 22). Chunks split lines, JSON records and multi-byte characters arbitrarily.
nodes.norm_label: a chunk is not a line

nodes.label: Streams keep memory constant
nodes.rationale: Process data in chunks so peak memory is independent of input size. 216 MB log: 670 MB RSS buffered vs 88 MB streamed.

nodes.label: V8 MAX_STRING_LENGTH
nodes.rationale: 0x1fffffe8 characters (~512 MB). readFile utf8 or toString on a larger file throws ERR_STRING_TOO_LONG with no workaround except streaming.

nodes.label: readline createInterface
nodes.rationale: Line-oriented async iterable. crlfDelay: Infinity treats \r\n as one break so Windows files do not leave a stray \r.

nodes.label: SplitLines framing Transform
nodes.rationale: Holds everything after the last newline as #tail; _flush emits the remainder. Frame into records first, then operate on whole records.

nodes.label: gzip compression level
nodes.rationale: Default 6. Level 9 is 2.2× CPU for 0.8% smaller. Level 1 is half the CPU for 16% larger — usually right for dynamic responses.

nodes.label: Phase 3 Buffers and streams
nodes.rationale: Two ideas: a Buffer is raw bytes outside the V8 heap, and a stream keeps memory constant no matter how much data arrives. 19 pages, Node 24.19.0.

nodes.label: Phase 3 gate pipeline
nodes.rationale: Stream-process a file larger than RAM: read, SplitLines, redact, gzip level 1, write, with signal. Must explain write false, pipe leaks, and redaction without framing.

nodes.label: Character vs token boundaries
nodes.rationale: StringDecoder fixes character boundaries only. A regex still misses a token split across chunks — that needs a framing Transform.

nodes.label: When not to stream
nodes.rationale: If data is bounded and small, buffer it. Streaming costs error handling, backpressure, and forbids whole-value ops like JSON.parse.

nodes.label: Frame then match
nodes.rationale: One stage re-frames bytes into records; downstream transforms then work on complete records and become trivially correct.

nodes.label: Child process environment inheritance
nodes.rationale: spawn/exec/fork inherit the full environment by default. Pass an explicit env allowlist; helpers can dump process.env.

nodes.label: Node --env-file
nodes.rationale: No expansion, real env wins, missing file exits 9. Values never enter /proc/self/environ. Development convenience, not a secret manager.

nodes.label: Committed secret in git history
nodes.rationale: git rm plus .gitignore leaves history intact. Rotate first; history rewrite is optional cleanup that never reaches existing clones.

nodes.label: Secret rotation
nodes.rationale: Two values valid at once (kid), read at use not import, schedule so first rotation is not during an incident, expiry beats revocation.

nodes.label: Secret wrapper type
nodes.rationale: toString, toJSON and util.inspect.custom return [redacted]; only .expose() yields the value. Pair with logger key-name redaction.

nodes.label: extractable: false
nodes.rationale: node:crypto KeyObject can always be exported. A non-extractable CryptoKey still signs; exportKey throws InvalidAccessError. Containment node:crypto cannot express.

nodes.label: Envelope encryption
nodes.rationale: KEK wraps a per-row DEK stored beside ciphertext with v and kid. Rotating the KEK re-wraps DEKs and never re-encrypts data. Two keys valid during overlap.

nodes.label: Audit event schema
nodes.rationale: Actor+type, closed action vocabulary, target type+id, before/after, outcome including denials, requestId. Write next to the update, not in the controller.

nodes.label: HMAC hash chain
nodes.rationale: Each record HMACs canonical({payload, seq, prev}). Unkeyed sha256 lets an editor recompute the chain. Canonical key order is required.

nodes.label: Hash-chain truncation blindness
nodes.rationale: Deleting from the end leaves a shorter valid chain. Publish the head MAC to a system the app cannot rewrite; the anchoring period is the attacker window.

nodes.label: Secrets handling
nodes.rationale: Getting a secret into the process is configuration; keeping it from leaving is the hard part. Verified sandbox/p8-security/ex17-secrets.mjs.

nodes.label: Audit logging and tamper-evidence
nodes.rationale: Who did what to which record, when, and did it work. When Needed — privileged actions, regulated data, multi-tenant.

nodes.label: Append-only is a storage property
nodes.rationale: Opening with 'a' does not stop the same process truncating. Enforce with chattr +a, object-lock, or no UPDATE/DELETE for the app user.

nodes.label: CSPRNG APIs
nodes.rationale: Math.random is not for secrets. randomUUID 0.45 µs (122 bits); randomBytes(32) base64url for tokens. Async randomBytes for kilobyte-scale output.

nodes.label: HMAC vs length-extension
nodes.rationale: sha256(secret+msg) is length-extendable. HMAC closes it at 6.87 vs 3.68 µs. Compare tags with timingSafeEqual. HMAC proves key-holder, not which party.

nodes.label: KeyObject vs Buffer key
nodes.rationale: A raw Buffer is converted every call. createSecretKey once at startup: HMAC 9.41 vs 35.91 µs; GCM 13.07 vs 38.48 µs.

nodes.label: Modulo bias
nodes.rationale: byte % 100 is 40.7% bucket spread; crypto.randomInt(100) is 2.9%. Use randomInt for ranges, shuffles, numeric OTPs.

nodes.label: node:crypto primitives
nodes.rationale: crypto.hash for one-shot, createHash for streams. MD5 is slower than SHA-256 on this CPU (5.11 vs 3.68 µs). SHA-256 is not password storage.

nodes.label: Web Crypto SubtleCrypto
nodes.rationale: globalThis.crypto === crypto.webcrypto. Every subtle op returns a promise. verify() is constant-time inside the API. No MD5, no scrypt, no streaming.

nodes.label: AES-256-GCM AEAD
nodes.rationale: ECB leaks structure. CBC decrypts tampered data with no error and its padding is an oracle. GCM fails authentication on tamper. AAD binds context.

nodes.label: Ed25519 vs RSA-2048
nodes.rationale: Ed25519 for new work: keygen 0.4 vs 107 ms, sign 151 vs 998 µs, 64 vs 256-byte signatures. RSA verifies faster. HMAC when both sides share a secret.

nodes.label: GCM IV reuse
nodes.rationale: Same key+IV → same keystream; c1 XOR c2 XOR known plaintext recovers the other message. Random 96-bit IV per message, or a persisted never-reset counter.

nodes.label: node:crypto
nodes.rationale: About six calls from 52 hashes and 134 ciphers. Verified Node 24.19.0 / OpenSSL 3.5.7 via sandbox/p8-security/ex19-crypto.mjs.

nodes.label: Web Crypto API
nodes.rationale: Same primitives as node:crypto via the browser standard. Global, entirely async, stricter. Verified sandbox/p8-security/ex23-webcrypto.mjs.

nodes.label: Encryption, signing and key management
nodes.rationale: Most app code needs AES-256-GCM used correctly, plus the key management that makes rotation possible.

nodes.label: Web Crypto vs node:crypto choice
nodes.rationale: Shared with browser/Workers → Web Crypto. Server-only streaming or scrypt → node:crypto. Do not mix for one concern. HMAC ~5× slower (43 vs 8.85 µs).

nodes.label: EXPLAIN ANALYZE
nodes.rationale: Honest and costs you the query: ANALYZE executes the statement, including INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE, and does not roll it back.

nodes.label: EXPLAIN loops
nodes.rationale: actual time and rows are per loop; multiply by loops for the total. The single most misread part of a plan.

nodes.label: EXPLAIN
nodes.rationale: Free and lies a little: prints the chosen plan with estimates without running the query.

nodes.label: BUFFERS
nodes.rationale: The only plan measurement independent of cache state and machine load. Two plans 3× apart in time were 108× apart in buffer accesses.

nodes.label: Correlated-column estimate error
nodes.rationale: Planner multiplied two independent-looking filters and estimated 33080 against actual 100000; hunt the deepest node with the worst actual-to-estimated ratio.

nodes.label: shared hit vs shared read
nodes.rationale: hit is in shared_buffers; read is from OS cache or disk — PostgreSQL cannot distinguish those two. shared read is an upper bound on physical I/O.

nodes.label: pg_stat_statements.max and dealloc
nodes.rationale: Default 5000 distinct statements; unbounded IN-list shapes evict useful rows. Growing dealloc means raise max or fix query generation.

nodes.label: Literal normalisation in pg_stat_statements
nodes.rationale: Constants become $n so three literal variants collapse to one row; no parameter values are stored, which is why the view is safe to expose.

nodes.label: pg_stat_statements
nodes.rationale: Ranks by total time so a 4 ms query run 500 times beats an 87 ms query run twice. Requires shared_preload_libraries and a restart.

nodes.label: \timing
nodes.rationale: Measures the full client round trip — network, planning, execution, transfer and rendering — not server execution alone.

nodes.label: total_exec_time vs mean_exec_time
nodes.rationale: Mean flags rare heavyweight queries; total finds the frequent moderate ones that dominate the workload. Measured 9240 ms versus 173 ms.

nodes.label: \o /dev/null to discard rendering
nodes.rationale: A large SELECT * spends real time formatting an ASCII table; that time is in \timing and is not the database's fault.

nodes.label: Foreign key
nodes.rationale: The database refuses a row that points at nothing. Application check-then-insert cannot close the concurrency window.

nodes.label: NO ACTION vs RESTRICT
nodes.rationale: Difference appears only when deferred. NO ACTION can check at COMMIT; RESTRICT always fires immediately.

nodes.label: ON DELETE actions
nodes.rationale: NO ACTION 23503, RESTRICT 23001, CASCADE deletes children, SET NULL, SET DEFAULT. Map both error codes to HTTP 409.

nodes.label: Constraint SQLSTATE to HTTP map
nodes.rationale: 23502 not-null 422; 23503 FK 409; 23505 unique 409; 23514 check 422; 23001 restrict 409. Match err.constraint for field-level messages.

nodes.label: One-to-many
nodes.rationale: FK on the many side. NOT NULL makes it mandatory. Index the referencing column. Choose ON DELETE CASCADE or RESTRICT.

nodes.label: One-to-one
nodes.rationale: Make the FK the primary key. Without uniqueness it is one-to-many wearing a 1-1 name (second profile → 23505).

nodes.label: Self-referencing tree
nodes.rationale: parent_id nullable marks a root. ON DELETE CASCADE deletes whole subtrees. Arbitrary depth needs a recursive CTE.

nodes.label: Constraint names are an API
nodes.rationale: err.constraint turns 23505 + users_email_key into a field-level 409. Auto-generated names change on column rename; name them explicitly.

nodes.label: Third normal form
nodes.rationale: No dependency between non-key columns. customer_city belongs on customers, not orders, or a move leaves contradictory cities.

nodes.label: Circular foreign keys
nodes.rationale: DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED lets both inserts succeed; immediate fails 23503. Often a modelling smell versus a nullable FK plus is_primary.

nodes.label: Deferrable constraint
nodes.rationale: Checked at COMMIT. Applies to UNIQUE, PRIMARY KEY, EXCLUDE, FK. Not NULL and CHECK in practice cannot be deferred. Cannot serve as ON CONFLICT arbiter.

nodes.label: Index every FK referencing column
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL indexes the referenced side only. Unindexed child FK: parent delete 33.6 ms vs 8.7 ms indexed at 300k children.

nodes.label: DEFERRABLE INITIALLY IMMEDIATE
nodes.rationale: Fail fast by default; SET CONSTRAINTS … DEFERRED opts in. Preferred declaration so nothing pays until a transaction asks.

nodes.label: client.end vs release
nodes.rationale: end() closes a standalone Client. A client from pool.connect() gets release(). end() on a pooled client is a bug.

nodes.label: Dedicated Client for LISTEN
nodes.rationale: LISTEN is session state. pool.query returns the connection immediately so notifications are lost. Sending via pool is fine.

nodes.label: NOTIFY dedup within a transaction
nodes.rationale: Identical channel/payload pairs fold to one delivery. You cannot count notifications.

nodes.label: NOTIFY delivery on COMMIT
nodes.rationale: Nothing is delivered while the transaction is open. ROLLBACK discards them. Notify in the same transaction as the write.

nodes.label: LISTEN/NOTIFY from Node
nodes.rationale: Push to a connected client. Needs a dedicated Client, delivers on COMMIT, stores nothing. Treat as a hint, never a queue.

nodes.label: NOTIFY 8000-byte payload limit
nodes.rationale: Over 8000 bytes raises 22023. Send an id and let the listener fetch the row.

nodes.label: pg_notify function
nodes.rationale: NOTIFY channel and payload are syntax. pg_notify takes ordinary parameters so a dynamic payload is not concatenated.

nodes.label: TRUNCATE RESTART IDENTITY
nodes.rationale: Plain TRUNCATE left next id at 10001. Tests asserting id === 1 fail on the second run. Prefer not asserting on generated ids.

nodes.label: Resetting between test runs
nodes.rationale: Strategy sets suite speed. Timed on 10000 rows: DELETE 12.7 ms, TRUNCATE 4.4 ms, RESTART IDENTITY 4.7 ms, BEGIN/ROLLBACK 0.8 ms.

nodes.label: TRUNCATE for test reset
nodes.rationale: List every table in one statement, CASCADE for FKs, RESTART IDENTITY for sequences. Separate TRUNCATEs deadlock under parallel files.

nodes.label: NOTIFY plus queue table
nodes.rationale: No persistence, ack, or replay. Queue table is truth; NOTIFY only removes latency. Poll with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED.

nodes.label: Inject client into repositories
nodes.rationale: Module-level pool writes commit outside the test transaction and leak. Testability is why repositories take a client first.

nodes.label: Transaction rollback per test
nodes.rationale: 16x faster than TRUNCATE because seeds survive. Requires every query on the injected client. Cannot test commit-only behaviour.

nodes.label: useReducer is the named queue fold
nodes.norm_label: usereducer is the named queue fold

nodes.label: Three cases where updater form is required
nodes.norm_label: three cases where updater form is required

nodes.label: Four documented fetching-in-Effect downsides
nodes.rationale: No server run so HTML is a spinner; structural waterfalls; no preload or cache; enough boilerplate that most codebases ship the buggy version.

nodes.label: Framework fetching or a client cache
nodes.rationale: A framework can start the request before render. TanStack Query, useSWR and React Router 6.4+ address cache and ergonomics but still fetch after mount.
nodes.norm_label: framework fetching or a client cache

nodes.label: Network waterfall
nodes.rationale: A child cannot render until its parent has, and an effect cannot run until its component has rendered, so requests serialize along tree depth.

nodes.label: Move 4 — call a pure function prop during render
nodes.rationale: getOptions() must be safe during render. An impure function prop belongs in useEffectEvent instead.
nodes.norm_label: move 4 — call a pure function prop during render

nodes.label: useEffectEvent
nodes.rationale: Read the latest props and state from inside an effect without making them dependencies. The only sanctioned way to do that.

nodes.label: ref.current is not tracked
nodes.rationale: The ref object is stable; reading ref.current does not make the effect reactive. That is occasionally correct and also how people hide dependencies.

nodes.label: Ref guard anti-fix
nodes.rationale: hasRun hides the extra cycle but the resource survives unmount. The question is how to survive remounting, not how to run once.

nodes.label: Lift the state up instead of copying
nodes.rationale: If two components need the same value, ask which should own it, not how to copy it. One source of truth cannot disagree with itself.
nodes.norm_label: lift the state up instead of copying

nodes.label: Notifying the parent from an Effect runs too late
nodes.rationale: Child sets state, renders, then the effect notifies the parent — two commits. Both updates in one handler batch into one render.
nodes.norm_label: notifying the parent from an effect runs too late

nodes.label: Pass data down, do not push it up
nodes.rationale: A child pushing via onFetched breaks the one-directional walk that makes a wrong value traceable. Fetch in the parent and pass down.
nodes.norm_label: pass data down, do not push it up

nodes.label: Fetching on mount is the weak strategy
nodes.rationale: The four downsides apply to fetching after mount in any library. Effects are just the most direct way to express it.
nodes.norm_label: fetching on mount is the weak strategy

nodes.label: Race guards are not a cache
nodes.rationale: Neither ignore nor abort deduplicates, remembers a return visit, or starts the request earlier.
nodes.norm_label: race guards are not a cache

nodes.label: Ref used to hide a dependency
nodes.rationale: The same lie with no comment. The sanctioned way to read latest without reacting is useEffectEvent. Test: replace the ref with the value.
nodes.norm_label: ref used to hide a dependency

nodes.label: Multer multipart uploads
nodes.rationale: multipart/form-data is not JSON. Use Multer 2.x on Express 5. Cap size, allow-list MIME, treat the file as untrusted.

nodes.label: Body size limit
nodes.rationale: Treat limit as a production control. Different routes can use different limits via route-level parsers.

nodes.label: Never trust upload Content-Type
nodes.rationale: Clients lie. Prefer file-signature checks; generate your own object keys. Large files belong in object storage, not the API container disk.

nodes.label: globalThis
nodes.rationale: One spec name for the global object: window, self, or global. Measured globalThis === global on Node 24.

nodes.label: CJS bindings are not globals
nodes.rationale: require, __dirname and module are absent in ESM. Use import.meta.dirname, import.meta.filename and import.

nodes.label: Top-level this differs by host
nodes.rationale: undefined in ESM, module.exports in CJS, window in a classic script. Use globalThis for the global object.

nodes.label: 02 · Primitives are copied, objects are shared
nodes.norm_label: 02 · primitives are copied, objects are shared

nodes.label: Script top-level var as non-configurable global
nodes.rationale: In a classic script, top-level var becomes a non-configurable globalThis property. Modules do not do this.
nodes.norm_label: script top-level var as non-configurable global

nodes.label: Accidental global
nodes.rationale: Assigning to an undeclared name creates a global in sloppy mode and throws ReferenceError in strict/modules.

nodes.label: Module top level is not global
nodes.rationale: Top-level var is a global only in a classic script. ES modules and CommonJS keep it off globalThis.
nodes.norm_label: module top level is not global

nodes.label: new this binding
nodes.rationale: Create object, link Fn.prototype, call with this bound, return it unless the constructor returns another object. A returned primitive is ignored.

nodes.label: Class constructors require new
nodes.rationale: Calling without new is TypeError. A constructor function would silently assign to the wrong this.

nodes.label: [[Prototype]] vs Fn.prototype
nodes.rationale: [[Prototype]] is the lookup link on every object. Fn.prototype is an ordinary property used by new. Object.getPrototypeOf(Fn) is Function.prototype.

nodes.label: libuv thread pool
nodes.rationale: Four threads for files, DNS lookups, crypto and zlib. Sockets never touch them.

nodes.label: Buffer
nodes.rationale: Raw bytes outside the V8 heap. subarray shares memory; allocUnsafe can leak a previous request's data.

nodes.label: module.enableCompileCache()
nodes.rationale: Containers that wipe /tmp every start get no cross-restart benefit unless the cache directory is persisted.

nodes.label: Startup time — compile cache, snapshots, lazy requires
nodes.norm_label: startup time — compile cache, snapshots, lazy requires

nodes.label: Non-root container USER
nodes.rationale: CVE classes that write to the filesystem or load code become worse as root.

nodes.label: Node.js core contribution
nodes.rationale: Contribute when the bug is truly in core and you can provide tests — not to work around app bugs.

nodes.label: C++ addons and the embedder API
nodes.norm_label: c++ addons and the embedder api

nodes.label: return await inside try is not redundant
nodes.norm_label: return await inside try is not redundant

nodes.label: CORS
nodes.rationale: CORS is a browser rule, not access control. A Node fetch with a spoofed Origin reads the whole response.

nodes.label: pg_try_advisory_lock schedule lock
nodes.rationale: Must use a checked-out client. pool.query can reuse one session so both instances report true.

nodes.label: Queue-owned repeatable jobs
nodes.rationale: BullMQ upsertJobScheduler or a platform CronJob: one run across N workers, survives deploys.

nodes.label: setInterval is not a scheduler
nodes.rationale: It drifts, overlaps, runs once per process, and dies on restart.

nodes.label: Fixed window limiter
nodes.rationale: Boundary permits double the limit: 5/s allowed 10 requests in 80 ms.

nodes.label: public schema CREATE revoked in PG15
nodes.norm_label: public schema create revoked in pg15

nodes.label: interval calendar arithmetic
nodes.rationale: interval '1 month' equals interval '30 days' for comparison but addition uses the real calendar.

nodes.label: Metadata in Postgres bytes in object storage
nodes.rationale: Large uploads belong outside the database because backups, WAL, replication and memory all grow with the blobs.
nodes.norm_label: metadata in postgres bytes in object storage

nodes.label: application_name carries tenant
nodes.rationale: pg_stat_statements normalises tenant id as a parameter. Put tenant in application_name so pg_stat_activity and the slow-query log attribute work per tenant.

nodes.label: BYPASSRLS analytics role
nodes.rationale: Cross-tenant admin/billing queries need a dedicated BYPASSRLS role, not the table owner. Owner bypass is implicit and indistinguishable from an oversight.

nodes.label: Noisy neighbour in shared schema
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL has no intra-database isolation. Per-role timeouts, separate pools per tier, rate limits, reporting replica. Hybrid: long tail shared, whales dedicated.

nodes.label: length vs octet_length
nodes.rationale: 'héllo' is 5 characters and 6 bytes. varchar(n) counts characters; btree entries have a byte limit.

nodes.label: SQL strings are 1-indexed
nodes.rationale: substring('abcdef' FROM 2 FOR 3) is 'bcd'. FOR is a length, not an end position.

nodes.label: PostgreSQL string functions
nodes.rationale: Everyday set is case, trim, substring, split, pad, replace, and format. SQL strings are 1-indexed.

nodes.label: connectionString overwrites object fields
nodes.rationale: A URL plus database: 'postgres' still connects to the URL database, with no warning. Mix only pool-level options (max, timeouts, ssl object).

nodes.label: Three connection config sources
nodes.rationale: URL, config object, or libpq env vars (PGHOST, PGPORT, PGUSER, PGPASSWORD, PGDATABASE). They do not merge as expected.

nodes.label: sslmode=require is changing
nodes.rationale: pg 8.x treats require as verify-full (stricter than libpq). pg 9.0 will adopt libpq semantics and silently stop verifying. Write sslmode=verify-full now.

nodes.label: ADD COLUMN DEFAULT without rewrite
nodes.rationale: Since PG 11, ADD COLUMN NOT NULL DEFAULT stores the default as catalog metadata. relfilenode unchanged. Type changes generally rewrite.

nodes.label: ACCESS EXCLUSIVE
nodes.rationale: ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN takes AccessExclusiveLock. CREATE INDEX takes ShareLock (writes block, reads proceed). CONCURRENTLY permits writes.

nodes.label: Lock queue convoy
nodes.rationale: 12 ms ALTER behind a 3 s read blocked later SELECTs for 2.4 s. Locks grant in request order so strong lockers cannot starve. Pool exhausts as 'too many clients'.

nodes.label: Identifiers cannot be parameters
nodes.rationale: CREATE TABLE $1 raises 42601 at parse time. Dynamic identifiers need format('%I')/quote_ident/escapeIdentifier behind an allowlist.

nodes.label: Allowlist as a key-to-SQL map
nodes.rationale: Lookup of request keys to SQL you wrote, not validation. ORDER BY $1 binds as a constant and silently does nothing; concatenating an identifier can stacked-DROP.

nodes.label: Assembled list query
nodes.rationale: buildWhere + orderClause + LIMIT/OFFSET as last parameters. Clamp limit. Number() junk input; uncoerced 'abc' is 22P02.

nodes.label: lock_timeout vs statement_timeout
nodes.rationale: lock_timeout bounds lock wait (55P03). statement_timeout bounds execution; a waiter is not executing. Set lock_timeout per migration session.

nodes.label: SET LOCAL lock_timeout
nodes.rationale: SET LOCAL scopes to the transaction so it does not leak onto a pooled connection. 55P03 plus transactional DDL means retry is safe.

nodes.label: NOWAIT vs SKIP LOCKED
nodes.rationale: NOWAIT raises 55P03 immediately (409). SKIP LOCKED omits locked rows — right for job queues, wrong for point lookup (looks like not found). lock_timeout also 55P03, different message.

nodes.label: INSERT ... RETURNING
nodes.rationale: Generated id, DEFAULT now(), GENERATED columns and trigger-set values come back in one round trip. currval is session-scoped and unsafe through a pool.

nodes.label: Hard delete with RETURNING
nodes.rationale: rowCount 0 is 404, not an error. ON DELETE CASCADE fires. Missing-row delete is not thrown.

nodes.label: Name RETURNING columns
nodes.rationale: RETURNING * publishes whatever the table has, including a later password_hash. Name the mapper's columns. 201 + Location is the usual response.

nodes.label: Remap BEGIN/COMMIT to savepoints in tests
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL has no nested transactions. An inner COMMIT ends the test transaction; 1 row leaked. After remapping, 0 rows survived.
nodes.norm_label: remap begin/commit to savepoints in tests

nodes.label: 25P02 aborted transaction
nodes.rationale: After the first error every later statement is refused, including SELECT 1. COMMIT on an aborted transaction rolls back and reports success.

nodes.label: SAVEPOINT for an optional step
nodes.rationale: ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT rewinds to the savepoint, not the failing statement — both item inserts vanished including the one that succeeded. Thousands of savepoints overflow the 64-XID subtransaction cache.

nodes.label: this binding in class handlers
nodes.rationale: Extracted methods lose the receiver; class bodies are strict so this is undefined. Prefer class-field arrows.

nodes.label: Shallow Object.is comparison
nodes.rationale: New objects, arrays or inline functions make every check fail. You pay the comparison and never skip.

nodes.label: Inline render props defeat memoization
nodes.rationale: A new function each render makes PureComponent or memo always see a change. useCallback only if the child is memoized.

nodes.label: React 19 class API removals (string refs, legacy context)
nodes.norm_label: react 19 class api removals (string refs, legacy context)

nodes.label: ES6 default parameters fire only on undefined
nodes.norm_label: es6 default parameters fire only on undefined

nodes.label: Re-render blast radius moves up
nodes.rationale: A child re-renders because its parent did. Prop comparison is not the default path.

nodes.label: Start uncontrolled, control when needed
nodes.rationale: Control for coordination, persistence, validation, programmatic set or external data. Not in case.

nodes.label: Own state at the closest common parent
nodes.rationale: Every extra level adds a subtree. Push state down when only one branch reads it.
nodes.norm_label: own state at the closest common parent

nodes.label: Inverse data flow
nodes.rationale: Data down as props, changes up as function calls. The child does not know what the parent does with the event.

nodes.label: One-way data flow
nodes.rationale: Props down, events up. Only the owner can change a value, so debugging walks up to that useState.

nodes.label: Pass handlers not setters
nodes.rationale: A setter leaks the owner's shape. A named event callback survives array-to-Map or local-to-server.

nodes.label: Portal accessibility obligation
nodes.rationale: React provides none of focus move, trap, restore, Escape or inert background. Follow WAI-ARIA Modal practices.

nodes.label: dialog showModal top layer
nodes.rationale: Native top layer escapes stacking without moving the node and brings focus trap, Escape and inertness.

nodes.label: Portals escape CSS containment
nodes.rationale: overflow:hidden, stacking contexts and transformed fixed ancestors trap overlays. document.body sidesteps all three.

nodes.label: Phase 8 — Concurrent rendering, Suspense and transitions
nodes.norm_label: phase 8 — concurrent rendering, suspense and transitions

nodes.label: Phase 9 — Forms, Actions and optimistic UI
nodes.norm_label: phase 9 — forms, actions and optimistic ui

nodes.label: Concurrent, Suspense, Actions, and RSC are one idea
nodes.rationale: Concurrent rendering makes a render interruptible. Suspense turns unreadiness into a state. Actions build on transitions. Server Components exist because Suspense can stream.
nodes.norm_label: concurrent, suspense, actions, and rsc are one idea

nodes.label: abstract new construct signature
nodes.rationale: abstract new (...args: any[]) => T accepts abstract classes; a plain new signature rejects them. Needed for mixins and registries over bases.

nodes.label: Construct signature
nodes.rationale: new (id: string) => Widget types the constructor, not an instance. Generic factory: Ctor: new (id: string) => T.

nodes.label: typeof MyClass is the static side
nodes.rationale: Every class creates two types: C is the instance; typeof C is constructor plus statics. 'Property create does not exist on Repo' is this confusion.
nodes.norm_label: typeof myclass is the static side

nodes.label: Fail boot if required env missing
nodes.rationale: Validate env at boot, not on first request, so the process fails fast before taking traffic. Node 12-factor.
nodes.norm_label: fail boot if required env missing

nodes.label: Validated config module
nodes.rationale: Edge code only reads process.env via a validated config module.

nodes.label: Express 5 path-to-regexp break
nodes.rationale: app.get('*') and :id? throw on Express 5.2.1; SPA history fallback must use /*splat.

nodes.label: SPA history fallback /*splat
nodes.rationale: express.static plus history fallback; app.get('*') throws on Express 5.
