nodes.label: Validate at the HTTP boundary
nodes.rationale: Untrusted input never reaches services raw; the habit outlives any schema library. Master row.

nodes.label: Validate at boundary is Master
nodes.rationale: The habit outlives Zod; flip Zod schemas to Understand and promote the HTTP-boundary principle to Master.

nodes.label: Express over node:http
nodes.rationale: Express is a routing and middleware layer on http.Server, not a language and not an application architecture.

nodes.label: Middleware contract
nodes.rationale: next() vs next(err) vs never calling next: hang, double-send, or silent drop. Order is load-bearing.

nodes.label: Overloaded + concatenation
nodes.rationale: If either operand is a string after ToPrimitive, + concatenates. Other arithmetic operators coerce to number. Unary + throws on BigInt.

nodes.label: += inherits + overloading
nodes.rationale: One string operand turns an accumulator into text. Classic reduce bug when the seed is ''.

nodes.label: + string position changes the answer
nodes.rationale: 1+2+'3' is '33'; '1'+2+3 is '123'. Left-to-right; first string poisons the rest.

nodes.label: Parameter list TDZ
nodes.rationale: The parameter list is its own scope and initialises left to right. A default that reads a later parameter throws Cannot access before initialization.

nodes.label: Parameter scope is parent of body
nodes.rationale: Default initialisers run in the parameter scope, a parent of the body. Body functions and even var bindings are not visible; the error is X is not defined, not a TDZ access.
nodes.norm_label: parameter scope is parent of body

nodes.label: var shadowing a parameter
nodes.rationale: A var of the same name in the body is a separate binding. A closure created in a default captures the parameter, never the body's var.

nodes.label: String.prototype.substring
nodes.rationale: Treats negatives as 0 and swaps start > end, hiding bugs behind a plausible substring.

nodes.label: Use slice, not substring
nodes.rationale: slice matches Array.prototype.slice, supports negative indices, and returns empty when start > end so mistakes surface.

nodes.label: Map keys can be any value
nodes.rationale: Object keys stringify, so 1 collides with "1" and any two objects become [object Object]. Map compares object keys by identity.
nodes.norm_label: map keys can be any value

nodes.label: SameValueZero key equality
nodes.rationale: NaN equals NaN and 0 equals -0. Same algorithm as Set and Array.prototype.includes.

nodes.label: WeakMap
nodes.rationale: Holds keys weakly so entries die with the key object. A plain Map in that role is a memory leak. Not iterable, no size.

nodes.label: Array vs object destructuring
nodes.rationale: Arrays match by position, objects by name. Object rename syntax is key-left, binding-right — opposite an object literal.

nodes.label: Promise.all array destructuring
nodes.rationale: Positional binding is right when order is the call order. Reordering silently reassigns same-typed results.

nodes.label: for...of await vs Promise.all map
nodes.rationale: forEach(async) discards promises. Sequential for...of bounds load; Promise.all starts every request at once.

nodes.label: Array.prototype.forEach
nodes.rationale: Index is a number. Skips holes. Cannot break. Does not await.

nodes.label: return inside forEach
nodes.rationale: Returns from the callback like continue, not from the enclosing function. findUser always returns null.

nodes.label: Loop capability table
nodes.rationale: Need break, continue, enclosing return or await? forEach and array methods are out. Produce a value with map/filter/find.

nodes.label: Performance marks and measures
nodes.rationale: Named timestamps and the duration between them. Clear entries in long-running processes or the buffer grows.

nodes.label: performance.now monotonic clock
nodes.rationale: Monotonic high-resolution clock inside the process. Date.now can step on NTP adjustments and skew durations.

nodes.label: Staged request timings
nodes.rationale: Three spans (load, charge, save) beat a single 'checkout is slow' log. Sample or push the same boundaries as OTel spans under volume.

nodes.label: Git Part 2 Working with other people
nodes.norm_label: git part 2 working with other people

nodes.label: Default initial branch still master
nodes.rationale: On git 2.55.0 git init still defaults to master; the change is scheduled for Git 3.0.

nodes.label: Git Part 3 Git in a real project
nodes.norm_label: git part 3 git in a real project

nodes.label: Shared-checkout claims table
nodes.rationale: Sessions claim a language before writing so parallel work does not collide.

nodes.label: Git content-addressed object store
nodes.rationale: Git is a key-value database keyed by content hash plus refs. Explains snapshots, rebase hashes, and reset flags.

nodes.label: autocannon HTTP load
nodes.rationale: Right tool when the claim is about the running service: RPS plus p50/p95/p99, error rate, and server saturation under concurrency.

nodes.label: Microbenchmarks lie
nodes.rationale: V8 over-optimizes monomorphic toys, DCE can erase unused work, and a 3 ns win does not move p99 when the DB takes 40 ms.

nodes.label: Observe-result sink
nodes.rationale: Consume the microbench result into a sink the runtime cannot prove unused, or the work may vanish.

nodes.label: Writable stream
nodes.rationale: _write callback means done with this chunk. Forget it and the stream hangs with no error. end() is required for final/finish.

nodes.label: Custom Writable _write _writev _final
nodes.rationale: _writev receives the queued batch — one INSERT per drain instead of per row. _final flushes the partial batch; forget it and last rows vanish.

nodes.label: _write callback contract
nodes.rationale: Call callback exactly once on every path. Never calling it hangs forever; twice throws ERR_MULTIPLE_CALLBACK.

nodes.label: Dirent.parentPath
nodes.rationale: Replaced deprecated Dirent.path. Full path is path.join(parentPath, name).

nodes.label: opendir async iterator
nodes.rationale: Constant-memory walk; one directory handle per open level. Also the cheap empty-directory test.

nodes.label: readdir withFileTypes
nodes.rationale: Avoids one stat syscall per entry and the libuv thread-pool cost on large directories.

nodes.label: EMFILE too many open files
nodes.rationale: Per-process fd limit. Exhaustion fails every subsequent file and socket. ulimit varies by orders of magnitude.

nodes.label: FileHandle
nodes.rationale: Positional I/O, fh.stat on the descriptor, fh.sync, exclusive-create flags. GC does not reliably close it.

nodes.label: Close FileHandle in finally
nodes.rationale: Any throw between open and close leaks the descriptor for the process lifetime. close is idempotent.

nodes.label: os.availableParallelism
nodes.rationale: Respects CPU affinity but not CFS quota --cpus=0.5. Prefer over cpus().length, still clamp and configure.

nodes.label: process vs os memory and CPU
nodes.rationale: Alerts use process.memoryUsage and process.cpuUsage. os.totalmem and freemem describe a shared machine.
nodes.norm_label: process vs os memory and cpu

nodes.label: os reports host not cgroup
nodes.rationale: A 0.5-CPU pod on a 64-core node still sees 64 cpus and host RAM. Size pools from config.

nodes.label: int8 and numeric as strings
nodes.rationale: Neither fits JS number safely. Returning a float would corrupt money and large ids, so count(*) + 1 concatenates to "50001".

nodes.label: Driver types must not leak
nodes.rationale: One file owns SQL and mapping. Domain tests run without a database: four tests in 139 ms with a three-line fake.

nodes.label: SQLite integers throw above MAX_SAFE_INTEGER
nodes.rationale: ERR_OUT_OF_RANGE rather than silent rounding. setReadBigInts(true) returns BigInt.

nodes.label: Jest native ESM friction
nodes.rationale: Needs NODE_OPTIONS=--experimental-vm-modules plus transform: {}. Without them: SyntaxError Cannot use import statement outside a module. Hardest of the three to justify on a new ESM project.

nodes.label: Vitest
nodes.rationale: Earns its place for a shared frontend runner, DOM (jsdom/happy-dom), expect/vi.mock, interactive UI, and first-class TypeScript.

nodes.label: node:test as default backend runner
nodes.rationale: describe/it, hooks, mocks, timers, coverage, snapshots, watch, sharding, JUnit with zero dependencies. Startup ~6× faster than Vitest or Jest.

nodes.label: t.assert.snapshot()
nodes.rationale: Records output and fails when it changes. First run needs --test-update-snapshots. Commit the .snapshot file — it is the expected value.

nodes.label: Snapshot normalization
nodes.rationale: Scrub ids and timestamps, sort collections, or inject a clock and id generator. Multiple snapshot() calls in one test are keyed by call order — prefer one per test.

nodes.label: Blind --test-update-snapshots trap
nodes.rationale: Measured: after changing the renderer the flag rewrote the file and reported ✔ with zero failures. The regression became the new expectation. Run without the flag first; review the diff.

nodes.label: autocannon
nodes.rationale: Quick single-URL answer: connections, duration, warmup. Scriptable enough to assert p99 and non2xx. Run against a production-like build.

nodes.label: k6
nodes.rationale: When the shape of load matters: ramps, user journeys, think time. thresholds make it exit non-zero so CI can gate. Failures cluster at transitions.

nodes.label: Stress, soak, and spike tests
nodes.rationale: Stress increases until break. Soak is moderate load for hours (leaks, pool exhaustion). Spike is instant 10× for autoscaling and cold starts. Nightly against staging, not in the PR pipeline.

nodes.label: Baseline widely / newly / limited
nodes.rationale: Widely = all core browsers for 30 months (just use). Newly = all core browsers now (use, fallback if conservative). Limited = at least one missing (enhancement only, always guarded).

nodes.label: web-features Baseline dataset
nodes.rationale: npm package behind MDN/web.dev badges (1186 features in 3.34.3). status.baseline is high|low|false. Checkable in CI; :has, nesting, layers Widely since 2023.

nodes.label: CSS.supports and style round-trip
nodes.rationale: The only APIs that volunteer validity: CSS.supports(property, value), or assign to element.style and read back — empty string means rejected.

nodes.label: CSS fails silently
nodes.rationale: A mistake is discarded with no console message, exception, or build failure. A typo and a future feature are indistinguishable to the engine.

nodes.label: @supports tests parse not correctness
nodes.rationale: An engine can parse a property, apply it partially, and pass. Cannot test at-rules directly — test a declaration that implies them, e.g. container-type: inline-size.

nodes.label: @supports feature queries
nodes.rationale: Asks the engine whether it can parse a declaration or selector, then styles accordingly. Parentheses required; selectors need selector().

nodes.label: Vendor prefixes in 2026
nodes.rationale: Mostly history. New features ship behind flags. Exceptions: -webkit-line-clamp still required; -webkit-backdrop-filter for Safari. Manage the rest with Autoprefixer/Lightning CSS.

nodes.label: -webkit-line-clamp still required
nodes.rationale: Unprefixed line-clamp is false in Firefox 153; -webkit-line-clamp is true. Full incantation still needs display:-webkit-box and -webkit-box-orient:vertical.

nodes.label: Local support is not shipping safety
nodes.rationale: Firefox 153 supports anchor-positioning and accent-color (both Limited). One engine's CSS.supports true is how Limited features reach production broken.
nodes.norm_label: local support is not shipping safety

nodes.label: Silent drop enables forward compatibility
nodes.rationale: If unknown syntax were fatal, no new CSS feature could ship without breaking older browsers. Progressive enhancement depends on this generosity.

nodes.label: Cascade-safe fallback without @supports
nodes.rationale: Declare the fallback value first and the modern value second. Engines that cannot parse the second keep the first. Use @supports only when the fallback needs different properties.

nodes.label: A -webkit- prefix is not a browser detector
nodes.rationale: Firefox implements -webkit-user-select, -webkit-box-shadow, -webkit-appearance for compatibility. Authors shipped WebKit-only CSS; prefixes as detectors failed.
nodes.norm_label: a -webkit- prefix is not a browser detector

nodes.label: Contract test
nodes.rationale: Tests the agreement between sides, not each side's beliefs. A createdAt rename failed the provider suite in 18 ms: expected string, received undefined.

nodes.label: Schema compatibility — breaking vs non-breaking
nodes.rationale: Verified 2026-08 on Node 24.19.0 with zod 4.4.3. Mechanical answer to is this change breaking.

nodes.label: Consumer-owned contract
nodes.rationale: Only the consumer knows which fields it reads. A provider-written contract describes the implementation and grows to cover everything, so it stops constraining anything.

nodes.label: Phase 4 — Filesystem, paths, and URLs
nodes.rationale: fs/promises default. Path traversal as a security bug. Large payloads streamed to a sink with size limits and cleanup on every exit path.

nodes.label: Phase 7 — Background work and resilience
nodes.rationale: Framework-free. Job idempotency, transactional outbox, timeout budgets, retry only safe failures, exponential backoff with jitter, concurrency limiting.

nodes.label: What PostgreSQL is
nodes.rationale: Understand-tier. PostgreSQL is a free open-source object-relational database server, not a library, not a document store, not SQL syntax alone.

nodes.label: PostgreSQL explanation pages
nodes.rationale: Target PostgreSQL 18.4 · Node 24 · pg. Phase 0–1 executed against the sandbox; remaining pages follow measured conventions.

nodes.label: PostgreSQL syllabus
nodes.rationale: 14 phases, 233 topics in 4 parts. Relational model, SQL, planner, concurrency, ops, plus Node-side raw pg. Verified 2026-08 against PostgreSQL 18.4.

nodes.label: Extension available vs installed
nodes.rationale: Available = files on disk (60 in postgres:18-alpine). Installed = CREATE EXTENSION in this database. pg_available_extensions vs pg_extension.

nodes.label: Extensions are per database not per cluster
nodes.rationale: CREATE DATABASE does not copy extensions. digest() works in one database and raises 42883 in another on the same server.
nodes.norm_label: extensions are per database not per cluster

nodes.label: pgvector is not in the stock image
nodes.rationale: Absent from postgres:18-alpine, not merely uninstalled. Needs pgvector/pgvector:pg18 or a provider that ships it.
nodes.norm_label: pgvector is not in the stock image

nodes.label: jsonb_to_recordset
nodes.rationale: One parameter for any number of rows when the body is already JSON. Column types declared in the AS list. unnest is generally faster.

nodes.label: unnest bulk-insert bridge
nodes.rationale: 5000 rows through 3 parameters. VALUES needs 15000 and caps at 21845 rows because the protocol allows 65535 parameters. Mismatched arrays pad with NULL.

nodes.label: WITH ORDINALITY
nodes.rationale: The only way to preserve array input order once values become rows. pos is bigint; pg returns it as text.

nodes.label: DEFAULT partition safety net
nodes.rationale: No matching range without DEFAULT raises 23514. Attaching a new range that overlaps the default scans it under ACCESS EXCLUSIVE.

nodes.label: Partition pruning
nodes.rationale: With the key in WHERE: 15.6 ms one partition. Without: 32.9 ms Parallel Append of all five — about 2× not 5×. An index would have done more.

nodes.label: RANGE LIST HASH partitioning
nodes.rationale: RANGE for time series, LIST for tenant/region/status, HASH to spread writes. Parent holds no rows.

nodes.label: CALL vs SELECT for procedures
nodes.rationale: SELECT a procedure raises 42809. Procedures return no rows and cannot appear in a query.

nodes.label: Procedure can COMMIT mid-body
nodes.rationale: The same COMMIT inside a FUNCTION raises 2D000. A function runs inside the caller's transaction and may not end it.

nodes.label: Procedure transaction control only when outermost
nodes.rationale: CALL inside an explicit BEGIN raises 2D000. Inside an application withTransaction wrapper a procedure behaves like a function.
nodes.norm_label: procedure transaction control only when outermost

nodes.label: Schema USAGE before table verbs
nodes.rationale: GRANT SELECT on a table is unreachable until USAGE on the schema passes. The error noun is the diagnosis: permission denied for schema vs for table.

nodes.label: TRUNCATE is not DELETE
nodes.rationale: DELETE is MVCC row removal; TRUNCATE takes ACCESS EXCLUSIVE and discards the file. Withholding TRUNCATE from the app role turns an injected TRUNCATE into 42501.

nodes.label: UPDATE needs SELECT to read
nodes.rationale: UPDATE covers writing only. WHERE, RETURNING and SET x = x + 1 read columns and need SELECT. A write-only role cannot run a qualified update.

nodes.label: pg rejectUnauthorized false is require
nodes.rationale: ssl: true is not verify-full. Pass the CA explicitly with rejectUnauthorized: true. Check pg_stat_ssl per connection.

nodes.label: Six libpq sslmodes
nodes.rationale: prefer is the default and silently falls back to plaintext. allow tries plaintext first. require encrypts but verifies nothing.

nodes.label: verify-full hostname check
nodes.rationale: verify-ca accepted CN=devbible-pg-hba while connecting to 127.0.0.1; verify-full rejected it. Production should use verify-full.

nodes.label: CORS in Express
nodes.rationale: Browsers enforce CORS, not servers alone. Dynamic origin reflection must allow-list.

nodes.label: CSRF for cookie APIs
nodes.rationale: CSRF matters when auth relies on cookies automatically sent cross-site. Bearer Authorization usually does not.

nodes.label: csurf archived
nodes.rationale: csurf is archived — do not teach it as current. Prefer double-submit cookie, SameSite, framework guidance.

nodes.label: Open redirect
nodes.rationale: Never res.redirect(userInput) unchecked. Allow-list relative paths.

nodes.label: Content-Security-Policy
nodes.rationale: CSP matters more for HTML apps than pure JSON APIs. APIs may disable noisy browser-only policies after review.

nodes.label: Helmet
nodes.rationale: Helmet mounts secure default headers. It is not a full security program and does not replace auth or injection defenses.

nodes.label: Login rate limits
nodes.rationale: Brute-force protection on /login is tighter than global API limits and sits on the auth routes.

nodes.label: express-rate-limit
nodes.rationale: Limit by IP or user. Skip liveness probes. Keys must use the real client IP via trust proxy.

nodes.label: req.ip behind proxy
nodes.rationale: Without trust proxy, req.ip is the load balancer so rate limits ban everyone as one IP and secure cookies misbehave.

nodes.label: trust proxy
nodes.rationale: app.set('trust proxy', 1) for one hop you control. Never set true on an open internet edge without understanding spoofed X-Forwarded-For.

nodes.label: CORS credentials vs wildcard
nodes.rationale: Credentials plus wildcard origins do not mix. Browsers forbid Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * with cookies.

nodes.label: pg_upgrade --link and --swap destroy rollback
nodes.rationale: --link makes the old cluster unusable once the new one starts. --swap destructively modifies the old cluster once transfer begins. Verified backup is a precondition.

nodes.label: pg_upgrade catalog migration
nodes.rationale: --check works with the old server running. Install new extension .so files but do not CREATE EXTENSION on the new cluster.

nodes.label: PostgreSQL 18 transfers most optimizer statistics
nodes.rationale: Pre-18 transferred none. CREATE STATISTICS objects still do not transfer. Keep vacuumdb --analyze-in-stages in the runbook.

nodes.label: -At unaligned tuples-only
nodes.rationale: No header, no padding, no row-count footer. Pipe-friendly pair for a single value into a shell variable.

nodes.label: --csv
nodes.rationale: Proper CSV including quoting. Prefer over -A -F ',' which does not quote commas or quotes.

nodes.label: --no-psqlrc / -X
nodes.rationale: Stops a developer's .psqlrc from changing script behaviour. Required in every scripted invocation.

nodes.label: ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES
nodes.rationale: GRANT ON ALL TABLES applies only to tables that exist now; default privileges cover the next migration's table.

nodes.label: GRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA
nodes.rationale: Without schema USAGE every table is invisible however many table grants exist.

nodes.label: bytea
nodes.rationale: Binary round-trips to a Node Buffer. Measured 102400 bytes in and out, identical. Hex text form is 2×; pg uses the binary protocol so Buffers are unaffected. Use octet_length().

nodes.label: TOAST for bytea
nodes.rationale: Above ~2 KB, attstorage x compresses and moves the value to a side table. Measured pg_column_size 1185 for a compressible 100 KB buffer. Queries that omit the column never read the blob.

nodes.label: Object storage instead of large bytea
nodes.rationale: Backups, WAL, and replicas grow with blobs; values materialise whole in memory; no range requests or signed URLs. Keep metadata and sha256 in PostgreSQL, bytes in object storage, reconcile deletes with a queue. Prefer bytea over large objects (not deleted with the row).
nodes.norm_label: object storage instead of large bytea

nodes.label: Unquoted identifiers fold to lower case
nodes.rationale: CREATE TABLE "UserAccounts" then SELECT FROM UserAccounts → 42P01 relation useraccounts does not exist. Quoted names must be quoted forever.
nodes.norm_label: unquoted identifiers fold to lower case

nodes.label: user is reserved
nodes.rationale: SELECT * FROM user returns current_user, not a table. Plural users dodges this and most reserved-word collisions.

nodes.label: snake_case convention
nodes.rationale: What unquoted identifiers become anyway. Plural tables, singular columns, <table>_<cols>_key/fkey/check/idx matching PostgreSQL generated names.

nodes.label: NOT EXISTS over NOT IN
nodes.rationale: Null-safe anti-join and usually plans better. Prefer NOT EXISTS for subqueries always.

nodes.label: NOT IN with NULL returns nothing
nodes.rationale: x NOT IN (a, NULL) expands to x != a AND x != NULL, which can never be true. Usually arrives from a subquery with a nullable column.
nodes.norm_label: not in with null returns nothing

nodes.label: = ANY($1) for IN lists
nodes.rationale: One array parameter, no generated $1..$n, no ceiling, avoids the NOT IN null trap.

nodes.label: COALESCE PATCH semantics
nodes.rationale: SET col = COALESCE($n, col) leaves omitted fields alone but cannot set a column to null. For that, build SET from present keys over an allowlist.

nodes.label: COALESCE
nodes.rationale: First non-null argument; short-circuits. NULLIF(a, b) returns NULL when equal, used as x / NULLIF(y, 0) to avoid 22012.

nodes.label: || versus concat versus concat_ws
nodes.rationale: 'x' || NULL is NULL; concat('x', NULL) is x. concat_ws skips null values including their separator; a null separator voids the call.

nodes.label: musl versus glibc collation split
nodes.rationale: Identical PostgreSQL 18.4, both reporting datcollate en_US.utf8. Alpine musl sorts by byte value; Debian glibc uses dictionary order. Range queries change too.

nodes.label: Pin an ICU collation
nodes.rationale: ICU ships with PostgreSQL and is identical across images. builtin C.UTF-8 is fast and stable for identifiers. Nondeterministic ICU can do case-insensitive equality but forbids LIKE.

nodes.label: libc upgrade can corrupt text btrees
nodes.rationale: Index is physically ordered by the old collation. New rules miss present rows. Remedy REINDEX; prevention is ICU or C/builtin.
nodes.norm_label: libc upgrade can corrupt text btrees

nodes.label: bool_and
nodes.rationale: Set version of all. Empty set is NULL, not true — same aggregate-empty rule as sum(). JS if (row.all_paid) treats NULL as false, so a customer with no orders looks unpaid. coalesce(..., true). every() is the SQL alias.

nodes.label: bool_or
nodes.rationale: Set version of any. Pair with a FILTERed count. Empty-set default should be coalesce(..., false).

nodes.label: every()
nodes.rationale: Standard-SQL alias for bool_and. Measured identical. Pick one spelling.

nodes.label: value={x ?? ''} fix
nodes.rationale: ?? only replaces null and undefined. || also replaces 0 and empty string.

nodes.label: undefined decides controlled mode
nodes.rationale: value === undefined on first render is uncontrolled. Empty string and 0 are controlled. Mode cannot change over the input lifetime.

nodes.label: The switch warning, and supporting both
nodes.norm_label: the switch warning, and supporting both

nodes.label: do...while cursor pagination
nodes.rationale: Body must run once before the next-cursor condition exists.

nodes.label: for...in walks the prototype
nodes.rationale: Yields inherited enumerable keys and string indices; prefer Object.keys or for...of.

nodes.label: for...of
nodes.rationale: Default over iterables; supports break/continue/return and await; index via entries().

nodes.label: forEach cannot break or await
nodes.rationale: return only exits the callback; async callbacks' promises are discarded, causing silent races.

nodes.label: Array vs object spread
nodes.rationale: [...x] uses Symbol.iterator; {...x} copies own enumerable keys. [...{}] throws; {...[]} works.

nodes.label: Rest parameters
nodes.rationale: Must be last; excluded from fn.length; object rest omits a key without mutation.

nodes.label: Spread is a shallow copy
nodes.rationale: Nested references are shared; later keys win; undefined still overwrites a default.

nodes.label: Spread argument stack limit
nodes.rationale: Math.max(...hugeArray) can throw RangeError; reduce instead.

nodes.label: Arrow inherited arguments
nodes.rationale: Inside a function an arrow reports the outer arguments.length; use rest parameters.

nodes.label: apply and spread stack limit
nodes.rationale: Both overflow at ~200k arguments with RangeError; reduce has no such limit. Limit depends on remaining stack.

nodes.label: Loops
nodes.rationale: Choose a loop by whether you can break and whether you can await; forEach answers no to both.

nodes.label: Spread and rest
nodes.rationale: Same ... syntax; rest collects on the left of = or in parameters, spread expands everywhere else.

nodes.label: Symmetrical cleanup
nodes.rationale: Read setup line by line and name each inverse. Symmetry is about the observable effect: a fetch is undone by ignoring its result.

nodes.label: dialog.showModal needs close
nodes.rationale: A second showModal on an already-open dialog throws. Cleanup makes the extra cycle legal and closes on unmount.

nodes.label: removeEventListener needs the same handler reference
nodes.rationale: Declare the handler inside setup so both calls close over one binding. A recreated function silently removes nothing.
nodes.norm_label: removeeventlistener needs the same handler reference

nodes.label: Snapshot trap when collapsing a chain
nodes.rationale: Inside a handler, state is a snapshot. Name nextRound = round + 1. The chain had been getting fresh values only because each link ran in a later render.
nodes.norm_label: snapshot trap when collapsing a chain

nodes.label: An effect chain cannot be replayed
nodes.rationale: Attached to state changing, not the user acting. Undo, history, session restore and tests that seed state re-fire the cascade. Handler logic is inert until called.
nodes.norm_label: an effect chain cannot be replayed

nodes.label: Chains are often stored derived state
nodes.rationale: isGameOver was always round > 5. Each stored derivation needs a maintaining effect. Delete the storage and the effect goes with it.
nodes.norm_label: chains are often stored derived state

nodes.label: React page verification policy
nodes.rationale: Phases 0–1 are sandbox-proven; from Phase 2 onward pages are validated against react.dev and carry no reconstructed console blocks.

nodes.label: extends evaluated at declaration
nodes.rationale: extends is an expression run when the class statement executes, not at new. Mutual extends is impossible.

nodes.label: Declaration closes the TDZ
nodes.rationale: let x; initialises to undefined and ends the zone. const without an initializer is a parse-time SyntaxError.

nodes.label: Per-iteration loop binding
nodes.rationale: for (const item of items) is legal because each iteration declares a new binding rather than reassigning one.

nodes.label: Self-reference initializer
nodes.rationale: let x = x throws because the RHS is evaluated before the binding is initialised. var y = y silently assigns undefined.

nodes.label: Temporal dead zone
nodes.rationale: A stretch of time, not of code. The binding exists from block entry but is empty until the declaration runs; a read throws ReferenceError.

nodes.label: Three binding error types
nodes.rationale: 'x is not defined' means no binding; 'x is not a function' means the binding holds a non-callable; 'Cannot access before initialization' means uninitialised TDZ.

nodes.label: globalThis feature detection
nodes.rationale: globalThis.X !== undefined is a property access and cannot hit a dead zone.

nodes.label: Engine TDZ error messages
nodes.rationale: V8 names the variable; SpiderMonkey says lexical declaration; JavaScriptCore omits the name.

nodes.label: typeof throws in the TDZ
nodes.rationale: typeof still reads the binding. It returns 'undefined' only for names with no binding at all.

nodes.label: Function expression not hoisted
nodes.rationale: var f = function(){} hoists the binding as undefined; calling it above the line is TypeError, not ReferenceError.

nodes.label: TDZ is temporal not positional
nodes.rationale: A function defined above a let may mention it; only a read that runs before the declaration throws.

nodes.label: TDZ is a feature
nodes.rationale: Fails at the wrong line instead of later undefined; lets const have one observable value; makes a shadow own the name for the whole block.

nodes.label: Declaration hoisting
nodes.rationale: var is referenceable before its line without ReferenceError, but the value is always undefined until assignment.

nodes.label: var declaration vs initialization split
nodes.rationale: var x = 1 is two operations: the declaration hoists to function scope as undefined; the assignment stays where it is.

nodes.label: Direct eval
nodes.rationale: Can introduce bindings into the surrounding scope. Indirect eval (0, eval)(...) runs in global scope instead.

nodes.label: Lexical scope
nodes.rationale: A function's free variables resolve where it is written, not where it is called. That is what makes closures possible.

nodes.label: Scope chain
nodes.rationale: Lookup walks innermost to outermost and stops at the first match. Outer scopes never see inner bindings.

nodes.label: What creates a scope
nodes.rationale: Functions, modules, blocks for let/const/class, for-heads with let/const, and catch. Object literals do not.

nodes.label: Shadowing
nodes.rationale: An inner binding hides the outer one for its scope without overwriting it. let cannot redeclare a parameter at function top level.

nodes.label: with statement
nodes.rationale: Injects an object's properties into the scope chain, defeating static slot resolution. SyntaxError in strict mode.

nodes.label: Function scope vs block scope
nodes.rationale: var ignores blocks and attaches to the nearest function. let/const attach to the nearest block.

nodes.label: Parameter scope vs body scope
nodes.rationale: Any default creates a parameter scope. A var of the same name in the body is a different binding.

nodes.label: const by default
nodes.rationale: const first, let when you reassign, var never. Use-before-declaration then throws instead of producing undefined.

nodes.label: Worker thread V8 isolate
nodes.rationale: Each worker is an OS thread with its own isolate and event loop, for CPU-bound JS only. Startup ~60 ms — same as a fork — so never create one per request.

nodes.label: postMessage transfer list
nodes.rationale: Default postMessage copies via structured clone. Transfer list moves a buffer zero-copy and detaches it (byteLength 0). SharedArrayBuffer when both sides need it.

nodes.label: pool.on('error') idle listener
nodes.rationale: Idle pooled connections can die (failover, pg_terminate_backend). Unhandled 'error' on the pool kills Node. Log and do not rethrow; the pool replaces the socket.

nodes.label: pg.Pool
nodes.rationale: One pool per process at module scope. max is a concurrency ceiling, not a speed limit — callers queue as waitingCount. Size from max_connections / processes.

nodes.label: PostgreSQL server-side cursor
nodes.rationale: pool.query buffers the whole result (300 MB RSS for 500k rows). A cursor holds one batch on a checked-out client. QueryStream adds backpressure but is ~5.7x slower for a pure loop.

nodes.label: Driver vs builder vs ORM
nodes.rationale: The choice is who writes the SQL and what happens when it is wrong. Layer overhead is sub-millisecond; N+1 and indexes dominate. One tool owns schema, migrations and the pool.

nodes.label: N+1 query
nodes.rationale: One query for the list plus one per item. Cost is round trips, not query work — 101 queries 111 ms vs 2 batched 7 ms on localhost. Promise.all makes pool exhaustion worse.

nodes.label: DatabaseSync
nodes.rationale: Bundled SQLite 3.53.3, fully synchronous because it is a local file. Slow queries block the event loop. Not a networked PostgreSQL replacement.

nodes.label: Prisma include is two queries
nodes.rationale: include issues a second IN (...) query, not a join. Batched, not N+1, but nested includes multiply round trips.

nodes.label: Prisma 7 driver adapter
nodes.rationale: url in datasource is a hard error (P1012); URL moves to prisma.config.ts. Client requires PrismaPg adapter over a pg pool.

nodes.label: Drizzle SQL-first schema
nodes.rationale: Schema is TypeScript; queries compose into SQL you can print with .toSQL(). Sits on your pg.Pool. Safer default when queries get non-trivial.

nodes.label: Read-your-own-writes
nodes.rationale: Async replica can miss a just-committed write — measured 0 rows on idle localhost. Pin post-write reads to primary via ALS, endpoint intent, or session pin.

nodes.label: Primary and replica pools
nodes.rationale: Replica is physically read-only (25006 / pg_is_in_recovery). Adds read capacity, not latency. A transaction must stay entirely on the primary.

nodes.label: Concurrency limiting
nodes.rationale: Promise.all peaked at 200 in-flight; mapLimit(8) at 8.

nodes.label: Worker thread pool
nodes.rationale: Fixed workers, a queue, replace on death, reject in-flight tasks, close() for shutdown. Size availableParallelism()-1. Production: piscina.

nodes.label: Keyset pagination
nodes.rationale: Paginated APIs should not hold a cursor across requests. Use WHERE id > $1 ORDER BY id LIMIT n. OFFSET walks and discards skipped rows.

nodes.label: Batch with ANY / $in
nodes.rationale: Collect parent ids, one child query with = ANY($1) or $in, group in memory. Works across services where a join is impossible. DataLoader is this per tick.

nodes.label: mapLimit bounded parallelism
nodes.rationale: Promise.all starts everything at once (peak 200 for 200 items). N runners pull a shared synchronous index. Bind limit to the scarcest resource; count the product across layers.

nodes.label: Default parameter expression
nodes.rationale: Stored unevaluated; runs at call time, left to right, only for omitted arguments.

nodes.label: Function.length and defaults
nodes.rationale: length counts parameters before the first default or rest. Express and Mocha dispatch on arity.

nodes.label: No Python mutable-default trap
nodes.rationale: list = [] constructs per call. The trap returns if the default names a shared outer binding.

nodes.label: Parameter list TDZ
nodes.rationale: Defaults initialise left to right. A forward reference throws only when that argument is omitted.

nodes.label: Only undefined triggers a default
nodes.rationale: null is a value. APIs that return null for missing data will not fall back unless you use ?? in the body.

nodes.label: arguments object
nodes.rationale: Array-like, no array methods, absent in arrows. Prefer rest in new code.

nodes.label: Arity is never enforced
nodes.rationale: Too few arguments become undefined; extras are ignored by the parameter list but still counted by arguments.

nodes.label: Destructured parameter = {}
nodes.rationale: x = 0 defaults a missing property; = {} defaults a missing object. Every nesting level needs its own default.

nodes.label: Non-simple parameter list
nodes.rationale: Any default, rest, or destructured parameter. Disables aliasing, forbids a body 'use strict', and changes .length.

nodes.label: Rest parameters
nodes.rationale: A real array, empty rather than undefined when nothing extra is passed. Must be last; cannot have a default.

nodes.label: Sloppy-mode arguments aliasing
nodes.rationale: On a simple sloppy parameter list, arguments[i] and the parameter share one slot. Strict, default, rest, or destructuring turns it off.

nodes.label: Positional plus options object
nodes.rationale: Two or three required positionals, then a destructured options object. JavaScript will not check arity for you.

nodes.label: push pop shift unshift
nodes.rationale: Adders return the new length; removers return the element or undefined. All four mutate in place.

nodes.label: shift re-indexes the array
nodes.rationale: shift and unshift re-index every remaining element; pop and push touch one slot.

nodes.label: Array.from
nodes.rationale: Accepts iterables and array-likes; never sparse; optional mapFn maps during construction with only (element, index).

nodes.label: Array-like vs iterable
nodes.rationale: Array-likes have length and indices but no Symbol.iterator. Spread throws; Array.from works.

nodes.label: Code units vs code points
nodes.rationale: split("") and length are UTF-16 code units; spread and Array.from yield code points. Intl.Segmenter for graphemes.

nodes.label: String.prototype.split
nodes.rationale: No separator yields [whole]. "".split(",") is [""] not []. limit truncates and discards the rest.

nodes.label: String immutability
nodes.rationale: Strings are immutable so string methods never mutate and need no defensive copy.

nodes.label: Spread argument RangeError
nodes.rationale: Math.max(...huge) or push(...huge) can exceed the engine argument limit.

nodes.label: Spread two operations
nodes.rationale: Array/arg spread needs an iterable; object spread copies own enumerable properties. [...obj] throws; {...arr} works; {...map} is {}.

nodes.label: O(n²) shift queue
nodes.rationale: n shifts re-index up to n elements. Use an index cursor or reverse-then-pop.

nodes.label: reduce spread O(N²) anti-pattern
nodes.rationale: Spreading the accumulator each step copies N²/2 keys. Mutate the private acc or use a for-of loop.

nodes.label: Spread-in-loop is quadratic
nodes.rationale: out = [...out, x] each iteration copies the growing array. Quadratic by construction.

nodes.label: includes vs indexOf on holes
nodes.rationale: includes(undefined) is true on a hole; indexOf(undefined) is -1 because indexOf skips holes.

nodes.label: WeakMap weak keys
nodes.rationale: Keys must be objects; entries are collectable. Not iterable, no size. A strong Map here leaks memory.

nodes.label: Map
nodes.rationale: set returns the map for chaining and reduce. delete returns whether the key existed.

nodes.label: Map SameValueZero
nodes.rationale: Like === except NaN equals NaN and 0 equals -0. Same algorithm as Set and Array.prototype.includes.

nodes.label: Six Map vs Object differences
nodes.rationale: Accidental prototype keys, any key type, insertion order, size property, direct iteration, frequent add/remove.

nodes.label: Destructuring
nodes.rationale: Array patterns match by position; object patterns match by name. Defaults apply to undefined, not null.

nodes.label: Destructured param = {}
nodes.rationale: function f({a} = {}) so a missing argument is not TypeError on undefined.

nodes.label: Destructuring detaches this
nodes.rationale: const {start} = timer is assignment; start() loses this. APIs meant to be destructured return closures.

nodes.label: Destructuring and fn.length
nodes.rationale: A destructured parameter counts as 1; a default stops the count, so ({a}={}) => {} has length 0.

nodes.label: Options object parameters
nodes.rationale: Named, order-independent args. Cost is one allocation. Worth it past two or three parameters.

nodes.label: Map when keys are data
nodes.rationale: Use Map when keys come from data; use an object when keys are a small fixed set you wrote. JSON edges stay objects.

nodes.label: Three destructuring traps
nodes.rationale: null bypasses defaults; function f({a}){} throws without = {}; destructuring methods detaches this.

nodes.label: devbible-pg container
nodes.rationale: podman run -d --name devbible-pg maps 55432:5432. Connect at 127.0.0.1:55432 as user/db/password devbible. Use pg from this folder (npm install pg).

nodes.label: postgres:18-alpine
nodes.rationale: Image docker.io/library/postgres:18-alpine is the Phase 0 measurement database.

nodes.label: Object rest omit-a-key
nodes.rationale: Rest must be last. Object rest is the idiomatic omit-a-key, better than delete: new object, stable shape, no mutation. Shallow; own enumerable only.

nodes.label: Array and call spread
nodes.rationale: In array literals and argument lists, ... consumes an iterable via Symbol.iterator. Plain objects throw TypeError.

nodes.label: Object spread
nodes.rationale: Copies own enumerable properties. Does not need an iterable. Spreading a Map/Set/Date/class instance yields {} or method-less objects.

nodes.label: Spread is shallow
nodes.rationale: MDN: multidimensional arrays are not safe to copy with spread. Use structuredClone for a genuinely independent graph; shallow is usually the right default.

nodes.label: Later-wins object merge
nodes.rationale: { ...defaults, ...overrides } is replace, not deep merge. A later spread after an explicit key overrides it.

nodes.label: Quadratic spread-in-loop
nodes.rationale: out = [...out, x] copies the accumulated array each iteration. Use map or push.

nodes.label: Spread argument-count limit
nodes.rationale: Spreading a large array into a call can RangeError. Use reduce for max, loop or concat for append.

nodes.label: Spread replaces apply
nodes.rationale: f(...args) does what f.apply(null, args) did, composes with fixed args and new. apply remains only for setting this.

nodes.label: Conditional object-spread no-op
nodes.rationale: Spreading a non-object into an object is silently a no-op, which makes ...(cond && { key }) work.

nodes.label: Spread vs rest
nodes.rationale: Same three dots, opposite directions. Rest collects on the left or in parameters (must be last, only one). Spread expands on the right or in a call.

nodes.label: Array.from vs spread
nodes.rationale: Array.from accepts array-likes without iterators, maps while converting, and builds n slots. Spread is shorter when an iterator exists.

nodes.label: Immutable spread updates
nodes.rationale: Copies only the changed level and shares untouched branches — what makes prev.items === next.items a valid change check.

nodes.label: LVHA link order
nodes.rationale: Equal-specificity link states must be :link :visited :hover :active or visited links lose hover.

nodes.label: :visited privacy restrictions
nodes.rationale: Only colour properties apply and getComputedStyle lies, so sites cannot leak browsing history.

nodes.label: await does not block the thread
nodes.rationale: await suspends the async function, not the thread. It cannot slice a long synchronous computation.
nodes.norm_label: await does not block the thread

nodes.label: Event loop
nodes.rationale: Enables asynchronous programming while remaining single-threaded. An agent has a heap, a stack, and a job queue.

nodes.label: setTimeout delay is a floor
nodes.rationale: setTimeout(fn, 10) means not before 10 ms. The callback also waits for the current job, queued jobs, and the entire microtask queue.

nodes.label: One thread, many I/O
nodes.rationale: A 3-second for-loop stalls every request; a 3-second database query does not.

nodes.label: Event loop lag
nodes.rationale: Idle p50 is the resolution; max is the smoke alarm.

nodes.label: Run to completion
nodes.rationale: A function cannot be preempted. That is why JS needs no locks, and why a long sync loop freezes rendering.

nodes.label: Job complete when stack is empty
nodes.rationale: That is the definition of run-to-completion and why rendering cannot happen until the call stack fully unwinds.
nodes.norm_label: job complete when stack is empty

nodes.label: Third-party middleware checklist
nodes.rationale: Check Express 5 support, maintenance, mutation surface, and next(err) vs throw before installing.

nodes.label: Prefer thin middleware wrappers
nodes.rationale: Battle-tested packages hide CVEs you never researched, but every dependency is supply-chain surface. Prefer fewer, better mounts.

nodes.label: Query field allow-list
nodes.rationale: Never pass raw req.query into Mongo or SQL builders. Allow-list prevents sorting on unindexed or sensitive columns and injection-style operators.

nodes.label: Mongo operator injection
nodes.rationale: ?filter[$gt]=… succeeds when query objects are merged blindly.

nodes.label: Feature folders
nodes.rationale: orders/routes.ts with orders/service.ts; scales by domain.

nodes.label: Layer folders
nodes.rationale: routes/, services/, repos/; scales by role.

nodes.label: SHA-256 object format
nodes.rationale: Chosen at init with --object-format=sha256. 64 hex characters. No in-place conversion.

nodes.label: SHA-1 and SHA-256 cannot interoperate
nodes.rationale: Object names are the protocol vocabulary. Hosts, tooling, and remotes assume SHA-1, so SHA-256 adoption is blocked.

nodes.label: TC39 stage process
nodes.rationale: Stage 3 is where engines ship and risk lives. Stage 4 is two implementations plus tests. Never build on Stage 2 or below.

nodes.label: Temporal Stage 3
nodes.rationale: Measured absent on Node 24.19.0. Right long-term Date replacement; wrong to ship today. Tiered Know.

nodes.label: Detached method this is undefined
nodes.rationale: In a class body, a detached method throws immediately. In sloppy mode this is globalThis and the bug becomes a silent leak.

nodes.label: Number vs parseInt prefixes
nodes.rationale: Number understands 0x/0o/0b. parseInt('0o755') is 0 because parsing stops at the letter. Always pass radix 10.

nodes.label: Octal file-mode literals
nodes.rationale: 0o755 is 493, the correct Unix mode. chmod(path, 755) silently sets wrong permissions. Legacy 0755 is SyntaxError in strict/modules.

nodes.label: autocannon HTTP load
nodes.rationale: Right tool when the claim is about the running service: RPS plus p50/p95/p99, error rate, and server saturation under concurrency.

nodes.label: microbenchmarks
nodes.rationale: Lie because V8 over-optimizes monomorphic toys, DCE can erase unused work, and a 3 ns win does not move p99 when the DB takes 40 ms. Consume results into a sink.

nodes.label: --cpu-prof
nodes.rationale: Samples during the run and writes .cpuprofile on exit. Hard kill (-9) skips flush. Wrong tool when lag is low and you are I/O bound.

nodes.label: 0x flame graphs
nodes.rationale: Low-ceremony capture plus interactive HTML around the same family of data as --cpu-prof.

nodes.label: Clinic.js
nodes.rationale: Doctor for early triage (CPU vs I/O vs memory); Flame when CPU is already known hot; Bubbleprof for async delay; Heapprofiler for allocation views.

nodes.label: flame graph width
nodes.rationale: Width is portion of CPU samples in that stack subtree. Will not show await time; empty app frames usually mean I/O bound.

nodes.label: latency traffic errors saturation
nodes.rationale: From Google SRE workbook. Node examples: duration histograms, QPS, 5xx ratio, event-loop lag / pool wait / queue depth. Alert on percentiles and error ratio, not averages or raw counts.

nodes.label: Prometheus label cardinality
nodes.rationale: route must be the template (/orders/:id), never raw URL or userId. Identity belongs in logs and traces.

nodes.label: bottleneck-first method
nodes.rationale: The bottleneck is the resource that is full. Quantify, check golden signals and loop lag, time dependencies, profile only if CPU/loop is hot, change one thing, remeasure.

nodes.label: Symbol unique primitive
nodes.rationale: Every Symbol('id') is unique. Hidden from Object.keys, for…in and JSON.stringify, but getOwnPropertySymbols and spread expose/copy them. Not privacy — use #private fields.

nodes.label: delete creates array holes
nodes.rationale: delete arr[1] does not shorten the array; it leaves a hole that map preserves. Use splice or filter/toSpliced. Never delete on arrays.

nodes.label: in vs Object.hasOwn
nodes.rationale: in walks the prototype chain so 'toString' in {} is true. Object.hasOwn checks own keys only.

nodes.label: const fixes the binding not the value
nodes.rationale: The name cannot be pointed at something else; object and array contents can still change.
nodes.norm_label: const fixes the binding not the value

nodes.label: Object.freeze
nodes.rationale: Shallow. Nested objects remain mutable. Strict mode throws on a frozen write; sloppy fails silently.

nodes.label: V8 dictionary mode
nodes.rationale: Slow mode: properties in a hash table, no descriptor array, inline caches do not work. One delete is not documented to trigger it.

nodes.label: V8 HiddenClass
nodes.rationale: Objects sharing a shape share a HiddenClass so inline caches stay fast. Frequent add/delete generates HiddenClass and descriptor-array overhead.

nodes.label: Array push and pop
nodes.rationale: Back-of-array adders return the new length; removers return the element. Do not re-index the rest of the array. Non-mutating twins: [...arr, x] and arr.slice(0, -1).

nodes.label: Array shift and unshift
nodes.rationale: Front operations re-index the whole array. Draining a large queue with shift() is quadratic.

nodes.label: Node vs browser event loop
nodes.rationale: Both drain one job at a time with microtasks before tasks. Node uses libuv phases plus process.nextTick; the browser also schedules rendering.

nodes.label: Node event loop phases
nodes.rationale: Six phases in a fixed order, plus nextTick and the microtask queue which are not phases at all.

nodes.label: Phase 13 Complexity and JavaScript's real costs
nodes.norm_label: phase 13 complexity and javascript's real costs

nodes.label: PID 1 and signals
nodes.rationale: npm start as PID 1 swallows SIGTERM.

nodes.label: Graceful shutdown
nodes.rationale: server.close() alone hangs forever. Sweep idle connections and force at the deadline.

nodes.label: ESM and CommonJS interop
nodes.rationale: On Node 24, require(esm) works; top-level await is the one hard boundary. require(esm) returns the namespace, so default is at .default.

nodes.label: closure retention of large objects
nodes.rationale: A timer callback that closes over hugeBuffer keeps the allocation alive. Close over the derived scalar instead.

nodes.label: unbounded cache leak
nodes.rationale: Module-level Map with no max or TTL. Bound by count and bytes; LRU or Redis maxmemory.

nodes.label: uncleared timers and handles
nodes.rationale: setInterval without clearInterval, plus unclosed servers, Redis clients, and fs.watch keep the process from settling.

nodes.label: unremoved event listeners
nodes.rationale: Emitter retains the function, which retains its closed-over scope. on/off must share the same function reference.

nodes.label: --heap-prof
nodes.rationale: Allocation timeline-style profile. For what is retained right now, prefer heap snapshots.

nodes.label: Node Inspector --inspect
nodes.rationale: Live CPU/Memory session without waiting for exit. Exposing --inspect on a public IP is a remote code surface — treat like a root shell.

nodes.label: v8.writeHeapSnapshot
nodes.rationale: Returns a path to a .heapsnapshot. Diff two snapshots under the same load; sort by retained size growth. Snapshotting is expensive — canary only.

nodes.label: leak vs large cache
nodes.rationale: A cache with a cap is a policy. An unbounded Map is a leak with a product name. Restart 'fixes' heap until the curve returns.

nodes.label: heap retainer path
nodes.rationale: The reference chain to a GC root (module-scope Map, timer, server) is the line of code that should have released the object.

nodes.label: Atomic writes
nodes.rationale: Temp file in the same directory, fsync, rename. Skip the same-directory step and you get EXDEV.

nodes.label: Path traversal
nodes.rationale: join vs resolve is a security boundary. Resolve, check with the separator, then realpath.

nodes.label: import.meta.dirname
nodes.rationale: ESM replacement for __dirname on Node 21.2+. Undefined for non-file: URLs; then use fileURLToPath(import.meta.url).

nodes.label: fileURLToPath / pathToFileURL
nodes.rationale: Only correct file: conversions. file://+path misses %20 and Windows drive letters. Most fs APIs accept a file: URL directly.

nodes.label: stat().mode & 0o777
nodes.rationale: mode includes file type (0o100644). Compare only after masking. Always write octal 0o600; chmod(600) is 0o1130.

nodes.label: umask
nodes.rationale: Per-process bits to remove. Common 022 turns requested 0o666 into 0o644. mode is a maximum, not a guarantee.

nodes.label: Open redirect
nodes.rationale: //evil and /\evil start with / and resolve off-origin. startsWith('/') is not a check.

nodes.label: safeNext origin compare
nodes.rationale: new URL(next, BASE) then compare origin. Return pathname+search+hash, never a full URL.

nodes.label: INCR then EXPIRE race
nodes.rationale: Death between INCR and EXPIRE leaves ttl -1 and locks that client forever. Use one atomic Lua script.

nodes.label: Fail open vs fail closed
nodes.rationale: Open for fairness APIs; closed for login/payment. Never fail open silently.

nodes.label: Provenance attestations
nodes.rationale: Stronger than a registry signature: Sigstore statement that the tarball was built by a specific CI workflow from a specific commit.

nodes.label: min-release-age cooldown
nodes.rationale: Most malicious versions are unpublished within days; refusing anything younger than a week removes nearly the whole window.

nodes.label: listen(0) ephemeral port
nodes.rationale: Hardcoded ports race under file concurrency and produce intermittent EADDRINUSE in CI.

nodes.label: Node-API (N-API)
nodes.rationale: Stable C ABI for native addons so a binary can survive Node major upgrades better than NAN/V8-bound addons.

nodes.label: node-addon-api
nodes.rationale: C++ wrappers over Node-API (types, maybe-unwrap) that make addon code less error-prone.

nodes.label: Native addon prebuilds
nodes.rationale: Ship per-platform binaries (prebuildify/prebuild) so users and CI do not need a compiler.

nodes.label: process.versions.napi
nodes.rationale: Reports the Node-API version of the runtime; Node 24.19.0 reports 10.

nodes.label: Startup snapshot
nodes.rationale: Freezes a V8 heap after bootstrap so the next launch skips re-parsing and re-running init.

nodes.label: Snapshot tied to Node/V8 build
nodes.rationale: Snapshots are invalid after a Node patch; rebuild in CI per runtime artifact.

nodes.label: --max-old-space-size
nodes.rationale: Most common production V8-related flag; caps old-space growth. Heap limit is not always equal to the number passed.

nodes.label: --trace-gc
nodes.rationale: GC logging for debugging; noisy and not a production default.

nodes.label: V8 flags
nodes.rationale: Engine knobs for heap limits, GC tracing, and compilation. Listed with node --v8-options on the deployed binary.

nodes.label: Node-API sits between C++ and V8
nodes.rationale: Early addons called V8 APIs and broke every Node major. Node-API is the stable surface: Your C++ → Node-API → Node/V8.
nodes.norm_label: node-api sits between c++ and v8

nodes.label: Snapshot versus compile cache versus SEA
nodes.rationale: enableCompileCache stores compilation artifacts; a snapshot stores initialised heap; SEA packages a single binary. Compile cache is the practical first win.
nodes.norm_label: snapshot versus compile cache versus sea

nodes.label: V8 flags are diagnostics not casual perf knobs
nodes.rationale: Most apps need none beyond --max-old-space-size. Random blog flags add risk; document any non-default with an owner.
nodes.norm_label: v8 flags are diagnostics not casual perf knobs

nodes.label: Missing await after test ended
nodes.rationale: On Node 24 the test still prints a tick; the file fails. A swallowed catch makes it truly silent.

nodes.label: Consumer-driven contract
nodes.rationale: Consumer owns the schema of fields it actually reads. A generated-from-model contract can never fail.

nodes.label: Coverage is not verification
nodes.rationale: Measures which lines executed, not whether anything was checked. 100% can ship a float-money bug.

nodes.label: Test data factory
nodes.rationale: Valid defaults plus one-field overrides so a schema change is a one-line edit, not forty.

nodes.label: LISTEN NOTIFY
nodes.rationale: At-most-once delivery. Not a durable event bus.

nodes.label: Transactional outbox
nodes.rationale: Events that cannot be lost: write the event in the same transaction as the business row.

nodes.label: Why streams exist
nodes.rationale: Process data in chunks so peak memory stays constant. Buffered 216 MB log peaked 670 MB RSS vs 88 MB streamed.

nodes.label: Default highWaterMark 64 KB
nodes.rationale: stream.getDefaultHighWaterMark(false) is 64 KB (raised from 16 KB in Node 22). Chunks split lines, JSON, and multi-byte characters freely.

nodes.label: ERR_STRING_TOO_LONG
nodes.rationale: V8 strings cap at 0x1fffffe8 characters (~512 MB). readFile(path,'utf8') on a larger file throws with no workaround except streaming.

nodes.label: child_process.exec
nodes.rationale: Runs through /bin/sh -c so pipes and globs work. Buffers with maxBuffer 1 MB. Never interpolate untrusted input.

nodes.label: child_process.execFile
nodes.rationale: No shell; argv array to execve. Default choice for running one binary. Same 1 MB maxBuffer as exec.

nodes.label: child_process.fork
nodes.rationale: Another Node process plus an IPC message channel.

nodes.label: maxBuffer
nodes.rationale: Cap on buffered stdout/stderr for exec/execFile, 1 MB default. Exceeding kills the child with ERR_CHILD_PROCESS_STDIO_MAXBUFFER.

nodes.label: child_process.spawn
nodes.rationale: No shell, streams stdout/stderr. Output bounded by what you consume. Child blocks if the pipe fills and nobody reads.

nodes.label: Time to first byte
nodes.rationale: A streamed response sends as soon as the first chunk exists; buffering waits for the last byte and can time out proxies.

nodes.label: When not to stream
nodes.rationale: Buffer bounded small data (config, 10 KB JSON). Streams add backpressure complexity and cannot JSON.parse or sort without a streaming parser.

nodes.label: Explicit child env
nodes.rationale: Children inherit process.env by default, handing DB URLs and API keys to ffmpeg. Pass a minimal env with PATH only.

nodes.label: Workers vs child processes
nodes.rationale: Child process ~56 ms to ready and ~49 MB RSS. Four workers ~23 MB vs ~196 MB for four processes. Children are for other programs or crash isolation.

nodes.label: Cast the literal never the column
nodes.rationale: A cast on the indexed column turned a 0.199 ms index-only scan into a 47.9 ms sequential scan.
nodes.norm_label: cast the literal never the column

nodes.label: cidr type
nodes.rationale: Holds a network only; host bits set raise 22P02. That distinction is why both inet and cidr exist: cidr is a range, inet is an address that may know its range.

nodes.label: inet type
nodes.rationale: Holds a host address with optional netmask, 10 bytes vs 16 as text, validates input (22P02), normalises IPv6 so equivalent forms compare equal, and supports GiST-indexable containment operators.

nodes.label: Built-in geometric types
nodes.rationale: point, line, lseg, box, path, polygon, circle with <->, @>, && — Cartesian and GiST-indexable. point arrives in Node as {x,y}.

nodes.label: PostGIS geography for Earth
nodes.rationale: Built-in geometry is Cartesian; <-> on lat/lng degrees is not metres. PostGIS geography, SRS and real distance functions are required for maps.

nodes.label: Node undefined becomes SQL NULL
nodes.rationale: pg converts undefined parameters to NULL, so a missing request key silently nulls a column. Build partial updates from present keys.

nodes.label: Explicit NULL bypasses DEFAULT
nodes.rationale: DEFAULT applies only when the column is omitted or DEFAULT. ORMs that send null for unset fields override every default.

nodes.label: COMMENT ON
nodes.rationale: Catalog documentation; pg_dump includes it. Read with obj_description/col_description or \d+. information_schema does not expose comments.

nodes.label: Comments belong in migrations
nodes.rationale: A hand-typed psql comment is lost on rebuild. Comments are not inherited and vanish when an object is dropped/recreated. COMMENT ON replaces; NULL deletes.

nodes.label: NULLS NOT DISTINCT
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL 15+: NULLs compare as equal so only one is allowed (second → 23505). Works on index and constraint forms; no sentinel COALESCE needed.

nodes.label: Unique column accepts unlimited NULLs
nodes.rationale: Two NULLs are not equal under SQL three-valued logic. Measured: 3 NULLs inserted into a UNIQUE column. SQL-standard, not a PostgreSQL quirk.

nodes.label: age() vs timestamp subtraction
nodes.rationale: age returns a symbolic interval (1 mon is 28–31 days). Subtraction is elapsed time. pg returns interval as PostgresInterval, not a number.

nodes.label: interval 1 day vs 24 hours
nodes.rationale: Differ on DST: 1 day keeps wall-clock time (23 or 25 h); 24 hours is elapsed. Same time tomorrow vs token expires in 24 hours.

nodes.label: date and timestamp read in Node TZ
nodes.rationale: date becomes Date at local midnight (2026-08-12 → 2026-08-11T18:30Z under UTC+5:30). timestamp assumes local time. Only timestamptz is a real instant.
nodes.norm_label: date and timestamp read in node tz

nodes.label: Override date (1082) to string
nodes.rationale: A date is a calendar label. Converting it to Date at local midnight produces off-by-one days. The almost-always-right global override.

nodes.label: rowMode: 'array'
nodes.rationale: Rows as positional arrays. Preserves duplicate names and skips object allocation on large results.

nodes.label: SELECT * join column collapse
nodes.rationale: Duplicate column names collapse in the row object with no error. fields still lists all four; the last name wins. Alias or use rowMode array.

nodes.label: Simple vs extended query protocol
nodes.rationale: No params or []: simple protocol, multi-statement, array of results. One parameter: extended, one statement only. Empty array is not 'some parameters'.

nodes.label: Multi-statement .sql result array
nodes.rationale: No params: simple protocol, query() is an array, res.rows is undefined. Non-empty params: 42601 cannot insert multiple commands. Keep app query files to one statement.

nodes.label: uncaughtException
nodes.rationale: Handlers exist to log a fatal error before dying. Installing a listener suppresses default termination; the handler must exit non-zero.

nodes.label: uncaughtExceptionMonitor
nodes.rationale: Observes a fatal error without suppressing Node's default termination. Correct hook for crash reporters like Sentry.

nodes.label: http.createServer
nodes.rationale: Hands two streams and nothing else. A thrown handler never becomes a 500.

nodes.label: headersTimeout requestTimeout connectionsCheckingInterval
nodes.rationale: Timeouts are enforced by a 30s default sweep. Lowering requestTimeout alone does nothing until the next check.

nodes.label: Lexical migration filename order
nodes.rationale: Filename sort is lexical: 1, 10, 11, 2. Surfaces as 42P01 on a fresh database. Fix with zero-padding or UTC timestamps.

nodes.label: Timestamped migration filenames
nodes.rationale: UTC timestamps avoid branch collisions on counter names. Ordering is authorship time, which may not be dependency order. Tools generate these.

nodes.label: Statements that cannot be in a transaction
nodes.rationale: CREATE/DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY, VACUUM, CREATE DATABASE fail with 25001. Runners use a per-file -- migrate: no-transaction directive.
nodes.norm_label: statements that cannot be in a transaction

nodes.label: Batch vs per-file transaction
nodes.rationale: Batch is all-or-nothing and simpler. Per-file resumes after failure, releases locks between files, and is the only way a CONCURRENTLY file can opt out. Tools default to per-file.

nodes.label: Partial unique index for live emails
nodes.rationale: Full unique index blocks re-registration (23505). UNIQUE (email) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL. A lookup without the predicate can hit either row; a partial index is unusable without it.
nodes.norm_label: partial unique index for live emails

nodes.label: Soft delete UPDATE
nodes.rationale: SET deleted_at = now() WHERE id AND deleted_at IS NULL. No FK cascade. Not an audit log. AND deleted_at IS NULL keeps retries from overwriting the timestamp.

nodes.label: rowCount 0 is 404 or 409
nodes.rationale: Missing row and stale version look identical. Re-read or a data-modifying CTE (updated/conflict/empty). Never report 404 for a conflict.

nodes.label: findX vs getX
nodes.rationale: find returns null when absence is expected; get throws NotFoundError when absence is impossible. rows[0] ?? null, never undefined (JSON drops the key).

nodes.label: SELECT ... FOR UPDATE inside a request
nodes.rationale: Pessimistic answer to lost updates: lock at read, queue instead of retry. Meaningless outside a transaction.
nodes.norm_label: select ... for update inside a request

nodes.label: Optimistic concurrency
nodes.rationale: Default for human-timescale edits. No locks when uncontended. Lost updates span two HTTP requests that no transaction can cover.

nodes.label: Tuple comparison (created_at, id) < ($1, $2)
nodes.rationale: Row constructor matches a composite index. Hand-written OR form looks equivalent and is ~160× slower. Sort key must be total; nullables silently truncate the walk.

nodes.label: OFFSET is the wrong default
nodes.rationale: OFFSET n produces and discards n rows. Concurrent inserts shift the window. Keyset for infinite scroll/public APIs; OFFSET for page-number admin UIs. Prefer hasMore over count(*).

nodes.label: Instance fields become useRef
nodes.rationale: Timer ids, sockets and caches persist without triggering a render. useState would re-render on every assignment.

nodes.label: Three lifecycles collapse into one effect
nodes.rationale: Setup covers mount and update, cleanup covers unmount. Mimicking three methods misses the sync model.
nodes.norm_label: three lifecycles collapse into one effect

nodes.label: Class components still supported
nodes.rationale: Not recommended for new code, no new features, not scheduled for removal. defaultProps kept; string refs and legacy context gone.

nodes.label: this.setState merges
nodes.rationale: useState replaces. Porting a state object wholesale silently drops unspread fields.

nodes.label: Silent no-render values
nodes.rationale: null, undefined, true, false, symbols and functions render nothing. Functions warn in development only.

nodes.label: Lowercase component is a silent host element
nodes.rationale: function button() in scope plus <button/> never calls it. No error in either build.
nodes.norm_label: lowercase component is a silent host element

nodes.label: Element type is invalid: undefined
nodes.rationale: Capitalized identifier is undefined — default vs named import. Production: Minified React error #130.

nodes.label: Four conditional forms
nodes.rationale: && for render-or-nothing; ternary for either/or; early return null for the whole component; lookup object for three-plus keyed states.

nodes.label: Early return after every hook
nodes.rationale: A return above a hook changes hook count between renders and throws.

nodes.label: Duplicate keys may omit children
nodes.rationale: React's own warning: children may be duplicated and/or omitted. A missing row with no error is usually this.

nodes.label: Index keys rewrite text in place
nodes.rationale: Measured: index keys do not remount. React keeps DOM nodes and rewrites contents, so uncontrolled input state stays with the slot.
nodes.norm_label: index keys rewrite text in place

nodes.label: Key on the map callback's outermost child
nodes.rationale: A key on an inner element is silent and useless. Shorthand <> cannot take a key — syntax error; use Fragment.
nodes.norm_label: key on the map callback's outermost child

nodes.label: Stable keys move DOM nodes
nodes.rationale: key={item.id} moves real nodes and rewrites no text. Same three Row instances either way.

nodes.label: Missing-key warning is deduplicated
nodes.rationale: The first offending list with a given parent tag warns; later ones stay silent even in other components. Absence proves nothing.

nodes.label: Fragment allows only key and children
nodes.rationale: No DOM node, so className or onClick warn. Need a real element to style or listen.
nodes.norm_label: fragment allows only key and children

nodes.label: Fragment occupies a React-tree position
nodes.rationale: Transparent to depth while it stays a fragment. Swapping a fragment for a div is a type change and destroys subtree state.

nodes.label: Shorthand fragment accepts no attributes
nodes.rationale: <> cannot take key — syntax error. Keyed dt/dd lists need <Fragment key={…}>.

nodes.label: Phase 1 gate
nodes.rationale: Hand-compile JSX including key; say what a swapped list does with index vs stable keys; explain {items.length && <List/>}.

nodes.label: sandbox/react-p1
nodes.rationale: Every console block comes from a named script run on Node 24.19.0 / Firefox 153.0. Scratch stays under sandbox/react-p1/tmp/.

nodes.label: Phase 1 — JSX and what a component returns
nodes.norm_label: phase 1 — jsx and what a component returns

nodes.label: Do not call components as functions
nodes.rationale: Header() has no fiber: hooks belong to the caller, no independent state or bail-out.
nodes.norm_label: do not call components as functions

nodes.label: Capitalization decides host vs component
nodes.rationale: Lowercase compiles to a string (host). Uppercase compiles to the identifier. Hyphen is a custom element. Any member expression is a component.

nodes.label: The && zero trap
nodes.rationale: && returns the falsy left operand. 0, NaN, -0 and 0n render as text. Put a boolean on the left.

nodes.label: Conditionals decide identity
nodes.rationale: Same type at the same depth keeps the instance. Different depth remounts. && / ternary-to-null unmount when false.

nodes.label: Wrapper div breaks HTML nesting and flex
nodes.rationale: div inside tr is invalid HTML and a hydration error. A wrapper inside flex/grid becomes the item; intended children are no longer laid out.
nodes.norm_label: wrapper div breaks html nesting and flex

nodes.label: Two folklore contradictions
nodes.rationale: Index keys do not remount; the missing-key warning is suppressed after the first offending parent tag.

nodes.label: Load-bearing pages 01, 02, 04, 07
nodes.rationale: JSX-as-a-call, embedding expressions, attributes vs props, and lists/keys are the four to read if you read only four.

nodes.label: fetch Response body is single-use
nodes.rationale: An unread body holds its pooled connection. Consume or cancel every body including error paths.

nodes.label: TCP is a byte stream
nodes.rationale: TCP preserves order and delivery, not grouping. Three writes can arrive as one data event.

nodes.label: req is a readable stream
nodes.rationale: There is no req.body. An unbounded read is a denial-of-service vector.

nodes.label: Mid-stream body size limit
nodes.rationale: Content-Length is a client claim and is absent on chunked transfers. Count bytes as they arrive.

nodes.label: value={x ?? ''} fix
nodes.rationale: ?? only replaces null and undefined. || also wipes 0 and empty string.

nodes.label: Mode is value === undefined
nodes.rationale: Decided on first render and must not change. Empty string and 0 are controlled; null and missing are not.

nodes.label: Why hooks replaced HOCs
nodes.rationale: Silent prop collisions and unreadable wrapper stacks. Hooks name values at the call site.

nodes.label: Why hooks replaced render props
nodes.rationale: No extra tree nodes, values usable anywhere in the component, linear composition, better types.

nodes.label: Mutating a prop appears to work
nodes.rationale: The write and the read are microseconds apart. Failure arrives later via remount, siblings, memo, StrictMode or abandoned renders.
nodes.norm_label: mutating a prop appears to work

nodes.label: PureComponent and mutation are exclusive
nodes.rationale: A mutated same-reference update is silently dropped. Wrong UI, no warning.

nodes.label: What StrictMode cannot catch
nodes.rationale: Production-only paths, unrun branches, idempotent writes, event handlers, later-update effects. A clean run is not proof.

nodes.label: useRef guard is the wrong StrictMode fix
nodes.rationale: Hides the symptom. The effect still cannot be remounted safely under navigation or Activity.
nodes.norm_label: useref guard is the wrong strictmode fix

nodes.label: Writing a ref during render
nodes.rationale: A ref exists before the render. Mutability by design does not exempt it.

nodes.label: Eight legitimate dependency-removal moves
nodes.rationale: Move outside, move inside, depend on primitives, call during render, updater form, useEffectEvent, event handler, split effects.

nodes.label: Edit the code, not the array
nodes.rationale: You cannot choose dependencies. To remove one, prove to the linter it is not read.
nodes.norm_label: edit the code, not the array

nodes.label: Four object-and-function moves
nodes.rationale: Move static values outside the component; construct dynamic ones inside the effect; depend on primitives; call a function prop during render.

nodes.label: Objects and functions differ if created at different times
nodes.rationale: Object.is fails every render for a literal created in the component body. Contents did not change; identity did.
nodes.norm_label: objects and functions differ if created at different times

nodes.label: Split into several Effects
nodes.rationale: Different parts that re-run for different reasons belong in different Effects.

nodes.label: One effect per concern
nodes.rationale: Merging concerns unions their dependency lists, so each concern tears down for the other's reasons.

nodes.label: Reactive values
nodes.rationale: Props and all variables and functions declared directly inside the component. Setters, dispatch, and ref objects are stable and not dependencies.

nodes.label: You cannot choose Effect dependencies
nodes.rationale: Every reactive value the setup reads must be declared. The list is determined by the surrounding code.

nodes.label: Measure then place
nodes.rationale: Tooltip renders anywhere, measures height, re-renders in the right place. Two renders either way; layout effect only hides the first.

nodes.label: useLayoutEffect blocks paint
nodes.rationale: The guarantee is the blocking: React refuses to let the browser paint until the code and its state updates finish. Prefer useEffect.

nodes.label: VACUUM does not shrink index files
nodes.norm_label: vacuum does not shrink index files

nodes.label: An effect chain cannot be replayed
nodes.rationale: It is attached to state changing, not to the user acting. Undo, history, and time-travel re-fire the whole cascade.
nodes.norm_label: an effect chain cannot be replayed

nodes.label: Compute all next state in the event handler
nodes.rationale: A chain of effects is often stored derived values. Compute during render; put the rest in the one handler that knows a card was played.
nodes.norm_label: compute all next state in the event handler

nodes.label: Lift state up instead of copying it
nodes.rationale: If two components need the same value, the question is which one should own it, not how to copy it with an Effect.
nodes.norm_label: lift state up instead of copying it

nodes.label: Notify the parent in the same event
nodes.rationale: An Effect calling onChange(isOn) runs too late and costs two renders. Calling setIsOn and onChange in the same handler batches into one.
nodes.norm_label: notify the parent in the same event

nodes.label: Phase 13 — Routing, structure and the app shell
nodes.norm_label: phase 13 — routing, structure and the app shell

nodes.label: Four state buckets
nodes.rationale: Server state, URL state, form state, and UI state. Most global state is a cache of somebody else's data.

nodes.label: Phase 12 — Data and state in a real app
nodes.norm_label: phase 12 — data and state in a real app

nodes.label: Phase 10 — Server Components and Server Functions
nodes.norm_label: phase 10 — server components and server functions

nodes.label: Phase 11 — Server rendering, hydration and the DOM APIs
nodes.norm_label: phase 11 — server rendering, hydration and the dom apis

nodes.label: Do not clobber core req/res properties
nodes.rationale: Do not overwrite req.url, method, headers, query, params, or res.end/json wholesale. Routing and security depend on them.
nodes.norm_label: do not clobber core req/res properties

nodes.label: Namespaced req.ctx
nodes.rationale: Docs do not enumerate a reserved list; treat request and response references as the list. A single namespaced object is the safe habit.

nodes.label: Open redirect via res.redirect
nodes.rationale: Never res.redirect(userInput) unchecked; allow-list relative paths. Cross-link Node SSRF and open-redirect pages.

nodes.label: query parser default simple
nodes.rationale: Express 5 default is simple not extended; nested a[b]=1 becomes a literal key; proto pollution vector is off by default.

nodes.label: Body parsers and size limits
nodes.rationale: express.json and urlencoded with hard size limits are a DoS control; empty-body and malformed JSON have their own error path.

nodes.label: Generated tsvector column
nodes.rationale: Same speed as an expression index (17.87 vs 17.36ms). Chosen to combine columns, carry weights, and stop expression-mismatch misses. coalesce required.

nodes.label: setweight A–D
nodes.rationale: Default rank weights {0.1,0.2,0.4,1.0} for D–A. Title match counts 5× a body match. Weights do nothing until ranking.

nodes.label: ts_rank
nodes.rationale: Not indexable. Index finds matches; rank runs on each. Narrow the match rather than optimise the rank.

nodes.label: ts_rank_cd
nodes.rationale: Also accounts for cover density. Better for multi-word queries. Not bounded 0–1.

nodes.label: AFTER trigger
nodes.rationale: Return value is ignored; the row is already written. Use to react: audit, notify, cascade.

nodes.label: Alphabetical trigger firing order
nodes.rationale: Fires by trigger name, not creation order. Prefix 01_/02_/03_ if order matters.

nodes.label: BEFORE trigger
