nodes.rationale: Can modify NEW and cancel the row with RETURN NULL. Use to change the row (updated_at, normalisation).

nodes.label: RETURN NULL cancels the row
nodes.rationale: Silent drop: 10 submitted, 5 stored, rowCount reported 5. Prefer RAISE EXCEPTION when the caller should know.

nodes.label: Row vs statement trigger
nodes.rationale: One UPDATE of 1000 rows: 1000 row firings, 1 statement firing. Statement triggers also fire on zero-row statements.

nodes.label: Transition tables
nodes.rationale: REFERENCING OLD TABLE / NEW TABLE lets a statement trigger audit bulk changes in one insert.

nodes.label: PostgreSQL triggers
nodes.rationale: A trigger runs code the application cannot see, skip, or ask for. Right for data invariants; wrong for business behaviour and external side effects.

nodes.label: Trigger WHEN clause
nodes.rationale: Evaluated before the plpgsql call. Measured 0.86× of an unconditional row trigger. Cannot be used on INSTEAD OF.

nodes.label: Express 5 async error forwarding
nodes.rationale: Rejected promises from async handlers forward to next(err) automatically.

nodes.label: Controller service repository wiring
nodes.rationale: Controllers parse HTTP and call services; services own rules; repositories own queries. Mechanism stays in Node.

nodes.label: createApp factory
nodes.rationale: Pure function returns app; no listen inside; inject db/redis/queue clients so tests import the factory.

nodes.label: reset soft mixed hard
nodes.rationale: All three move HEAD. mixed also resets the index. hard also overwrites the working tree and is the only variant that can destroy uncommitted work.

nodes.label: Number vs parseInt prefixes
nodes.rationale: Number understands 0x, 0o, 0b. parseInt honours 0x but parseInt('0o755') and parseInt('0b1010') are 0. Always pass radix 10.

nodes.label: Octal file-mode literal 0o755
nodes.rationale: 0o755 is decimal 493. chmod(path, 755) silently sets wrong permissions. Legacy 0755 is SyntaxError in strict/modules.

nodes.label: & is looser than ===
nodes.rationale: flags&MASK===0 parses as flags&(MASK===0). Write (flags&MASK)!==0.

nodes.label: Bitwise permission flag set
nodes.rationale: 1<<n, combine with |, test (flags&MASK)!==0, add |=, remove &= ~MASK, toggle ^=. Prefer Set of strings in app code.

nodes.label: Inferred function .name
nodes.rationale: Assigned functions pick up the binding name. Only never-bound expressions have name ''. Named expressions appear in stack traces.

nodes.label: Named function expression inner binding
nodes.rationale: const fact=function inner(n){…} — inner is visible only inside the body, a recursion handle that survives reassignment of fact.

nodes.label: this is bound at call time
nodes.rationale: Not a property of the function. Behaves like a hidden first parameter the call site fills in.
nodes.norm_label: this is bound at call time

nodes.label: this is an argument not a variable
nodes.rationale: Decided by how a function is called, not where it was written. Look at the call site, not the definition.
nodes.norm_label: this is an argument not a variable

nodes.label: Concise arrow body
nodes.rationale: Expression position only. if and return are SyntaxError. Ternary and ?? remain legal.

nodes.label: Arrow object-literal trap
nodes.rationale: n => { value: n } is a labelled statement returning undefined. One property parses; two properties are SyntaxError. Parenthesise: ({value: n}).

nodes.label: Arrow this in an object literal
nodes.rationale: Neither method nor function-valued property gives lexical this. An arrow in a literal captures enclosing this, undefined at module top level.
nodes.norm_label: arrow this in an object literal

nodes.label: Arrow-function class field
nodes.rationale: Own property per instance whose this is lexical. Survives being detached as a callback. Cost: one function per instance and it cannot be super-called.

nodes.label: Base backups and WAL archiving
nodes.rationale: Physical backup + WAL archive enables PITR. archive_command failure fills pg_wal and becomes an outage.

nodes.label: Archiving fails dangerously
nodes.rationale: Unlike pg_dump, a failing archive_command retains WAL on disk until the disk fills — a backup problem becomes an outage.

nodes.label: #field in obj brand check
nodes.rationale: Asks whether the object was constructed by this class. More trustworthy than instanceof. Only legal inside the declaring class body. Avoids try/catch around private access.

nodes.label: constructor back-reference
nodes.rationale: An own property of Fn.prototype pointing back at Fn. Replacing prototype wholesale discards it. Writable and forgeable — never use it for type checks.

nodes.label: Strings are immutable
nodes.rationale: Every string method returns a new string, so no defensive copy is needed.

nodes.label: String trim family
nodes.rationale: Removes Unicode whitespace, takes no argument, and belongs at the input boundary. Use Start/End names, not Left/Right.

nodes.label: stringify throws on BigInt and cycles
nodes.rationale: BigInt refusal forces an explicit serialisation. A cycle is a hard limit; structuredClone clones but does not produce a string.
nodes.norm_label: stringify throws on bigint and cycles

nodes.label: reviver context.source
nodes.rationale: value is already a double past MAX_SAFE_INTEGER. context.source is the original text, only for primitives.

nodes.label: Object rest omit-a-key
nodes.rationale: const { password, ...safeUser } = user builds a new object without mutating. Shallow; own enumerable only.

nodes.label: Spread versus rest
nodes.rationale: Same dots, opposite direction. Rest collects and must be last; spread expands in a call or literal.

nodes.label: Low-cardinality metric labels
nodes.rationale: route is the template (/orders/:id), never the raw URL or userId. Unbounded labels kill Prometheus.

nodes.label: Metric cardinality
nodes.rationale: Each unique label combination is a separate time series. userId, orderId, full URL, or exception message unbounded-series the cluster.

nodes.label: Active handles and requests
nodes.rationale: Open servers, timers, sockets keep the loop alive — correct for a server, a bug for a CLI that should exit. Underscore APIs are not a public contract.

nodes.label: Uncleared timers and handles
nodes.rationale: setInterval without clearInterval, plus unclosed servers, Redis clients, and fs.watch keep the process from settling.

nodes.label: /metrics endpoint
nodes.rationale: Internal only — NetworkPolicy, sidecar scrape, or a separate port. Same public API hostname without auth is a leak.

nodes.label: Prometheus pull scrape
nodes.rationale: Prometheus scrapes GET /metrics. Pull keeps service discovery, failure detection, and timestamps with the collector. Pushgateway is for short-lived jobs.

nodes.label: Cache stampede
nodes.rationale: Many concurrent misses on one expired hot key overload the origin. Mitigate with single-flight, distributed locks, jittered TTLs, or stale-while-revalidate.

nodes.label: Single-flight cache fill
nodes.rationale: In-process Map of inflight promises collapses concurrent misses in one process. Does not protect a 20-pod fleet.

nodes.label: Honest staging
nodes.rationale: SQLite in staging while prod uses Postgres is a lie for dialects, transactions, and concurrency.

nodes.label: Environment parity
nodes.rationale: Parity is runtime version, config shape, and dependency graph — not copying production secrets onto laptops.

nodes.label: Distroless Node image
nodes.rationale: Minimal shell and package manager reduce attack surface; debug with kubectl debug, not bash.

nodes.label: Node image hardening checklist
nodes.rationale: Non-root USER, read-only root FS, no secrets in layers, pin digests, drop capabilities.

nodes.label: Logical replication
nodes.rationale: Copies decoded row changes, not WAL bytes. Cross-major-version, per-table, writable target. Wrong tool for HA.

nodes.label: Replica identity
nodes.rationale: How the subscriber identifies the row for UPDATE/DELETE. Default PK. Without it inserts work and the first update fails.

nodes.label: Replication slot
nodes.rationale: Guarantees WAL retention until consumed. An abandoned slot fills the publisher disk. Alert on inactive + retained; set max_slot_wal_keep_size.

nodes.label: Sequences are not replicated
nodes.rationale: The single most common upgrade-day failure: 23505 unique violations on first insert after cutover.

nodes.label: Logical-replication upgrade path
nodes.rationale: Near-zero downtime because publisher and subscriber may differ in major version. Downtime is stop-writes, advance sequences, flip the connection string.

nodes.label: Minor vs major upgrade
nodes.rationale: 18.3→18.4 is a restart; 17→18 is a data migration. On-disk format is the dividing line.

nodes.label: pg_upgrade
nodes.rationale: Migrates the catalog rather than rewriting rows. Run --check days in advance with the old server still running.

nodes.label: pg_upgrade --link / --swap
nodes.rationale: Trade rollback for speed. After the new cluster starts (link) or transfer begins (swap), the old cluster is unsafe. Verified backup is the only rollback.

nodes.label: Post-upgrade statistics
nodes.rationale: PG18 transfers most optimizer stats (not CREATE STATISTICS). Still run vacuumdb --all --analyze-in-stages.

nodes.label: archive_command
nodes.rationale: A failing archive_command is an outage: unarchived WAL is retained until the disk fills. Alert on pg_stat_archiver.failed_count.

nodes.label: import.meta.dirname
nodes.rationale: ESM replacement for __dirname on Node 21.2+; undefined for non-file: URLs.

nodes.label: fileURLToPath and pathToFileURL
nodes.rationale: file:// plus a path is wrong: spaces need %20 and Windows drives need conversion.

nodes.label: fs.rm recursive force
nodes.rationale: Replaces deprecated rmdir recursive (DEP0147). force makes a missing path a no-op for finally cleanup.

nodes.label: Boot-time orphan temp sweeper
nodes.rationale: SIGKILL leaks temp dirs. Sweep stale .incoming-* with a grace period so in-flight uploads survive boot.

nodes.label: ino plus dev file identity
nodes.rationale: Hard links, symlinks, bind mounts and case-insensitive filesystems make path comparison lie. ino is unreliable on Windows.

nodes.label: Hard link
nodes.rationale: Second name for the same inode; one filesystem only. Space is freed when last link and last fd are gone.

nodes.label: stat.mode file-type bits
nodes.rationale: Mask with 0o777 before comparing. A 644 file reports 0o100644. Always write octal literals.

nodes.label: umask
nodes.rationale: Per-process mask of bits to remove. mode is a maximum: requested 0o666 with umask 022 becomes 644.

nodes.label: server.keepAliveTimeout
nodes.rationale: Default 5s. If a proxy idle timeout is longer, reuse of a closing socket surfaces as 502.

nodes.label: Proxy 502 from keepAliveTimeout race
nodes.rationale: Raise server.keepAliveTimeout above the proxy idle timeout (65s vs ALB 60s) and keep headersTimeout higher.

nodes.label: node:http — the server
nodes.rationale: createServer hands you two streams. Frameworks are a router on exactly this.

nodes.label: Request bodies are streams
nodes.rationale: There is no req.body. An unbounded read is a denial-of-service you wrote yourself.

nodes.label: fetch
nodes.rationale: Global stable undici fetch. Two outage behaviours: no throw on HTTP errors, unread bodies pin the pool.

nodes.label: Outbound timeouts
nodes.rationale: A fetch with no timeout has no upper bound. One slow dependency takes down the service.

nodes.label: find() returns a cursor
nodes.rationale: Nothing is sent until toArray() or iteration. 200000 docs: 486 MB RSS vs 143 MB iterating.

nodes.label: pool.query buffers the result
nodes.rationale: 500000 rows: 300 MB RSS vs 111 MB Cursor.read(1000). Peak memory scales with the result, enough to OOM a 256 MB container.

nodes.label: Hooks are per-operation
nodes.rationale: pre('save') does not fire for updates. Password hashing in pre-save plus updateOne writes plaintext.

nodes.label: Validators skip on update
nodes.rationale: updateOne wrote a 40-character name past maxlength 30. Pass runValidators: true; they only see fields in the update.

nodes.label: Point-in-time recovery
nodes.rationale: PITR trades procedure for precision: more steps than a logical restore, in exchange for landing on the exact second before the damage. Value is contingent on rehearsal.

nodes.label: recovery_target_action pause
nodes.rationale: Default pause lets you verify the landing point before promoting; promote immediately forecloses a retry.

nodes.label: Recovery time objective
nodes.rationale: A restore you have never timed is not a recovery plan, it is a hope.

nodes.label: PostgreSQL timelines
nodes.rationale: A new timeline after recovery keeps original WAL history intact so a wrong PITR is not fatal.

nodes.label: hot_standby_feedback
nodes.rationale: Eliminates early-cleanup conflicts by exporting the standby snapshot into the primary vacuum horizon, causing primary bloat.

nodes.label: Hot-standby recovery conflict
nodes.rationale: Replay of primary VACUUM can cancel a replica SELECT with retryable SQLSTATE 40001.

nodes.label: 08.2 Query conflicts and routing reads safely
nodes.norm_label: 08.2 query conflicts and routing reads safely

nodes.label: Expand and contract
nodes.rationale: A rename is three deploys: add nullable, write both, drop old later. Old and new code run together during rollout.

nodes.label: Migrations as a gated deploy step
nodes.rationale: Not at app boot: every instance races and a failure crash-loops. Use a DDL role the app does not have.
nodes.norm_label: migrations as a gated deploy step

nodes.label: Factory with defaults and overrides
nodes.rationale: Sensible valid defaults plus a spread override. Each test names only the field it is about. A schema change is a one-place edit.

nodes.label: Shared fixture rot
nodes.rationale: A shared JSON imported by 40 tests cannot change, hides the subject field, and goes stale when the state machine adds required fields.

nodes.label: 100% coverage is actively harmful
nodes.rationale: Rewards assertion-free tests, makes defensive code a liability, ends in istanbul ignore comments, and buys false confidence.

nodes.label: Coverage threshold as a ratchet
nodes.rationale: Set slightly below current (80 when at 84) to fail large untested additions. Do not ratchet toward 100.

nodes.label: Four ways a load test lies
nodes.rationale: No warmup (JIT/cold caches), generator is the bottleneck, one hot cached row, and reporting the average. A 45 ms mean can hide a 4-second p99.
nodes.norm_label: four ways a load test lies

nodes.label: Report p99 not the average
nodes.rationale: With 100 requests per page load, most sessions hit the tail. Report p50, p95, p99 and max. Also check event-loop lag and memory after the run.

nodes.label: Backpressure
nodes.rationale: write() returning false means stop. Ignoring it exhausts memory. Gate: stream-process a file larger than RAM with errors propagating.

nodes.label: Phase 3 — Buffers and streams
nodes.rationale: Buffer, encodings, allocUnsafe. Four stream types. Backpressure is the streaming concept. pipeline over pipe.

nodes.label: RETURNING
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL returns affected rows in one round trip. MySQL ERROR 1064 near returning.

nodes.label: UPDATE … ORDER BY … LIMIT
nodes.rationale: MySQL allows a bounded ordered UPDATE. PostgreSQL syntax error at order. On PG use WHERE id IN (SELECT id … ORDER BY … LIMIT n).

nodes.label: jsonb_build_object allowlist
nodes.rationale: Explicit keys so a new column does not leak into the client payload, unlike to_jsonb(row).

nodes.label: Shape JSON in JS not SQL
nodes.rationale: jsonb_agg 284.8 ms vs flat join + JS 90.7 ms; json_agg 131.2 ms. Use SQL constructors when the shape is the point.
nodes.norm_label: shape json in js not sql

nodes.label: Plain REFRESH AccessExclusiveLock
nodes.rationale: Readers waited 32 ms of a 142 ms plain REFRESH. CONCURRENTLY waited 2 ms. No incremental refresh exists.

nodes.label: REFRESH CONCURRENTLY unique index
nodes.rationale: CONCURRENTLY diffs old against new and needs a key. Without a unique index it raises 55000. 1.6× slower than plain REFRESH.

nodes.label: SCRAM-SHA-256 verifier
nodes.rationale: Since PostgreSQL 14 the default store is a verifier in pg_authid.rolpassword, not the password. The exposure is CREATE ROLE … PASSWORD plaintext in logs and pg_stat_activity; \password computes the verifier client-side.

nodes.label: ALTER ROLE PASSWORD plaintext in the log
nodes.rationale: The database stores a SCRAM verifier while the logger writes the plaintext statement. Use \password or SET LOCAL log_statement=none around the change.
nodes.norm_label: alter role password plaintext in the log

nodes.label: VALID UNTIL and CONNECTION LIMIT
nodes.rationale: Role attributes, not grants. CONNECTION LIMIT 1 yields 53300. Expired VALID UNTIL reports 28P01, identical to a wrong password, and only affects password auth.

nodes.label: Short-lived credentials
nodes.rationale: A leak with a deadline beats storage choice. pg accepts a password function invoked per new connection for IAM tokens. VALID UNTIL revokes without a deploy.

nodes.label: Parameters cannot be identifiers
nodes.rationale: ORDER BY $1 sorts by a constant string with no error. Table, column, and ASC/DESC slots are structure, not values.

nodes.label: Extended query protocol
nodes.rationale: Parse then bind. Multi-statement text fails with 42601. An empty params array stays on the simple protocol.

nodes.label: format %I identifier quoting
nodes.rationale: For genuinely unknown names, format('%I') quotes the payload as one identifier. %s quotes nothing.

nodes.label: Identifier allowlist
nodes.rationale: Map user input to a hard-coded identifier and reject the rest. Interpolate only your own object values.

nodes.label: 65535 parameter ceiling
nodes.rationale: The protocol stores the count in 16 bits. 21845 three-column rows succeed; one more fails with 08P01.

nodes.label: Parameterized queries
nodes.rationale: Values go in as $1, never into the SQL string. Safety is the wire protocol, not escaping.

nodes.label: Simple query protocol
nodes.rationale: The SQL string is a script and may contain several statements. Concatenated ORDER BY dropped a table in one request.

nodes.label: Optional filter $1 IS NULL OR col = $1
nodes.rationale: One statement serves filtered and unfiltered lists so the plan cache stays warm. Cast $1 so the type can be inferred.
nodes.norm_label: optional filter $1 is null or col = $1

nodes.label: format %I %L %s
nodes.rationale: %I quotes identifiers, %L quotes literals, %s does nothing. Application values still belong in $1 parameters.

nodes.label: unnest bulk-parameter bridge
nodes.rationale: 5000 rows through exactly 3 parameters. One statement shape forever, so the plan cache does not fragment.

nodes.label: unnest
nodes.rationale: Several arrays unnest in parallel, not as a cross join. Shorter arrays pad with NULL.

nodes.label: VALUES as a table
nodes.rationale: SELECT FROM (VALUES …) AS t(cols) joins a client list without a temp table. Types are inferred from the first row.

nodes.label: max_connections
nodes.rationale: Default 100, postmaster context, restart-only. Sizes shared memory whether slots are used. superuser_reserved_connections=3 is the last-resort admin reserve. Failure is FATAL: sorry, too many clients already.

nodes.label: Process-per-connection
nodes.rationale: postgres forks a backend per connection with its own caches, prepared statements and snapshot. Isolation is the gain; memory and fork cost are why max_connections=500 is almost never the answer.

nodes.label: max_client_conn vs default_pool_size
nodes.rationale: max_client_conn (default 100) bounds cheap connections to PgBouncer. default_pool_size (default 20) bounds expensive backends per user/database pair.

nodes.label: A smaller pool is usually faster
nodes.rationale: Past cores × 2, extra backends add contention not throughput. Size default_pool_size small and query_wait_timeout short, or neither. Large max_client_conn, small default_pool_size.
nodes.norm_label: a smaller pool is usually faster

nodes.label: autovacuum_work_mem
nodes.rationale: Caps background vacuum so N workers cannot each claim the large maintenance_work_mem used for interactive index builds.

nodes.label: maintenance_work_mem
nodes.rationale: One maintenance op per session — safer to raise than work_mem. Autovacuum multiplies it by worker count; decouple with autovacuum_work_mem.

nodes.label: fsync = off risks corruption
nodes.rationale: Never off on real data. synchronous_commit = off is the safe durability trade: can lose recent commits, no corruption.

nodes.label: synchronous_commit
nodes.rationale: Safe way to trade durability for speed. With empty synchronous_standby_names, remote_apply/remote_write/local behave like on.

nodes.label: jsonlog destination
nodes.rationale: Structured JSON per line. Prefer over regex on log_line_prefix when shipping logs.

nodes.label: log_line_prefix
nodes.rationale: Default is only timestamp and PID. Add %u@%d %a %e. %a only works if services set application_name.

nodes.label: Managed PostgreSQL
nodes.rationale: Which of the previous twelve topics are still your job. Provider facts checked 2026-08-13 and move fast.

nodes.label: Managed hosting removes sysadmin not application work
nodes.rationale: Backups, replicas, failover, patching become theirs. Missing indexes, long transactions, connection exhaustion and locking migrations remain yours — and cause most incidents.
nodes.norm_label: managed hosting removes sysadmin not application work

nodes.label: Most likely disaster is a bad write
nodes.rationale: Replicas faithfully replicate a bad DELETE. Only PITR with a long enough retention window helps. Retention is chosen against how long a bug might go unnoticed.
nodes.norm_label: most likely disaster is a bad write

nodes.label: Measured RTO from a drill
nodes.rationale: Logical restore measured at 4× dump time. -j 4 bought nothing when one table held 97% of the data. If RTO exceeds the business assumption, that is the finding.

nodes.label: -c vs -f vs stdin
nodes.rationale: Several -c flags are separate statements/transactions. -c does not expand psql variables. Use -f or stdin when :var is involved.

nodes.label: -c does not interpolate
nodes.rationale: Identical -v variable and query: syntax error at or near ":" via -c; correct answer 4 via stdin or -f.

nodes.label: Half-open time ranges
nodes.rationale: BETWEEN is inclusive on both ends so monthly reports double-count midnight. Use >= start AND < end.

nodes.label: date_trunc bucketing
nodes.rationale: Returns a timestamp so it sorts and indexes. Pass a timezone or a Berlin 00:30 order lands in the previous UTC day. Prefer over to_char grouping.

nodes.label: Predicates that defeat indexes
nodes.rationale: An index on col serves a predicate on bare col. date(created_at), lower(email), or col + 1 require a rewrite or a matching expression index.

nodes.label: LIKE ILIKE and POSIX regex
nodes.rationale: Btree serves only anchored LIKE prefix. ILIKE and leading-wildcard LIKE need lower() plus expression index or pg_trgm. Escape user wildcards.

nodes.label: count(DISTINCT) after fan-out
nodes.rationale: Rescues counts only. sum(DISTINCT o.total) collapses two orders that happen to share a total. There is no useful sum(DISTINCT) for money.

nodes.label: Join fan-out
nodes.rationale: A joined parent row is repeated once per child. sum(o.total) after joining items returned 450 against a true 350. The join does not corrupt data; it changes grain.

nodes.label: Result grain
nodes.rationale: What one row represents. A join sets grain to the finest side. An aggregate is only correct on columns at that grain. Detect fan-out with count(*) versus count(DISTINCT parent.id).

nodes.label: Pre-aggregate then join
nodes.rationale: Reduce the child to one row per parent before joining so the grain stays one row per parent. LEFT JOIN plus coalesce so parents with no children survive as 0.

nodes.label: Join cardinality from FK
nodes.rationale: Child to parent via a NOT NULL FK yields exactly one row per child. Parent to child yields the children and silently drops unmatched parents. A nullable FK removes the guarantee both ways.

nodes.label: INNER JOIN matching pairs
nodes.rationale: Output is the set of pairs that satisfy ON. Simultaneously a filter (no match → dropped) and a multiplier (N matches → N copies). JOIN is INNER JOIN; INNER is optional.

nodes.label: Semi and anti joins
nodes.rationale: A semi join answers whether a match exists without emitting the matched row, so it cannot fan out. Its negation, the anti join, has a quietly broken spelling: NOT IN.

nodes.label: EXISTS semi join
nodes.rationale: Filters the left side by whether a match exists, short-circuits, emits the left row at most once, exposes no right-hand columns. Must be correlated.

nodes.label: INTERSECT
nodes.rationale: Whole-row intersection; same customers-with-orders answer as a semi join but compares entire rows and deduplicates. INTERSECT ALL keeps min(count_left, count_right).

nodes.label: Comma join silent CROSS JOIN
nodes.rationale: FROM a, b WHERE … is an inner join, but omitting the condition is a silent cross join. Explicit JOIN … ON makes the same omission a syntax error.

nodes.label: JOIN plus DISTINCT costs 2.5×
nodes.rationale: HashAggregate at 189.98 ms versus Hash Semi Join at 73–91 ms. The join materialises duplicates then hashes them away; a semi join never produces them.

nodes.label: In-place increment SET qty = qty + 1
nodes.rationale: When the new value is a function of the old one, compute it in SQL. Otherwise FOR UPDATE, optimistic version, or SERIALIZABLE plus 40001 retry.

nodes.label: Lost update from read-modify-write
nodes.rationale: 20 concurrent SELECT-then-UPDATE increments produced 2 with no errors. SET qty = qty + 1 produced 20 under a row lock.

nodes.label: format %I for dynamic identifiers
nodes.rationale: Quotes as an identifier so a DROP payload becomes a nonexistent column name. %L quotes literals; %s quotes nothing. Values in app code still use $1.

nodes.label: format placeholders
nodes.rationale: %I identifier, %L literal, %s unquoted. Injection payload became a quoted column name rather than executed SQL.

nodes.label: Identifier allowlist
nodes.rationale: User input selects a key in a map of hard-coded identifiers. Interpolated text never comes from the request. Injection payload rejected 400 before SQL.

nodes.label: Parameters cannot be identifiers
nodes.rationale: ORDER BY $1 sorts by a constant string. name and price produced identical order with no error. Allowlist columns or format %I.

nodes.label: Gap filling with generate_series
nodes.rationale: LEFT JOIN from the series so empty days survive. count(e.id) not count(*) or every gap reads 1. Planner assumes 1000 SRF rows.

nodes.label: generate_series
nodes.rationale: Set-returning function. Both endpoints inclusive so one day hourly is 25 rows. Descending needs a negative step or silently no rows. Step 0 raises 22023.

nodes.label: pg parses date as local midnight
nodes.rationale: TZ=Asia/Calcutta turns 2026-03-01 into 2026-02-28T18:30:00.000Z. Return the day as to_char text so the driver cannot reinterpret it.
nodes.norm_label: pg parses date as local midnight

nodes.label: date_trunc uses session time zone
nodes.rationale: UTC server groups by UTC days. An 18:00+00 order is already tomorrow in Delhi. Name AT TIME ZONE explicitly. Bug only appears for rows past local midnight.

nodes.label: HashAggregate Batches spill
nodes.rationale: Batches: 1 fits. Batches: 5 with Disk Usage 3696kB spilled (PG 13+ partitions instead of exceeding work_mem). 59.57 ms → 117.68 ms at work_mem=64kB.

nodes.label: work_mem is per node per worker
nodes.rationale: A plan with three hashes and three sorts peaks at a multiple of the setting. Raise with SET LOCAL inside a transaction, never globally.
nodes.norm_label: work_mem is per node per worker

nodes.label: A row containing NULL is not NULL
nodes.rationale: count(DISTINCT (status, coupon)) is 4 including (open,NULL) and (cancelled,NULL). Composite comparison uses IS NOT DISTINCT FROM per field.
nodes.norm_label: a row containing null is not null

nodes.label: count(DISTINCT (a, b)) row constructor
nodes.rationale: count(DISTINCT a, b) parses as two-argument count and fails 42883. Wrap columns in a row constructor.

nodes.label: lock_timeout
nodes.rationale: Fail fast when waiting on a lock. Use before ALTER TABLE so ACCESS EXCLUSIVE does not queue the whole site.

nodes.label: SET LOCAL lock_timeout in migrations
nodes.rationale: SET LOCAL reverts at commit. Plain SET on a pooled connection leaks into later app queries. 55P03 is the good fail-fast outcome.

nodes.label: Controlled API naming
nodes.rationale: value/onChange, checked/onChange, open/onOpenChange, defaultX for the uncontrolled initial. Call the handler with the next value.

nodes.label: Inverse data flow
nodes.rationale: Data down as props, changes up as function calls. Name handlers for the event so the owner keeps its state shape private.

nodes.label: pg-cursor streaming
nodes.rationale: Needs a checked-out client. read(n) until empty array, then close() then release(). Live set is one batch regardless of result size.

nodes.label: pool.query buffers the whole result
nodes.rationale: 300000 rows grew the heap by 101 MB, proportional to row count. The first row is unavailable until the last arrives.

nodes.label: ANY($1::int[]) for lists
nodes.rationale: One parameter regardless of list length, so statement text and the plan stay constant and you avoid the 65535-parameter ceiling.

nodes.label: 65535 parameter ceiling
nodes.rationale: Wire protocol encodes the count in 16 bits. 21845 rows × 3 columns succeeds; 21846 fails with 08P01 that does not mention the limit. Batch by floor(65535 / columns).

nodes.label: Per-row INSERT cost
nodes.rationale: 10000 autocommit inserts: 20165 ms. One transaction: 2559 ms (WAL flush once). One unnest statement: 84 ms. 240× spread.

nodes.label: INSERT … SELECT unnest
nodes.rationale: One array parameter per column; statement text is constant. Casts are required. Supports ON CONFLICT and RETURNING. Materialises everything in JS (201 MB heap at 500k rows).

nodes.label: COPY csv vs text format
nodes.rationale: Default is text (tab, \N for NULL). Feeding CSV to default COPY puts the whole line in the first column. In CSV an unquoted empty field is NULL; "" is empty string.

nodes.label: pg-copy-streams COPY FROM STDIN
nodes.rationale: Turns client.query into a writable stream. Needs a checked-out client; COPY puts the connection in a distinct protocol mode.

nodes.label: UNLOGGED staging table for COPY
nodes.rationale: COPY is all-or-nothing with no skip. Load all-text UNLOGGED staging, then INSERT … SELECT with validation, ON CONFLICT and rejects inspectable.

nodes.label: Keyset batching instead of a cursor
nodes.rationale: Each chunk is a short pooled transaction: no long snapshot, no held client, interruptible. A cursor is right only when the export must reflect one point in time.
nodes.norm_label: keyset batching instead of a cursor

nodes.label: COPY vs unnest from Node
nodes.rationale: unnest beat pg-copy-streams by 2.7–3× at 10k/100k/500k because CSV formatting in JS dominates. COPY wins on streaming memory and unlimited size.

nodes.label: pipeline not .pipe() for COPY
nodes.rationale: pipeline propagates errors and destroys both ends. .pipe() leaves the connection stuck mid-COPY and returns a broken client to the pool.

nodes.label: State in two places test
nodes.rationale: If you can delete one copy and compute it from the other, delete it. A draft that is supposed to differ until save is not duplication.

nodes.label: Single source of truth
nodes.rationale: One owner per piece, not all state in one store. The forbidden case is the same information in two places.

nodes.label: Error boundaries stay classes
nodes.rationale: The conversion that cannot be done. A hook cannot implement an error boundary.

nodes.label: HOC wraps around a component
nodes.rationale: A hook cannot wrap from the outside. memo, forwardRef, error boundaries, instrumentation and injected Suspense stay HOC-shaped.

nodes.label: Class components still supported
nodes.rationale: Not recommended for new code and receive no new features. Not scheduled for removal. Read them; do not write them except error boundaries.

nodes.label: Class defaultProps survives
nodes.rationale: Kept because there is no ES6 default-parameter equivalent for a class.

nodes.label: propTypes removed silently in React 19
nodes.rationale: React 19 ignores propTypes with no warning, so an upgrade quietly deletes runtime prop checks.

nodes.label: Move 3 — destructure object props to primitives
nodes.rationale: Destructure during render, not inside setup. A parent that rebuilds options every render then causes no reconnection.
nodes.norm_label: move 3 — destructure object props to primitives

nodes.label: Move 2 — build the object inside the Effect
nodes.rationale: The effect makes the object rather than reading it. What remains is a primitive like roomId. This is the default answer.
nodes.norm_label: move 2 — build the object inside the effect

nodes.label: useLayoutEffect blocks paint
nodes.rationale: The guarantee is the blocking. Code and state updates scheduled inside sit on the critical path. Prefer useEffect when possible.

nodes.label: Measure then place before paint
nodes.rationale: A tooltip renders, measures height, re-renders in the right place. Two renders either way; useLayoutEffect only decides whether the user sees the first.

nodes.label: Automatic batching
nodes.rationale: Multiple setState calls become one render, including inside promises, timeouts and native handlers since React 18; flushSync is the escape.

nodes.label: State is a snapshot
nodes.rationale: The value in a given render is frozen for that render. This is the whole explanation for stale closures, and it is not a bug.

nodes.label: React Compiler v1.0
nodes.rationale: Build-time automatic memoization, stable as of Oct 2025. Changes the ending of the memoization story, not the reasoning.

nodes.label: Rules of Hooks
nodes.rationale: Call at the top level only, from a component or another hook. Hooks are stored positionally; a conditional hook shifts the list.

nodes.label: Preact
nodes.rationale: 13.0 KB min / 5.4 KB gzip vs React 189.8 / 59.2 for the same counter. Near-identical API; no RSC.

nodes.label: Compiler bail-out is silent
nodes.rationale: Conditional hooks leave the function as written. Symptom is a missing speed-up, never a broken build.

nodes.label: React Compiler
nodes.rationale: babel-plugin-react-compiler 1.0.0 since 7 Oct 2025. Per-fiber cache array via react/compiler-runtime. Memoizes JSX itself.

nodes.label: What the compiler compiles
nodes.rationale: Components and hooks that actually call hooks. use-prefixed helpers with no hooks are left alone.

nodes.label: Compiler is React's answer to signals
nodes.rationale: Keep the re-render model; move memoization into a build step.
nodes.norm_label: compiler is react's answer to signals

nodes.label: Signals vs re-render
nodes.rationale: React's unit of update is the component; signals update bindings. Stale closures, deps and memo are consequences of React's choice.

nodes.label: Compiler is not a linter
nodes.rationale: Compiled a component that mutates a prop with no complaint. Validation is eslint-plugin-react-hooks.

nodes.label: Declarative UI
nodes.rationale: Write what the UI is for a given value; never write transitions. Trade-off: give up direct DOM control and pay a diff.

nodes.label: Purity
nodes.rationale: Same inputs, same output; no writes to anything that existed before.

nodes.label: Bail-out is not a promise
nodes.rationale: useState caveat: React may still call your component before skipping children. Safe only because purity is assumed.

nodes.label: Hydration
nodes.rationale: hydrateRoot attaches React to server HTML. Hydration costs roughly a full render's worth of JavaScript.

nodes.label: Partial Pre-rendering
nodes.rationale: React 19.2 resume APIs: prerender a static shell at build time, resume per request to fill dynamic holes.

nodes.label: Construct signature
nodes.rationale: new (...) => T describes a constructor, not an instance. abstract new accepts abstract classes that a plain new rejects.

nodes.label: typeof Class static side
nodes.rationale: Widget is the instance type. typeof Widget is the constructor plus static members. Property 'create' does not exist on type 'Repo' means the static lives on typeof Repo.

nodes.label: $$typeof
nodes.rationale: Symbol mark of a genuine element. Cannot survive JSON, so a server cannot send a fake renderable element — XSS mitigation.

nodes.label: JSX compiles to jsx()
nodes.rationale: Automatic runtime from react/jsx-runtime. Children become a children prop; key is a third argument.

nodes.label: React element
nodes.rationale: Frozen plain object: $$typeof, type, key, props. Not a DOM node. Creating one runs nothing.

nodes.label: Lowercase component is a silent host element
nodes.rationale: function button() in scope + <button/> never calls it. No error in either build.
nodes.norm_label: lowercase component is a silent host element

nodes.label: Element type is invalid … undefined
nodes.rationale: Capitalized identifier is undefined — default vs named import. Production: minified error #130.

nodes.label: Function components
nodes.rationale: React calls it, not you — a new function object per render destroys the subtree.

nodes.label: key is not a prop
nodes.rationale: React 19 installs a non-enumerable getter that warns and returns undefined. Pass the value again under another name.

nodes.label: <Greeting /> does not call Greeting
nodes.rationale: It holds a reference. React decides whether, when, and how many times to call it.

nodes.label: Do not call components as functions
nodes.rationale: Header() has no fiber: hooks belong to the caller, no independent state or bail-out.
nodes.norm_label: do not call components as functions

nodes.label: Capitalization decides host vs component
nodes.rationale: Lowercase → string type (host). Uppercase → identifier. Hyphen → custom element. Member expression is always a component.

nodes.label: Checking is not transpiling
nodes.rationale: A transpiler reads one file; a checker reads the whole program. That structural difference is why esbuild is fast, cannot type-check, and why isolatedModules exists.

nodes.label: tsc --emitDeclarationOnly
nodes.rationale: Transpilers cannot emit .d.ts because declarations need the type graph they skip. Publishing always involves tsc even when JS is bundled elsewhere.

nodes.label: const enum is not erasable
nodes.rationale: const enum disappears by inlining values — a transform — so it errors under erasableSyntaxOnly and isolatedModules. Do not use preserveConstEnums.

nodes.label: erasableSyntaxOnly
nodes.rationale: Makes tsc reject non-erasable syntax with TS1294 at check time. Defaults false in 7.0.2. Enable whenever anything runs .ts directly.

nodes.label: Published libraries always need tsc
nodes.rationale: Node refuses to strip types inside node_modules (ERR_UNSUPPORTED_NODE_MODULES_TYPE_STRIPPING). Libraries ship .js plus .d.ts from tsc.

nodes.label: Three ways to run TypeScript
nodes.rationale: tsc checks then emits; esbuild/swc/Vite/Babel strip and emit without checking; Node 24 strips and executes. Only tsc reads types.

nodes.label: isolatedModules
nodes.rationale: Guarantee every file can be transpiled alone. Rejects type re-exports without export type, const enum, ambient-only scripts.

nodes.label: Separate typecheck and build scripts
nodes.rationale: dev: vite; build: vite build; typecheck: tsc --noEmit; ci: typecheck && test && build. Nothing depends on the build catching type errors.

nodes.label: tsc --noEmit as CI gate
nodes.rationale: Bundlers and Node strip without checking. A required tsc --noEmit with a respected exit code is the only automatic check.

nodes.label: Pair a fast runner with tsc --noEmit
nodes.rationale: Whatever runs the code, tsc --noEmit runs beside it. The build step became optional; the check never did.
nodes.norm_label: pair a fast runner with tsc --noemit

nodes.label: Transpiler is fast because it is blind
nodes.rationale: esbuild deleted a Cart annotation, assigned a string to total, exited 0; runtime TypeError. Speed is skipping the type graph, not doing it better.
nodes.norm_label: transpiler is fast because it is blind

nodes.label: const enum is the worst option
nodes.rationale: Inlines values at call sites — a whole-program transform. Banned by isolatedModules; breaks esbuild/swc/Vite.
nodes.norm_label: const enum is the worst option

nodes.label: instanceof fails across realms and duplicate packages
nodes.norm_label: instanceof fails across realms and duplicate packages

nodes.label: Compiler does not check guard body
nodes.norm_label: compiler does not check guard body

nodes.label: Sandbox artifacts stay inside the project
nodes.rationale: Scratch output is kept inside the project deliberately so sandbox artifacts do not land in the host /tmp. Everything here is regenerable; scripts recreate what they need on each run. Set 2026-08-13.
nodes.norm_label: sandbox artifacts stay inside the project

nodes.label: @import request serialisation
nodes.rationale: Browser cannot discover the imported file until the importer is parsed. 500 ms delay: chained @import FCP 1076 ms vs parallel links 636 ms.

nodes.label: CSS blocks first paint
nodes.rationale: Browser chooses a blank frame over a wrong frame. 47 ms no CSS vs 671 ms with one 600 ms delayed sheet.

nodes.label: Non-matching media does not block paint
nodes.rationale: media=print painted at 38 ms vs 671 ms for a matching sheet. Still downloaded, just not waited for.
nodes.norm_label: non-matching media does not block paint

nodes.label: media print onload flip
nodes.rationale: Load non-critical CSS without blocking; styles land after first paint so only use below the fold.

nodes.label: Form controls do not inherit font
nodes.rationale: UA sets 13.3333px sans-serif on button and input. Explicit declaration beats inheritance; fix is font: inherit.
nodes.norm_label: form controls do not inherit font

nodes.label: User-agent cascade origin
nodes.rationale: Weakest origin: any author rule beats any UA default. !important inverts so user accessibility overrides cannot be defeated.

nodes.label: box-sizing border-box universal
nodes.rationale: Applied to *, *::before, *::after so generated content is not left on content-box.

nodes.label: Modern small reset
nodes.rationale: Six justified lines beat a 300-line library. Normalize.css patched 2012 engine differences that have largely converged.

nodes.label: @layer
nodes.rationale: First mention sets order. Layer order is compared before specificity; unlayered styles beat all layered ones.

nodes.label: Never remove focus outline
nodes.rationale: *:focus { outline: none } is an accessibility defect. Replace with :focus-visible, never delete.

nodes.label: app.listen is createServer sugar
nodes.rationale: app.listen(port) is http.createServer(app).listen(port). Prefer explicit server for TLS, WebSockets, or tests that import app without listening.

nodes.label: Four-argument error middleware
nodes.rationale: Signature must be exactly (err, req, res, next). Register last. Express 5 forwards thrown/rejected handlers here.

nodes.label: next(err)
nodes.rationale: Skip remaining normal middleware and jump to the error-handling stack.

nodes.label: express()
nodes.rationale: Returns an application — a request-handler function with use, get, settings, and listen sugar.

nodes.label: x-powered-by
nodes.rationale: Default true; advertises Express. Disable in production APIs. Not a security boundary by itself. Measured: app.disable sets it to false.

nodes.label: Async handler rejections forward to next
nodes.rationale: Rejected promises from async handlers go to error middleware. express-async-errors is an Express 4 habit. Still need try/catch to handle locally. Measured: 500 { error: 'async boom' }.
nodes.norm_label: async handler rejections forward to next

nodes.label: createApp(deps)
nodes.rationale: Returns app without listening. Inject db/redis/queue clients. Tests and serverless adapters need the app without binding a port.

nodes.label: Supertest
nodes.rationale: Hit the real Express stack with mocked services. Do not mock Express itself. request(app).get(...).expect(200).

nodes.label: Auth test token helper
nodes.rationale: Mint sessions or JWTs without copying production crypto. Keep secrets local and deterministic.

nodes.label: Separate createApp from listen
nodes.rationale: listen is a side effect. Tests import the app without binding a port; production controls boot order. Never listen at import time (EADDRINUSE).

nodes.label: Mock outbound deps not req/res
nodes.rationale: Mock DB and mail, not Express plumbing. Node Phase 9 covers the broader testing curriculum.

nodes.label: Do not hit the real IdP in route tests
nodes.rationale: Slow, flaky, and out of process. Contract tests can cover IdP separately.
nodes.norm_label: do not hit the real idp in route tests

nodes.label: :disabled vs aria-disabled
nodes.rationale: disabled removes the control from tab order and the accessibility tree; aria-disabled keeps it announceable.

nodes.label: :target
nodes.rationale: Matches the element whose id equals the URL fragment; can drive tabs without JS at the cost of history entries.

nodes.label: req.accepts / req.is / req.get
nodes.rationale: Small req helpers avoid reinventing Accept negotiation, Content-Type checks, and case-insensitive header reads.

nodes.label: Express 5.2.1 current line
nodes.rationale: npm latest is 5.2.1; latest-4 is 4.22.2. 'Express is unmaintained' FUD is outdated social posts.

nodes.label: Raw node:http
nodes.rationale: Learn HTTP itself here first. Possible for production APIs, rarely pleasant. Leaving Express does not mean leaving Node.

nodes.label: First match wins
nodes.rationale: A param route registered before a static sibling steals the static path. Express will not warn. /users/export hits :id with id export.

nodes.label: Express 5.x target
nodes.rationale: Inventory verified on Express 5.2.1. Do not start before Node Phase 5 (node:http). Prefer Node Phase 8 before Express Phases 8–9.

nodes.label: Foundations part (phases 0–2)
nodes.rationale: Express over node:http, routing, middleware. Do not skip: every middleware-did-not-run bug traces here.

nodes.label: Node Phase 5 prerequisite
nodes.rationale: node:http, request bodies as streams, signals, graceful HTTP shutdown. Learning Express first means learning the abstraction without the thing it abstracts.

nodes.label: Phase 0 — Express over node:http
nodes.rationale: Express is not a second language and not an application architecture. Seven pages; first three are load-bearing.

nodes.label: Phase 1 — Routing and path matching
nodes.rationale: How URLs become handlers. Order is load-bearing — Express will not warn you when the wrong route wins. 9 of 9 topics documentation-validated 2026-08-14.

nodes.label: Express.js explanation pages
nodes.rationale: Claimed by session 8679dc8c on 2026-08-14. 78 pages exist; progress counts topics brought to standard. Phases 0–3 done (38 of 114).

nodes.label: Express.js syllabus
nodes.rationale: 11 phases in 4 parts, 114 topics. Roughly half is HTTP API design that Node refused to absorb. Target Express 5.2.1 on Node 24.19.0.

nodes.label: Static segments before params
nodes.rationale: More specific paths before general ones. No universal catch-all until every real route is registered. Express does not rank by specificity.

nodes.label: Documentation-validated from Phase 2 on
nodes.rationale: No sandbox runs from Phase 2 on. No console block unless a run actually produced it.

nodes.label: Bare repository
nodes.rationale: No working tree; .git contents sit at the top level. What a server hosts.

nodes.label: Git is not a deployment tool
nodes.rationale: git pull on a server leaves .git on the host, no atomic switch, no rollback, no build step.
nodes.norm_label: git is not a deployment tool

nodes.label: Error.stackTraceLimit default 10
nodes.rationale: V8 truncates at ten frames by default. Raise to 50 or Infinity while debugging; capturing stacks is not free.

nodes.label: nomodule two-bundle pattern
nodes.rationale: Module-aware browsers ignore nomodule; older ones ignore type=module. Largely historical in 2026.

nodes.label: DevTools lazy object expansion
nodes.rationale: Logged objects expand lazily. Log structuredClone(obj) to capture the value at that instant.

nodes.label: Unicode NFC vs NFD
nodes.rationale: é can be one code point (NFC) or e plus combining acute (NFD). They render identically and are not ===. Normalise to NFC at the boundary. macOS filenames are NFD.

nodes.label: ** right-associative
nodes.rationale: 2 ** 3 ** 2 is 512. -2 ** 2 is a SyntaxError because the committee refused to pick between -4 and 4.

nodes.label: JSON.stringify omits undefined
nodes.rationale: A console block that prints body: undefined cannot be a real res.json run — undefined object properties are omitted. Known error left in place.

nodes.label: req.body
nodes.rationale: By default undefined, populated when you use body-parsing middleware.

nodes.label: express.urlencoded
nodes.rationale: For HTML form posts. Express 5 default extended is false (querystring library); true uses qs for nested objects.

nodes.label: urlencoded extended:false default
nodes.rationale: Express 5 change. Nested form fields are missing unless you set extended:true and still validate.

nodes.label: query parser extended
nodes.rationale: Opt-in via app.set('query parser', 'extended'). a[b]=1 becomes {a:{b:'1'}} via qs. Allow-list filter keys if enabled.

nodes.label: Nested query prototype pollution
nodes.rationale: Nested objects are historically used in prototype-pollution payloads (?__proto__[x]=y). Never pass raw req.query into Mongo/SQL builders.

nodes.label: express.raw
nodes.rationale: Parses into a Buffer. Default type application/octet-stream, limit 100kb. Widen type for JSON webhooks.

nodes.label: Known body:undefined console error
nodes.rationale: Pages 01 and 02 print body:undefined which no real run can produce. Left unrewritten because inventing replacement output is worse than a flagged error.

nodes.label: res.json
nodes.rationale: Sends a JSON response converted with JSON.stringify. Prefer json for JSON APIs.

nodes.label: res.status
nodes.rationale: Chainable alias of Node response.statusCode. Must precede the terminal body call.

nodes.label: Webhook HMAC over raw bytes
nodes.rationale: JSON parsing destroys the exact bytes. Signatures are over the exact byte sequence, not a re-serialized object. Verify then JSON.parse if needed.

nodes.label: Comma operator
nodes.rationale: Evaluates left to right, returns the last. Lowest precedence so x = 1, 2, 3 assigns 1. One readable use: two-pointer for header.

nodes.label: Lexical scope and the scope chain
nodes.norm_label: lexical scope and the scope chain

nodes.label: JSON __proto__ is ordinary
nodes.rationale: JSON.parse treats __proto__ as an own property. Pollution comes from a later merge assigning through it.

nodes.label: Top-level await
nodes.rationale: Allowed in modules only, not CommonJS. Delays evaluation of every importing module; reserve for genuine initialisation.

nodes.label: Object name is SHA of header plus content
nodes.rationale: blob 6\0hello\n hashed with sha1sum reproduces ce013625…; filename is not part of the name, so identical files share one object.
nodes.norm_label: object name is sha of header plus content

nodes.label: Refs are names pointing at hashes
nodes.rationale: A branch is a 41-byte file; creating one copies no objects. Deleting a branch does not delete commits.
nodes.norm_label: refs are names pointing at hashes

nodes.label: Packfile delta compression
nodes.rationale: Deltas are a packfile storage layer. No command's behaviour depends on them; 51 loose objects packed to 6.03 KiB on git 2.55.0.

nodes.label: Snapshot model
nodes.rationale: Every commit names a complete tree. Diffs are derived. Unchanged files reuse existing blobs so snapshots are cheap.

nodes.label: Lightweight tag
nodes.rationale: A file in refs/tags containing a hash; creates no object. Releases should use annotated tags.

nodes.label: Git is a content-addressed object store
nodes.rationale: Not a diff engine or a timeline: a key-value database keyed by content hash plus refs that name entry points.
nodes.norm_label: git is a content-addressed object store

nodes.label: Default initial branch still master
nodes.rationale: git init on 2.55.0 still defaults to master; the hint says the default will change to main in Git 3.0.

nodes.label: History is immutable and cumulative
nodes.rationale: A committed secret is an incident: later deletes do not remove the blob. Large blobs make every clone heavier forever.

nodes.label: node:vm is not a security sandbox
nodes.norm_label: node:vm is not a security sandbox

nodes.label: Exec-form PID 1
nodes.rationale: CMD npm run worker makes a shell PID 1; SIGTERM never reaches node. Use CMD ["node", "src/worker.js"].

nodes.label: JSON.parse is inert
nodes.rationale: JSON.parse cannot construct classes or execute. Risk is eval, new Function, YAML tags, or revive libraries.

nodes.label: TLS 1.3 session event
nodes.rationale: getSession() in the connect callback looks like a ticket and does not resume. Cache the 'session' event.

nodes.label: Modulo bias
nodes.rationale: 256 does not divide 100, so randomBytes(1)[0] % 100 skews buckets; use crypto.randomInt.

nodes.label: CORS is not access control
nodes.rationale: CORS relaxes the browser same-origin rule. Dangerous only with cookie auth plus reflected Origin and Allow-Credentials.

nodes.label: mock.module Stability 1.0
nodes.rationale: Early development; namedExports already renamed to exports in Node 24. Pin the Node version if the suite depends on it.

nodes.label: libuv
nodes.rationale: libuv is the hands: the event loop and the ability to wait for files and sockets without freezing.

nodes.label: process.versions
nodes.rationale: Proof that Node is a bundle of C libraries — V8, libuv, OpenSSL — not one thing.

nodes.label: Read-modify-write race across await
nodes.rationale: The function yields at await; a second request can run the same code and both write back a value computed from the same stale read.

nodes.label: Network I/O uses no extra threads
nodes.rationale: Sockets are handled by epoll/kqueue/IOCP. The libuv pool is for filesystem, dns.lookup, parts of crypto, and zlib.
nodes.norm_label: network i/o uses no extra threads

nodes.label: One callback at a time, no locks
nodes.rationale: Two functions can never execute simultaneously. The guarantee stops at every await.
nodes.norm_label: one callback at a time, no locks

nodes.label: Wrapping blocking code in async does not unblock it
nodes.rationale: async only changes how the function returns a value. Unless you await something that genuinely yields, the code still runs to completion on the main thread.
nodes.norm_label: wrapping blocking code in async does not unblock it

nodes.label: Four fixes for a blocked loop
nodes.rationale: Use the async version; chunk and yield with setImmediate; move to worker_threads; queue it and return 202.
nodes.norm_label: four fixes for a blocked loop

nodes.label: monitorEventLoopDelay
nodes.rationale: Values are in nanoseconds. Healthy web process: mean delay under a few milliseconds, p99 under ~50ms.

nodes.label: Sync suffix in a request path is a bug
nodes.rationale: Sync is fine at startup — reading a config file before the server listens blocks nothing.
nodes.norm_label: sync suffix in a request path is a bug

nodes.label: dns.lookup uses the thread pool
nodes.rationale: Every outbound fetch, http.request and database connection resolves through dns.lookup by default, so a burst of HTTP can make unrelated fs reads slow.

nodes.label: dns.resolve does not use the thread pool
nodes.rationale: resolve4 talks to a DNS server directly and ignores /etc/hosts. The usual fix for pool pressure is a DNS cache in front of lookup, not swapping to resolve.
nodes.norm_label: dns.resolve does not use the thread pool

nodes.label: UV_THREADPOOL_SIZE
nodes.rationale: Default 4, max 1024. Created lazily on first use; size is fixed from then on. Set it in the environment before the process starts.

nodes.label: Thread pool versus worker_threads
nodes.rationale: The pool is internal and runs C/C++ only. worker_threads each run their own V8 isolate and JavaScript.

nodes.label: Phase 0 gate
nodes.rationale: Explain why a 3-second for loop stalls every incoming request but a 3-second database query does not, and name three ways to fix the first one.

nodes.label: await suspends the function, not the thread
nodes.rationale: await cannot rescue a synchronous hot loop. Once the continuation resumes, it runs to completion like any other job.
nodes.norm_label: await suspends the function, not the thread

nodes.label: One thread, and never let it wait
nodes.rationale: Cheap concurrency for I/O-heavy work, paid for with a hard rule: never make that one thread do anything slow.
nodes.norm_label: one thread, and never let it wait

nodes.label: One slow function slows every request
nodes.rationale: The users who suffer are not the ones who called the slow endpoint. They are everyone else.
nodes.norm_label: one slow function slows every request

nodes.label: Four spare threads to block on your behalf
nodes.rationale: Portable filesystem calls block, so libuv hands the call to a worker thread and posts the result back. Network I/O uses no threads.
nodes.norm_label: four spare threads to block on your behalf

nodes.label: V8 micro-optimisation is last
nodes.rationale: For a typical Node web service the ranking is database, network, blocking the loop, serialisation, algorithms, then V8.

nodes.label: Do not skip Phase 0
nodes.rationale: Every Node is weird complaint traces back to skipping the runtime model.

nodes.label: Blob
nodes.rationale: File bytes only: no name, path, mode, or timestamp. The filename lives in the tree.

nodes.label: Tree
nodes.rationale: Sorted listing of mode, type, hash, name. Empty directories cannot be committed because they produce no entries.

nodes.label: Tree modes 100644 100755 120000 040000 160000
nodes.rationale: Git records the executable bit and symlink-versus-file only. Owner, group, and other permissions are lost.

nodes.label: AM status short
nodes.rationale: A is index versus HEAD added; M is working tree versus index modified. Commit would record the earlier staged content.

nodes.label: git add -p
nodes.rationale: The index can hold a blob that exists in neither HEAD nor the working tree, so hunks can be staged independently.

nodes.label: .git/index binary file
nodes.rationale: Staged is not a flag. git add writes a blob then records mode, hash, stage, path. Staging is a copy, not a bookmark.

nodes.label: Cached stat data
nodes.rationale: status skips re-hash when size and mtime match. Network or Windows shares that lie about modes make every file look modified.

nodes.label: Index merge stages 0 1 2 3
nodes.rationale: Stage 0 is normal. During a conflict a path holds 1 base, 2 ours, 3 theirs. UU means those three exist and no stage 0.

nodes.label: Field meaning change same type
nodes.rationale: Worst change: euros becoming cents validates perfectly and is off by 100. Never redefine a field — add a new one and deprecate.

nodes.label: Testcontainers under podman
nodes.rationale: Needs DOCKER_HOST at the rootless podman socket and TESTCONTAINERS_RYUK_DISABLED=true. Without the second, Ryuk fails with an unhelpful log-stream error.

nodes.label: PostgreSQL License
nodes.rationale: BSD-style permissive license; no single commercial owner of core. The engine is free; managed hosting is the product.

nodes.label: No-new-sandboxes validation
nodes.rationale: Topics 07–18 validated against official docs. No page carries a console block that was not produced by a run that happened.

nodes.label: Explicit this binding
nodes.rationale: call and apply invoke immediately; bind returns a new function with this fixed forever.

nodes.label: Four this binding rules
nodes.rationale: new, then explicit call/apply/bind, then implicit obj.fn(), then default. Arrows are outside the tree.

nodes.label: Implicit this binding
nodes.rationale: obj.fn() binds this to whatever is left of the last dot. nested.inner.read() binds inner, not nested.

nodes.label: new this binding
nodes.rationale: Fresh object, prototype linked to Fn.prototype, this bound, returned unless the constructor returns an object. A returned primitive is ignored.

nodes.label: this precedence
nodes.rationale: new beats bind beats call/apply beats implicit beats default. new on a bound function discards bound this but keeps bound arguments.

nodes.label: Arrow has no prototype
nodes.rationale: hasOwnProperty('prototype') is false, so new A() throws TypeError: A is not a constructor.

nodes.label: Arrow inherited bindings
nodes.rationale: this, arguments, super, and new.target are inherited, not banned. Only prototype is genuinely absent.

nodes.label: No generator arrow
nodes.rationale: async () => is supported. *() => {} is SyntaxError. Generators must be function*.

nodes.label: new discards bound this
nodes.rationale: [[Construct]] discards bound this, keeps bound arguments, and delegates the prototype chain to the target. Still instanceof the original.

nodes.label: Bound function exotic object
nodes.rationale: Name prefixed bound , length reduced by bound args, no own prototype, this permanently fixed. Later bind still accumulates arguments.

nodes.label: Hand-written bind
nodes.rationale: Naive apply misses new. Use new.target ? this : thisArg and set bound.prototype from the target. User code cannot match native name, length, or absent prototype.

nodes.label: Partial application with bind
nodes.rationale: Fills arguments from the left only. Bindings accumulate. null thisArg is safe only if the function never touches this.

nodes.label: MAINTAIN privilege
nodes.rationale: VACUUM without MAINTAIN returns success and only a WARNING, so automated jobs can silently skip tables.

nodes.label: Annex B sloppy-mode block functions
nodes.rationale: Non-strict block function declarations behave strangely and differ across Chrome, Firefox and Safari. Scope setup still runs even if the if body never executes.

nodes.label: Block-level function declaration
nodes.rationale: A function declaration inside a block is not top-level hoisting. Strict mode scopes it to that block; sloppy mode is Annex B and engine-dependent.

nodes.label: Strict-mode block functions
nodes.rationale: In strict mode (every module and class body) block-level function declarations hoist to the top of that block and do not exist outside it.

nodes.label: Const-like inner class binding
nodes.rationale: Inside the class body the class name is an immutable binding. Outside it is a reassignable let-like binding. The class body always runs in strict mode.

nodes.label: Class lexical declaration and TDZ
nodes.rationale: class is commonly regarded as non-hoisted. Using one above its declaration throws Cannot access before initialization. Classes are block-scoped and do not create globalThis properties.

nodes.label: extends evaluated at declaration
nodes.rationale: extends is an expression evaluated when the class statement runs, not at new. Two classes cannot extend each other; method bodies have no such constraint.

nodes.label: Import hoisting
nodes.rationale: Import declarations are hoisted: imported values are available before their line and the imported module's side effects run first. Position in the file does not change evaluation order.

nodes.label: Live read-only import bindings
nodes.rationale: Imports are read-only views like const. You cannot reassign the imported binding; only the exporting module can change the value, and the change is live.

nodes.label: Hoisting and the temporal dead zone
nodes.rationale: Nothing is moved. Entering a scope creates a binding for every declaration before any code runs. What went into the slot differs by declaration kind.
nodes.norm_label: hoisting and the temporal dead zone

nodes.label: Declaration binding table
nodes.rationale: function is usable before its line; var is undefined; let/const/class throw ReferenceError; import is a live binding with side effects first.

nodes.label: Prefer const-assigned function expressions in blocks
nodes.rationale: Never write a function declaration inside a block. Assign a function expression to let or const so the binding is exactly where you wrote it in every engine.
nodes.norm_label: prefer const-assigned function expressions in blocks

nodes.label: Nothing is moved to the top
nodes.rationale: The spec has no hoisting. Bindings are created at scope entry. The TDZ is a stretch of time, not a region of source.
nodes.norm_label: nothing is moved to the top

nodes.label: macaddr and macaddr8
nodes.rationale: 6-byte and 8-byte hardware addresses with the same normalisation pattern as inet.

nodes.label: Aggregates ignore NULL
nodes.rationale: count(*) counts rows; count(col) counts non-nulls. sum() over all-NULL is NULL not 0 — wrap with coalesce(sum(v), 0).

nodes.label: NULL sort order
nodes.rationale: NULLs sort last ASC and first DESC. Reversing a sort changes LIMIT results; override with NULLS FIRST/LAST and match the index.

nodes.label: NULL is not the empty string
nodes.rationale: '' IS NULL is false. || with NULL yields NULL; concat() ignores NULLs. Oracle conflates them; PostgreSQL does not.
nodes.norm_label: null is not the empty string

nodes.label: Map is directly iterable
nodes.rationale: for...of over a Map yields [k, v] pairs. Objects need Object.entries and are not iterable.

nodes.label: for...in
nodes.rationale: Iterates enumerable string keys including inherited ones. An Object.hasOwn guard is the signal to switch to Object.keys.

nodes.label: for...of
nodes.rationale: Iterates values via Symbol.iterator. Strings yield code points. Works on Map and Set directly.

nodes.label: Plain objects are not iterable
nodes.rationale: A record is not a sequence. Object.entries states whether you want keys, values or pairs.

nodes.label: Iterating while modifying
nodes.rationale: forEach fixes its range up front. for...of re-reads length, so push inside the same array is an infinite loop.

nodes.label: Array and call spread
nodes.rationale: Requires Symbol.iterator. [...obj] throws on a plain object. [...new Set(items)] is the idiomatic dedupe.

nodes.label: Spread argument-count RangeError
nodes.rationale: Math.max(...hugeArray) and arr.push(...huge) pass each element as an argument. Use reduce, a loop, or concat.

nodes.label: Array.from vs spread
nodes.rationale: Array.from accepts array-likes without an iterator, maps while converting, and builds n slots.

nodes.label: Spread replacing apply
nodes.rationale: Composes with fixed arguments and works with new, which apply cannot. apply remains only for setting this.

nodes.label: Never for...in on an array
nodes.rationale: Indices arrive as strings, non-index properties are included, and property enumeration skips holes that for...of visits.

nodes.label: Spread inside a growing loop is quadratic
nodes.rationale: out = [...out, x] copies the whole accumulation each iteration. Use map or push.
nodes.norm_label: spread inside a growing loop is quadratic

nodes.label: Collation from libc (musl vs glibc)
nodes.rationale: Sort order comes from the column/database collation via the C library, so Alpine musl and Debian glibc can order the same strings differently.

nodes.label: date to JS Date midnight trap
nodes.rationale: pg turns date into Date at local midnight; in Asia/Calcutta that is 18:30 UTC the previous day. Fix with to_char or setTypeParser(1082, v => v).
nodes.norm_label: date to js date midnight trap

nodes.label: Batch ALTER subcommands
nodes.rationale: One statement = one lock acquisition and at most one rewrite pass covering all changes.

nodes.label: DISTINCT aggregate ORDER BY 42P10
nodes.rationale: array_agg(DISTINCT a ORDER BY b) is rejected: after de-duplicating by a there is no single b. ORDER BY must use the DISTINCT expressions.

nodes.label: json versus jsonb
nodes.rationale: json stores source text (duplicates, whitespace, key order). jsonb parses to binary, collapses duplicates, reorders keys. Difference is invisible from Node because JSON.parse also collapses duplicates. jsonb is 2.6× larger here (60 vs 23 bytes) but indexable with GIN.

nodes.label: jsonb_object_agg
nodes.rationale: NULL key raises 22023 field name must not be null. Duplicate keys silently keep the last value. Aggregate over a pre-grouped subquery.

nodes.label: DECLARE cursor needs a transaction
nodes.rationale: FETCH after COMMIT is 34000 cursor does not exist. WITH HOLD materialises the whole result at commit. pg-cursor uses a protocol portal bound to the connection.

nodes.label: application_name
nodes.rationale: Shows up in pg_stat_activity so every connection is attributable to a service.

nodes.label: undefined becomes SQL NULL
nodes.rationale: A misspelled property inserts NULL instead of failing. Validate the object before building the values array.

nodes.label: lock_timeout
nodes.rationale: Give up rather than queue behind ACCESS EXCLUSIVE. An ALTER TABLE waiting for that lock is an outage for every query behind it.

nodes.label: Microtask
nodes.rationale: Created by .then/.catch/.finally, await continuations, queueMicrotask, MutationObserver. Entire queue drains after the current task.

nodes.label: Microtask starvation
nodes.rationale: A self-re-arming microtask chain never returns to the task queue — no timers, events or rendering. Worse than while(true) because it looks async.

nodes.label: Rendering between tasks
nodes.rationale: The browser schedules a rendering opportunity between tasks, after the microtask queue is empty. Yield a task to paint.

nodes.label: requestAnimationFrame
nodes.rationale: Neither a task nor a microtask — a separate callback list in the rendering step, just before layout and paint.

nodes.label: Task (macrotask)
nodes.rationale: One job per event-loop turn. Created by setTimeout, setInterval, event dispatch, the initial script. A task yields; a microtask does not.

nodes.label: length === 1 microtask batching
nodes.rationale: First call schedules the flush; later calls in the same turn join the array. Runs after all sync code and before paint — the mechanism behind framework batching.

nodes.label: queueMicrotask
nodes.rationale: Runs after the current execution context exits but before event handlers and timeouts. Prefer over Promise.resolve().then: no allocation, exceptions surface as uncaught errors.

nodes.label: then always runs asynchronously
nodes.rationale: Even on an already-settled promise the handler is a microtask. The returned promise is always pending when returned.

nodes.label: Every chain link costs a microtask
nodes.rationale: A three-link chain over an already-resolved promise takes three ticks. A long chain of sync handlers freezes the frame the way a loop does.
nodes.norm_label: every chain link costs a microtask

nodes.label: Promise executor runs synchronously
nodes.rationale: new Promise(fn) calls fn immediately on the current stack. Wrapping slow work in a promise does not make it non-blocking.

nodes.label: Microtask drain until empty
nodes.rationale: A task runs one job. A microtask drain runs every microtask, including ones queued during the drain.

nodes.label: PostgresInterval object
nodes.rationale: Months and days are not fixed durations, so there is no correct millisecond conversion. Use extract(epoch FROM …) for a number.

nodes.label: Baselining an existing database
nodes.rationale: pg_dump --schema-only as one baseline, mark applied without running. History before the baseline is no longer replayable.

nodes.label: One client for lock and apply
nodes.rationale: BEGIN, advisory lock and every migration must share one session. pool.query would split them across connections.
nodes.norm_label: one client for lock and apply

nodes.label: Generate drift expectation in CI
nodes.rationale: Hand-maintained EXPECTED drifts. Generate after migrations, or catalog-diff a scratch DB against production, or generate types.

nodes.label: Identity consumed on skipped conflict
nodes.rationale: ON CONFLICT still evaluates the row and draws identity first. Three runs of two rows left last_value at 6. Sequences are not gapless.

nodes.label: sql() file loader
nodes.rationale: Resolve from import.meta.url, cache in a Map in production. process.cwd() works in tests and fails in production.

nodes.label: Named SQL parameters
nodes.rationale: Comment headers or a :name shim that emits real $n placeholders. Regex must not rewrite :: casts. Values never enter SQL text.

nodes.label: Drop and migrate once per suite
nodes.rationale: Only strategy that tests migrations. Seconds, not milliseconds. Combine with rollback per test.
nodes.norm_label: drop and migrate once per suite

nodes.label: TRUNCATE RESTART IDENTITY CASCADE
nodes.rationale: One statement lists every table to avoid deadlock. CASCADE for FKs (0A000 otherwise). RESTART IDENTITY or next id is 10001 after 10k rows.

nodes.label: INVALID leftover CONCURRENTLY index
nodes.rationale: Failed CONCURRENTLY build leaves an unused index that still costs writes. Find with pg_index WHERE NOT indisvalid; DROP and rebuild.

nodes.label: Callback
nodes.rationale: A function passed as an argument and invoked by the outer function. You write it; the caller decides when, how often, and with what arguments.

nodes.label: Synchronous vs asynchronous callbacks
nodes.rationale: Syntax is identical. map/forEach/sort are sync; setTimeout/then are not. Only the callee's documentation answers timing.

nodes.label: Inversion of control (callbacks)
nodes.rationale: The rest of your program is a function in a third party's hands. Failures — too early, too late, never, twice, wrong args, swallowed — are all silent.

nodes.label: once() wrapper
nodes.rationale: A called flag that ignores a second invocation. Exactly what a promise provides structurally — it settles once.

nodes.label: Promise
nodes.rationale: An object representing eventual completion or failure. You attach callbacks to a returned object instead of passing them into a function.

nodes.label: Promise three states
nodes.rationale: pending, fulfilled, rejected. Settled means fulfilled or rejected. Transition happens at most once and is irreversible.

nodes.label: Resolved vs fulfilled
nodes.rationale: Resolved is the decision, not the outcome — settled or locked onto another promise. resolve(inner) can leave the outer pending. The executor parameter is named resolve, not fulfill.

nodes.label: MDN promise guarantees
nodes.rationale: Never invoked before the current event-loop run ends; invoked even if attached after settling; multiple then handlers in insertion order. Promises fixed the contract, not the indentation.

nodes.label: Promise for one result, callback for many
nodes.rationale: Use a promise for one result later; a callback for a function to run or many results over time. Promises are one-shot.
nodes.norm_label: promise for one result, callback for many

nodes.label: Null-prototype or Map allowlist
nodes.rationale: A plain object resolves ?sort=constructor or ?sort=__proto__ to something truthy that is not a column.

nodes.label: create — INSERT ... RETURNING
nodes.rationale: Answer with the row the database stored, not the one the client sent. RETURNING avoids a second query and a race.

nodes.label: createMany via unnest
nodes.rationale: One array parameter per column stays under the 65535-parameter cap. RETURNING order is not guaranteed; return a correlating column.

nodes.label: 22P02 malformed id is 400
nodes.rationale: GET /users/abc against bigint raises 22P02. Validate at the edge; map SQLSTATE as backstop. Not 404.

nodes.label: Lock rows in consistent order
nodes.rationale: Opposite lock orders deadlock (40P01). ORDER BY id FOR UPDATE. FOR UPDATE OF table restricts join locking.

nodes.label: idempotency_keys response table
nodes.rationale: Store status+response when the body cannot be recomputed from the row. request_hash rejects key reuse with a different body (422). Scope PRIMARY KEY (user_id, key). In-flight → 409.

nodes.label: Idempotent writes
nodes.rationale: Any network write will be called twice. The second call is a condition to handle, not a bug to prevent.

nodes.label: Fetch limit + 1 for hasMore
nodes.rationale: The extra row is cheaper than count(*) over the predicate. nextCursor is null at the end of the collection.

nodes.label: Nullable sort column excludes later pages
nodes.rationale: Comparison against NULL is never true. Page 1 includes nulls (no WHERE); later pages drop them. Measured 250000 of 500000 excluded. NULLS LAST does not fix the predicate.
nodes.norm_label: nullable sort column excludes later pages

nodes.label: Readiness gate and SIGTERM drain
nodes.rationale: On SIGTERM mark not-ready immediately, close the server, finish in-flight work, then exit.

nodes.label: Kubernetes-style rolling update
nodes.rationale: Ready too early means users hit 500s; platform knobs are maxUnavailable and maxSurge.

nodes.label: terminationGracePeriodSeconds
nodes.rationale: Bounds how long SIGTERM has before SIGKILL; keep-alive sockets can hang server.close.

nodes.label: Zero-downtime deploy
nodes.rationale: New pods take traffic before old pods die; old pods stop receiving work before they exit.

nodes.label: systemd as VM supervisor
nodes.rationale: OS-native restart policy, env files, TimeoutStopSec, journald; ExecStart should be node, not npm.

nodes.label: Blue/green deploy
nodes.rationale: Two full environments; rollback is a second flip if sessions and schemas allow.

nodes.label: Expand/contract migrations
nodes.rationale: Old and new code run together during a rollout; schema must be compatible with both briefly.

nodes.label: Readiness is not liveness
nodes.rationale: Failing readiness removes traffic without killing the pod mid-drain; liveness restarts.

nodes.label: One owner for restarts and signals
nodes.rationale: In Kubernetes the orchestrator already restarts and health-checks; a second supervisor fights it.
nodes.norm_label: one owner for restarts and signals

nodes.label: pm2 inside Docker/K8s is double supervision
nodes.rationale: pm2 plus kubelet murky PID 1, disagreeing metrics, and logs stolen from stdout.
nodes.norm_label: pm2 inside docker/k8s is double supervision

nodes.label: Rolling vs canary vs blue/green
nodes.rationale: Rolling is default K8s; canary shrinks blast radius at analysis cost; blue/green needs 2x capacity.

nodes.label: Unique ORDER BY tiebreaker
nodes.rationale: ORDER BY grp over 30k rows: 54 distinct / 46 repeats paging 100. Append , id. Instability is between offsets, so repeating page 1 does not catch it.

nodes.label: A missing row is not an error
nodes.rationale: SELECT matching nothing is success: rowCount 0, rows [], rows[0] undefined. Normalise to null so JSON.stringify does not drop the key.
