nodes.norm_label: a missing row is not an error

nodes.label: rowCount vs rows.length
nodes.rationale: rowCount is rows affected; rows is what was returned. UPDATE without RETURNING has rowCount 3 and rows.length 0. rowCount is null, not 0, for CREATE TABLE.

nodes.label: ILIKE wildcard escaping
nodes.rationale: A user searching % is not injection — the parameter is still a value — but it matches every row and can DoS a large table. Escape \, %, _ and declare ESCAPE '\'.

nodes.label: Omit WHERE when there are no filters
nodes.rationale: WHERE 1=1 works but leaves a permanently true predicate in every plan and log. Emit WHERE only when where.length > 0.
nodes.norm_label: omit where when there are no filters

nodes.label: Shaping the response in SQL vs in JavaScript
nodes.norm_label: shaping the response in sql vs in javascript

nodes.label: Mapping snake_case columns to camelCase fields
nodes.norm_label: mapping snake_case columns to camelcase fields

nodes.label: Sequences are not transactional
nodes.rationale: A rolled-back insert still consumed an id (last_value 2002 → 2003). Never assert on a literal id.

nodes.label: created_at DEFAULT now()
nodes.rationale: A DEFAULT covers every insert path including COPY. No trigger needed. Use timestamptz, not timestamp.

nodes.label: CommonJS
nodes.rationale: Node's original module system: synchronous, dynamic, and cached by resolved path. Not deprecated; most of npm is still published this way.

nodes.label: module.exports vs exports
nodes.rationale: exports starts as a second name for the same object as module.exports. Only module.exports is what require returns.

nodes.label: CommonJS module singleton
nodes.rationale: Module-scope state is process-wide. That is how you get one connection pool, and how one test leaks state into the next.

nodes.label: CommonJS module wrapper
nodes.rationale: Node wraps every CJS file in a function(exports, require, module, __filename, __dirname). Those five names are parameters, not globals, which is why they do not exist in ESM.

nodes.label: CommonJS has no live bindings
nodes.rationale: require returns an object; destructuring copies values at that moment. Export a function or getter, or read through the module object.

nodes.label: require.cache
nodes.rationale: A module body runs once per resolved path per process. Later requires return the same object. Core modules are not in require.cache.

nodes.label: Circular dependencies
nodes.rationale: A requires B, B requires A. Neither module system hangs. Neither outcome is one you want to design around.

nodes.label: CommonJS partial exports object
nodes.rationale: When B requires A while A is still executing, the cache holds whatever A has assigned so far. Behaviour depends on statement order.

nodes.label: ESM cycle temporal dead zone
nodes.rationale: ESM links bindings before evaluating. Reading a const export during the cycle throws ReferenceError. A crash at startup beats a silent undefined.

nodes.label: Function declarations survive cycles
nodes.rationale: Function declarations are hoisted at link time. A cycle can sit for years and break the day someone converts a function to a const arrow.

nodes.label: Never assign to bare exports
nodes.rationale: exports = {…} rebinds the local parameter and exports {}. Use module.exports everywhere.

nodes.label: Extract the shared piece
nodes.rationale: Two modules that each need the other are usually one concept that got split. Extract, invert the dependency, or only then defer with await import().

nodes.label: created_at and updated_at — trigger or application code
nodes.norm_label: created_at and updated_at — trigger or application code

nodes.label: Naming a SET column does not defeat HOT
nodes.rationale: COALESCE naming indexed b kept 1090 HOT of 2500; built SET of unindexed a had 1096. Changing b dropped HOT to 0.
nodes.norm_label: naming a set column does not defeat hot

nodes.label: Partial updates — COALESCE vs a built SET list
nodes.norm_label: partial updates — coalesce vs a built set list

nodes.label: React onChange is the DOM input event
nodes.norm_label: react onchange is the dom input event

nodes.label: SSRF URL validation
nodes.rationale: Check protocol and hostname on the parsed object, never with a regex on the raw string. DNS can still resolve public names to private IPs.

nodes.label: url.parse deprecated DEP0169
nodes.rationale: Legacy parser differs from the standard and has caused SSRF and open-redirect bypasses.

nodes.label: URLSearchParams
nodes.rationale: Decodes on read, encodes on write. get returns only the first value; spaces serialise as +.

nodes.label: WHATWG URL
nodes.rationale: Same objects as the browser. A leading slash on the two-argument form discards the base path.

nodes.label: http.createServer
nodes.rationale: req is IncomingMessage, res is ServerResponse. Header names are lower-cased; req.url is path plus query only.

nodes.label: ERR_HTTP_HEADERS_SENT
nodes.rationale: Headers flush on the first body byte. Guard error paths with res.headersSent and destroy if too late.

nodes.label: headersTimeout requestTimeout connectionsCheckingInterval
nodes.rationale: Timeouts are swept every 30s by default. Lowering requestTimeout alone does nothing until the next check.

nodes.label: req is a readable stream
nodes.rationale: Handler runs when headers are parsed. Body arrives in Buffer chunks; concat then decode.

nodes.label: Cookie request header
nodes.rationale: Duplicates join with semicolon, not comma. Parse with indexOf equals; first occurrence wins.

nodes.label: Set-Cookie as an array
nodes.rationale: One cookie per header line. Joining with semicolon produces one malformed cookie.

nodes.label: Thrown handler is not a 500
nodes.rationale: node:http has no error handling. Exceptions become uncaughtException or unhandledRejection and the client hangs.

nodes.label: URLSearchParams is the wrong cookie parser
nodes.rationale: Form decoding: plus becomes space, last duplicate wins, valueless tokens become empty keys.
nodes.norm_label: urlsearchparams is the wrong cookie parser

nodes.label: What error boundaries do not catch
nodes.rationale: Event handlers, async, SSR and the boundary itself. React 19 adds onUncaughtError and onCaughtError.
nodes.norm_label: what error boundaries do not catch

nodes.label: Slots, children and the context hole
nodes.norm_label: slots, children and the context hole

nodes.label: Twelve-boolean component costs
nodes.rationale: Unbounded API, untested combinations, bundled unused deps, hidden markup.

nodes.label: The switch warning, and supporting both
nodes.norm_label: the switch warning, and supporting both

nodes.label: Controlled API naming
nodes.rationale: value/onChange, open/onOpenChange, defaultX for initial. Call with the next value, name for what happened.

nodes.label: eslint no-unstable-nested-components
nodes.rationale: Not in the recommended set. Enable it; React itself cannot warn.

nodes.label: Capitalization makes JSX emit a function
nodes.rationale: Lowercase emits a string tag. The function never runs.
nodes.norm_label: capitalization makes jsx emit a function

nodes.label: HOC displayName convention
nodes.rationale: Without displayName DevTools shows WithUser or Anonymous for every wrap.

nodes.label: HOC wrappers do not copy statics
nodes.rationale: The wrapper is a different function object; copy statics or use hoist-non-react-statics.
nodes.norm_label: hoc wrappers do not copy statics

nodes.label: Split state or components by update frequency
nodes.norm_label: split state or components by update frequency

nodes.label: createPortal is client-only
nodes.rationale: There is no DOM on the server. Render after mount or use a framework portal.

nodes.label: Reassigning a destructured prop is not a mutation
nodes.rationale: A local rebinding is unobservable outside the call. Writes through the object are the violation.
nodes.norm_label: reassigning a destructured prop is not a mutation

nodes.label: Webhook event id dedupe
nodes.rationale: Persist event id so the same delivery is processed at most once.

nodes.label: express.raw on webhook path
nodes.rationale: Signature is over exact bytes, not re-serialized JSON. Need the raw body from Phase 3 express.raw.

nodes.label: HMAC with crypto.timingSafeEqual
nodes.rationale: Verify HMAC or provider scheme with a constant-time compare so signature checks do not leak via timing.

nodes.label: Inbound webhooks
nodes.rationale: Receive with raw body, HMAC (or provider scheme), timestamp replay window, persist event id for dedupe, then enqueue and respond quickly.

nodes.label: Outbound webhooks
nodes.rationale: Fire-and-forget from the route is a bug under load. Express accepts the command and returns 202; Node Phase 7 jobs deliver.

nodes.label: Webhook timestamp replay window
nodes.rationale: Reject old timestamps so a captured signed payload cannot be replayed later.

nodes.label: Phase 6 REST surface and API features
nodes.rationale: Product surface clients depend on. Node handed these topics to Express on purpose. Gate: cursor pagination, versioned mount, idempotent POST, OpenAPI matching handlers.
nodes.norm_label: phase 6 rest surface and api features

nodes.label: Controller layer
nodes.rationale: Parse and validate input already on req, call the service, map status. Does not own SQL or business rules.

nodes.label: Repository layer
nodes.rationale: Queries and commands via drivers. Does not decide HTTP status. Node Phase 6 owns how repositories and transactions work.

nodes.label: Service layer
nodes.rationale: Owns invariants and orchestration. No res.json and no Express types so services stay testable without spinning an HTTP server.

nodes.label: DTO at the edge
nodes.rationale: Stable API shapes when persistence models change. Controller maps req.validated into the service and toUserDto on the way out.

nodes.label: req.validated
nodes.rationale: Parsed input attached by Zod middleware. Controllers pass it into services instead of raw req.body.

nodes.label: Fat controller
nodes.rationale: If a handler needs scrolling, logic leaked upward. Smells: SQL in the route, 200-line try/catch with five status codes, copy-pasted auth checks.

nodes.label: createApp(deps)
nodes.rationale: Phase 10 completes composition with createApp(deps).use('/users', usersRouter({userService})).

nodes.label: usersRouter factory
nodes.rationale: usersRouter({userService}) builds an express.Router and delegates list to the injected service.

nodes.label: HTTP 202 Accepted for queued work
nodes.rationale: 202 means accepted for processing, not necessarily completed.

nodes.label: Transactional outbox from routes
nodes.rationale: orders.create(input) in a transaction with outbox when needed. Cross-link Node Phase 7 for outbox, retries, and worker shutdown.

nodes.label: Map API DTOs at the edge
nodes.rationale: Map API DTOs at the edge so persistence models can change without shifting the public shape.
nodes.norm_label: map api dtos at the edge

nodes.label: Feature folders
nodes.rationale: orders/routes.ts plus orders/service.ts. Feature scales by domain. Teams pick one convention and stay consistent.

nodes.label: Layer folders
nodes.rationale: routes/, services/, repos/. Layer scales by role rather than by domain.

nodes.label: Transaction-per-request middleware
nodes.rationale: A thin Express wrapper; the transaction mechanism stays Node Phase 6.

nodes.label: Phase 7 layering at the Express edge
nodes.rationale: Thin HTTP edge. Repository and transaction mechanism stay in Node Phase 6. Gate: short handlers, services unit-test without req/res, one slow side effect enqueued.
nodes.norm_label: phase 7 layering at the express edge

nodes.label: Attach parsed data on req.validated
nodes.rationale: On success attach parsed data under a clear name on req, not mixed with the raw body.

nodes.label: validate middleware factory
nodes.rationale: validate({body, params, query}) returns middleware. Schemas are Understand-level library surface; the factory and boundary habit are Master.

nodes.label: VALIDATION_ERROR 400
nodes.rationale: On parse failure set statusCode 400 and code VALIDATION_ERROR, then next(err).

nodes.label: Boolean("false") trap
nodes.rationale: ?active=false is the string "false", which is truthy. Non-empty strings are truthy in JavaScript. Use explicit enums or coerce helpers.

nodes.label: Query and params are strings
nodes.rationale: ?limit=20 is the string "20". z.number() without coerce fails; use z.coerce.number() deliberately.

nodes.label: 401 UNAUTHENTICATED
nodes.rationale: No resolvable user from session or token. Identity is missing.

nodes.label: req.user principal
nodes.rationale: Authn middleware puts the authenticated principal on req, not permissions alone.

nodes.label: requireAuth middleware
nodes.rationale: Parse session or Bearer JWT, attach req.user, else 401. Does not re-teach argon2 or JWT structure — Node Phase 8.

nodes.label: connect-redis session store
nodes.rationale: Session store is integration only. Redis syllabus owns Redis.

nodes.label: res.cookie flags
nodes.rationale: httpOnly, secure, sameSite — Phase 4. Express mounts cookie/session middleware and sets flags. Sessions vs JWT is Node Phase 8.

nodes.label: cookie-parser before session
nodes.rationale: Session libraries read cookies from the parsed object, so cookie-parser must mount first.

nodes.label: 403 FORBIDDEN
nodes.rationale: 403 when identity is known but the role is not allowed. 401 when identity is missing.

nodes.label: requireRole middleware
nodes.rationale: Role checks after authentication. Fail closed with 403, not 401. Missing req.user is still 401.

nodes.label: Resource ownership
nodes.rationale: Load the resource, compare owner id to req.user.id. Prefer 404 when existence should stay secret; 403 when the resource is visible but forbidden. Document the choice.

nodes.label: Logout cookie clear and revocation
nodes.rationale: Logout clears cookies or hits revocation. Storage is Node/Redis.

nodes.label: Optional auth middleware
nodes.rationale: Enriches req.user when a token is present but does not 401 when absent. Useful for public plus personalized routes.

nodes.label: Tenant hopping IDOR
nodes.rationale: Trusting a client-supplied tenantId lets a caller hop tenants.

nodes.label: Phase 8 validation and authorization at the edge
nodes.rationale: Passwords and JWT structure live in Node Phase 8. Here: middleware surface. Gate: missing token 401, wrong role 403, bad body 400; services never see raw req.body.
nodes.norm_label: phase 8 validation and authorization at the edge

nodes.label: req.ip behind a proxy
nodes.rationale: Without trust proxy, req.ip is the load balancer. Rate limits and secure cookies misbehave. All traffic appears as one IP and rate limiting bans everyone.

nodes.label: trust proxy
nodes.rationale: app.set('trust proxy', 1) for one hop of reverse proxy you control. Never set true on an open internet edge without understanding spoofed X-Forwarded-For.

nodes.label: X-Forwarded-For spoofing
nodes.rationale: trust proxy true on an open edge trusts client-supplied forwarded headers. Nginx syllabus covers termination in depth.

nodes.label: CORS in Express
nodes.rationale: Browsers enforce CORS, not servers alone. cors({origin: allow-list, credentials: true}).

nodes.label: Credentials cannot use wildcard origin
nodes.rationale: Browsers forbid credentialed requests with Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *. Credentials and wildcard origins do not mix.

nodes.label: CSP for HTML vs JSON APIs
nodes.rationale: CSP matters more for HTML apps than pure JSON APIs. APIs may disable noisy browser-only policies; still review each toggle.
nodes.norm_label: csp for html vs json apis

nodes.label: Helmet
nodes.rationale: Helmet mounts secure default headers. Addresses common missing security headers, not auth or injection by itself. Not a full security program.

nodes.label: Stricter login rate limits
nodes.rationale: Brute-force protection on /login is tighter than global API limits and sits on the auth routes.

nodes.label: express-rate-limit
nodes.rationale: Limit by IP or user. Keys must use the real client IP via trust proxy. standardHeaders true, legacyHeaders false.

nodes.label: Skip liveness probes in rate limits
nodes.rationale: skip when req.path === '/health' so probes do not consume the window.
nodes.norm_label: skip liveness probes in rate limits

nodes.label: Controller service repository
nodes.rationale: Controllers translate HTTP. Services own rules. Repositories own queries. Driver types do not leak upward. Express owns where the HTTP layer stops.

nodes.label: Domain vs transport
nodes.rationale: Transport is HTTP. Domain is product language. Crossing them freely couples tests to Express. No Request types in domain.

nodes.label: Thin handler pipeline
nodes.rationale: Auth middleware then validate middleware then thin handler then service. One use-case per handler. RBAC lives in route-level middleware or the service for multi-resource rules.

nodes.label: Router factory dependency injection
nodes.rationale: Pass dependencies into router factories. Do not import a global db singleton if you care about tests. Tests substitute fakes; boot order stays explicit.

nodes.label: Enqueue side effects from routes
nodes.rationale: Validate, persist, enqueue, respond. Never await email, webhooks, or PDF generation on the request path. Use an outbox in the same transaction when needed (Node 7).

nodes.label: Validate at the HTTP boundary
nodes.rationale: Everything from the network is untrusted. Parse it before services run. The principle outlives Zod, Valibot, or hand parsers. Validating only in the database is late, worse errors, and injection risk.

nodes.label: 404 to hide private resource existence
nodes.rationale: 404 instead of 403 for another user's private doc avoids leaking that the id exists.

nodes.label: tenantId from identity
nodes.rationale: Force tenantId from identity, never from raw body alone. Client-supplied tenantId enables tenant hopping / IDOR.

nodes.label: Dynamic origin reflection allow-list
nodes.rationale: Reflecting any Origin with credentials is a bug. Dynamic origin reflection must allow-list.

nodes.label: Signed outbound webhook payload
nodes.rationale: HMAC over the body with a per-subscriber secret plus a timestamp so a captured request cannot be replayed. Include an event id for receiver dedup.

nodes.label: Four outbound-job properties
nodes.rationale: Idempotent on a domain-derived key, bounded by a timeout, classified so 4xx die permanently, and recorded locally as the idempotency guard.

nodes.label: Provider idempotency key
nodes.rationale: Domain-derived key such as order-receipt:orderId, plus the provider's own key, closes the window a local sent-table cannot.

nodes.label: Timeout budget
nodes.rationale: One deadline for the operation; each step gets the remainder. After a 200 ms step of a 500 ms budget the next call got 300 ms and aborted at 301 ms.

nodes.label: fetch has no default timeout
nodes.rationale: Node fetch waits as long as the socket stays open. AbortSignal.timeout(300) aborted after 306 ms with TimeoutError.

nodes.label: statement_timeout vs query_timeout
nodes.rationale: statement_timeout is enforced by PostgreSQL and cancels the query. query_timeout is client-side: the client stops waiting while the server keeps running.

nodes.label: A timeout is an unknown state
nodes.rationale: The remote side may have completed after you stopped waiting. Retrying a timed-out write requires idempotency. Timeouts are not a circuit breaker.
nodes.norm_label: a timeout is an unknown state

nodes.label: AbortSignal.any composition
nodes.rationale: Compose timeout, client disconnect, and shutdown. Whichever fires first stops the operation through a single signal parameter.

nodes.label: Abort on request close
nodes.rationale: req close fires on normal completion too. Check !req.readableEnded before aborting or successful work is cancelled.

nodes.label: Cancellation is cooperative
nodes.rationale: fetch, timers, streams, and fs/promises honour a signal. Your loops need throwIfAborted(). A synchronous JSON.parse cannot be interrupted.

nodes.label: Domain-derived idempotency key
nodes.rationale: Provider header or unique constraint plus ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING. Then repetition is harmless and retrying is free.

nodes.label: Retry at one layer
nodes.rationale: Client × service × job attempts: 5×5×5 is 125 hits on a struggling dependency. In a job, throw and let the queue reschedule — do not sleep in the handler.

nodes.label: Transient vs permanent HTTP failures
nodes.rationale: 429 and 5xx retry. Other 4xx fail identically forever. 409 only after re-read. Retrying 422 burns the attempt budget and looks like an outage.

nodes.label: Transient and safe-to-repeat
nodes.rationale: Both must be yes. Three of four matrix cells say do not retry. Duplicate charges come from retrying a transient but unsafe POST.

nodes.label: Circuit breaker after repeated failures
nodes.rationale: Backoff does not reduce total load during a long outage. Fail fast after N consecutive failures, then probe with a single request.

nodes.label: Background work
nodes.rationale: Producer/consumer shape for work that must not sit in the request path. Framework-free: AbortSignal, plain functions, separate processes.

nodes.label: Resilience
nodes.rationale: Timeouts, cancellation, retry classification, backoff, and concurrency limits that keep a process from becoming the outage.

nodes.label: Queue every outbound call
nodes.rationale: A third party's latency and availability become yours in the request path. Their p99 is your p99, their 503 is your 500, and the request cannot retry.

nodes.label: Acknowledge after the effect
nodes.rationale: Ack after the effect and a crash is a duplicate, which idempotency handles. Ack first and a crash is silent loss, which nothing handles.

nodes.label: Timeouts must shrink down the stack
nodes.rationale: If the caller allows 2 s and the callee has 3 s, the client gives up first and the callee's work is wasted while still holding resources. Retries live inside the budget.
nodes.norm_label: timeouts must shrink down the stack

nodes.label: A timeout is not a failure
nodes.rationale: The request may have succeeded after you stopped listening. Retrying an unguarded POST /charge is a second execution of work that already happened.
nodes.norm_label: a timeout is not a failure

nodes.label: What StrictMode double-invokes
nodes.rationale: Component body, useState init, useMemo, useCallback, reducers, class constructor/render/SCU, setState updaters.

nodes.label: Ref cleanup functions
nodes.rationale: A callback may return a cleanup. Implicit arrow returns now look like cleanups: add braces.

nodes.label: findDOMNode removed in React 19
nodes.rationale: Slow, fragile, first-child only, broke abstraction. Replace with a ref on the real element.

nodes.label: When render props still win
nodes.rationale: The host controls placement, values are per-item, or render must happen inside a boundary. A hook cannot render.

nodes.label: Wrapper hell
nodes.rationale: Each render prop adds a JSX nesting level. Hooks compose as lines instead.

nodes.label: Animation cleanup resets, it does not reverse
nodes.rationale: Undo means restore the initial value or reset the tween timeline, not play the animation backwards.
nodes.norm_label: animation cleanup resets, it does not reverse

nodes.label: Idempotent widget setup
nodes.rationale: setZoomLevel twice is a no-op. showModal twice throws and needs close() in cleanup. The test is the API, not the widget.

nodes.label: pg Pool vs Client
nodes.rationale: Pool is the default for servers. Client or pool.connect() only when consecutive statements must share one connection: transactions, cursors, LISTEN, migrations.

nodes.label: MongoClient is the pool
nodes.rationale: One per process at module scope. Default maxPoolSize 100; one client per request opens unbounded connections.

nodes.label: 25P02 and SAVEPOINT
nodes.rationale: A failed statement poisons the Postgres transaction. Continuing requires a SAVEPOINT taken beforehand.

nodes.label: withTransaction helper
nodes.rationale: pool.connect, BEGIN, fn(client), COMMIT or ROLLBACK, release in finally. Write it once; never write BEGIN in a handler.

nodes.label: Prisma 7 driver adapter
nodes.rationale: url in datasource is P1012. Connection lives in prisma.config.ts; client requires PrismaPg over a pg pool.

nodes.label: Keyset pagination
nodes.rationale: APIs should not hold a server cursor across requests. where id > $1 order by id limit $2. offset walks and discards skipped rows.

nodes.label: pg-cursor
nodes.rationale: Server-side state on one checked-out client. Same dedicated-connection rule as transactions.

nodes.label: Worker concurrency
nodes.rationale: In-flight promises on one event loop, not threads. Helps I/O; CPU work needs more processes. Match pool size to concurrency.

nodes.label: Ledger insert guards relative updates
nodes.rationale: Insert ledger on idempotency_key, apply delta only if rowCount is 1, both in one transaction.

nodes.label: Dual-write problem
nodes.rationale: Two systems cannot commit together. Queue down: order exists, jobs enqueued = 0. try/catch is a third write that can also fail.

nodes.label: Outbox table
nodes.rationale: Insert the intent in the same transaction as the business row. Rollback left neither. Same checked-out client required.

nodes.label: Retry the whole transaction
nodes.rationale: Never retry a statement inside an aborted tx (25P02). Retry from BEGIN on a fresh checkout. Correct for 40001 and 40P01.

nodes.label: Declare the listener inside setup
nodes.rationale: removeEventListener matches on identity. A handler recreated between setup and cleanup removes nothing and listeners accumulate.

nodes.label: Neither race guard is a cache
nodes.rationale: Both stop the wrong data rendering. Neither deduplicates, caches, or starts the request earlier.
nodes.norm_label: neither race guard is a cache

nodes.label: Callback refs get the same extra cycle
nodes.rationale: Missing ref cleanup doubles registry counts. React 19 ref cleanup functions make symmetry expressible.
nodes.norm_label: callback refs get the same extra cycle

nodes.label: Double render vs extra effect cycle
nodes.rationale: Double render finds impurity; extra effect cycle finds missing cleanup. Event handlers are in neither.
nodes.norm_label: double render vs extra effect cycle

nodes.label: Partial StrictMode skips the extra effect cycle
nodes.rationale: Child-only double mount cannot happen in production, so React declines to simulate it. The check requires StrictMode at the root.
nodes.norm_label: partial strictmode skips the extra effect cycle

nodes.label: Async setup is not allowed
nodes.rationale: An async function returns a Promise, not a cleanup. Declare an inner async function and return a real cleanup.

nodes.label: Unstable Effect Event identity is a runtime assertion
nodes.rationale: Identity changes every render on purpose. Putting one in a dependency array re-runs the effect every render and makes the bug obvious.
nodes.norm_label: unstable effect event identity is a runtime assertion

nodes.label: Layout-effect setState runs remaining Effects immediately
nodes.rationale: A state update inside useLayoutEffect executes all remaining Effects including useEffect, dragging unrelated work onto the paint-blocking path.
nodes.norm_label: layout-effect setstate runs remaining effects immediately

nodes.label: useLayoutEffect does nothing on the server
nodes.rationale: No layout information and no paint on the server. Options: useEffect, client-only, isMounted, or useSyncExternalStore.
nodes.norm_label: uselayouteffect does nothing on the server

nodes.label: Resolve then check containment
nodes.rationale: path.resolve then p === root || p.startsWith(root + sep). Bare startsWith(root) matches uploads-evil. Also catches resolve(root, '/etc/passwd').

nodes.label: Symlink escape
nodes.rationale: path.resolve is string arithmetic. A file inside the root can point outside. fs.realpath and re-check for attacker-controlled uploads.

nodes.label: Zip slip
nodes.rationale: Archive entry named ../../etc/cron.d/x escapes the extraction directory. Validate every entry path against the destination root before writing.

nodes.label: DNS rebinding
nodes.rationale: Check-then-fetch resolves twice. A one-second TTL can return public to the validator and private to the connection. Only a check at connect time closes it.

nodes.label: Egress proxy for user URLs
nodes.rationale: Allowlist hosts when destinations are knowable. For webhooks, send outbound through a host whose firewall permits public ranges only. Node 24 has no --allow-net.

nodes.label: Literal IPs bypass custom lookup
nodes.rationale: lookup is NEVER CALLED for http://127.0.0.1/ — there is no name. Parse-time net.isIP is required alongside the connect-time guard.

nodes.label: Unvalidated fetch redirects
nodes.rationale: fetch follows redirects by default. A public URL that 302s to 169.254.169.254 passes any up-front check. Use redirect:manual and re-validate each hop.

nodes.label: Parse, connect-time, and redirect re-check
nodes.rationale: Allowlist http/https at parse (data: returns 200). guardedLookup rejects private names. Re-parse every Location. Need all three.

nodes.label: WHATWG URL IP normalisation
nodes.rationale: 2130706433, 0x7f000001, 0177.0.0.1 and 127.1 all become hostname 127.0.0.1. Strip IPv6 brackets; ::ffff:127.0.0.1 becomes ::ffff:7f00:1.

nodes.label: path.join is not a security boundary
nodes.rationale: join('/srv/app/uploads', '../../../etc/passwd') returns /etc/passwd with no error. Normalising .. is its job, not a defence.
nodes.norm_label: path.join is not a security boundary

nodes.label: Effects only run on the client
nodes.rationale: They cannot produce server HTML. They are the legal place for window, document, localStorage after mount.
nodes.norm_label: effects only run on the client

nodes.label: Logic that belongs to an event
nodes.norm_label: logic that belongs to an event

nodes.label: State-as-a-trigger antipattern
nodes.rationale: setJsonToSubmit in the handler plus an Effect that posts when it is non-null reconstructs intent after the fact. Both the state and the Effect should disappear.

nodes.label: Phase 6 — Rendering performance and the React Compiler
nodes.norm_label: phase 6 — rendering performance and the react compiler

nodes.label: Phase 7 — Custom hooks and the Rules of React
nodes.norm_label: phase 7 — custom hooks and the rules of react

nodes.label: Phase 1 — JSX and what a component returns
nodes.norm_label: phase 1 — jsx and what a component returns

nodes.label: Insecure deserialization
nodes.rationale: JSON.parse is inert data. RCE appears when eval, new Function, vm, YAML custom tags, or function-reviving libraries sit on top.

nodes.label: Mass assignment
nodes.rationale: Spreading req.body onto a record lets the client set isAdmin/credits. prisma.user.update({ data: req.body }) is the same bug with a DB round trip.

nodes.label: Open redirect
nodes.rationale: //evil and /\evil both start with / and resolve off-origin. includes(own-domain) matches fragments. Bypass of OAuth redirect_uri is account takeover.

nodes.label: safeNext origin check
nodes.rationale: Parse with new URL(next, BASE), compare origin, return pathname+search+hash only. Fail closed to a fixed path, never throw on malformed next.

nodes.label: Request body size cap
nodes.rationale: A schema cannot defend a payload it has not received. .max() on an array runs after every element is parsed and can be slower than no max.

nodes.label: HTTP boundary check order
nodes.rationale: Content-type → size cap → JSON.parse → schema. JSON.parse of 20 MB is 40.7 ms of event loop; the cap rejects at 1 KB in 0.002 ms.

nodes.label: Zod coercion pitfalls
nodes.rationale: z.coerce.number is Number(): '', [] and null become 0. z.coerce.boolean maps 'false' to true. Repeated query keys arrive as arrays.

nodes.label: Zod unknown-key modes
nodes.rationale: z.object strips, z.strictObject rejects, z.looseObject keeps and copies inherited properties. Privileged fields must be omitted from the schema, not validated.

nodes.label: Deserialization, open redirects, mass assignment
nodes.rationale: Three bugs, one root: the request decided the data shape and the code accepted it. Fix: name what you accept and ignore the rest.

nodes.label: Input validation at the boundary
nodes.rationale: The one Master practice in front of the prior nine bugs. Content-type, size cap, JSON.parse, then schema. Verified zod 4.4.3 / valibot 1.4.2.

nodes.label: Field allowlist over denylist
nodes.rationale: A denylist fails open on the column added next month. An allowlist (or schema that strips unknown keys) fails safe when the schema grows.

nodes.label: Parse, don't validate
nodes.rationale: A validator returns a boolean and leaves the untrusted object. A parser returns a new typed value; unchecked fields no longer exist.

nodes.label: sandbox/ts-p0 measurement suite
nodes.rationale: ex1-erasure.sh … ex9-node-runs-ts.sh. typescript 7.0.2 and typescript5 5.9.3 side by side.

nodes.label: Phase 1 measurement corrections
nodes.rationale: Weak-type detection stops when a required property is added; interface vs type error folklore failed; TS2589 only at depth 5000; reduce infers from elements; plain symbol accepted as computed key.

nodes.label: Phase 1 phase gate
nodes.rationale: Model an API payload — optional fields, a status union, a nested object, a list — without any, and say why each choice is not a neighbour.

nodes.label: sandbox/ts-p1 measurement suite
nodes.rationale: ex1-inference-widening.sh … ex7-object-types.sh. Emit declarations and read inferred types from .d.ts.

nodes.label: Removed Express 4 APIs
nodes.rationale: app.del, old req.param() behaviour, etc. Stay on 4 to avoid migration cost; move to 5 for supported async and modern path rules (Multer 2.x bump).

nodes.label: compression middleware
nodes.rationale: Compressing in Node costs event-loop time. Terminate gzip at Nginx or the CDN when you have one. Never double-compress. Use the middleware when Express is the edge or you need per-route control.

nodes.label: Phase 9 gate
nodes.rationale: Behind a proxy req.ip is correct; CORS allows the SPA with credentials; rate limits key properly.

nodes.label: Unit vs integration vs e2e
nodes.rationale: Draw the boundary at I/O. Many unit, some integration (one real dependency), few e2e on money paths. Separate by filename glob, not experimental tags.

nodes.label: Dependency injection via parameters
nodes.rationale: Factory closing over deps, or db as first argument so a pool or a transactional client can be handed in. Defaults keep tests from constructing the world.

nodes.label: Hidden dependency
nodes.rationale: new Date, Math.random, process.env at import, module-scope Pool, fixed-URL fetch, top-level logger. ESM evaluates config before any test body.

nodes.label: mock.fn
nodes.rationale: Records callCount and calls[].arguments/result/error/this/target. mockImplementationOnce varies per call. resetCalls clears history; restore puts the original back.

nodes.label: mock.method spy vs stub
nodes.rationale: Two args spies (original runs); a third stubs. Zero recorded calls usually means the code captured the original reference before the mock.

nodes.label: mock.timers
nodes.rationale: Enable only the APIs needed; tick one ms before the boundary then over it. Do not mix fake time with real I/O. Pass now when faking Date.

nodes.label: t.mock vs top-level mock
nodes.rationale: Top-level mock.method stayed fake in the next test. Use t.mock, or mock.restoreAll() in afterEach.

nodes.label: Unit, integration and e2e
nodes.rationale: Categories are about what you replace, not size. 50-test unit suite 0.22 s; Postgres container start ~5.6 s.

nodes.label: Writing testable code
nodes.rationale: Hard-to-test is usually a hidden grab. Pass the dependency in. Verified ESM import-time process.env bake-in.

nodes.label: Mocking — mock.fn, mock.method and timers
nodes.rationale: Built-in mocking. t.mock auto-restores; the top-level mock leaks. Verified Node 24.19.0.

nodes.label: Do not mock the thing that can be wrong
nodes.rationale: If mocking the dependency removes the risk, it is an integration test. Do not mock the DB driver. An in-memory SQLite is not Postgres.
nodes.norm_label: do not mock the thing that can be wrong

nodes.label: No DI container in Node
nodes.rationale: A function taking an object already is DI. Wire by hand in main.mjs. A container is a signal about design, not a missing framework.

nodes.label: 114 Express topics 28 Master
nodes.rationale: After Claude's six additive rows and one tier flip: 114 topics, Master 25%, about 90 explanation pages.

nodes.label: Master tier share about 28 percent
nodes.rationale: Demote JSON parse failures, custom errors, templates, complex Multer, advanced CORS so Master stays on routing, middleware lifecycle, Zod basics, Helmet and rate-limit.

nodes.label: Approve proposed Express structure
nodes.rationale: 108 topics, 28 Master (26%), 4 parts under the 300-line cap; additions only, nothing removed.

nodes.label: Request-id correlation middleware
nodes.rationale: Mint or accept X-Request-Id on req and carry it with AsyncLocalStorage; mechanism is Node Phase 10, mount is Express.

nodes.label: pagesPlanned bookkeeping
nodes.rationale: progress.js recorded pages with no pagesPlanned so the UI treated 78 short pages as finished. First recommended pass is visibility, not rewrite.

nodes.label: Git is not a deployment tool
nodes.norm_label: git is not a deployment tool

nodes.label: Testcontainers under rootless podman
nodes.rationale: DOCKER_HOST=unix:///run/user/1000/podman/podman.sock and TESTCONTAINERS_RYUK_DISABLED=true. Missing first: no working container runtime. Missing second: Ryuk wait '/.*Started.*/' never received.

nodes.label: PostgreSqlContainer
nodes.rationale: Starts a real database from inside the test process. getConnectionUri() uses a random host port so parallel files and CI jobs never collide.

nodes.label: Real SQLSTATE from a real engine
nodes.rationale: Measured 23505 orders_sku_key and 23514 orders_qty_check. A mocked pool can only return whatever you already believed.
nodes.norm_label: real sqlstate from a real engine

nodes.label: Container start cost
nodes.rationale: 5585 ms and 6355 ms on a warm postgres:18-alpine image; queries 15–20 ms after. Start once per file in before, not per test. Separate script from the unit suite.

nodes.label: --test-global-setup
nodes.rationale: globalSetup runs before any file, teardown after the summary. Start one database for the whole run; pass the connection string via env because files are separate processes.

nodes.label: Database cluster
nodes.rationale: One data directory on disk; may contain many databases. Distinct from the server process, the SQL catalog, and the client.

nodes.label: PostgreSQL object-relational server
nodes.rationale: Long-running program that stores data, enforces rules, and answers queries over a network protocol. Custom types, jsonb, arrays, full-text, extensions.

nodes.label: select version() PostgreSQL 18.4
nodes.rationale: Verified 2026-08 via psql and pg.Pool against 127.0.0.1:55432. PostgreSQL 18.4 on x86_64-pc-linux-musl, Alpine gcc 15.2.0.

nodes.label: PostgreSQL 18.4 target
nodes.rationale: Server and psql 18.4, pg on Node 24, postgres:18-alpine on 127.0.0.1:55432 never localhost. Node Phase 6/7 pages were measured on 17.10 — re-check version-sensitive links.

nodes.label: Never double your own database driver
nodes.rationale: Stubbing pool.query goes green against invalid SQL, a missing column, and a missing constraint. If mocking removes the risk, it is an integration test.
nodes.norm_label: never double your own database driver

nodes.label: App is a guest with a connection
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL owns the durable truth. Application code is bad at concurrent writers, crash recovery, indexes, and access control. The server does not care whether the client is psql or pg.
nodes.norm_label: app is a guest with a connection

nodes.label: PostgreSQL example policy
nodes.rationale: Every page carries SQL or shell and the Node pg code that issues it. A psql-only page is incomplete for Phases 2–13. Real output, not plausible-looking.

nodes.label: Git syllabus stops at push
nodes.rationale: If it still applies when every framework is deleted, it is Git's. CI and deploy start in Node Phase 11.

nodes.label: node --check
nodes.rationale: Parses and reports SyntaxErrors with no execution and no side effects.

nodes.label: Loose equality ==
nodes.rationale: Same NaN/-0 outcomes as === in this table; used only by ==.

nodes.label: Numeric separators
nodes.rationale: Underscores ignored by the parser. Illegal leading, trailing, doubled, or next to the decimal. _1000 is a ReferenceError (identifier), not SyntaxError.

nodes.label: Prefix vs postfix increment
nodes.rationale: Postfix returns before mutate; prefix after. Use as statements or in for headers, never nested.

nodes.label: do…while cursor pagination
nodes.rationale: Body runs at least once — fetch a page before you know whether a next cursor exists.

nodes.label: let fresh binding per iteration
nodes.rationale: var is one shared binding (timers log 3 3 3). let creates a fresh binding per iteration so closures capture their own value.

nodes.label: typeof binds tighter than +
nodes.rationale: typeof 1+1 is 'number1'. Unary operators bind very tightly.

nodes.label: void operator
nodes.rationale: Evaluates operand, always returns undefined. void 0 was a safe undefined before ES5. Modern leftover: discard a floating promise for a linter.

nodes.label: Function.prototype.toString source
nodes.rationale: Returns exact source. Method shorthand m(){return 1;} is not a valid standalone expression, so DI that evals toString breaks.

nodes.label: 8 KB pages
nodes.rationale: Unit of table/index I/O in shared buffers and on disk.

nodes.label: OS page cache
nodes.rationale: Kernel caches file pages the server read or wrote. PostgreSQL benefits from it but does not manage it as its own API. A shared-buffer miss may still be an OS-cache hit.

nodes.label: Shared buffers
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL's shared-memory cache of 8 KB table/index pages used by all backends. Measured alpine default 128MB. Too large fights the OS cache.

nodes.label: work_mem
nodes.rationale: Backend-private sort/hash memory. Not the main row cache. Distinct from shared buffers.

nodes.label: Checkpoint
nodes.rationale: Writes dirty buffers out so data files catch up with WAL. Lagging checkpoints can grow pg_wal.

nodes.label: wal_level = replica
nodes.rationale: Measured usual default on PostgreSQL 18.4. Supports physical replication.

nodes.label: Write-ahead log
nodes.rationale: Sequential record of changes flushed so the database can recover after a crash and stream changes to replicas. Never delete WAL files by hand.

nodes.label: Background writer
nodes.rationale: Writes dirty buffers between checkpoints so checkpoints are cheaper.

nodes.label: Checkpointer
nodes.rationale: Writes dirty buffers out and advances checkpoints. A stuck checkpointer is an ops signal (Phase 13).

nodes.label: WAL writer
nodes.rationale: Helps flush WAL efficiently. backend_type walwriter.

nodes.label: COMMIT flushes WAL
nodes.rationale: Under default synchronous settings COMMIT succeeds only after the needed WAL is flushed. BEGIN is cheap; modifying data generates WAL; commit makes it durable.

nodes.label: Change is written twice
nodes.rationale: Once to WAL immediately for durability/order, later to heap/index files via dirty shared buffers, checkpoints, and the background writer. Normal, not a bug.

nodes.label: Shorthand property names
nodes.rationale: { a } means { a: a }. It cannot rename, so API boundaries that change casing still need the full form.

nodes.label: undefined and holes sort last
nodes.rationale: Comparator is never called for them. Missing properties on objects still reach it. Map to a sentinel to put missing values first.

nodes.label: String.prototype.at
nodes.rationale: Accepts negative indices; bracket notation does not. Out of range returns undefined, unlike charAt which returns empty string.

nodes.label: String.prototype.padStart
nodes.rationale: First argument is target total length. Already-long strings are unchanged; multi-character pads are repeated then cut.

nodes.label: String.prototype.repeat
nodes.rationale: Negative count throws RangeError. Replaces the old new Array(n+1).join(str) idiom.

nodes.label: JSON.stringify replacer
nodes.rationale: Function form returning undefined omits a key at every level. Array form is a deny-by-default allowlist. Symbol keys stay ignored.

nodes.label: JSON.parse is not prototype pollution
nodes.rationale: "__proto__" is an ordinary own property in JSON. Pollution happens later if a merge assigns through that key.

nodes.label: JSON.parse SyntaxError
nodes.rationale: Trailing commas, single quotes and empty bodies throw. JSON is stricter than object-literal syntax.

nodes.label: Map add/remove performance
nodes.rationale: If you are calling delete in a loop, you wanted a Map. No multiplier is claimed.

nodes.label: Published host port 55432
nodes.rationale: Non-default host port so nothing collides with a system Postgres on 5432. Inside the container the listen port remains 5432.

nodes.label: postgres:18-alpine sandbox
nodes.rationale: podman run docker.io/library/postgres:18-alpine with POSTGRES_USER/DB/PASSWORD=devbible. Verified PostgreSQL 18.4 on x86_64-pc-linux-musl.

nodes.label: inet_server_port()
nodes.rationale: Shows the server listen port inside its network namespace (5432), not Docker's published host port (55432).

nodes.label: Five-year major support
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL ships a new major roughly once a year and supports each major for about five years. Upgrade minors promptly; treat majors as a project.

nodes.label: Major vs minor versions
nodes.rationale: Major (17→18) needs planned upgrade via pg_upgrade, dump/restore, or logical replication. Minor (18.3→18.4) is same on-disk major: install and restart.

nodes.label: Target PostgreSQL 18.4
nodes.rationale: Every Phase 0 example was executed against postgres:18-alpine. Use 127.0.0.1, never localhost.

nodes.label: musl vs glibc sort order
nodes.rationale: version() names the platform (x86_64-pc-linux-musl on alpine). musl and glibc sort text differently, which can explain local-vs-production ORDER BY differences.

nodes.label: podman exec psql over unix socket
nodes.rationale: podman exec -it devbible-pg psql -U devbible -d devbible. No host, port, or password. Fastest check that the server itself is healthy.
nodes.norm_label: podman exec psql over unix socket

nodes.label: PostgreSQL vs MySQL vs SQLite
nodes.rationale: Most folklore is out of date. MySQL 8 is strict by default, SQLite has transactional DDL, sequence gaps happen everywhere. Surviving differences change the schema.

nodes.label: Phase 0 — PostgreSQL architecture
nodes.rationale: Twelve pages on what the server is before serious SQL. Target PostgreSQL 18.4 from Node 24 with pg, measured on postgres:18-alpine at 127.0.0.1:55432.

nodes.label: Use 127.0.0.1 not localhost
nodes.rationale: Node's DNS order prefers ::1; IPv4 port publishes fail with confusing errors if you use localhost.

nodes.label: Container-first local Postgres
nodes.rationale: Pin major version, reset in one command, match CI. Prefer that over fighting a distro package until you have a reason to go native.

nodes.label: Map insertion order vs object order
nodes.rationale: Integer-like object keys enumerate ascending first. A Map keyed by numeric IDs keeps insertion order.
nodes.norm_label: map insertion order vs object order

nodes.label: Map has no structural typing
nodes.rationale: A Map of string keys cannot catch config.get("retires") the way config.retires would.

nodes.label: Nested destructuring
nodes.rationale: Intermediate names are paths, not bindings. A missing level applies the inner pattern to undefined and throws.

nodes.label: Parentheses for object assignment
nodes.rationale: A statement starting with { is a block. ({ a, b } = obj) forces expression position. Array patterns have no such problem.

nodes.label: Destructuring swap idiom
nodes.rationale: The right-hand array is fully evaluated before assignment, so no temporary is needed.

nodes.label: Destructuring detaches this
nodes.rationale: const { start } = timer is assignment, same as const f = obj.f. APIs meant to be destructured return closures.

nodes.label: Labelled break
nodes.rationale: outer: for (...) { break outer } exits both loops. No labelled escape from forEach.

nodes.label: setTimeout returns a Timeout object in Node
nodes.norm_label: settimeout returns a timeout object in node

nodes.label: server_version_num
nodes.rationale: Integer form useful in scripts. Measured 180004 = 18.4. Gate multi-major features on this, rarely needed for one product database.

nodes.label: \d family
nodes.rationale: \l databases, \dn schemas, \dt tables, \di indexes, \dv views, \ds sequences, \df functions, \dm materialized views. + adds detail; S includes system objects.

nodes.label: psql -E echo hidden
nodes.rationale: Prints the catalog query behind each meta-command so you can pin it in application code for a target version.

nodes.label: \d table
nodes.rationale: Columns, defaults, every index (including partial WHERE), check constraints, FKs with ON DELETE, and Referenced by on the parent. Adapts to indexes, views, and sequences.

nodes.label: \d+
nodes.rationale: Adds storage (plain vs extended/TOAST), stats target, comment, named NOT NULL constraints (PostgreSQL 17+), access method, sizes, and view definition.

nodes.label: Normalised CHECK display
nodes.rationale: \d shows the server's stored expression, not typed DDL. IN ('open','paid','shipped') displays as = ANY (ARRAY[...]). Compare semantics, not text.

nodes.label: pg_dump --schema-only
nodes.rationale: Produces replayable DDL. \d is a report, not source of truth for migrations.

nodes.label: \sv and \sf
nodes.rationale: Print the source of a view or function, ready to copy into a migration.

nodes.label: \h SQL syntax
nodes.rationale: Offline grammar plus doc URL for the connected major (measured /docs/18/sql-createindex.html). Covers SQL commands only, not functions — those use \df/\sf.
Documents psql's own backslash commands. \? variables lists AUTOCOMMIT, ON_ERROR_STOP, VERBOSITY. \? options is psql --help.

nodes.label: Built-in psql variables
nodes.rationale: DBNAME, USER, HOST, PORT, SERVER_VERSION_NAME, VERSION_NUM, ROW_COUNT, ERROR, SQLSTATE, LAST_ERROR_MESSAGE, plus ON_ERROR_STOP, AUTOCOMMIT, VERBOSITY.

nodes.label: Backslash commands are not SQL
nodes.rationale: psql interprets them locally and issues catalog queries. Unavailable from pg, Prisma, or any driver. Line-oriented; cannot mix into a statement.

nodes.label: Bun as a development tool on a Node deploy
nodes.norm_label: bun as a development tool on a node deploy

nodes.label: --max-old-space-size
nodes.rationale: Raise it when you have proven a legitimately large working set — not to postpone a memory leak.

nodes.label: process.resourceUsage
nodes.rationale: CPU attribution over a window (user vs system) and cumulative FS ops. Export deltas between scrapes.

nodes.label: Closure retention of large objects
nodes.rationale: A timer callback that closes over hugeBuffer keeps the allocation alive for the full delay. Close over the derived scalar instead.

nodes.label: Unremoved event listeners
nodes.rationale: The emitter retains the function, which retains its closed-over scope. on and off must share the same function reference.

nodes.label: Dockerizing Node
nodes.rationale: A good Node image is small, runs as non-root, caches dependencies separately from app code, and does not copy secrets or laptop node_modules.

nodes.label: Behind a reverse proxy
nodes.rationale: TLS usually terminates at the load balancer. Trust hop-by-hop headers only from that proxy or attackers forge client IPs.

nodes.label: path.extname last extension only
nodes.rationale: report.tar.gz yields .gz. File-type checks from extname are bypassed by evil.php.jpg.

nodes.label: path.posix
nodes.rationale: Use for URL paths, S3 keys, tar and git paths — always forward slashes. Default path is the host platform.

nodes.label: View optimisation fence
nodes.rationale: Aggregates then filtered, DISTINCT, window functions, LIMIT inside the view, and set operations materialise the view before the outer filter.

nodes.label: View predicate pushdown
nodes.rationale: Filtering on a GROUP BY key pushed down (0.8 ms); filtering the aggregate result forced a full scan (135.8 ms, 170×).

nodes.label: View is a stored query not stored data
nodes.rationale: pg_relation_size is 0 bytes. The view is substituted before planning so the planner optimises one combined query.
nodes.norm_label: view is a stored query not stored data

nodes.label: DROP EXTENSION blocked by type users
nodes.rationale: 2BP01 while any column uses a type the extension provides. CASCADE drops those columns.
nodes.norm_label: drop extension blocked by type users

nodes.label: Materialized view stores its result
nodes.rationale: 256 kB against a plain view's 0 bytes. Needs its own indexes. Not automatically faster if the view already pushes down.

nodes.label: dblink autonomous query
nodes.rationale: No foreign tables, no pushdown. Still useful for a query on another database that is not part of your transaction.

nodes.label: IMPORT FOREIGN SCHEMA
nodes.rationale: Snapshot of remote definitions. Does not track later schema changes; re-import after remote migrations.

nodes.label: FDW has no two-phase commit
nodes.rationale: Local commit can succeed while the remote fails. Treat FDW as a read tool, not a write path.

nodes.label: postgres_fdw foreign table
nodes.rationale: Looks like a table and is a query against another server. User mapping holds a password in the catalog.

nodes.label: FDW Remote SQL pushdown
nodes.rationale: Full pushdown 2.9 ms vs 41.9 ms with a VOLATILE predicate (14×). EXPLAIN VERBOSE Remote SQL is the only tool that matters.

nodes.label: Views — naming a query, and their limits
nodes.norm_label: views — naming a query, and their limits

nodes.label: URL host vs hostname
nodes.rationale: host includes the port; hostname does not. Allowlists must compare hostname.

nodes.label: node:url
nodes.rationale: WHATWG URL and URLSearchParams are globals. url.parse is deprecated DEP0169.

nodes.label: File streams
nodes.rationale: createReadStream and createWriteStream live on node:fs, not fs/promises.

nodes.label: createWriteStream default truncate
nodes.rationale: flags 'w' creates or empties the file immediately, even if nothing is written. Use 'a' to append.

nodes.label: Directories
nodes.rationale: readdir gives names; withFileTypes gives type without a stat per entry.

nodes.label: readdir order is not guaranteed
nodes.rationale: Filesystem-dependent. Unsorted numbered migrations fail when ext4 vs overlayfs differ.

nodes.label: stat and checking existence
nodes.rationale: Does this file exist is almost always the wrong question.

nodes.label: File handles
nodes.rationale: open returns a FileHandle owning an OS descriptor. One leak per request takes the server down with EMFILE.

nodes.label: os.EOL
nodes.rationale: For local human text files only. HTTP is always CRLF; protocols and JSON must not follow the host.

nodes.label: node:os
nodes.rationale: os reports the host. In a container that is a lie for CPU and memory.

nodes.label: Git (in scope)
nodes.rationale: Moved into scope 2026-08-13; was parked as universal tooling rather than part of the stack itself.

nodes.label: GraphQL (parked)
nodes.rationale: Parked because it is an API-design layer that would overlap Express if pulled in early.

nodes.label: Kubernetes (parked)
nodes.rationale: Parked: a layer above Docker & Nginx; only earns its place at real scale.

nodes.label: Parked technologies
nodes.rationale: GraphQL, tRPC and Kubernetes are named on the homepage but not committed until the eleven (now twelve with Git) are done.

nodes.label: In-scope tech stack
nodes.rationale: Twelve technologies: CSS, JavaScript, TypeScript, React, Node.js, MongoDB, PostgreSQL, Express, Docker & Podman, Redis, Nginx, Git.

nodes.label: tRPC (parked)
nodes.rationale: Parked: only pays off in an end-to-end TypeScript stack.

nodes.label: CSS scope rule
nodes.rationale: If deleting the stylesheet would delete the topic, it is CSS's.

nodes.label: Trigger firing order is alphabetical
nodes.rationale: Created zebra, alpha, middle; fired alpha, middle, zebra. Name with numeric prefixes if order matters.

nodes.label: BEFORE vs AFTER triggers
nodes.rationale: BEFORE can modify NEW and cancel with RETURN NULL. AFTER assignment to NEW is silently discarded — the row is already written.

nodes.label: BEFORE RETURN NULL cancels the row
nodes.rationale: 10 submitted, 5 stored; rowCount reported 5. Prefer RAISE EXCEPTION so the caller sees a rejection.
nodes.norm_label: before return null cancels the row

nodes.label: FOR EACH ROW vs FOR EACH STATEMENT
nodes.rationale: One UPDATE of 1000 rows: 1000 row firings, 1 statement firing. A statement trigger still fires when zero rows match.
nodes.norm_label: for each row vs for each statement

nodes.label: Trigger transition tables
nodes.rationale: REFERENCING OLD TABLE / NEW TABLE lets a statement trigger audit bulk changes in one insert instead of 1000 row inserts.

nodes.label: Trigger WHEN clause
nodes.rationale: Evaluated before the plpgsql call. Measured 0.86× of an unconditional row trigger. Cannot be used on INSTEAD OF.

nodes.label: RAISE EXCEPTION USING ERRCODE
nodes.rationale: Without an explicit SQLSTATE everything is P0001. Use 23xxx integrity codes so the app maps them like constraint violations.

nodes.label: Trigger functions must be plpgsql
nodes.rationale: NEW, OLD, RETURN NEW/NULL, TG_OP/TG_NAME/TG_LEVEL are the vocabulary. The honest list for plpgsql is trigger bodies plus rare data-heavy loops.

nodes.label: pg_notify from a trigger
nodes.rationale: AFTER trigger so the announced row exists. PERFORM rather than SELECT. Row-level 500 inserts → 500 notifications; statement-level → 1.

nodes.label: AFTER row audit trigger
nodes.rationale: Attached to the table so migrations, psql and other services cannot bypass it. to_jsonb(OLD/NEW) survives schema changes. Cost ~1.24×.

nodes.label: SET LOCAL app.user_id
nodes.rationale: current_setting(..., true) returns NULL if unset (avoids 42704). Plain SET behind a pooler lands on another backend.

nodes.label: WHEN OLD IS DISTINCT FROM NEW
nodes.rationale: <> is NULL when either side is NULL so NULL→value would not audit. WHEN is cheaper (0.86×) because the body never runs.
nodes.norm_label: when old is distinct from new

nodes.label: Watching files
nodes.rationale: fs.watch is fast and inconsistent; fs.watchFile is consistent and expensive. Production uses chokidar.

nodes.label: Directory execute is traverse
nodes.rationale: r without x lists names and cannot open entries. chmod 644 on a directory is a half-broken state.

nodes.label: Permissions and symlinks
nodes.rationale: POSIX octal bits, umask subtracts, and symlinks make a validated path read something else.

nodes.label: node:sea Single Executable Applications
nodes.rationale: Stability 1.1 prefix-only builtin. Assets are inside the binary; readFile cannot find them. Branch on isSea().

nodes.label: server clientError
nodes.rationale: Malformed request line or illegal header never becomes req/res. Write 400 on the raw socket.

nodes.label: HTTP in practice
nodes.rationale: Methods, status codes, negotiation and CORS — the parts argued in review.

nodes.label: HTTP status semantics
nodes.rationale: 401 vs 403 is who vs may-not; 400 vs 422 is parse vs business rule. Node drops bodies on 204 and HEAD.

nodes.label: Cookies
nodes.rationale: Node has no cookie API. Cookie attributes are the security model of session authentication.

nodes.label: Do not set Content-Type on FormData
nodes.rationale: A hand-set header overwrites the generated multipart boundary and the receiver cannot parse fields.
nodes.norm_label: do not set content-type on formdata

nodes.label: Keep-alive and connection pooling
nodes.rationale: Two unrelated pools: http.Agent for http.request and undici Dispatcher for fetch.

nodes.label: pg returns bigint as a string
nodes.rationale: int8 exceeds Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER. Measured 9007199254740993 arrived as a string. Compare as strings or BigInt. setTypeParser(20, parseInt) is a global decision.
nodes.norm_label: pg returns bigint as a string

nodes.label: PostgreSQL integer types
nodes.rationale: smallint 2 bytes ±32767, integer 4 bytes ±2.1e9, bigint 8 bytes ±9.22e18. No unsigned variant; use CHECK (n >= 0). Overflow raises 22003 rather than wrapping.

nodes.label: Integer cents in bigint
nodes.rationale: Exact and as fast as float: 27.7 ms vs 76.8 ms for 300k-row sum, 8 bytes vs 10. Units become implicit; a missed conversion is a 100× error.

nodes.label: pg returns numeric as a string
nodes.rationale: Converting to a JavaScript number would throw away exactness. Prefer SQL arithmetic or a decimal library. Never setTypeParser(1700, parseFloat).
nodes.norm_label: pg returns numeric as a string

nodes.label: numeric vs float
nodes.rationale: numeric is exact software decimal; double precision and real are approximate IEEE floats. 1000 additions of 0.01 gave 9.999999999999831 in float8 and 10.00 in numeric. numeric(p,s) overflow is 22003; extra scale rounds silently.

nodes.label: Amount plus currency
nodes.rationale: An amount alone is not money. Store numeric(14,2) plus char(3) currency. A composite FK (invoice_id, currency) referencing invoices (id, currency) makes mismatched lines impossible. Always declare scale; unconstrained numeric allows 16383 fractional digits.

nodes.label: ISO 4217 minor units
nodes.rationale: Not every currency has two decimals: JPY has none, some have three. Hard-coded ÷100 is wrong by 10 or 100. Store minor_units per currency. Unit prices need more scale than totals.

nodes.label: Store the FX rate with the transaction
nodes.rationale: Without fx_rate and fx_rate_at, next year's report reconverts at today's rate. Never convert for comparison on the fly. Rates need numeric(18,8) against amounts numeric(14,2).
nodes.norm_label: store the fx rate with the transaction

nodes.label: Append-only ledger
nodes.rationale: Do not store a mutable balance. Immutable signed entries; derive the balance with SUM. When reads get slow, add a materialised snapshot plus entries since. A wrong UPDATE permanently corrupts a mutable balance and loses history.

nodes.label: Money never in float
nodes.rationale: 0.01 has no exact binary form. An unbalanced ledger costs more than any query. Default numeric(12,2); move to integer cents only when a measurement says you must.

nodes.label: Do not use the money type
nodes.rationale: Locale-dependent via lc_monetary; dump/restore can break across locales; no currency identity. The documentation's own best-practice note prefers numeric.
nodes.norm_label: do not use the money type

nodes.label: Never parseFloat numeric
nodes.rationale: pg returns numeric as a string on purpose. parseFloat or overriding the type parser reintroduces IEEE-754 imprecision. Compute in SQL or a decimal library. Mixing SQL and JS-float totals is how two parts of one system disagree.

nodes.label: Outbound client discipline
nodes.rationale: One shared client, a deadline, bounded retries with backoff, Retry-After honoured, idempotency on money.

nodes.label: pg date column trap
nodes.rationale: DATE becomes a Date at local midnight; JSON.stringify ships yesterday in UTC+05:30. Keep DATE as YYYY-MM-DD via setTypeParser(1082).

nodes.label: Named prepared statements
nodes.rationale: Server plans once per connection. Measured 120 ms to 78 ms for 200 lookups. One name must always mean one SQL.

nodes.label: RETURNING
nodes.rationale: Generated row in the same round trip as the write, with no race. select max(id) after insert can see another transaction.

nodes.label: ObjectId type-strict equality
nodes.rationale: findOne({_id: urlString}) returns null forever. Wrap with new ObjectId after ObjectId.isValid.

nodes.label: updateOne vs replaceOne
nodes.rationale: updateOne applies operators to named fields. replaceOne substitutes the whole document, so omitted fields disappear.

nodes.label: w=majority
nodes.rationale: Write acknowledged by a majority so it survives failover. Costs latency; single-node ack can vanish when the primary steps down.

nodes.label: Query count per request
nodes.rationale: An endpoint whose query count grows with result size is an N+1. Assert it in tests; slow-query logs miss it.

nodes.label: Mongoose query buffering
nodes.rationale: Queries issued before connect hang for bufferTimeoutMS (10s) instead of failing at boot. Await connect at startup.

nodes.label: Named methods per aggregate
nodes.rationale: A generic Repository<T> findWhere becomes a query language. Named methods leave SQL free.

nodes.label: Aggregates ignore NULL
nodes.rationale: count(*) counts rows; count(col) counts non-nulls. sum() over no rows or all NULLs is NULL, not 0 — wrap with coalesce. NULLs sort last ASC and first DESC.

nodes.label: Empty string is not NULL
nodes.rationale: Oracle conflates them; PostgreSQL does not. || with a NULL operand yields NULL; concat() and concat_ws() skip NULLs. undefined parameters become NULL in pg.

nodes.label: NOT IN with NULL returns nothing
nodes.rationale: 2 NOT IN (1, NULL) is NULL because it expands to true AND (2 <> NULL). Prefer NOT EXISTS, which handles NULL and usually plans as an anti-join.
nodes.norm_label: not in with null returns nothing

nodes.label: NULL three-valued logic
nodes.rationale: NULL is absence. NULL = NULL is unknown. WHERE keeps only true, so col = NULL matches nothing. Use IS NULL or IS NOT DISTINCT FROM.

nodes.label: UNIQUE allows many NULLs
nodes.rationale: NULLs are not equal, so they do not conflict. Measured three NULLs accepted. UNIQUE NULLS NOT DISTINCT (PostgreSQL 15+) allows at most one.

nodes.label: boolean type
nodes.rationale: 1 byte. true/t/yes/y/on/1 and false/f/no/n/off/0; else 22P02. Three-valued unless NOT NULL. Count trues with count(*) FILTER (WHERE b); sum(b::int) is NULL-poisoned.

nodes.label: Enum cannot drop values
nodes.rationale: 0A000 dropping an enum value is not implemented. ALTER TYPE ADD VALUE then using it in the same transaction is 55P04, breaking atomic migrations. Enums sort by declaration order.

nodes.label: enum vs CHECK vs lookup table
nodes.rationale: Invalid value SQLSTATEs: enum 22P02, CHECK 23514, FK 23503. Enum 4-byte OID, ~18% smaller (7080 vs 8656 kB / 200k). All three arrive in Node as strings.
nodes.norm_label: enum vs check vs lookup table

nodes.label: citext
nodes.rationale: Case-insensitive text via CREATE EXTENSION citext. UNIQUE rejects case variants with 23505. A forgotten lower() on a text column silently misses rows. Folds case, not Unicode composition.

nodes.label: Domain type
nodes.rationale: Base type plus reusable CHECK, e.g. CREATE DOMAIN email AS citext. Violations 23514 name the domain constraint. Inherits base behaviour. Cannot hold FKs or deferred constraints. Adding a CHECK validates every table using it.

nodes.label: Exclusion constraint
nodes.rationale: EXCLUDE USING gist (room WITH =, during WITH &&) means no two rows share a room and overlapping times. Violations 23P01. Enforced by an index, so concurrent read-then-write cannot both succeed. Needs btree_gist for the scalar equality.

nodes.label: Default to a lookup table
nodes.rationale: Adding a value is an INSERT (3.4 ms), not DDL, and can carry label, colour, sort_order, is_terminal. CHECK re-validates every row (62.9 ms / 200k) unless NOT VALID then VALIDATE.

nodes.label: SQLite autocommit fsync
nodes.rationale: Each write outside a transaction is its own fsync. 1000 inserts: 66 ms autocommit vs 1 ms in one transaction.

nodes.label: DatabaseSync
nodes.rationale: Synchronous by design: a local file, not a socket. A slow query blocks the event loop.

nodes.label: SQLite defensive mode
nodes.rationale: Blocks writing sqlite_schema and loading extensions because a database file is untrusted input.

nodes.label: pg retries nothing; mongodb retries once
nodes.rationale: mongodb retryWrites/retryReads attach a server-side txn id. pg is one query, one outcome. Mongo selection timeout stacks under your loop.
nodes.norm_label: pg retries nothing; mongodb retries once

nodes.label: Primary and replica pools
nodes.rationale: A mis-routed write errors with 25006 cannot execute INSERT in a read-only transaction. Alert on it.

nodes.label: Object-mode QueryStream cost
nodes.rationale: Same memory as a raw cursor, 5.7× slower (6353 vs 1110 ms). Use streams when piping with backpressure; Cursor.read when looping.

nodes.label: Payload is an identifier
nodes.rationale: {orderId: 42}, not the whole order. The job may run minutes later; a copied object is stale.

nodes.label: Versioned updates ignore stale events
nodes.rationale: Jobs are not ordered. update … where status_version < $2 makes late refunds/payments no-ops.

nodes.label: Alert on DLQ arrival rate
nodes.rationale: Depth becomes noise. Alert on new arrivals and oldest unreviewed age. Replay into the original queue.

nodes.label: DST and wall-clock schedules
nodes.rationale: 2 a.m. New York skips a day in March and runs twice in November. Billing wants wall-clock; batches want fixed intervals.

nodes.label: Row-level security tenant isolation
nodes.rationale: USING (tenant_id = current_setting('app.tenant_id')::bigint). A rule the application can forget is not a rule.

nodes.label: Schema as namespace
nodes.rationale: A namespace inside a database. Also used for extensions, staging areas, and GRANT USAGE access-control boundaries.

nodes.label: Schema per tenant
nodes.rationale: Wrong search_path shows an empty table, not another tenant. Stops scaling around the low thousands (1000×50 = 50000 tables).

nodes.label: search_path
nodes.rationale: Default "$user", public. The same SELECT FROM items returned different rows under tenant_a vs tenant_b. Most dangerous session setting in a pooled app.

nodes.label: Shared tables with tenant_id
nodes.rationale: Cheapest layout; one missing WHERE leaks. Pair with row-level security so the guarantee travels with the row.

nodes.label: RESTRICTIVE RLS plus FORCE
nodes.rationale: RESTRICTIVE applies regardless of permissive policies. FORCE stops the table owner bypassing RLS — the role a careless app connects as.

nodes.label: set_config LOCAL app.tenant_id
nodes.rationale: Plain SET persisted across pooled handoff (ex54). SET LOCAL x = $1 is 42601; use set_config(name, value, true) inside a transaction.

nodes.label: Shared schema default
nodes.rationale: Scales to millions of tenants, migrations run once, reporting is one query. Isolation is configuration (RLS, non-owner role, SET LOCAL) not structure.

nodes.label: Schema-qualify DDL in migrations
nodes.rationale: Unqualified CREATE TABLE follows search_path ("$user", public). A role with its own schema silently creates tables elsewhere.

nodes.label: SET LOCAL search_path
nodes.rationale: SET search_path persists on a pooled connection. SET LOCAL reverts on commit. Schema name cannot be $1; validate against pg_namespace then escapeIdentifier.

nodes.label: Choosing a tenancy model
nodes.rationale: Decision page, not mechanism. Migrations and cross-tenant reporting pull opposite isolation. Shared schema is the usual SaaS default.

nodes.label: tenant_id leads every index
nodes.rationale: Every query is tenant-scoped, including the RLS predicate. An index on (created_at) cannot serve the filter on every query.

nodes.label: mock.module exports option
nodes.rationale: namedExports is deprecated on 24.19.0. Use options.exports for named and default exports.

nodes.label: Captured static fixture
nodes.rationale: Right for input you did not author — webhooks, OAuth responses, a real CSV that broke the importer. Comment provenance; never edit captured payloads.

nodes.label: toEqual vs deepStrictEqual
nodes.rationale: expect(a).toEqual(b) ignores undefined properties and does not compare prototypes; deepStrictEqual does both. Migrations surface real object-shape mismatches.

nodes.label: GenericContainer wait strategy
nodes.rationale: Mapped port exists before the process is listening. Without Wait.forLogMessage or Wait.forListeningPorts you get intermittent ECONNREFUSED.

nodes.label: --test-force-exit
nodes.rationale: Exits after the last test regardless of open handles. Legitimate for a third-party leak you cannot close. On your own code it hides a production shutdown bug.

nodes.label: Node 24.19.0 phase 9 target
nodes.rationale: Active LTS as of August 2026. Third-party pins: vitest 4.1.10, jest 30.4.2, testcontainers 12.1.0, fast-check 4.9.0, stryker 9.6.1, biome 2.5.8, zod 4.4.3.

nodes.label: Do not start Express before Phase 5
nodes.rationale: Express is a thin layer over node:http. Learning it first means learning the abstraction without the thing it abstracts.
nodes.norm_label: do not start express before phase 5

nodes.label: Phase 12 — Native and advanced
nodes.rationale: Optional. node:vm is not a security sandbox. Wasm, N-API, FFI, WASI, custom loaders.

nodes.label: IS DISTINCT FROM
nodes.rationale: Null-safe comparison: NULL differs from everything except another NULL. NULL = NULL is null; NULL IS NOT DISTINCT FROM NULL is true.

nodes.label: Three-valued logic in WHERE
nodes.rationale: WHERE keeps only true. Unknown is discarded like false, silently. NULL != 5 is unknown so the NULL row is dropped.

nodes.label: Keyset pagination
nodes.rationale: WHERE id > $1 ORDER BY id LIMIT 20 seeks the index. Same depth: 0.93 ms and 4 buffers versus 105.85 ms and 5045. Costs random access.

nodes.label: OFFSET cost grows with depth
nodes.rationale: OFFSET is defined as produce then discard. Measured 1.22 ms at 0 vs 105.85 ms at 499980 on 500000 rows; EXPLAIN showed rows=500000 feeding Limit of 20.

nodes.label: OFFSET pages drift under writes
nodes.rationale: A count, not a position. An insert between requests serves the boundary row twice; a delete hides a row. Keyset uses a value cursor.

nodes.label: GREATEST and LEAST skip nulls
nodes.rationale: GREATEST(NULL, 2) returned 2. Opposite of almost every other operator. Row-wise, not aggregates.

nodes.label: Lexicographic row comparison
nodes.rationale: (a, b) > ($1, $2) is left-to-right like words. Equivalent to an OR chain the planner handles worse. Tuple, ORDER BY and index must match columns and direction.

nodes.label: NULL in a row constructor
nodes.rationale: (1, NULL) < (1, 2) is null so WHERE discards it and pagination silently stops. Only paginate on NOT NULL columns.

nodes.label: Opaque keyset cursor
nodes.rationale: Encode the sort-key pair server-side. Meaning is tied to sort order. Base64 is not encryption; validate decoded types before binding.

nodes.label: PostgreSQL License
nodes.rationale: Permissive BSD-style. No single commercial owner of the core. The engine is free; hosting is the product.

nodes.label: Autovacuum launcher
nodes.rationale: Starts workers that clean dead tuples. Why updates/deletes do not free space instantly (Phase 11). CPU after bulk load is expected.

nodes.label: I/O workers
nodes.rationale: Assist asynchronous I/O paths (v16+). Measured three io worker rows on 18.4 alpine.

nodes.label: Non-transactional sequence gaps
nodes.rationale: A rolled-back insert consumes its id on PostgreSQL and MySQL (1,3). Sequences never block. Never present ids as a count. First measurement was wrong because batched psql -c shared a transaction.

nodes.label: pg bigint as string
nodes.rationale: pg hands bigint and numeric as strings to protect precision. node:sqlite throws above Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER. Quiet failure vs loud throw.

nodes.label: jsonb #> and #>> path operators
nodes.rationale: Path form takes text[]; prefer #>> when the path is fixed and deeper than two levels.

nodes.label: jsonb_agg empty-collection trap
nodes.rationale: Need FILTER to drop the LEFT JOIN null row and coalesce to [] — either half alone ships null.

nodes.label: tsquery prefix :*
nodes.rationale: Full-text matches whole lexemes; rout returns 0 rows, rout:* returns 13336. Type-ahead appends :*.

nodes.label: tsvector tsquery and @@
nodes.rationale: Documents become tsvector; queries become tsquery; @@ matches them. Most apps never need a separate search server.

nodes.label: shared_preload_libraries for pg_stat_statements
nodes.rationale: CREATE EXTENSION alone is not enough; the library must be preloaded and the server restarted.

nodes.label: Joins chain left to right
nodes.rationale: Each ON may reference any table already introduced. Referencing a later table is 42P01.

nodes.label: Inner joins reorder, outer joins do not
nodes.norm_label: inner joins reorder, outer joins do not

nodes.label: join_collapse_limit default 8
nodes.rationale: Past the limit the planner stops exploring and textual order starts to matter. Split wide joins rather than raising it.

nodes.label: Junction table composite primary key
nodes.rationale: Composite PK identifies the pair, forbids duplicates, and indexes the first column. Add a separate index on the second FK.

nodes.label: Has ALL tags relational division
nodes.rationale: IN is has-any. GROUP BY parent HAVING count(DISTINCT tag_id) = cardinality($1) is has-all.

nodes.label: Phase 5 gate: LEFT JOIN WHERE bug, NOT IN trap, join plus sum()
nodes.norm_label: phase 5 gate: left join where bug, not in trap, join plus sum()

nodes.label: Two-query parent then children is not N+1
nodes.rationale: Two round trips regardless of page size. Prefer when parents are paginated or child sets are large.
nodes.norm_label: two-query parent then children is not n+1

nodes.label: generate_series
nodes.rationale: Endpoints inclusive (hourly over one day = 25 rows). Descending needs a negative step. Step 0 raises 22023. Gap-fill needs count(e.id) not count(*).

nodes.label: CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW WITH NO DATA
nodes.rationale: Querying before populate raises 55000. Check pg_class.relispopulated in a health check.
nodes.norm_label: create materialized view with no data

nodes.label: NOTIFY identifier vs pg_notify string
nodes.rationale: NOTIFY folds unquoted names; pg_notify uses the string exactly and can compute a channel. Prefer pg_notify from application or trigger code.

nodes.label: Phase 12 gate columns vs jsonb and FTS
nodes.norm_label: phase 12 gate columns vs jsonb and fts

nodes.label: REASSIGN OWNED then DROP OWNED
nodes.rationale: DROP ROLE fails with 2BP01 while the role owns objects or holds grants. REASSIGN then DROP OWNED, in that order, in every database; reverse order drops the objects. DROP ROLE is cluster-wide.

nodes.label: public schema CREATE removed in PG15
nodes.rationale: PUBLIC now has USAGE only on public. Apps that created tables in public as a non-owner fail after upgrade with 42501. pg_database_owner resolves to whoever owns the current database.
nodes.norm_label: public schema create removed in pg15

nodes.label: pg_dump version compatibility
