nodes.rationale: pg_dump may be newer than the server, never older. Restoring into an older major is unsupported. Downgrading is a logical-replication job.

nodes.label: Non-existent role same as wrong password
nodes.rationale: Prevents role enumeration. Check pg_roles yourself; the error will never say the role is misspelled.
nodes.norm_label: non-existent role same as wrong password

nodes.label: The memory settings
nodes.rationale: Four settings account for most tuning; only one allocates the memory people think it does. Phase 0 shared_buffers benchmark was confounded and is not reused.

nodes.label: default_statistics_target
nodes.rationale: Default 100. Raise per-column (SET STATISTICS 250–500) for skewed data rather than globally. Correlated columns want CREATE STATISTICS.

nodes.label: Adjacency-list hierarchy
nodes.rationale: Cheapest hierarchy to write; reads need N joins or WITH RECURSIVE. Opposite trade to materialised path or closure table.

nodes.label: lag() beats self join for previous row
nodes.rationale: Joining on id - 1 assumes contiguous ids and breaks after deletes.
nodes.norm_label: lag() beats self join for previous row

nodes.label: Self join via aliases
nodes.rationale: FROM j_emp JOIN j_emp is 42712. Aliases give two roles. LEFT JOIN keeps the NULL-parent root.

nodes.label: WITH RECURSIVE hierarchy walk
nodes.rationale: Anchor plus recursive term until empty. UNION ALL. A cycle loops forever; CYCLE (PG14+) or a path array stops it.

nodes.label: Union column names come from the first branch
nodes.norm_label: union column names come from the first branch

nodes.label: UNION deduplicates and blocks
nodes.rationale: HashAggregate 491 ms vs Append 142 ms over 600k rows — 3.5×. UNION cannot stop early under LIMIT.

nodes.label: Alias replaces the table name
nodes.rationale: Referring to the original name after aliasing is 42P01. That replacement is what makes self joins possible.

nodes.label: Default to UNION ALL
nodes.rationale: Use UNION only when duplicates are possible and wrong. Disjoint sources cannot produce them.

nodes.label: jit default on
nodes.rationale: Helps long analytics; can add overhead to short queries mis-costed above the JIT threshold. Test SET jit = off after upgrades.

nodes.label: max_wal_size checkpoint loop
nodes.rationale: 1 GB default on write-heavy systems forces frequent checkpoints and full-page write bursts. Raise to several GB; cost is longer crash recovery.

nodes.label: Planner costs, WAL, and changing a setting
nodes.rationale: Settings that decide whether the planner picks an index are one-line, no-restart changes. pg_settings.context values sandbox-measured on PG 18.4.
nodes.norm_label: planner costs, wal, and changing a setting

nodes.label: Changing a setting
nodes.rationale: A reload that silently does nothing wastes an afternoon. Check context and pending_restart first.

nodes.label: What to log and what it costs
nodes.rationale: Defaults disable duration, statement, lock-wait and temp-file logging. Each is a one-line reload.
nodes.norm_label: what to log and what it costs

nodes.label: The lock queue
nodes.rationale: A 5 ms ALTER can cause a 30-second outage because ACCESS EXCLUSIVE queues and later ACCESS SHARE cannot jump it.

nodes.label: Zero-downtime schema changes
nodes.rationale: The migration that takes the site down is fast; it spends its time waiting. Deployment view; statement timings live in Phase 3.

nodes.label: sslmode=verify-full on managed TLS
nodes.rationale: Traffic crosses a network you do not control. require encrypts but verifies nothing. Pass the provider CA; never rejectUnauthorized: false.

nodes.label: Minor vs major upgrade
nodes.rationale: 18.3→18.4 is binaries plus restart. 17→18 changes on-disk format. Minor upgrades carry security fixes and should be applied promptly.

nodes.label: Built-in geometric types
nodes.rationale: point, box, polygon, circle and friends with <->, @>, &&, GiST-indexable. Cartesian only — distances on lat/long degrees are not metres. Use PostGIS geography for Earth. point arrives in Node as {x, y}.

nodes.label: Aggregate return types
nodes.rationale: count and sum(int) return bigint; sum(bigint) and avg return numeric; min/max keep the input type. avg is numeric so money does not drift.

nodes.label: avg(x) is sum(x)/count(x)
nodes.rationale: Not sum(x)/count(*). Measured 50.00 vs avg(coalesce(total,0))=25.00 on the open group. Which is correct is a product question.

nodes.label: bigint and numeric arrive as strings
nodes.rationale: pg will not guess a JS number that cannot represent the range. rows[0].n + 1 is '61'. Cast ::int for bounded counts or setTypeParser OID 20.
nodes.norm_label: bigint and numeric arrive as strings

nodes.label: sum()::int overflow 22003
nodes.rationale: The ::int that makes JS convenient reintroduces the overflow bigint exists to prevent. (sum(amount)*20)::int raised 22003; left as bigint returned 3936859560.

nodes.label: NULL-skipping aggregate rule
nodes.rationale: count(*) counts rows; count(expr) counts non-NULL expr. sum/avg/min/max skip NULLs. Open group: two rows, avg 50.00 over one priced value.

nodes.label: sum over nothing is NULL
nodes.rationale: count over nothing is 0. NULL propagates: sum(total)+shipping is NULL. coalesce(sum(x),0) in SQL before any arithmetic.

nodes.label: Three count forms
nodes.rationale: count(*) counts rows. count(expr) counts non-NULL. DISTINCT then de-duplicates survivors and does not bring NULLs back. count(DISTINCT coupon)=2, not 3.

nodes.label: count(CASE … ELSE 0) counts every row
nodes.rationale: count counts non-NULL and 0 is not NULL. Working CASE omits ELSE so non-matches are NULL. FILTER has no ELSE to get wrong.

nodes.label: FILTER vs CASE on empty match
nodes.rationale: Rows exist but none match: sum FILTER is NULL, sum(CASE ELSE 0) is 0. No rows at all: both sums are NULL. count FILTER is 0 in every case.
nodes.norm_label: filter vs case on empty match

nodes.label: Three different questions
nodes.rationale: How many orders, how many have a total, how many different coupons — spelled almost identically.

nodes.label: The LEFT JOIN trap and fan-out
nodes.rationale: LEFT JOIN invents a row for every unmatched left row. count(*) counts it. Eve is reported as having one order.
nodes.norm_label: the left join trap and fan-out

nodes.label: What counting costs
nodes.rationale: Over the same 500000 rows, counting cost 27 ms to 209 ms. The expensive form is count(DISTINCT) because it cannot be parallelised.

nodes.label: inet versus cidr
nodes.rationale: inet holds a host optionally with a mask (10 bytes vs 16 as text). cidr is a network only and rejects host bits (22P02 for 192.168.1.10/24). << containment is GiST-indexable. inet normalises IPv6 so equivalent forms compare equal.

nodes.label: char(n) blank-pads
nodes.rationale: char(3) holding 'US' compares and returns as 'US '. Use only for genuinely fixed-width codes; prefer text.

nodes.label: timestamptz not timestamp
nodes.rationale: timestamp stores no zone so the same value means different instants. timestamptz stores an instant. Converting later rewrites the table.

nodes.label: Database per tenant
nodes.rationale: Strongest isolation. A connection pool per tenant; cross-tenant queries impossible.

nodes.label: 63-byte identifier limit
nodes.rationale: Truncated silently with a NOTICE. Two long index names that differ after byte 63 collide and the second CREATE INDEX fails as a duplicate.

nodes.label: application_name includes the tenant
nodes.rationale: pg_stat_statements normalises tenant id into a parameter and aggregates across tenants. application_name gives pg_stat_activity and the slow-query log per-tenant attribution.

nodes.label: SELECT * is for psql not code
nodes.rationale: New columns silently widen payloads, defeat index-only scans, leak column order, and collapse duplicate join names to the last one.
nodes.norm_label: select * is for psql not code

nodes.label: LIMIT n+1 next-page flag
nodes.rationale: count(*) on 500000 rows was 25.69 ms; reltuples 0.49 ms. Asking for one extra row answers has-next at no extra scan. Clamp user LIMIT.

nodes.label: Always name INSERT target columns
nodes.rationale: Positional VALUES binds to current column order so a schema change silently rewires inserts. Omit vs DEFAULT apply the default; explicit NULL overrides it.

nodes.label: RETURNING old and new (PostgreSQL 18)
nodes.rationale: New in 18: RETURNING old.qty AS was, new.qty AS now. Pre-18 needs a self-join. INSERT old is null; DELETE new is null.

nodes.label: NULL as a grouping key
nodes.rationale: Three NULL coupons form one group. Grouping, DISTINCT, UNION and PARTITION BY use IS NOT DISTINCT FROM. Predicates use three-valued =.

nodes.label: No GROUP BY always returns one row
nodes.rationale: Implicit group over everything. With GROUP BY, empty selection emits zero rows. Check rows[0].n without GROUP BY; check rows.length with it.
nodes.norm_label: no group by always returns one row

nodes.label: DISTINCT ON one whole row per group
nodes.rationale: Every column comes from the same row. min(id), max(total) can invent a pair that never existed. ORDER BY must start with the DISTINCT ON keys; add NULLS LAST.
nodes.norm_label: distinct on one whole row per group

nodes.label: 42803 grouping error
nodes.rationale: MySQL loose mode picks an arbitrary row. ONLY_FULL_GROUP_BY restores strictness; PostgreSQL never had the loose mode.

nodes.label: Four ways out of 42803
nodes.rationale: Add to GROUP BY (changes grouping), take min/max/array_agg[1], collect all values, or take one whole row via DISTINCT ON / row_number. Do not add to GROUP BY reflexively.

nodes.label: Functional dependency on primary key
nodes.rationale: GROUP BY o.id licenses o.status. Per table only; grouping by the other side's key is 42803. Lost inside UNION/DISTINCT/SRF views.

nodes.label: UNIQUE does not grant functional dependency
nodes.rationale: A unique column can be NULL and NULLs group together, so uniqueness alone does not guarantee one row per group. Requires a declared PRIMARY KEY.
nodes.norm_label: unique does not grant functional dependency

nodes.label: 42703 vs 42803
nodes.rationale: 42703 is no such column (alias too early or typo). 42803 is grouping error (column exists but is not one-per-group). Aggregate in GROUP BY is 42803 because it is circular.

nodes.label: HAVING cannot see output aliases
nodes.rationale: Both WHERE and HAVING run before SELECT materialises. Error is 42703. Repeat the expression, or wrap and filter outside — the only way to filter a window result.

nodes.label: HAVING without GROUP BY
nodes.rationale: Filters the single implicit group. HAVING count(*)>99 on six rows returns zero rows, not a row containing 6. The only way an ungrouped aggregate returns nothing.

nodes.label: jsonb_object_agg
nodes.rationale: Rows into a keyed map. NULL key raises 22023 at runtime. Duplicate keys silently keep the last value — aggregate over already-grouped input.

nodes.label: 22023 field name must not be null
nodes.rationale: jsonb_object_agg rejects a NULL key only when such a row exists, so a query that works for months breaks on the first NULL grouping value.
nodes.norm_label: 22023 field name must not be null

nodes.label: RETURNING feeding a CTE
nodes.rationale: DELETE RETURNING into INSERT archive is one atomic statement. Sub-statements share a snapshot and can only see another CTE via its RETURNING output. No ORDER BY on RETURNING itself.

nodes.label: UPDATE FROM join update
nodes.rationale: FROM supplies rows, WHERE joins, SET reads source columns. Unmatched targets stay untouched. Duplicate sources pick one row arbitrarily with no error.

nodes.label: Empty params array stays simple protocol
nodes.rationale: [] still uses the simple query protocol and runs multiple statements. Safety comes from bound values, not from the argument being present.
nodes.norm_label: empty params array stays simple protocol

nodes.label: WHERE versus HAVING
nodes.rationale: WHERE filters rows before grouping; HAVING filters groups after. Aggregates in WHERE raise 42803. Non-aggregates in WHERE reduce work.

nodes.label: NULLS LAST and NULLS FIRST
nodes.rationale: Default NULLS LAST for ASC and NULLS FIRST for DESC. Reversing a UI sort moves empty rows from bottom to top. Indexes record null ordering too.

nodes.label: ctid batched DELETE
nodes.rationale: DELETE takes no LIMIT (42601). Batch via ctid IN (SELECT ctid ... LIMIT n). 100000 rows: one shot 115 ms, 10 batches 484 ms, but locks release, VACUUM is not held back, job is interruptible.

nodes.label: DISTINCT ON versus row_number versus LATERAL
nodes.rationale: DISTINCT ON for top-1 over a whole table. row_number for top-N or the rank. LATERAL when the outer set is small and indexed, and to keep groups with no match.
nodes.norm_label: distinct on versus row_number versus lateral

nodes.label: TRUNCATE fires no row triggers
nodes.rationale: AFTER DELETE FOR EACH ROW logged 2 for DELETE and nothing more for TRUNCATE. Audit and counters silently skip. Use AFTER TRUNCATE FOR EACH STATEMENT.

nodes.label: TRUNCATE CASCADE versus DROP CASCADE
nodes.rationale: TRUNCATE CASCADE empties referencing tables transitively. DROP CASCADE removes dependent objects and leaves child data. Prefer naming every table.

nodes.label: TRUNCATE is transactional in PostgreSQL
nodes.rationale: 100 rows, TRUNCATE inside a transaction, ROLLBACK, all 100 back. Unlike MySQL and Oracle where TRUNCATE commits implicitly.

nodes.label: SQL evaluation order
nodes.rationale: FROM → WHERE → GROUP BY → HAVING → SELECT (aliases born) → windows → DISTINCT → ORDER BY → LIMIT. WHERE cannot see aliases (42703); ORDER BY can.

nodes.label: GROUP BY ordinals
nodes.rationale: GROUP BY 1,2 breaks silently when a column is inserted in the select list. Reserve ordinals for long expressions; name columns in anything that ships.

nodes.label: GROUP BY output alias is a PG extension
nodes.rationale: GROUP BY runs before SELECT, yet PostgreSQL permits output names including computed expressions. Standard SQL does not; it will not port.
nodes.norm_label: group by output alias is a pg extension

nodes.label: WHERE vs HAVING
nodes.rationale: WHERE status='paid' is a row predicate. HAVING count(*)>1 is a group predicate. HAVING may use an aggregate not in the select list. HAVING a non-key column is 42803.

nodes.label: HAVING on grouping columns is rewritten
nodes.rationale: GROUP BY user_id, kind HAVING kind='purchase' becomes Group Key: user_id and Filter on the seq scan. Plans identical to WHERE. Rewrite requires a non-volatile grouping-column predicate.
nodes.norm_label: having on grouping columns is rewritten

nodes.label: 42P20 window functions not allowed in HAVING
nodes.rationale: Windows run after HAVING. Filter a window in an outer WHERE. rank() OVER (ORDER BY count(*) DESC) is legal because windows run after aggregation.
nodes.norm_label: 42p20 window functions not allowed in having

nodes.label: Filtering groups, not rows
nodes.rationale: HAVING can see aggregates; WHERE cannot, because when WHERE runs no aggregate has been computed yet.

nodes.label: What HAVING costs
nodes.rationale: HAVING on a grouping column is rewritten into WHERE and costs nothing. HAVING on an aggregate cannot be, and every discarded group was still built.

nodes.label: HAVING vs WHERE
nodes.rationale: WHERE filters rows into groups; HAVING filters groups out. Test: can the predicate be decided by looking at one row?

nodes.label: Conditional aggregation
nodes.rationale: FILTER attaches a predicate to a single aggregate. Other aggregates in the same select list still see all rows. Standard SQL since PG 9.4.

nodes.label: When FILTER pays
nodes.rationale: FILTER is not faster than CASE. It is faster than one subquery per number: 4× the buffers and 2.5× the time.

nodes.label: FILTER (WHERE ...)
nodes.rationale: Restricts one aggregate without restricting the query. Not pure CASE sugar: the two disagree about the empty set.

nodes.label: CASE expression
nodes.rationale: First match wins; implicit ELSE NULL. Short form uses = so WHEN NULL never matches. Put IS NULL first in the long form.

nodes.label: length versus octet_length
nodes.rationale: 'héllo' is length 5 and octet_length 6. varchar(n) counts characters. Btree index entries have a byte limit.

nodes.label: SQL strings are 1-indexed
nodes.rationale: substring('abcdef' FROM 2 FOR 3) is bcd; FOR is a length not an end. split_part field 2 is the second field. Unlike JavaScript.

nodes.label: age() versus timestamp subtraction
nodes.rationale: age returns a symbolic interval where 1 mon is 28 to 31 days. Subtraction is elapsed days and hours. pg returns PostgresInterval objects.

nodes.label: interval 1 day versus 24 hours
nodes.rationale: 1 day keeps wall-clock time across DST (23 or 25 hours). 24 hours is elapsed. Same time tomorrow versus expires in 24 hours.

nodes.label: now() is transaction start
nodes.rationale: Alias for transaction_timestamp(). Two inserts 150 ms apart shared a timestamp. statement_timestamp is per statement; clock_timestamp advances mid-statement.

nodes.label: MVCC prevents a stored row count
nodes.rationale: The correct count depends on the asking transaction's snapshot. A stored counter would also serialise every insert and delete.
nodes.norm_label: mvcc prevents a stored row count

nodes.label: Outbound objects need JSON.stringify
nodes.rationale: Parameters do not auto-serialise objects. Insert JSON.stringify(obj) with $1::jsonb or the column stores [object Object].

nodes.label: idleTimeoutMillis
nodes.rationale: Close unused pooled connections. Set below intermediary idle TCP drops to avoid connection terminated unexpectedly.

nodes.label: Hanging request
nodes.rationale: If middleware does not end the cycle it must call next(); otherwise the request is left hanging. Audit if-arms and async paths.

nodes.label: return next() style
nodes.rationale: return next() only returns from your function; next is what continues the chain. return avoids running code after next by accident.

nodes.label: Route handlers are middleware
nodes.rationale: Same contract with a method and path filter in front.

nodes.label: Middleware signature (req, res, next)
nodes.rationale: (req, res, next) => void for normal middleware; four args for errors. An Express app is a series of middleware function calls.

nodes.label: App, router, and route middleware levels
nodes.rationale: App stack in registration order, then the mounted router stack, then route-specific middleware and handler.
nodes.norm_label: app, router, and route middleware levels

nodes.label: Router mount path stripped
nodes.rationale: A router's own mount path is stripped and not visible to the middleware.

nodes.label: First registered runs first
nodes.rationale: Express does not sort middleware by specificity. Registration order on app is absolute.

nodes.label: next()
nodes.rationale: Continues to the next non-error middleware. next after a response means header errors.

nodes.label: next('route')
nodes.rationale: Advanced skip-to-next-route feature — rare. Default is next().

nodes.label: Factory passed as middleware
nodes.rationale: app.use(requireHeader) passes the factory, not the instance — wrong arity and behaviour. Call it: app.use(requireHeader('x-api-key')).

nodes.label: res.on('finish') timing
nodes.rationale: Only store scalars you need; do not retain req in global arrays or you leak memory.

nodes.label: res.locals
nodes.rationale: Documented request-scoped place for values.

nodes.label: Phase 2 gate
nodes.rationale: Place body parser, auth, routes, and error middleware in the only order that works, and diagnose a hang as forgot next vs forgot to send.

nodes.label: Phase 2 — Middleware architecture
nodes.rationale: Target Express 5.2.1 on Node 24.19.0. The whole framework is a stack of functions. Order, next, and termination are the job.

nodes.label: Three legal middleware endings
nodes.rationale: Respond, next(), or next(err). Returning without one of those is not an ending Express understands — the socket waits.

nodes.label: bigint arrives as a String
nodes.rationale: pg will not silently lose precision past Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER. Treat ids as opaque strings; Number() is only safe under 2^53.

nodes.label: Expanded OR comparison is 160× slower
nodes.rationale: a < $1 OR (a = $1 AND b < $2) looks equivalent and returned the same rows, but became a Filter that discarded 250001 rows (158.12 ms vs 0.99 ms).

nodes.label: Index Cond versus Filter
nodes.rationale: Index Cond chooses where the scan starts and stops. Filter is applied after rows are produced. A Filter on a large table is usually why a query is slow despite using the index.

nodes.label: OFFSET versus keyset at depth
nodes.rationale: OFFSET 499980 produced 500000 rows and 501918 buffers to return 20 (295.87 ms). Keyset sought with Index Cond, 23 buffers, 1.23 ms.

nodes.label: Row-constructor tuple comparison
nodes.rationale: (created_at, id) < ($1, $2) is one lexicographic comparison, the same rule ORDER BY uses, and becomes a single B-tree seek.

nodes.label: base64url cursor encoding
nodes.rationale: JSON of [ISO timestamp, String(id)] as base64url. Preserve full precision; bigint id as string. Base64 is not security — sign if unforgeable.

nodes.label: Fetch limit + 1 for hasMore
nodes.rationale: The extra row is whether another page exists. Costs one row instead of count(*). nextCursor is null at the end.

nodes.label: Tuple form cannot express mixed directions
nodes.rationale: (a,b) < (x,y) means DESC on both. Against ORDER BY a DESC, b ASC it returns a plausible wrong page. Write the comparison out and index (a DESC, b ASC), or avoid mixed directions.
nodes.norm_label: tuple form cannot express mixed directions

nodes.label: Nullable sort column silently truncates the walk
nodes.rationale: Comparisons against NULL are never true. Page 1 includes nulls (no WHERE); later pages drop them. Measured 250000 of 500000 excluded. NULLS LAST does not fix the predicate. Prefer NOT NULL.
nodes.norm_label: nullable sort column silently truncates the walk

nodes.label: Keyset (cursor) pagination
nodes.rationale: Remember the last row and ask for what comes after it. The query starts at the right place in the index rather than walking to it.

nodes.label: Order by an immutable key
nodes.rationale: Keyset is stable against inserts elsewhere. A row whose sort key changes (updated_at) can be seen twice or missed. Prefer created_at or the primary key.

nodes.label: OFFSET is still right for shallow page-number UIs
nodes.rationale: At 50 pages OFFSET was 0.9× (slightly faster). At 500 pages keyset was 6.4× faster. Keyset for feeds, APIs, exports, crawlers; OFFSET for admin tables with page numbers.
nodes.norm_label: offset is still right for shallow page-number uis

nodes.label: Phase 9 gate
nodes.rationale: Move on when list/filter/sort is allowlisted and transactions use try/catch/finally release.

nodes.label: PostgreSQL tier distribution
nodes.rationale: Master 62 (27%), Understand 127 (54%), Know 35 (15%), When Needed 9 (4%). Master by part: 20 / 14 / 14 / 14.

nodes.label: react-test-renderer
nodes.rationale: Still published in lockstep but deprecated in React 19 docs; React Testing Library is the replacement.

nodes.label: Props are one argument
nodes.rationale: JSX builds a fresh object each render so identity comparison on props is always false. React 19 put ref in that same object.

nodes.label: children is the free slot
nodes.rationale: A hole the parent fills with arbitrary JSX. Use when there is one content area and no opinion about it.

nodes.label: HOC displayName convention
nodes.rationale: Set displayName from the wrapped component or DevTools shows anonymous wrappers.

nodes.label: HOC does not copy static methods
nodes.rationale: The wrapper is a different function object. Copy statics or use hoist-non-react-statics. Mostly historical now.
nodes.norm_label: hoc does not copy static methods

nodes.label: forceUpdate
nodes.rationale: Forces a re-render without a state change. Almost always means state is kept somewhere React cannot see.

nodes.label: Never deep-compare in shouldComponentUpdate
nodes.rationale: JSON.stringify makes cost proportional to data size and breaks on undefined, functions, Map, Set, cycles and key order.

nodes.label: idle in transaction
nodes.rationale: A 1240 ms external await held the xact open 1223 ms. Occupies a pool slot, holds locks, and pins xmin so VACUUM cannot clean tables the endpoint never touches.

nodes.label: idle_in_transaction_session_timeout
nodes.rationale: Kills sessions that sit idle in a transaction, turning an unbounded stall into a specific error. ALTER ROLE api_user SET … = '15s'.

nodes.label: Index must match ORDER BY column order
nodes.rationale: (created_at DESC, id DESC) matches the sort. A B-tree can be read backwards, so both-ASC also serves. (id, created_at) is useless for ORDER BY created_at, id.
nodes.norm_label: index must match order by column order

nodes.label: Part 1 Foundations (proposed)
nodes.rationale: Phases 0–3, 63 topics, 19 Master. Architecture, psql mastered, types, DDL. Not Node-specific; every page still shows the pg counterpart.

nodes.label: Part 2 SQL (proposed)
nodes.rationale: Phases 4–6, 49 topics, 14 Master. CRUD/DML, joins, aggregation, windows, CTEs. Tuple comparison is the keyset primitive.

nodes.label: Part 3 Node + raw pg (proposed)
nodes.rationale: Phases 7–9, 48 topics, 14 Master. Raw-SQL-first. Overlap with Node Phase 6 is recap-plus-link, never a second full treatment.

nodes.label: Part 4 Performance and production (proposed)
nodes.rationale: Phases 10–13, 68 topics, 13 Master. Indexes/planner, MVCC, advanced features, security and ops. Most defensible part to defer.

nodes.label: Part 1 Foundations (live syllabus)
nodes.rationale: Phases 0–3, 65 topics, 20 Master. Adds Modelling money (Master) and Multi-tenancy as a decision. Phase 0–3 explanation pages already written.

nodes.label: Modelling money
nodes.rationale: numeric vs integer cents vs float, rounding, and the ledger shape. Live-syllabus addition versus the proposed 63-topic Foundations part.

nodes.label: Multi-tenancy as a decision
nodes.rationale: Shared schema with tenant_id vs schema-per-tenant vs database-per-tenant, and what each costs to operate.

nodes.label: Do external work outside the transaction
nodes.rationale: Charge first, then withTransaction. The new failure is money taken with no order — fix with idempotent charges and reconcile, not by putting the call back inside.
nodes.norm_label: do external work outside the transaction

nodes.label: Node Phase 6 versus PG Part 3 boundary
nodes.rationale: Pool sizing, transaction propagation, N+1, repository rationale, ORM stay in Node 6. Writing SQL through the driver, DDL/seeding, CRUD patterns are PG Part 3. Needs explicit sign-off.
nodes.norm_label: node phase 6 versus pg part 3 boundary

nodes.label: isValidElement
nodes.rationale: True only for React elements. Strings, numbers and arrays render but return false.

nodes.label: Undo an animation by resetting, not reversing
nodes.rationale: opacity 1 then 0 then 1 matches setting 1 once. For tweening libraries reset the timeline to its initial state.
nodes.norm_label: undo an animation by resetting, not reversing

nodes.label: Callback refs get the same extra cycle
nodes.rationale: React 19 ref cleanup functions make the symmetry expressible. A missing cleanup doubles registry counts.
nodes.norm_label: callback refs get the same extra cycle

nodes.label: DevTools dims second-render logs
nodes.rationale: A missing second log is not evidence of a single render. Effect setup logs are not dimmed.

nodes.label: Transform during render; handle events in handlers
nodes.rationale: An Effect has lost the information about what caused it. That is the defining property that makes effects wrong for event logic.
nodes.norm_label: transform during render; handle events in handlers

nodes.label: useEffectEvent is stable in React 19.2
nodes.rationale: Re-checked 2026-08-14: the reference has no experimental banner. The React 19.2 release post (1 Oct 2025) lists it as shipped.

nodes.label: Restructuring the effect
nodes.rationale: Four moves that change what the effect is, rather than what it reads, so the unwanted dependency becomes genuinely irrelevant.

nodes.label: The illegitimate fixes
nodes.rationale: Two ways to silence the linter without changing what the effect depends on. Both freeze one render's values forever.

nodes.label: Effects run children before parents
nodes.rationale: A parent measuring a child needs the child's refs attached. That is why ref.current is null during render and populated in effects.

nodes.label: INSERT ... RETURNING
nodes.rationale: Returns the stored row including generated id and DEFAULT now() without a second query. currval is per-session and unsafe through pool.query.

nodes.label: Named RETURNING columns
nodes.rationale: RETURNING * publishes every later column, including password_hash. Name the mapper's columns.

nodes.label: unnest multi-row insert
nodes.rationale: One array parameter per column stays under the 65535-parameter wire limit. RETURNING order is not guaranteed.

nodes.label: Hard delete with RETURNING
nodes.rationale: ON DELETE CASCADE fires. Missing row is rowCount 0, not an error — map to 404.

nodes.label: jsonb_agg LEFT JOIN empty-children trap
nodes.rationale: Plain jsonb_agg yields [{sku:null}]. Need FILTER WHERE child.id IS NOT NULL plus coalesce to [].

nodes.label: jsonb_agg is slower than grouping in JS
nodes.rationale: 5000 orders: jsonb_agg 284.8 ms vs JS group 90.7 ms. json_agg 131.2 ms. Server CPU parsing jsonb, and a larger payload.
nodes.norm_label: jsonb_agg is slower than grouping in js

nodes.label: N+1 per-parent queries
nodes.rationale: 2986 ms extrapolated for 5000 parents. Still the one to avoid.

nodes.label: Explicit row-to-domain mapper
nodes.rationale: One place, an allowlist by construction. Reverse sort params via a lookup map, not camelToSnake.

nodes.label: Generic snake-to-camel rewriter
nodes.rationale: Publishes every column. Fails to round-trip oauth2_token. 2.3× slower than an explicit mapper over 20000 rows.

nodes.label: Unquoted identifiers fold to lower case
nodes.rationale: fullName becomes fullname. Quoted camelCase requires quoting forever or 42703.
nodes.norm_label: unquoted identifiers fold to lower case

nodes.label: Quoted SQL alias trap
nodes.rationale: AS "customerName" then ORDER BY customerName raises 42703 column customername. Fine for a fixed SELECT, awkward when dynamic.

nodes.label: Who owns the response shape
nodes.rationale: SQL that emits the API payload couples schema to contract. Default to one join grouped in JS behind the mapper.

nodes.label: Render phase
nodes.rationale: React calls component functions; the result may be repeated or discarded. The DOM still shows the previous UI.

nodes.label: Declarative UI model
nodes.rationale: You describe what the UI is for a given value and never write transitions; cost is a diff on every update and losing direct DOM control.

nodes.label: Re-render + diff vs signals
nodes.rationale: React's unit of update is the component; signals update the exact binding. Stale closures and dependency arrays follow from React's choice.

nodes.label: Phase 0 load-bearing pages
nodes.rationale: Pages 01, 03, 04 and 07 are the four to read if you only read four.

nodes.label: React computes a description of the UI
nodes.rationale: A renderer applies the description. This split is why react and react-dom are separate, why Server Components can exist, why keys matter, and why mutation never works.
nodes.norm_label: react computes a description of the ui

nodes.label: Inputs are props state and context
nodes.rationale: Output depending on time, window, localStorage or a module variable is impure no matter how stable that source looks.
nodes.norm_label: inputs are props state and context

nodes.label: Module-level write during render
nodes.rationale: react.dev Cup example yields guests 2, 4, 6 under StrictMode because output depends on call count.

nodes.label: Writing a ref during render is unsupported
nodes.rationale: A ref exists before the render. Mutate refs in effects and handlers.
nodes.norm_label: writing a ref during render is unsupported

nodes.label: useSyncExternalStore for external sources
nodes.rationale: The hook for mutable sources React can track, including under concurrent rendering. Window size belongs here.

nodes.label: Class instance fields become useRef
nodes.rationale: Timer ids, sockets and caches persist without triggering a render. useState would re-render on every assignment.

nodes.label: setState merges useState replaces
nodes.rationale: Porting a state object wholesale to useState silently drops unrespread fields. The classic conversion bug.

nodes.label: PureComponent and mutation are mutually exclusive
nodes.rationale: Mutating then setState of the same reference drops the update silently. Wrong UI, not slow UI.
nodes.norm_label: purecomponent and mutation are mutually exclusive

nodes.label: The two rules of a pure component
nodes.norm_label: the two rules of a pure component

nodes.label: Component purity
nodes.rationale: Mind your own business and same inputs same output. React assumes this of every component and does not verify it at runtime.

nodes.label: Side effects belong in event handlers
nodes.rationale: Handlers run after render so they sit outside the rule. useEffect is the fallback after handlers are exhausted. Derivations are neither — compute during render.
nodes.norm_label: side effects belong in event handlers

nodes.label: Local mutation
nodes.rationale: Objects created during this render are yours to mutate. The test is whether the object existed before the render started.

nodes.label: Clear stale data before the next fetch
nodes.rationale: setBio(null) at the top of setup. Without it Alice's bio stays on screen labelled as Bob. Ignore prevents applying the wrong response; clearing prevents displaying it.
nodes.norm_label: clear stale data before the next fetch

nodes.label: AbortController
nodes.rationale: Stops the request. Catch must ignore DOMException named AbortError. Only works with APIs that accept a signal.

nodes.label: ignore flag
nodes.rationale: let ignore = false inside setup; cleanup sets it true. One flag per request. Fixes the render. Does not cancel the transfer.

nodes.label: Responses may arrive out of order
nodes.rationale: The most recent response is not the most recent request. Both succeed; the last arrival wins. Intermittent on slow or uneven networks.
nodes.norm_label: responses may arrive out of order

nodes.label: Move 8 — split into several Effects
nodes.rationale: Merged, [country, city] refetches cities when the city changes. Each request keeps its own ignore flag.

nodes.label: Phase 4 gate
nodes.rationale: Rewrite a keystroke-fetching effect so it debounces, cancels superseded requests, never renders an old query, and survives StrictMode — and name which mechanism does each.

nodes.label: Setup function cannot be async
nodes.rationale: React expects a cleanup function; async returns a Promise. Declare an inner async function and return a real cleanup.

nodes.label: One effect per concern
nodes.rationale: Merging concerns unions their dependency lists, so each tears down for the other's reasons. Split by what is synchronized, not when it runs.

nodes.label: useData fixes ergonomics only
nodes.rationale: One race-condition guard instead of twenty. Still no cache, still after mount, still a waterfall and empty server HTML.

nodes.label: AbortError is not a failure
nodes.rationale: An aborted fetch rejects with AbortError. Treating every rejection as failure turns cancel into a visible error.

nodes.label: One synchronization process per Effect
nodes.rationale: A connection and a visit log start together but are unrelated. The test: if you need the word and, split.

nodes.label: Do not use effect order as coordination
nodes.rationale: Order explains failures; it is not timing under concurrent rendering, a render is not a commit, and insertion vs DOM mutation is unspecified.
nodes.norm_label: do not use effect order as coordination

nodes.label: react-hooks/exhaustive-deps
nodes.rationale: Computes the correct array from the code. A disable comment converts a compile-time complaint into a runtime stale-value bug.

nodes.label: Reactive values
nodes.rationale: Props and all variables and functions declared directly inside the component. Module constants, setters, dispatch and ref objects are not.

nodes.label: Omitted dependency freezes the first render
nodes.rationale: Each render creates a new setup closure. An empty array means only the first ever runs. The component re-renders; the connection stays on the old room.
nodes.norm_label: omitted dependency freezes the first render

nodes.label: Cleanup closes over the old render
nodes.rationale: A cleanup that saw new values would disconnect a room it never connected to. A missing dependency leaves handles never released.
nodes.norm_label: cleanup closes over the old render

nodes.label: Mutable-outside-React values cannot be dependencies
nodes.rationale: location.pathname and ref.current can change outside the render data flow. A dependency array records what a render produced.

nodes.label: Move 5 — updater form
nodes.rationale: setMessages(msgs => [...msgs, msg]) stops reading messages, so the chat no longer reconnects on every received message.

nodes.label: Suppressed interval freezes the counter at 1
nodes.rationale: onTick from the first render closed over count 0 and increment 1, so every tick calls setCount(0 + 1). Not lagging — frozen.
nodes.norm_label: suppressed interval freezes the counter at 1

nodes.label: Dependency array must be a constant-size literal
nodes.rationale: Dependencies are compared positionally. A changing size is meaningless; a variable defeats exhaustive-deps.
nodes.norm_label: dependency array must be a constant-size literal

nodes.label: You cannot choose Effect dependencies
nodes.rationale: Every reactive value the setup reads must be declared. To remove a dependency you must prove to the linter it is not read.

nodes.label: All linter errors on dependencies are legitimate
nodes.rationale: There is always a way to fix the code without breaking the rules. The array is the input React uses to decide whether to re-synchronize.
nodes.norm_label: all linter errors on dependencies are legitimate

nodes.label: Do not use useEffectEvent to avoid dependencies
nodes.rationale: Wrapping the whole setup to reach [] hides real staleness. Only genuinely event-like logic belongs in an Effect Event.
nodes.norm_label: do not use useeffectevent to avoid dependencies

nodes.label: Suppressing exhaustive-deps is a lie
nodes.rationale: There's always a better solution than ignoring the linter. If none of the eight moves apply, the effect probably should not exist.

nodes.label: Double render versus extra effect cycle
nodes.rationale: Double render finds impurity in the component body and useState/useMemo/useReducer functions. Extra effect cycle finds missing cleanup. Event handlers are in neither.
nodes.norm_label: double render versus extra effect cycle

nodes.label: Extra setup+cleanup cycle
nodes.rationale: Mount is setup → cleanup → setup where production is setup. If those are indistinguishable to the user, cleanup is complete.

nodes.label: Door-lock analogy
nodes.rationale: React starts and stops the Effect one extra time in development to check the lock — that start and stop are a matched pair.

nodes.label: Move 7 — move the code to an event handler
nodes.rationale: A submitted flag plus theme in the array re-registers the user when the theme changes. The trigger state and the effect disappear together.
nodes.norm_label: move 7 — move the code to an event handler

nodes.label: Analytics POST needs no cleanup
nodes.rationale: The double call is development-only and development traffic should not be in the metrics. A POST that changes application state has neither property.

nodes.label: Buying a product is not an Effect
nodes.rationale: You want to buy when the user clicks, not when they visit. Back-navigation remounts and would buy again. Same HTTP verb as analytics, opposite answer.
nodes.norm_label: buying a product is not an effect

nodes.label: Remount principle
nodes.rationale: Visiting a page should match visiting, clicking a link, then Back. StrictMode remounts once in development because that journey remounts in production.

nodes.label: Doubled development analytics is not a bug
nodes.rationale: You do not want development traffic in production metrics. The real bug nearby is a doubled mutation that belonged in a handler.
nodes.norm_label: doubled development analytics is not a bug

nodes.label: StrictMode only doubles the mount
nodes.rationale: The extra cycle is before the first real setup, not every setup. A leak on the dependency-change path passes StrictMode.

nodes.label: Partial StrictMode skips the extra effect cycle
nodes.rationale: When StrictMode is not at the root, React will not double child effects without parent effects, because that cannot happen in production.
nodes.norm_label: partial strictmode skips the extra effect cycle

nodes.label: POST placement depends on causation
nodes.rationale: Analytics stays in an Effect because the form was displayed. Registration belongs in the submit handler. Same verb, opposite answers.

nodes.label: State as a message queue
nodes.rationale: Handler sets jsonToSubmit so an effect will POST. Extra render, null skip, StrictMode double-submit. Delete both and call the function.

nodes.label: Node and Express verification backlog
nodes.rationale: Node: 229 Verified lines but only 10 cite sandbox (238 no proof). Express: 91 pages, 0 sandbox cites. PostgreSQL is the healthy corpus.

nodes.label: tsc --noEmit CI gate
nodes.rationale: If tsc --noEmit does not run somewhere automatic, you are writing JavaScript with extra syntax.

nodes.label: Numeric enum IIFE
nodes.rationale: enum emits an IIFE building a two-way map. It cannot be tree-shaken and Node strip-only rejects it.

nodes.label: Erasable vs non-erasable syntax
nodes.rationale: Erasable syntax describes values that already exist. Non-erasable syntax creates runtime objects: enum, runtime namespace, parameter properties, legacy decorators.

nodes.label: tsc, transpilers, and Node 24
nodes.rationale: Only tsc checks types. esbuild/swc/Vite/Babel and Node 24 strip and run. Pair a fast runner with tsc --noEmit.

nodes.label: erasableSyntaxOnly
nodes.rationale: tsc rejects non-erasable syntax with TS1294. Enable whenever anything runs .ts directly. Defaults to false.

nodes.label: Node strip-only mode
nodes.rationale: Annotations become whitespace so stack traces stay accurate. Syntax that must generate code is ERR_UNSUPPORTED_TYPESCRIPT_SYNTAX at load.

nodes.label: isolatedModules
nodes.rationale: Rejects constructs a single-file transpiler cannot compile: type re-exports without export type, const enum, ambient-only files.

nodes.label: TypeScript is a checker, not a runtime
nodes.norm_label: typescript is a checker, not a runtime

nodes.label: Whole-program check vs one-file transpile
nodes.rationale: A transpiler never opens imports. A checker must build a type graph over the whole program. They cannot be the same pass.

nodes.label: Types are erased
nodes.rationale: TypeScript is a build-time checker that leaves nothing behind at runtime. Downstream of this: validation still exists, as is dangerous, enum is unlike other type constructs.

nodes.label: Excess property checks
nodes.rationale: A fresh object literal assigned to a typed target is checked for unknown properties (TS2353). Store it in a variable and freshness is gone.

nodes.label: Object types
nodes.rationale: Optional properties, readonly, index signatures, and nesting cover almost every shape. ? and readonly are compile-time only.

nodes.label: Weak type detection
nodes.rationale: A type whose properties are all optional rejects a value with no properties in common (TS2559). Add one required property and the same typo through a variable passes silently.

nodes.label: Declaration merging
nodes.rationale: Two interfaces with the same name combine. Type aliases error TS2300 Duplicate identifier. Merging is how you augment Express.Request and ProcessEnv.

nodes.label: interface
nodes.rationale: Always an object shape. Needed when something must be augmentable. extends checks compatibility and reports TS2430 on conflict.

nodes.label: Branded types
nodes.rationale: type UserId = string is the same type as OrderId. Brand with string & { readonly __brand: 'UserId' } so the shapes differ. The brand is erased at runtime.

nodes.label: Structural typing
nodes.rationale: A is assignable to B when A has at least B's members of compatible types. Names never matter. Extra members are fine; missing ones are not. Opposite of Java nominal typing.

nodes.label: Recursive type aliases
nodes.rationale: A type may refer to itself through an object, array, or function member. Direct self-reference in an intersection circularly references itself.

nodes.label: TS2589 instantiation too deep
nodes.rationale: Depth 50 and 500 compiled; 5000 tripped it on 7.0.2. Means type-level arithmetic or a deep mapped type, not that ordinary nested data is too deep.

nodes.label: Phase 1 The type vocabulary
nodes.rationale: 17 pages. Every type you will write for the next year. Gate: model an API payload without any and say why each choice is not a neighbour.

nodes.label: Interface error-message folklore
nodes.rationale: Measured: a plain object alias and an equivalent interface produced identical TS2741 text, each naming its type. Aliases of intersections or mapped types can still expand.

nodes.label: Read assignability errors bottom-up
nodes.rationale: The innermost Type A is not assignable to type B names the real mismatch. Outer lines are the property path the compiler walked.

nodes.label: Build Optimized Websites
nodes.rationale: First tagline. 'optimized' is painted in brand green so performance of the generated site is the claimed differentiator.

nodes.label: Focus on Your Content
nodes.rationale: Second tagline. 'content' is painted in brand green. Pairs with the yellow document the mascot holds: authors write docs, the framework handles the site.

nodes.label: Open Graph Social Preview
nodes.rationale: Filename and landscape composition mark this as the site's default social-share image: brand identity plus a two-beat pitch that remain readable at thumbnail size.

nodes.label: Docusaurus Social Card
nodes.rationale: Default Docusaurus Open Graph / social-share card. Landscape branding layout: gradient wordmark on top, dinosaur mascot holding a document on the left, two-line value proposition on the right. Soft mint-to-white-to-sky background keeps the mark readable as a link preview.

nodes.label: Docusaurus Dinosaur Mascot
nodes.rationale: Flat green cartoon dinosaur (alligator-like body, four back spikes, closed smiling eyes, wavy mouth, rounded feet) standing on the left. The mascot personifies the Docusaurus name and makes the docs-site brand approachable rather than enterprise-formal.

nodes.label: Yellow Lined Document
nodes.rationale: Yellow page with four horizontal text lines, held against the mascot's chest. Visual stand-in for authored documentation — the content the product exists to publish.

nodes.label: Docusaurus Gradient Wordmark
nodes.rationale: Large sans-serif product name centered at the top. Letters shift from brand blue on the left through teal to green on the right, matching the keyword-highlight green used in the taglines.

nodes.label: Content-First Authoring
nodes.rationale: The card's second promise and the document-in-arms illustration argue that Docusaurus exists so writers stay in markdown/docs rather than site-engineering.

nodes.label: Green Keyword Highlight
nodes.rationale: Only 'optimized' and 'content' are green; the rest of each line is black. The two highlighted words are the product claims the card wants a scroller to retain.

nodes.label: Middleware contract (req, res, next)
nodes.rationale: Middleware is (req, res, next) => void. Route handlers are middleware that matched a method and path.

nodes.label: Three legal middleware endings
nodes.rationale: Respond, next(), or next(err). Returning without one of those hangs the socket.

nodes.label: Middleware factory
nodes.rationale: A factory returns middleware. Configure once, reuse with different options — no module-level mutable globals.

nodes.label: Hang: no next and no response
nodes.rationale: Neither response nor next means the request hangs until the client times out.
nodes.norm_label: hang: no next and no response

nodes.label: next() after a terminal response
nodes.rationale: Calling next after res.send lets a later layer write again and throw headers-already-sent. First body still wins.

nodes.label: next() vs next(err)
nodes.rationale: next() continues the stack. next(err) jumps to error handlers. On Express 5, async throws are forwarded like next(err).

nodes.label: Headers already sent
nodes.rationale: The first write wins. A second res.json/send throws Cannot set headers after they are sent to the client.

nodes.label: res.headersSent guard
nodes.rationale: In error middleware: if (res.headersSent) return next(err). Typical causes are next() after res.json or fall-through return paths.

nodes.label: res.json vs res.send
nodes.rationale: json always serializes as JSON with the right Content-Type. send branches on type. Chain status before the body is written.

nodes.label: res terminal methods
nodes.rationale: Pick one terminal: status, json, send, end, or redirect. Mixing json then send is how headers-already-sent starts.

nodes.label: Call the factory, do not mount it
nodes.rationale: app.use(requireHeader) passes the factory with the wrong arity. Mount requireHeader('x-api-key') so each instance closes over its options.
nodes.norm_label: call the factory, do not mount it

nodes.label: Bare star path invalid on Express 5
nodes.rationale: Bare * path tokens are invalid; registration throws. 2020 MERN tutorials crash on Express 5.
nodes.norm_label: bare star path invalid on express 5

nodes.label: Named splat {*splat}
nodes.rationale: On Express 5, app.get('*') throws at boot. Use a named splat.

nodes.label: SPA fallback
nodes.rationale: Client-side routers need index.html on unknown paths. Register the catch-all after API routes.

nodes.label: express.static
nodes.rationale: Serves files from a directory. Put it after API routes if the same app also hosts a SPA.

nodes.label: Static root isolation
nodes.rationale: A static root too high exposes node_modules or .env. Root only the build output directory.

nodes.label: compression middleware
nodes.rationale: Can help JSON APIs; many production stacks terminate gzip at Nginx. Do not double-compress.

nodes.label: File send path traversal
nodes.rationale: Always set root / resolve paths carefully. Prefer object-storage signed URLs when files are large or private.

nodes.label: res.download
nodes.rationale: Suggests a filename for the Save dialog; streams from disk.

nodes.label: API then static then splat
nodes.rationale: Catch-all before API makes /api/users return HTML. Correct order: API → static assets → HTML fallback.

nodes.label: Deploy to GitHub Pages
nodes.rationale: One deploy at a time; in-progress runs finish so a half-uploaded artifact never becomes the live site.

nodes.label: Yarn node-modules linker
nodes.rationale: Pinned so CI does not fall back to PnP: locally this comes from ~/.yarnrc.yml, which the runner has no copy of.

nodes.label: Grok memory store
nodes.rationale: Curated facts live in /mnt/Storage/my-learning/grok/; ignore ~/.grok/memory/.

nodes.label: Claude memory store
nodes.rationale: All project memory lives in /mnt/Storage/my-learning/claude/; ~/.claude/ memory dirs are banned.

nodes.label: Approved colour palette
nodes.rationale: Cool blue-biased neutrals; pine accent, deliberately not the acid-green Node cliché.

nodes.label: Broken-links report step
nodes.rationale: onBrokenLinks is warn, so dead links never fail the build; the job reports them rather than blocking.

nodes.label: Enable corepack before setup-node
nodes.rationale: Must precede setup-node: cache: yarn shells out to yarn cache dir, which Yarn 1 refuses once packageManager pins Yarn 4.

nodes.label: Explanation cadence
nodes.rationale: Each topic page must be visible in the UI as written; after a complete phase run yarn build once.

nodes.label: Never-delete rule
nodes.rationale: Docs, pages, reviews and prior work are additive only; ask if removal seems required.

nodes.label: Single-agent default
nodes.rationale: Do not spawn subagents unless the user explicitly asks.

nodes.label: Markdown link form
nodes.rationale: Every link ends in .md and keeps every numeric prefix. The directory-slug form broke 188 links.

nodes.label: Critical 300-line rule
nodes.rationale: Write the explanation the topic deserves first, then split. Clustering at ~200–290 is evidence of budgeting.

nodes.label: Global rules vs project memory split
nodes.rationale: Hard rules that must never be looked up live in ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md; project-specific memory lives in the store.
nodes.norm_label: global rules vs project memory split

nodes.label: Chunked topic layout
nodes.rationale: A topic that exceeds the cap becomes a directory with README index and numbered chunks that each repeat the tier badge and Verified line.

nodes.label: Concept page contents
nodes.rationale: Every concept needs runnable examples, 3–8 interview questions with answers, and gotchas as symptom → cause → fix.

nodes.label: Granularity rule
nodes.rationale: A topic is a concept, not a symbol. Group things only meaningful together; never group to reduce coverage.

nodes.label: One docs tree per language
nodes.rationale: Everything about a technology lives under docs/<lang>/ with syllabus/, pages/ and reviews/.

nodes.label: 300-line file cap
nodes.rationale: A file-size rule, never a content budget. Write the explanation first, then split on a concept boundary.

nodes.label: Incremental working process
nodes.rationale: Do the step that was asked, then stop. Syllabus first, then pages. Target Active LTS, not newest release.

nodes.label: req.user
nodes.rationale: Authn middleware puts the authenticated principal on req, not permissions alone.

nodes.label: requireAuth
nodes.rationale: Parse session or Bearer JWT, attach req.user, else 401. Do not re-teach argon2 or JWT structure.

nodes.label: Resource ownership
nodes.rationale: Load the resource and compare owner id to req.user.id; else 404 or 403 by policy.

nodes.label: requireRole
nodes.rationale: Role checks after authentication. Fail closed with 403, not 401.

nodes.label: Tenant hopping / IDOR
nodes.rationale: Trusting a client-supplied tenantId enables tenant hopping / IDOR.

nodes.label: Optional auth middleware
nodes.rationale: Enriches req.user when a token is present but does not 401 when absent; for public+personalized routes.

nodes.label: Ownership 404 vs 403
nodes.rationale: Prefer 404 when existence should stay secret; 403 when the resource is visible but forbidden. 404 avoids leaking that the id exists.

nodes.label: 401 vs 403 after role check
nodes.rationale: 403 when identity is known; 401 when missing.

nodes.label: Tenant from identity
nodes.rationale: Force tenantId from identity, never from raw body alone.

nodes.label: Reachability
nodes.rationale: rev-list is the engine under log, fetch negotiation, and gc. main..mybranch means reachable from mybranch, not from main.

nodes.label: Phase 0 — How Git stores things
nodes.rationale: No workflow yet. What is on disk, what a commit physically is, and why later commands behave as they do. reset --soft vs --hard, rebase hashes, and deleted-branch recovery are consequences of the storage model.

nodes.label: Working tree
nodes.rationale: Actual files on disk, editable by anything, tracked or not.

nodes.label: Phase 10 — Plumbing and internals
nodes.rationale: Phase 0 proved by hand. hash-object, cat-file, write-tree, commit-tree, rev-list, packfiles, reftable.

nodes.label: Part 1 — How Git works
nodes.rationale: Phases 0–3 · 61 topics · 27 Master. Storage model, daily loop, branching, reading history. Works with no network.

nodes.label: Phase 1 — The everyday loop
nodes.rationale: status, add -p, commit, the three diffs, gitignore, switch/restore, undo before push.

nodes.label: Phase 2 — Branching, merging and rebasing
nodes.rationale: A branch is a file with a hash; merging is three-input; rebasing replays patches and changes hashes.

nodes.label: Phase 3 — Reading history
nodes.rationale: Revision syntax, ranges, bisect, pickaxe, blame, show.

nodes.label: Commit graph is a DAG
nodes.rationale: Parents point backwards. Directed because pointers go one way; acyclic because a commit hash includes its parents; a graph because merges have multiple parents.

nodes.label: Dates are metadata, not structure
nodes.rationale: A commit dated 2030 can sit beneath one dated 2026. Never build logic on commit dates; use merge-base --is-ancestor.

nodes.label: The three trees
nodes.rationale: HEAD, index, working tree. Every core command is a move between two of them.

nodes.label: V8 does not implement tail-call optimisation
nodes.rationale: TCO is in ES2015; only JavaScriptCore ships it. Writing recursion in tail position buys nothing in Chrome or Node.
nodes.norm_label: v8 does not implement tail-call optimisation

nodes.label: JavaScriptCore
nodes.rationale: Safari and Bun. Broken in Safari almost always means JSC lacks a feature V8 shipped first.

nodes.label: V8
nodes.rationale: Ships in Chrome, Edge, Node, Deno, Electron. Semantics match other engines; performance and feature timing do not.

nodes.label: console.table and console.dir
nodes.rationale: table for arrays of objects. dir with depth null fixes Node's [Object] truncation at depth 2.

nodes.label: Cold vs warm micro-benchmarks
nodes.rationale: Identical function 28x apart cold versus warm, reproduced. A single timing measures compilation state, not the code.

nodes.label: Deoptimisation
nodes.rationale: Optimised add(a,b) fell out of TurboFan after strings and objects. Nothing in the function changed — only the shapes flowing through it.

nodes.label: V8 compilation tiers
nodes.rationale: Ignition interprets, Sparkplug baselines, Maglev mid-tier, TurboFan fully optimises hot type-stable functions.

nodes.label: map(parseInt) radix trap
nodes.rationale: map passes (value, index). parseInt('2', 1) and parseInt('3', 2) are NaN. Use map(Number).

nodes.label: Number vs parseInt
nodes.rationale: Number('42px') is NaN; parseInt('42px') is 42. Number('') is 0; parseInt('') is NaN. Use Number for validation.

nodes.label: Keep data shapes stable
nodes.rationale: Do not tune for the JIT. Normalise payloads at the boundary so every downstream object has the same keys in the same order.

nodes.label: Convert at the boundary
nodes.rationale: Form values, query params, localStorage and env vars are strings. Parse once on the way in. Apply ?? default before Number because Number(null) is 0.

nodes.label: Unpolyfillable engine features
nodes.rationale: Proxy, WeakRef, BigInt and real #private fields cannot be reconstructed in JavaScript. Raise the floor or design around them.

nodes.label: BigInt
nodes.rationale: Arbitrary-precision integers because Number cannot represent every integer past MAX_SAFE_INTEGER. Convert huge values from strings.

nodes.label: Cannot mix BigInt and Number
nodes.rationale: 1n + 1 throws TypeError. Comparison is exempt: 1n == 1 is true, 1n === 1 is false. Division truncates: 5n / 2n is 2n.

nodes.label: Automatic semicolon insertion
nodes.rationale: Five dangerous line starts break a file that omits semicolons. Phase gate requires the exact rules, not folklore.

nodes.label: ~~ 32-bit wrap
nodes.rationale: ~~1e10 is 1410065408. The fast-truncate trick wraps at 32 bits; Math.trunc gives 10000000000.

nodes.label: ?? mixed with || is a SyntaxError
nodes.rationale: a ?? b || c is a SyntaxError. Precedence of ?? with || is one of the five operators that actually bite.

nodes.label: Optional chaining does not protect non-functions
nodes.rationale: nf.notAFunction?.() still throws TypeError. ?.() only guards null/undefined.
nodes.norm_label: optional chaining does not protect non-functions

nodes.label: Phase 2 Operators, expressions and control flow
nodes.rationale: Fifteen high-frequency operator and control-flow topics. Invisible-on-review bugs are precedence (?? with ||, right-associative **) and ASI.
nodes.norm_label: phase 2 operators, expressions and control flow

nodes.label: Remainder vs modulo
nodes.rationale: % is remainder and takes the sign of the dividend: -7 % 3 is -1, not 2. Real modulo is ((a % b) + b) % b.

nodes.label: Right-associative **
nodes.rationale: 2 ** 3 ** 2 is 512, not 64. ** is the only right-associative arithmetic operator. -2 ** 2 is a SyntaxError.

nodes.label: Identifiers should be strings
nodes.rationale: Postgres bigint keys and snowflake IDs are never added or averaged. Send them as strings and skip BigInt serialisation entirely.

nodes.label: JSX && zero trap
nodes.rationale: 0 && element is 0; React renders 0 as text. Force a boolean with count > 0.

nodes.label: Nullish coalescing ??
nodes.rationale: Falls back only on null/undefined, so a legitimate 0 survives; mixing ?? with &&/|| unparenthesised is a SyntaxError.

nodes.label: && and || return operands
nodes.rationale: a && b yields a if falsy else b; only ! always returns a boolean.

nodes.label: Logical short-circuiting
nodes.rationale: The right side is skipped when the left decides; that is why &&/|| cannot be functions.

nodes.label: Optional chaining short-circuits the chain
nodes.rationale: From the nullish link onward nothing evaluates, including arguments; parentheses end the chain.

nodes.label: ?.() is not a callable guard
nodes.rationale: Guards only null/undefined; a present non-function still throws TypeError.

nodes.label: Optional chaining three forms
nodes.rationale: obj?.prop, obj?.[expr], fn?.(); obj?[k] is a SyntaxError because the dot stays.

nodes.label: ?. with ?? idiom
nodes.rationale: Missing path becomes undefined; ?? supplies the default without treating 0 as missing.

nodes.label: && binds tighter than ||
nodes.rationale: a || b && c is a || (b && c); mixed ?? is a SyntaxError instead.

nodes.label: Logical operators return operands
nodes.rationale: && and || return an operand, not a boolean; that one fact explains default-value bugs and the JSX 0 trap.

nodes.label: Optional chaining ?.
nodes.rationale: Short-circuits the chain to undefined on null/undefined only; over-applying hides bugs.

nodes.label: await only works in a real loop
nodes.rationale: forEach discards async callback promises: work is not awaited and rejections are unhandled. for...of+await is sequential; Promise.all+map is concurrent.
nodes.norm_label: await only works in a real loop

nodes.label: for...of live iterator vs forEach snapshot
nodes.rationale: forEach fixes its range before the first callback. for...of re-reads length, so push during iteration over the same array is an infinite loop.
nodes.norm_label: for...of live iterator vs foreach snapshot

nodes.label: return inside forEach is continue
nodes.rationale: return exits the callback only. The enclosing function always continues — a silent compile-clean bug. Use find or for...of.

nodes.label: Labeled break for nested loops
nodes.rationale: break/continue accept a label to exit two loops. Only works with real loops, not forEach. Extracting to a function and return is often cleaner.

nodes.label: for...in
nodes.rationale: Iterates enumerable string keys including inherited prototype properties. Almost never the right loop.

nodes.label: for...of
nodes.rationale: Iterates values via Symbol.iterator. Works on arrays, strings (code points), Map, Set, NodeList, generators. Not plain objects.

nodes.label: Array.prototype.forEach
nodes.rationale: Iterates values with numeric index. Skips holes, cannot break, does not await, returns undefined.

nodes.label: await inside forEach is ignored
nodes.rationale: forEach discards the callback return, so promises are never awaited and rejections float. Use for...of or Promise.all(map).

nodes.label: Loop capability table
nodes.rationale: If the body needs break, continue, return from the enclosing function, or await, forEach and array methods are out. MDN: no way to stop forEach except throwing.

nodes.label: Never for...in on arrays
nodes.rationale: Index arrives as a string, non-index properties are included, and property enumeration skips holes while for...of visits them as undefined.

nodes.label: Object.entries as iterable adapter
nodes.rationale: Plain objects are records, not sequences. Object.entries/keys state which view you want; for...of then consumes that iterable.

nodes.label: Phase 7 Asynchronous JavaScript
nodes.rationale: Centre of gravity of the JS syllabus. If only one phase is finished to Master, finish this one.

nodes.label: Phase 8 Modules, errors, memory and the toolchain
nodes.norm_label: phase 8 modules, errors, memory and the toolchain

nodes.label: Phase 17 Machine coding
nodes.rationale: The brief's custom-functions requirement: bind, debounce, Promise.all and EventEmitter from an empty file.

nodes.label: Returning a value vs a promise
nodes.norm_label: returning a value vs a promise

nodes.label: One thread, and what runs elsewhere
nodes.norm_label: one thread, and what runs elsewhere

nodes.label: path.extname last only
nodes.rationale: report.tar.gz yields .gz. Extension-based file-type checks are trivially bypassed (evil.php.jpg); sniff content.

nodes.label: path.join
nodes.rationale: Concatenates and normalises. An absolute later argument is treated as a relative segment, so join(root,'/etc/passwd') looks contained.

nodes.label: path.posix
nodes.rationale: Use for URL paths, S3 keys, tar entries, Docker and git paths — always forward slashes. Default path.join writes backslashes on Windows.

nodes.label: path.resolve
nodes.rationale: Always absolute; restarts at any absolute argument. The right tool for validating user input against a root.

nodes.label: Path traversal
nodes.rationale: Any filesystem path built from user input is a security boundary. ../, absolute paths, encoded separators, and symlinks each escape.

nodes.label: safeResolve containment check
nodes.rationale: path.resolve(ROOT, input), require equal-to-root or startsWith(ROOT+sep), then realpath and repeat to defeat symlinks.

nodes.label: Zip-slip
nodes.rationale: Archive entries named ../../etc/cron.d/x write outside the extract root. Apply the same containment check to every entry.

nodes.label: realpath
nodes.rationale: Fully resolved absolute path following every symlink. What a containment check needs. readlink returns the raw possibly-relative target.

nodes.label: symlink
nodes.rationale: symlink(target, path) mirrors ln -s. Relative targets resolve against the link's directory, which is the traversal escape.

nodes.label: Generated storage keys
nodes.rationale: Best defence: store under UUIDs, keep original name as metadata, address by ID. No user string reaches the filesystem.

nodes.label: ROOT + path.sep prefix
nodes.rationale: startsWith('/srv/uploads') is true for /srv/uploads-evil/x. The separator plus exact-equal for the root itself is required.

nodes.label: jobId vs handler dedup
nodes.rationale: jobId stops a duplicate enqueue. Only a handler-level unique insert stops redelivery of a claimed job.

nodes.label: BullMQ Redis queue
nodes.rationale: Retries, backoff, delayed jobs and dashboards already written. Enqueue is not transactional with the app database.

nodes.label: Webhook fan-out
nodes.rationale: One dispatcher enqueues one delivery job per subscriber. A loop over N subscribers retries the ones that already succeeded.

nodes.label: Event-loop blocking in handlers
nodes.rationale: 120 ms CPU produced 1246 ms p95 at 10 concurrent vs 19 ms queued. One loop serializes everyone.

nodes.label: 202 Accepted for queued work
nodes.rationale: 200 lies that the work is done. 202 plus a status the client can read.

nodes.label: Dual-write problem
nodes.rationale: A row and a queue message cannot commit together. Reversing order or try/catch leaves a new window.

nodes.label: Worker concurrency
nodes.rationale: In-flight promises on one event loop. Helps I/O, not CPU. Must match the DB pool size.

nodes.label: Outbound side-effects as jobs
nodes.rationale: Email, webhooks and CRM calls belong on the queue so a provider outage delays a job instead of failing checkout.

nodes.label: Request path minimum
nodes.rationale: Keep only what the next screen depends on. Email, media, exports and fan-out are jobs.

nodes.label: Transactional outbox
nodes.rationale: Insert the event in the same database transaction as the business row. One commit, no divergence.

nodes.label: Worker as a separate process
nodes.rationale: Same image, two entry points. CPU isolation, independent scale, independent failure.

nodes.label: Default isolation READ COMMITTED vs REPEATABLE READ
nodes.norm_label: default isolation read committed vs repeatable read

nodes.label: The folklore that no longer holds
nodes.norm_label: the folklore that no longer holds

nodes.label: Lazy pool connect
nodes.rationale: new pg.Pool() does no I/O. Bad host/password surfaces on the first query — after the process joined the load balancer. Await select 1 at boot.

nodes.label: statement_timeout vs query_timeout
nodes.rationale: statement_timeout is server-side (57014, connection survives). query_timeout only rejects the promise — the server keeps running the query.

nodes.label: pg_advisory_lock for migrations
nodes.rationale: Lock on a fixed key before reading schema_migrations so two deploys cannot both run the same file. Session lock; take it on a dedicated client.

nodes.label: MongoClient
nodes.rationale: MongoClient is the pool and topology monitor — one per process, default maxPoolSize 100. connect() at boot turns a bad URL into a failed deploy.

nodes.label: ObjectId vs string _id
nodes.rationale: BSON equality is type-strict: findOne({_id: urlString}) returns null forever. Wrap with new ObjectId after ObjectId.isValid.

nodes.label: w=majority write concern
nodes.rationale: Majority acknowledgement survives failover. Single-node ack is faster and can lose the write when the primary steps down.

nodes.label: Mongoose .lean()
nodes.rationale: Returns plain objects instead of hydrated documents — 136 ms vs 57 ms for 5001 docs. Lose save(), virtuals, getters. Default on reads that go to JSON.

nodes.label: Mongoose validators skip updates
nodes.rationale: updateOne/findOneAndUpdate skip validators because no document is hydrated. pre('save') likewise does not fire for updates — password hashing in that hook stores plaintext.

nodes.label: MongoDB operator injection
nodes.rationale: JSON body {password: {$ne: null}} matches any password. Validate types at the boundary and compare with {$eq: String(value)}. Disable $where.

nodes.label: SQL placeholders $1
nodes.rationale: Parameters are bound after the statement is planned, so values cannot become syntax. Identifiers (ORDER BY column) cannot be parameters — use an allow-list.

nodes.label: Simple query protocol stacked statements
nodes.rationale: pool.query with no parameters uses the simple protocol, which runs multiple semicolon-separated statements — DROP TABLE works. Any parameter switches to extended protocol (42601).

nodes.label: pg date local-midnight trap
nodes.rationale: A DATE becomes a JS Date at local midnight, then JSON.stringify ships yesterday in UTC+offsets. Keep DATE as a string via setTypeParser(1082).

nodes.label: pg int8 and numeric as strings
nodes.rationale: bigint exceeds 2^53 and numeric is arbitrary-precision decimal. Returning a float would corrupt money. count(*) + 1 concatenates to "50001".
nodes.norm_label: pg int8 and numeric as strings

nodes.label: PostgreSQL SQLSTATE error codes
nodes.rationale: Match err.code not err.message. 23505 unique → 409; 25P02 aborted transaction; 57014 statement_timeout; 53300 too many clients.

nodes.label: Liveness vs readiness probes
nodes.rationale: Liveness must not hit the database — failure restarts the fleet. Readiness queries select 1 with its own timeout and returns 503 so traffic stops.

nodes.label: Expand and contract migrations
nodes.rationale: Old and new code run together during rollout. Add nullable columns first, deploy writers of both, drop later. A rename is three deploys. Prefer roll-forward over downs in production.

nodes.label: Driver-type boundary
nodes.rationale: One module owns SQL and mapping so business logic never sees rows, snake_case, Number(bigint), or 23505. Domain tests then need no database.

nodes.label: Heap Fetches
nodes.rationale: Count of rows that still needed a heap visit during an index-only scan. One UPDATE took Heap Fetches from 0 to 58.

nodes.label: INCLUDE columns
nodes.rationale: Payload stored in index leaves but not part of the sort key: returnable, not searchable or sortable. Required when UNIQUE must stay on the key alone.

nodes.label: Index-only scan
nodes.rationale: Answers from the index without touching the heap when every selected column is in the index and the visibility map marks pages all-visible.

nodes.label: Visibility map
nodes.rationale: VACUUM sets all-visible bits (relallvisible). A freshly loaded table has relallvisible=0 so a covering index still heap-scans.

nodes.label: fillfactor
nodes.rationale: Reserves free space per page for future versions. fillfactor 100: 0.1% HOT, 4→24 MB. fillfactor 70: 76.6% HOT, ended at 13 MB. Requires VACUUM FULL to rewrite existing pages.

nodes.label: HOT update
nodes.rationale: Heap-Only Tuple: new version on the same page and no indexed column changed, so indexes are untouched. Index on the updated column disables HOT entirely (0%).

nodes.label: MVCC
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL never overwrites a row. UPDATE writes a new version and marks the old one ending; DELETE only stamps xmax. Explains lock-free reads, table growth, and why VACUUM exists.

nodes.label: Snapshot
nodes.rationale: xmin:xmax:in-progress — oldest still-running xid, one past last completed, and older-than-completed still-running ids. Visible if xmin committed before the snapshot and xmax had not.

nodes.label: xmin xmax ctid
nodes.rationale: xmin created this version, xmax ended it, ctid is the physical (page, slot). ctid moves on every UPDATE and is not a stable identifier.

nodes.label: Index-only scans, INCLUDE and the visibility map
nodes.norm_label: index-only scans, include and the visibility map

nodes.label: Advisory lock
nodes.rationale: Named mutex keyed by a number, not a row. For single-runner cron, migrations, file imports. Advisory: the database enforces the lock, not the invariant.

nodes.label: pg_try_advisory_lock
nodes.rationale: Never waits; returns true/false immediately. Re-entrant and reference-counted within a session. Two-int form is a separate key space from the bigint form.

nodes.label: Idle in transaction
nodes.rationale: BEGIN then silence. wait_event=ClientRead: the server waits on the client. Holds a pool slot, locks, and possibly the vacuum horizon. Distinct from idle (no transaction).

nodes.label: idle_in_transaction_session_timeout
nodes.rationale: Kills a backend idle in transaction longer than N (25P03). statement_timeout does not help — no statement is running. Terminates the connection; pg emits 'error', not a rejected promise.

nodes.label: transaction_timeout
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL 17+. Kills any transaction older than N whether idle or busy (25P04). Covers the always-active long batch the idle timeout misses.

nodes.label: VACUUM blockers
nodes.rationale: Find by xact_start, backend_xmin, backend_xid in pg_stat_activity. Outside that: replication slots xmin, hot_standby_feedback, prepared xacts. File grew 27→40 MB with a blocker.

nodes.label: Long-running transactions and the xmin horizon
nodes.norm_label: long-running transactions and the xmin horizon

nodes.label: Session vs transaction advisory lock
nodes.rationale: Prefer pg_advisory_xact_lock — released at COMMIT/ROLLBACK and cannot leak. Session locks survive COMMIT and a pooled connection can return still holding them; release(true) if state is unknown.

nodes.label: xmin horizon
nodes.rationale: VACUUM may only remove versions no running transaction could need. One old transaction pins cleanup for every table. Idle read-only READ COMMITTED does not pin; RR/SERIALIZABLE, any writer, and a running SELECT do.

nodes.label: Dirty read
nodes.rationale: Reading uncommitted data. PostgreSQL never permits this; READ UNCOMMITTED is mapped to READ COMMITTED.

nodes.label: Non-repeatable read
nodes.rationale: Same row changes mid-transaction (balance 100 → 999). Allowed by READ COMMITTED.

nodes.label: Phantom read
nodes.rationale: New matching rows appear mid-transaction (count 2 → 3). Allowed by READ COMMITTED.

nodes.label: READ COMMITTED
nodes.rationale: Default isolation: a fresh snapshot per statement. Maximum concurrency and no 40001 retries; a read-then-write sequence can silently produce wrong data.

nodes.label: FOR KEY SHARE
nodes.rationale: Weakest mode; what an FK insert takes. Conflicts only with FOR UPDATE so parent non-key updates are not blocked.

nodes.label: FOR NO KEY UPDATE
nodes.rationale: Update non-key columns only. Conflicts with all modes except KEY SHARE.

nodes.label: FOR SHARE
nodes.rationale: Row must not change while you read it. Conflicts with UPDATE and NO KEY UPDATE.

nodes.label: FOR UPDATE
nodes.rationale: Strongest row lock; conflicts with every other row-lock mode. Held until the transaction ends, not the statement.

nodes.label: Statement-level snapshot
nodes.rationale: Snapshot is fixed when the statement starts. A long SELECT is internally consistent even if another session commits mid-scan.

nodes.label: UPDATE WHERE re-evaluation
nodes.rationale: An UPDATE that waited on a row lock re-evaluates WHERE against the newly committed version and may report rowCount 0.

nodes.label: Tuple-header row locks
nodes.rationale: Row locks live in xmax plus flag bits, not the lock manager. pg_locks is empty; use pg_blocking_pids().

nodes.label: RELEASE SAVEPOINT
nodes.rationale: Discards the marker but keeps the work. Later ROLLBACK TO that name is 3B001.

nodes.label: ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT
nodes.rationale: Undoes work after the marker and leaves the transaction open. Plain ROLLBACK ends it. Must be taken before the failing statement.

nodes.label: SAVEPOINT
nodes.rationale: Only way to survive a statement error inside a transaction. PostgreSQL has no real nested transactions.

nodes.label: Autovacuum
nodes.rationale: Fires at threshold + scale_factor × live_rows (default 50 + 20%). Large hot tables need a per-table override.

nodes.label: HOT updates
nodes.rationale: fillfactor 70 raised HOT from 0.1% to 76.6% and cut a 24 MB table to 13 MB. An index on the updated column drives HOT to 0%.

nodes.label: VACUUM
nodes.rationale: Marks dead row versions reusable under SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE. Does not return space to the OS.

nodes.label: Anti-wraparound autovacuum
