nodes.rationale: Starts at autovacuum_freeze_max_age = 200 million. Alert here, not at the 2.134-billion WARNING which is only ~10 million xids before writes stop.

nodes.label: XID freezing
nodes.rationale: Marks a row visible to everyone, immune to wraparound. relfrozenxid / age() is what you monitor.

nodes.label: XID wraparound
nodes.rationale: 32-bit xids; if the counter advances 2^31 past xmin the row looks future-dated and vanishes. VACUUM freezes old rows to prevent it.

nodes.label: DETACH and DROP PARTITION
nodes.rationale: DETACH 5 ms (metadata); DROP 10 ms for 103353 rows vs a DELETE that writes a dead tuple per row.

nodes.label: Savepoint subtransaction
nodes.rationale: Each writing savepoint burns a real xid. Per-statement SAVEPOINT/RELEASE cost 2.3×; past 64 subxids the cache overflows and other sessions pay SubtransSLRU waits.

nodes.label: jsonb_agg
nodes.rationale: Over zero rows returns NULL not []; over a LEFT JOIN with no match returns [{nulls}]. Need FILTER plus coalesce to [].

nodes.label: jsonb_build_object
nodes.rationale: Explicit key allowlist. Prefer over to_jsonb(row) for client payloads so new columns do not leak.

nodes.label: jsonb_to_recordset
nodes.rationale: Turns a JSON array parameter into typed rows for INSERT ... SELECT.

nodes.label: No foreign key on a jsonb key
nodes.rationale: CHECK on a jsonb key works; a FOREIGN KEY cannot reference one (42601). Referential integrity is the guarantee you actually give up.
nodes.norm_label: no foreign key on a jsonb key

nodes.label: jsonb expression index
nodes.rationale: Index (doc->>'tag') for a hot key: 0.9 ms and 1352 kB. Expression must match the query exactly, including casts.

nodes.label: GIN jsonb_ops
nodes.rationale: Default GIN: indexes keys and values separately. Serves @> (4.5 ms) and ?; 17 MB; cannot serve ->>.

nodes.label: GIN jsonb_path_ops
nodes.rationale: One hash per path-plus-value. Smaller/faster for @> (1.1 ms, 13 MB) but cannot serve ?.

nodes.label: jsonb operator families
nodes.rationale: Accessors dig a value out; predicates ask a question. Which family you use decides whether a GIN index can help.

nodes.label: Shape JSON in JS not SQL
nodes.rationale: jsonb_agg 284.8 ms vs flat join + JS 90.7 ms; json_agg 131.2 ms. Use SQL constructors when the shape is the point, not serialisation.
nodes.norm_label: shape json in js not sql

nodes.label: Column versus jsonb
nodes.rationale: If you can name the field in a requirement it is a column. jsonb is for unenumerable shape. Same two facts: 22 MB vs 1736 kB (~13×).

nodes.label: Generated column hybrid
nodes.rationale: Promote queried keys to GENERATED ALWAYS AS (payload->>'k') STORED columns. Derived from the document so it cannot drift.

nodes.label: CREATE EXTENSION
nodes.rationale: Installs a package of types/functions per database. Available means files on disk; installed means CREATE EXTENSION ran here.

nodes.label: pg_stat_statements
nodes.rationale: First extension to enable. Also needs shared_preload_libraries and a restart; CREATE EXTENSION alone returns nothing.

nodes.label: dblink
nodes.rationale: Older string-query mechanism with no pushdown. Still useful for a query not tied to the local transaction.

nodes.label: postgres_fdw
nodes.rationale: Foreign table is a query against another server. IMPORT FOREIGN SCHEMA snapshots remote definitions.

nodes.label: HNSW 2000-dimension limit
nodes.rationale: Column holds up to 16000 dimensions; HNSW indexes at most 2000 (54000). halfvec indexes up to 4000.

nodes.label: Vector distance operators
nodes.rationale: <-> L2, <=> cosine, <#> negative inner product. All are distances so ORDER BY ASC is nearest-first.

nodes.label: HNSW index
nodes.rationale: 50k 384-d vectors: 88 ms exact → 2.1 ms (42×). Build 22.9 s; index 98 MB vs 78 MB table. Results are approximate.

nodes.label: pgvector
nodes.rationale: Embeddings next to the row so a relational filter and similarity search share one query and transaction. Not bundled in stock images.

nodes.label: Extensions are per database
nodes.rationale: CREATE DATABASE does not copy extensions. digest() worked in one DB and raised 42883 in a new one on the same server.

nodes.label: FDW is not two-phase commit
nodes.rationale: Local commit can succeed while the remote fails. Treat FDW as a read tool.

nodes.label: FDW pushdown
nodes.rationale: Full remote aggregate 2.9 ms vs 41.9 ms when a VOLATILE predicate forces shipping rows. Read EXPLAIN VERBOSE Remote SQL.

nodes.label: Identity sequence needs no USAGE grant
nodes.norm_label: identity sequence needs no usage grant

nodes.label: bigint primary keys
nodes.rationale: Exhausting an int sequence is 2200H and a full ACCESS EXCLUSIVE rewrite; measured cost of bigint is about 20% on a narrow table.

nodes.label: bigint arrives as a JavaScript string
nodes.norm_label: bigint arrives as a javascript string

nodes.label: Keep numeric money as a string in JS
nodes.norm_label: keep numeric money as a string in js

nodes.label: numeric plus currency column
nodes.rationale: Never double precision — 1000 × 0.01 sums to 9.999999999999831. Never the money type.

nodes.label: Uniqueness is per tenant
nodes.rationale: UNIQUE (tenant_id, slug) so tenant B can reuse a slug tenant A took. A global unique is unintended cross-tenant coupling.

nodes.label: Constraint names are an API
nodes.rationale: err.constraint plus SQLSTATE turns a database error into a field-level message (23505 + users_email_key). Auto-generated names change on column rename; name constraints explicitly.

nodes.label: Case-insensitive uniqueness
nodes.rationale: UNIQUE (email) treats Alice@x.com and alice@x.com as different. Fix with unique index on lower(email) (queries must match the expression) or a non-deterministic ICU collation.

nodes.label: Unique constraint vs unique index
nodes.rationale: Same btree. FK can only target a constraint. Only an index can be partial, on an expression, or built CONCURRENTLY. Production: CONCURRENTLY then UNIQUE USING INDEX.

nodes.label: Partial unique index for soft delete
nodes.rationale: UNIQUE among live rows: CREATE UNIQUE INDEX … (email) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL. Constraints cannot be partial, so tombstones would block re-registration.
nodes.norm_label: partial unique index for soft delete

nodes.label: Soft delete is an UPDATE
nodes.rationale: Setting deleted_at fires no cascade, unique constraints still see the row, every query needs WHERE deleted_at IS NULL. Idempotent: second delete rowCount 0.

nodes.label: DO NOTHING returns no row
nodes.rationale: rowCount 0 and empty RETURNING on skip. Workarounds: no-op DO UPDATE (a real write) or follow-up SELECT.

nodes.label: EXCLUDED row
nodes.rationale: The row that would have been inserted. SET qty = stock.qty + EXCLUDED.qty accumulates; SET qty = EXCLUDED.qty overwrites. WHERE on DO UPDATE skips no-op writes.

nodes.label: INSERT … ON CONFLICT
nodes.rationale: Atomic upsert. Only correct insert-if-absent. Check-then-insert raced: 20 workers, 20 duplicates, 0 errors. Conflict target needs a unique index (42P10 otherwise).

nodes.label: xmax = 0 as was_insert
nodes.rationale: RETURNING (xmax = 0) is true for insert, false for update. Implementation detail; prefer created_at vs updated_at if the distinction is load-bearing.

nodes.label: Uniqueness only under concurrency via the constraint
nodes.rationale: Application pre-check has a window between read and write. 20 workers produced 20 duplicates and no errors. Map 23505 to 409 via err.constraint.
nodes.norm_label: uniqueness only under concurrency via the constraint

nodes.label: Unique ORDER BY tiebreaker
nodes.rationale: ORDER BY plus LIMIT on a non-unique column is not a total order. Measured 46 duplicate page rows of 100; append the primary key.

nodes.label: Keyset pagination
nodes.rationale: Seek to the last row's sort key. Tuple, ORDER BY, and index must match; the last column must be unique.

nodes.label: NULL in a row constructor
nodes.rationale: (1,NULL) < (1,2) is unknown. WHERE discards it, so pagination silently stops. Only paginate NOT NULL columns.

nodes.label: Opaque keyset cursor
nodes.rationale: Round-trip both values as one server-issued token. Base64 is not encryption; validate types before binding.

nodes.label: Row constructors and tuple comparison
nodes.rationale: (a, b) > ($1, $2) is lexicographic. It replaces an OR chain the planner handles worse.

nodes.label: IS DISTINCT FROM
nodes.rationale: Null-safe comparison. qty != 5 dropped the NULL row; IS DISTINCT FROM 5 kept it.

nodes.label: Three-valued WHERE logic
nodes.rationale: WHERE keeps only true. Unknown is discarded like false, silently.

nodes.label: Joining on expressions
nodes.rationale: ON accepts any boolean. Non-equality leaves only nested loops; hash and merge joins need equality.

nodes.label: Range join with @>
nodes.rationale: Price-at-sale via tstzrange @> sold_at. Guard overlaps with EXCLUDE USING gist; index the range with GiST.

nodes.label: Half-open time ranges
nodes.rationale: BETWEEN is inclusive on both ends and double-counts midnight boundaries. Use >= start AND < end.

nodes.label: Expression indexes need selectivity
nodes.rationale: A 200k×200k join on lower() was 211 ms with or without the index. The same index made a 50-row driving side 59× faster.

nodes.label: Nested Loop Hash Merge join strategies
nodes.rationale: Equijoin unlocks all three. Non-equality leaves only nested loop. Planner reorders inner joins freely; outer-join order is semantic.
nodes.norm_label: nested loop hash merge join strategies

nodes.label: Emulate FULL OUTER with LEFT plus anti-join
nodes.rationale: LEFT JOIN UNION ALL the reverse NOT EXISTS branch. Use UNION ALL because the branches are disjoint; UNION only pays the 3.5× dedup cost. Fallback when the condition is not hash- or merge-joinable.
nodes.norm_label: emulate full outer with left plus anti-join

nodes.label: FULL OUTER JOIN
nodes.rationale: Keeps unmatched rows from both sides. The only join with no substitute for reconciliation, migration verification, and snapshot diffs. Requires merge- or hash-joinable equality conditions.

nodes.label: IS DISTINCT FROM for diffs
nodes.rationale: a.col <> b.col is NULL when either side is NULL, so changed rows drop silently. IS DISTINCT FROM treats NULL as a value and keeps them.

nodes.label: Symmetric difference filter
nodes.rationale: WHERE a.pk IS NULL OR b.pk IS NULL after FULL OUTER JOIN returns only unmatched rows from both sides in one pass.

nodes.label: USING coalesce on FULL JOIN
nodes.rationale: USING merges the join column as coalesce(left.col, right.col), so the key is never NULL for a row present on either side — the one place USING is clearly better than ON.

nodes.label: Set-op column and type rules
nodes.rationale: Column counts must match (42601). Types resolve like CASE. Names come from the first branch only. INTERSECT binds tighter than UNION and EXCEPT.

nodes.label: UNION
nodes.rationale: Deduplicates via HashAggregate and blocks until both branches are consumed. Measured 491 ms vs 142 ms for UNION ALL over 600000 rows (3.5×).

nodes.label: UNION ALL
nodes.rationale: Streaming Append that can stop under LIMIT. Default when branches are disjoint. Also the joining operator of a recursive CTE.

nodes.label: FULL JOIN merge/hash restriction
nodes.rationale: A full join must track unmatched rows on both sides. Hash marks hits then sweeps unhit entries; merge sees both sorted streams. Nested loop has no cheap bookkeeping, so PostgreSQL rejects non-equijoin FULL JOIN.

nodes.label: pg_dump client must be newer or equal
nodes.norm_label: pg_dump client must be newer or equal

nodes.label: Roles are cluster-wide, not in pg_dump
nodes.norm_label: roles are cluster-wide, not in pg_dump

nodes.label: Dump formats and what is in them
nodes.rationale: Four formats. -Fc is the default: compressed, TOC, selective and parallel restore. Roles are not in pg_dump.
nodes.norm_label: dump formats and what is in them

nodes.label: Restoring
nodes.rationale: Restore is ~4x dump because indexes rebuild. Dump is a REPEATABLE READ snapshot holding ACCESS SHARE.

nodes.label: Roles, GRANT and REVOKE
nodes.rationale: Least privilege is GRANT statements; a new role can do almost nothing. Role=identity, privilege=verb on an object, ownership outranks both, effective privileges are the union of inherited roles.

nodes.label: Least privilege as GRANT statements
nodes.rationale: Least privilege is not a written policy; it is GRANT statements, and a new role can do almost nothing.

nodes.label: ORDER BY inside collection aggregates
nodes.rationale: The query's outer ORDER BY orders result rows, not aggregate input. Put ORDER BY inside the parentheses of every collection whose order a consumer can see.

nodes.label: array_agg
nodes.rationale: Keeps NULLs as elements — opposite of string_agg. FILTER (WHERE x IS NOT NULL) preferred over array_remove; if every value is NULL, FILTER yields NULL and array_remove yields {}.

nodes.label: Unordered aggregate inherits sibling ORDER BY
nodes.rationale: When one aggregate has an internal ORDER BY, the executor may sort the shared input once. An unordered sibling silently inherits that order — output can change when an unrelated column is added.
nodes.norm_label: unordered aggregate inherits sibling order by

nodes.label: string_agg
nodes.rationale: Drops NULLs and emits no delimiter for them. Empty group is NULL not ''. text-only: 42883 on integer without ::text. coalesce(string_agg(...), '') before concatenation.

nodes.label: jsonb_agg
nodes.rationale: Arrives as a real JavaScript array; pg already JSON.parsed it. JSON.parse on the result throws. Same internal ORDER BY rule as array_agg.

nodes.label: jsonb_build_object
nodes.rationale: Alternating key, value. The API contract is written in the query so adding a table column cannot change the response shape.

nodes.label: to_jsonb of a row
nodes.rationale: Emits every column named by column name. Never point it at a table whose columns you do not control — later migrations leak into the API. Safe form: to_jsonb over a subquery that names columns.

nodes.label: The empty-array trap
nodes.rationale: Naked array_agg/jsonb_agg over LEFT JOIN yields [null] because the invented NULL child is a real group member. FILTER removes it and then the empty group is NULL. Both FILTER and coalesce(..., '[]'::jsonb) are required to reach []. '{}'' is an empty JSON object, not an array.

nodes.label: Two-level LATERAL JSON payload
nodes.rationale: LEFT JOIN LATERAL … ON true so the inner query can see c.id and childless parents stay. Inner GROUP BY o.id stops fan-out compounding. Measured 292 shaped bytes vs 580 flat.

nodes.label: bool_and / every()
nodes.rationale: every() is a standard-SQL alias. Empty set is NULL not true — vacuous truth is not what SQL returns. coalesce(bool_and(...), true) or a customer with no orders is reported unpaid because NULL is falsy.

nodes.label: Canonical child-collection expression
nodes.rationale: coalesce(jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object(...) ORDER BY ...) FILTER (WHERE child.id IS NOT NULL), '[]'::jsonb). Four parts: name fields, stable order, drop [null], empty group to [].

nodes.label: Produce undefined, accept null at the boundary
nodes.norm_label: produce undefined, accept null at the boundary

nodes.label: Docusaurus CSS P2 Brand Mark
nodes.rationale: Replaces the default Docusaurus infima logo so the CSS phase-2 build reads as CSS-education branding rather than a generic docs theme.

nodes.label: Cactus Green and Notepad Yellow Palette
nodes.norm_label: cactus green and notepad yellow palette

nodes.label: CSS-Tricks Cactus Mascot
nodes.rationale: Recognizable CSS-Tricks cactus character: jagged left spines, yellow notepad body, two circular pads, face, and two top dots. Used here as the CSS-track brand mark.

nodes.label: CSS P2 Site Logo SVG
nodes.rationale: 200x200 square SVG (viewBox 0 0 200 200) used as the Docusaurus CSS phase-2 site mark. Flat fills, evenodd fill-rule, no strokes.

nodes.label: Flat Evenodd Vector Illustration
nodes.rationale: No strokes, no gradients, fill-rule evenodd, geometric rounded-rect and circle primitives. Scales as a navbar/favicon-style mark.

nodes.label: Writing-About-CSS Notepad Metaphor
nodes.rationale: Yellow ruled paper over the cactus body frames the character as a note-taker, matching a CSS reference / tutorial site.

nodes.label: Powered by React
nodes.rationale: Explicit SVG title; the illustration's message is that Docusaurus documentation sites run on React.

nodes.label: Facebook-Blue Center Monitor
nodes.rationale: Center screen is #4267b2 (Facebook/Meta blue) while side screens stay dark slate, visually privileging the React-associated pane.

nodes.label: Powered by React Illustration
nodes.rationale: Default Docusaurus hero graphic: a seated developer at a three-monitor desk with the Keytar mascot and React atom, branding the site as React-powered rather than depicting a real UI.

nodes.label: Undraw Flat Illustration Style
nodes.rationale: Faceless pastel figures, slate furniture (#3f3d56/#65617d), coral clothing (#ff6584), peach skin (#fbbebe) — stock undraw language customized with official Docusaurus green and React cyan.

nodes.label: Declaring layers and fixing their order
nodes.norm_label: declaring layers and fixing their order

nodes.label: Four equality algorithms
nodes.rationale: == and === treat NaN unequal and 0 equal to -0. SameValueZero (includes, Map/Set) treats NaN equal. SameValue (Object.is) also distinguishes -0.

nodes.label: == versus ===
nodes.rationale: === never converts. == converts: null/undefined only to each other; string to number; boolean to number first; object via ToPrimitive.

nodes.label: Eight falsy values
nodes.rationale: false, 0, -0, 0n, '', null, undefined, NaN. Everything else is truthy including '0', 'false', [], {}, and new Boolean(false).

nodes.label: Empty objects are truthy
nodes.rationale: Check array.length, Object.keys(obj).length, or map.size. if (items) is always true even for [].

nodes.label: ToBoolean
nodes.rationale: if (x) uses ToBoolean and never converts an object to a primitive. [] is truthy while [] == false is true because equality does convert.

nodes.label: Nullish coalescing ??
nodes.rationale: ?? falls back only on null and undefined. || falls back on every falsy value including 0, '', false, and NaN. Mixing ?? with || or && is a SyntaxError without parens. NaN ?? 1 is NaN.

nodes.label: includes versus indexOf for NaN
nodes.rationale: indexOf uses === so [NaN].indexOf(NaN) is -1. includes and Map/Set keys use SameValueZero so NaN is found and deduped.

nodes.label: NaN !== NaN
nodes.rationale: IEEE-754: two failed computations are not the same value. Only JS value not equal to itself. Propagates silently through later arithmetic.

nodes.label: Number.isNaN versus isNaN
nodes.rationale: Global isNaN coerces first so isNaN('abc') is true. Number.isNaN is true only for the NaN value. Prefer Number.isFinite to also reject Infinity.

nodes.label: Cannot mix BigInt and Number
nodes.rationale: 1n + 1 throws TypeError. Comparison is allowed: 1n == 1 is true, 1n === 1 is false. Mixing would silently lose precision.

nodes.label: Wrapper constructors
nodes.rationale: new String/Number/Boolean produce objects. typeof is object; === fails; new Boolean(false) is truthy. Called without new they convert to primitives.

nodes.label: Object literal is not a scope
nodes.rationale: An arrow used as a method looks past the object literal to module this (undefined).
nodes.norm_label: object literal is not a scope

nodes.label: What creates a scope
nodes.rationale: Function bodies, blocks for let/const/class, modules, for heads with let/const, and catch. Object literals, if parentheses, templates, and var-in-a-block do not.

nodes.label: const fixes the binding not the value
nodes.rationale: The name cannot be pointed at something else; object and array contents can still change. Redeclaration is SyntaxError; reassignment is TypeError.
nodes.norm_label: const fixes the binding not the value

nodes.label: Function scope vs block scope
nodes.rationale: var ignores blocks and attaches to the nearest function. let/const attach to the nearest block.

nodes.label: Object.freeze
nodes.rationale: Shallow. Nested objects remain mutable. Strict throws on a frozen write; sloppy fails silently.

nodes.label: Declaration hoisting
nodes.rationale: var is referenceable before its line without ReferenceError, but the value is always undefined until assignment.

nodes.label: Three binding error types
nodes.rationale: x is not defined means no binding; x is not a function means the binding holds a non-callable; Cannot access before initialization means uninitialised TDZ.

nodes.label: Function expression not hoisted
nodes.rationale: var f = function(){} hoists the binding as undefined; calling it above the line is TypeError, not ReferenceError.

nodes.label: var declaration vs initialization split
nodes.rationale: var x = 1 is two operations: the declaration hoists to function scope as undefined; the assignment stays where it is.

nodes.label: TDZ engine error messages
nodes.rationale: V8: Cannot access 'X' before initialization. SpiderMonkey names the declaration. JavaScriptCore omits the identifier.

nodes.label: const by default
nodes.rationale: const first, let when you reassign, var never. Use-before-declaration then throws instead of producing undefined.

nodes.label: Closure captures the variable not the value
nodes.rationale: A live reference to the binding, read at call time. Explains both counter factories and the loop bug.
nodes.norm_label: closure captures the variable not the value

nodes.label: IIFE loop-variable capture
nodes.rationale: A function parameter is a fresh binding per call. Pre-ES6 fix that let automates.

nodes.label: let per-iteration binding
nodes.rationale: for (let) copies the loop variable into a fresh binding each iteration. Closures that mutate n do not interfere.

nodes.label: setTimeout is not the loop-bug cause
nodes.rationale: The synchronous var loop also yields [3,3,3]. The timer only guarantees callbacks run after the loop.
nodes.norm_label: settimeout is not the loop-bug cause

nodes.label: var-in-a-loop bug
nodes.rationale: var is function-scoped so one i is shared. Closures report the final 3. Fixes: let, IIFE parameter, or forEach.

nodes.label: Counter factory
nodes.rationale: count is unreachable from outside. Each factory call creates a new scope so instances are independent.

nodes.label: One scope per enclosing call
nodes.rationale: Closures created during one call share that call's bindings. Not one scope per closure.

nodes.label: Stale closure
nodes.rationale: Closing over a copy or a previous-render binding freezes the value. Fix with the live variable, a mutable ref, a recreated closure, or an updater.

nodes.label: Closure
nodes.rationale: A function together with the variables it still has access to. Every JS function is one; the word matters when the function outlives its defining scope.

nodes.label: Per-iteration TDZ binding
nodes.rationale: for (const item of items) is legal because each iteration declares a new binding. Same machinery as let-in-a-loop closures.

nodes.label: TDZ is temporal not positional
nodes.rationale: A function defined above a let may close over it. Only a read that runs before the declaration throws.

nodes.label: in operator
nodes.rationale: True for own or inherited properties, including Object.prototype names. Right for capability detection. Throws on primitives; does not auto-box.

nodes.label: Existence checks and delete
nodes.rationale: Four answers disagree on purpose along two axes: whether the prototype chain counts, and whether a property holding undefined counts as present.

nodes.label: A miss traverses the entire chain
nodes.rationale: Accessing a non-existent property walks to null. A miss is the most expensive lookup, not the cheapest.
nodes.norm_label: a miss traverses the entire chain

nodes.label: Prototype chain
nodes.rationale: Every object has an internal [[Prototype]] link. Lookup walks until it finds a name or reaches null, then returns undefined. Nothing is copied onto instances.

nodes.label: this is the receiver not the home
nodes.rationale: An inherited method is found on the prototype but this is the object it was called on. Finding the method and resolving each property are two separate lookups.
nodes.norm_label: this is the receiver not the home

nodes.label: Object.create
nodes.rationale: Sets [[Prototype]] directly with no constructor call. Descriptor defaults are all false. Object.create(null) gives no chain at all.

nodes.label: prototype vs [[Prototype]]
nodes.rationale: [[Prototype]] is an internal slot on every object. Fn.prototype is an ordinary property only functions have, the object new will install. A function's own prototype is Function.prototype.

nodes.label: The prototype chain topic
nodes.rationale: An object is own properties plus a link. This topic makes class stop being magic and comes before topic 06 deliberately.

nodes.label: Phase 4 — Objects, prototypes and classes
nodes.rationale: Everything non-primitive. Prototype rows make class stop being magic; the copy row is the one that costs teams real money. Master topics 01, 03–08 are written.

nodes.label: in for behaviour, hasOwn for data
nodes.rationale: Use in for feature detection where inheritance should count. Never use in for user-supplied keys.
nodes.norm_label: in for behaviour, hasown for data

nodes.label: Keep the prototype chain short
nodes.rationale: A miss visits every level. Two or three levels is normal; ten is a smell. Extending built-in prototypes lengthens the chain for every object of that type.

nodes.label: Default sort is UTF-16 string order
nodes.rationale: Elements are converted to strings then compared as UTF-16 code units, so [1, 30, 4, 21, 100000] becomes [1, 100000, 21, 30, 4].
nodes.norm_label: default sort is utf-16 string order

nodes.label: sort mutates and returns the same array
nodes.rationale: const sorted = arr.sort() is the same reference, so change detection sees no new identity and shared callers are reordered.
nodes.norm_label: sort mutates and returns the same array

nodes.label: ES2023 non-mutating array family
nodes.rationale: toSorted, toReversed, toSpliced and with leave the original alone and produce dense arrays.

nodes.label: Array.prototype.reverse
nodes.rationale: Like sort, reverse mutates in place and returns the same reference.

nodes.label: Array.prototype.toSorted
nodes.rationale: ES2023 non-mutating counterpart: returns a shallow-copied sorted array. [...arr].sort() is the portable form.

nodes.label: Spread is a shallow copy
nodes.rationale: Multidimensional arrays are not safe to copy with spread. structuredClone is for a genuinely independent graph.

nodes.label: Four sort rules
nodes.rationale: Always pass a numeric comparator; copy before sorting shared arrays; keep the comparator total and consistent; undefined and holes always go last.

nodes.label: Immutable updates with spread
nodes.rationale: Copy only changed levels and share untouched branches so prev.items === next.items remains a valid change check.

nodes.label: five reasons that justify a split
nodes.norm_label: five reasons that justify a split

nodes.label: Composition over configuration
nodes.rationale: Pass the <Button>, not three props describing one.

nodes.label: Map and Set stringify as {}
nodes.rationale: Contents live in internal slots, not own enumerable properties.

nodes.label: undefined omitted in objects, nulled in arrays
nodes.rationale: undefined, functions and symbols vanish from objects and become null in arrays — same values, opposite treatment.
nodes.norm_label: undefined omitted in objects, nulled in arrays

nodes.label: JSON.stringify is silently lossy
nodes.rationale: It sees the same own enumerable string-keyed set as Object.keys. Prototype, symbols and non-enumerables are gone.

nodes.label: Object accidental inherited keys
nodes.rationale: A Map has no default keys. An object dictionary keyed by user input inherits toString and friends.

nodes.label: Map.groupBy vs Object.groupBy
nodes.rationale: Grouping keys are data. Map.groupBy keeps any key type and insertion order; Object.groupBy stringifies and re-sorts numeric keys.

nodes.label: Map does not serialise
nodes.rationale: Biggest reason objects survive at network and storage edges. JSON.stringify([...map]) keeps key types; fromEntries stringifies them.

nodes.label: Destructuring defaults apply to undefined only
nodes.rationale: JSON payloads use null for missing values because stringify drops undefined, so every default is routinely bypassed. Follow with ??.
nodes.norm_label: destructuring defaults apply to undefined only

nodes.label: Object spread
nodes.rationale: Copies own enumerable properties. {...map} is {}. Spreading false or undefined is a silent no-op that enables ...(cond && { k }).

nodes.label: Later spreads win
nodes.rationale: Object spread is a replace, not a deep merge. A spread after an explicit key overrides it.

nodes.label: stringify is not deep equality
nodes.rationale: Key order follows enumeration, so same content in different insertion order produces different strings.

nodes.label: Use Map when keys are data
nodes.rationale: Keys from user input, non-strings, open-ended sets, frequent add/remove, insertion order or size want Map. Fixed typed keys and JSON edges want objects.
nodes.norm_label: use map when keys are data

nodes.label: acceptingTraffic flag
nodes.rationale: Flip true only after validate config, connect pools, and listen. Ready before the pool exists means health already passed while first requests fail.

nodes.label: Liveness probe
nodes.rationale: Answers 'should this process be killed?'. Must depend on almost nothing. If /live checks the database and it blips, every pod restarts at once.

nodes.label: Readiness drain on SIGTERM
nodes.rationale: Set readiness false, wait for in-flight requests, close server, exit. The balancer stops new traffic because readiness failed, not because the process vanished mid-request.

nodes.label: Readiness probe
nodes.rationale: Answers 'should this process receive traffic?'. Allowed to be strict: DB pool, required caches, acceptingTraffic flag. Temporary and reversible without a kill.

nodes.label: Shutdown is the reverse of boot
nodes.rationale: SIGTERM → fail readiness → drain → close server → close pools → exit.
nodes.norm_label: shutdown is the reverse of boot

nodes.label: Exec-form CMD
nodes.rationale: CMD ["node", "dist/server.js"] so Node is PID 1 and receives signals. CMD npm start is a different footgun.

nodes.label: Node as PID 1
nodes.rationale: Exec Node directly in the image. Use npm scripts on the laptop. Register SIGTERM and SIGINT to drain and exit.

nodes.label: npm start swallows SIGTERM
nodes.rationale: npm is often PID 1 and may not forward SIGTERM to the Node child, so graceful shutdown never runs.

nodes.label: SIGTERM then SIGKILL
nodes.rationale: Orchestrators send SIGTERM to PID 1, wait terminationGracePeriodSeconds (often 30s), then SIGKILL.

nodes.label: tini / dumb-init
nodes.rationale: If you must use a shell wrapper, a tiny init reaps zombies and forwards signals. Prefer avoiding the wrapper.

nodes.label: PID 1 and signal handling
nodes.rationale: If PID 1 is a shell or npm that never passes SIGTERM to Node, every deploy becomes a hard kill after the grace period.

nodes.label: .env local only
nodes.rationale: Node 24 --env-file is for local development. Never the only copy of prod secrets. Env values are strings — parse booleans explicitly.

nodes.label: Env validation at boot
nodes.rationale: required() throws on missing DATABASE_URL. A throw here is a failed deploy, not a half-up process accepting traffic.

nodes.label: NODE_ENV is not a feature flag
nodes.rationale: NODE_ENV=production changes dependency behaviour. Do not overload it for customer tier. Use explicit flags.
nodes.norm_label: node_env is not a feature flag

nodes.label: .dockerignore
nodes.rationale: Without it you send host node_modules and .env into the build context — slow and dangerous.

nodes.label: Multi-stage Docker build
nodes.rationale: deps / build / runner stages. Copy lockfile + package.json before source so code edits do not invalidate the dependency layer.

nodes.label: Non-root container user
nodes.rationale: USER after files are copied with correct ownership. Limits blast radius of filesystem and some remote exploits.

nodes.label: CI as an environment
nodes.rationale: Failures that only happen in CI are still production risks if CI matches prod closer than the laptop does.

nodes.label: Same Node major and lockfile
nodes.rationale: Same Active LTS line in CI, staging, prod. One lockfile; immutable install. Same variable names, different values.

nodes.label: 12-factor config
nodes.rationale: Config is injected by the environment, parsed once at boot, and refused loudly when required values are missing.

nodes.label: Boot sequence
nodes.rationale: Any other order accepts requests the process cannot serve, or fails half-way with sockets already open.

nodes.label: No default secrets
nodes.rationale: A default DATABASE_URL lets a misconfigured deploy silently talk to localhost or a shared dev DB.

nodes.label: Canary deploy
nodes.rationale: Gradual traffic slice with metrics gates; include write paths so the mix is representative.

nodes.label: Canary metrics gates
nodes.rationale: Pods ready is not enough — watch errors, latency percentiles, lag, and business KPIs.

nodes.label: Zero-downtime deploys — rolling restarts, drain, readiness
nodes.norm_label: zero-downtime deploys — rolling restarts, drain, readiness

nodes.label: CI/CD — Node version matrix, caches, artifacts
nodes.norm_label: ci/cd — node version matrix, caches, artifacts

nodes.label: Image size and hardening — distroless, alpine, slim, libc
nodes.norm_label: image size and hardening — distroless, alpine, slim, libc

nodes.label: Process managers — pm2, systemd, or the orchestrator
nodes.norm_label: process managers — pm2, systemd, or the orchestrator

nodes.label: Scaling — vertical vs horizontal, cluster vs replicas
nodes.norm_label: scaling — vertical vs horizontal, cluster vs replicas

nodes.label: Serverless Node — cold starts, connection reuse, pooling
nodes.norm_label: serverless node — cold starts, connection reuse, pooling

nodes.label: vm constructor-chain breakout
nodes.rationale: this.constructor.constructor("return process")() returned process.version v24.19.0 against createContext({}).

nodes.label: node:vm
nodes.rationale: Runs a JS string in a configured V8 context for soft isolation, tests, and REPLs — not hostile code.

nodes.label: WebAssembly in Node
nodes.rationale: Portable near-native compute after a profile shows a CPU kernel; not a default architecture.

nodes.label: uvwasi 0.0.23
nodes.rationale: Node's WASI implementation version via process.versions.uvwasi on Node 24.19.0.

nodes.label: WASI
nodes.rationale: Portable Wasm syscalls for files, clocks, and similar, mediated by the host — not a full OS.

nodes.label: WASI preopens
nodes.rationale: Map guest paths to host directories; overly broad maps leak or overwrite data. WASI is not safe because Wasm.

nodes.label: node:vm is not a security sandbox
nodes.rationale: Node documents vm as not a security mechanism; hostile code reaches the outer realm and process.
nodes.norm_label: node:vm is not a security sandbox

nodes.label: vm timeout is best-effort
nodes.rationale: Timeouts focus on the synchronous run; async scheduled work can outlive the option.

nodes.label: Wasm security is only as strong as imports
nodes.rationale: Not a security sandbox if the host exposes dangerous imports; no ambient Node fs inside the module.
nodes.norm_label: wasm security is only as strong as imports

nodes.label: Wasm vs worker_threads vs N-API
nodes.rationale: Workers solve parallelism; Wasm solves faster sandboxed compute; N-API is full native power with a build matrix.

nodes.label: module.builtinModules
nodes.rationale: Array of every built-in name. Node 24 has 72 built-ins; four names start with node:.

nodes.label: Core modules resolve before node_modules
nodes.rationale: A package named path or fs cannot hijack require('path') or require('fs'). Core wins already in both CJS and ESM.

nodes.label: node: prefix
nodes.rationale: Marks a specifier as a built-in. Node returns it immediately — no node_modules walk, no filesystem probing.

nodes.label: Prefix-only built-ins
nodes.rationale: On Node 24 four built-ins exist only as node:sea, node:sqlite, node:test, node:test/reporters. Bare names fall through to npm packages.

nodes.label: CJS vs ESM resolution
nodes.rationale: CommonJS probes .js/.json/.node and directory index.js. ESM resolves the exact URL and fails with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND or ERR_UNSUPPORTED_DIR_IMPORT.

nodes.label: Module resolution
nodes.rationale: How a string in an import becomes a file on disk. Node decides from specifier shape before anything else.

nodes.label: require.resolve
nodes.rationale: Runs the resolution algorithm and returns the filename without loading the module.

nodes.label: Three kinds of specifier
nodes.rationale: Built-in (node:fs/fs), relative/absolute path, or bare package name. Only bare specifiers search node_modules.

nodes.label: Import the .ts extension
nodes.rationale: ESM does not rewrite .js to .ts. Running .ts directly requires ./helper.ts and allowImportingTsExtensions.

nodes.label: module.isBuiltin
nodes.rationale: Whether a specifier is a built-in, prefix or not. isBuiltin('fs') and isBuiltin('node:fs') are both true.

nodes.label: Prefixed imports as bundler signal
nodes.rationale: Bundlers and edge runtimes use the prefix to tell a Node built-in from a package, producing better errors when node:fs does not exist.

nodes.label: Promise.all
nodes.rationale: Settles when all fulfil; rejects immediately on first failure. Attaches handlers to every input so later rejections are handled but silently discarded. Starts everything at once — not a concurrency limiter.

nodes.label: map plus Promise.all
nodes.rationale: Preserves input order regardless of completion. Starts every item at once — a few dozen is fine; thousands need a bounded pool.

nodes.label: Picking a concurrency limit
nodes.rationale: Derive from the bottleneck: API rate limit, pool size, or in-flight memory. Right value is where throughput stops improving. CPU-bound work is not helped by concurrency.

nodes.label: mapLimit worker pool
nodes.rationale: Exactly N workers claim the next index with next++. Single-threaded so the increment needs no lock. results[i] preserves order. First worker rejection can abandon the rest.

nodes.label: Unbounded Promise.all
nodes.rationale: Starts every item immediately. Hits 429s, pool timeouts, EMFILE, memory, then a burst of callbacks. Fine at 20 items; an outage at 10,000.

nodes.label: Async crypto on the libuv thread pool
nodes.rationale: crypto.pbkdf2, scrypt and async bcrypt run off the loop; *Sync variants block it. Often the cheapest real fix.
nodes.norm_label: async crypto on the libuv thread pool

nodes.label: worker_threads for CPU work
nodes.rationale: Real parallelism on another thread. Spawning is expensive — use a piscina pool, not one worker per request. Data copies via structured clone; transfer ArrayBuffers.

nodes.label: Chunked Promise.all vs worker pool
nodes.rationale: Each batch waits for its slowest member so one slow item idles workers. A pool keeps every worker busy. Batching is fine when items are uniform.

nodes.label: AsyncLocalStorage.run
nodes.rationale: Scopes the store to fn and its async descendants. getStore() is undefined outside any run. Prefer a fresh object per request.

nodes.label: AsyncLocalStorage
nodes.rationale: Per-request store that Node restores across await, timers and I/O. Solves request-id-in-every-log without a ctx parameter. A module-level variable is overwritten by interleaved requests.

nodes.label: executionAsyncId and triggerAsyncId
nodes.rationale: Every async operation gets an id and the id of what created it. That tree is what AsyncLocalStorage walks. Context is lost wherever the tree is broken.

nodes.label: AsyncResource.bind
nodes.rationale: Captures async context at bind time and restores it when the callback runs. Fix for EventEmitter listeners and queues that store callbacks.

nodes.label: async_hooks.createHook
nodes.rationale: Stability 1 experimental. Fires on every async operation. console.log inside a hook recurses. Exists for APM vendors. Use ALS or diagnostics_channel instead.

nodes.label: diagnostics_channel
nodes.rationale: Supported instrumentation: named channels, near-zero cost when nobody is subscribed. Prefer over createHook.

nodes.label: EventEmitter listener context loss
nodes.rationale: Listeners run in the context of emit, not registration. A listener registered inside als.run still loses the store if emit happens in a timer.

nodes.label: enterWith leaks context
nodes.rationale: Sets the store for the rest of the current async context with no visible boundary. Prefer run(). enterWith is for framework points with no callback.

nodes.label: ALS is hidden state with a cost
nodes.rationale: Use only for cross-cutting concerns (trace ids, tenant, current transaction). Pass real arguments for domain data. Async context tracking makes operations measurably slower.
nodes.norm_label: als is hidden state with a cost

nodes.label: brotli default quality 11
nodes.rationale: 75.7 s on 19 MB vs 0.78 s gzip level 6. Intended for pre-compressed static assets. Per-request brotli needs quality 4.

nodes.label: zlib on libuv thread pool
nodes.rationale: Async zlib runs on the four-thread pool shared with fs and dns.lookup. *Sync variants block the main thread for the whole duration.

nodes.label: Zip bomb maxOutputLength
nodes.rationale: A few KB of gzip can expand to gigabytes. maxOutputLength throws ERR_BUFFER_TOO_LARGE. Never decompress untrusted input without a ceiling.

nodes.label: zlib Transform streams
nodes.rationale: createGzip, createDeflate, createBrotliCompress drop into a pipeline with constant memory. Use streams for file- or response-sized data.

nodes.label: fs error codes
nodes.rationale: Branch on err.code never err.message. ENOENT, EEXIST, EACCES, EISDIR, ENOSPC, EMFILE, EXDEV. Swallowing every error hides EACCES as an empty config.

nodes.label: node:fs/promises
nodes.rationale: Default filesystem API. Every operation returns a promise, errors are ordinary exceptions with a code, nothing blocks the event loop.

nodes.label: rename atomicity
nodes.rationale: Atomic within one filesystem. EXDEV across devices — common when /tmp is a separate mount. Put the temp file in the destination directory.

nodes.label: fs on libuv thread pool
nodes.rationale: 200 async reads 45 ms with 23 timer ticks; 200 sync reads 86 ms with 0 ticks. Unbounded Promise.all still hits EMFILE.

nodes.label: writeFile truncates
nodes.rationale: writeFile overwrites an existing file. appendFile or { flag: 'a' } appends; { flag: 'wx' } fails with EEXIST if the file exists.

nodes.label: Compress in nginx or CDN
nodes.rationale: Keeps CPU off the event loop and the libuv pool. Compress in Node only for files you write, required upstreams, or no proxy.

nodes.label: readFile vs stream
nodes.rationale: readFile is correct for bounded small files. If a user controls size, stream and cap — peak RSS is file size × concurrency.

nodes.label: pipeline over pipe for streaming responses
nodes.norm_label: pipeline over pipe for streaming responses

nodes.label: Default to SSE unless the client sends often
nodes.norm_label: default to sse unless the client sends often

nodes.label: Unsupported at-rule drops whole block
nodes.rationale: Rules inside @container do not exist for an engine without container queries. Base styling must stay outside.

nodes.label: -webkit-line-clamp still required
nodes.rationale: Unprefixed line-clamp is false in Firefox 153; -webkit-line-clamp is true. Feature is Limited availability.

nodes.label: Silent discard of unknown CSS
nodes.rationale: Forward compatibility: a typo and a future feature are indistinguishable. Unknown syntax as error would prevent new CSS from shipping.

nodes.label: Cascade-safe value fallback
nodes.rationale: Declare fallback then modern value. @supports is for when the fallback needs different properties, not just a different value.

nodes.label: @supports tests parse not correctness
nodes.rationale: An engine can parse a property, apply it partially, and pass the test.

nodes.label: Progressive enhancement contract
nodes.rationale: Base outside any recent at-rule; enhancement inside; enhancement must undo the base. Delete the guard once Baseline is Widely available.

nodes.label: Local support is not shipping safety
nodes.rationale: Firefox 153 CSS.supports is true for anchor-positioning and accent-color, both Limited. It works here is how those reach production broken.
nodes.norm_label: local support is not shipping safety

nodes.label: Vendor prefixes failed as a strategy
nodes.rationale: Authors shipped -webkit- only. Browsers now ship behind flags. Firefox implements several -webkit- properties for compatibility.
nodes.norm_label: vendor prefixes failed as a strategy

nodes.label: CSS debugging order
nodes.rationale: In the DOM? Parsed? Matched ($0.matches)? Won (strike-through / Computed)? Box where expected? Steps 2 and 3 are the ones people skip.

nodes.label: Phase 0 gate parsed matched won
nodes.rationale: Move on when a rule that is not working can be diagnosed as parsed, matched, or won — without editing at random.

nodes.label: Prefer container replicas over cluster on an orchestrator
nodes.norm_label: prefer container replicas over cluster on an orchestrator

nodes.label: Close worker before resources
nodes.rationale: Closing the pool first turns every in-flight job into a connection error — graceful-looking SIGKILL. Drain timeout must sit under terminationGracePeriodSeconds.

nodes.label: node must be PID 1
nodes.rationale: CMD npm run worker or sh -c makes the shell PID 1; SIGTERM never reaches the handler. Use exec-form CMD ["node", "src/worker.js"].

nodes.label: SIGKILL leaves the job active
nodes.rationale: No error, no retry scheduled. Recovered only when the visibility timeout expires and the stall sweep redelivers from the beginning — the deploy-duplication bug.

nodes.label: SIGTERM drain via worker.close
nodes.rationale: Measured: killed 1.2s into a 3s job, await worker.close() finished in 2125 ms and completed exactly once. Stop claiming, finish in-flight, then close resources.

nodes.label: One AbortSignal threaded through
nodes.rationale: When the client leaves, the work they started should stop. Measured: one abort() cancelled three children and signal.reason carried 'client disconnected'.

nodes.label: Exponential backoff with cap
nodes.rationale: min(cap, base * 2^(attempt-1)). Uncapped doubling from 100 ms is 200 seconds by attempt 12. Cap delay and attempt count.

nodes.label: Full jitter
nodes.rationale: random(0, backoff). AWS full-jitter default. Equal jitter when a minimum spacing is required. Decorrelated for long-running pollers.

nodes.label: Thundering herd of synchronised retries
nodes.rationale: 500 clients, no jitter: all 500 in one 100 ms bucket at 700 ms. Full jitter: busiest bucket 122. Failures are correlated; deterministic schedules stay correlated.

nodes.label: Propagation stops at the queue
nodes.rationale: A cancelled request must not cancel a job it already enqueued — the work still needs doing. Also stop before anything already committed.

nodes.label: npm 12 allowScripts
nodes.rationale: Install scripts blocked unless allowlisted. An approved postinstall read 103 env vars. Yarn uses enableScripts; npm ci --ignore-scripts is belt-and-braces.

nodes.label: Lockfile integrity
nodes.rationale: npm ci, never npm install, in CI. Integrity hashes produce EINTEGRITY on a swapped tarball. Review lockfile diffs for packages with no package.json change.

nodes.label: Release cooldown min-release-age
nodes.rationale: Most malicious versions are unpublished in days. npm min-release-age / yarn npmMinimalAgeGate of 7–14 days. ENOVERSIONS rather than a quiet newer install.

nodes.label: npm audit limits
nodes.rationale: Matches known disclosed advisories only. Misses a package compromised today; reports build-only ReDoS. Pair --audit-level=high with signatures and a cooldown.

nodes.label: npm provenance attestations
nodes.rationale: Registry signatures say the registry served what it recorded. Provenance is Sigstore SLSA that a CI workflow built this commit. Signal, not a gate (3 of 11 here).

nodes.label: npm supply-chain threat
nodes.rationale: Dependency minimisation is the only defence that scales. Node stdlib absorbed fetch, --env-file, node:test, parseArgs, randomUUID, structuredClone, glob.

nodes.label: --allow-child-process escape
nodes.rationale: The child is a new process with no permission model. Granting it discards every other restriction. Same for --allow-addons / process.dlopen.

nodes.label: No --allow-net on Node 24
nodes.rationale: --allow-net is a bad option. A process with only --allow-fs-read still opened TCP. process.permission.has('net') is false for any unrecognised scope. Cannot contain SSRF.

nodes.label: Node Permission Model
nodes.rationale: --permission denies all; grant fs-read/write, child-process, worker, addons, wasi, inspector. No runtime re-grant API. Policy lives only on the command line.

nodes.label: Supply chain
nodes.rationale: Installed code runs at install and at runtime with your env. Verified Node 24.19.0 / npm 12.0.2 / yarn 4.18.

nodes.label: The Permission Model
nodes.rationale: In-process sandbox from the CLI. Blast-radius reduction against chosen dependencies, not a sandbox for untrusted code.

nodes.label: Cluster
nodes.rationale: One data directory / one running server instance. You do not switch cluster without a new connection target.

nodes.label: Database
nodes.rationale: Named catalog inside the cluster; a connection picks exactly one. Stronger isolation than schemas, but no ordinary cross-database joins without FDW.

nodes.label: Four-level namespace
nodes.rationale: cluster → database → schema → relation. Confusing any two levels is the root of relation does not exist bugs and multi-tenant layout mistakes.

nodes.label: Schema
nodes.rationale: Namespace inside one database (public, app, billing). Not a separate database. Default landing place is public.

nodes.label: search_path
nodes.rationale: Schemas checked for unqualified names, in order. Measured default "$user", public. Session state, changeable with SET search_path; attacker-influenced path is a later least-privilege topic.

nodes.label: Identifier case folding
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL down-cases unquoted identifiers (createdAt → createdat). Quoted MixedCol keeps case forever. MySQL and SQLite preserve what you typed. Corpus convention is snake_case.

nodes.label: postgres database
nodes.rationale: Ordinary DB created for admin connections; not magic beyond convention. Not a template (datistemplate false).

nodes.label: psql name patterns
nodes.rationale: Use * and ?, not SQL % and _. Unquoted names fold to lower. \dt *.* lists every table in every schema.

nodes.label: \c reconnect
nodes.rationale: Connects to another database or user. Discards SET, temp tables, prepared statements, and any open transaction.

nodes.label: Qualify names in migrations
nodes.rationale: Always write app.users, not bare users, so a path change cannot silently hit another table.

nodes.label: Phase 0 gate
nodes.rationale: Move on when you can explain why a Node process must pool connections, name the four namespace levels, and open psql into the container without guessing the port.

nodes.label: Dump formats and what is in them
nodes.norm_label: dump formats and what is in them

nodes.label: effective_cache_size allocates nothing
nodes.rationale: Planner hint for shared buffers plus OS page cache. Higher makes index scans look cheaper. Default 4 GB on a large server biases sequential scans.

nodes.label: random_page_cost = 4 models spinning disk
nodes.rationale: On SSD/NVMe use 1.1. Leaving 4.0 over-costs index scans so the planner ignores indexes. Highest-value one-line change; test with EXPLAIN first.

nodes.label: ALTER SYSTEM vs postgresql.conf
nodes.rationale: Writes postgresql.auto.conf, read after postgresql.conf and overrides it. RESET undoes. Reload is refused on syntax error; restart with a bad file fails to start.

nodes.label: pg_settings.context
nodes.rationale: postmaster=restart (shared_buffers, max_connections); sighup=reload (ssl, random_page_cost); user/superuser=SET. pending_restart shows staged changes. Measured PG 18.4.

nodes.label: Setting precedence order
nodes.rationale: postgresql.conf → auto.conf → ALTER DATABASE → ALTER ROLE → SET → SET LOCAL. Narrowest scope wins.

nodes.label: logging_collector
nodes.rationale: Captures stderr into rotating files. Requires a restart. In containers, stderr to the container log is often preferred.

nodes.label: Extension allowlist
nodes.rationale: CREATE EXTENSION only for vetted extensions. pg_stat_statements is usually already in shared_preload_libraries. Check niche extensions before designing around them.

nodes.label: Managed role is not SUPERUSER
nodes.rationale: RDS gives rds_superuser, not PostgreSQL superuser. No postgresql.conf, pg_hba, often no ALTER SYSTEM, no arbitrary extensions, no server-side COPY from a path.

nodes.label: Parameter groups replace config files
nodes.rationale: Default RDS parameter group cannot be edited. Custom group + attach; static vs dynamic is the same restart/reload distinction as pg_settings.context.

nodes.label: Key configuration
nodes.rationale: Reason about what a managed provider already set. Four facts: work_mem per operation, effective_cache_size allocates nothing, random_page_cost=4 models spinning disk, context tells restart vs reload.

nodes.label: Tuning start order for PERN
nodes.rationale: 1 random_page_cost 1.1, 2 effective_cache_size ~75% RAM, 3 timeouts per role, 4 work_mem with spill evidence, 5 max_wal_size, 6 shared_buffers last (restart).

nodes.label: RLS default-deny empty table
nodes.rationale: ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY with no policy: queries succeed and return zero rows. Not an error.

nodes.label: FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY
nodes.rationale: Makes the owner subject to policies. Real fix is connecting as a non-owner. Verify relrowsecurity and relforcerowsecurity.

nodes.label: Table owners bypass RLS by default
nodes.rationale: Superusers, BYPASSRLS, and table owners skip policies. Connecting as schema owner makes RLS a no-op and tests pass while proving nothing.
nodes.norm_label: table owners bypass rls by default

nodes.label: Permissive OR restrictive AND
nodes.rationale: PERMISSIVE grants (OR); RESTRICTIVE constrains (AND) and grants nothing alone. Tenant isolation is the canonical restrictive policy.

nodes.label: USING versus WITH CHECK
nodes.rationale: USING filters existing rows; WITH CHECK validates the row after a write. UPDATE needs both or a user can reassign owner_id. USING alone is copied into WITH CHECK.

nodes.label: BYPASSRLS job role
nodes.rationale: Exactly one unfiltered role, named for that purpose; the application must not use it. Implicit owner bypass hides unrestricted access.

nodes.label: Index policy predicate columns
nodes.rationale: A policy is a silent predicate on every query. Tenant tables want (tenant_id, …) leading indexes. Confirm with EXPLAIN.

nodes.label: RLS leakproofness limit
nodes.rationale: Strong on rows returned, weaker on inference. Non-leakproof user predicates may not be pushed below the barrier. SECURITY DEFINER is the common practical hole.

nodes.label: Test RLS as the application role
nodes.rationale: Owner-run tests always pass. Assert negatives: other tenant 0 rows, cross-tenant INSERT/UPDATE rejected, missing context empty or error.
nodes.norm_label: test rls as the application role

nodes.label: Row-level security
nodes.rationale: Authorization that cannot be forgotten. Know tier generally; Master on Supabase where it is the entire authorization model.

nodes.label: Filter in the app and enable RLS underneath
nodes.rationale: App WHERE is clearer and faster; RLS converts a forgotten tenant_id into an empty result and covers psql. On Supabase, RLS is the whole mechanism.
nodes.norm_label: filter in the app and enable rls underneath

nodes.label: Managed provider restore duties
nodes.rationale: Choose retention against how long a corrupting bug might go unnoticed. Keep logical dumps for per-table recovery. Snapshot restore usually yields a new endpoint. The provider guarantees the backup exists, not that you can use it.

nodes.label: Point-in-time recovery
nodes.rationale: Stop the server, move the old data directory aside, restore the base backup, set restore_command and a recovery_target_*, touch recovery.signal, then start. The target must be after the end of the base backup.

nodes.label: Oldest recoverable point is backup end
nodes.rationale: The recovery target must be after the end of the base backup. You cannot recover into a backup that was still in progress. Base backup frequency sets the recovery floor.
nodes.norm_label: oldest recoverable point is backup end

nodes.label: recovery.signal versus standby.signal
nodes.rationale: recovery.signal performs recovery then becomes a normal read-write server. standby.signal keeps the server in continuous recovery as a replica.

nodes.label: recovery_target_action pause default
nodes.rationale: Default pause stops recovery so you can connect and confirm the landing point before promoting. Immediate promote forecloses a retry. Combined with timelines, a wrong attempt can be repeated.

nodes.label: Recovery point objective
nodes.rationale: How much data may we lose. Set by archive frequency, archive_timeout, and replication mode. Continuous archiving: last archived WAL segment (seconds to minutes). Nightly pg_dump: up to 24 hours.

nodes.label: Recovery time objective
nodes.rationale: How long may we be down. Set by backup size, restore speed, and whether anyone has practised. A restore never timed is a hope, not a plan.

nodes.label: PostgreSQL timelines
nodes.rationale: When recovery completes, PostgreSQL starts a new timeline so post-recovery WAL does not overwrite original history. recovery_target_timeline (default latest) selects which branch to follow. A wrong PITR is not fatal.

nodes.label: Failing archive_command is an outage
nodes.rationale: WAL that cannot be archived is retained until the disk fills. Alert on pg_stat_archiver.failed_count.

nodes.label: Physical backup and PITR
nodes.rationale: Base backup plus every WAL record since equals the ability to land on any second. The base backup need not be filesystem-consistent because log replay repairs it, the same mechanism as crash recovery. A managed provider runs this, but RPO and RTO remain product decisions.

nodes.label: PITR trades procedure for precision
nodes.rationale: A logical restore is one command; PITR is a stopped server, restored directory, configured target, signal file, and verification. All value is contingent on rehearsal.

nodes.label: Natural key
nodes.rationale: Right for immutable reference data (ISO 4217). Needing ON UPDATE CASCADE is the signal the key is mutable and wrong.

nodes.label: Surrogate key
nodes.rationale: Settles identity, not uniqueness. A users table with id and no UNIQUE(email) accumulates duplicate accounts.

nodes.label: ALTER TABLE
nodes.rationale: Every ALTER takes ACCESS EXCLUSIVE. Catalog-only is milliseconds; a rewrite is linear in row count. Both block every reader and writer.

nodes.label: CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY
nodes.rationale: 25001 cannot run inside a transaction. VACUUM and CREATE/DROP DATABASE also cannot. A failed CONCURRENTLY build leaves an INVALID index.

nodes.label: INVALID concurrent index
nodes.rationale: Ignored by the planner and still maintained on every write. Find with pg_index WHERE NOT indisvalid, then drop and rebuild.

nodes.label: UNIQUE constraint vs unique index
nodes.rationale: Same btree. FK can only target a constraint. Only an index can be partial, on an expression, or built CONCURRENTLY.

nodes.label: Partial unique index
nodes.rationale: CREATE UNIQUE INDEX … WHERE deleted_at IS NULL allows re-registration after soft delete. Constraints cannot be partial.

nodes.label: Deferred unique column swap
nodes.rationale: Swapping unique positions collides mid-statement (23505). Needs a deferrable constraint, not a bare unique index.

nodes.label: Uniqueness is per tenant
nodes.rationale: UNIQUE (tenant_id, slug). A global unique slug is unintended cross-tenant coupling. tenant_id is NOT NULL with an FK.

nodes.label: Batch ALTER subcommands
nodes.rationale: One statement is one lock acquisition and at most one rewrite pass covering all sub-commands.

nodes.label: Rename before drop
nodes.rationale: Two deploys: stop referencing, rename to _deprecated_DATE (42703 for stragglers), drop later. Dropping makes data unreachable immediately.

nodes.label: agg_events 500000-row table
nodes.rationale: 5000 users, 4 kinds, 40 MB / 3783 heap pages, 71428 NULL amounts. Used for every timing in chunk 05 and later performance pages.

nodes.label: Aggregation fixture
nodes.rationale: Six orders, five customers, five items. Eve has no orders; order 15 has NULL total; coupon is NULL on three orders; cancelled total is 0 not NULL.

nodes.label: Collapsing rows
nodes.rationale: An aggregate takes many values and returns one. GROUP BY decides which values go into each many. Every aggregate except count(*) skips NULL inputs.

nodes.label: Empty groups and grouping keys
nodes.rationale: Two things decide result shape: one row vs zero over an empty selection, and what the grouping key does with NULLs and expressions.

nodes.label: What you are allowed to select
nodes.rationale: Every expression must reduce to one value per group. PostgreSQL refuses to guess; the error is 42803, the most-seen SQL error in this phase.
nodes.norm_label: what you are allowed to select

nodes.label: Ordinals, aliases and DISTINCT
nodes.rationale: Where 1 and an output alias are legal, and why GROUP BY x with no aggregate is SELECT DISTINCT x, all fall out of evaluation order.

nodes.label: How GROUP BY executes
nodes.rationale: Two strategies: hash table or sort-and-walk. Same query over 500000 rows was 59 ms or 118 ms depending on work_mem.

nodes.label: GROUP BY and aggregates
nodes.rationale: GROUP BY emits one row per group. Every select-list column must be a grouping key or an aggregate. Most bugs satisfy that rule in letter and violate it in spirit.

nodes.label: count variants
nodes.rationale: count(*), count(col) and count(DISTINCT col) return 6, 5 and 2 over the same six rows. The wrong one is never a syntax error.

nodes.label: Independent fixture columns
nodes.rationale: kind from g/5000 not g%4. With user_id = g%5000, g%4 is determined by user_id when 4 divides 5000, so every user has one kind. Two moduli that share a factor are not independent.

nodes.label: FOR UPDATE
nodes.rationale: Strongest row lock; held until the transaction ends. Transaction length is blocking length. Lock only rows you will write, in a deterministic order.

nodes.label: lock_timeout
nodes.rationale: Bounds only the wait for a lock (55P03). Prefer SET LOCAL so it does not leak on a pooled connection — pg does not reset session state on release().

nodes.label: Row locks live in the tuple header
nodes.norm_label: row locks live in the tuple header

nodes.label: FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED
nodes.rationale: Omits locked rows instead of waiting. 8 workers, 200 jobs: 168.6 ms, 0 duplicates, all 8 busy. Plain FOR UPDATE 499 ms and only 3 workers; no lock 593 duplicates.

nodes.label: DDL lock queue convoy
nodes.rationale: A waiting ACCESS EXCLUSIVE ALTER queues every later query, even SELECTs compatible with the current holder. How a 2 ms ADD COLUMN takes a site down.

nodes.label: lock_timeout on migrations
nodes.rationale: Fail with 55P03 after a few seconds and retry, instead of queuing the pool empty.

nodes.label: Metadata-only vs table-rewrite DDL
nodes.rationale: Constant DEFAULT is metadata since PG11 (2.0 ms). Volatile default or non-binary-coercible type rewrite (319–345 ms on 200000 rows).

nodes.label: ADD CONSTRAINT NOT VALID then VALIDATE
nodes.norm_label: add constraint not valid then validate

nodes.label: Deadlock
nodes.rationale: Two transactions each hold what the other needs. Detected after deadlock_timeout (1 s), one aborted with 40P01. Opposite lock order 1155 ms; same order both committed in 326.2 ms.

nodes.label: Consistent lock order
nodes.rationale: ORDER BY id FOR UPDATE in every path. Sorting an array passed to ANY() does nothing — lock order is plan order unless a locking SELECT has ORDER BY.

nodes.label: Advisory lock
nodes.rationale: A named mutex keyed by a number, not a row. The database enforces the lock, not the invariant. Visible in pg_locks as locktype=advisory.

nodes.label: release(held) after session advisory lock
nodes.rationale: If unlock fails, destroy the pooled connection. A leaked session lock makes every later runIfLeader return false for the process lifetime.

nodes.label: Session vs transaction advisory locks
nodes.rationale: Prefer pg_advisory_xact_lock: released at COMMIT/ROLLBACK and cannot leak. Session locks survive COMMIT and return to the pool still held.

nodes.label: SKIP LOCKED and the job queue
nodes.norm_label: skip locked and the job queue

nodes.label: ANY($1::int[])
nodes.rationale: One parameter for a variable-length list. Statement text stays constant for the plan cache. Sidesteps NOT IN null trap and the 65535-parameter ceiling.

nodes.label: 65535 parameter ceiling
nodes.rationale: 21845 rows ok (65535 params); 21846 rows → 08P01 bind message has 2 parameter formats but 0 parameters. Fix with unnest or chunk. Parameterized calls also reject multi-statement text (42601).

nodes.label: pool.query
nodes.rationale: query(text), query(text, values), query(configObject). Object form needed for name, rowMode, types. All return the same Result. Callback form exists; do not use it in new code.

nodes.label: Positional $n placeholders
nodes.rationale: $1 is values[0], 1-based, may repeat. Numbering must be contiguous; extra values are silently ignored. Wire-protocol $n unchanged. Renumbering is the failure mode — build fragments and the array together.

nodes.label: Result.fields
nodes.rationale: Column metadata: name and dataTypeID (OID). 20=int8, 25=text, 23=int4. Present even when zero rows. Driver uses OID to choose a parser — why int8 arrives as a string.

nodes.label: pg Result object
nodes.rationale: Public fields: rows, rowCount, command, fields, oid. Underscore fields are internal. Multi-statement without params resolves to an array of Results, so result.rows is undefined.

nodes.label: rowCount
nodes.rationale: Rows the statement acted on, not rows.length. UPDATE without RETURNING: rowCount 1, rows []. DDL: rowCount null, not 0 — if (!rowCount) treats CREATE as failure. MERGE sums inserts, updates and deletes.

nodes.label: rowMode: array
nodes.rationale: Rows as positional arrays. Preserves duplicate names, suits CSV, skips object construction on large results. Cost is position-dependent code.

nodes.label: Identifiers are not parameters
nodes.rationale: ORDER BY $1 sorts every row by the same constant string and raises no error. Column names, table names and sort direction need an allowlist.

nodes.label: undefined becomes SQL NULL
nodes.rationale: null and undefined both become SQL NULL with no error. A misspelled property inserts NULL. Validate the object before building the array.

nodes.label: SELECT * duplicate column collapse
nodes.rationale: Joined SELECT * can return four columns in fields and two keys in the row object. Last name wins, no error. Alias columns or use rowMode array.

nodes.label: Pooled connection leak
nodes.rationale: A thrown query before release() loses the client for process lifetime. After max leaks, later requests hang until connectionTimeoutMillis.

nodes.label: DISCARD ALL before release
nodes.rationale: release() keeps search_path, temp tables, and prepared statements. DISCARD ALL resets them but cannot run inside a transaction.

nodes.label: pool.connect and release
nodes.rationale: Checkout is yours until release(). A missed release never returns the connection. release() does not close, roll back, or reset session state.

nodes.label: Pool total idle waiting counters
nodes.rationale: totalCount, idleCount, waitingCount. A request past max waits rather than errors. Sustained waitingCount > 0 is the leak or undersize signal.

nodes.label: Custom vs generic plan after five executions
nodes.rationale: First five executions use custom plans with real values. From the sixth PostgreSQL may switch to a generic plan, which is wrong on skewed data.
nodes.norm_label: custom vs generic plan after five executions

nodes.label: Named prepared statements
nodes.rationale: query({name}) issues server PREPARE. First call Parse; later Bind/Execute. Measured 1.6x on a hot single-row lookup.

nodes.label: Prepared statements are per session
nodes.rationale: A name prepared on one backend is invisible to another. A pool of N prepares up to N times. Names must be a small fixed unique set.

nodes.label: PgBouncer breaks named statements
nodes.rationale: Transaction or statement pooling routes consecutive queries to different backends. Symptom: 26000 prepared statement does not exist.

nodes.label: plan_cache_mode
nodes.rationale: force_custom_plan always plans with values; force_generic_plan never replans; auto is default. Use force_custom_plan on skewed tables.

nodes.label: connectionTimeoutMillis
nodes.rationale: Give up acquiring a connection, including waiting for a free pooled one. Fires when a leak saturates the pool.

nodes.label: withClient helper
nodes.rationale: Never write checkout by hand. connect, run fn(client), release in finally so every path returns the client.

nodes.label: release(true) destroys the connection
nodes.rationale: Truthy release discards the socket. Use after FATAL, client-side query_timeout, or unknown session state so one bad request cannot poison later borrows.

nodes.label: query_timeout
nodes.rationale: Client-side: pg rejects while the server keeps executing. Use with statement_timeout set slightly lower. release(true) afterwards.

nodes.label: statement_timeout
nodes.rationale: Server-side cancel. Raises 57014; connection stays usable. The only timeout that stops the database doing work. Prefer ALTER ROLE.

nodes.label: Module-scope pool keeps the event loop alive
nodes.rationale: An open socket keeps Node running. Tests hang after results; scripts never exit. await pool.end() in teardown or finally.
nodes.norm_label: module-scope pool keeps the event loop alive

nodes.label: pool.end
nodes.rationale: Waits for in-flight queries, closes every connection, permanently retires the pool. Second end() throws. Queries after end reject.

nodes.label: postgres.js
nodes.rationale: Tagged templates replace $1. Result is the array. Built-in pool, sql.begin, sql.listen, cursors. Smaller ecosystem than pg.

nodes.label: Interpolation is parameterization
nodes.rationale: ${} inside the tag is a bind parameter, never SQL text. Identifiers need sql(name) and still an allowlist.

nodes.label: Phase 7 — The pg driver, end to end
nodes.rationale: Target PostgreSQL 18.4, Node 24, pg. Gate: open a pool, parameterize queries, map 23505, and never leak clients.
nodes.norm_label: phase 7 — the pg driver, end to end

nodes.label: One statement per call
nodes.rationale: Default everywhere except schema files. Buys parameters, attributable errors, and a consistent Result. Use a CTE, not concatenated statements.

nodes.label: HTTP close then pool.end
nodes.rationale: server.close first, drain in-flight requests, then pool.end. Reverse order turns every deploy into a burst of 500s.

nodes.label: Choose pg unless greenfield ESM
nodes.rationale: Most tooling expects a pg Pool. Migrating every query for API polish is rarely worth it. Neither driver changes schema, indexes, or plans.

nodes.label: Boot-time schema check
nodes.rationale: Compare expected columns against information_schema at boot and process.exit(1). A container that will not start is rollback-able; a running container serving 500s is not.

nodes.label: Generate expected schema in CI
nodes.rationale: A hand-maintained EXPECTED object drifts. Generate after migrations and commit, or diff a scratch migrated catalog against production.

nodes.label: information_schema type flattening
nodes.rationale: data_type reports numeric for every numeric(p,s), varchar as character varying, identity column_default as null. Privilege-filtered views can hide existing columns.

nodes.label: db:check CI type diff
nodes.rationale: Regenerate types and git diff --exit-code so drift fails the merge, not the deploy.

nodes.label: Creating tables from Node
nodes.rationale: pg will run CREATE TABLE. The question is when: from a replayable migration, never from a request handler or application startup.

nodes.label: Generating TypeScript types from the schema
nodes.norm_label: generating typescript types from the schema

nodes.label: Phase 8 Schema and data from Node
nodes.norm_label: phase 8 schema and data from node

nodes.label: Schema drift
nodes.rationale: Live schema no longer matches what the code assumes. With migrations it still happens via manual psql fixes, env-only applies, restored backups, ORM sync, or rolled-back deploys. Failure surfaces later as 42703.

nodes.label: Generated TypeScript types
nodes.rationale: A hand-written interface is a guess. Types plus a boot check cover different moments; types are not runtime validation.

nodes.label: Introspect live database for types
nodes.rationale: drizzle-kit pull, kanel. Migrations stay source of truth; types are a committed build artefact.

nodes.label: pg default JS type mappings
nodes.rationale: bigint and numeric return as strings; timestamptz and date return Date. Generated id: number for bigint is wrong; user.id + 1 becomes '11'.

nodes.label: pool.query generic is an assertion
nodes.rationale: pg does not validate rows against User. A dropped or renamed column still compiles.

nodes.label: Query-level type inference
nodes.rationale: pgtyped types the actual SELECT projection. Table-level types still let user.name compile after SELECT id, email.

nodes.label: Malformed bigint id is 400
nodes.rationale: GET /users/abc raises 22P02. Validate at the edge; map SQLSTATE as a backstop.

nodes.label: Missing row is a successful empty result
nodes.rationale: rowCount 0, rows [], no throw. Any 404 is application-added.
nodes.norm_label: missing row is a successful empty result

nodes.label: Do not return undefined
nodes.rationale: JSON.stringify drops undefined keys. rows[0] ?? null keeps the response shape.

nodes.label: numeric through jsonb becomes number
nodes.rationale: Column path keeps '11.00' string; jsonb path yields JS number 11. jsonb also reorders keys.

nodes.label: findX null vs getX throw
nodes.rationale: Return null when absence is expected; throw when the caller cannot continue. Names at the call site document the choice.

nodes.label: BEGIN is a statement on a connection
nodes.rationale: A transaction is a property of one connection. connect() before BEGIN; every statement inside uses that client.
nodes.norm_label: begin is a statement on a connection

nodes.label: pool.query('BEGIN') is not a transaction
nodes.rationale: Each pool.query is a separate checkout. Idle-pool tests reuse one pid and pass. With 8 concurrent inserts, 7 survived ROLLBACK. No error is raised.

nodes.label: try COMMIT catch ROLLBACK finally release
nodes.rationale: Swallowing the error turns a failed request into a silent 200. release() outside finally leaks a connection per failed request.
nodes.norm_label: try commit catch rollback finally release

nodes.label: withTransaction wrapper
nodes.rationale: One place that knows connect/BEGIN/fn(client)/COMMIT/ROLLBACK/release. A handler cannot forget finally.

nodes.label: 25P02 current transaction is aborted
nodes.rationale: After the first error the transaction is dead. SELECT 1 was refused after 22012. Accepts only ROLLBACK, COMMIT (as rollback), or ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT.

nodes.label: COMMIT on an aborted transaction reports success
nodes.rationale: It rolls back and does not raise. Catch-log-commit produces HTTP 200 with nothing written.
nodes.norm_label: commit on an aborted transaction reports success

nodes.label: SAVEPOINT for an optional step
nodes.rationale: ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT rewinds to the savepoint, not the failing statement, and clears aborted state. Place it immediately before the group that belongs together.

nodes.label: Savepoint-per-row overflows the 64-XID cache
nodes.rationale: Each writing subtransaction gets an XID. Thousands of savepoints push lookups to disk and degrade every backend. Batch instead of a savepoint per row.

nodes.label: Transactions in a request
nodes.rationale: Hold one connection for the request and give it back exactly once. Get the wrapper right and everything inside composes.

nodes.label: db as first parameter
nodes.rationale: The same function runs standalone on a Pool or inside a transaction on a Client without knowing which. Pool and Client are interchangeable at the query API.

nodes.label: ROLLBACK catch must not replace the original error
nodes.rationale: If ROLLBACK throws (broken connection), wrap it and rethrow the original. Logs otherwise describe cleanup instead of the business failure.
nodes.norm_label: rollback catch must not replace the original error

nodes.label: Lost update across requests
nodes.rationale: Two concurrent read-modify-writes both reported ok and left 120 instead of 130. No transaction can span GET then later PUT.

nodes.label: rowCount 0 is 404 or 409
nodes.rationale: Missing row and stale version both yield rowCount 0. Re-read or a data-modifying CTE distinguishes them.

nodes.label: Version column guard
nodes.rationale: UPDATE ... SET version = version + 1 WHERE version = $n. Increment must be in the same statement. updated_at fails when two updates share now().

nodes.label: Lock rows in deterministic order
nodes.rationale: Opposite lock orders deadlock with 40P01. ORDER BY id FOR UPDATE. FOR UPDATE OF table restricts which join rows lock.

nodes.label: SELECT ... FOR UPDATE
nodes.rationale: Locks writers until commit. Meaningless without BEGIN because autocommit releases immediately. Readers still see the old MVCC version.

nodes.label: Committed test suite
nodes.rationale: Deferred constraints, LISTEN/NOTIFY, and two-connection lock tests need real COMMIT and TRUNCATE cleanup.

nodes.label: Per-test transaction rollback
nodes.rationale: 1.66 ms vs 42.50 ms truncate+reseed with 2000 seed rows. Parallel-safe because nothing commits.

nodes.label: BEGIN/COMMIT remapped to savepoints
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL has no nested transactions. Inner COMMIT ends the test transaction. Map to SAVEPOINT / RELEASE / ROLLBACK TO.

nodes.label: Sequences are not transactional
nodes.rationale: Rolled-back insert still consumes an id. Never assert on a literal id.

nodes.label: Retry only recomputable operations
