nodes.rationale: Retry add-N. Do not retry an absolute assignment the user made against stale data — that is a 409.

nodes.label: Do slow work then lock last
nodes.rationale: Eight requests × 100 ms: 863 ms with work inside the lock, 143 ms with lock taken only to write. Re-read the locked row before acting.
nodes.norm_label: do slow work then lock last

nodes.label: Iterables as children
nodes.rationale: Set renders. Map yields key/value pairs and is warned. A generator is consumed by render, so StrictMode blanks it on the second pass.

nodes.label: Objects are not valid as a React child
nodes.rationale: Plain objects and Date throw. Production is Minified React error #31 with args[] naming the shape.
nodes.norm_label: objects are not valid as a react child

nodes.label: Promise child suspends
nodes.rationale: React 19 unwraps a promise only under Suspense. Without a boundary the root withholds its commit — no DOM, no error.

nodes.label: Renderable child types
nodes.rationale: React renders strings, numbers, bigints, elements, and iterables of those (arrays, Set, Map, generators).

nodes.label: Returning undefined throws
nodes.rationale: Nothing was returned from render. Return null to render nothing on purpose. Missing return or JSX after return is the usual cause.

nodes.label: Reset a subtree with key
nodes.rationale: Do not fake a remount with a conditional. <ProfileForm key={userId} /> is the deliberate reset.

nodes.label: key inside a spread is warned
nodes.rationale: key compiles to a separate argument, so a spread key is pulled out at runtime. Pass key directly.
nodes.norm_label: key inside a spread is warned

nodes.label: Uncontrolled-to-controlled warning
nodes.rationale: value was undefined then defined — usually a fetch. Fix with ?? '' or do not render the form until data exists.

nodes.label: createPortal
nodes.rationale: createPortal(children, domNode, key?). Called in the return position. The node must already exist. Not a component or a hook.

nodes.label: A key is an identity, not an index
nodes.rationale: Answers which sibling from last render this is. Scoped to siblings, not a prop, stringified, compared before position.
nodes.norm_label: a key is an identity, not an index

nodes.label: Four host-prop outcomes
nodes.rationale: A JSX prop on a host element is renamed, passed through, dropped, or — in React 19 — class/for accepted with a warning.

nodes.label: Mutating array methods on props
nodes.rationale: sort, reverse, splice, push and friends mutate in place. sort is the trap because it reads like a query. Use toSorted / a copy.

nodes.label: Mutating a prop appears to work
nodes.rationale: Breaks later: parent refresh drops the field, a sibling reads undefined, memo skips the mutating render, StrictMode doubles, concurrent abandon leaves the write.
nodes.norm_label: mutating a prop appears to work

nodes.label: Reassigning a destructured prop is legal
nodes.rationale: Changes only a local binding. The violation is a write through the prop to the object it points at.
nodes.norm_label: reassigning a destructured prop is legal

nodes.label: Compound components via context
nodes.rationale: Parent provides shared state; caller arranges parts freely. Context beats cloneElement because it ignores intervening structure.

nodes.label: react.dev Passing Props to a Component
nodes.norm_label: react.dev passing props to a component

nodes.label: Prop vs attribute
nodes.rationale: A prop is a JSX object key. An attribute is what lands in the DOM. Host elements are mapped; custom components are not.

nodes.label: Props are immutable by contract, not enforcement
nodes.rationale: React does not freeze props or the objects they reference. Each render builds a fresh props object; a mutation is discarded on the next parent render.
nodes.norm_label: props are immutable by contract, not enforcement

nodes.label: One-way data flow
nodes.rationale: Props down, events up. Only the owner can change a value, so debugging walks up to the useState. Mutation destroys that guarantee.

nodes.label: Capital letter is a JSX compilation rule
nodes.rationale: Lowercase compiles to a string tag, so React creates an unknown DOM element and the function never runs.
nodes.norm_label: capital letter is a jsx compilation rule

nodes.label: key for deliberate remount
nodes.rationale: A changed key is treated as a different position. Reset forms with key={record.id}, not by swapping types.

nodes.label: Type change remount cost
nodes.rationale: State, refs, effects, DOM, focus, scroll, animations and uncontrolled inputs are all destroyed and recreated.

nodes.label: What makes a function a component
nodes.norm_label: what makes a function a component

nodes.label: Component identity and the nesting rule
nodes.norm_label: component identity and the nesting rule

nodes.label: React calls the component not you
nodes.rationale: A helper is a function you call. Ownership of the call is what lets React attach state, effects, position and identity.
nodes.norm_label: react calls the component not you

nodes.label: Nesting rule
nodes.rationale: Reconciliation compares type by Object.is. A new function each render is a different component, so the subtree remounts. Never nest definitions.

nodes.label: in operator narrowing
nodes.rationale: When two object types differ by which properties they have and there is no discriminant or constructor, in is the only built-in narrowing left. It costs clarity: the check names a property rather than a variant, so a rename silently changes which branch runs.

nodes.label: k in obj narrows obj never k
nodes.rationale: A common misreading: k in obj narrows the object, never the key. Narrow the key with a type predicate returning k is keyof T.
nodes.norm_label: k in obj narrows obj never k

nodes.label: Optional properties break in narrowing
nodes.rationale: in narrows on declared properties. If the distinguishing property is optional, a value of that type may lack it at runtime, so the else branch stays a union.

nodes.label: in walks the prototype chain
nodes.rationale: in checks the prototype chain, so 'toString' in {} is true. Object.hasOwn is the safer runtime check for untrusted data even though it does not narrow.

nodes.label: instanceof narrowing
nodes.rationale: instanceof is precise, needs no helper, and narrows unknown in one step inside a single application. It is nominal, so it breaks across realms and duplicate package copies, and cannot see plain object types.

nodes.label: instanceof fails across realms
nodes.rationale: A value from an iframe, vm context, worker, or a duplicate package copy has a different constructor identity, so instanceof Error is false.

nodes.label: Structural isError predicate
nodes.rationale: typeof e === 'object' && e !== null && 'message' in e && 'stack' in e survives realm and duplicate-package boundaries. Node also provides util.types.isNativeError.

nodes.label: instanceof on unknown catch
nodes.rationale: catch (err) is unknown under strict. Check most-specific class first, then Error, then stringify non-Error throws — JavaScript can throw anything.

nodes.label: Discriminated union
nodes.rationale: One literal-typed property shared by every member lets the compiler tell variants apart from ===. Highest-value pattern: illegal states become unrepresentable and exhaustiveness checking becomes possible. Costs a property on every member and more verbose construction.

nodes.label: Literal-typed discriminant
nodes.rationale: A discriminant widened to string matches every member, so nothing is eliminated. Validate at the boundary so the validator produces the literal type.

nodes.label: Result ok discriminated union
nodes.rationale: { ok: true; data: T } | { ok: false; error: Error } — one check gives a fully-typed branch either way, and there is no state where both data and error exist.

nodes.label: assertNever
nodes.rationale: A helper whose parameter is never: compile-time error when a variant is added, and a runtime throw if unvalidated data carries an impossible variant. Types are erased; the throw is the only runtime protection.

nodes.label: Exhaustiveness with never
nodes.rationale: Handle every variant and the residual type becomes never. Miss one and the error names it. Turns adding a status from a bug hunt into a compile error at every site that must change.

nodes.label: Record union exhaustive map
nodes.rationale: Record<Union, T> for value lookups is exhaustive by construction — a missing key is TS2739 at the table, with no helper. Prefer this for pure lookups; switch when branches do work.

nodes.label: isDefined filter guard
nodes.rationale: filter(v => v != null) keeps (T | null)[] because the arrow is not a type predicate. A named isDefined<T>(v): v is T lets filter narrow to T[].

nodes.label: isKeyOf type predicate
nodes.rationale: The only way to convince the compiler a string is a valid key: k is keyof T. The in operator narrows the object, never the key.

nodes.label: Type predicate
nodes.rationale: A return type of the form x is T lets narrowing survive a function call. A plain boolean return narrows nothing. Reuses one check everywhere and works with filter/find, but the compiler takes your word for the body.

nodes.label: TypeScript type erasure
nodes.rationale: TypeScript type-checks then throws the types away. Annotations, interfaces and type aliases vanish; enum, namespace, parameter properties and decorators emit code.

nodes.label: Phase 2 narrowing and CFA
nodes.rationale: The compiler reads if statements. This phase makes unions usable and is the most common source of 'why is this still possibly undefined?'.

nodes.label: strict tsconfig flag
nodes.rationale: One line in tsconfig.json that changes what the language means; never start a project without it.

nodes.label: Structural typing
nodes.rationale: TypeScript compares shapes, not names. An unrelated object is assignable; the object literal still errors via excess property checks.

nodes.label: Three ways to run TypeScript
nodes.rationale: tsc emit, transpile-only tools (esbuild/swc/Babel/tsx), and Node 24 running .ts directly. Only one of the three actually type-checks.

nodes.label: import type and verbatimModuleSyntax
nodes.rationale: A type-only import must be erasable. A vanished runtime import can break a side effect.

nodes.label: Module augmentation
nodes.rationale: declare module adds properties to somebody else's types — how req.user, custom globalThis keys and library plugins are typed.

nodes.label: module and moduleResolution
nodes.rationale: Pick the setting that matches what actually loads the code. Most 'it compiles but crashes at runtime' reports come from the compiler modelling a module system the runtime does not use.

nodes.label: Path aliases trap
nodes.rationale: tsc resolves @/lib; Node does not. The alias must be resolved again at runtime by a bundler, imports map or loader.

nodes.label: JSON does not round-trip types
nodes.rationale: Date becomes a string, undefined disappears, BigInt throws, Map/Set flatten.

nodes.label: pg query T is an assertion
nodes.rationale: query<T>() is an assertion, not a check: the driver never verifies the row shape, so a renamed column is a runtime undefined with a green build.
nodes.norm_label: pg query t is an assertion

nodes.label: Schema-first with zod or valibot
nodes.rationale: z.infer as the single source of truth. Never hand-write a type that duplicates a schema.

nodes.label: Typed Express handlers
nodes.rationale: Request generics (Params, ResBody, ReqBody, Query) type the slots. A typed body is a promise the compiler cannot keep.

nodes.label: useReducer discriminated actions
nodes.rationale: The pattern where TypeScript pays for itself most obviously in React: the action union types both dispatch and every reducer case from one declaration.

nodes.label: allowJs incremental migration
nodes.rationale: allowJs first, file-by-file conversion, leaf modules before shared ones, and never converting and refactoring in the same commit.

nodes.label: noUncheckedIndexedAccess
nodes.rationale: arr[0] and record[key] become T | undefined. The flag that finds the most real bugs and annoys people the most.

nodes.label: tsc --noEmit CI gate
nodes.rationale: A transpile-only build cannot replace type checking. A green vite build proves nothing about types.

nodes.label: Prefer a discriminant for designed types
nodes.rationale: in is right for shapes you do not control. For shapes you design, a discriminant is clearer, survives refactoring, and enables exhaustiveness checking.
nodes.norm_label: prefer a discriminant for designed types

nodes.label: Illegal states unrepresentable
nodes.rationale: A single object with optional data/error and status: string type-checks illegal combinations. The union makes those combinations unrepresentable and turns a new variant into a compile error.

nodes.label: Default fallback swallows variants
nodes.rationale: A default that returns a fallback compiles forever no matter how many variants you add. Either assertNever in default, or no default with an explicit return type.

nodes.label: Schema validator over hand-written guards
nodes.rationale: Guards for small structural checks. A validator (zod, valibot) for anything crossing a boundary: it performs the runtime check and derives the type from one declaration.

nodes.label: Compiler does not check guard body
nodes.rationale: function isCat(p): p is Cat { return true } compiles. A predicate is an assertion in function form — written once and trusted at every call site, so a wrong one is more expensive than a wrong as.
nodes.norm_label: compiler does not check guard body

nodes.label: Parse, don't validate
nodes.rationale: Types are erased, so nothing crosses the network typed. Convert unknown into a domain type once at the edge and let the type system carry it from there.

nodes.label: TypeScript unsound by design
nodes.rationale: Assertions, any, index access, method bivariance, mutation through an alias, and Object.keys returning string[]. Trusting a guarantee you do not have is worse than having no guarantee.

nodes.label: Boolean host attributes
nodes.rationale: Known booleans: true emits the empty attribute, false removes it. disabled="false" is truthy. aria-* and data-* stringify.

nodes.label: className and htmlFor
nodes.rationale: class and for are reserved words. Raw class/for also reach the DOM since React 16, with a development warning.

nodes.label: null/undefined remove attributes
nodes.rationale: Idiomatic conditional omit: href={isExternal ? url : undefined}.

nodes.label: style must be an object
nodes.rationale: A string throws. The one attribute where pasted HTML fails loudly.

nodes.label: Unknown host props
nodes.rationale: String/number: lowercased with a warning. Boolean: dropped. on*: dropped as unknown event.

nodes.label: Spreading onto a component has no DOM rules
nodes.rationale: Every key arrives untouched. Unknown-attribute warnings fire only when something later spreads onto a host element.
nodes.norm_label: spreading onto a component has no dom rules

nodes.label: CSS custom properties in style
nodes.rationale: {'--gap': 8} is --gap: 8 with no px. Cleanest way to pass a runtime value into a stylesheet.

nodes.label: Hyphenated style keys still apply
nodes.rationale: React warns and applies. A camelCase typo is silent. null/undefined/false remove a declaration.

nodes.label: style is a camelCase object with automatic px
nodes.rationale: Numbers get px except the unitless list. A unitless string such as fontSize: '12' is invalid CSS and is dropped silently.
nodes.norm_label: style is a camelcase object with automatic px

nodes.label: Unitless style properties
nodes.rationale: lineHeight, zIndex, opacity, flex, flexGrow, fontWeight, order, columnCount, gridRow, aspectRatio, scale, tabSize — ratios, counts, indexes.

nodes.label: value without onChange is read-only
nodes.rationale: Warns unless readOnly. value={null} is controlled-with-nothing; use '' to clear and undefined to go uncontrolled.

nodes.label: Default parameters fire only on undefined
nodes.rationale: null, 0, '' and false suppress the default. For props that can be null, use ?? in the body.
nodes.norm_label: default parameters fire only on undefined

nodes.label: defaultProps removed for function components
nodes.rationale: Replaced by ES6 default parameters. Class components keep defaultProps — there is no ES6 equivalent for a class's props.

nodes.label: propTypes is silently ignored in React 19
nodes.rationale: No error, no warning. The migration hazard is the silence. TypeScript is the documented replacement.
nodes.norm_label: proptypes is silently ignored in react 19

nodes.label: Rest destructuring for wrappers
nodes.rationale: Name consumed props so they stay out of ...rest; the rest forwards onClick, disabled, aria-* to the host.

nodes.label: onclick is silently dropped
nodes.rationale: Unknown on* is parsed as an event and discarded. Production prints nothing. Highest-cost typo on the page.

nodes.label: Rest spread leaks component props to the DOM
nodes.rationale: Unknown on* and unknown booleans are dropped; other unknowns become attributes. Destructure non-DOM props out first.
nodes.norm_label: rest spread leaks component props to the dom

nodes.label: Inline style cannot express pseudos or queries
nodes.rationale: One declaration block: no :hover, ::before, @media, @supports, keyframes, or cascade. Use for JS-known runtime values only.
nodes.norm_label: inline style cannot express pseudos or queries

nodes.label: ?? rather than || for fallbacks
nodes.rationale: || swallows every falsy value, so 0 disappears. Almost every 'the zero disappeared' bug is this.

nodes.label: strict defaults to true in TypeScript 7
nodes.rationale: TS 7 default true; 5.9.3 default false. Old projects that never set strict light up on upgrade.
nodes.norm_label: strict defaults to true in typescript 7

nodes.label: strictNullChecks
nodes.rationale: Without it null is assignable to every type so | null is decoration. Load-bearing flag of the seven; required by strictPropertyInitialization.

nodes.label: Classic ts.* API moved
nodes.rationale: require('typescript') exports only version and versionMajorMinor. Sync/async API plus 409-export AST live under typescript/unstable/*.

nodes.label: Editor vs CI disagreements
nodes.rationale: Different compiler version, file set, unsaved buffers, or tsconfig. Same file: four errors on 7.0.2, silence on 5.9.3.

nodes.label: Upgrade path 5.9 to 6.0 to 7.0
nodes.rationale: 6.0 is the JavaScript-implemented deprecation bridge. Tooling that imports typescript is the risky part of jumping to 7.

nodes.label: Phase 0 How TypeScript runs
nodes.rationale: 13 pages written. Phases 1–12 planned except Phase 1 also written.

nodes.label: TypeScript 7.0.2 native compiler
nodes.rationale: Native Go compiler. Root export is only version keys; classic ts.createProgram moved to typescript/unstable/*.

nodes.label: Pin the TypeScript compiler
nodes.rationale: Minors add checks, so a caret range lets a colleague's npm install produce errors yours does not have. Semver intuition does not transfer.

nodes.label: Devbible Site Brand Mark
nodes.rationale: Primary static logo asset for the Docusaurus site. A cactus-plus-notepad mark signals a written reference rather than the default Infima dinosaur.

nodes.label: Cactus Green and Notepad Yellow Palette
nodes.norm_label: cactus green and notepad yellow palette

nodes.label: CSS-Tricks Cactus Mascot
nodes.rationale: Recognizable CSS-Tricks cactus character: jagged left spines, yellow notepad body, two circular pads, face, and two top dots. Used here as the site brand mark.

nodes.label: Devbible Site Logo SVG
nodes.rationale: 200x200 square SVG (viewBox 0 0 200 200) used as the live Docusaurus navbar/site mark under static/img. Flat fills, evenodd fill-rule, no strokes.

nodes.label: Flat Evenodd Vector Illustration
nodes.rationale: No strokes, no gradients, fill-rule evenodd, geometric rounded-rect and circle primitives. Scales as a navbar/favicon-style mark.

nodes.label: Documentation Notepad Metaphor
nodes.rationale: Yellow ruled paper over the cactus body frames the character as a note-taker, matching a written fullstack reference site.

nodes.label: Powered by React
nodes.rationale: Explicit SVG title; the illustration's message is that Docusaurus documentation sites run on React.

nodes.label: Facebook-Blue Center Monitor
nodes.rationale: Center screen is #4267b2 (Facebook/Meta blue) while side screens stay dark slate, visually privileging the React-associated pane.

nodes.label: Powered by React Illustration
nodes.rationale: Default Docusaurus hero graphic: a seated developer at a three-monitor desk with the Keytar mascot and React atom, branding the site as React-powered rather than depicting a real UI.

nodes.label: Undraw Flat Illustration Style
nodes.rationale: Faceless pastel figures, slate furniture (#3f3d56/#65617d), coral clothing (#ff6584), peach skin (#fbbebe) — stock undraw language customized with official Docusaurus green and React cyan.

nodes.label: Focus on What Matters
nodes.rationale: Default Docusaurus homepage feature art. A docs file tree beside a clean content pane argues that authors should write pages, not assemble site chrome.

nodes.label: Dev Bible
nodes.rationale: One reference that explains everything needed to build a fullstack application across MERN and PERN.

nodes.label: CSS Master share 65%
nodes.rationale: Master is 65% because the syllabus was cut to critical-only; do not relabel rows to hit the 25–30% band.

nodes.label: Priority tiers
nodes.rationale: Tiers allocate effort, not importance. Keep MASTER to roughly 25–30% of topics.

nodes.label: Hardened SHA-1 sha1dc
nodes.rationale: Git 2.13+ detects known collision attack patterns and aborts rather than writing the object.

nodes.label: SHA-1 default object format
nodes.rationale: Fresh repos use sha1. 40 hex characters. No sign of the default changing soon.

nodes.label: Object name is reproducible without Git
nodes.rationale: printf 'blob 6\0hello\n' | sha1sum matches git hash-object. The filename is not part of the hash.
nodes.norm_label: object name is reproducible without git

nodes.label: Hash is over type size NUL content
nodes.rationale: blob 6\0hello\n hashed with sha1sum reproduces ce013625… with no Git involved.
nodes.norm_label: hash is over type size nul content

nodes.label: hash-object without -w only computes a name
nodes.rationale: Computing a name is not storing it. cat-file fails until hash-object -w writes the object.
nodes.norm_label: hash-object without -w only computes a name

nodes.label: Diffs are derived output
nodes.rationale: Git never recorded what you did, only what things became. A rename is inferred; git diff output depends on myers, histogram, or patience.

nodes.label: A commit is a snapshot, not a diff
nodes.rationale: The model is snapshots; the storage uses deltas. Confusing the two makes packfiles sound like they contradict the snapshot claim.
nodes.norm_label: a commit is a snapshot, not a diff

nodes.label: Unchanged files reuse existing blobs
nodes.rationale: Change one file in 10 000: one new blob, one new tree per directory on the path, one commit. Every other entry is a pointer.

nodes.label: Delta compression is below the model
nodes.rationale: cat-file still returns whole objects. Hashes are over content, never stored form. Deltas are chosen by similarity, not commit adjacency.
nodes.norm_label: delta compression is below the model

nodes.label: Content-addressed object store
nodes.rationale: Git is a key-value store keyed by the SHA of the content, plus names pointing into it. Deduplication is unavoidable once the name is the hash.

nodes.label: hooks/ is not tracked
nodes.rationale: Sample scripts ship with .sample suffix. Teams need core.hooksPath or husky to share hooks.

nodes.label: Part 4 — Depth and repair
nodes.rationale: Phases 10–12 · 41 topics · 6 Master. Plumbing, repository-scale rewrite, error-message catalogue.

nodes.label: Phase 11 — History surgery and migration
nodes.rationale: Every topic changes every hash after the point it touches. git-filter-repo is not installed on this machine.

nodes.label: Phase 12 — When Git goes wrong
nodes.rationale: Symptom → cause → fix catalogue. Diagnostic index to the rest of the bible.

nodes.label: Part 3 — Git in a real project
nodes.rationale: Phases 7–9 · 42 topics · 7 Master. Assumes node_modules, lockfile, .env, migrations, and a front end plus API.
nodes.norm_label: part 3 — git in a real project

nodes.label: Phase 7 — The repository in a fullstack project
nodes.rationale: gitignore for Node/React, secrets never enter, lockfiles always committed, migrations are append-only.
nodes.norm_label: phase 7 — the repository in a fullstack project

nodes.label: Phase 8 — Hooks, CI and automation
nodes.rationale: Hooks are skippable with --no-verify. Anything that must hold is re-checked server-side.

nodes.label: Phase 9 — Speed, scale and daily ergonomics
nodes.rationale: Clone strategy for CI, deliberate global config, maintenance, auditing history size.
nodes.norm_label: phase 9 — speed, scale and daily ergonomics

nodes.label: History is immutable and cumulative
nodes.rationale: Reachable objects are never collected. A committed secret or binary is an incident; deleting the file later does not remove the blob.

nodes.label: Git is not a place for secrets
nodes.rationale: Deleting a credential in a later commit removes nothing. Rotate first, then rewrite, then force-push.
nodes.norm_label: git is not a place for secrets

nodes.label: includes vs indexOf for NaN
nodes.rationale: indexOf uses === so [NaN].indexOf(NaN) is -1; includes and Map/Set keys use SameValueZero, so NaN is found and Set([NaN,NaN]).size is 1.

nodes.label: NaN
nodes.rationale: IEEE-754: NaN means a failed computation, and two unrelated failures are not the same value, so NaN !== NaN. It never throws and poisons every later arithmetic step.

nodes.label: Number.isNaN
nodes.rationale: Use Number.isNaN, not global isNaN. The global coerces first so isNaN('abc') is true; Number.isNaN answers only 'is this the NaN value?'.

nodes.label: Object.is / SameValue
nodes.rationale: Fourth equality algorithm: === with NaN treated equal and 0 vs -0 treated unequal. React uses it so NaN state does not re-render forever. Everyday code still uses ===.

nodes.label: Signed zero -0
nodes.rationale: IEEE-754 signed zero from underflow, 0*-1, or Math.round(-0.2). Invisible under ===, String, JSON. Detect with Object.is(x,-0) or 1/x === -Infinity. Matters for Math.atan2 and Object.is deep-equals.

nodes.label: ToNumber
nodes.rationale: null becomes 0; undefined becomes NaN. A missing value fails loudly; a null price silently becomes free.

nodes.label: IEEE-754 double number type
nodes.rationale: JavaScript has one number type: a 64-bit float. 0.1 + 0.2 !== 0.3 because both are repeating binary fractions. This is not a JS-only flaw.

nodes.label: Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER
nodes.rationale: 53-bit significand: integers above 2^53-1 collapse. JSON.parse silently corrupts bigint IDs; send IDs as strings or recover via reviver ctx.source + BigInt.

nodes.label: Infinity
nodes.rationale: Division by zero does not throw. Math.max() is -Infinity (identity). JSON.stringify turns Infinity and NaN into null.

nodes.label: + concatenation vs arithmetic
nodes.rationale: If either operand of + is a string after ToPrimitive, + concatenates. -, *, / and % always ToNumber both sides.

nodes.label: Number.isFinite validation
nodes.rationale: Validate where the value enters with Number.isFinite, which rejects NaN and both infinities. !Number.isNaN lets Infinity through.

nodes.label: Store money as integer minor units
nodes.rationale: Do arithmetic in paise/cents; Math.round once where a fraction is created; divide by 100 only when formatting with Intl.NumberFormat. Never toFixed money — 1.005 stores as slightly less so toFixed(2) is '1.00'.
nodes.norm_label: store money as integer minor units

nodes.label: Convert at the boundary
nodes.rationale: Form values, query params, localStorage and env vars are strings. Parse and Number.isFinite once on the way in so the rest of the code works with real types.

nodes.label: Bitwise & looser than ===
nodes.rationale: flags & MASK === 0 parses as flags & (MASK === 0); parenthesise the mask test.

nodes.label: Comma operator lowest precedence
nodes.rationale: Evaluates every operand and returns the last; looser than assignment.

nodes.label: ** is right-associative
nodes.rationale: 2 ** 3 ** 2 is 512; only **, ternary, and assignment associate right.

nodes.label: + string poison
nodes.rationale: + groups left to right; where the first string sits changes 1+2+"3" vs "1"+2+3.

nodes.label: Comparisons do not chain
nodes.rationale: 3 > 2 > 1 is (true) > 1 → 1 > 1 → false; write a < x && x < b.

nodes.label: switch fallthrough
nodes.rationale: Without break/return/throw, execution continues; stacked empty cases are the idiomatic share.

nodes.label: switch body is one block
nodes.rationale: Cases are labels, so two let x collide; brace each case body.

nodes.label: switch uses ===
nodes.rationale: 1 and '1' are different cases; case NaN never matches because NaN !== NaN.

nodes.label: Operator precedence
nodes.rationale: Do not memorise twenty levels; learn the five cases that bite and parenthesise the rest.

nodes.label: switch
nodes.rationale: Compares with === and falls through unless stopped; use object lookup for key-to-value maps.

nodes.label: Circular ES module import TDZ
nodes.rationale: Depth-first evaluation can read a hoisted import before the exporter initialises it. Same error string as a local let.

nodes.label: CommonJS circular require
nodes.rationale: require has no dead zone: a cycle returns a partially populated module.exports, usually with undefined properties.

nodes.label: Import live read-only view
nodes.rationale: Imports are const-like live views. Only the exporting module can reassign; property mutation is allowed.

nodes.label: Behavioral hoisting
nodes.rationale: let/const/class create a dead zone above their line: the binding exists but is uninitialised.

nodes.label: HoistableDeclaration
nodes.rationale: The spec term is not 'hoisting'. HoistableDeclaration covers function declarations only.

nodes.label: Side-effect hoisting
nodes.rationale: import bindings are available early and the imported module's side effects run before the rest of the file.

nodes.label: Value hoisting
nodes.rationale: Functions (and function*, async function) are usable before their line because the slot holds the finished function.

nodes.label: Function declaration value hoisting
nodes.rationale: The only form that is usefully hoisted: the slot holds the finished function before the first line runs.

nodes.label: var and function name collision
nodes.rationale: At scope entry the function wins regardless of source order. Only an initializer overwrites it at execution time.

nodes.label: Two-step scope entry
nodes.rationale: Nothing is relocated. Scope entry first creates a binding for every declaration, then code runs. What differs is whether the slot is initialised.

nodes.label: Object.fromEntries
nodes.rationale: Inverse of Object.entries. Accepts any pair iterable including Map, URLSearchParams, FormData, Headers. Always builds a plain object; unlike Array.from it ignores this.

nodes.label: entries-fromEntries object map/filter
nodes.rationale: Objects have no map/filter. Convert to pairs, use array methods, convert back. Safer pick than delete. Loses symbols, non-enumerables, inherited keys, prototype, accessors, descriptors, and numeric key order. Shallow.

nodes.label: fromEntries duplicate-key loss
nodes.rationale: URLSearchParams/FormData can repeat keys; an object cannot. Last assignment wins, so tag=a&tag=b becomes {tag:"b"}. Use getAll or keep the params object.

nodes.label: Getter and setter properties
nodes.rationale: Look like data properties but run functions. Spread and Object.assign invoke getters and store a snapshot. Preserve with getOwnPropertyDescriptors.

nodes.label: Object.assign
nodes.rationale: Mutates the target and triggers its setters (MDN warning). Keeps the target prototype. Not interchangeable with { ...a, ...b }.

nodes.label: Object spread
nodes.rationale: Copies own enumerable string and symbol keys shallowly, excluding the prototype. Spreading a class instance drops methods. Later spreads win; a spread after an explicit key silently overwrites it.

nodes.label: Conditional property spread idiom
nodes.rationale: ...(cond && {key}) keeps one expression. Spreading a falsy non-object is a defined no-op. Avoids delete, which is slower on hot objects.

nodes.label: Deep copy
nodes.rationale: Duplicates the whole graph so nothing is shared. Reach for it only for snapshots, defensive copies of input you will mutate, or data handed to untrusted code.

nodes.label: Shallow copy
nodes.rationale: Top-level properties become independent; nested objects stay shared. Spread, Object.assign, slice, Array.from, concat are all shallow. [...users] is a new array of the same user objects.

nodes.label: Copy the path, share the rest
nodes.rationale: Idiomatic React/Redux updates copy only changed levels. Shared identity makes prev===next a valid change check and is what React.memo needs. Deep-cloning state defeats memoisation.
nodes.norm_label: copy the path, share the rest

nodes.label: Active handles and requests
nodes.rationale: Open servers, timers, and sockets keep the loop alive; prefer process.report over underscore APIs in production.

nodes.label: GET /metrics endpoint
nodes.rationale: Keep /metrics off the public internet via an internal listener, NetworkPolicy, or sidecar scrape.

nodes.label: Node diagnostic report
nodes.rationale: JSON dump of stacks, handles, versions, and resource usage; may contain sensitive env and is not free to write.

nodes.label: node:trace_events
nodes.rationale: Low-level Node/V8 categories, not product distributed tracing; scope to a critical section.

nodes.label: Prometheus pull scrape
nodes.rationale: Pull keeps service discovery, failure detection, and timestamps with the collector; Pushgateway is the short-lived-job exception.

nodes.label: AbortController
nodes.rationale: Standard cancellation remote: abort() stops in-flight work that accepted the paired signal.

nodes.label: AbortSignal
nodes.rationale: Read-only side handed to callees: aborted, reason, throwIfAborted(), abort event. Never hand out the controller.

nodes.label: AbortSignal.any
nodes.rationale: Combined signal that aborts when the first input does and adopts that reason — cancellation counterpart of Promise.race.

nodes.label: AbortSignal.timeout
nodes.rationale: Deadline signal that actually aborts work, unlike Promise.race against setTimeout. Timer is unrefed.

nodes.label: AbortSignal.throwIfAborted
nodes.rationale: Throws signal.reason if already aborted; check before starting and between units of work.

nodes.label: Promise.any
nodes.rationale: Settles with the first fulfilment, ignoring rejections. All-reject throws AggregateError with .errors.

nodes.label: Promise.race
nodes.rationale: Settles with the first to settle, success or failure. Used for timeouts; does not stop losers.

nodes.label: AggregateError
nodes.rationale: Several failures in one error (.errors). Promise.any throws one when every input rejects.

nodes.label: Promises cannot be cancelled
nodes.rationale: A promise is a view of a result with many consumers. Cancellation belongs to the work, via AbortController.

nodes.label: Combinators do not cancel losers
nodes.rationale: race/all stop waiting, not working. Timed-out HTTP still holds a socket. Real stop requires AbortSignal.

nodes.label: async generator
nodes.rationale: async function* can await and yield. Consumer pull pauses the producer — free pull-based backpressure.

nodes.label: for await...of
nodes.rationale: Loop for sequences that arrive over time. Awaits each value; strictly sequential, one item in memory.

nodes.label: Pull-based backpressure
nodes.rationale: The generator is suspended at yield until the consumer asks for the next value, so a slow consumer slows the producer.

nodes.label: Symbol.asyncIterator
nodes.rationale: Protocol: a method returning { next() → Promise<{value, done}> }. Async generators produce it.

nodes.label: Error-first callback convention
nodes.rationale: cb(err) or cb(null, value), exactly once, always asynchronously. The contract util.promisify depends on.

nodes.label: util.promisify.custom
nodes.rationale: Author-supplied promise form checked first when the mechanical (err, value) translation is wrong.

nodes.label: util.promisify
nodes.rationale: Wraps an error-first last-argument callback API into a promise. Prefer built-in fs/promises etc. when they exist.

nodes.label: Bounded mapLimit worker pool
nodes.rationale: Exactly N workers claim a shared cursor. JS single-thread makes next++ atomic; results[i] preserves order.

nodes.label: new Promise only to wrap callbacks
nodes.rationale: The one legitimate use of the Promise constructor is wrapping a callback or event API. Wrapping already-promise code is an antipattern.
nodes.norm_label: new promise only to wrap callbacks

nodes.label: Pool versus chunked Promise.all
nodes.rationale: Chunking waits for the slowest in each batch and idles workers. A pool keeps every worker busy continuously.

nodes.label: Chunked transfer encoding
nodes.rationale: Omit Content-Length and Node sets Transfer-Encoding: chunked automatically so the first byte reaches the client while the rest is still being produced.

nodes.label: Last-Event-ID resumption
nodes.rationale: The browser stores SSE id: and replays it as Last-Event-ID on reconnect so the server can resume instead of replaying or dropping events.

nodes.label: Server-Sent Events
nodes.rationale: One long-lived chunked HTTP response, server to client only — no upgrade, survives HTTP/1.1 proxies. Prefer over WebSockets when traffic is one-way.

nodes.label: WebSocket Origin check
nodes.rationale: Handshakes are not covered by CORS or same-origin policy. Any origin can open a socket with the user's cookies. Validate Origin and authenticate on upgrade.

nodes.label: WebSocket HTTP upgrade handshake
nodes.rationale: Client GET with Upgrade: websocket and Sec-WebSocket-Key; server replies 101 Switching Protocols. Begins as HTTP so it carries cookies and traverses HTTP proxies.

nodes.label: ws npm WebSocketServer
nodes.rationale: Node ships only a WebSocket client (global WebSocket, stable from v22.4.0). Server side is ws from npm — what Socket.IO and Fastify wrap.

nodes.label: pipeline over pipe for streaming
nodes.rationale: .pipe() leaves both ends open when a client disconnects, so a database query keeps running. pipeline propagates destruction.

nodes.label: WebSocket ping/pong heartbeat
nodes.rationale: Sleeping laptops, dropped mobile signal and expired NAT mappings leave TCP open. Periodic ping plus isAlive and terminate() reaps dead sockets.

nodes.label: CIC cannot run in a transaction
nodes.norm_label: cic cannot run in a transaction

nodes.label: Includes are not a migration runner
nodes.norm_label: includes are not a migration runner

nodes.label: Aborted transaction 25P02
nodes.rationale: After a statement error the transaction accepts nothing but ROLLBACK. COMMIT on an aborted transaction is silently executed as ROLLBACK.

nodes.label: ACID
nodes.rationale: Atomicity via abort-on-error, consistency via constraints, isolation via snapshots, durability via WAL flush before COMMIT returns.

nodes.label: DEFERRABLE constraint
nodes.rationale: UNIQUE/PK/EXCLUDE/FK can be deferred to commit, enabling legal intermediate states such as a unique-column swap. CHECK and NOT NULL are always immediate.

nodes.label: synchronous_commit
nodes.rationale: Off buys ~6× on 500 single-row commits (1042→170 ms) for a window of lost recent commits, not corruption. One transaction of 500 inserts was faster (128 ms) with durability on.

nodes.label: WAL
nodes.rationale: Every change writes a WAL record before the data file. Measured 112 bytes for one small UPDATE. WAL volume is what replication and PITR ship.

nodes.label: Autocommit
nodes.rationale: Every unwrapped statement is its own transaction. Two pool.query calls get two xids.

nodes.label: withTransaction helper
nodes.rationale: pool.connect(), BEGIN on that client, COMMIT, ROLLBACK.catch in catch, release() in finally. Isolation goes on BEGIN itself (25001 if SET after first query). Nested BEGIN only warns 25001.

nodes.label: pool.query BEGIN bug
nodes.rationale: BEGIN via pool.query works on an idle pool (same connection) and fails under load: UPDATE autocommits on another backend while ROLLBACK hits an empty transaction. Load-dependent.

nodes.label: effective_cache_size
nodes.rationale: Allocates nothing. Leaving it at 4 GB on a large server biases the planner to sequential scans.

nodes.label: pg_settings.context
nodes.rationale: Tells you restart vs reload before planning a change. Read pending_restart after.

nodes.label: random_page_cost
nodes.rationale: Default 4.0 models a spinning disk. On SSD, 1.1 is the usual highest-value one-line change.

nodes.label: work_mem
nodes.rationale: Per sort/hash operation. Worst case is work_mem × operations × concurrency — how servers get OOM-killed.

nodes.label: First matching HBA rule wins
nodes.rationale: A broad rule near the top makes every rule below it dead. Order specific before general.

nodes.label: HBA failure messages
nodes.rationale: no entry = no match; rejects connection = reject method; password failed covers wrong password, missing role, and expired VALID UNTIL.

nodes.label: pg_hba.conf
nodes.rationale: Runs before privileges exist. First matching rule only; if its method fails the connection fails — no fall-through.

nodes.label: pg_hba_file_rules
nodes.rationale: Parsed view with evaluation order. A syntax error survives reload (old rules stay); a restart turns it into an outage.

nodes.label: scram-sha-256
nodes.rationale: Default password method. A scram rule cannot authenticate an md5-stored password; the reverse works.

nodes.label: trust authentication
nodes.rationale: Does not check the password. Measured: a deliberately wrong password connected. POSTGRES_HOST_AUTH_METHOD=trust replaces the image's scram line.

nodes.label: Exhaustion, sizing and the Node side
nodes.rationale: One idle-in-transaction bug exhausts the pool. query_wait_timeout defaults to 120s. Smaller pool is usually faster.
nodes.norm_label: exhaustion, sizing and the node side

nodes.label: The Node side, observing, and alternatives
nodes.rationale: Set connectionTimeoutMillis. Release in finally. Alert on SHOW POOLS cl_waiting/maxwait.
nodes.norm_label: the node side, observing, and alternatives

nodes.label: Idle-in-transaction pool blast radius
nodes.rationale: Five open transactions exhausted default_pool_size=5; two more clients waited 120204 ms then 08P01.

nodes.label: Smaller pool is usually faster
nodes.rationale: Beyond cores×2 extra backends add contention not throughput. Size small and timeout short, or neither.

nodes.label: synchronous_commit
nodes.rationale: Only remote_apply waits for replay. on does not mean synchronous replication unless synchronous_standby_names is set.

nodes.label: SET LOCAL app identity
nodes.rationale: Plain SET on a pooled connection leaks tenant identity into the next request — a cross-tenant data leak, measured in ex54.

nodes.label: Invalid concurrent index
nodes.rationale: A failed CONCURRENTLY build is ignored for queries but still consumes write overhead.

nodes.label: ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock queue
nodes.rationale: A 5 ms ALTER can outage for 30 s because later readers cannot jump the queue behind waiting DDL.

nodes.label: JS Part 4 DSA and machine coding
nodes.norm_label: js part 4 dsa and machine coding

nodes.label: JavaScript syllabus
nodes.rationale: Largest syllabus on purpose: language + Web APIs + DSA + applied storefront.

nodes.label: Node release schedule
nodes.rationale: Odd/even unstable-vs-stable ends with v27: one major each April, LTS each October.

nodes.label: erasableSyntaxOnly and strip-only mode
nodes.rationale: Node 24 runs .ts with no flag, but enum fails: TypeScript enum is not supported in strip-only mode.

nodes.label: TS Part 3 TypeScript in the stack
nodes.norm_label: ts part 3 typescript in the stack

nodes.label: TypeScript 7 native Go compiler
nodes.rationale: typescript@7.0.2 ships platform binaries; require('typescript') exports only version keys. The classic ts.* API moved.

nodes.label: Node 24 Active LTS target
nodes.rationale: Build on Node 24 until October 2026, then 26. Never use an API the target LTS lacks.

nodes.label: Network split at the wire
nodes.rationale: fetch, AbortController, FormData and how CORS fails in the console are JS; status-code design and server headers are Express.

nodes.label: JavaScript has no prerequisites
nodes.rationale: First syllabus in the bible with no prerequisite outside itself.

nodes.label: JS verification policy
nodes.rationale: Parts 1, 2, 4 run in Node 24. Parts 3 and 5 never invent browser console output; unmeasured pages get a VERIFY marker.

nodes.label: React scope rule
nodes.rationale: If removing React would remove the topic, it is React's.

nodes.label: TypeScript scope rule
nodes.rationale: If removing the types would remove the topic, it is TypeScript's.

nodes.label: Types are erased
nodes.rationale: A checker that runs at build time and leaves nothing at runtime. Why validation still exists, why as is dangerous, why enum is unlike other types.

nodes.label: Safe SET NOT NULL via CHECK
nodes.norm_label: safe set not null via check

nodes.label: PostgreSQL ENUM
nodes.rationale: Cannot drop a value (0A000); cannot use a newly added value in the same transaction (55P04).

nodes.label: Lookup table for statuses
nodes.rationale: Default choice: adding a value is an INSERT, and the table can carry labels and sort order.

nodes.label: enum vs CHECK vs lookup table
nodes.norm_label: enum vs check vs lookup table

nodes.label: Expand/contract migration
nodes.rationale: Every deploy must be compatible with the schema before and after it; never remove in the same step that adds a replacement.

nodes.label: Identical username and password auth errors
nodes.norm_label: identical username and password auth errors

nodes.label: AT TIME ZONE in the query
nodes.rationale: Makes day-bucketing independent of the session. Two events at 21:00Z/23:30Z on 15 June group to 15 June in UTC and 16 June in Asia/Kolkata.
nodes.norm_label: at time zone in the query

nodes.label: IANA time zone names
nodes.rationale: Follow DST and historical rules. Abbreviations like IST are ambiguous; fixed offsets silently get DST wrong. Store the name, not an offset.

nodes.label: Session TimeZone setting
nodes.rationale: Display and interpretation only, not storage. Changes timestamptz print, bare timestamp literals, current_date, date_trunc and ::date grouping.

nodes.label: set_config for bindable timezone
nodes.rationale: SET has no parameter slots (42601 at $1). set_config($1,$2,true) is the LOCAL form; interpolating a user zone is an injection hole.

nodes.label: Unqualified CREATE TABLE follows search_path
nodes.rationale: Default "$user", public can land the table in an unexpected schema. Schema-qualify DDL in migrations.

nodes.label: Schema- or database-per-tenant
nodes.rationale: Structural isolation at the cost of N migrations, hard cross-tenant queries, and a permanent operational tax. Choose when isolation is a contract.

nodes.label: SET LOCAL never SET for tenant identity
nodes.rationale: Plain SET persists on a pooled connection into the next request — cross-tenant exposure under concurrency when RLS keys on that setting.
nodes.norm_label: set local never set for tenant identity

nodes.label: tenant_id leads every index
nodes.rationale: Every query is tenant-scoped via code and RLS, so an index that does not lead with tenant_id cannot serve the filter.

nodes.label: Pin pool timezone to UTC
nodes.rationale: options: '-c timezone=UTC'. Plain SET leaks across pooled release(); SET LOCAL is safe inside a transaction.

nodes.label: Shared schema with RLS
nodes.rationale: Default tenancy model: one migration, trivial cross-tenant queries, scales to millions. Schema/DB-per-tenant for contractual isolation, not reassurance.

nodes.label: Collation and libc vs ICU
nodes.rationale: musl Alpine sorts en_US.utf8 by byte value; glibc applies dictionary order. libc upgrades can silently corrupt text btrees.

nodes.label: No default SELECT order
nodes.rationale: A SELECT with no ORDER BY may return any order and can change after VACUUM, a plan switch, or an UPDATE that relocates a heap row.

nodes.label: NULLS FIRST and NULLS LAST
nodes.rationale: Default is NULLS LAST for ASC and NULLS FIRST for DESC. Indexes record null placement; a mismatch forces an in-memory sort.

nodes.label: ORDER BY
nodes.rationale: Without ORDER BY there is no row order. Sorting is free only when an index supplies the order; otherwise it spills past work_mem.

nodes.label: LIKE wildcard abuse
nodes.rationale: A parameter keeps % as data, but LIKE still matches everything. Escape % and _ when the user means them literally.

nodes.label: Multi-row RETURNING has no order
nodes.rationale: RETURNING takes no ORDER BY. Wrap in a CTE and sort the outer SELECT.

nodes.label: Case-insensitive matching
nodes.rationale: lower() needs an expression index; ILIKE needs pg_trgm for leading wildcards; citext or a CI collation compare directly.

nodes.label: Sargable predicates
nodes.rationale: An index on col serves bare col. date(created_at) or lower(email) needs a matching expression index.

nodes.label: Pin an ICU or builtin collation
nodes.rationale: Do not inherit collation from the container image. ICU is versioned by PostgreSQL; builtin C.UTF-8 is stable byte order.
nodes.norm_label: pin an icu or builtin collation

nodes.label: Sort in SQL not JavaScript
nodes.rationale: LIMIT must sort server-side; sorting a page in JS reorders the wrong twenty rows.

nodes.label: Adjacency-list hierarchy
nodes.rationale: FK pointing at the same table. Cheapest hierarchy to write (one UPDATE moves a subtree) and most expensive to read. Use LEFT JOIN so a NULL parent id does not drop the root.

nodes.label: Recursive CTE cycle detection
nodes.rationale: CYCLE id SET is_cycle USING path_arr on PostgreSQL 14+, or WHERE NOT e.id = ANY(c.path_arr). A depth cap plus statement_timeout limits damage but does not detect the cycle.

nodes.label: Self join
nodes.rationale: An ordinary join where both sides are the same table. Aliases are mandatory (42712 without them). One self join walks one hierarchy level.

nodes.label: WITH RECURSIVE
nodes.rationale: Anchor plus recursive term joined to the previous iteration until none. UNION ALL is almost always correct. A cycle loops forever; CYCLE (PG 14+) or a path array is the defence.

nodes.label: WITH CTE
nodes.rationale: Binds a name to a subquery for one statement. Since PostgreSQL 12 a qualifying CTE is inlined rather than fenced; MATERIALIZED restores the boundary and cost 6× here.

nodes.label: Data-modifying CTE
nodes.rationale: A CTE can INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/MERGE. WITH moved AS (DELETE … RETURNING *) INSERT INTO archive SELECT * FROM moved archives in one atomic statement. Always a fence.

nodes.label: Recursive term restrictions
nodes.rationale: May reference the CTE once only; may not appear on the right of a LEFT JOIN, in a subquery, or under EXCEPT/INTERSECT; no aggregates or ORDER BY/LIMIT inside the recursive term.

nodes.label: CTE inlining rule
nodes.rationale: Inlined when referenced once, not MATERIALIZED, not recursive, does not write, and contains no volatile function. Otherwise materialized into a tuplestore. Referenced twice runs once.

nodes.label: Write-CTE snapshot rule
nodes.rationale: A write CTE always runs, referenced or not. Its effect is visible only through its own RETURNING; a sibling SELECT sees the pre-statement snapshot. Two writes touching the same row can lose one silently.

nodes.label: DISTINCT ON
nodes.rationale: DISTINCT ON keeps one row per key using ORDER BY, without requiring the rest of the SELECT to be aggregated.

nodes.label: ERROR 42803
nodes.rationale: A selected column that is neither grouped nor aggregated raises 42803.

nodes.label: Functional dependency on PK
nodes.rationale: Grouping by a primary key lets other columns of that table be selected without aggregating.

nodes.label: dense_rank()
nodes.rationale: Tied peers share a rank; the next rank does not skip.

nodes.label: ntile()
nodes.rationale: Splits the partition into N buckets as evenly as possible; remainder buckets get one extra row.

nodes.label: rank()
nodes.rationale: Tied peers share a rank; the next rank skips so the sequence has gaps.

nodes.label: row_number()
nodes.rationale: Always unique within the partition; ties still get consecutive numbers in ORDER BY order.

nodes.label: Ranking ties
nodes.rationale: rank and dense_rank treat equal ORDER BY values as peers; row_number never ties.

nodes.label: DISCARD ALL before release
nodes.rationale: release() does not reset the session. SET search_path, temp tables and open transactions persist. DISCARD ALL cannot run inside a transaction.

nodes.label: withTransaction helper
nodes.rationale: BEGIN/COMMIT on one checked-out client; wrap ROLLBACK so a dead connection does not mask the original error; release in finally.

nodes.label: Pool options string for server settings
nodes.rationale: options: '-c search_path=app,public -c statement_timeout=5000' applies on every new connection. A SET via pool.query lands on one arbitrary connection.
nodes.norm_label: pool options string for server settings

nodes.label: Multi-statement implicit transaction
nodes.rationale: A valid INSERT followed by a failing one left zero rows. The whole simple-query string is one implicit transaction.

nodes.label: Pool vs Client
nodes.rationale: Use Pool almost always. pool.query borrows, runs, and returns; two calls may land on different connections.

nodes.label: Generic vs custom plan
nodes.rationale: Custom plans for the first five executions; from the sixth PostgreSQL may switch to a generic plan. Skewed data then gets the wrong plan. force_custom_plan restores per-value planning.

nodes.label: Named prepared statements
nodes.rationale: Adding name issues server-side PREPARE. Measured 1.6× on 2000 trivial lookups (772 ms unnamed vs 481 ms named).

nodes.label: Prepared statements are per session
nodes.rationale: A statement prepared on pid 1932 is invisible to pid 1933. A pool of N prepares up to N times. Dynamic names leak server memory.

nodes.label: PgBouncer breaks named statements
nodes.rationale: Transaction/statement pooling routes consecutive queries to different backends → 26000 prepared statement does not exist. Use session pooling or disable names.

nodes.label: Session state needs a checked-out client
nodes.rationale: Transactions, SET, cursors, advisory locks and named prepared statements cannot use pool.query because session state lives on one connection.
nodes.norm_label: session state needs a checked-out client

nodes.label: Transaction rollback per test
nodes.rationale: 0.8 ms measured vs TRUNCATE 4.4 ms. Discards only the test's writes; seed survives. Requires injected client and no nested COMMIT. Cannot test commit-only effects.

nodes.label: db as first argument
nodes.rationale: Only the handler names pool. Services that open their own transaction cannot be composed. grep pool in services/repositories should be empty.

nodes.label: Pool instead of client half-commit
nodes.rationale: insertOrder(client) rolled back; insertItem(pool) committed. orders=0 items=1. Different backend pids; PostgreSQL has no reason to object.

nodes.label: Executor contract
nodes.rationale: db first. Pool and Client are interchangeable if the repo never calls pool.connect() itself. That leak is why tests inject a client.

nodes.label: Resetting between test runs
nodes.rationale: Reset strategy sets suite speed. Fastest option requires every query on one injected client.

nodes.label: Passing a client through services
nodes.rationale: One transaction across repositories works only if every function uses the same client. Handing the pool breaks atomicity with no error.

nodes.label: delete hard vs soft
nodes.rationale: Hard delete removes the row and cascades. Soft delete is an UPDATE that makes every query wrong until you add deleted_at IS NULL. Schema-wide, not per-endpoint.

nodes.label: findById and the not-found decision
nodes.rationale: A missing row is a successful empty result. Every 404 is application policy. The decision is where you add it.

nodes.label: A repository module per resource
nodes.rationale: Not a class or SQL abstraction. A module of functions whose first argument is whatever will run the query, so the same function works standalone and in a transaction.

nodes.label: AsyncLocalStorage ambient client
nodes.rationale: Removes the forgotten-argument bug. ?? pool fallback reintroduces silent autocommit when async context is lost. Throw if no store.

nodes.label: Mutating array methods on props
nodes.rationale: sort, reverse, splice, push mutate in place. Use a copy or toSorted, toReversed, toSpliced.

nodes.label: Component identity and the nesting rule
nodes.norm_label: component identity and the nesting rule

nodes.label: What makes a function a component
nodes.norm_label: what makes a function a component

nodes.label: StrictMode, the Compiler and how purity is enforced
nodes.norm_label: strictmode, the compiler and how purity is enforced

nodes.label: The two rules of a pure component
nodes.norm_label: the two rules of a pure component

nodes.label: memo vs useState bail-out
nodes.rationale: Bail-out compares new state vs old on every set. memo compares props shallowly when the parent re-renders. Neither substitutes for the other.

nodes.label: Same-value updater idiom
nodes.rationale: Return the existing reference from an updater to signal no change. More reliable than wrapping the setter when the current value is out of scope.

nodes.label: useState bail-out
nodes.rationale: If the new value is Object.is-identical, React skips re-rendering the component and its children. React may still call the component first; the optimisation is safe only because purity is assumed.

nodes.label: structuredClone vs Immer
nodes.rationale: A deep clone destroys structural sharing, throws on functions/DOM nodes, and costs the whole tree. Immer copies only touched paths.

nodes.label: Immutable updates
nodes.rationale: React compares state with Object.is. Mutate and the reference is unchanged, so the update vanishes with no error.

nodes.label: Two mutation failures
nodes.rationale: Mutate without a setter: React is never asked. Mutate then set the same reference: Object.is bails out. The second looks correct.

nodes.label: Shape 3: new object identity in a dependency array
nodes.rationale: Dependencies are compared with Object.is. A fresh object, array, or function literal is a new reference every render, so the effect always re-runs.
nodes.norm_label: shape 3: new object identity in a dependency array

nodes.label: Four things that stop render descent
nodes.rationale: useState bail-out, memo, unchanged element identity (children trick), and the React Compiler.
nodes.norm_label: four things that stop render descent

nodes.label: effective_cache_size
nodes.rationale: Allocates nothing; planner hint about shared buffers plus OS page cache.

nodes.label: work_mem
nodes.rationale: Allocated per sort/hash operation per query, not per connection; worst case work_mem × ops × concurrent queries.

nodes.label: Cache hit ratio (blks_hit)
nodes.rationale: blks_read is shared-buffer misses, often served from OS page cache; treat as trend not purchase signal.

nodes.label: Changing a setting, and where to start
nodes.rationale: pg_settings.context decides restart vs reload vs SET. ALTER SYSTEM writes postgresql.auto.conf which overrides postgresql.conf.
nodes.norm_label: changing a setting, and where to start

nodes.label: The memory settings
nodes.rationale: shared_buffers, work_mem, maintenance_work_mem, effective_cache_size. Only one allocates what people think; effective_cache_size allocates nothing.

nodes.label: Why connections cost
nodes.rationale: A connection is a process. replicas × pg.Pool max is the real count. pg.Pool ≠ PgBouncer.

nodes.label: Process-per-connection
nodes.rationale: Each connection is an OS process; isolation is the point and the price. Do not raise max_connections — put a pooler in front.

nodes.label: Mutating vs copying array methods
nodes.rationale: push/unshift, pop/shift/splice, index assignment, sort and reverse mutate. Prefer spread, filter, slice, map, or copy-then-mutate.

nodes.label: Local mutation exception
nodes.rationale: Mutating a freshly created object nothing else holds is fine. Only the object handed to the setter must be new.

nodes.label: Spread is shallow
nodes.rationale: {...person} copies the artwork reference. Mutating next.artwork.city still mutates the original. Copy every level on the path; share the rest.

nodes.label: Treat objects in state as read-only
nodes.rationale: Mutation does not merely skip a render — it retroactively corrupts every previous snapshot that captured the same object.
nodes.norm_label: treat objects in state as read-only

nodes.label: Flatten nested state
nodes.rationale: A lookup table keyed by id turns deep spreads into single-level updates. Flatten in response to pain, not pre-emptively.

nodes.label: type by default, interface when merging
nodes.norm_label: type by default, interface when merging

nodes.label: Docusaurus Open Graph social card
nodes.rationale: Wide landscape marketing card (OG/Twitter preview): top wordmark, left mascot holding a document, right two-line value proposition, large type and empty space so the brand stays readable as a social thumbnail.

nodes.label: Content-first authoring
nodes.rationale: The card sells Docusaurus as a docs product: authors write content; the framework owns site chrome and performance.

nodes.label: Open Graph preview layout
nodes.rationale: Brand-first OG composition rather than a product screenshot: oversized wordmark, friendly mascot, two short slogans, pale gradient, no UI chrome so it still reads at social-thumbnail size.

nodes.label: Focus on What Matters
nodes.rationale: Default Docusaurus homepage feature art. A docs file tree beside a clean content pane argues that authors should write pages, not assemble site chrome.

nodes.label: Class selector
nodes.rationale: Default because it says nothing about the document. .card survives a div becoming an article.

nodes.label: ID selector
nodes.rationale: Avoid in component CSS: specificity 1,0,0, cannot repeat, and ids belong to anchors and ARIA.

nodes.label: Type selector
nodes.rationale: For content you do not control. Scope under .prose so bare h2 does not leak into components.

nodes.label: ~= vs *= on class
nodes.rationale: *= is a substring match over the whole string and also matches column-header. ~= matches a whole list item.

nodes.label: Style on aria attributes
nodes.rationale: Visual state and accessibility state cannot drift because they are the same attribute. A parallel .is-open class can be forgotten.

nodes.label: :has() replaces ancestor class toggles
nodes.rationale: body:has(dialog[open]) cannot get out of sync the way classList.add/remove on an error path can.

nodes.label: Collection, item, and sub-resource
nodes.rationale: GET /users list+POST create; GET /users/:id read/update/delete one; /users/:id/orders owned hierarchy.

nodes.label: REST resource modeling
nodes.rationale: Resources are nouns. Collections are lists of them. Prefer /orders/12/items over /getOrderItems.

nodes.label: RPC-style action routes
nodes.rationale: Fine when the domain is an action, not a thing — POST /payments/:id/refund. Name them honestly instead of inventing fake nouns. Acceptable for multi-step operations that are not natural CRUD.

nodes.label: 201 Created with Location
nodes.rationale: Signals a new resource; pairs with Location when useful.

nodes.label: CRUD to HTTP status mapping
nodes.rationale: Create 201 + Location; read 200; replace/update 200 or 204; delete 204 or 200. Failures: 400 validation, 404 missing, 409 conflict.

nodes.label: Cursor pagination
nodes.rationale: Stable for infinite scroll; opaque cursors hide storage details. Encode nothing sensitive without signing/encrypting. Prefer for large or volatile lists.

nodes.label: Offset pagination
nodes.rationale: GET /items?limit=20&offset=40. Easy, slow on deep pages, unstable if rows insert while paging.

nodes.label: Deep hierarchy vs flatten
nodes.rationale: Deep hierarchies mirror the domain and complicate authorization and caching. Flatten when joins explode.

nodes.label: Static segments before :id
nodes.rationale: /users/export is captured by :id if the param route is registered first. Static segments first.

nodes.label: Cap pagination limit
nodes.rationale: Default limit (e.g. 20) and max (e.g. 100). Never allow limit=999999. Protects DB and API CPU from accidental or malicious full-table pulls.

nodes.label: Detached HEAD
nodes.rationale: Legitimate for inspecting a commit or building a tag. Commits made there are abandoned on switch-away unless you branch first; recovery is via reflog.

nodes.label: .git/logs reflog
nodes.rationale: Enabled by logallrefupdates=true. Local, not pushed; expires 90 days reachable / 30 unreachable.

nodes.label: Cruft pack
nodes.rationale: gc parks unreachable objects with mtimes for a two-week grace period. Why rewritten repos do not shrink immediately.

nodes.label: Primitives copied objects shared
nodes.rationale: Always pass-by-value; for objects the value is a reference. A function can mutate the referent but cannot rebind the caller's name.

nodes.label: Shallow copy
nodes.rationale: Spread and Object.assign copy one level. Nested arrays stay shared; pushing to shallow.items mutates cart.items.

nodes.label: structuredClone
nodes.rationale: Default deep copy: handles cycles, Map, Set, Date. Throws DataCloneError on functions and DOM nodes. JSON round-trip mangles those plus undefined, Symbol, NaN.

nodes.label: const let var
nodes.rationale: const and let are block-scoped with TDZ. var is function-scoped and initialises undefined. for-of creates a fresh binding so const is correct there.

nodes.label: Object.freeze is shallow
nodes.rationale: Blocks add/remove/change of own properties one level deep. Nested writes still work. Throws in strict, silent in sloppy. Deep freeze needs an isFrozen cycle guard.

nodes.label: Deep equality
nodes.rationale: Recurse with Date/RegExp/Map/Set and prototype checks. Track visited pairs for cycles. Prefer ETag or updatedAt over comparing API bodies.

nodes.label: JSON.stringify equality trap
nodes.rationale: Key order changes the string; undefined is dropped; Date becomes ISO; Map/Set become {}; NaN and Infinity become null. Throws on cycles.

nodes.label: Shallow equality
nodes.rationale: Same key set, each value compared with Object.is. What React uses for props and deps because immutable updates give changed branches new references.

nodes.label: Structural sharing
nodes.rationale: React change detection is a reference compare. Return new objects along the changed path; leave untouched branches shared so updates stay cheap.

nodes.label: const protects the binding
nodes.rationale: const cart = {}; cart.qty = 1 is legal; cart = {} throws TypeError. The name never points at something else.

nodes.label: Strict equality ===
nodes.rationale: NaN not equal to itself; 0 equals -0. Used by ===, indexOf, and switch.

nodes.label: Dates compare but do not equal
nodes.rationale: Relational uses valueOf timestamps so d1<=d2&&d1>=d2 can be true while d1==d2 is false (identity). Compare +date or getTime().
nodes.norm_label: dates compare but do not equal

nodes.label: Intl.Collator / localeCompare
nodes.rationale: Code-unit sort puts Z before a and é after z. numeric:true also fixes item2 vs item10.

nodes.label: Lexicographic string comparison
nodes.rationale: '2'>'10' is true. '10'>9 is true (numeric) but '10'>'9' is false (text). Convert numeric strings at the boundary.

nodes.label: Object relational comparison is silent
nodes.rationale: {}<={} is true because both ToPrimitive to '[object Object]'. Compare a field.

nodes.label: Relational comparison algorithm
nodes.rationale: ToPrimitive hint number, then both strings → lexicographic else ToNumber. No null special case, so null>=0 is true while null==0 is false. NaN makes every comparison false.

nodes.label: switch body is one block
nodes.rationale: Cases are labels, not scopes. Two let x declarations collide. Brace each case body.

nodes.label: switch uses ===
nodes.rationale: switch(1) and switch('1') differ. switch(NaN) matches no case NaN. Convert form/query strings before switching.

nodes.label: Comparisons do not chain
nodes.rationale: 3>2>1 is false: true>1 becomes 1>1. 1<2<3 being true is coincidence. Write a<x&&x<b.

nodes.label: Object lookup instead of branching
nodes.rationale: When every branch maps a key to a value, STATUS_LABEL[status]??'Unknown' beats switch. Not for branches with different shapes or side effects.

nodes.label: Logical assignment skips the write
nodes.rationale: a||=b is a&&(a=b) with assignment inside the short-circuit. Setters, proxies, Vue/MobX, and frozen objects see zero writes when the condition fails.

nodes.label: Nullish assignment ??=
nodes.rationale: Fills only null/undefined. ||= overwrites 0, '', false. Idiom: (byCategory[k]??=[]).push(item).

nodes.label: Short-circuit evaluation
nodes.rationale: Right side is not evaluated when the left decides. Guards expensive or unsafe calls.

nodes.label: ?. short-circuits the entire chain
nodes.rationale: empty?.a?.[side()] does not call side(). Parentheses end the chain: (u?.profile).name throws. One ?. does not protect later links.

nodes.label: Optional chaining ?.
nodes.rationale: Short-circuits the chain to undefined when the left is null or undefined. Forms: obj?.prop, obj?.[expr], fn?.().

nodes.label: Optional chaining is read-only
nodes.rationale: obj?.a=1 is SyntaxError: Invalid left-hand side in assignment.

nodes.label: for…in walks prototypes and stringifies indices
nodes.rationale: Includes inherited enumerable keys; array indices arrive as strings so i+1 concatenates. Prefer Object.keys and for…of.
nodes.norm_label: for...in walks prototypes and stringifies indices

nodes.label: Object spread later keys win
nodes.rationale: {...defaults,...overrides}. A key present as undefined still overwrites — spread does not skip it.

nodes.label: in vs Object.hasOwn
nodes.rationale: 'toString' in {} is true (prototype). hasOwn is false. hasOwn distinguishes missing from present-undefined. On arrays in tests indices.

nodes.label: Reserve ?. for genuinely optional values
nodes.rationale: On a guaranteed value, ?. converts a loud TypeError into an undefined that fails far away. Assert the invariant instead.

nodes.label: await evaluates its expression immediately
nodes.rationale: The expression runs now; only the waiting is deferred. That is why starting work before awaiting it turns a waterfall into parallel work.

nodes.label: await converts non-promises via Promise.resolve
nodes.rationale: The value comes back unchanged, so await is safe on a value that may or may not be a promise — but it is converted, not skipped, which is why the tick is spent either way.

nodes.label: await suspends and returns control to the caller
nodes.rationale: After the expression is evaluated, the rest of the body is registered as a continuation and control exits the function.
nodes.norm_label: await suspends and returns control to the caller

nodes.label: await continuation is a microtask
nodes.rationale: An await loop never yields to rendering, because rendering happens between tasks.

nodes.label: await always costs at least one tick
nodes.rationale: Even when the promise is already fulfilled, execution still pauses until the next tick. There is no fast path.
nodes.norm_label: await always costs at least one tick

nodes.label: Async body is synchronous until the first await
nodes.rationale: An async function is not asynchronous until it reaches an await. Top-level code, up to and including the first await, runs synchronously on the caller's stack.
nodes.norm_label: async body is synchronous until the first await

nodes.label: Thenables are assimilated by await
nodes.rationale: await cares about the shape, not the class. An object with an unrelated then field gets assimilated rather than returned.

nodes.label: Two async functions interleave
nodes.rationale: Both run synchronously to their first await, then resume in queue order. Concurrency without parallelism: one thread, two suspended functions taking turns.

nodes.label: await inside forEach does nothing
nodes.rationale: forEach discards the callback's return value, so the promises are never awaited and their rejections float free.

nodes.label: await in a for loop is sequential
nodes.rationale: Each iteration suspends until its request settles. The loop is the correct shape when each step depends on the previous one, and the wrong shape when the steps are independent.
nodes.norm_label: await in a for loop is sequential

nodes.label: Each await re-queues at the back of the microtask queue
nodes.rationale: A function with two awaits does not resume all at once — it rejoins the back of the queue at each one, which is why interleaving with other microtasks is possible.
nodes.norm_label: each await re-queues at the back of the microtask queue

nodes.label: An async function never throws synchronously
nodes.rationale: A throw becomes a rejection, so a bare try/catch around the call catches nothing.
nodes.norm_label: an async function never throws synchronously

nodes.label: Phase 7 — Asynchronous JavaScript
nodes.rationale: If you only ever finish one phase to Master depth, finish that one — it is what every interview probes and what every production incident traces back to.

nodes.label: Search box three bugs
nodes.rationale: Debounce the input, abort the in-flight request, and discard out-of-order responses.

nodes.label: Sequential await waterfall
nodes.rationale: Three 300ms queries sequential ~902ms, Promise.all ~301ms. Sequential await in a loop is the single most common performance bug in Node code.

nodes.label: await-split pieces share one scope
nodes.rationale: user is an ordinary const visible to every later line, where a chain would have to thread it through handler arguments.

nodes.label: Three-pass ordering method
nodes.rationale: Walk the synchronous path, drain the microtask queue, then run one task. The interview question is always an ordering question.

nodes.label: async/await is syntax over chaining with shared scope
nodes.rationale: Syntax over the machinery of chaining, with one thing genuinely added: the pieces share a scope.
nodes.norm_label: async/await is syntax over chaining with shared scope

nodes.label: Waterfalls are a choice, not a consequence
nodes.rationale: await evaluates its expression immediately and defers only the code that depends on it.
nodes.norm_label: waterfalls are a choice, not a consequence

nodes.label: arguments object
nodes.rationale: Array-like ([object Arguments]), no .map, absent in arrows. Prefer rest in new code.

nodes.label: Arity is never enforced
nodes.rationale: Too few arguments become undefined; extras are ignored by the parameter list but still counted by arguments.length. Downstream TypeError is the usual symptom.

nodes.label: Destructured parameters
nodes.rationale: Property defaults cover missing keys; = {} covers a missing object. Every optional destructured level needs its own default.

nodes.label: Non-simple parameter list
nodes.rationale: Any default, rest, or destructured parameter. Turns off sloppy arguments aliasing, forbids a body use-strict directive, and changes .length.

nodes.label: Rest parameters
nodes.rationale: A real array, empty rather than undefined when nothing extra is passed. Must be last; cannot have a default. Works in arrows.

nodes.label: Sloppy-mode arguments aliasing
nodes.rationale: On a simple parameter list, arguments[i] and the parameter share one slot both ways. Off in strict, and if any default, rest, or destructured parameter makes the list non-simple.

nodes.label: Arrow inherited arguments
nodes.rationale: At module scope arguments is not defined. Inside a function the arrow reports the outer call count, not its own. Use rest.

nodes.label: Method borrowing
nodes.rationale: Array methods are generic: they need length and integer keys. [].slice.call(arrayLike) and push on a plain object both work. Array.from replaced most of this.

nodes.label: Positional plus options-object signature
nodes.rationale: Two or three required positionals, then an options object destructured with defaults. Explicit guards replace the arity check JavaScript will not do.

nodes.label: Parameter list is its own language
nodes.rationale: Own scope, own TDZ, own evaluation order, and a simple vs non-simple rule that silently changes arguments.
nodes.norm_label: parameter list is its own language

nodes.label: bind identity trap
nodes.rationale: bind returns a new function each call, so removeEventListener never matches. Store the bound function once.

nodes.label: call apply bind cannot change arrow this
nodes.rationale: They silently do nothing to this and still pass arguments. bind still returns a function so nothing signals failure.
nodes.norm_label: call apply bind cannot change arrow this

nodes.label: call apply bind
nodes.rationale: All three set this. Only bind defers the call. apply takes an array. bind returns a new function every time.

nodes.label: Sloppy primitive boxing
nodes.rationale: Each call(42) boxes a fresh Number, so state written to this is discarded. Strict throws TypeError on the write.

nodes.label: thisArg coercion
nodes.rationale: Strict passes thisArg untouched. Sloppy boxes primitives and replaces null/undefined with globalThis.

nodes.label: bind reduces function.length
nodes.rationale: Reduced by the number of bound arguments. Express error handlers that dispatch on fn.length === 4 change behaviour.

nodes.label: apply and spread argument limit
nodes.rationale: Both hit RangeError Maximum call stack size exceeded at large arity. Spread is not a fix. Use reduce or chunk.

nodes.label: call apply bind cost
nodes.rationale: Direct call is about 3x faster than any indirect form. call, apply, and spread are indistinguishable. Hoist bind out of loops. Tens of nanoseconds per call.

nodes.label: Object.prototype.toString.call type check
nodes.rationale: Reads the internal tag. typeof cannot distinguish array, null, Date, or Map. Defeated by Symbol.toStringTag; user classes are always [object Object].

nodes.label: The three methods that make this explicit
nodes.rationale: Spread replaced most of apply. call and bind remain load-bearing. toString.call is still the only correct built-in type check.
nodes.norm_label: the three methods that make this explicit

nodes.label: sort compareFn contract
nodes.rationale: Negative means a before b, positive after, zero or NaN equal. Only the sign matters, which is why a - b works.

nodes.label: Fisher–Yates shuffle
