nodes.rationale: sort(() => Math.random() - 0.5) breaks every consistency requirement and is a biased, engine-dependent shuffle.

nodes.label: Well-formed comparator requirements
nodes.rationale: Pure, stable, reflexive, anti-symmetric, transitive. Violations do not throw; they yield implementation-defined order.

nodes.label: Intl.Collator
nodes.rationale: Build one Collator and reuse compare; creating one per comparison is wasteful on large lists.

nodes.label: String.prototype.localeCompare
nodes.rationale: Default UTF-16 order puts Z before a and mis-sorts accents. localeCompare returns a signed number that plugs into compareFn.

nodes.label: Multi-key || comparator chain
nodes.rationale: A tie returns 0, which is falsy, so evaluation falls through. Negate one term for a descending key.

nodes.label: ES2019 sort stability
nodes.rationale: Equal elements keep original relative order since ES2019. Earlier engines varied by array length, which is why old code carries index tiebreaks.

nodes.label: Locale-dependent case mapping
nodes.rationale: Turkish i uppercases to dotted İ. Prefer localeCompare with sensitivity accent over lowercasing both sides.

nodes.label: Decorate–sort–undecorate
nodes.rationale: An expensive key computed inside compareFn runs O(n log n) times and a variable key violates stability. Map to {item, key}, sort, map back.

nodes.label: Two-pass multi-column sort
nodes.rationale: Sort secondary first then primary; stability preserves the secondary inside each primary group. Use the || chain for a one-shot sort.

nodes.label: Node CI/CD pipeline
nodes.rationale: Lockfile-faithful install, tests on production Node, and a reproducible artifact — not a rebuild on the deploy agent.

nodes.label: Node CI version matrix
nodes.rationale: Apps match production Node 24; libraries may matrix 22+24; canary Current is optional.

nodes.label: yarn install --immutable
nodes.rationale: Fail when the lockfile would change so CI cannot silently drift.

nodes.label: Custom module loaders
nodes.rationale: Power tools for tooling authors — transpile, mock, policy — not the default for application code.

nodes.label: Cache package downloads not node_modules
nodes.rationale: Restored node_modules across OS/arch runners can restore wrong native binaries.

nodes.label: Promote image digest
nodes.rationale: Production must run the exact bits that passed staging, not a hopeful rebuild.

nodes.label: Immutable digest plus human version tag
nodes.rationale: Kubernetes apps deploy by digest; a marketing/version tag is for humans, not latest.
nodes.norm_label: immutable digest plus human version tag

nodes.label: Do not transpile on the fly in production
nodes.rationale: Hurts startup, complicates debugging, and drifts from the artifact tested in CI.
nodes.norm_label: do not transpile on the fly in production

nodes.label: node:timers/promises
nodes.rationale: Cancellable sleep, async-iterable interval, awaitable setImmediate, scheduler.yield and scheduler.wait. Stop writing a hand-rolled sleep that leaks when abandoned.

nodes.label: Promise.race
nodes.rationale: Settles with the first to settle, success or failure. Stops waiting, not working — losers keep running. Use AbortSignal for real cancellation.

nodes.label: AbortController
nodes.rationale: The remote: only the owner calls abort(). Hand callees the signal, never the controller.

nodes.label: AbortSignal
nodes.rationale: Read-only side: aborted, reason, throwIfAborted, abort event. Operations reject with a generic AbortError; custom reason is on signal.reason. Check aborted before listening — the event does not re-fire.

nodes.label: AbortSignal.any
nodes.rationale: Aborts when any input aborts and adopts that reason. Cancellation counterpart of Promise.race for combining user cancel, deadline and shutdown.

nodes.label: AbortSignal.timeout
nodes.rationale: Replaces racing a promise against setTimeout and actually stops the work. Timer is unrefed so it will not hold the process open.

nodes.label: Promises have no cancellation
nodes.rationale: all rejecting or race resolving does not stop other work. Timed-out HTTP still holds its socket; raced queries still occupy pool connections.

nodes.label: Promises cannot be cancelled
nodes.rationale: A promise is a view of a result, not a handle on the work. Many consumers can await the same promise; cancelling for one would break the rest.

nodes.label: Thread { signal } through every layer
nodes.rationale: Cancellation is cooperative. One layer that drops the signal makes everything below uncancellable. Call throwIfAborted between units of work.

nodes.label: LISTEN / NOTIFY
nodes.rationale: Needs a dedicated Client. Fire-and-forget: a disconnected listener misses payloads. Cache invalidation or wake-up, never a queue.

nodes.label: 202 Accepted for queued work
nodes.rationale: Work is accepted, not done. 200 plus fire-and-forget is how a frontend polls a receipt that failed silently.

nodes.label: BullMQ
nodes.rationale: Retries, delayed jobs, priorities, rate limits. Enqueue is not transactional with the database. Set removeOnComplete or Redis grows forever.

nodes.label: Durable exclusive claim visibility ack
nodes.rationale: Exactly-once is not on the list. Every queue is at-least-once, which is why jobs must be idempotent.

nodes.label: FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED
nodes.rationale: Each worker locks a different row. 3 workers, 20 jobs: 94 ms and unique 20. Without skip locked 189 ms serialising on the first row.

nodes.label: Domain-derived idempotency key
nodes.rationale: order-paid-email:${orderId}. A UUID generated inside the job is new every attempt and deduplicates nothing.

nodes.label: Outbox relay
nodes.rationale: Marks published_at then enqueues; crash republishes. At-least-once with jobId outbox:${id}. A jobs table in the same DB is the outbox.

nodes.label: res.json then doSlowThing is not a queue
nodes.rationale: No retry, no visibility, no backpressure; a restart deletes it. Still runs on the API event loop.
nodes.norm_label: res.json then doslowthing is not a queue

nodes.label: jobId vs handler dedup
nodes.rationale: jobId stops duplicate enqueue. Only on conflict do nothing in the handler stops redelivery of a claimed job.

nodes.label: setInterval is not a scheduler
nodes.rationale: Drifts (35 ms over 8 ticks with a 30 ms job), overlaps (3 concurrent 250 ms jobs on a 100 ms interval), runs once per process, dies on restart.

nodes.label: Mongo causal consistency
nodes.rationale: A session with causalConsistency: true sees its own prior writes wherever routed. LSN tracking done for you.

nodes.label: Read-your-own-writes
nodes.rationale: Write then immediate replica read returned 0 rows on an idle localhost pair with 1.6 ms replay_lag. Pin post-write reads to primary.

nodes.label: PostgreSQL from Node
nodes.rationale: pg is the driver Knex, Drizzle, Prisma adapters and TypeORM sit on; learn it so the layer above is never magic.

nodes.label: Sync vs background
nodes.rationale: The request path should do the minimum the user is waiting on. One event loop: 120 ms resize produced 1246 ms p95 at 10 concurrent vs 19 ms queued.

nodes.label: Worker processes
nodes.rationale: Same codebase, two entry points. Same image, different command. CPU isolation, independent scale, independent failure.

nodes.label: Pass executor vs AsyncLocalStorage
nodes.rationale: Repos take a db that is pool or tx client, or ALS holds the client. Explicit is greppable; ALS keeps call sites clean. One statement on the wrong executor undoes the point.

nodes.label: No HTTP inside a transaction
nodes.rationale: A transaction pins a connection and locks. Four open txs in a max:4 pool left the next query waiting 103 ms.

nodes.label: timingSafeEqual for secrets
nodes.rationale: === leaks how much of the value matched through timing. Guard length first — timingSafeEqual throws on mismatched buffers.

nodes.label: Double-submit CSRF token
nodes.rationale: Random value in a readable cookie must be echoed in a header. Attacker can cause a request carrying cookies but cannot read them. Compare with timingSafeEqual.

nodes.label: SameSite cookie attribute
nodes.rationale: Lax is the current browser default and stops classic cross-site POSTs. Strict logs users out from external links. None re-opens CSRF and requires Secure plus a token.

nodes.label: OAuth state parameter
nodes.rationale: CSRF defence for the callback. Without it an attacker feeds you their authorization code and links their provider account to the victim's session.

nodes.label: CORS does not stop CSRF
nodes.rationale: CORS governs whether the attacker may read the response. The write still happens. A form-urlencoded POST is a simple request with no preflight.

nodes.label: Origin allowlist check
nodes.rationale: Compare new URL(origin).origin. Origin:null is a real value and new URL('null') throws. Prefer Origin; Referer is often stripped.

nodes.label: SameSite=Lax default
nodes.rationale: Withholds cookies from cross-site POST/fetch/XHR. Node writes the Set-Cookie string unvalidated — measured sid=abc123; Path=/; HttpOnly with no SameSite. Set it explicitly.

nodes.label: Signed double-submit CSRF token
nodes.rationale: Plain double-submit trusts only you can write the cookie; a subdomain XSS breaks that. HMAC over sid.nonce so a token from another session fails. Verified.

nodes.label: CSRF is an authority problem
nodes.rationale: Nothing in the request is malformed. The browser attaches the destination's cookie to a request the attacker composed. The server sees a valid authenticated POST.

nodes.label: --experimental-test-coverage
nodes.rationale: Built in on Node 24 — no nyc or c8. Include/exclude, per-metric thresholds, lcov output.

nodes.label: Uncovered lines column
nodes.rationale: The useful part of the report: error branches, catch blocks, leftover functions. Read the column, not the percentage.

nodes.label: fast-check
nodes.rationale: Found a slugify trailing-dash bug after a 12-char cap: Counterexample ["0 0 00 A AA    0"], shrunk 35 times. Default fc.string() never reached the cap.

nodes.label: Round-trip, idempotence, invariant, oracle
nodes.rationale: Round-trip is the highest-value backend property: encoders, JWT, query-string builders, money formatting. Not useful for orchestration.

nodes.label: Mutation testing
nodes.rationale: Changes source (>= to >, + to -) and reruns. A surviving mutant means nothing checked that line's behaviour. Asks: do your tests actually check anything?

nodes.label: Property-based testing
nodes.rationale: State a rule for all inputs; the library generates cases and shrinks failures. Asks: are there inputs you did not think of?

nodes.label: Stryker
nodes.rationale: On discount() with 100% line coverage: 13 killed, 2 survived at total >= 10, mutation score 86.67%. Directory positional node --test test/ fails the initial run.

nodes.label: Determinism beats faker
nodes.rationale: Random faker data produces unreproducible fortnightly failures. Use a counter for uniqueness; use property-based testing when you genuinely want random input.

nodes.label: Coverage records execution not assertions
nodes.rationale: withVat(19.99) returns 23.987999999999996 under 100% line, branch and function coverage. A float-money bug ships green because the line executed.

nodes.label: Mutation testing cost
nodes.rationale: Runs the suite once per mutant. Fifteen mutants on a tiny file took 2 seconds; a codebase is hours. Scope to one module; run occasionally, not per commit.

nodes.label: Backend process
nodes.rationale: Parses SQL, plans, executes, holds session state, and can crash without taking down other clients. Appears as backend_type client backend in pg_stat_activity.

nodes.label: Node connection pool
nodes.rationale: One global pg.Pool at module scope reuses backends. Two checkouts produced two client backends. pool.query borrows and returns a client; it does not start a new process each time.

nodes.label: max_connections
nodes.rationale: Server-wide cap on concurrent backends. Measured default 100 on PostgreSQL 18.4 alpine. Exceeding it yields sorry, too many clients already.

nodes.label: pg_stat_activity
nodes.rationale: Catalog view of backends and workers. Measured 18.4 types: autovacuum launcher, background writer, checkpointer, client backend, io worker, logical replication launcher, walwriter.

nodes.label: PgBouncer
nodes.rationale: External pooler that exists because process-per-connection is expensive. Taught in Phase 13, not Phase 0.

nodes.label: Client backend
nodes.rationale: The process that runs your SQL for one connection. Scales with connections.

nodes.label: Postmaster
nodes.rationale: Supervisor parent that accepts connections and starts backends. Managed by the service or container; do not kill random postgres PIDs.

nodes.label: Default isolation level
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL READ COMMITTED vs MySQL REPEATABLE READ. A second SELECT in one transaction sees new commits on PG and the same rows on MySQL. Silent port behaviour change.

nodes.label: SQLite single-writer lock
nodes.rationale: Whole-database write lock. Second writer errors with database is locked rather than waiting. PostgreSQL row-locks and both succeed. Line between application and embedded database.

nodes.label: Process-per-connection model
nodes.rationale: Each client connection is a dedicated OS backend process. Isolation and simpler memory accounting cost startup time and RAM, so Node pools instead of opening a connection per request.

nodes.label: Element versus direct call
nodes.rationale: Widget() inlines output into the caller. Hooks join the caller list; a conditional call breaks hook order.

nodes.label: Hooks matched by call order
nodes.rationale: No name, no key — just position on the fiber. Conditional hooks shift every subsequent slot.

nodes.label: Elements are ordinary values
nodes.rationale: Creating an element does not render it. Where it is created decides what it can close over.

nodes.label: Passing children skips wrapper re-renders
nodes.rationale: The element object is created by the outer owner. When the wrapper re-renders, props.children is identical so React skips that subtree.

nodes.label: RSC composition requirement
nodes.rationale: A Client Component cannot import a Server Component but can receive one as children. Composition keeps server code out of the client bundle.

nodes.label: Five triggers to control a value
nodes.rationale: Coordination, persistence, validation, programmatic control, or reflecting external data. Do not control in case.
nodes.norm_label: five triggers to control a value

nodes.label: Closest common parent owns state
nodes.rationale: Count components that render based on the value, not ones that only pass it through. Invent a component solely to own state if needed.

nodes.label: Lifting moves the re-render
nodes.rationale: A state change re-renders that component and all descendants by default. Children re-render because the parent did, not because a prop changed.

nodes.label: Phase 2 Dialog gate
nodes.rationale: A Dialog through a portal, header and footer as element props, Escape and backdrop close, dual-mode open.

nodes.label: The cost, and how to pay less of it
nodes.norm_label: the cost, and how to pay less of it

nodes.label: Composition over configuration
nodes.rationale: A prop that exists only to be rendered should have been the rendered thing. Pass the Button, not actionLabel plus onAction plus actionVariant.

nodes.label: Configuration trap
nodes.rationale: A component becomes an interpreter of a private option language. API grows without bound, combinations go untested, every caller pays unused imports, and markup is hidden.

nodes.label: When configuration is the right answer
nodes.rationale: Keep a prop for data, component-owned behaviour, closed design-system variants, or consistency. Design decisions are props; caller markup is composition.
nodes.norm_label: when configuration is the right answer

nodes.label: Context hole
nodes.rationale: Create the element in the scope that has the value and pass the finished object down. Intermediates never mention the value.

nodes.label: Controlled versus uncontrolled
nodes.rationale: Informal terms asked per piece of state. Controlled means the important information is driven by props; uncontrolled means local state the parent cannot influence.

nodes.label: Controlled flexibility versus uncontrolled ease
nodes.rationale: Uncontrolled needs less API but cannot coordinate. Controlling lifts state, so updates re-render the owner and everything below.

nodes.label: Dual-mode controlled component
nodes.rationale: Decide with !== undefined, own internal state only when uncontrolled, always notify, never sync the prop into state with an effect.

nodes.label: Lift state in three steps
nodes.rationale: Remove child state, pass hardcoded data from the parent, then add state and handlers. The middle step separates wiring bugs from update bugs.

nodes.label: Lift then compose then context then store
nodes.rationale: Two or three siblings lift. Threads through unused layers compose. Rarely changing many-depth values use context. Frequent sliced updates use an external store. Server data is a cache.
nodes.norm_label: lift then compose then context then store

nodes.label: Push state down
nodes.rationale: If only one branch reads the state, extract that branch and move the state into it. The large component stops re-rendering.

nodes.label: Bitmap Heap Scan
nodes.rationale: Collect matching locations first, then read the heap in physical order so each page is visited at most once.

nodes.label: Index Scan
nodes.rationale: Walk the index and fetch each heap row directly. Chosen for a handful of rows.

nodes.label: random_page_cost
nodes.rationale: Default 4.0 dates from spinning disks; ~1.1 on SSD is the knob that actually shifts the index/seq balance.

nodes.label: Seq Scan
nodes.rationale: Not a failure: forcing an index on 80% of 500000 rows took 272 ms and 400358 buffers versus 91 ms and 3712 for the sequential scan.

nodes.label: Cast on the indexed column
nodes.rationale: Casting the column is casting every row. pg sends parameters as untyped text so the danger is the :: you add by hand.

nodes.label: Stale statistics
nodes.rationale: Signature is estimated rows=1 against actual rows=400001; ANALYZE dropped the query from 157 ms to 58 ms.

nodes.label: Seq scan vs index scan vs bitmap heap scan
nodes.norm_label: seq scan vs index scan vs bitmap heap scan

nodes.label: Why an index is not being used
nodes.norm_label: why an index is not being used

nodes.label: enable_seqscan = off
nodes.rationale: A diagnostic, not a fix: it prices sequential scans absurdly high. Never leave it in a migration or connection setup.

nodes.label: Low selectivity
nodes.rationale: Not a bug: forcing the index for a value matching 99.89% of rows took 115.8 ms versus 101.9 ms for the sequential scan.

nodes.label: PostgreSQL 18 skip scan
nodes.rationale: Safety net for low-cardinality leading columns, shown by Index Searches: 7; not a licence to stop thinking about column order.

nodes.label: INCLUDE columns
nodes.rationale: Payload in the leaves only — returnable, not searchable or sortable. Required when the index is UNIQUE and the key must not change.

nodes.label: Index-only scan
nodes.rationale: Answers from the index alone only if every selected column is in the index and the visibility map says heap pages are all-visible.

nodes.label: Visibility map
nodes.rationale: VACUUM sets all-visible bits. Without them PostgreSQL must check each row in the heap; one UPDATE took Heap Fetches from 0 to 58.

nodes.label: Duplicate indexes
nodes.rationale: PRIMARY KEY and UNIQUE already create indexes; grouping pg_index by full definition finds exact duplicates.

nodes.label: Index-only scans, INCLUDE and the visibility map
nodes.norm_label: index-only scans, include and the visibility map

nodes.label: Equality first, range second
nodes.rationale: (user_id, created_at) used 23 buffers where (created_at, user_id) used 396 for the same query.

nodes.label: Leftmost-prefix rule
nodes.rationale: An index on (a, b, c) serves any leading prefix but not b or c alone. Measured 0.226 ms on the leading column, 56.9 ms on the second.

nodes.label: Phase 13 complete 18 of 18
nodes.rationale: Topics 07–18 validated against official docs under the no-new-sandboxes rule. No page carries a console block that was not produced by a real run.

nodes.label: The app role should not own the schema
nodes.norm_label: the app role should not own the schema

nodes.label: Logical replication is not for HA
nodes.rationale: Schema, sequences and replica identity are all manual. Every one of those is a step that will not have been done at 4am failover.
nodes.norm_label: logical replication is not for ha

nodes.label: An untested backup is a belief
nodes.rationale: Having backups, being able to restore, and being able to restore in time under pressure are three different claims. Only rehearsal establishes the third.
nodes.norm_label: an untested backup is a belief

nodes.label: Defensible production alert set
nodes.rationale: Alert on few things: connections >80% of max, oldest xact >5 min, idle-in-transaction, lag, dead tuples >20%, deadlock rate, rising temp_bytes, disk >80%.

nodes.label: Disk space and WAL fill
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL handles a full disk badly. A stuck replication slot accumulating WAL can fill one surprisingly fast.

nodes.label: idle_in_transaction_session_timeout
nodes.rationale: Kills transactions left open. Default 0. Worst blockers of vacuum and DDL hold locks while doing nothing.

nodes.label: log_statement
nodes.rationale: all fills disks and logs bound parameters. ddl is the safe continuous production value.

nodes.label: ALTER ROLE PASSWORD logs plaintext
nodes.rationale: SCRAM stores a verifier; the statement still contains the literal. log_statement=ddl captures it. Use psql \password to send only the verifier.

nodes.label: log_parameter_max_length_on_error defaults to 0
nodes.rationale: Failed statements do not log parameters by default. Why many developers never see parameter logging and conclude it never happens.

nodes.label: Parameters do not protect the log
nodes.rationale: Measured: pg_stat_activity shows $1, but log_statement=all writes DETAIL Parameters. log_parameter_max_length defaults to -1 (full). Treat logs as credential-bearing.
nodes.norm_label: parameters do not protect the log

nodes.label: archive_command
nodes.rationale: Must return non-zero on failure or WAL is deleted locally and never stored. test ! -f refuses overwrite. archive_mode=on requires a restart.

nodes.label: pg_stat_archiver failed_count
nodes.rationale: Growing failed_count is an emergency: recovery window stops advancing and unreycled WAL fills pg_wal until the disk is full.

nodes.label: Oldest transaction age as leading indicator
nodes.rationale: Bloat, lock waits, pool exhaustion and replication conflicts all trace back to a transaction open too long. Monitor this after disk space.
nodes.norm_label: oldest transaction age as leading indicator

nodes.label: ON_ERROR_STOP
nodes.rationale: A session setting that governs the whole run including every \ir; not the default.

nodes.label: \conninfo
nodes.rationale: Superuser | on explains most works-here-not-there reports; a superuser bypasses every privilege check.

nodes.label: current_user vs session_user
nodes.rationale: session_user is who authenticated; current_user is who you act as after SET ROLE or inside SECURITY DEFINER. Privilege checks use current_user.

nodes.label: psql -X / --no-psqlrc
nodes.rationale: A colleague's .psqlrc can change how a script's output parses; measured NULL displayed as (null) with the file and blank with -X.

nodes.label: ON_ERROR_ROLLBACK interactive
nodes.rationale: Implicit savepoint before each interactive statement so a typo does not abort the whole transaction (25P02); deliberately does not apply to scripts.

nodes.label: PROMPT1 %x and %#
nodes.rationale: %x shows an open transaction; %# shows superuser. Colour the production prompt red as the cheapest safety measure.

nodes.label: .psqlrc
nodes.rationale: Makes interactive psql pleasant and everyone else's psql different; configure freely, pass -X in every script.

nodes.label: Test as the application role
nodes.rationale: Working as a superuser hides every privilege problem until production; develop against a production-like role.

nodes.label: Cron psql flags
nodes.rationale: -X so no .psqlrc, -w so it fails instead of hanging on a password, -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 for a real exit code, -At for bare output.

nodes.label: set -o pipefail
nodes.rationale: A pipeline reports the last command's status; measured exit=0 naively and exit=1 with pipefail.

nodes.label: Modelling money
nodes.rationale: An amount is not a number and arithmetic on it is not ordinary arithmetic. The bugs are the ones that make accounts fail to balance.

nodes.label: numeric rounds 2.5 away from zero
nodes.rationale: numeric 2.5 → 3 (away from zero); double precision 2.5 → 2 (to even). A second independent reason money is never float.

nodes.label: CREATE TABLE
nodes.rationale: Writes the contract every client must obey. Type changes on a large table rewrite it under a lock that blocks everything.

nodes.label: pg returns bigint as a string
nodes.rationale: 64-bit exceeds JavaScript safe integer range. user.id + 1 yields '11'. Treat ids as opaque strings; do not install a global int8 parser.
nodes.norm_label: pg returns bigint as a string

nodes.label: bigint primary key
nodes.rationale: int stops at 2147483647 and sequences advance on attempts. int→bigint is a full rewrite under ACCESS EXCLUSIVE (431 ms / 200k).

nodes.label: GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY
nodes.rationale: SQL-standard key. Refuses a manual id with 428C9 so the sequence cannot drift. Catalog property is_identity, not column_default.

nodes.label: serial
nodes.rationale: Not a type: integer plus owned sequence plus default. Accepts manual ids without advancing the sequence, later 23505.

nodes.label: ALTER SEQUENCE OWNED BY
nodes.rationale: Lifecycle only: owned sequences drop with the table (serial/identity). Hand-created sequences survive DROP TABLE. Does not restrict nextval.

nodes.label: Phase 3 DDL tables constraints schema design
nodes.rationale: Design a 1-N and N-N schema with identity PKs, FKs, and CHECKs without an ORM. Target PostgreSQL 18.4, Node 24, pg.
nodes.norm_label: phase 3 ddl tables constraints schema design

nodes.label: Five money modelling rules
nodes.rationale: numeric plus currency; round once; allocate remainders; store the FX rate used; keep it a string in JavaScript. Never double precision (1000×0.01 = 9.999999999999831) or the locale-dependent money type.

nodes.label: now() is transaction start time
nodes.rationale: Two inserts 150ms apart in one transaction share created_at. Use clock_timestamp() for per-row wall-clock time. now() cannot be a generated column (42P17).

nodes.label: Explicit NULL bypasses DEFAULT
nodes.rationale: DEFAULT applies only when the column is omitted or given DEFAULT. ORMs that send null for unset fields override every default.

nodes.label: Case-insensitive unique email
nodes.rationale: Index on lower(email) requires WHERE lower(email)=lower($1). Non-deterministic ICU collation makes plain equality case-insensitive but disables LIKE.

nodes.label: Historical price snapshot
nodes.rationale: unit_cents on the order line is a different fact from products.price_cents. Not denormalization; joining would rewrite past invoices.

nodes.label: Generated column
nodes.rationale: Computed from other columns of the same row. Writing it raises 428C9 so it cannot drift. Prefer over a trigger when the value is a pure same-row function.

nodes.label: Generated expression must be IMMUTABLE
nodes.rationale: now(), random(), nextval(), other tables, STABLE functions → 42P17. Falsely marking IMMUTABLE silently corrupts stored values.

nodes.label: STORED generated columns only
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL 18 has no VIRTUAL. Use a view or expression index for computed-on-read. ADD COLUMN with a generated expression rewrites the table.

nodes.label: COMMENT ON
nodes.rationale: Catalog documentation via obj_description/col_description. information_schema does not expose comments. \d hides them; \d+ shows them. NULL deletes.

nodes.label: Denormalize against a measurement
nodes.rationale: A slow read is fixable later; inconsistent data is often unfixable. Prefer generated columns and materialized views the database maintains.

nodes.label: Comments in migrations
nodes.rationale: Hand-typed comments vanish on rebuild. pg_dump includes them. Lost when an object is dropped and recreated; not inherited by partitions.

nodes.label: SELECT alias visibility
nodes.rationale: WHERE runs before the select list exists so aliases raise 42703. ORDER BY runs after so the alias works. Repeat the expression in WHERE.

nodes.label: Unique ORDER BY tiebreaker
nodes.rationale: Ties have undefined order. Paging 100 rows by 5 without a unique column: 54 distinct ids and 46 repeats. Append the primary key.

nodes.label: FROM WHERE GROUP BY HAVING SELECT DISTINCT ORDER BY LIMIT
nodes.rationale: SELECT is seventh so aliases do not exist in WHERE. DISTINCT applies after the select list. LIMIT without ORDER BY is arbitrary.
nodes.norm_label: from where group by having select distinct order by limit

nodes.label: No default row order
nodes.rationale: Not insertion order. Can change after VACUUM, a plan switch, or an UPDATE that relocates a heap tuple. If order matters, state it.

nodes.label: Logical order is not execution order
nodes.rationale: Defines semantics. Planner may push predicates, use top-N heapsort, reorder joins. Putting the most selective WHERE first has no effect.
nodes.norm_label: logical order is not execution order

nodes.label: JOIN is INNER JOIN
nodes.rationale: INNER is optional. Comma form is also inner but a missing condition is a silent cross join.

nodes.label: Phase 5 join fixture j_customers j_orders j_order_items
nodes.rationale: Dee has no orders; order 13 has no items. From topic 03 onward order 14 is an orphan with NULL customer_id.
nodes.norm_label: phase 5 join fixture j_customers j_orders j_order_items

nodes.label: Calendar spine gap fill
nodes.rationale: CROSS JOIN generate_series then LEFT JOIN facts with the date filter in ON. count(fact.id) not count(*); coalesce(sum, 0); to_char the date.

nodes.label: Accidental comma join
nodes.rationale: FROM a, b with a missing WHERE is legal and silent: 4×5=20 with no error. Explicit JOIN ON makes the omission a syntax error.

nodes.label: date parsed as local midnight then UTC-shifted
nodes.rationale: TZ=Asia/Calcutta makes 2026-01-01 come back as 2025-12-31T18:30:00.000Z. Format with to_char or setTypeParser(1082).
nodes.norm_label: date parsed as local midnight then utc-shifted

nodes.label: NATURAL JOIN infers from schema
nodes.rationale: A shared created_at silently cut two rows to one. No shared names degenerates to a cross join. Do not write NATURAL JOIN.

nodes.label: array_agg
nodes.rationale: Keeps NULLs as elements. Prefer FILTER (WHERE x IS NOT NULL) over array_remove: if every value is NULL, remove gives {} and FILTER gives NULL. Arrives as a real JS array.

nodes.label: 42P10 DISTINCT ORDER BY must match arguments
nodes.rationale: array_agg(DISTINCT status ORDER BY id) is incoherent: after de-duplicating by status there is no single id. De-duplicate in a subquery if you need min(id).
nodes.norm_label: 42p10 distinct order by must match arguments

nodes.label: ORDER BY inside the collection aggregate
nodes.rationale: An unordered array_agg changed order when a sibling aggregate with its own ORDER BY was added, because the executor sorted the shared input. Outer ORDER BY orders result rows, not aggregate input.
nodes.norm_label: order by inside the collection aggregate

nodes.label: string_agg
nodes.rationale: Drops NULLs and emits no delimiter for them. Empty group is NULL not ''. text-only; integer needs ::text or 42883. coalesce before concatenation.

nodes.label: json versus jsonb
nodes.rationale: json stores verbatim text; jsonb stores parsed binary, collapses duplicates, drops whitespace, reorders keys. jsonb is 60 vs 23 bytes here, GIN-indexable. Difference is invisible from Node because JSON.parse collapses duplicates too.

nodes.label: jsonb_agg
nodes.rationale: Collects rows into a JSON array. Arrives as a JS array; JSON.parse throws. Put ORDER BY inside, same sibling-sort inheritance as array_agg.

nodes.label: jsonb_build_object
nodes.rationale: Alternating key, value. Verbose on purpose: the API contract is written in the query, so adding a table column cannot change the response.

nodes.label: to_jsonb
nodes.rationale: Emits every column. Never point it at a table you do not control. Safe form names columns in a subquery. numeric becomes a JSON number; cast money to text first.

nodes.label: Arrays and strings
nodes.rationale: array_agg and string_agg collect a group into one value and disagree about NULL handling, empty groups, and what arrives in JavaScript.

nodes.label: JSON shapes
nodes.rationale: jsonb_build_object, to_jsonb, jsonb_agg and jsonb_object_agg cover naming fields, converting a row, collecting an array, and building a keyed map.

nodes.label: percentile_cont
nodes.rationale: Interpolates; can return a value not in the input (2.5 from 1,2,3,4). Numeric and interval only. Standard choice for p95/p99 latency. Ignores NULLs. two-arg round needs ::numeric.

nodes.label: percentile_disc
nodes.rationale: Returns an actual value from the set. Works on anything sortable. percentile_disc(1.0) is max(); percentile_disc(0.0) is min().

nodes.label: WITHIN GROUP
nodes.rationale: Supplies the ordering an ordered-set aggregate is defined over. Syntax tell of the family. percentile_cont(0.5, amount) is a syntax error; the column goes in WITHIN GROUP.

nodes.label: Hypothetical-set aggregates
nodes.rationale: Where a value would rank if inserted: rank, dense_rank, percent_rank, cume_dist. Argument list must match ORDER BY in number and type. Window rank ranks existing rows; this ranks a value that is not there.

nodes.label: mode()
nodes.rationale: Most common value. Ties broken by WITHIN GROUP order, with no tie flag. Four kinds tied at 125000 each returned click (or view if reversed). Empty set is NULL. Prefer top-N with counts for a UI.

nodes.label: percent_rank() WITHIN GROUP
nodes.rationale: Maps a value to a fraction — inverse of percentile_cont. percent_rank(150) returned 0.1334. Use when you have a score and want its percentile.

nodes.label: rank() WITHIN GROUP
nodes.rationale: rank(150) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY amount) returned 66721. bigint in the driver until ::int.

nodes.label: Ordered-set aggregates
nodes.rationale: Aggregates that need input ordered first. Syntax: fraction as argument, column in WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY ...). That ORDER BY is the aggregate's definition order, not query output order. Family costs 3.1× avg() because sorting is unavoidable.

nodes.label: percentile_cont array form
nodes.rationale: percentile_cont(ARRAY[0.5, 0.9, 0.99]) sorts once and returns an array. Separate calls would sort three times. Dashboard form.

nodes.label: Percentiles do not compose
nodes.rationale: You cannot average hourly p95s to get a daily p95. Store enough per bucket to recompute, or use a mergeable sketch (t-digest). Measured 178.32 ms vs 57.41 ms for avg() on 500k rows.

nodes.label: Empty params array is not parameterized
nodes.rationale: pg switches protocols on present-and-non-empty values. query(sql, []) still uses the simple protocol.
nodes.norm_label: empty params array is not parameterized

nodes.label: Extended query protocol
nodes.rationale: A values argument permits exactly one statement. Extra commands raise 42601, which is stacked-statement injection protection.

nodes.label: Multi-statement implicit transaction
nodes.rationale: A simple-query string is one implicit transaction. A later failure rolls back earlier successes. Feature for migration files.

nodes.label: Simple query protocol
nodes.rationale: No values argument: the string is a script. Several statements run and query() returns an array of Result objects.

nodes.label: sql.begin transaction API
nodes.rationale: Makes release-in-finally structural. Same semantics as withTransaction; you cannot forget the rollback.

nodes.label: Resolve SQL paths from import.meta.url
nodes.rationale: process.cwd() is launch directory and differs in tests vs production. import.meta.url is the module location.

nodes.label: Named parameter shim
nodes.rationale: Rewrite :name to $n at load time. Values never enter SQL text. Regex must not match :: casts.

nodes.label: SQL in .sql files
nodes.rationale: Template-literal SQL is invisible to formatters, linters, and psql. Files restore tooling, reviewable diffs, and a boundary against concatenation.

nodes.label: Cached sql file loader
nodes.rationale: Read once per process into a Map. Skip the cache in development so edits take effect without restart.

nodes.label: withTransaction helper
nodes.rationale: BEGIN/COMMIT must share one connection. Wrap ROLLBACK so a dead connection does not mask the original error. release() stays in finally.

nodes.label: Three shapes of infinite render loops
nodes.norm_label: three shapes of infinite render loops

nodes.label: Five rules for set during render
nodes.norm_label: five rules for set during render

nodes.label: exclude only removes roots
nodes.rationale: A file imported by an included file is still checked even if listed in exclude.

nodes.label: types empty array
nodes.rationale: Stops auto-including every @types/* walked from node_modules. This repo's 5.9.3 run pulled @types/mdx from three directories up.

nodes.label: Compiler speed benchmark confound
nodes.rationale: First run reported 10x because 5.9.3 auto-included ancestor @types via cwd. Honest figure is 3x (0.76s vs 2.32s) after asserting zero diagnostics on both sides.

nodes.label: Set rootDir explicitly
nodes.rationale: Unset rootDir is the common ancestor of all inputs. One extra file silently moves output from dist/server.js to dist/src/server.js.

nodes.label: The three ways to run TypeScript
nodes.norm_label: the three ways to run typescript

nodes.label: strict and the flags it turns on
nodes.norm_label: strict and the flags it turns on

nodes.label: void
nodes.rationale: Return value is not part of the contract. A function returning something is assignable to () => void. That lets forEach(push) compile and lets async arrows slip into useEffect.

nodes.label: Contextual typing
nodes.rationale: The one place parameters infer: when the target type is known. Callbacks to typed functions need no annotations; a standalone function always does (TS7006).

nodes.label: Default makes parameter optional
nodes.rationale: subject = 'none' is subject? for callers and string in the body. subject?: string is string | undefined in the body.

nodes.label: Fewer parameters assignability
nodes.rationale: Ignoring an argument is safe; demanding one the caller never sends is not. Makes arr.map(x => ...) legal without declaring index and array.

nodes.label: Function types
nodes.rationale: A contract with a caller. Two unintuitive rules: fewer parameters are assignable where more are expected, and a function returning something is assignable where void is expected.

nodes.label: Function overloads
nodes.rationale: Implementation signature is not callable. Only declared overloads are visible. First matching overload wins. Prefer a union or generic unless return type truly depends on arguments.

nodes.label: Function parameter contravariance
nodes.rationale: A function may accept less and return more. Returns compare covariantly. Method parameters are bivariant; strictFunctionTypes tightens function-typed properties, not method shorthand.

nodes.label: Call signature
nodes.rationale: The arrow form cannot carry properties. An interface with a call signature types middleware, memoised functions with .cache, and decorated handlers.

nodes.label: Hybrid type
nodes.rationale: Call or construct signature plus ordinary properties. Rare in new code, common in .d.ts for pre-module libraries such as jQuery $.

nodes.label: Annotate inputs infer outputs
nodes.rationale: Parameters are not inferred (TS7006 under noImplicitAny). Defaults make parameters optional. Returns are inferred from the body. Annotate exported returns to pin the public contract.

nodes.label: Optional property vs undefined union
nodes.rationale: ? means the key may be absent. T | undefined means the key must exist and may hold undefined. exactOptionalPropertyTypes stops ? accepting explicit undefined.

nodes.label: null vs undefined
nodes.rationale: undefined is not provided; null is deliberately empty. Produce undefined internally, accept null from JSON/SQL, normalise at the boundary. JSON.stringify drops undefined and keeps null.

nodes.label: ?? vs ||
nodes.rationale: ?? falls back only on null/undefined. || falls back on every falsy value, so a legitimate 0 or '' is replaced.

nodes.label: Optional chaining ?.
nodes.rationale: Short-circuits the whole chain to undefined, never to null, even when the missing link was null. Result is always T | undefined.

nodes.label: Symbol keys skipped by JSON
nodes.rationale: JSON.stringify and Object.keys skip symbol keys. Useful for in-process metadata; silent data loss across a network or structuredClone.

nodes.label: symbol
nodes.rationale: Unique key that cannot collide. Invisible to Object.keys, JSON.stringify, and for...in. let widens to symbol; const keeps unique symbol.

nodes.label: Well-known symbols
nodes.rationale: Symbol.iterator, asyncIterator, toPrimitive, hasInstance, toStringTag hook a class into language behaviour.

nodes.label: JavaScript falsy values
nodes.rationale: false, 0, -0, 0n, '', null, undefined, NaN. [] , {}, '0', and 'false' are truthy, so if (arr) is true for an empty array.

nodes.label: != null nullish check
nodes.rationale: The one legitimate use of loose equality: excludes null and undefined and nothing else. Use it for string, number, and boolean that may be missing.

nodes.label: Truthiness narrowing
nodes.rationale: if (v) and v != null produce identical types. At runtime if (v) also skips '' and 0. The compiler cannot warn because '' is still string. Safe only for objects and functions.

nodes.label: Easy to Use
nodes.rationale: Default Docusaurus homepage feature art titled Easy to Use. A night climb with a summit flag, a seated observer, and the Keytar mascot at the base frames documentation as an approachable ascent rather than a technical slog.

nodes.label: Bare resource response
nodes.rationale: Matches pure REST textbooks and OpenAPI components cleanly; no wrapper nesting.

nodes.label: Envelope response
nodes.rationale: Envelopes extend with pagination meta without breaking clients; they add nesting noise.

nodes.label: Response shapes
nodes.rationale: Pick envelope vs bare resource and keep it consistent. Mixing both is worse than either choice.

nodes.label: Stable error JSON shape
nodes.rationale: Clients parse one schema; you can add code without breaking UIs.

nodes.label: OpenAPI contract
nodes.rationale: The contract is part of the product. Drift between OpenAPI and handlers is a bug. Swagger UI is optional sugar — the artifact is the spec.

nodes.label: Cursor pagination
nodes.rationale: Stable for infinite scroll; opaque cursors hide storage details. Encode nothing sensitive without signing/encrypting.

nodes.label: Pagination limit cap
nodes.rationale: Always cap limit. Default e.g. 20 and max e.g. 100. Never allow limit=999999. Protects DB and API CPU.

nodes.label: Offset pagination
nodes.rationale: Easy, slow on deep pages, unstable if rows insert while paging.

nodes.label: Shared OpenAPI Zod schemas
nodes.rationale: Use the same schemas as Zod when possible to avoid double sources of truth.

nodes.label: Always-200 RPC-over-HTTP
nodes.rationale: Always HTTP 200 with {success:false} is an RPC-over-HTTP habit. Use real statuses; keep error body for details.

nodes.label: HTTP status as contract
nodes.rationale: Useful APIs pick 201/204/400/401/403/404/409 deliberately — not always 200. Rich codes help clients; over-fine codes confuse them.

nodes.label: REST resource modeling
nodes.rationale: Resources are nouns. Prefer /orders/12/items over /getOrderItems. Deep hierarchies complicate authorization and caching.

nodes.label: RPC-style action route
nodes.rationale: RPC-style routes are fine when the domain is an action, not a thing — name them honestly instead of inventing fake nouns.

nodes.label: Static segments before :id
nodes.rationale: /users/export captured by :id unless static segments are registered first.

nodes.label: 201 plus Location
nodes.rationale: Signals a new resource; pairs with Location when useful.

nodes.label: DELETE 204 vs 200
nodes.rationale: 204 if no body; 200 if you return the deleted representation — pick one style.

nodes.label: Merge commit second parent
nodes.rationale: Second parent is the branch merged in; first parent is the branch you were on. --first-parent reads the trunk.

nodes.label: Commit object contents
nodes.rationale: One tree, zero or more parents, author, committer, message. No file contents and no diff.

nodes.label: Author versus committer
nodes.rationale: Author wrote the change; committer created this commit object. Rebase and cherry-pick preserve author.

nodes.label: Annotated tag
nodes.rationale: A real object with tagger, date, message, optional signature. Releases should use git tag -a.

nodes.label: Commit object
nodes.rationale: One tree, parents, author, committer, message. Author and committer diverge on rebase, cherry-pick, and apply.

nodes.label: Lightweight tag
nodes.rationale: Only a file in refs/tags/ containing a hash. Creates no object; git describe ignores it unless --tags.

nodes.label: Commit by hand with plumbing
nodes.rationale: hash-object -w, mktree, commit-tree, update-ref. Omitting update-ref leaves a valid commit reachable from no branch.

nodes.label: Plumbing
nodes.rationale: Stable machine-readable layer for scripts: rev-parse, cat-file, hash-object, commit-tree, update-ref.

nodes.label: Porcelain
nodes.rationale: Human-facing commands whose output may change. 46 main porcelain commands of 172 on PATH.

nodes.label: ECMAScript vs JavaScript
nodes.rationale: ECMAScript is ECMA-262 by TC39. JavaScript is the language plus host APIs. Names differ mostly for trademark reasons.

nodes.label: defer vs async vs type=module
nodes.rationale: defer waits for parse and keeps document order. async runs on arrival with no order. type=module is deferred automatically because the import graph must be fetched first.

nodes.label: Native ESM request waterfall
nodes.rationale: The graph is discovered one level at a time. modulepreload or bundling is why bundlers remain standard despite universal ESM.

nodes.label: browserslist and useBuiltIns usage
nodes.rationale: Targets come from real traffic. useBuiltIns: usage injects only referenced core-js polyfills. Stale IE11 targets bloat every user.

nodes.label: Ponyfill
nodes.rationale: Exports the implementation instead of patching the global. Prefer in libraries. Global polyfills only in an application entry point.

nodes.label: Transpiler vs polyfill
nodes.rationale: A transpiler rewrites syntax at build time. A polyfill adds a missing API at runtime. Neither substitutes for the other.

nodes.label: JSON.stringify throws on BigInt
nodes.rationale: JSON has no BigInt type. Use a replacer to string. Do not patch BigInt.prototype.toJSON.

nodes.label: Engines implement proposals, not editions
nodes.rationale: Since ES2016 one small June edition snapshots Stage 4. Supported in Safari 16.4+ is useful; supported in ES2022 is not.

nodes.label: Hoisting as the creation pass
nodes.rationale: Not code moving. Pass 2 registers declarations: functions fully built, var as undefined, let/const/class with no value.

nodes.label: Temporal dead zone
nodes.rationale: The binding exists but has no value. typeof on a TDZ name throws; typeof on a never-declared name is undefined. TDZ turns silent NaN into an immediate ReferenceError.

nodes.label: Parse, compile, execute
nodes.rationale: The engine reads the entire file before running a line. SyntaxError happens before any code runs; ReferenceError happens during execute.

nodes.label: node --check
nodes.rationale: Parses and reports SyntaxErrors with no execution. Diagnostic for nothing printed at all.

nodes.label: Strict mode
nodes.rationale: ES modules and class bodies are always strict. Know sloppy mode to recognise old files, not to opt in.

nodes.label: const protects the binding, not the value
nodes.rationale: const cart forbids reassignment. cart.qty = 99 is legal. Default to const; let only when the binding changes.
nodes.norm_label: const protects the binding, not the value

nodes.label: Object.freeze is shallow
nodes.rationale: Top-level writes throw in strict mode; nested objects mutate freely. Deep freeze must skip already-frozen objects to survive cycles.

nodes.label: Hoisting and the temporal dead zone
nodes.norm_label: hoisting and the temporal dead zone

nodes.label: Strict mode turns silent failures into errors
nodes.rationale: Undeclared assignment throws, frozen writes throw, this in a plain call is undefined, duplicate params and octals are SyntaxErrors.
nodes.norm_label: strict mode turns silent failures into errors

nodes.label: Primitive copy vs object share
nodes.rationale: Assigning a primitive copies it; assigning an object copies the reference. JS is always pass-by-value, but for objects the value is the reference.

nodes.label: structuredClone
nodes.rationale: Default deep copy: handles cycles, Map, Set, Date. Throws on functions and DOM nodes. JSON.parse(JSON.stringify) drops undefined/functions/symbols, empties Map/Set, NaN→null.

nodes.label: Deep equality
nodes.rationale: Prefer a library (fast-deep-equal, isDeepStrictEqual). Prefer an ETag/updatedAt over deep-comparing API bodies.

nodes.label: JSON.stringify equality failures
nodes.rationale: Key order, dropped undefined, Date→string, Map/Set→{}, NaN/Infinity→null, throws on cycles. Wrong as a general equality function.

nodes.label: Shallow equality
nodes.rationale: One level, Object.is per field, Object.hasOwn not in. Right for immutable React props because a changed branch already has a new reference.

nodes.label: Date relational vs identity
nodes.rationale: Two Dates for the same instant satisfy <= and >= via valueOf timestamps but ==/=== are identity and false. Compare +d1 === +d2.

nodes.label: Immutable updates / structural sharing
nodes.rationale: React change detection is a reference comparison. Mutating in place leaves the reference identical. Return new objects only along the changed path; untouched branches keep their references.

nodes.label: Mixed-direction keyset trap
nodes.rationale: (a,b) < (x,y) means DESC on both. Against ORDER BY created_at DESC, id ASC it returned plausible wrong ids. Needs the expanded comparison plus a matching mixed-direction index.

nodes.label: Index Cond vs Filter
nodes.rationale: Index Cond decides where the scan starts and stops. Filter is applied to rows already produced.

nodes.label: OFFSET vs keyset at depth
nodes.rationale: OFFSET 499980 produced 500000 rows and 501918 buffers to return 20 — 295.87 ms vs 1.23 ms keyset. OFFSET does not skip rows; it produces and discards them.

nodes.label: Row constructor (a, b) < ($1, $2)
nodes.rationale: Lexicographic comparison matching ORDER BY. Becomes Index Cond (0.99 ms, 23 buffers). Expanded OR becomes Filter and removed 250001 rows (158.12 ms).

nodes.label: Forgotten client.release
nodes.rationale: With max: 2, call 3 failed after 1501 ms. pool.end stayed pending until stranded clients were released.

nodes.label: Executor db argument
nodes.rationale: Every repository function takes something with .query(text, params) as its first argument. It never imports the pool. BoundPool and Client returned identical results from the same function body.

nodes.label: Pool vs Client at the wire
nodes.rationale: pool.query checks out, runs one statement, and returns the connection. Consecutive calls can be different sessions and snapshots. A client is one connection held for a transaction.
nodes.norm_label: pool vs client at the wire

nodes.label: Per-test transaction rollback
nodes.rationale: BEGIN in beforeEach, ROLLBACK in afterEach. 1.66 ms vs 42.50 ms truncate-and-reseed (25×). Parallel-safe because nothing is committed.

nodes.label: Pool cannot see the test fixture
nodes.rationale: Uncommitted data is invisible to other connections. Test client saw 1 row; pool saw 0. The harness enforces the executor contract.
nodes.norm_label: pool cannot see the test fixture

nodes.label: BEFORE UPDATE updated_at trigger
nodes.rationale: App-managed updated_at stayed stale on an UPDATE that never mentioned it. Trigger moved it. Cost 1.23–1.29× on the update (328.9 vs 266.8 ms). BEFORE can assign NEW; AFTER would need a second UPDATE.

nodes.label: now() is the transaction timestamp
nodes.rationale: Every row in one transaction shares updated_at. clock_timestamp() moved 303 ms. That is why updated_at cannot be an optimistic-concurrency version.

nodes.label: Idle in transaction from a non-query await
nodes.rationale: A 1240 ms payment call held the transaction open 1223 ms: occupies a pool slot, holds locks, and pins xmin so VACUUM cannot clean tables the endpoint never touches.
nodes.norm_label: idle in transaction from a non-query await

nodes.label: pool.query BEGIN is not a transaction
nodes.rationale: Each pool.query checks out its own connection. On an idle pool it appears to work (same pid). With 8 concurrent inserts, 7 of 8 writes survived ROLLBACK.
nodes.norm_label: pool.query begin is not a transaction

nodes.label: withTransaction
nodes.rationale: connect, BEGIN, fn(client), COMMIT; ROLLBACK in catch (its own try/catch so it cannot replace the original error); release in finally.

nodes.label: IS DISTINCT FROM no-op skip
nodes.rationale: SET city = city still wrote a row version (rowCount 1). AND city IS DISTINCT FROM $2 skipped it. <> is NULL when either side is NULL.

nodes.label: Phase 10 — Indexes and the query planner
nodes.norm_label: phase 10 — indexes and the query planner

nodes.label: When OFFSET is still right
nodes.rationale: At 50 pages OFFSET was 0.9× keyset. At 500 pages keyset was 6.4× faster. Use OFFSET for shallow page-number UIs; keyset for feeds, APIs, exports, crawlers.

nodes.label: var loop shared binding
nodes.rationale: var is function-scoped so every closure sees the final value; let creates one binding per iteration.

nodes.label: Counter factory private state
nodes.rationale: Each factory call is a new scope; closures created together share that one scope.

nodes.label: Stale-closure bug
nodes.rationale: Closing over a copy freezes the creation-time value; React effects hit the same mechanism.

nodes.label: V8 captures referenced variables
nodes.rationale: Unused 300k-row arrays added 0 MB; referencing one element retained 69 MB. Engine optimisation, not a spec guarantee.

nodes.label: IIFE loop-variable capture
nodes.rationale: A parameter is a fresh binding per call; let automates the pre-ES6 IIFE fix.

nodes.label: let per-iteration binding
nodes.rationale: Closures mutating their own n yield [10,11,12] then [20,21,22]; one shared binding would be [10,20,30].

nodes.label: Closure captures the variable
nodes.rationale: A reader created while x was 'first' returns later values after reassignment.

nodes.label: Private state and memory
nodes.rationale: The same capture that gives privacy also keeps memory alive as long as the function lives.

nodes.label: What is captured
nodes.rationale: A closure holds the binding and reads it at call time, not a snapshot.

nodes.label: Arrow has no prototype
nodes.rationale: prototype is genuinely absent; new throws TypeError: A is not a constructor. this/arguments/super/new.target are inherited, not missing.

nodes.label: Class field arrow vs prototype method
nodes.rationale: One closure per instance, own enumerable, not stubbable on the prototype; use when a detached handler must keep this.
nodes.norm_label: class field arrow vs prototype method

nodes.label: Concise-body object-literal trap
nodes.rationale: n => { value: n } is a labelled statement returning undefined; wrap as ({ value: n }).

nodes.label: Four this binding rules
nodes.rationale: Default, implicit, explicit, and new; extracting a method into a variable loses implicit this.

nodes.label: Arrow functions and this
nodes.rationale: An arrow is a different callable: no own this, arguments, super, new.target, or prototype.

nodes.label: Lexical this and missing bindings
nodes.rationale: An arrow has no this; this is a free variable resolved through the scope chain.

nodes.label: Arrow syntax and when not to use one
nodes.rationale: Concise bodies are expressions; braces start a block. Arrows are for callbacks, not methods or constructors.
nodes.norm_label: arrow syntax and when not to use one

nodes.label: call, apply and bind
nodes.rationale: call/apply invoke now; bind returns a new function with this fixed.

nodes.label: this
nodes.rationale: this is an argument decided by the call site, not a variable decided by definition.

nodes.label: Class inner immutable binding
nodes.rationale: Inside the class body the class name is const-like. Outside it is a reassignable let-like binding.

nodes.label: Class lexical declaration
nodes.rationale: class is TDZ, block-scoped, and never creates globalThis properties — like let, not like function.

nodes.label: Three class member destinations
nodes.rationale: Fields are own per instance; methods live on Ctor.prototype; statics live on the class object; #fields are private slots.

nodes.label: Five non-sugar class features
nodes.rationale: Always-strict body; TypeError without new; non-enumerable methods; TDZ/block scope; private elements.

nodes.label: Static initialization block
nodes.rationale: Statements plus private-scope access. Evaluated at the class statement, top to bottom with static fields.

nodes.label: Static members
nodes.rationale: Live on the class object, which is not on the instance prototype chain. instance.staticThing is undefined.

nodes.label: this in a static method is the class
nodes.rationale: new this(...) makes a factory inherit: User.create builds a User because extends also links class objects.
nodes.norm_label: this in a static method is the class

nodes.label: Class body is always strict
nodes.rationale: No opt-out. Unbound this is undefined; implicit globals and several silent failures become errors.

nodes.label: class is half sugar
nodes.rationale: Lookup machinery is unchanged — methods go on Ctor.prototype. Five other behaviours are real language features.

nodes.label: Private field brand check
nodes.rationale: ES2022 #field in obj asks whether this class constructed the object. Unforgeable unlike instanceof (Symbol.hasInstance, reassigned prototype, cross-realm). Legal only inside the declaring class; avoids try/catch TypeError on undeclared privates.

nodes.label: Property shadowing
nodes.rationale: The first own match hides the further one. The prototype value is untouched and still reachable via Object.getPrototypeOf(o).b.

nodes.label: Prototype chain lookup
nodes.rationale: Walk own then each [[Prototype]] until a match or null. A miss is the most expensive lookup. Nothing is copied onto instances. Array methods live on Array.prototype, not the array.

nodes.label: class as prototype sugar
nodes.rationale: Class methods land on Ctor.prototype; the chain is identical. Adds #private, extends, strict bodies, throw-without-new, and non-enumerable methods. Hand-assigned prototype methods stay enumerable.

nodes.label: prototype.constructor back-reference
nodes.rationale: Own property of Fn.prototype. Replacing prototype wholesale drops it — hence Child.prototype.constructor = Child. Writable and forgeable; never use for type checks. Some built-ins read it via Symbol.species.

nodes.label: Constructor.prototype property
nodes.rationale: Ordinary property only functions have — the [[Prototype]] given to new instances. Not the function's own prototype; Object.getPrototypeOf(Box) is Function.prototype.

nodes.label: new operator
nodes.rationale: Creates an object whose [[Prototype]] is Fn.prototype, calls Fn with this bound to it, returns it unless the body returns an object. Methods are shared, not copied. Lookup is dynamic.

nodes.label: Shared mutable prototype state
nodes.rationale: Fn.prototype.items = [] is one array. push mutates after a read, so no shadow is created and every instance sees the change. Put mutable values on the instance (class field or constructor).

nodes.label: Writes create own properties
nodes.rationale: Reads walk the chain; assignment does not. Inherited setters intercept the write; inherited read-only throws in strict mode. Inherited defaults work because assignment shadows.

nodes.label: Hole-skipping array methods
nodes.rationale: forEach map filter some every reduce skip holes. for-of spread Array.from find includes join sort treat holes as undefined.

nodes.label: Iteration callback arity
nodes.rationale: Callbacks receive (element, index, array). Most methods take thisArg; reduce and sort do not.

nodes.label: find visits holes
nodes.rationale: find/findIndex visit every index treating holes as undefined; forEach/map/filter/every skip holes.

nodes.label: map(parseInt) radix trap
nodes.rationale: map passes index as parseInt radix, so ["1","2","3"].map(parseInt) is [1, NaN, NaN].

nodes.label: reduce initialValue
nodes.rationale: Without it the first element is the acc, iteration starts at 1, empty throws TypeError, single element skips the callback.

nodes.label: reduce pipe and asyncPipe
nodes.rationale: Fold over functions: pipe applies each; asyncPipe sequences via acc.then(fn).

nodes.label: Array.prototype.reduce
nodes.rationale: Callback is (acc, cur, index, array). Second argument is initialValue, so no thisArg. Equivalent to a for-of fold.

nodes.label: Array.prototype.reduceRight
nodes.rationale: Needed only when the operation is not associative — compose, string building, nested wrapping.

nodes.label: reduce readability rule
nodes.rationale: Scalar folds and folds over functions are clear. A growing-collection reduce is usually a loop or groupBy.

nodes.label: forEach async trap
nodes.rationale: forEach does not wait for promises. async callbacks are discarded; filter(async) keeps everything because promises are truthy.

nodes.label: every vacuous truth
nodes.rationale: every([]) is true; some([]) is false. Gates need length > 0 && every(...).

nodes.label: Array.prototype.filter
nodes.rationale: New array of all matches after a full pass. filter(...)[0] is a misuse of find.

nodes.label: Array.prototype.find
nodes.rationale: First match or undefined; stops early. findIndex returns -1; never truthiness-check the index.

nodes.label: Array.prototype.forEach
nodes.rationale: Always returns undefined and cannot break except by throwing. Wrong tool for early exit or await.

nodes.label: Map.groupBy vs Object.groupBy
nodes.rationale: Prefer Map.groupBy: any key type and insertion order. Object.groupBy stringifies and re-sorts integer-like keys.

nodes.label: for...of
nodes.rationale: Iterates values via Symbol.iterator. Supports break and await. Default for values.

nodes.label: forEach cannot break or await
nodes.rationale: return inside forEach returns from the callback only. forEach(async) discards promises.

nodes.label: Named methods instead of reduce
nodes.rationale: flat, groupBy, flatMap, Set dedupe, find, filter. Grouping is the most common legitimate-looking misuse.

nodes.label: Array.prototype.map
nodes.rationale: Allocates a same-length array of return values. Not a loop for side effects.

nodes.label: String.prototype.at
nodes.rationale: Accepts negative indices; brackets do not. Out of range is undefined; charAt returns "".

nodes.label: String.prototype.slice
nodes.rationale: Negatives count from the end; start>end yields "". Matches Array.prototype.slice. Prefer over substring.

nodes.label: Replacement $ patterns
nodes.rationale: $& $` $' $1 $<name> $$ are special. Use the function form so dynamic replacements stay literal.

nodes.label: padStart target length
nodes.rationale: First arg is total length, not pad count. Never truncates. Multi-char pads repeat then cut.

nodes.label: String.prototype.replace
nodes.rationale: With a string pattern replaces only the first match.

nodes.label: String.prototype.replaceAll
nodes.rationale: Replaces all. Regex must be global or TypeError. String patterns are literal — safer than RegExp(userInput).

nodes.label: String trim family
nodes.rationale: trim/trimStart/trimEnd remove whitespace only; no trim(char). Use at the input boundary.

nodes.label: slice vs substring and replace vs replaceAll
nodes.rationale: Use slice not substring; never build a regex from user input — replaceAll with a string matches literally.
nodes.norm_label: slice vs substring and replace vs replaceall

nodes.label: PG Part 3 Node and raw pg
nodes.norm_label: pg part 3 node and raw pg

nodes.label: Never use localhost for pg
nodes.rationale: Examples run against 127.0.0.1:55432, never localhost — the IPv6 trap.

nodes.label: Recap rule Node Phase 6
nodes.rationale: Pool sizing, transaction propagation, N+1 and ORM comparison recap in ≤40 lines and link to Node Phase 6.

nodes.label: lag vs I/O wait
nodes.rationale: Downstream API slowness is not loop lag. Sync bcrypt/image resize is. GC thrashing shows as bursty lag. Lag says you are stuck, not why.

nodes.label: monitorEventLoopDelay
nodes.rationale: Histogram values are nanoseconds. Idle p50 sits near the sampling resolution, so do not alert on p50 below that floor. max is the smoke alarm; p99 is the trend.

nodes.label: low lag high p99
nodes.rationale: Waiting on I/O or a queue, not blocking the event loop. Look at downstream and pool wait times, not a CPU profile.

nodes.label: acceptingTraffic flag
nodes.rationale: Flip true only after config, pools, and listen. Flip false on SIGTERM before closing the server.

nodes.label: liveness probe
nodes.rationale: Kill me if I am stuck. Must depend on almost nothing. A DB check here turns a dependency blip into a restart storm.

nodes.label: readiness probe
nodes.rationale: Stop sending me traffic if I cannot serve. Allowed to check the pool (select 1, short timeout). Fail first on SIGTERM so the balancer drains before exit.

nodes.label: V8 heapUsed
nodes.rationale: heapUsed climbing under flat traffic is the leak signal; heapTotal growth can just be V8 reservation.

nodes.label: process.memoryUsage()
nodes.rationale: Returns rss, heapTotal, heapUsed, external, and arrayBuffers so you can tell OS charge from V8 live heap.

nodes.label: RSS resident set size
nodes.rationale: Alert on RSS and cgroup memory for Kubernetes OOM risk; kubelet kills on container memory, not V8 heapUsed.

nodes.label: v8.getHeapStatistics()
nodes.rationale: heap_size_limit is not always equal to --max-old-space-size; the limit covers more than old space.

nodes.label: cluster module vs replicas
nodes.rationale: Inside Kubernetes prefer replicas over nesting cluster in each pod.

nodes.label: Vertical vs horizontal scaling
nodes.rationale: One Node process uses one JS core well; extra cores need more processes.

nodes.label: Warm isolate connection reuse
nodes.rationale: Hundreds of isolates times pool size exhausts Postgres; cap pool at 1 or use a proxy.

nodes.label: One process supervisor
nodes.rationale: Do not run pm2 inside Kubernetes; double supervision fights on restarts and muddies PID 1.

nodes.label: Phase 0 gate
nodes.rationale: Explain type-change remounts without saying virtual DOM; what the DOM contains during render; what StrictMode double-mount tests.

nodes.label: sandbox/react-p0
nodes.rationale: Every Phase 0 console block is produced by a named script in sandbox/react-p0/.

nodes.label: defaultProps ignored on function components
nodes.rationale: Use default parameters. Silent — not an error.

nodes.label: Phase 1 gate
nodes.rationale: Hand-compile JSX including where key goes; predict swap with index vs stable keys; explain the && zero.

nodes.label: Lifting state up
nodes.rationale: Remove, hardcode, add state — and the re-render that moves with it.

nodes.label: Portals
nodes.rationale: Moves the DOM node, keeps the React tree — including events.

nodes.label: propTypes removed silently
nodes.rationale: React 19 ignores propTypes with no warning, so an upgrade quietly deletes runtime prop checks.

nodes.label: Object.is comparison
nodes.rationale: React compares state with Object.is. Mutate and the update vanishes with no error.

nodes.label: React claimed by session 52a29103
nodes.rationale: Owner since 2026-08-13 for the whole of docs/react/. Other sessions must not write React pages.

nodes.label: Phase 1 — JSX and what a component returns
nodes.norm_label: phase 1 — jsx and what a component returns

nodes.label: React 19 ships no UMD build
nodes.rationale: Browser experiments are bundled with esbuild and served to Firefox over puppeteer-core.

nodes.label: Phase 0 is not optional
nodes.rationale: Every 'React is weird' complaint — reset state, doubled effects, one-update-behind values — traces back to how React runs.

nodes.label: The && zero trap
nodes.rationale: {items.length && <List/>} can put a 0 on the screen because 0 and NaN do not vanish.

nodes.label: JSX is not a template language
nodes.rationale: JSX is syntax for one function call. Costly mistakes: 0 appearing in a list, onclick never firing, typed text following the wrong row.
nodes.norm_label: jsx is not a template language

nodes.label: Skipping a render is a hint
nodes.rationale: shouldComponentUpdate docs say React may re-render anyway — memoization is not a correctness mechanism.
nodes.norm_label: skipping a render is a hint

nodes.label: Phase 2 has no sandbox
nodes.rationale: Validated against react.dev Learn/Reference, React 19 upgrade guide, and legacy.reactjs.org.

nodes.label: Sandbox-proven versus documentation-validated
nodes.rationale: Phases 0–1 keep sandbox console blocks. From Phase 2 onward claims are validated against react.dev/MDN with no invented output.

nodes.label: console.log stdout backpressure
nodes.rationale: console is synchronous on some destinations; a slow stdout pipe can block the event loop under a traffic spike.

nodes.label: Log data minimization vs redaction
nodes.rationale: Minimization means not putting sensitive fields on the object; redaction is a seatbelt for fields that slipped through.

nodes.label: Never log secrets or payment data
nodes.rationale: Passwords, tokens, PAN/CVV, government ids, and private keys must not appear; log stores often have wider read access than the database.
nodes.norm_label: never log secrets or payment data

nodes.label: NODE_ENV is not a feature flag
nodes.rationale: NODE_ENV=production changes dependency behaviour; use explicit flags for product tiers.
nodes.norm_label: node_env is not a feature flag

nodes.label: 12-factor config
nodes.rationale: Config in the environment, validated at start, no production secrets in the repo, no silent defaults for connection strings.

nodes.label: AbortSignal.any composition
nodes.rationale: Compose timeout, client disconnect and shutdown; whichever fires first cancels the shared signal.

nodes.label: Cooperative cancellation
nodes.rationale: A signal is not preemptive. Loops must throwIfAborted; a synchronous JSON.parse cannot be interrupted.

nodes.label: Deadline propagation
nodes.rationale: Thread one AbortSignal through every layer so a cancelled request stops the DB, outbound calls and worker slot it started.

nodes.label: Timeout is unknown not failure
nodes.rationale: The request may have completed after you stopped waiting. The retry is a second execution.

nodes.label: statement_timeout vs query_timeout
nodes.rationale: statement_timeout is server-enforced and cancels the query. query_timeout only stops the client wait.

nodes.label: Propagation stops at the queue
nodes.rationale: A cancelled request must not cancel work already enqueued or already committed.

nodes.label: Retry at one layer
nodes.rationale: Client × service × job attempts multiply (5×5×5=125). Pick the outermost layer that knows the operation.

nodes.label: Timeouts shrink down the stack
nodes.rationale: A caller's timeout must exceed the callee's. Otherwise the client gives up while you still hold resources.

nodes.label: Timeout budget
nodes.rationale: One deadline for the operation; each step gets remaining time. Three 5s timeouts are a 15s request.

nodes.label: PostgreSQL connection URI
nodes.rationale: postgresql://USER:PASSWORD@HOST:PORT/DATABASE, or PGHOST/PGPORT/PGUSER/PGPASSWORD/PGDATABASE. DATABASE_URL is an app convention, not read by psql.

nodes.label: pg_hba.conf
nodes.rationale: Decides who may connect how (trust, scram-sha-256, peer) from which addresses. Managed providers force TLS plus password/SCRAM.

nodes.label: SQLSTATE 28P01
nodes.rationale: invalid_password / authentication failure. Map this when diagnosing auth failures from Node.

nodes.label: session_user vs current_user
nodes.rationale: session_user is who authenticated; current_user can change after SET ROLE. Node uses the connection-string role.

nodes.label: Role is user and group
nodes.rationale: A user is a role with LOGIN; a group is a role usually without LOGIN used for membership. One catalog concept.

nodes.label: Least privilege GRANT REVOKE
nodes.rationale: Master-tier: Roles, GRANT and REVOKE. Phase gate: privileges are least.

nodes.label: Secrets: no URI in logs
nodes.rationale: Master-tier secrets page. Completes the Phase 13 gate: secrets are safe.

nodes.label: Never log the connection string
nodes.rationale: URIs embed secrets. Error handlers and APM breadcrumbs become credential stores if they print DATABASE_URL.

nodes.label: Least-privilege app role
nodes.rationale: Container bootstrap is a superuser — fine for learning, wrong as the production app role. App DML only; not arbitrary DDL.

nodes.label: Case-insensitive unique index
nodes.rationale: CREATE UNIQUE INDEX ON users (lower(email)) enforces case-insensitive uniqueness without citext.

nodes.label: Expression index
nodes.rationale: Index the function result when the query cannot leave the column bare. The query must spell the expression identically; each queried expression needs its own index.

nodes.label: Expression-index statistics
nodes.rationale: ANALYZE collects statistics for the expression itself under the index name in pg_stats, so the planner stops guessing selectivity.

nodes.label: Partial index
nodes.rationale: CREATE INDEX ... WHERE indexes only matching rows. 8792 kB full vs 104 kB for 4000 live of 400000. Writes to the other 99% never touch it.

nodes.label: Partial UNIQUE
nodes.rationale: CREATE UNIQUE INDEX ON slugs (slug) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL: any number of deleted duplicates, exactly one live. Still raises 23505.

nodes.label: IMMUTABLE index expression
nodes.rationale: Anything whose result depends on session TimeZone or now() is STABLE, not IMMUTABLE, and cannot be indexed (42P17). Name the zone: date_trunc('day', ts, 'UTC') or (ts AT TIME ZONE 'UTC')::date.

nodes.label: Partial-index predicate implication
nodes.rationale: The planner must prove the query WHERE implies the index WHERE. Write the predicate as a literal, not a parameter, so generic plans still match.

nodes.label: pg_notify
nodes.rationale: Takes a string channel used exactly as given and can be computed. NOTIFY folds unquoted identifiers.

nodes.label: Materialized view
nodes.rationale: Stores the query result as a table. Not automatically faster; wins only when the underlying query is genuinely expensive.

nodes.label: REFRESH CONCURRENTLY
nodes.rationale: Diffs new vs old so it needs a unique index (else 55000). 1.6× slower but does not block readers (2 ms vs 32 ms wait).

nodes.label: LANGUAGE sql
nodes.rationale: Can be inlined so the planner sees real statistics (60 rows vs plpgsql's 1000). Standalone timing is the same; joins are where it matters.

nodes.label: PL/pgSQL
nodes.rationale: Required for trigger bodies. A black box to the planner: fixed 1000-row estimate wrecks joins. Default: sql for one query, plpgsql for triggers, app otherwise.

nodes.label: Function volatility markers
nodes.rationale: IMMUTABLE foldable and indexable; STABLE inlinable; VOLATILE (default) blocks inlining. Lying about IMMUTABLE gives wrong answers, not errors.

nodes.label: CREATE PROCEDURE
nodes.rationale: Exists so it can COMMIT mid-body. Invoked with CALL. Useless inside an application BEGIN/COMMIT wrapper (2D000).

nodes.label: Matview staleness
nodes.rationale: Nothing refreshes it. Schedule the refresh; a trigger-driven refresh puts a full recompute inside a write transaction.

nodes.label: Procedure mid-body COMMIT
nodes.rationale: Same COMMIT in a FUNCTION is 2D000. Only works when no transaction is already open. Failures leave work partly done; the procedure must be resumable.

nodes.label: Database health and alerting
nodes.rationale: pg_stat_database for system health. Alert on connections, oldest xact, idle-in-xact, lag, dead tuples, deadlocks, temp_bytes, disk.

nodes.label: Table health
nodes.rationale: pg_stat_user_tables for seq scans, dead tuples, autovacuum. Unused indexes via idx_scan=0 with cautions.

nodes.label: The query buffer and the editor
nodes.norm_label: the query buffer and the editor

nodes.label: GIN-indexable array containment
nodes.rationale: @> uses GIN; = ANY(arr) does not, even though they are logically equivalent.

nodes.label: Composite type as column
nodes.rationale: No per-field constraints or FKs; adding a field rewrites every table using the type; pg returns an unparsed string.

nodes.label: jsonb
nodes.rationale: Only jsonb supports equality, containment and GIN; json cannot be GIN-indexed (42704).

nodes.label: Array versus child table
nodes.rationale: Arrays cannot carry foreign keys (42804) or per-element metadata; MVCC rewrites the whole row on any element change.

nodes.label: jsonb key versus real column
nodes.rationale: Promote a key to a column as soon as you filter or join on it; a jsonb key has no CHECK, FK or cheap B-tree.

nodes.label: UNLOGGED tables
nodes.rationale: Skip WAL: ~1.5× faster (150→98 ms / 100k inserts). Truncated on crash recovery, never replicated, survive clean restart. Right for regenerable staging and caches.

nodes.label: date maps to JS Date at local midnight
nodes.rationale: pg maps date to Date at local midnight. On UTC+5:30, date '2026-01-01' becomes 2025-12-31T18:30:00Z. Return to_char or setTypeParser(1082).
nodes.norm_label: date maps to js date at local midnight

nodes.label: now() is transaction start time
nodes.rationale: now() aliases transaction_timestamp(); two inserts 150 ms apart share a timestamp. statement_timestamp() is per statement; clock_timestamp() is wall clock.

nodes.label: Gap filling with generate_series
nodes.rationale: LEFT JOIN from the series so missing days survive. count(e.id) not count(*) — count(*) is 1 even with no match. Series must be the left side.

nodes.label: generate_series
