nodes.rationale: Set-returning function that invents rows. Both endpoints inclusive (hourly over one day → 25). Descending needs a negative step; default +1 silently returns no rows. Step 0 → 22023.

nodes.label: SRF planner assumes 1000 rows
nodes.rationale: No statistics for a generated set; unbounded series is a memory problem. Materialise and ANALYZE a huge series if join order goes wrong.

nodes.label: WITH ORDINALITY
nodes.rationale: Adds a position column to any SRF so client-supplied order survives a join. unnest(ARRAY['c','a','b']) WITH ORDINALITY → positions 1,2,3.

nodes.label: INSERT speed ladder
nodes.rationale: 10k rows: per-row autocommit 19551 ms; one tx 2262 ms (8.6×); multi-row VALUES 148 ms; unnest 81 ms; COPY 243 ms. WAL flush per statement plus round trips dominate.

nodes.label: 65535 bind-parameter ceiling
nodes.rationale: Protocol stores parameter count in 16 bits. 21845×3 ok; 21846 → 08P01 about parameter formats, not the limit. Chunk or unnest one array per column.

nodes.label: LEFT JOIN count(*) trap
nodes.rationale: count(*) after a one-to-many LEFT JOIN counts joined rows, not left-side parents.

nodes.label: Join fan-out
nodes.rationale: Each matching child duplicates the parent; aggregates on the parent then inflate.

nodes.label: LATERAL pre-aggregation
nodes.rationale: Aggregate the many-side first, then join one row back, so the parent is never duplicated.

nodes.label: count(column)
nodes.rationale: Skips NULL in that column; not a faster count(*).

nodes.label: count(*)
nodes.rationale: Counts rows, including rows whose columns are NULL.

nodes.label: sum(DISTINCT) is not a fix
nodes.rationale: Distinct values can still collide across parents; it hides the fan-out instead of removing it.

nodes.label: count(1) folklore
nodes.rationale: count(1) is not cheaper than count(*); both count rows.

nodes.label: Macrotasks
nodes.rationale: Timers, setImmediate and I/O callbacks belong to event-loop phases and get one turn per lap. Microtasks and nextTick are not phases; they drain between every phase and every callback.

nodes.label: process.nextTick queue
nodes.rationale: Drains completely at a checkpoint, including entries added while draining, before the microtask queue. That complete drain is what makes recursive nextTick starvation possible.

nodes.label: queueMicrotask vs process.nextTick
nodes.rationale: Prefer queueMicrotask: portable, same queue as promises, less starvation. nextTick only when you must run before pending promise continuations, classically deferring an emit so a caller can subscribe.

nodes.label: setImmediate
nodes.rationale: Schedules into the check phase, after poll in the same lap. Use it to run after the current phase, yield so I/O can run, or chunk CPU work. Does not escape a blocked thread.

nodes.label: setTimeout(fn, 0) 1ms clamp
nodes.rationale: There is no true zero delay. The timer is clamped to 1ms and runs in the timers phase on a later lap. Almost always the wrong tool versus setImmediate.

nodes.label: nextTick starvation
nodes.rationale: Recursive process.nextTick never empties the queue, so the loop never advances. Process stays alive at 100% CPU with no error; timers, I/O and setImmediate never run.

nodes.label: setInterval drift and overlap
nodes.rationale: Schedules by period, not completion. Slow async work queues and spacing collapses. Prefer a self-scheduling timeout after the work finishes.

nodes.label: Timeout object
nodes.rationale: Node setTimeout/setInterval return a Timeout with unref, ref and refresh, not a number as in browsers. Treat the return as opaque.

nodes.label: TimeoutOverflowWarning
nodes.rationale: Delays above 2147483647 ms (~24.8 days) overflow and fire immediately with a warning. Long schedules need stages or an absolute-time check.

nodes.label: Chunk CPU work with setImmediate
nodes.rationale: Yield to check so pending I/O runs. Aim 10–50ms per chunk. Improves others' latency, not throughput. Occasional work that splits naturally.

nodes.label: Phase 2 output-order gate
nodes.rationale: Move on when you can predict order of nextTick, queueMicrotask, resolved promise, setTimeout(0) and setImmediate, including that nextTick priority depends on already being inside a microtask.

nodes.label: Phase 2 — Async and the event loop
nodes.norm_label: phase 2 — async and the event loop

nodes.label: ESM top-level is a microtask
nodes.rationale: Module evaluation is a promise job, so nextTick scheduled at ESM top level runs after pending microtasks. Identical code as .cjs and .js prints different order.

nodes.label: setImmediate wins inside an I/O callback
nodes.rationale: I/O callbacks run in poll; check is the next phase in the same lap. A timer must wait a full lap, so setImmediate always runs first inside any I/O callback.
nodes.norm_label: setimmediate wins inside an i/o callback

nodes.label: Main-module setImmediate vs setTimeout race
nodes.rationale: Order depends on whether process startup took >=1ms before the first timers phase. Both orders are correct. CI machines are slower so the timer more often wins.

nodes.label: nextTick drain-to-exhaustion rule
nodes.rationale: The nextTick queue drains including entries added during draining. Bounded recursion still delays the loop for the whole drain; await cannot fix it because microtasks also drain before the loop.

nodes.label: Recursive setImmediate does not starve
nodes.rationale: setImmediate schedules into check, one turn per lap, so timers fire and I/O is served. Recursion belongs on setImmediate, never on nextTick.

nodes.label: Timer delay is a floor
nodes.rationale: The callback runs no earlier than the delay, when the loop next reaches timers and the thread is free. A long callback elsewhere delays it arbitrarily.

nodes.label: GroupAggregate
nodes.rationale: Aggregates already-sorted input; used when an index or Sort already matches the grouping keys.

nodes.label: HashAggregate
nodes.rationale: Builds a hash table of groups in work_mem; preferred when no ordered input is required.

nodes.label: work_mem Batches spill
nodes.rationale: When the hash table exceeds work_mem, HashAggregate spills Batches to disk.

nodes.label: GROUP BY equals DISTINCT
nodes.rationale: GROUP BY on every selected column is the same uniqueness as SELECT DISTINCT.

nodes.label: GROUP BY evaluation order
nodes.rationale: GROUP BY ordinals refer to SELECT-list positions; aliases are visible there after the SELECT is parsed.

nodes.label: MixedAggregate is not parallel
nodes.rationale: Grouping-sets plans use MixedAggregate and do not parallelize the way a single HashAggregate can.

nodes.label: GROUP BY does not order
nodes.rationale: HashAggregate returns groups in hash order; only ORDER BY is a contract.

nodes.label: Retry 40001 and 40P01
nodes.rationale: Serialization failure and deadlock are isolation machinery, not bugs. Retry the whole transaction with backoff and jitter.

nodes.label: Branch on err.code SQLSTATE
nodes.rationale: Never branch on err.message. Messages are localised and version-dependent. SQLSTATEs are a stable five-character contract.

nodes.label: Creating tables from Node
nodes.rationale: pg will run CREATE TABLE. The question is when: from a replayable migration, never from a request handler and never from application startup.

nodes.label: IF NOT EXISTS is a name-only check
nodes.rationale: Does not compare columns, types, constraints or indexes. ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS with a different type is a silent no-op and a type mismatch.
nodes.norm_label: if not exists is a name-only check

nodes.label: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS race
nodes.rationale: 228 of 500 concurrent attempts failed with 23505 on pg_type_typname_nsp_index. Catalog check and insert are not one atomic step.
nodes.norm_label: create table if not exists race

nodes.label: DDL from Node three chunks
nodes.rationale: 01 issuing DDL through the driver; 02 DDL locks and blocking; 03 startup races and advisory locks.

nodes.label: err.detail leaks data
nodes.rationale: detail contains the submitted value and enables user enumeration. Log it; never serialise the raw error to a client.

nodes.label: IF NOT EXISTS is not a migration system
nodes.rationale: Idempotent, not concurrency-safe, not a definition check, and leaves no version record. Migrations fail loudly when a database is in an unexpected state.
nodes.norm_label: if not exists is not a migration system

nodes.label: Initializer purity (Strict Mode)
nodes.rationale: Strict Mode double-invokes the initializer in development and discards one result. Side effects belong in an effect, which has cleanup.

nodes.label: Lazy initial state
nodes.rationale: useState(expensive()) evaluates every render and discards the result after the first. Passing a function runs the work once per instance.

nodes.label: Lazy ref pattern
nodes.rationale: useRef has no lazy form; a function argument becomes the ref contents. Initialise to null and assign inside if (ref.current === null).

nodes.label: Hook call order / state slots
nodes.rationale: There is no name. React matches slots by call order. A hook inside a condition shifts later slots when the condition flips.

nodes.label: Initial value is only initial
nodes.rationale: useState's argument is read once at that position. A later prop change does not update it. Derive, remount with key, or accept a deliberate draft.

nodes.label: useState
nodes.rationale: Returns a per-render snapshot and a setter. State lives outside the component, keyed by position, matched by hook call order.

nodes.label: State preserved by position and type
nodes.rationale: Same type at the same render-tree position keeps state. A different type at that position destroys the entire subtree. Position is not DOM position.
nodes.norm_label: state preserved by position and type

nodes.label: Conditional wrapper remount
nodes.rationale: Adding a wrapper in one branch changes depth, so React unmounts the old subtree. Keep one tree shape and vary className instead.

nodes.label: What a key change destroys
nodes.rationale: State, refs, DOM nodes, focus, scroll, CSS animations, uncontrolled inputs, and every effect cleanup. Use when a reset is wanted, not as a general refresh.

nodes.label: Resetting state with key
nodes.rationale: A key becomes part of position. A changed key unmounts the old subtree and mounts a new one with fresh state, covering children an effect would miss and avoiding a stale frame.

nodes.label: Index keys attach state to position
nodes.rationale: Index keys do not remount. React matches key 0 to key 0, so per-row state stays with the slot while data moves underneath.
nodes.norm_label: index keys attach state to position

nodes.label: Lift per-row UI state to the list
nodes.rationale: Keying expandedId by item id removes per-position state that can attach to the wrong row. Uncontrolled inputs still need correct keys.
nodes.norm_label: lift per-row ui state to the list

nodes.label: Editor vs CI file-set disagreement
nodes.rationale: A file nobody imports and include misses is checked when opened and never in CI. Ambient @types also depend on cwd.

nodes.label: Language server is not the build
nodes.rationale: Editor is a long-lived server on open files, often the bundled compiler, including unsaved buffers. CI is tsc --noEmit, cold, the include set, the repo version.
nodes.norm_label: language server is not the build

nodes.label: Stale TS Server state
nodes.rationale: Incremental cache can go stale after checkout, install, or tsconfig edit. Restart TS Server; delete .tsbuildinfo if it persists.

nodes.label: TypeScript Playground
nodes.rationale: Isolation: reproduce without your tsconfig/@types/editor version, toggle one option, switch compiler versions, inspect emitted JS, share a runnable link.

nodes.label: exclude dist from the program
nodes.rationale: Otherwise a previous build's .d.ts and .js become inputs and produce duplicate-identifier errors.

nodes.label: exclude only removes roots
nodes.rationale: An excluded file imported by an included file is still checked. exclude is not a veto.

nodes.label: tsconfig.json two jobs
nodes.rationale: Defines which files are the project (include/exclude/files/references) and what rules they are checked under (compilerOptions).

nodes.label: verbatimModuleSyntax
nodes.rationale: Emit imports exactly as written. Forces import type for type-only imports; removes compiler guesswork a single-file transpiler cannot perform.

nodes.label: Second tsconfig when rules differ
nodes.rationale: Need two configs when lib/types/module differ (app vs vite.config), not merely when folders differ. Keep rootDir/outDir/include out of the shared base.

nodes.label: Phase 0 measurement corrections
nodes.rationale: strict defaults true in TS7; TS7 speed-up is 3× not 10×; compiler API moved to unstable/; tsc emits broken JS and exits 2.

nodes.label: 5 → 6 → 7 upgrade path
nodes.rationale: 5.9.3 last JS 5.x; 6.0 deprecation bridge; 7.0.2 native. Application code often jumps 5→7; tooling that imports typescript is the risk.

nodes.label: tsc emit-on-error default
nodes.rationale: Default tsc reports errors and still emits JS, exiting 2. --noEmitOnError and --noEmit exit 1 and write nothing. Ignoring exit 2 ships rejected output.

nodes.label: "types": [] ambient inclusion off
nodes.rationale: Default auto-includes every @types/* found walking up node_modules. [] means none unless imported. Measured: 5.9.3 pulled @types/mdx from three directories up.

nodes.label: Compiler API moved to typescript/unstable
nodes.rationale: require('typescript') exports only version and versionMajorMinor. createProgram is undefined. Live surface: typescript/unstable/sync, /async, /ast (409 exports).

nodes.label: TypeScript 7 measured 3× speedup
nodes.rationale: 300 files, 1500 lines, --noEmit --strict: 7.0.2 0.76s vs 5.9.3 2.32s. First run claimed 10× because 5.9.3 also loaded ancestor @types.

nodes.label: TypeScript 7 native compiler
nodes.rationale: Compiler rewritten as a native binary in platform optional deps (@typescript/typescript-linux-x64 etc). tsc is a thin Node wrapper. Language unchanged.

nodes.label: TypeScript 6.0 deprecation bridge
nodes.rationale: JavaScript-implemented 6.0 carries deprecations so a large project can fix issues on the familiar compiler before the native 7 jump. Tooling is the risky part.

nodes.label: Ambient @types follows cwd not sources
nodes.rationale: 5.9.3 resolves @types relative to cwd. Moving fixture to /tmp did not help while cwd stayed in the repo. Assert equal diagnostic counts before comparing timings.

nodes.label: Set rootDir explicitly
nodes.rationale: Unset, rootDir is the common ancestor of every input. A scripts/seed.ts silently moves output from dist/server.js to dist/src/server.js.

nodes.label: package.json and tsconfig module agreement
nodes.rationale: "type": "module" with module: nodenext. main/types/exports must point at what outDir produces.

nodes.label: noUncheckedIndexedAccess is not in strict
nodes.rationale: Separate opt-in; tsc --init enables it anyway. Makes arr[0] and record[key] return T | undefined.

nodes.label: strict flag
nodes.rationale: A switch over seven checks that decides what the language means. Without strictNullChecks, string includes null.

nodes.label: strictNullChecks
nodes.rationale: Load-bearing flag. Without it null is assignable to every type so | null is decoration. With it, user.name after a nullable find is TS18047 until narrowed.

nodes.label: TS5052 strictPropertyInitialization requires strictNullChecks
nodes.rationale: Never-assigned and assigned-undefined are the same without null tracking, so the flag cannot stand alone.

nodes.label: tsc --init TypeScript 7 scaffold
nodes.rationale: nodenext, esnext, types:[], strict, noUncheckedIndexedAccess, exactOptionalPropertyTypes, verbatimModuleSyntax, isolatedModules, skipLibCheck. No include/outDir/rootDir.

nodes.label: Array types T[] / Array<T>
nodes.rationale: Same type. Inference unions elements and forgets length. mixed[99] type-checks as the element union.

nodes.label: readonly T[]
nodes.rationale: Removes mutating methods from the type; does not freeze at runtime. T[] → readonly T[] is fine; reverse is not. Parameters you do not mutate should be readonly T[].

nodes.label: Cascade
nodes.rationale: Last one wins is only the final tiebreak after origin, importance, layer and specificity.

nodes.label: Parse-time value normalisation
nodes.rationale: Authored text is not retained. #ff0000 reads back as rgb(255, 0, 0); shorthands expand to longhands.

nodes.label: Shorthand expansion
nodes.rationale: A later shorthand writes every longhand it owns, including ones you never named, so border: 1px solid resets border-color to currentcolor.

nodes.label: Inline style attribute
nodes.rationale: Beats every author rule except author !important. Right only for script-computed values, preferably custom properties.

nodes.label: Styles pane strike-through
nodes.rationale: Struck through means the rule matched and lost, or failed to parse if a warning triangle is present. Those need opposite fixes.

nodes.label: CSS is resolved not executed
nodes.rationale: A stylesheet is claims about elements. There is no call stack; you debug by asking which rule won.

nodes.label: CSS owns what the browser paints
nodes.rationale: If deleting the stylesheet would delete the topic, it is CSS's. classList and requestAnimationFrame stay in JavaScript.
nodes.norm_label: css owns what the browser paints

nodes.label: transform and opacity composite-only
nodes.rationale: transform moves x without changing width/height. Neighbours do not reflow, so overlap is a feature and a trap.

nodes.label: visibility hidden vs display none
nodes.rationale: visibility:hidden keeps the box in layout (paint change). display:none removes it and forces reflow of neighbours.

nodes.label: :has() matching cost
nodes.rationale: 5000 rows: querySelectorAll class 0.15 ms vs :has(:checked) 1.25 ms. Not free; JS to keep a class in sync costs more.

nodes.label: Owl selector * + *
nodes.rationale: Applies spacing to every child except the first. Vertical rhythm without a :first-child exception.

nodes.label: Right-to-left selector matching
nodes.rationale: Engine finds the key selector first. main * is heavier than main > .thing because the candidate set is every element.

nodes.label: :has()
nodes.rationale: Parent selector and previous-sibling selector. Widely available since 2023-12-19. Unforgiving; no nested :has().

nodes.label: Hidden sync I/O
nodes.rationale: require(), existsSync, template-engine loaders, and console.log to a file all do synchronous disk I/O.

nodes.label: fs.createReadStream
nodes.rationale: Constructor never throws; open happens later. Failures arrive as error events. Use pipeline.

nodes.label: HTTP range request via createReadStream
nodes.rationale: stat, parse Range, 206 with Content-Range, or 416. Content-Length is end-start+1.

nodes.label: Inclusive start/end byte range
nodes.rationale: {start:3,end:7} returns five bytes, matching HTTP Range: bytes=3-7.

nodes.label: fs.access is still TOCTOU
nodes.rationale: Node docs say not to use access before open/read/write. Use it as a boot self-check only.

nodes.label: existsSync
nodes.rationale: Not deprecated, unlike fs.exists (DEP0018). Fine at startup and CLI; never a security check or request-path guard.

nodes.label: TOCTOU race
nodes.rationale: Between existsSync and readFile the file can be deleted, replaced, or swapped for a symlink.

nodes.label: FileHandle.sync fsync
nodes.rationale: write resolving means the OS accepted bytes, not that they reached disk. datasync skips metadata.

nodes.label: wx exclusive create
nodes.rationale: Atomic create-if-absent; fails with EEXIST. How you implement a lock file without a check-then-create race.

nodes.label: Temp plus fsync plus rename
nodes.rationale: rename is atomic within one filesystem. Readers of the old inode keep the old contents.

nodes.label: EXDEV cross-device rename
nodes.rationale: os.tmpdir is often a different mount in a container. Write the temp in the destination directory.

nodes.label: chokidar
nodes.rationale: Debounces, distinguishes add/change/unlink, awaitWriteFinish, and falls back to polling for container mounts.

nodes.label: ENOSPC inotify watch limit
nodes.rationale: Not disk space. One watch per directory; recursive node_modules exhausts max_user_watches.

nodes.label: fs.watch
nodes.rationale: inotify/FSEvents/ReadDirectoryChangesW. eventType is only rename or change. One writeFile produced two change events.

nodes.label: fs.watchFile
nodes.rationale: Polls with stat. Reliable on network mounts. Deletion is mtimeMs === 0. unwatchFile is mandatory.

nodes.label: inotify misses Docker bind mounts
nodes.rationale: inotify is a local kernel mechanism. macOS/Windows volumes into Linux containers often deliver no events.

nodes.label: Atomic current symlink deploy
nodes.rationale: ln -sfn releases/X current.tmp && mv -T current.tmp current swaps the app directory with no missing window.

nodes.label: memfs
nodes.rationale: In-memory fs with the same API. Hides EXDEV, umask, permissions, symlinks, EMFILE.

nodes.label: stat then writeHead then pipeline
nodes.rationale: stat first so 404 is possible before headers; treat ERR_STREAM_PREMATURE_CLOSE as a normal disconnect.

nodes.label: fsync before rename
nodes.rationale: Without sync the rename can persist before contents; power loss leaves the new name on an empty file.

nodes.label: Do not watch config in production
nodes.rationale: Containers are immutable, events miss production volumes, partial writes get loaded, reload paths are untested.
nodes.norm_label: do not watch config in production

nodes.label: Inject filesystem as a dependency
nodes.rationale: Tests pass memfs, production passes node:fs/promises. Stream constructors also accept an fs option.

nodes.label: Pseudo-elements are not in the DOM
nodes.norm_label: pseudo-elements are not in the dom

nodes.label: Phase 0 How Git stores things complete
nodes.norm_label: phase 0 how git stores things complete

nodes.label: A commit is a snapshot not a diff
nodes.norm_label: a commit is a snapshot not a diff

nodes.label: The index is a real file
nodes.norm_label: the index is a real file

nodes.label: Branch is a moving ref
nodes.rationale: A branch is a ref under refs/heads that advances on commit. Creating one writes 41 bytes and no objects; deleting one deletes no commits.

nodes.label: Unset config uses built-in defaults
nodes.rationale: On 2.55.0 unset init.defaultBranch is master, not main. Unset pull.rebase makes a divergent pull fail rather than guess.

nodes.label: Five config scopes
nodes.rationale: system → global → local → worktree → -c. Last wins; nothing merges for a single-valued key.

nodes.label: Branching is a 41-byte file write
nodes.rationale: git branch writes 41 bytes; object count is unchanged. Delete-the-branch is recoverable because objects stay reachable via the reflog.

nodes.label: Exponentiation ** right-associative
nodes.rationale: Only right-associative arithmetic operator. 2**3**2 is 512. Replaces Math.pow.

nodes.label: -2 ** 2 SyntaxError
nodes.rationale: Committee refused to pick between -(2**2)=-4 and (-2)**2=4. Grammar requires parentheses.

nodes.label: Assignment is an expression
nodes.rationale: Associates right to left. Why a=b=5 works and if(x=5) assigns then tests truthiness.

nodes.label: ?? cannot mix with && or ||
nodes.rationale: Unparenthesised mix is SyntaxError, same philosophy as -2**2. (a??b)||c and a??(b||c) can differ.

nodes.label: Ternary chooses a value
nodes.rationale: Wrong for actions. One level inline; two or more align as a decision table or extract a function.

nodes.label: && binds tighter than ||
nodes.rationale: a||b&&c is a||(b&&c). Always parenthesise mixed &&/||. Mixing ?? is SyntaxError instead.

nodes.label: Five precedence bugs
nodes.rationale: Do not memorise twenty levels. Learn ** right-assoc, + string poison, && tighter than ||, typeof tighter than +, comparisons do not chain.

nodes.label: Right-associative operators
nodes.rationale: Only ** , ternary, and assignment. Ternary chaining makes aligned decision tables parse as a?x:(b?y:z).

nodes.label: Comma operator
nodes.rationale: Evaluates left to right, returns last. Lowest precedence so x=1,2,3 assigns 1. One readable use: two-pointer for header.

nodes.label: Arrow callback this fix
nodes.rationale: An arrow has no this, so the inner obj.method() keeps its receiver. Wrong as the method itself at module scope.

nodes.label: Class field arrow
nodes.rationale: Per-instance own property capturing constructor this. Survives detach; not on the prototype so it cannot be stubbed or overridden there.

nodes.label: Lost this
nodes.rationale: Implicit binding is a property of the call site. Assigning, destructuring, or passing a method drops the receiver.

nodes.label: thisArg
nodes.rationale: forEach/map/filter/some/every/find/findIndex/flatMap honour thisArg. reduce and sort do not.

nodes.label: Lexical this
nodes.rationale: An arrow has no this. The identifier is a free variable resolved through the scope chain like any other.

nodes.label: Prototype method vs class-field arrow
nodes.rationale: Prototype methods are shared and stubbable. Field arrows are per-instance own enumerable keys. Use a field arrow only when the method is passed as a value.

nodes.label: Closure private state
nodes.rationale: The oldest privacy and the oldest leak. Variables stay alive as long as the function does.

nodes.label: V8 captures referenced bindings only
nodes.rationale: Unused 300k-object arrays added 0 MB; referenced ones retained 69 MB. Optimisation, not a spec guarantee. heapUsed misses typed-array external memory.

nodes.label: Arrow is a different kind of callable
nodes.rationale: Not shorter function syntax. No own this, arguments, super, or new.target, and no prototype at all.
nodes.norm_label: arrow is a different kind of callable

nodes.label: Method shorthand is not a function property
nodes.rationale: Methods cannot be constructors and only methods have super, because they have a home object. Prefer method shorthand in literals.
nodes.norm_label: method shorthand is not a function property

nodes.label: Enumeration method comparison
nodes.rationale: Object.keys is own enumerable strings. Reflect.ownKeys is the only one-call way to get all own keys including symbols. for...in walks the prototype chain.

nodes.label: Integer-index keys
nodes.rationale: Only the canonical string form of a non-negative integer. -1, 01, 1.5 and 1e2 are ordinary strings. Zero-padded IDs sort into a different tier.

nodes.label: Three-tier property enumeration order
nodes.rationale: Integer-index keys first, ascending; then other strings by insertion; then symbols by insertion. An object keyed by numeric IDs reorders itself.

nodes.label: Object literals
nodes.rationale: Three surprises: method shorthand is not a function-valued property; { __proto__: x } is not a property; key order is not insertion order.

nodes.label: class is the same lookup machinery
nodes.rationale: Class methods go on Ctor.prototype. class adds private fields, extends wiring, strict bodies, non-enumerable methods and a constructor that throws without new.
nodes.norm_label: class is the same lookup machinery

nodes.label: What new actually does
nodes.rationale: Creates a fresh object whose [[Prototype]] is Fn.prototype, calls Fn with this bound to it, and returns it. No methods are copied; instances share one function object.

nodes.label: What class desugars to
nodes.rationale: The wiring is identical: methods go on Ctor.prototype. class is sugar for prototype wiring and a genuine language feature for everything else.

nodes.label: Five non-sugar class features
nodes.rationale: Always-strict body; TypeError without new; non-enumerable methods; TDZ and block scope; private elements with no desugaring.

nodes.label: Callback hell / pyramid of doom
nodes.rationale: Forced because a callback API returns nothing to sequence on. Real cost is per-level if (err) return, not indentation.

nodes.label: Thenable
nodes.rationale: Any object with a callable then. Promise.resolve and await assimilate thenables. A data field named then is accidentally adopted.

nodes.label: Promise adoption
nodes.rationale: Return a value and it is wrapped; return a promise or thenable and it is adopted, never nested. Lets a handler switch between sync and async without callers changing.

nodes.label: Forgotten return / floating promise
nodes.rationale: A handler that returns nothing fulfils immediately with undefined. The inner promise floats: sequencing breaks and its rejection becomes unhandled.

nodes.label: reduce sequential composition
nodes.rationale: [f1,f2,f3].reduce((p, f) => p.then(f), Promise.resolve()). Seed is an already-fulfilled promise; pass functions by reference.

nodes.label: then returns a new promise
nodes.rationale: Each link represents the previous step and the handler. Combined with adoption, that is why a chain is flat where a callback pyramid was not.

nodes.label: Nesting to scope a catch
nodes.rationale: A nested catch only swallows failures in its scope. Flat mid-chain catch would swallow critical errors too. Nesting is a scoping tool, not a style.

nodes.label: Named functions do not fix callback hell
nodes.rationale: Flattens indentation, hides sequence, loses closures, keeps per-level error branches, and leaves every trust problem in place.
nodes.norm_label: named functions do not fix callback hell

nodes.label: async/await desugars to a promise chain
nodes.rationale: await 1 becomes Promise.resolve(1).then(() => undefined). Non-promises are wrapped; code after await is a continuation.
nodes.norm_label: async/await desugars to a promise chain

nodes.label: Idle p50 is the sampling resolution
nodes.rationale: At resolution 10, idle p50 sits near 10 ms. Alerting on p50 > 5 ms at that resolution is alerting on arithmetic.
nodes.norm_label: idle p50 is the sampling resolution

nodes.label: Lag max vs p99
nodes.rationale: One 100 ms block moved only max (10.29 → 115.34 ms). Five blocks raised p99 to ~109 ms. max is the smoke alarm; p99 is the trend.

nodes.label: monitorEventLoopDelay histogram
nodes.rationale: Values are nanoseconds; divide by 1e6 for milliseconds. Enable process-wide at boot; export p99 and max each scrape; reset or slide the window so one incident does not poison the day.

nodes.label: Saturation signal
nodes.rationale: Leading indicator: event loop lag, pool wait, heap ratio, queue depth, CPU. Traffic and latency go bad after the constrained resource is full.

nodes.label: Generational GC
nodes.rationale: New objects start young and cheap to collect (scavenges). Survivors age into old space with more expensive major GC.

nodes.label: Event loop lag
nodes.rationale: The metric that turns 'the server feels slow' into a number you can alert on. One thread runs all JS — if the loop is late, every request on that process is late.

nodes.label: perf_hooks
nodes.rationale: Built-in stopwatch and observer bus for in-process timings. Does not replace OpenTelemetry across services.

nodes.label: Exposing metrics for Prometheus
nodes.rationale: Expose low-cardinality time series that map to the golden signals — not every event as a metric.

nodes.label: CPU and heap profiling
nodes.rationale: When the event loop is hot or CPU is pegged, a profile shows which functions ate the samples.

nodes.label: MODULE_TYPELESS_PACKAGE_JSON
nodes.rationale: Since v22.7.0 / v20.19.0 a typeless .js that fails as CommonJS is reparsed as ESM, with a warning about the cost.

nodes.label: Nearest package.json type field
nodes.rationale: Resolution finds the file; the nearest package.json decides how to parse it. .mjs is always ESM, .cjs always CommonJS.

nodes.label: engines as a floor
nodes.rationale: A declaration, not enforcement, unless engine-strict=true. State a floor, not a ceiling.

nodes.label: files allowlist
nodes.rationale: Without it npm publishes everything except a small default-ignored set. README, LICENSE and package.json always ship; node_modules never does.

nodes.label: node --run
nodes.rationale: Runs package.json scripts without the npm process. No pre/post scripts, no .npmrc resolution.

nodes.label: package.json essentials
nodes.rationale: The file that decides how code is parsed, what ships, and what runs. Six fields carry almost all of it.

nodes.label: package.json type field
nodes.rationale: Decides how every .js file in the package is parsed. Set it explicitly; module for new work.

nodes.label: npm pack --dry-run
nodes.rationale: The only way to see what you are actually shipping. Catches secrets going out and needed files staying home.

nodes.label: Avoid postinstall scripts
nodes.rationale: pre/post hooks run implicitly. postinstall executes on every npm install of your package — a supply-chain concern.

nodes.label: Caret vs tilde ranges
nodes.rationale: ^1.2.3 allows <2.0.0; ~1.2.3 allows <1.3.0. For 0.x, ^ tightens to patch-level because the minor slot carries breaking changes.

nodes.label: package.json overrides
nodes.rationale: Forces a nested dependency version when the parent has not updated. You override the parent's declared compatibility.

nodes.label: Semantic versioning
nodes.rationale: MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH records the maintainer's intent, not a guarantee. A patch that fixes a bug your code depended on is still a break for you.

nodes.label: save-exact
nodes.rationale: Makes npm install write exact versions instead of ^ ranges. Useful for applications; less so for libraries.

nodes.label: Pre-release dist-tag
nodes.rationale: Without --tag a pre-release becomes latest and everyone running npm install gets a beta.

nodes.label: npm publish --provenance
nodes.rationale: Attaches a signed statement linking the tarball to the exact commit and workflow. Only works from supported CI.

nodes.label: A published version is permanent
nodes.rationale: npm unpublish is restricted to 72 hours and only when nothing depends on it. Recovery is npm deprecate plus a new version.

nodes.label: Publishing a package
nodes.rationale: A checklist rather than a skill. The two irreversible parts are what ends up in the tarball and the version number you burn.

nodes.label: Scoped package names
nodes.rationale: A scope is a namespace you own. Scoped packages default to private; publish publicly with --access public or publishConfig.access.

nodes.label: Buffer
nodes.rationale: Fixed-length raw bytes outside the V8 heap. Strings are UTF-16; network and disk are bytes. Every Node I/O boundary hands you one.

nodes.label: Buffer.from and Buffer.alloc
nodes.rationale: from encodes text or copies exact bytes; alloc zeros safely. new Buffer is deprecated DEP0005 and unsafe.

nodes.label: Collect HTTP body with a size limit
nodes.rationale: Sum chunk.length, destroy and 413 past the limit, then Buffer.concat(chunks, size). Counting characters lets multi-byte payloads through.
nodes.norm_label: collect http body with a size limit

nodes.label: Buffer.concat
nodes.rationale: Pass totalLength when known to skip a summing pass. Collect HTTP body as buffers then concat once — never string-concatenate chunks.

nodes.label: JSON.stringify of a Buffer
nodes.rationale: Produces {type:Buffer,data:[...]}. Convert with toString(base64) or toString() before res.json.

nodes.label: Buffer.subarray shares memory
nodes.rationale: A view, not a copy. Buffer.prototype.slice is an alias and unlike Array/Uint8Array.slice does not copy. Return a copy for anything you store.

nodes.label: crypto.timingSafeEqual vs Buffer.equals
nodes.rationale: equals short-circuits on the first differing byte — a timing oracle for tokens and HMACs.

nodes.label: Buffer.length is bytes
nodes.rationale: héllo is 5 characters and 6 UTF-8 bytes. Content-Length and size limits must use Buffer.byteLength, not str.length.

nodes.label: rejectUnauthorized false is never the fix
nodes.norm_label: rejectunauthorized false is never the fix

nodes.label: Do not use a shell with user input
nodes.norm_label: do not use a shell with user input

nodes.label: Batch with ANY / $in
nodes.rationale: Collect ids, one child query, group in memory. Two queries regardless of page size; works across services. DataLoader does this per tick.

nodes.label: json_agg join
nodes.rationale: One query, JSON arrays already shaped. Need left join plus filter to avoid dropping childless parents or [null].

nodes.label: N+1 query
nodes.rationale: One query for the list, then one per item. Cost is round trips, not query work — 101 queries 111 ms vs 2 queries 7 ms on localhost.

nodes.label: Prisma include is two queries
nodes.rationale: Batched IN pair, not a join. Avoids one-to-many row multiplication. Nested includes multiply statements.

nodes.label: Promise.all is not the N+1 fix
nodes.rationale: 111 ms to 49 ms but 100 simultaneous queries demand 100 pool connections and can exhaust the process.
nodes.norm_label: promise.all is not the n+1 fix

nodes.label: Driver, query builder, ORM
nodes.rationale: The choice is who writes the SQL and what happens when it is wrong. 500 lookups: pg 296 ms, Drizzle 388 ms, Prisma 597 ms — noise next to an N+1.

nodes.label: Schema-first vs SQL-first
nodes.rationale: Prisma owns a .prisma file and generates a client. Drizzle declares schema in TypeScript and prints SQL via toSQL().

nodes.label: Tagged-template escape hatches parameterize
nodes.rationale: sql`…` and $queryRaw send hostile strings as $1. sql.raw() and $queryRawUnsafe interpolate.

nodes.label: Replicas add capacity not speed
nodes.rationale: Same query plus a hop. Fix N+1, add indexes, cache first. A replica is not automatic failover.

nodes.label: REPEATABLE READ turns lost updates into 40001
nodes.norm_label: repeatable read turns lost updates into 40001

nodes.label: SQLSTATE 40001 serialization failure
nodes.rationale: due to concurrent update = you wrote a row someone else wrote. due to read/write dependencies = SSI found a cycle involving what you read. Same SQLSTATE, different detection.

nodes.label: REPEATABLE READ
nodes.rationale: One snapshot for the whole transaction, taken at the first statement. Read-only work cannot fail with 40001. Writers that touch a changed row get 40001 concurrent update.

nodes.label: SERIALIZABLE
nodes.rationale: Outcome equals some serial execution via SSI. Degrades sharply with conflict rate: 135 attempts and 12.4 s vs ordered FOR UPDATE 20 attempts and 71.2 ms for 20 transfers.

nodes.label: Write skew
nodes.rationale: Two transactions write different rows after reading an overlapping set and together break an invariant neither saw break. REPEATABLE READ allows it; SERIALIZABLE aborts one.

nodes.label: Transactions that pin the horizon
nodes.rationale: REPEATABLE READ/SERIALIZABLE even idle (snapshot lives); any writer (backend_xid); any still-executing statement including a long SELECT.

nodes.label: Row locks: FOR UPDATE and friends
nodes.norm_label: row locks: for update and friends

nodes.label: 8 GB notification queue
nodes.rationale: A stuck listener is database-wide: the queue cannot truncate past it and NOTIFY errors for everyone. Monitor pg_notification_queue_usage().

nodes.label: Partition key must be in every unique constraint
nodes.rationale: PRIMARY KEY (id) is rejected. No global index across partitions. A partition-key UPDATE is DELETE + INSERT and cannot be HOT.
nodes.norm_label: partition key must be in every unique constraint

nodes.label: What logical replication does not copy
nodes.rationale: DDL/schema, sequence data, large objects; only tables. TRUNCATE is replicated but fails if FKs point outside the subscription.
nodes.norm_label: what logical replication does not copy

nodes.label: PUBLICATION and SUBSCRIPTION
nodes.rationale: wal_level = logical requires a restart. Snapshot then stream in commit order. Schema must already exist on the subscriber.

nodes.label: Replica identity
nodes.rationale: Without a PK or marked unique index, INSERTs replicate and the first UPDATE/DELETE fails. REPLICA IDENTITY FULL breaks for types like point/box.

nodes.label: Abandoned replication slot fills publisher disk
nodes.rationale: A slot whose subscriber is gone retains WAL forever. Alert on pg_replication_slots; set max_slot_wal_keep_size to sacrifice the subscriber.
nodes.norm_label: abandoned replication slot fills publisher disk

nodes.label: Logical vs physical replication
nodes.rationale: Physical copies WAL bytes of the whole cluster, same major, read-only. Logical copies decoded row changes, per table, writable, cross-major.

nodes.label: Logical-replication upgrade cutover
nodes.rationale: Near-zero downtime across majors. Advance sequences as an explicit cutover step or the first insert raises 23505.

nodes.label: Disaster runbook outside the system
nodes.rationale: Exact commands, who decides, credentials, verification queries, endpoint change, measured timings. Someone who did not write it must be able to follow it.

nodes.label: UUIDv7
nodes.rationale: Time-ordered UUID restores insert locality. Random v4 scatters btree inserts. 16 bytes vs 8. Adding uuid DEFAULT gen_random_uuid() rewrites (902 ms / 200k).

nodes.label: Table rewrite via relfilenode
nodes.rationale: Rewrite when on-disk representation changes: int→bigint, narrowing varchar, volatile default, SET LOGGED/UNLOGGED. Widening varchar and varchar→text do not.

nodes.label: Volatile default rewrites ADD COLUMN
nodes.rationale: Constant default is catalog-only since PG11 (4 ms). gen_random_uuid() rewrites 902 ms. now() is statement-stable and did not rewrite.

nodes.label: Constant default ADD COLUMN since PG11
nodes.rationale: bool NOT NULL DEFAULT false is 4 ms catalog-only. Volatile gen_random_uuid() still rewrites 902 ms and needs the old three-step dance.
nodes.norm_label: constant default add column since pg11

nodes.label: TEMPORARY table
nodes.rationale: Private to one session (pg_temp_N). Shadows same-named permanent tables via search_path. Lives in temp_buffers (default 8 MB).

nodes.label: UNLOGGED table
nodes.rationale: ~1.5× faster inserts (150→98 ms / 100k). Truncated on crash recovery, never replicated, empty after failover. SET LOGGED/UNLOGGED rewrites (230 ms / 200k).

nodes.label: Liberal constraints conservative types
nodes.rationale: Constraints can be relaxed with ALTER and NOT VALID. Type changes that alter on-disk representation rewrite under ACCESS EXCLUSIVE.

nodes.label: Add backfill swap type change
nodes.rationale: Add new column, backfill in batches, keep current with a trigger, swap in a short lock_timeout transaction. Interruptible unlike one ALTER TYPE.

nodes.label: ON COMMIT DROP
nodes.rationale: Pooled connections reuse sessions. A leftover temp table leaks into the next request. Hold one checked-out client; prefer a CTE if the data is one-statement only.

nodes.label: ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING RETURNING trap
nodes.rationale: A skipped row is not returned. Retry path reading rows[0].id crashes. Force a row with a no-op DO UPDATE; xmax = 0 distinguishes insert from update.
nodes.norm_label: on conflict do nothing returning trap

nodes.label: RETURNING on every write
nodes.rationale: INSERT and UPDATE return the row after the change; DELETE returns it just before disappearing. Same statement, no READ COMMITTED race, one round trip.

nodes.label: xmax = 0 as was_insert
nodes.rationale: xmax is 0 for a freshly inserted tuple. Implementation detail; prefer created_at versus updated_at if the distinction is load-bearing.

nodes.label: Soft delete is an UPDATE
nodes.rationale: Setting deleted_at fires no cascade, unique constraints still see the row, every query needs WHERE deleted_at IS NULL. Orphaned orders stayed visible.

nodes.label: FILTER empty group is NULL
nodes.rationale: FILTER (WHERE child.id IS NOT NULL) removes the fake row, leaving an empty group. Every aggregate over an empty input is NULL — same rule as sum over no rows.

nodes.label: LEFT JOIN NULL row kept by array_agg
nodes.rationale: LEFT JOIN invents a childless parent row with NULL child columns. array_agg and jsonb_agg keep NULLs, so the client sees [null] and length 1.
nodes.norm_label: left join null row kept by array_agg

nodes.label: array_agg
nodes.rationale: Returns an array of the input type and keeps NULLs as elements.

nodes.label: json_agg / jsonb_agg
nodes.rationale: Returns a JSON array and keeps NULL inputs as null. jsonb_agg(child.*) also leaks every child column.

nodes.label: jsonb_object_agg
nodes.rationale: Returns a jsonb object. Key must not be NULL (error 22023).

nodes.label: string_agg
nodes.rationale: Returns text and skips NULL inputs. Opposite of array_agg and jsonb_agg on NULLs.

nodes.label: The empty-array trap
nodes.rationale: A parent with no children should return []. The naked aggregate returns [null]; FILTER alone returns null. Getting [] takes FILTER plus coalesce.

nodes.label: string_agg, array_agg, jsonb_agg
nodes.rationale: These aggregates fold a group into a collection, enabling a one-query nested API payload. Every one returns NULL where empty was expected, and [null] where [] was expected.

nodes.label: Canonical child-collection idiom
nodes.rationale: coalesce(jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object(...) ORDER BY k) FILTER (WHERE id IS NOT NULL), '[]'::jsonb). Four parts: build_object, ORDER BY, FILTER, coalesce. '{}' is the empty PostgreSQL array, not a JSON array.

nodes.label: --test-force-exit
nodes.rationale: Legitimate for a third-party leak you cannot close. For your own code it hides a defect that also blocks production shutdown.

nodes.label: Phase 2 — Async and the event loop
nodes.norm_label: phase 2 — async and the event loop

nodes.label: Two-level LATERAL nested payload
nodes.rationale: LEFT JOIN LATERAL … ON true nests inner GROUP BY so each order aggregates its items before the outer aggregate collects orders. Flat dual joins multiply fan-out.

nodes.label: CTE (WITH)
nodes.rationale: Readability feature, not a performance feature. Referenced like a table anywhere a table can appear. WITH attaches to SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE and MERGE.

nodes.label: CTE name shadows a real table
nodes.rationale: No warning. Inside the statement the CTE wins and the table is unreachable by that name. Give CTEs names that cannot collide.
nodes.norm_label: cte name shadows a real table

nodes.label: CTE forward reference 42P01
nodes.rationale: A CTE sees only earlier declarations. Forward reference is 42P01 relation does not exist. WITH RECURSIVE lifts the restriction for the whole list. Duplicate names are 42712.

nodes.label: Naming a subquery
nodes.rationale: A CTE binds a name to a subquery for one statement. It is not a temp table. One WITH, comma-separated list; lives only while the statement runs.

nodes.label: The inlining rule
nodes.rationale: Before PG12 every CTE was an optimization fence. Since 12 a qualifying CTE is folded in. Same query 28.42 ms inlined vs 174.49 ms MATERIALIZED — 6.1×.

nodes.label: CTEs (WITH)
nodes.rationale: WITH binds a name for one statement so a four-step report reads as four named steps. The non-obvious part is the plan: qualifying CTEs fold in; MATERIALIZED costs 6× here.

nodes.label: Data-modifying CTEs
nodes.rationale: Three rules: a write CTE always runs; its effect is visible only through RETURNING; execution order is unspecified so two writes on one row are a silent bug.

nodes.label: Shape in SQL versus stitch in JS
nodes.rationale: Shape in SQL when nesting is fixed and child sets are small — one round trip, atomic, untyped. Stitch in JS when pieces are needed separately or children need pagination. Either beats N+1. Measured 292 vs 580 bytes.
nodes.norm_label: shape in sql versus stitch in js

nodes.label: CTE inlining conditions
nodes.rationale: Inlined when referenced once, not MATERIALIZED, not recursive, does not write, and has no volatile function. Inlined CTE leaves no CTE node; filter can reach the scan and parallelise.

nodes.label: LIMIT does not fence a CTE
nodes.rationale: The CTE is still inlined. Limit stays below the outer filter so 10 rows then filter to 5, not first 10 matching the filter. Protects semantics, not cost.
nodes.norm_label: limit does not fence a cte

nodes.label: MATERIALIZED fence
nodes.rationale: Forces a CTE Scan after materialising every row (500000 into Disk 21344kB, no parallelism). Use only when the query depends on the fence.

nodes.label: Volatility classes and CTE inlining
nodes.rationale: IMMUTABLE and STABLE (now()) inline. VOLATILE (random(), clock_timestamp()) fences because re-evaluation could change the answer. Same classification as indexability.

nodes.label: Multiply-referenced CTE computed once
nodes.rationale: Automatic materialization: Buffers 3803, 56.5 ms. NOT MATERIALIZED doubled work (7606 buffers, 124.1 ms). This is the one execution guarantee a CTE gives that a repeated subquery does not.

nodes.label: NOT MATERIALIZED is advisory
nodes.rationale: Ignored when inlining would change the answer — volatile, recursive, or data-modifying CTEs stay fenced. A random() CTE still planned as CTE Scan despite the hint.

nodes.label: OFFSET 0 subquery fence
nodes.rationale: Classic pre-12 fence. Still blocks subquery pull-up in PG18: no CTE node, but filter stuck above Subquery Scan and no parallelism. Removing a pointless OFFSET 0 can change the plan.

nodes.label: Data-modifying CTE always fenced
nodes.rationale: One of the five inlining exclusions. NOT MATERIALIZED cannot override it, because inlining would execute the write once per reference.

nodes.label: References, hints and the plan
nodes.rationale: Referenced twice, a CTE is computed once. NOT MATERIALIZED is a request the planner may ignore. No CTE node is not the same as the filter reaching the scan.

nodes.label: Correlated subquery
nodes.rationale: A reference to an outer column makes any of the three kinds correlated and changes the cost class entirely — SubPlan loops per outer row, an N+1 inside one statement.

nodes.label: Scalar subquery
nodes.rationale: Returns exactly 1 row × 1 column. Runs once if uncorrelated. Error 21000 if more than one row, often only in production.

nodes.label: Subqueries
nodes.rationale: A subquery is a query used as a value, a set, or a table. Which of those three it is decides row cardinality, how often it runs, and whether a NULL in a negated set form empties the result.

nodes.label: Table subquery
nodes.rationale: Appears in FROM; alias required. Any rows × any columns. Runs once if uncorrelated.

nodes.label: Capped count
nodes.rationale: count(*) over a subquery with LIMIT cap. Exact below the ceiling, report 1000+ at the cap. Pays only when matches are plentiful: 1.46 ms vs 33.85 ms (23×) at 125000 matches; 3.01 vs 3.02 ms at 120 matches — no saving.

nodes.label: Recursive CTE cycle
nodes.rationale: A cycle means an iteration never produces no new rows. Measured 107 rows from an 8-row table before d<40 stopped it. A self-referencing FK guarantees the parent exists, not acyclicity. No standard constraint enforces a tree.

nodes.label: CYCLE clause
nodes.rationale: PG 14+. CYCLE id SET is_cycle USING path. Only option that reports the cycle. Measured root twice, second is_cycle true, then stop. Prefer when cycles may be legitimate. Pair with a depth guard.

nodes.label: Recursive depth guard
nodes.rationale: WHERE t.d < N in the recursive term. Universal, production-mandatory even on believed trees. Cannot distinguish a deep hierarchy from a loop; truncates both silently. Choose a bound above any legitimate depth.

nodes.label: UNION instead of UNION ALL
nodes.rationale: Discards already-produced rows so a second lap yields nothing and recursion stops. Measured 8 unique rows and termination. Pays comparison cost. Incompatible with depth or path columns — every lap is a different row. UNION and a path column do not compose.

nodes.label: Recursive CTE anchor
nodes.rationale: Starting set, run once. Cast types here so UNION ALL branches agree (name::text). Anchor row is included in subtree aggregates — off-by-one for descendant counts.

nodes.label: Recursive term
nodes.rationale: Joins the table to the CTE, not to itself. c.parent_id = t.id descends; t.parent_id = c.id climbs. Carries depth and path. Table is scanned once per iteration — index the join column or cost is depth × full scan.

nodes.label: Recursive Union
nodes.rationale: Plan node for the whole construct. First child is the anchor; second is the recursive term. loops= on the term is iteration count (depth). Measured loops=4 on a 4-level tree.

nodes.label: WorkTable Scan
nodes.rationale: Rows produced by the previous iteration — the only input the recursive term reads. Not everything found so far.

nodes.label: 42P19 recursive term restrictions
nodes.rationale: Recursive reference must not appear more than once; aggregates forbidden in the recursive term (would summarise only the previous iteration). Also bars LEFT JOIN against the CTE, ORDER BY and LIMIT inside the term. Aggregate outside.

nodes.label: Missing RECURSIVE is 42P01
nodes.rationale: Plain WITH cannot self-reference. Error is the ordinary relation does not exist, so it is misdiagnosed as a typo or search_path problem. Keyword attaches to WITH, not the CTE name.

nodes.label: SEARCH clause
nodes.rationale: SEARCH DEPTH FIRST BY id SET ord (or BREADTH FIRST). Creates a sortable column; you must still ORDER BY ord. Replaces a hand-rolled path used only for sorting.

nodes.label: WITH RECURSIVE
nodes.rationale: Follows a parent pointer to arbitrary depth in one statement. Anchor plus recursive term joined by UNION ALL, repeated until the rule produces nothing. The only construct in this phase whose stopping condition lives in the data.

nodes.label: generate_series instead of recursion
nodes.rationale: Use WITH RECURSIVE when following data shape (hierarchy, graph). When the next value is a pure function of the last, generate_series is simpler and faster.

nodes.label: DDL as ordinary query
nodes.rationale: CREATE TABLE via client.query returns command CREATE, rowCount null, empty fields. Success is no thrown error.

nodes.label: Identifiers cannot be parameters
nodes.rationale: CREATE TABLE $1 raises 42601 at parse time. Dynamic identifiers need format('%I') plus an allowlist.

nodes.label: Simple vs extended query protocol
nodes.rationale: No params or [] uses simple protocol and returns an array of results. A non-empty params array forces extended protocol: 42601 cannot insert multiple commands.

nodes.label: Transactional DDL
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL rolls DDL back with the transaction. CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY, VACUUM, CREATE DATABASE cannot run inside BEGIN (25001).

nodes.label: CREATE INDEX lock modes
nodes.rationale: CREATE INDEX takes ShareLock (reads ok, writes block). CONCURRENTLY permits writes at the cost of two scans and no transaction.

nodes.label: Assembled list query
nodes.rationale: Filter values and limit/offset are parameters. Filter fields, sort column and direction come from an allowlist. Clamp limit to avoid DoS.

nodes.label: OFFSET pagination cost
nodes.rationale: OFFSET n produces and discards n rows and cannot stay correct under concurrent writes. Use keyset for deep or crawlable lists.

nodes.label: ORDER BY unique tiebreaker
nodes.rationale: ORDER BY on a non-unique column is underspecified. Paging 100 rows without , id returned 54 distinct and 46 duplicates. Instability is between offsets, not per-query jitter.

nodes.label: Expensive total count
nodes.rationale: Filtered count(*) scans matching rows. Prefer limit+1 hasMore. Count and page must share one transaction snapshot.

nodes.label: 65535 parameter wire limit
nodes.rationale: Protocol encodes parameter count in 16 bits. 21845 rows of 3 columns ok; 21846 is 08P01. Batch by floor(65535/columns) or use unnest.

nodes.label: Autocommit WAL flush cost
nodes.rationale: Each standalone INSERT commits and flushes WAL. One transaction around the loop: 20165 to 2559 ms. Remaining cost is 10000 round trips.

nodes.label: Bulk insert that scales
nodes.rationale: One row per query is the common Node performance bug. 10000 rows: 20165 ms autocommit loop vs 84 ms unnest — 240x.

nodes.label: COPY FROM STDIN from Node
nodes.rationale: Streaming, bounded memory, no ON CONFLICT or RETURNING. From Node, unnest beat pg-copy-streams 2.7–3x because of JS CSV formatting.

nodes.label: INSERT SELECT unnest
nodes.rationale: One array per column; statement text is constant. Casts required. Supports ON CONFLICT and RETURNING. Materialises all values in heap.

nodes.label: COPY text vs csv format
nodes.rationale: text is default: tab delimiter, \N is NULL. csv needs WITH (FORMAT csv). Comma data on text dumps the line into column one.

nodes.label: COPY NULL representation
nodes.rationale: text: \N is NULL, empty field is ''. csv: unquoted empty is NULL, "" is ''. Common NOT NULL violation source.

nodes.label: pg-copy-streams
nodes.rationale: Turns client.query into a writable stream. Needs a checked-out client because COPY is a distinct protocol mode.

nodes.label: pipeline not pipe for COPY
nodes.rationale: pipeline propagates errors and destroys both ends. .pipe() leaves the connection stuck mid-COPY and poisons the pool.

nodes.label: Mapper is an allowlist by construction
nodes.rationale: A column added later does not appear in responses until named here. SELECT * plus no mapper leaks password_hash the day it is added.
nodes.norm_label: mapper is an allowlist by construction

nodes.label: Missing SELECT row is not an error
nodes.rationale: A matching-nothing SELECT succeeds with rowCount 0 and rows []. rows[0] is undefined; normalise to null so JSON.stringify keeps the key.
nodes.norm_label: missing select row is not an error

nodes.label: rowCount versus rows.length
nodes.rationale: rowCount is rows affected; rows is what came back. They match for SELECT and diverge on writes without RETURNING. rowCount is null, not 0, for DDL/BEGIN/SET.

nodes.label: toDomain row mapper
nodes.rationale: Maps a pg row to the API contract: String(id), snake_case to camelCase, Date to ISO, and only named fields. Lives in the repository next to the SELECT list.

nodes.label: FILTERABLE column and operator map
nodes.rationale: Any field name (filter, groupBy, fields) has the same hole. Both column and operator come from the map; a client-supplied op is injection.

nodes.label: Allowlist is a lookup not validation
nodes.rationale: Use the request key into an object whose values are SQL you authored. The user's string never reaches the query. Unknown key is 400.
nodes.norm_label: allowlist is a lookup not validation

nodes.label: Null-prototype or Map for user keys
nodes.rationale: A plain object resolves ?sort=constructor or __proto__ to something truthy that is not a column.
nodes.norm_label: null-prototype or map for user keys

nodes.label: Keep mapper adjacent to the SELECT
nodes.rationale: The mapper can only produce what the query selected. Splitting them yields undefined fields instead of errors and makes SELECT * tempting. Alias for shape, mapper for contract.
nodes.norm_label: keep mapper adjacent to the select

nodes.label: Allowlist is also the index contract
nodes.rationale: Sortable columns are a deliberate API decision and the set you have agreed to index. Reflecting information_schema re-adds the leak and exposes internal names.
nodes.norm_label: allowlist is also the index contract

nodes.label: Switch on constraint name not message
nodes.rationale: err.message is locale-dependent prose. constraint is populated only for 23xxx; column only for 23502. Name constraints explicitly in DDL.
nodes.norm_label: switch on constraint name not message

nodes.label: err.detail leaks submitted values
nodes.rationale: 23505 detail echoes the key value; 23514 detail is the entire failing row. Log it; return a mapped machine-readable string.

nodes.label: toHttpError
nodes.rationale: Allowlists known codes to statuses; unrecognised errors are rethrown so they stay 500s. Returns constraint when present.

nodes.label: unique_violation 23505
nodes.rationale: Every unique index shares code 23505. Switch on err.constraint (named in DDL) to tell email_taken from username_taken.

nodes.label: Repository module per resource
nodes.rationale: Not a class or SQL abstraction — a module of plain functions whose first argument is whatever will run the query.

nodes.label: 42xxx codes must stay 500s
nodes.rationale: 42703/42601/42P01 mean deployed SQL is wrong. Mapping them to 400 blames the client and hides a broken deploy.

nodes.label: Validate in the app and still map 23505
nodes.rationale: SELECT then INSERT races. Only the unique index closes uniqueness. App checks are UX; the constraint is the correctness boundary.
nodes.norm_label: validate in the app and still map 23505

nodes.label: Map SQLSTATE in middleware not the repository
nodes.rationale: The same 23505 is a 409 from signup and a retry signal inside an idempotent write. Only the caller knows which. Translate to domain errors in the repository only when it has intent the middleware cannot.
nodes.norm_label: map sqlstate in middleware not the repository

nodes.label: = ANY($1::bigint[])
nodes.rationale: One array parameter keeps statement text constant across list lengths. Empty ANY('{}') matches nothing; generated IN () is a syntax error.

nodes.label: Bound parameter cannot become SQL
nodes.rationale: The statement is parsed before the value is bound. apple'; DROP TABLE … as $1 returned 0 rows and left the table intact.

nodes.label: Escape ILIKE pattern metacharacters
nodes.rationale: A user % is not injection but forces a full scan. Escape \, %, _ then wrap; declare ESCAPE '\'. Leading-wildcard ILIKE needs pg_trgm.

nodes.label: Concatenated ORDER BY drops the table
nodes.rationale: ?sort=name; DROP TABLE fs_items CASCADE; -- executed as two statements. The same payload as $1 left the table intact.
nodes.norm_label: concatenated order by drops the table

nodes.label: ORDER BY $1 is a silent no-op
nodes.rationale: The parameter binds as a constant string, so every row sorts by the same value. Sorting by name and price returned byte-identical output and no error. ORDER BY 1 is a column index; $1 is not.
nodes.norm_label: order by $1 is a silent no-op

nodes.label: Simple query protocol stacked statements
nodes.rationale: query() with no parameter array uses the simple protocol, which permits multiple statements separated by ;. pg reported 2 statements executed.

nodes.label: format %I %L %s
nodes.rationale: %I quotes as an identifier, %L as a literal, %s is plain substitution. %s on user-influenced input is injection.

nodes.label: quote_ident and format('%I')
nodes.rationale: Quoting wraps a payload so ; and -- are characters in a name. It does not check existence, authorization, or sensibility. Use in addition to an allowlist.

nodes.label: The payload is not the problem — the position is
nodes.rationale: A value can always be a parameter and is then inert. An identifier can never be a parameter, so concatenation is the only way to vary it — which is why it needs an allowlist.
nodes.norm_label: the payload is not the problem — the position is

nodes.label: Database clock for created_at
nodes.rationale: DEFAULT now() is one clock. Node-generated timestamps disagree across API instances.

nodes.label: Built SET list
nodes.rationale: Assignments from keys the client sent distinguish absent from null. Keys go through an allowlist; values are parameters.

nodes.label: COALESCE patch form
nodes.rationale: Static statement, but absent and explicit null are both null in JS so clearing a field is impossible.

nodes.label: SET naming does not defeat HOT
nodes.rationale: COALESCE naming all columns: 1090 HOT; single-column SET: 1096. Only changing the indexed value dropped HOT to 0 of 2500.
nodes.norm_label: set naming does not defeat hot

nodes.label: IS DISTINCT FROM no-op guard
nodes.rationale: SET city = city still writes a row version. IS DISTINCT FROM skips no-ops; <> is NULL when either side is NULL. rowCount 0 then means no change or not found.

nodes.label: jsonb shallow merge patch
nodes.rationale: data || $1 stores JSON null rather than removing a key. Removal is data - key. || is shallow.

nodes.label: created_at DEFAULT now()
nodes.rationale: A DEFAULT covers every insert path. No trigger needed for created_at.

nodes.label: now() is the transaction timestamp
nodes.rationale: Every row in one transaction shares now(). clock_timestamp() moved 303 ms. That is why updated_at cannot be an optimistic version.

nodes.label: BEFORE UPDATE updated_at trigger
nodes.rationale: App-managed stamp stays stale on migrations and psql fixes. Trigger cost ~1.23–1.29× on the update. BEFORE so NEW is written in the same row version.

nodes.label: fsync vs synchronous_commit
nodes.rationale: fsync=off risks unrecoverable corruption; synchronous_commit=off can lose recent xacts without corruption.

nodes.label: ADD CONSTRAINT … NOT VALID then VALIDATE
nodes.norm_label: add constraint ... not valid then validate

nodes.label: Planner, WAL, and timeouts
nodes.rationale: random_page_cost=4.0 models spinning disks. max_wal_size=1GB causes checkpoint spikes. Timeouts stop incidents.

nodes.label: What is happening right now
nodes.rationale: pg_stat_activity is the 90-second incident query: xact_age, state, wait_event, query.

nodes.label: Zero-downtime schema changes
nodes.rationale: A waiting ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock blocks everything behind it. Schema change and code deploy are never simultaneous; expand-and-contract.

nodes.label: Migrations must use direct endpoint
nodes.rationale: Transaction pooling breaks advisory locks and CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY.

nodes.label: Waiting ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock queue
nodes.rationale: A 5 ms ALTER can cause a 30 s outage because new queries do not jump the queue behind a waiting ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock.

nodes.label: React Compiler is a static purity checker
nodes.rationale: It bails out instead of rewriting impure components. Skipped components are a purity report covering code that never ran.
nodes.norm_label: react compiler is a static purity checker

nodes.label: Inline render prop defeats memoization
nodes.rationale: An inline arrow is a new function each render, so PureComponent or memo never skips. Fix with useCallback only if the child is actually memoized.

nodes.label: this binding in class handlers
nodes.rationale: Extracting this.handleClick loses the receiver. Class bodies are strict so this is undefined. Prefer a class-field arrow; call-site arrows defeat PureComponent.

nodes.label: Memoization does not stop context updates
nodes.norm_label: memoization does not stop context updates

nodes.label: memo compares props only
nodes.rationale: Unlike PureComponent, memo does not compare state because useState already bails out on the same value.

nodes.label: Shallow comparison Object.is
nodes.rationale: New objects, arrays or inline functions each render make the check always fail. You pay the comparison and skip nothing.

nodes.label: Component PureComponent shouldComponentUpdate
nodes.rationale: Always render, shallow skip, or custom comparison. Function equivalents are plain, memo, and memo with a compare function.

nodes.label: memo is last resort
nodes.rationale: Shallow compare is not free, fails on fresh objects, and does not stop context. Structural fixes survive the Compiler; hand memoization largely does not.

nodes.label: React 19 context as provider
nodes.rationale: Render the context object directly as ThemeContext value={theme}. The .Provider form still works.

nodes.label: Legacy context removed in React 19
nodes.rationale: contextTypes and getChildContext are gone. A class consumes one context via static contextType.

nodes.label: cloneElement
nodes.rationale: Returns a new element with merged props. Uncommon and fragile, not deprecated. Only reaches direct children and hides data flow.

nodes.label: Compound components
nodes.rationale: Parent provides shared state through context; parts consume it and can be arranged freely. Parts only work inside the parent.

nodes.label: Make data flow visible
nodes.rationale: Prefer exported parts, data props, render props, context or hooks. Cloning hides where values come from.

nodes.label: Portals escape overflow and stacking contexts
nodes.rationale: overflow:hidden clips; transform/filter/opacity create stacking contexts z-index cannot cross; position:fixed inside a transform is relative to the ancestor.
nodes.norm_label: portals escape overflow and stacking contexts

nodes.label: dialog showModal and the top layer
nodes.rationale: Native top layer escapes stacking without moving the node, and brings focus trap, Escape and inertness.
nodes.norm_label: dialog showmodal and the top layer

nodes.label: React events vs native events on portals
nodes.rationale: React bubbling follows the React tree; document click-outside sees the portal at body. Compare against the portal node or the dropdown closes as it opens.
nodes.norm_label: react events vs native events on portals

nodes.label: createPortal is client-only
nodes.rationale: Targets a real DOM node. Render after mount, or use a framework portal-aware component.

nodes.label: Portal accessibility obligation
nodes.rationale: React provides none. Focus in, trap, restore, Escape, inert background. react.dev flags this as a pitfall and points at WAI-ARIA.

nodes.label: Portal changes DOM placement only
nodes.rationale: Events, context, state, error boundaries, Suspense and unmount follow the React tree, not the DOM tree.

nodes.label: Effects only run on the client
nodes.rationale: They do not run during server rendering, so fetched data is absent from initial HTML, and they are where window, document and localStorage are legal.
nodes.norm_label: effects only run on the client

nodes.label: Application init belongs at module level
nodes.rationale: Module code runs once per page load. No component-scoped mechanism can promise once, because components mount more than once.
nodes.norm_label: application init belongs at module level

nodes.label: typeof window guard around module init
nodes.rationale: The module is also evaluated during server rendering, where localStorage does not exist. Without the guard the import throws.
nodes.norm_label: typeof window guard around module init

nodes.label: useSyncExternalStore
nodes.rationale: Reads the value when React needs it, takes a server snapshot, and will not resubscribe while subscribe keeps the same identity. Prevents tearing.

nodes.label: Twelve cases; only fetching survives
nodes.rationale: Cases 1–4 are Phase 3 state-shape. Case 12 is a legitimate effect that still prefers a framework or cache. That ratio is the point.

nodes.label: useLayoutEffect does nothing on the server
nodes.rationale: No layout information and no paint. Options: useEffect, client-only Suspense, isMounted after hydration, or useSyncExternalStore.
nodes.norm_label: uselayouteffect does nothing on the server

nodes.label: Fetching data in an effect
nodes.rationale: Fetching is the one You-Might-Not-Need case that survives as a legitimate effect, and react.dev still recommends something else.

nodes.label: subscribe must be declared outside the component
nodes.rationale: Inline it is a new function every render, so React tears down and rebuilds the subscription every time.
nodes.norm_label: subscribe must be declared outside the component

nodes.label: Eight legitimate dependency-removal moves
nodes.rationale: Move static values outside the component, build them inside the effect, depend on primitives, call during render, updater form, useEffectEvent, event handler, or split effects.

nodes.label: Illegitimate dependency fixes
nodes.rationale: Suppressing the linter, a counter that always shows 1, and refs used to hide a dependency produce confusing bugs.

nodes.label: useEffectEvent
nodes.rationale: Read the latest value without reacting to it — one of the eight legitimate moves.

nodes.label: StrictMode
nodes.rationale: Double-renders components and double-mounts effects in development only. A bug detector; switching it off ships the bug.

nodes.label: useEffect as synchronization
nodes.rationale: An effect synchronizes a component with an external system. Not a lifecycle callback and not the place to respond to a click.

nodes.label: useEffectEvent
nodes.rationale: Stable in 19.2. Read latest props and state from an effect without making them dependencies. Call only from effects in the same component.

nodes.label: Dependencies should match the code
nodes.rationale: You cannot choose Effect dependencies. To remove one, prove to the linter it is unnecessary by editing the surrounding code.

nodes.label: any
nodes.rationale: Assignable to and from everything. Spreads through inference. Measured: the two any lines produced no diagnostics. JSON.parse returns any.

nodes.label: unknown
nodes.rationale: Everything assigns to it; it assigns to nothing until narrowed. Correct type for input you did not create. catch is unknown under useUnknownInCatchVariables.

nodes.label: type alias
nodes.rationale: Only aliases can be unions, tuples, primitives, mapped, conditional, and template literal types. Discriminated unions force a large share of types to be aliases.

nodes.label: JsonValue
nodes.rationale: string | number | boolean | null | JsonValue[] | { [key: string]: JsonValue }. Honest alternative to any for arbitrary JSON. Interfaces lack an implicit index signature and may not satisfy it.

nodes.label: Array.isArray type guard
nodes.rationale: Built-in type guard. Narrows to string[] cleanly where typeof object cannot tell an array from a Date, a plain object, or null.

nodes.label: typeof narrowing
nodes.rationale: A typeof check changes the type inside the branch. Works on string, number, bigint, boolean, symbol, undefined, function. object is a bucket. Narrows the else by elimination too.

nodes.label: unknown at the door never any
nodes.rationale: Assign fetch/json to unknown and prove it with a schema. The narrowing step is the work any skips and the bug any ships.
nodes.norm_label: unknown at the door never any

nodes.label: reduce type argument pins accumulator
nodes.rationale: Without reduce<number>, the accumulator infers from the array element type (JsonValue), not from the initial 0. Measured TS18047 and TS2365 until the type argument was supplied.

nodes.label: Reveal narrowed type via impossible assignment
nodes.rationale: const r: 1 = v reports Type 'X' is not assignable to type '1', naming the exact type the checker holds. Settles narrowing arguments without a runtime print.
nodes.norm_label: reveal narrowed type via impossible assignment

nodes.label: Accessor infinite-recursion trap
nodes.rationale: get name() { return this.name; } calls itself until RangeError. Backing store must be a different name (#name).

nodes.label: Class getters and setters
nodes.rationale: Accessors go on the prototype like methods. Pair a #private field with a public get/set. static get/set put the accessor on the class object.

nodes.label: Static fields evaluated at class evaluation
nodes.rationale: MDN: evaluated during class evaluation with this set to the class. A throwing block prevents the class existing; expensive work is paid at module load.
nodes.norm_label: static fields evaluated at class evaluation

nodes.label: Static initialization blocks
nodes.rationale: Run statements (loops, try/catch) and access private scope during class evaluation. Evaluated at the class statement, not first construction.

nodes.label: static members
nodes.rationale: static puts a member on the class object itself, not on instances or the prototype. instance.staticThing is undefined because the instance chain never passes through Ctor.

nodes.label: this in a static method
nodes.rationale: this is the class it was called on. new this(...) in a factory returns the subclass because extends links class objects.

nodes.label: #x in obj brand check
nodes.rationale: Asks whether the object has that private element without throwing. Stronger than instanceof because privates cannot be forged or added later.

nodes.label: Private elements
nodes.rationale: The one class feature with no desugaring. # prefix; privacy enforced by JavaScript itself, in the grammar.

nodes.label: Private elements are not inherited
nodes.rationale: Not part of the prototypical inheritance model. A subclass cannot read the parent's #field. JS has no protected. Same name in parent and child are independent slots.

nodes.label: Private elements are not serialisable
nodes.rationale: JSON.stringify cannot see them; structuredClone does not duplicate them. A class with private state needs its own toJSON and clone.

nodes.label: Private access SyntaxError outside class
nodes.rationale: obj.#field outside the declaring class is a parse-time SyntaxError, so the file never runs. Not equivalent to _underscore.

nodes.label: Private access TypeError on wrong object
nodes.rationale: Inside the class, access on a non-instance throws TypeError: Cannot read private member #x from an object whose class did not declare it.
nodes.norm_label: private access typeerror on wrong object

nodes.label: Private identifier unique namespace
nodes.rationale: All private identifiers in a class must be unique; namespace shared between static and instance. Only get/set pairs may repeat. #constructor is reserved.

nodes.label: class
nodes.rationale: class is half syntactic sugar over prototypes; the false half is the part worth knowing.

nodes.label: Five class features that are not sugar
nodes.rationale: Always strict; TypeError without new; methods non-enumerable; block-scoped TDZ; private elements have no desugaring.
nodes.norm_label: five class features that are not sugar

nodes.label: Where class members live
nodes.rationale: Instance field = own per instance; method() = Ctor.prototype; static = class object; #field = private slot, not inherited.

nodes.label: Polymorphic static factory
nodes.rationale: Use new this(...) not new Model(...) so User.create() builds a User. Statics inherit through the class-object chain.

nodes.label: Private elements are encapsulation not security
nodes.rationale: A debugger shows them. Guarantee is that other code cannot accidentally depend on internals — a maintenance property, not secrecy.
nodes.norm_label: private elements are encapsulation not security

nodes.label: Promise.prototype.finally
nodes.rationale: Runs on both paths and passes the outcome through. Return value is ignored; throw inside finally replaces the outcome.

nodes.label: .then(f, g) vs .then(f).catch(g)
nodes.rationale: Two-argument g only sees upstream rejections, not errors thrown by f. A chained .catch is downstream of f. Prefer .then().catch().

nodes.label: Promise pending / fulfilled / rejected
nodes.rationale: Transitions exactly once from pending to fulfilled or rejected, then immutable. Settled means fulfilled or rejected. Resolved-with-a-promise stays pending until that one settles.

nodes.label: async function
nodes.rationale: Makes the function return a promise and permits await. Return fulfils; throw rejects. Adds no capability beyond promises, only syntax.

nodes.label: await inside forEach
nodes.rationale: Array.prototype.forEach ignores the returned promise, so the callback is fire-and-forget. Use for...of sequentially or Promise.all(map) in parallel.

nodes.label: await accepts any thenable
nodes.rationale: Non-promises are wrapped and still cost a microtask. await null is a cheap yield to microtasks only.

nodes.label: Top-level await
