nodes.rationale: ES modules can await outside a function; importers wait. The module cannot be require()d from CommonJS.

nodes.label: Floating promise
nodes.rationale: A promise-returning call nobody awaited or handled. Rejection is fatal since Node 15; fulfilment may silently skip a side effect. Happens via forgotten await, forEach, or missing return in .then.

nodes.label: @typescript-eslint/no-floating-promises
nodes.rationale: Flags discarded promise results; no-misused-promises catches forEach and async callbacks where sync is expected. Both need TypeScript types.

nodes.label: void plus .catch for fire-and-forget
nodes.rationale: void marks intent for readers and linters; .catch is what makes it safe. Never leave the catch off.

nodes.label: unhandledRejection
nodes.rationale: Fatal by default since Node 15 (exit code 1). --unhandled-rejections=warn restores the old warn-and-continue for a temporary audit only.

nodes.label: Async Promise executor
nodes.rationale: throw rejects the executor's own promise, which nobody holds. The constructed promise stays pending forever. On modern Node the orphaned rejection is a fatal unhandledRejection.

nodes.label: Forgotten return inside .then
nodes.rationale: a => { get(a); } returns undefined so the chain resolves immediately while inner work is unwatched. Concise a => get(a) avoids it.

nodes.label: Nesting .then instead of chaining
nodes.rationale: Rebuilds the callback pyramid. Inner promises are floating; an outer .catch never sees their rejections.

nodes.label: Promises are eager
nodes.rationale: Work starts when the promise is created, not when it is awaited. To defer, wrap creation in a function. Settling twice is a silent no-op.

nodes.label: Return or it is not chained
nodes.rationale: .then returns a new promise that adopts whatever the handler returns. Forget return and the inner work detaches; its rejection is unhandled.
nodes.norm_label: return or it is not chained

nodes.label: Create then await is already parallel
nodes.rationale: Promises are eager, so creating both before either await is parallel. Separate awaits risk unhandled rejection if one rejects before its await. Promise.all is the safer default.
nodes.norm_label: create then await is already parallel

nodes.label: Declaration vs selector blast radius
nodes.rationale: An invalid declaration is dropped locally; an invalid selector in a plain comma list discards the whole rule; an unclosed brace swallows following rules.

nodes.label: :is() vs :where() specificity
nodes.rationale: They match identically. :is() contributes the most specific argument (an id raises every match); :where() always contributes zero. Both have forgiving argument lists.

nodes.label: Native CSS nesting
nodes.rationale: Baseline Widely since 2023-12-11. & is the parent selector reference, not string concatenation. At-rules nest too. Write the &.

nodes.label: Native nesting is not Sass concatenation
nodes.rationale: Sass &__title builds .card__title. Native CSS treats that as invalid and drops it. BEM suffix generation cannot survive dropping the preprocessor.
nodes.norm_label: native nesting is not sass concatenation

nodes.label: :not() negation
nodes.rationale: Accepts lists and complex selectors. Specificity is the most specific argument. :not(.a, .b) means neither, not 'not a or not b'. Neutralise with :not(:where(#id)).

nodes.label: Forgiving :is() argument lists
nodes.rationale: :is() and :where() drop invalid members and keep valid ones. :not() and :has() are unforgiving. Uncertain selectors get their own rule or wrap in :is().

nodes.label: Unforgiving selector lists
nodes.rationale: One invalid selector in a plain comma list discards the entire rule. Adding :popover-open to a shared list silently unstyles every other component in unsupported engines.

nodes.label: Nesting hides specificity growth
nodes.rationale: Each level compiles to another descendant class. Four tidy levels become 0,4,0. & in a compound with a list behaves like :is() and takes the highest parent specificity. Keep nesting to two levels.

nodes.label: box-sizing: border-box
nodes.rationale: width/height include padding and border. Applied to *, *::before, *::after so generated content is not left on content-box.

nodes.label: Modern small CSS reset
nodes.rationale: A dozen justifiable lines beat a 300-line library: border-box on * plus pseudos, margin 0, line-height 1.5, block media, font inherit on controls, overflow-wrap.

nodes.label: Cascade origin order
nodes.rationale: Normal: user-agent < user < author. !important inverts so a user accessibility override beats author !important. Any author type selector beats any UA default.

nodes.label: Form controls do not inherit font
nodes.rationale: UA sets an explicit 13.3333px sans-serif on button/input, beating inheritance. Fix: font: inherit, then set the page font on body or :root.
nodes.norm_label: form controls do not inherit font

nodes.label: User-agent stylesheet
nodes.rationale: A page with no CSS is still styled: body 8px margin, heading sizes, list indent as padding, img inline, box-sizing content-box.

nodes.label: content is mandatory on ::before/::after
nodes.rationale: Without content the pseudo-element does not exist. content:"" still creates the box. They sit as first/last children, so padding and overflow apply and they can be flex/grid items.

nodes.label: Pseudo-elements are not in the DOM
nodes.rationale: Engine-created boxes with no node. querySelector('::before') is null; generated text is absent from textContent. Reachable only via getComputedStyle(el, '::before').
nodes.norm_label: pseudo-elements are not in the dom

nodes.label: Reset vs normalise vs nothing
nodes.rationale: Normalize.css patched 2012 engine differences that have largely converged. A small modern reset is the 2026 default; hard-resetting list-style or *:focus outline is a defect.

nodes.label: Attribute selector operators
nodes.rationale: Seven operators: presence, = exact, ~= space-list, |= hyphen prefix (lang), ^= starts, $= ends, *= contains. Specificity 0,1,0. Values case-sensitive unless i flag.

nodes.label: [class~=] vs [class*=]
nodes.rationale: ~= matches a whole space-separated token (like .a). *= is a substring over the whole string and also matches alpha/banana. *= on class is almost always wrong.

nodes.label: :placeholder-shown empty-field test
nodes.rationale: There is no :empty for inputs. :placeholder-shown requires a placeholder attribute — often placeholder=" " just to make the selector work.

nodes.label: Form-state pseudo-classes
nodes.rationale: :checked, :required/:optional, :valid/:invalid, :user-valid/:user-invalid, :placeholder-shown, :indeterminate, :in-range/:out-of-range, :autofill.

nodes.label: :invalid vs :user-invalid
nodes.rationale: :invalid matches from page load so empty required fields paint red on arrival. :user-invalid waits until the user has interacted — the CSS replacement for a JS touched flag.

nodes.label: :lang() and :dir()
nodes.rationale: :lang() matches inherited language including subtags. :dir() matches computed direction including dir=auto, unlike [dir=rtl] which only sees an explicit attribute.

nodes.label: Style on aria-* attributes
nodes.rationale: Visual state and accessibility state cannot drift if they are the same attribute. A parallel .is-open class can be forgotten.

nodes.label: Custom checkbox via appearance: none
nodes.rationale: Keep the real input and style it. Hiding it and styling a sibling div removes tab order and accessibility tree membership.

nodes.label: Avoid id selectors in CSS
nodes.rationale: 1,0,0 specificity, uniqueness that cannot style a component twice, and ids belong to fragments/ARIA.

nodes.label: :is() :not() :has() specificity
nodes.rationale: They add no weight of their own; they take the most specific argument. One id in the list raises every match.

nodes.label: Lexicographic specificity compare
nodes.rationale: Compare left to right; no carrying. #nav (1,0,0) beats thirteen classes. Not a base-10 number.

nodes.label: Nesting & specificity
nodes.rationale: & behaves like :is(): a parent list containing an id raises every nested rule.

nodes.label: Specificity triple (A,B,C)
nodes.rationale: A=ids, B=classes/attributes/pseudo-classes, C=types/pseudo-elements. * combinators and :where() add nothing.

nodes.label: :where() zero specificity
nodes.rationale: Always 0,0,0 regardless of contents — the tool for overridable resets and library defaults.

nodes.label: Flat specificity strategy
nodes.rationale: Do not fight: :where() for defaults, @layer for precedence, one class per component rule, never style by id.

nodes.label: Request-id middleware
nodes.rationale: Generate or accept X-Request-Id, set on req, return on the response, continue with AsyncLocalStorage.

nodes.label: Canonical Express middleware skeleton
nodes.rationale: disable x-powered-by, json parser, routes, 404, then four-arg error middleware. Keep one composition root.

nodes.label: Four-argument error middleware
nodes.rationale: Error middleware must be (err, req, res, next) so Express can detect it. A three-arg 404 is not an error handler.

nodes.label: entity.parse.failed 400
nodes.rationale: Bad JSON is a client error. Express surfaces status 400 and type entity.parse.failed.

nodes.label: 413 entity.too.large
nodes.rationale: Oversize bodies become 413 Payload Too Large with type entity.too.large. Map that in error middleware.

nodes.label: Accept inbound request ids
nodes.rationale: Accept inbound request ids for trace continuity across gateways and clients.

nodes.label: Parsers early, errors last
nodes.rationale: Handlers read req.body so parsers must run first. Error middleware is skipped in the normal chain and must be last.

nodes.label: Stable public parse-error envelope
nodes.rationale: Do not leak raw parser messages. Map to a stable code and log detail server-side with a request id.

nodes.label: 401 vs 403
nodes.rationale: 401 unauthenticated; 403 authenticated but not allowed.

nodes.label: HttpError
nodes.rationale: Carry statusCode and code on thrown errors. Map domain failures once in error middleware. Avoid deep inheritance trees.

nodes.label: Process-level errors
nodes.rationale: unhandledRejection / uncaughtException are Node topics, not Express request envelopes.

nodes.label: Operational error
nodes.rationale: Expected at the edge (bad input, not found). Expose a clear message + code. Log it.

nodes.label: Programmer error
nodes.rationale: Bugs. Hide messages (they leak paths, schemas, exploit detail) and return a generic 500. Do not keep the process alive after unknown programmer errors.

nodes.label: Hide stack in production
nodes.rationale: Stack traces and internal exception messages for unexpected 500s must never appear in production error JSON.

nodes.label: Headers fixed once body starts
nodes.rationale: Cannot set a header after the body is already sent. Set headers first.

nodes.label: Express 5 async rejection forwarding
nodes.rationale: Rejected promises from async handlers reach error middleware on Express 5. You do not need express-async-errors for that baseline.

nodes.label: Error response contract
nodes.rationale: One public JSON shape for errors. Include a stable code. Never send err.stack when NODE_ENV === production.

nodes.label: headersSent delegates to default handler
nodes.rationale: If res.headersSent, return next(err) instead of writing another body.

nodes.label: Express arity detection
nodes.rationale: Function length 4: (err, req, res, next).

nodes.label: Four-arg error middleware
nodes.rationale: Express detects error middleware by arity. Mount it last. Omit next and errors vanish into the wrong path.

nodes.label: 404 three-arg middleware
nodes.rationale: 404 is normal middleware (3 args) after routes, not error middleware. Always sends 404 when reached.

nodes.label: try/catch domain mapping
nodes.rationale: Still use try/catch when you convert errors to domain responses inside the handler without wanting the global mapper.

nodes.label: argon2id
nodes.rationale: Password Hashing Competition winner. Memory-hard and side-channel resistant. First choice for a new project; needs the argon2 package.

nodes.label: bcrypt
nodes.rationale: Acceptable and ubiquitous. Silently truncates input past 72 bytes.

nodes.label: Rehash at login
nodes.rationale: Parameters live in the stored string so cost can rise when you have the plaintext. Bulk recomputation is impossible — that is the point. Hash on unknown-email too.

nodes.label: Per-password salt
nodes.rationale: 16 random bytes from a CSPRNG, stored next to the hash. Not secret. Makes one precomputed table useless and identical passwords hash differently.

nodes.label: scrypt
nodes.rationale: Memory-hard, built into node:crypto. Store scheme$N$r$p$salt$hash. Uses ~128*N*r bytes per concurrent hash; never scryptSync on a request path.

nodes.label: libuv thread-pool login capacity
nodes.rationale: Default four threads. At N=2^15 four hashes take ~166 ms like one, then throughput flattens at about 23 logins/s per process.

nodes.label: Idle and absolute session timeouts
nodes.rationale: Idle alone lets a daily session live forever; absolute alone interrupts active users. Redis TTL is only idle; absolute reads stored createdAt.

nodes.label: Rotate session on privilege change
nodes.rationale: Destroy and recreate on login, logout, password/email change, MFA completion, role elevation. 32 bytes from randomBytes, never Math.random.

nodes.label: Server-side logout
nodes.rationale: clearCookie only removes this browser's copy. Anyone who captured the id still has a working credential. Delete the Redis row.

nodes.label: Session fixation
nodes.rationale: Attacker gets the victim to use a known session id, then rides it after login. Works whenever the identifier survives the privilege change.

nodes.label: Per-user session index
nodes.rationale: user-sessions:userId is how 'log out everywhere' and password-change revocation work. Cannot be added retroactively for sessions already issued.

nodes.label: Authorization Code with PKCE
nodes.rationale: The only flow to use for web, SPA, and mobile. PKCE binds the code to the starter so an intercepted code is useless without the verifier. Implicit and ROPC are deprecated.

nodes.label: Access token as identity (confused deputy)
nodes.rationale: An access token is a bearer credential for an API, not addressed to you. A token from another app may still call /userinfo. Validate an ID token whose aud is your client id.

nodes.label: (iss, sub) account link
nodes.rationale: sub is unique only within an issuer; email is mutable and can be reassigned. After OIDC, mint your own session rather than depending on provider tokens.

nodes.label: OAuth 2.0
nodes.rationale: Delegated authorization. Issues an access token so an application can act on the user's behalf. Says nothing reliable about who the user is.

nodes.label: OpenID Connect
nodes.rationale: Authentication layered on OAuth. ID token is a JWT with sub, iss, aud, exp addressed to your client. Sign in with Google is OIDC.

nodes.label: A password hash must be slow
nodes.rationale: SHA-256 is excellent at being fast, which is the attacker's advantage. Measured ~344k SHA-256/s vs ~11 scrypt hashes at N=2^15 on one core.
nodes.norm_label: a password hash must be slow

nodes.label: Revocation versus a database lookup
nodes.rationale: Sessions delete a row and the next request is denied. A JWT is valid because the maths says so until expiry. Short expiry plus refresh rebuilds sessions with extra steps.

nodes.label: Query string coercion
nodes.rationale: Query and params are strings. z.number() without coerce fails; use z.coerce.number() deliberately.

nodes.label: Validation middleware factory
nodes.rationale: validate({body, params, query}) returns middleware. Failure: 400 with stable codes. Success: attach parsed data.

nodes.label: Error response contract
nodes.rationale: Stable JSON error body (code, message, details), no stack in production.

nodes.label: Phase 5 — Error handling
nodes.rationale: Four-argument error middleware last. Express 5 forwards rejected promises to next(err).

nodes.label: Boolean false query trap
nodes.rationale: ?active=false is the string "false", which is truthy. Use explicit enums or coerce helpers.

nodes.label: Validate at the HTTP boundary
nodes.rationale: Everything from the network is untrusted. Services receive validated data, not req.body. DB-only validation is late, worse errors, and injection risk.

nodes.label: includeIf gitdir identity switch
nodes.rationale: includeIf gitdir:~/work/ points at a second file that sets user.email, so work and personal identities switch by directory.

nodes.label: Config layers and precedence
nodes.rationale: system → global → local → worktree → -c. Last one to set a key wins. --show-origin --show-scope names the file that won.

nodes.label: .git/ directory
nodes.rationale: The whole repository is one directory. Delete it and you have ordinary files; copy it and you copied history. One rm -rf .git is irreversible.

nodes.label: git init still creates master on 2.55.0
nodes.rationale: The hint says the default changes in Git 3.0. 'Git defaults to main now' is false on this build.
nodes.norm_label: git init still creates master on 2.55.0

nodes.label: Author identity required to commit
nodes.rationale: Author and committer are fields inside the commit object. Without them there is nothing to hash. Hard failure, not a warning.

nodes.label: Unset does not mean unused
nodes.rationale: Built-in defaults still apply. Unset init.defaultBranch is master on 2.55.0; unset pull.rebase makes a divergent pull fail.

nodes.label: Identity is asserted, not authenticated
nodes.rationale: user.email is free text. Audit value comes from host push authentication; cryptographic proof needs signed commits.

nodes.label: Git is not a backup
nodes.rationale: Git versions what you committed and by default lives on one machine. Uncommitted and ignored files are outside it.

nodes.label: Blob
nodes.rationale: File bytes only. No name, path, mode, or timestamp. Filename lives in the tree that points at the blob.

nodes.label: Tree
nodes.rationale: Sorted directory listing of mode, type, hash, name. Empty directories cannot be committed because there are no entries to store.

nodes.label: Tree entry modes
nodes.rationale: 100644 regular, 100755 executable, 120000 symlink, 040000 directory, 160000 gitlink. No owner, group, or timestamps.

nodes.label: Cached stat data
nodes.rationale: git status skips re-hashing if size and mtime match. Network or Windows shares that lie about modes make everything look modified.

nodes.label: The index is a real file
nodes.rationale: .git/index is a binary file of paths with blob hashes and cached stat data. git add writes content into the object store first.
nodes.norm_label: the index is a real file

nodes.label: Merge stage numbers
nodes.rationale: Stage 0 normally. During conflict: 1 base, 2 ours, 3 theirs. UU in status means stages 1/2/3 and no stage 0.

nodes.label: AM status code
nodes.rationale: Left column is index versus HEAD; right is working tree versus index. AM means staged and then edited; commit records the older content.

nodes.label: Staging is a copy, not a bookmark
nodes.rationale: The index recorded a hash, so later edits cannot change what is staged. Enables git add -p and recovery of staged-but-uncommitted blobs via fsck --lost-found.
nodes.norm_label: staging is a copy, not a bookmark

nodes.label: Nullish coalescing ??
nodes.rationale: Default to ??. It falls back only on null and undefined, so 0, '' and false survive. Mixing ?? with || or && is a SyntaxError without parentheses. NaN is a number so ?? does not catch it.

nodes.label: Array.isArray
nodes.rationale: instanceof Array fails across realms (iframe, vm). Array.isArray works regardless.

nodes.label: Eight JavaScript types
nodes.rationale: Seven primitives plus object. Arrays, dates, regexes, Map and classes are objects. Functions are objects; typeof reports 'function' as a convenience.

nodes.label: typeof null === 'object' bug
nodes.rationale: Historic tag-bit bug: objects used tag 000 and null was the all-zero pointer. Fix rejected because existing code depends on it. Always && v !== null.

nodes.label: Logical assignment ||= &&= ??=
nodes.rationale: The write is inside the short-circuit. a ||= b skips the setter when a is truthy; a = a || b always writes. Load-bearing on setters, proxies, Vue/MobX and frozen objects.

nodes.label: Autoboxing
nodes.rationale: Property access on a primitive temporarily wraps it, looks up the method on String/Number/Boolean.prototype, then discards the wrapper. Assignments do not persist. null and undefined have no wrapper.

nodes.label: Wrapper constructors
nodes.rationale: Never new String/Number/Boolean: they produce objects, so typeof is 'object' and new Boolean(false) is truthy. Without new they are conversion functions returning primitives.

nodes.label: Symbol implicit string coercion throws
nodes.rationale: '' + sym and `${sym}` throw so a unique value cannot silently become a non-unique string. String(sym) is the safe conversion.

nodes.label: ToBoolean
nodes.rationale: if (x) is ToBoolean. Objects never convert to a primitive here, so [] is truthy even though [] == false. '0', 'false', {} and new Boolean(false) are all truthy.

nodes.label: Never extend built-in prototypes
nodes.rationale: Prototype extension is global and collides. Array.prototype.flatten was renamed flat because a library had taken the name. Write a standalone function or ponyfill.

nodes.label: Phase 3 Functions, scope and closures
nodes.rationale: this, closures and the scope chain are the three mechanisms every later phase assumes and interviews probe.

nodes.label: Phase 4 Objects, prototypes and classes
nodes.rationale: Everything non-primitive. Prototype rows make class stop being magic; copying is four operations with four failure modes.

nodes.label: Shallow vs deep copy
nodes.rationale: Copying an object is four different operations with four different failure modes. structuredClone belongs here, not in Phase 5.

nodes.label: Phase 5 The built-in library
nodes.rationale: 26 topics grouped by object, not method. Grouping reduces noise, never coverage.

nodes.label: Phase 6 Iteration, destructuring and generators
nodes.rationale: The protocol layer. Small phase that lets for...of, spread, destructuring and Promise.all work on the same objects.

nodes.label: Phase 7 Asynchronous JavaScript
nodes.rationale: Centre of gravity of the syllabus. If you only finish one phase to Master depth, finish this one. Eleven Master topics; 06 of 11 done.

nodes.label: Master-first across all phases
nodes.rationale: Understand and Know tiers are deferred until every phase's Master topics are written. Next unit after 01-08 is Phase 4, not topic 09.

nodes.label: Nullish coalescing ?? versus ||
nodes.rationale: ?? falls back only on null/undefined so retries: 0 survives; || treats every falsy as missing. Mixing ?? with || or && is a SyntaxError without parentheses.

nodes.label: undefined versus missing key
nodes.rationale: !== undefined, ?., and ?? cannot tell a present undefined from absence. PATCH/options need Object.hasOwn. JSON.stringify drops undefined, so the wire distinction is present-vs-absent or null-vs-absent.

nodes.label: for...in enumeration
nodes.rationale: Same enumerable string keys as Object.keys but also walks the prototype chain. Smell on a plain object; Object.keys/entries should be the default.

nodes.label: Object.keys values entries
nodes.rationale: Same own enumerable string-keyed set that JSON.stringify serialises. Coerce non-objects; throw TypeError on null/undefined. Integer-index keys sort ascending and come back as strings.

nodes.label: JSON round-trip clone
nodes.rationale: Seven documented losses: undefined/functions/symbols omitted-or-nulled, NaN/Infinity→null, Date→string, Map/Set→{}, BigInt throws, cycles throw, symbol/non-enumerable skipped. Acceptable only for already-JSON-shaped data.

nodes.label: JSON.stringify
nodes.rationale: Lossy and silent except BigInt and cycles (TypeError). undefined/functions/symbols omitted in objects, nulled in arrays. Sees the same own enumerable string-keyed set as Object.keys. Map/Set become {}.

nodes.label: JSON.parse reviver
nodes.rationale: Must end with return value or every other key is deleted. Innermost-first. Only place to repair stringify losses (e.g. revive *At dates). context.source for 64-bit precision.

nodes.label: Own enumerable string-keyed set
nodes.rationale: Those three words decide what keys/values/entries, JSON.stringify, and (almost) spread silently drop: inherited, non-enumerable, and symbol keys.

nodes.label: reviver context.source
nodes.rationale: Primitives only. Original JSON text before double rounding. Use to rebuild BigInt IDs past MAX_SAFE_INTEGER.

nodes.label: JSON.parse
nodes.rationale: Invalid JSON throws SyntaxError. Trailing commas and single quotes are illegal. Empty body throws.

nodes.label: JSON.parse reviver
nodes.rationale: Transforms parsed values depth-first, children first, root last under key "". Must return value or the property is deleted.

nodes.label: JSON.stringify
nodes.rationale: Lossy and silent except BigInt and cycles, which throw. Sees own enumerable string keys like Object.keys.

nodes.label: JSON.stringify replacer
nodes.rationale: Function redacts (undefined omits); array is a deny-by-default key allowlist. Symbol keys cannot be re-included.

nodes.label: JSON.stringify silent drops
nodes.rationale: undefined/functions/symbols omitted in objects and null in arrays; NaN/Infinity become null; Map/Set become {}.

nodes.label: toJSON hook
nodes.rationale: Serialiser uses toJSON's return value. Date uses it (ISO string). Cleanest per-type control.

nodes.label: Map does not serialise
nodes.rationale: JSON.stringify(map) is {}. Convert with fromEntries (string keys only) or JSON.stringify([...map]) to keep key types.

nodes.label: Array.prototype.sort
nodes.rationale: Default is a UTF-16 string sort; sort mutates and returns the same array.

nodes.label: ES2019 stable sort
nodes.rationale: Equal elements keep relative order. Enables two-pass multi-column sorts. Before ES2019 stability was engine-dependent.

nodes.label: sort comparator contract
nodes.rationale: Negative before, positive after, zero or NaN equal. Only the sign matters, so a-b works for numbers.

nodes.label: Decorate-sort-undecorate
nodes.rationale: Map to {item,key}, sort on key, map back. Avoids O(n log n) key recomputation and unstable computed keys.

nodes.label: Default sort is string sort
nodes.rationale: Converts to strings and compares UTF-16 code units, so [1,30,4,21,100000] becomes [1,100000,21,30,4].

nodes.label: Fisher-Yates shuffle
nodes.rationale: sort(() => Math.random()-0.5) breaks every consistency rule. Use Fisher-Yates.

nodes.label: Five comparator consistency rules
nodes.rationale: Pure, stable, reflexive, anti-symmetric, transitive. Violations do not throw; order is implementation-defined.

nodes.label: Four sort rules
nodes.rationale: Always pass a numeric comparator; copy or toSorted; keep the comparator total; undefined and holes go last.

nodes.label: Promise.prototype.catch
nodes.rationale: Shortcut for then(undefined, onRejected). A catch that returns normally restores the chain to fulfilled.

nodes.label: Promise.prototype.finally
nodes.rationale: Transparent: a return is ignored and the original outcome passes through. A throw or rejected/pending return still replaces the outcome.

nodes.label: Promise.prototype.then
nodes.rationale: Returns a new promise that is always pending when returned. The handler always runs asynchronously, even if the current promise is already settled.

nodes.label: Forgotten return in then
nodes.rationale: A handler that returns nothing fulfils immediately with undefined; the inner promise floats and its rejection is unhandled.

nodes.label: Identity and thrower default handlers
nodes.rationale: A missing onFulfilled is (x)=>x; a missing onRejected is (x)=>{throw x}. Error propagation is just the default thrower, one link at a time.

nodes.label: idx_scan
nodes.rationale: Zero over a full business cycle means the index is only costing you.

nodes.label: PostgreSQL index
nodes.rationale: A second sorted copy of some columns written on every INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE so some SELECTs can stop scanning. You buy read speed with write time and disk.

nodes.label: PRIMARY KEY is a unique index
nodes.rationale: A table is never truly at zero indexes if it has a PRIMARY KEY or UNIQUE constraint.
nodes.norm_label: primary key is a unique index

nodes.label: Index write cost
nodes.rationale: One index took a 200000-row insert from 1239 ms to 2266 ms; three took it to 4035 ms with indexes 36 MB against 15 MB of heap.

nodes.label: B-tree
nodes.rationale: The default CREATE INDEX; serves equality, ranges, ORDER BY, min/max endpoints, and prefix LIKE only with a byte-order opclass.

nodes.label: Prefix LIKE on a B-tree
nodes.rationale: LIKE 'abc%' is logically a range but under a non-C collation the B-tree sort is not byte order.

nodes.label: text_pattern_ops
nodes.rationale: Fixes prefix LIKE under a non-C collation (34.5 ms to 4.1 ms) but cannot serve collation-aware ORDER BY; keep both indexes.

nodes.label: Non-indexable predicate shape
nodes.rationale: <> / NOT IN / leading wildcard cannot seek; OR is fine only when every branch has its own usable index.

nodes.label: GIN
nodes.rationale: Indexes the parts of a value so @>, @@ and LIKE '%x%' become indexable. 130× faster on a one-row match, slower than seq scan on a 16% match.

nodes.label: gist_trgm_ops distance ordering
nodes.rationale: GIN cannot do <-> nearest-neighbour at all; GiST did it in 110 ms versus 766 ms seq scan, at 48 MB against GIN's 13 MB.

nodes.label: jsonb_ops vs jsonb_path_ops
nodes.rationale: path_ops is smaller and faster for @> but cannot serve ? / ?| / ?&. Default to jsonb_ops.

nodes.label: GIN pending list
nodes.rationale: Buffers inserts so the 3.2× write cost is deferred into VACUUM or a later query; fastupdate=off trades insert speed for predictable reads.

nodes.label: pg_trgm
nodes.rationale: Makes infix LIKE indexable. Short patterns under three characters return most of the table and can be slower than a sequential scan.

nodes.label: Unused-index audit
nodes.rationale: idx_scan=0 is necessary not sufficient: exclude UNIQUE/constraint-backing indexes, check stats_reset, audit every replica, wait a full business cycle.

nodes.label: stats_fetch_consistency cache
nodes.rationale: Backends flush counters on a timer and the reader caches its snapshot; never conclude unused from a reading taken seconds after the query.

nodes.label: GIN for jsonb, arrays and full text; pg_trgm for LIKE
nodes.norm_label: gin for jsonb, arrays and full text; pg_trgm for like

nodes.label: Lazy dynamic imports
nodes.rationale: Lazy speeds cold start but moves cost to first use; eager-import the hot path.

nodes.label: Boot sequence — validate, connect, listen, ready
nodes.norm_label: boot sequence — validate, connect, listen, ready

nodes.label: Time to readiness
nodes.rationale: Measure phases through listen+ready; DNS to Postgres often dominates import time.

nodes.label: Validate connect listen ready
nodes.rationale: Any other order accepts requests the process cannot serve, or fails halfway with sockets already open.

nodes.label: yarn install --immutable
nodes.rationale: Fail when the lockfile would change so CI cannot silently drift.

nodes.label: CI/CD — Node version matrix, caches, artifacts
nodes.norm_label: ci/cd — node version matrix, caches, artifacts

nodes.label: Behind a reverse proxy — X-Forwarded-*, trust proxy, TLS
nodes.norm_label: behind a reverse proxy — x-forwarded-*, trust proxy, tls

nodes.label: Zero-downtime deploys — rolling restarts, drain, readiness
nodes.norm_label: zero-downtime deploys — rolling restarts, drain, readiness

nodes.label: Environment parity
nodes.rationale: Align runtime version, lockfile, and config shape; secrets and scale must still differ.

nodes.label: Honest staging
nodes.rationale: SQLite in staging while prod uses Postgres is a lie for dialects, transactions, and concurrency.

nodes.label: Readable.toWeb / fromWeb
nodes.rationale: Convert once at the boundary. Node chunks are Buffers; web chunks are Uint8Array. Repeated conversion adds wrapper queues.

nodes.label: ReadableStream lock
nodes.rationale: Exactly one reader at a time. for-await, pipeTo, and getReader all lock; a second getReader throws TypeError.

nodes.label: ReadableStream.tee
nodes.rationale: Duplicates a stream into two branches. The faster branch buffers until the slower reads — an abandoned branch grows unbounded.

nodes.label: Web Streams
nodes.rationale: WHATWG ReadableStream, WritableStream, and TransformStream — globals in Node since v18; fetch bodies are web streams.

nodes.label: Async stream open errors
nodes.rationale: ENOENT, EACCES, EISDIR arrive as 'error' events. pipeline converts them into a rejection.

nodes.label: createReadStream / createWriteStream
nodes.rationale: Filesystem entry points into streams. Live on node:fs, not fs/promises. Constructor never throws; open happens later.

nodes.label: HTTP range requests
nodes.rationale: end is inclusive. {start:3,end:7} is five bytes, matching Range: bytes=3-7. Return 416 for out-of-range.

nodes.label: Prefer Node streams in Node
nodes.rationale: Use Node streams for pipeline, object mode, and Node APIs. Use web streams for edge/browser, fetch-only code, or CompressionStream.

nodes.label: fork IPC channel
nodes.rationale: Messages are copied JSON by default. An open channel keeps both processes alive.

nodes.label: Atomics
nodes.rationale: Non-atomic increment is read-modify-write. Four threads lost 1.8M of 8M updates in one run and zero in the next.

nodes.label: SharedArrayBuffer
nodes.rationale: The one piece of memory two threads can touch at once. Reach for it only when profiling says the copy is the problem.

nodes.label: At-least-once delivery
nodes.rationale: No queue offers exactly-once. A worker can finish and die before ack; the timeout redelivers.

nodes.label: Job queue four properties
nodes.rationale: Durable store, exclusive claim, visibility timeout, acknowledgement. Exactly-once is not on the list.

nodes.label: FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED claim
nodes.rationale: Atomic update ... where id = (select ... for update skip locked limit 1) returning. skip locked avoids serializing workers.

nodes.label: Fake queue after res.json
nodes.rationale: Work after the response has no retry, no visibility and dies on deploy.

nodes.label: Outbox relay
nodes.rationale: Mark published_at then enqueue. Crash republishes. At-least-once plus jobId outbox:${id}.

nodes.label: Identifier-only job payload
nodes.rationale: Put {orderId}, not the order. The job runs later; a copied object is stale and leaks PII into another store.

nodes.label: Postgres jobs table is the outbox
nodes.rationale: When the queue is the same database, writing the jobs row inside the transaction needs no relay.
nodes.norm_label: postgres jobs table is the outbox

nodes.label: Split queues by latency
nodes.rationale: Receipts on a fast queue, exports on a bulk one. A shared queue lets video starve password resets.

nodes.label: Audit event
nodes.rationale: Actor, closed-vocab action, target, before/after, outcome, requestId. Written next to the decision.

nodes.label: HMAC hash chain
nodes.rationale: Each record MACs a canonical body plus prev. Edit or mid-chain delete breaks verification.

nodes.label: AES-256-GCM AEAD
nodes.rationale: Confidentiality plus integrity. CBC decrypts tampered ciphertext with no error; GCM authenticates.

nodes.label: Ed25519 over RSA for new work
nodes.rationale: Faster keygen and signing, 64-byte signatures, no parameters. RSA only for interoperability or verify-heavy legacy.
nodes.norm_label: ed25519 over rsa for new work

nodes.label: GCM IV reuse
nodes.rationale: Same key and IV produce the same keystream. c1 XOR c2 XOR known plaintext recovers the other message.

nodes.label: Append-only is a storage property
nodes.rationale: Opening with 'a' does not stop the same process truncating. Enforce with chattr, object-lock or revoked DELETE.

nodes.label: External head-MAC anchor
nodes.rationale: Truncating the end leaves a shorter valid chain. Publish the head MAC somewhere the app cannot rewrite.

nodes.label: Envelope encryption
nodes.rationale: KEK wraps a per-row DEK stored with v and kid. Rotation re-wraps DEKs instead of re-encrypting data.

nodes.label: Authentication
nodes.rationale: Who you are. One chokepoint. 401 means unknown.

nodes.label: Authorization
nodes.rationale: What that identity may do. A decision at every object, not one middleware.

nodes.label: Broken object-level authorization
nodes.rationale: Logged in, no ownership check. Changing the id returns someone else's record. Put owner in the WHERE.

nodes.label: Mass assignment
nodes.rationale: Spreading req.body onto a record lets the client set isAdmin. Allowlist fields; a denylist fails open on new columns.

nodes.label: z.strictObject
nodes.rationale: Reject unknown keys on writes. z.object() strips them; looseObject keeps inherited properties.

nodes.label: 404 not 403 for foreign objects
nodes.rationale: A 403 confirms the record exists and leaks the thing you are protecting.

nodes.label: Identity in token authz from DB
nodes.rationale: JWT roles are a snapshot. A demoted admin keeps powers until expiry.
nodes.norm_label: identity in token authz from db

nodes.label: Validation is not authorization
nodes.rationale: role: z.enum(['user','admin']) is a valid escalation. Omit fields the caller may not set.

nodes.label: CSRF
nodes.rationale: The browser attaches the victim's cookie to an attacker-composed write. Authority problem, not input.

nodes.label: Origin allowlist check
nodes.rationale: Compare new URL(origin).origin. Guard Origin: null. Prefer Origin, fall back to Referer.

nodes.label: SameSite=Lax
nodes.rationale: Browser default withholds cookies from cross-site POST. Set it explicitly; Node writes no flags by default.

nodes.label: Signed double-submit CSRF token
nodes.rationale: HMAC the nonce over the session id. Plain double-submit fails if a subdomain can set the cookie.

nodes.label: Session cookie flags
nodes.rationale: HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax, Path=/, Max-Age, __Host- prefix. Node validates none of them.

nodes.label: HSTS
nodes.rationale: Browser refuses the first plaintext request. The header on HTTP is ignored. includeSubDomains and preload are commitments.

nodes.label: X-Forwarded-Proto is forgeable
nodes.rationale: Trust req.socket.encrypted when Node terminates TLS. Trust the header only if a controlled proxy overwrites it.

nodes.label: CORS does not prevent CSRF
nodes.rationale: CORS governs reading the response. A form POST still writes. Simple requests have no preflight.

nodes.label: 300-line page cap
nodes.rationale: Hard file-size cap. If the topic needs more, say so at the top and stop — do not compress by deleting code or gotchas.

nodes.label: progress.js UI bump
nodes.rationale: Bump pages after every landed page; keep pagesPlanned mid-phase. Do not wait for a green build to bump the count. yarn build once per completed phase.

nodes.label: Two-pass review
nodes.rationale: Pass 1 quality by a different model than the author. Pass 2 measures every VERIFY marker on Node 24. Self-review is worth nothing.

nodes.label: boolean-dates granularity merge
nodes.rationale: Phase 2 rows 9 and 10 were merged into 09-boolean-dates.md. Boolean three-valued logic and interval arithmetic have nothing in common; the time type has no section. Split restores the 229 topic count.

nodes.label: PostgreSQL fullstack fit 93 percent
nodes.rationale: Only 6 of 229 rows are genuine DBA territory and every one is already Know or When Needed. The gap is what is missing, not what is present.

nodes.label: Modelling money
nodes.rationale: numeric(12,2) vs bigint minor units. numeric arrives in JavaScript as a string, which is why the choice matters in Node.

nodes.label: Multi-tenancy as a decision
nodes.rationale: Shared table + tenant_id vs schema-per-tenant vs database-per-tenant. Schema-per-tenant turns every migration into N migrations at 400 tenants.

nodes.label: Transactional outbox
nodes.rationale: You cannot write to PostgreSQL and publish to a queue atomically. Insert the event in the same transaction as the business write, then a SKIP LOCKED poller drains it. Highest-value missing syllabus row.

nodes.label: EXPLAIN 186 vs count 821
nodes.rationale: Both Master, same corpus. EXPLAIN is the tool behind every performance diagnosis and got 23 percent of the space given to counting rows because Phase 10 was written before the rule was corrected.

nodes.label: MERGE RETURNING works on PostgreSQL 17+
nodes.rationale: 13-merge.md says seven times that MERGE has no RETURNING in PostgreSQL 18. RETURNING and merge_action() landed in 17 and were executed on the live 18.4 sandbox.

nodes.label: WHEN NOT MATCHED BY SOURCE
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL 17 clause that deletes target rows the source omits. The page's proxy WHEN MATCHED AND s.v IS NULL only fires for rows that are in the source.

nodes.label: Phase 0 under-explained
nodes.rationale: 12 topics, 116 lines each against a corpus median of 226. Treat as a rewrite, not a patch.

nodes.label: Phase 13 template stamps
nodes.rationale: Twelve files, 66 lines each, byte-identical in structure. They pass every structural check while containing nothing. Strip to one honest not-yet-written line.

nodes.label: Shared buffers measurement confound
nodes.rationale: 44.52 ms vs 2.64 ms includes TCP connect, SCRAM, backend fork and session startup on a never-connected Pool. Measure Buffers shared read then hit on one already-warm connection.

nodes.label: Gotchas as strongest feature
nodes.rationale: 1519 gotchas, 5.6 per page, every page has a section, symptom-first. Twelve of those are stamp boilerplate.

nodes.label: Interview star inflation
nodes.rationale: 74 percent of questions are starred. Cap at one third, defined as asked verbatim in a real interview more than once.

nodes.label: Three quality strata
nodes.rationale: Written corpus 8.8–9.7, Phase 0 3.7–5.1, stamps 0. No middle. A page is either genuinely good or unwritten.

nodes.label: Catalogue filter sort search paginate
nodes.rationale: Best single capstone candidate: six phases, the endpoint every product has.

nodes.label: Background job queue in PostgreSQL
nodes.rationale: FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED as the claim. LISTEN/NOTIFY is at-most-once and therefore an optimisation, never the transport.

nodes.label: Session and auth store scenario
nodes.rationale: Refresh-token rotation is a read-modify-write. UPDATE WHERE token_hash and revoked_at IS NULL with rowCount 0 means replay.

nodes.label: Twelve product spines
nodes.rationale: Not proposed pages. One scenario per phase group as a capstone. Nine of twelve need no new syllabus rows. Reach 13 of 14 phases.

nodes.label: Top five Fable fixes
nodes.rationale: If you only do five: correct MERGE RETURNING, remove the confounded shared-buffers benchmark, strip twelve stamps, chunk EXPLAIN, reframe client-server as a budget.

nodes.label: Fable corpus verdict
nodes.rationale: Strong. One factual error, one structural defect, twelve stamps. Written corpus is the best material in the repo; eight phases treated the 300-line cap as a content budget.

nodes.label: Connect with 127.0.0.1 never localhost
nodes.rationale: Node DNS order is verbatim by default, so localhost resolves ::1 first and every connection to a container published on IPv4 fails.

nodes.label: musl vs glibc collation
nodes.rationale: Alpine sorts en_US.utf8 by byte value; Debian applies dictionary rules. Same PostgreSQL 18.4. That is why ex6 needs both containers.

nodes.label: Syllabus review — accuracy and fullstack fit
nodes.norm_label: syllabus review — accuracy and fullstack fit

nodes.label: The 300-line cap read as a content budget
nodes.norm_label: the 300-line cap read as a content budget

nodes.label: Condensed syllabus scenarios and work order
nodes.norm_label: condensed syllabus scenarios and work order

nodes.label: Never invent a number or console output
nodes.rationale: Every figure must have been executed on the target runtime. A plausible invented number is worse than no number. Emit a <!-- VERIFY --> marker instead.
nodes.norm_label: never invent a number or console output

nodes.label: Cap treated as content budget
nodes.rationale: 269 files, max 299, zero overruns. Master topics median 530 lines where chunked, 220 where not. Clustering at 200–290 is evidence of budgeting, not of topics that happened to be that size.

nodes.label: Sandbox npm vs site yarn
nodes.rationale: Each phase folder is its own npm project so a sandbox install can never disturb the site's yarn 4 lockfile.

nodes.label: Run before you write
nodes.rationale: A number on a page that was not produced by a script here does not belong on the page. Scripts print, they do not assert.

nodes.label: Index bloat
nodes.rationale: Every UPDATE of an indexed column writes a new index entry and leaves the old one dead. Measured 8792 kB → 34 MB after six rewrites of a third of 400000 rows, row count unchanged.

nodes.label: REINDEX CONCURRENTLY
nodes.rationale: Builds a new index, swaps, drops old under SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE. Measured 34 MB → 9968 kB in 783 ms. Cannot run in a transaction; needs disk for both copies; can leave invalid _ccnew/_ccold.

nodes.label: One statement, one snapshot
nodes.rationale: Snapshot is fixed when the statement starts. A 400 ms SELECT saw pre-update values for every row even after a mid-scan commit.

nodes.label: HOT update
nodes.rationale: New version on the same page and no indexed column changed, so indexes stay untouched. fillfactor 100 → 0.1% HOT and 24 MB; fillfactor 70 → 76.6% HOT and 13 MB; index on updated column → 0% HOT.

nodes.label: MVCC
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL never overwrites a row. UPDATE writes a new version and marks the old one ending; DELETE only stamps xmax. Explains lock-free reads, table growth, and why VACUUM exists.

nodes.label: MVCC snapshot xmin:xmax:in-progress
nodes.rationale: Visible if xmin committed before the snapshot and is not in-progress, and xmax is absent or not yet committed. xmax is one past the last completed transaction.

nodes.label: At-least-once delivery
nodes.rationale: Commit the claim, then work. A crash leaves running; a reaper on started_at plus idempotent handlers. Exactly-once is not configurable.

nodes.label: Table-backed job queue
nodes.rationale: Use the table when enqueue must commit with the business write. Use a broker for tens of thousands/s, fan-out, or jobs unrelated to the database.

nodes.label: Replication slot and prepared-xact horizon pins
nodes.norm_label: replication slot and prepared-xact horizon pins

nodes.label: Idle READ COMMITTED read-only does not block VACUUM
nodes.rationale: Between statements a READ COMMITTED session holds no snapshot. All 100000 dead rows were still removed. Contradicts the common any-idle-in-transaction-stalls-cleanup advice.
nodes.norm_label: idle read committed read-only does not block vacuum

nodes.label: xmin horizon
nodes.rationale: VACUUM may only remove versions no running transaction could need. The oldest snapshot pins cleanup for every table. With a blocker, 0 of 100000 dead rows removed and the file grew 27 MB → 40 MB.

nodes.label: VACUUM
nodes.rationale: Marks dead space reusable under SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE; does not return space to the OS. Deleting half of a 46 MB table left it 46 MB after VACUUM; later inserts reused the space.

nodes.label: VACUUM FULL
nodes.rationale: Rewrites the table under ACCESS EXCLUSIVE and returns space to the OS (46 MB → 23 MB, 260 ms). Only when the table will not regrow. Never on a schedule.

nodes.label: VACUUM does not shrink indexes
nodes.rationale: Same asymmetry as heap VACUUM: dead entries become reusable inside the file so growth stops, but 34 MB stays 34 MB. Only REINDEX rebuilds the file.

nodes.label: partialDeepStrictEqual
nodes.rationale: Honest use is a response with server-generated fields. Dishonest use is hiding a shape you have not thought about.

nodes.label: Committed .snapshot file
nodes.rationale: The file is the expected value. Uncommitted, CI regenerates it and the test asserts nothing.

nodes.label: --test-update-snapshots
nodes.rationale: Blind updates rewrite the expectation and go green. Run without the flag first; a snapshot change is a code review event.

nodes.label: node:assert — strict mode and deep equality
nodes.norm_label: node:assert — strict mode and deep equality

nodes.label: At-least-once delivery
nodes.rationale: Publishing to the broker and marking published_at are two systems. Exactly-once delivery does not exist; exactly-once effect does.

nodes.label: Dual-write bug
nodes.rationale: Save-then-enqueue has no spanning transaction. Measured: orders=1 | jobs enqueued=0 when Redis was down.

nodes.label: Idempotent consumer
nodes.rationale: Unique idempotency key plus ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING; rowCount=0 means already handled.

nodes.label: LISTEN/NOTIFY as wake hint
nodes.rationale: NOTIFY is at-most-once; keep the poll as backstop. The table is the source of truth.

nodes.label: Outbox relay
nodes.rationale: A separate process claims unpublished rows and publishes them. At-least-once: can publish then crash before setting published_at.

nodes.label: FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED
nodes.rationale: Competing relays must not claim the same row. Measured 3 workers / 20 jobs: 20 unique claims, 94ms vs 189ms serialised.

nodes.label: Transactional outbox
nodes.rationale: You cannot write to a database and a queue atomically. Write the event in the same transaction as the business row, then publish separately.

nodes.label: log_statement=all leaks parameters
nodes.rationale: Parameterised queries keep values out of statement text and pg_stat_activity, not the log. DETAIL: Parameters: $1=… and log_parameter_max_length defaults to -1.

nodes.label: Oldest transaction age
nodes.rationale: Leading indicator for bloat, lock waits, pool exhaustion and replication conflicts. If you monitor one thing beyond disk, monitor that.

nodes.label: pg_stat_statements
nodes.rationale: total_exec_time beats mean_exec_time. queryid is not guaranteed stable across major versions.

nodes.label: Recovery conflict 40001
nodes.rationale: A read-only query is killed because replay needed to remove rows the query still required. Load-dependent and invisible in development.

nodes.label: Three-legged monitoring stool
nodes.rationale: pg_stat_activity (now), pg_stat_statements (aggregate), the log (which statement was slow). You need all three.

nodes.label: Column grants are additive
nodes.rationale: A column grant cannot restrict; table-wide SELECT via any inherited role makes the column list irrelevant. Use a view as the boundary.

nodes.label: SELECT alias invisible in WHERE
nodes.rationale: WHERE runs before the select list. WHERE total > 10 raises 42703; ORDER BY total works.

nodes.label: bigint and numeric as JS strings
nodes.rationale: pg returns bigint and numeric as text to preserve precision. id === 5 is false for id '5'.
nodes.norm_label: bigint and numeric as js strings

nodes.label: SELECT clause skeleton
nodes.rationale: Written order is SELECT FROM WHERE GROUP BY HAVING ORDER BY LIMIT. Evaluation order differs.

nodes.label: Join alias discipline
nodes.rationale: Alias every table and qualify every column. An unqualified unique name silently rebinds after a same-named column is added.

nodes.label: Alias replaces the table name
nodes.rationale: After FROM t AS c, t.id is 42P01. That replacement is what makes a self join possible.

nodes.label: 42702 ambiguous column
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL will not pick a side. The dangerous case is the unambiguous one that later becomes wrong.

nodes.label: SELECT * join column collapse
nodes.rationale: The server returns both id columns; pg keys objects by name and keeps the last. Six columns became four keys.

nodes.label: SELECT * is for psql
nodes.rationale: Star silently widens payloads, defeats index-only scans, and collapses duplicate join column names.

nodes.label: ROWS vs RANGE vs GROUPS
nodes.rationale: ROWS counts physical rows, GROUPS counts distinct ordering values present, RANGE with an offset counts units on the ordering scale whether present or not.

nodes.label: Window frame
nodes.rationale: A slice of the partition a window aggregate sees. Default is RANGE BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW, which merges peers. Write ROWS when you mean rows.

nodes.label: lag and lead
nodes.rationale: Return expr from a row offset rows before or after this one. Ignore the frame entirely. First row of each partition is NULL unless a default is supplied.

nodes.label: last_value default-frame trap
nodes.rationale: first_value, last_value and nth_value index the frame. The default frame ends at CURRENT ROW, so last_value famously returns the current row unless the frame is written out to UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING.

nodes.label: Planner estimate and capped count
nodes.rationale: Planner estimate is free at ~0.7% error here with no guarantee. A capped count saved 23× when matches are plentiful and nothing when they are not.

nodes.label: Exact pagination count
nodes.rationale: Twenty rows cost 2.11 ms; exact total: 125000 cost 48.83 ms. count(*) OVER () cost 152.77 ms because the window must see every row and defeats LIMIT.

nodes.label: limit + 1 Next button
nodes.rationale: Fetch page_size + 1. A leftover row means there is a next page. Exact, nearly free, and usually what a list endpoint is actually asked.

nodes.label: lag over self-join on id-1
nodes.rationale: lag() scans once and defines previous by ORDER BY. A self join on b.id = a.id - 1 breaks as soon as ids have gaps.

nodes.label: EXCLUDE CURRENT ROW GROUP TIES
nodes.rationale: EXCLUDE CURRENT ROW, GROUP, or TIES drops the current row and/or its peers from the frame.

nodes.label: GROUPS frame
nodes.rationale: GROUPS counts peer groups, not rows and not ORDER BY values.

nodes.label: RANGE offset calendar windows
nodes.rationale: RANGE BETWEEN INTERVAL '7 days' PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW is a value window, not a row count.

nodes.label: Default RANGE peer frame
nodes.rationale: The default frame is RANGE BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW, so peers share the current row's frame.

nodes.label: ROWS vs RANGE
nodes.rationale: ROWS counts physical offsets; RANGE groups by ORDER BY value so ties expand the frame.

nodes.label: Ranking ignores the frame
nodes.rationale: row_number, rank, dense_rank, and ntile use the partition and ORDER BY, not the frame clause.

nodes.label: LISTEN dedicated Client
nodes.rationale: LISTEN is session state. pool.query('LISTEN …') returns the connection with no handler; notifications are lost.

nodes.label: NOTIFY delivers on COMMIT
nodes.rationale: Zero delivered while the transaction is open, one after COMMIT, none after ROLLBACK. Notify inside the same transaction as the write.

nodes.label: LISTEN / NOTIFY
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL push to a connected client. Treat as a hint to look, never as a queue: nothing is stored.

nodes.label: LISTEN needs a bare Client
nodes.rationale: The only common case for new pg.Client(): a long-lived listener with a bound handler. Pooling buys nothing and would hand the connection away.

nodes.label: postgres.js tagged templates
nodes.rationale: ${} inside the tag is a bind parameter, never SQL text. The safe path is the default path. Result is the array itself with .count.

nodes.label: One pool per process
nodes.rationale: Two pools of max 10 are 20 connections against a shared max_connections of 100. Exceptions: replica pool, dedicated LISTEN Client, short-lived script pool.

nodes.label: NOTIFY plus poll queue table
nodes.rationale: The queue table is the truth; NOTIFY only removes latency. FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED makes several workers safe. Reconnect and re-LISTEN, then poll once.

nodes.label: pg vs postgres.js
nodes.rationale: Do not migrate an existing pg codebase for the API. Tooling expects a pg Pool. Neither driver changes schema, indexes or plans. Good default for greenfield ESM.

nodes.label: NOTIFY dedup and 8000-byte payload
nodes.rationale: Identical channel/payload pairs in one transaction fold (3 became 1). Payload over 8000 bytes is 22023. Send an id, not the data.

nodes.label: Empty values array is not parameterized
nodes.rationale: query(sql, []) still uses the simple protocol and runs multi-statement text. Safety comes from bound values, not from the argument existing.
nodes.norm_label: empty values array is not parameterized

nodes.label: Simple vs extended query protocol
nodes.rationale: No values → simple protocol, multi-statement script, array of Results. A non-empty values array → extended protocol, exactly one statement or 42601.

nodes.label: $n placeholders
nodes.rationale: Positional and 1-based. A placeholder may repeat. More values than $n references are silently ignored.

nodes.label: Identifiers cannot be parameters
nodes.rationale: ORDER BY $1 sorts by a constant string and raises no error. Column names need an allowlist.

nodes.label: pg Result object
nodes.rationale: Public fields: rows, rowCount, command, fields. oid is legacy. Underscored fields are internal.

nodes.label: rowCount vs rows.length
nodes.rationale: rowCount is rows affected; rows.length is rows sent back. UPDATE without RETURNING is 1 and []. DDL rowCount is null, not 0.

nodes.label: Type OIDs as parser keys
nodes.rationale: fields[i].dataTypeID selects the parser. Array OIDs are distinct (1700 numeric vs 1231 numeric[]). Custom types get per-database OIDs.

nodes.label: pg.types.setTypeParser
nodes.rationale: A single process-wide registry including third-party pg users. Register once before opening a pool. Never called for NULL.

nodes.label: pg TypeOverrides
nodes.rationale: Scopes a parser change to one query or one pool. The safe form when a single report needs numbers.

nodes.label: Default pg type mapping
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL sends text; pg converts by column OID. json arrives parsed, arrays as arrays, bytea as Buffer, NULL as null.

nodes.label: Generated TypeScript types from schema
nodes.rationale: A hand-written interface is a guess. Generate from the live schema so a dropped column is a type error. Commit the output and fail CI on git diff.

nodes.label: Three type-generation approaches
nodes.rationale: Introspect the live database, derive from a tool schema, or infer from queries. Query inference types the actual SELECT projection and needs a DB at build time.

nodes.label: Do not parse numeric to Number
nodes.rationale: numeric exists because floats cannot represent decimal fractions. Keep the string or store integer minor units.
nodes.norm_label: do not parse numeric to number

nodes.label: bigint and numeric arrive as strings
nodes.rationale: A JS number is exact only to 2^53-1. Number(9007199254740993) becomes 9007199254740992. numeric is for money where float rounding is unacceptable.
nodes.norm_label: bigint and numeric arrive as strings

nodes.label: pool.query<User> is an assertion
nodes.rationale: pg does not validate rows against User. A dropped or renamed column still compiles. Table-level types also let SELECT projections compile as full rows.

nodes.label: Fragment groups without a DOM node
nodes.rationale: A component returns one element; a fragment lets that element be several siblings with no extra box for CSS to match.
nodes.norm_label: fragment groups without a dom node

nodes.label: Four ways to pass content
nodes.rationale: Default slot (children); named element props; children as a function (render prop); a slot-object of per-item functions.

nodes.label: A fragment child counts as one
nodes.rationale: Children.count says 1 while markup has two elements. Layouts that branch on children.length fail when the caller wraps in a fragment.
nodes.norm_label: a fragment child counts as one

nodes.label: jsx vs jsxs decides children shape
nodes.rationale: One child is the element itself (jsx); two or more is an array (jsxs). props.children.map throws on a single child.
nodes.norm_label: jsx vs jsxs decides children shape

nodes.label: Children.toArray
nodes.rationale: Flattens nested arrays, drops null/undefined/booleans, keeps strings and numbers, rewrites keys with a path prefix (.$k1, .2:$k2).

nodes.label: Classic vs automatic JSX runtime
nodes.rationale: Classic emits React.createElement and needs React in scope, children as rest args, key in props. Automatic emits jsx/jsxs from react/jsx-runtime.

nodes.label: createElement is not deprecated
nodes.rationale: Still exported in 19.2.8 and correct without a build step. createFactory, ReactDOM.render, hydrate and unmountComponentAtNode were removed.

nodes.label: TypeScript jsx: preserve
nodes.rationale: Leave JSX for Babel/SWC/the bundler. A file compiled that way and never passed downstream ships literal JSX.

nodes.label: @jsxImportSource
nodes.rationale: Changes which package the automatic runtime is imported from — preact or a CSS-in-JS jsx factory. Compiler option preferred over per-file pragma.

nodes.label: ReferenceError: React is not defined
nodes.rationale: Signature of the classic transform without an import. A build-config problem — nested .babelrc, leftover @jsx pragma, test runner mismatch.

nodes.label: Function as children
nodes.rationale: A render prop named children. Hooks usually win; this survives when the component controls placement or values are per-item.

nodes.label: Layout with named element props
nodes.rationale: Name the region, keep primary content in children, make slots optional. Do not slice children positionally.

nodes.label: Five reasons that justify a split
nodes.rationale: Second caller; owns state nothing above needs; different update frequency; different data source; server/client boundary.
nodes.norm_label: five reasons that justify a split

nodes.label: Children helpers discouraged in new code
nodes.rationale: React docs prefer composition. Helpers remain correct when you must inspect an unknown children set.
nodes.norm_label: children helpers discouraged in new code

nodes.label: children is an ordinary prop
nodes.rationale: Nesting is syntax for setting it. Nesting wins over an explicit children attribute because JSX writes children last.

nodes.label: Hooks largely replaced function-as-children
nodes.rationale: No extra tree node, no wrapper hell, values usable anywhere, composable with other hooks.

nodes.label: Wrapper children pattern
nodes.rationale: Adds markup or behaviour around arbitrary content and does not inspect children. Cheapest performance tool: the caller's element object is unchanged.

nodes.label: Easy to Use
nodes.rationale: Default Docusaurus homepage feature art. A night climb with a summit flag and the Keytar mascot at the base frames documentation as an approachable ascent rather than a technical slog.

nodes.label: Invalid selector discards whole rule
nodes.rationale: .c, ::nonsense is not reduced to .c. One experimental selector in a list of eight silently disables the other seven.

nodes.label: @supports selector()
nodes.rationale: @supports (:has(a)) is a malformed declaration test and is always false. Selectors need selector().

nodes.label: Unforgiving selector list
nodes.rationale: Adding :popover-open to a six-selector shared rule silently unstyles all six in engines that do not know it.

nodes.label: :is()
nodes.rationale: Matches identically to :where() but contributes the specificity of its most specific argument to every match.

nodes.label: :where()
nodes.rationale: Always specificity zero. Tool for defaults meant to be overridden: resets, libraries, .prose content styles.

nodes.label: Express as middleware engine with a router
nodes.rationale: Not a language and not an application architecture. Programmable routing and middleware on top of Node's http.Server. Business rules, databases, and queues are called from handlers.
nodes.norm_label: express as middleware engine with a router

nodes.label: Fastify
nodes.rationale: Choose when schema-driven validation and throughput matter more than the widest Connect middleware ecosystem. Plugin/encapsulation model.

nodes.label: Hono
nodes.rationale: Edge / ultra-light routing, modern DX, not married to Connect middleware.

nodes.label: NestJS
nodes.rationale: Full batteries with DI and modules. Out of this bible's Express track. Can wrap Express or Fastify later.

nodes.label: Ecosystem over peak throughput
nodes.rationale: Express optimises for ecosystem and familiarity. Fastify can win raw benchmarks; you pay with a smaller middleware universe. Right default for most MERN/PERN APIs.

nodes.label: What Express is not
nodes.rationale: Not a language, ORM, or auth product. Password hashing lives in Node; Express only mounts identity middleware. Debugging hangs still needs node:http.

nodes.label: When Express is the right default
nodes.rationale: Team already knows it, largest middleware ecosystem, CRUD/JSON where clarity beats micro-benchmarks. This bible uses Express as the HTTP edge for MERN/PERN for those reasons.
nodes.norm_label: when express is the right default

nodes.label: Concept vs Express surface boundary
nodes.rationale: Concept → Node (or DB / Redis / Docker / Nginx). Middleware + route surface + HTTP contracts → Express.

nodes.label: express.Router
nodes.rationale: A portable stack of routes/middleware you mount on app or another router. Has no mountpath; inside a request the equivalent is req.baseUrl.

nodes.label: API versioning via router mounts
nodes.rationale: Mount v1 and v2 routers at /api/v1 and /api/v2. Phase 6 expands strategy.

nodes.label: mergeParams
nodes.rationale: Parent path params are not accessible from sub-routes by default. express.Router({mergeParams: true}) exposes postId inside /posts/:postId/comments.

nodes.label: Router as mini-app
nodes.rationale: Routing guide: a complete middleware and routing system. Mount at a prefix so feature modules stay small. Paths inside a router are relative to the mount.

nodes.label: req.baseUrl
nodes.rationale: URL path on which a router instance was mounted. req.path excludes the mount; req.originalUrl is full path + query.

nodes.label: sub-app mount event
nodes.rationale: A sub-app fires a mount event when attached, with the parent app passed to the callback.

nodes.label: mountpath is an app property
nodes.rationale: A Router never gets mountpath — mounted or not. Measured undefined before and after app.use. A sub-app (express()) reports /reports. Use req.baseUrl during a request.

nodes.label: Prefer shallow feature routers
nodes.rationale: Many routers keep files small. Deep nested mounts make req.baseUrl vs req.path debugging harder.

nodes.label: 404 middleware after all routes
nodes.rationale: After all routes, as normal middleware that sends 404 — not as error middleware (no err).

nodes.label: app.all
nodes.rationale: Matches all HTTP verbs, including QUERY. Convenient for CORS preflight experiments; hides method mistakes on public APIs.

nodes.label: app.get covers HEAD unless app.head registered first
nodes.rationale: Docs caveat: app.get covers HEAD if app.head was not called for the path before app.get. Body is stripped.
nodes.norm_label: app.get covers head unless app.head registered first

nodes.label: Wrong method is 404 not 405
nodes.rationale: Express has no built-in 405 or Allow header. FAQ: 404 is not an error — all middleware and routes ran and none responded. Implement 405 yourself for strict APIs.

nodes.label: Route is method + path
nodes.rationale: Register the methods you mean. Path match is not enough. Helpers: get, post, put, patch, delete, all, plus use.

nodes.label: SPA fallback last
nodes.rationale: Catch-all before API routers serves API JSON as index.html. API mounts first, static + /*splat fallback last.

nodes.label: app.route / router.route
nodes.rationale: Chain verbs on one path to reduce redundancy and typos. Organizational sugar, not required. Harder to split across files when handlers grow.

nodes.label: Request id middleware
nodes.rationale: X-Request-Id plus AsyncLocalStorage hook.

nodes.label: req field attachments
nodes.rationale: Attaching fields on req is how identity and timing flow down the chain. Typical later attachments: req.user, req.validated.

nodes.label: req.user
nodes.rationale: Authentication middleware attaches it after verifying session or token. Implicit req.user is convenient and hides dependencies.

nodes.label: req as IncomingMessage plus Express fields
nodes.rationale: Some properties exist only after middleware runs. Document what the app attaches so handlers do not assume ghosts.
nodes.norm_label: req as incomingmessage plus express fields

nodes.label: req.cookies
nodes.rationale: Needs cookie-parser and defaults to {} only once that middleware is mounted. Not built into Express.

nodes.label: cookie-parser
nodes.rationale: Not in Express built-in list. cookieParser('secret') populates req.signedCookies. Session middleware typically depends on cookie parsing.

nodes.label: Signed cookies
nodes.rationale: Detect tampering with a server secret; they are not encryption. Still visible to the client unless httpOnly and not encrypted by default.

nodes.label: Cookie read/write asymmetry
nodes.rationale: res.cookie is built in; req.cookies needs cookie-parser. Writing Set-Cookie works without the package.

nodes.label: Bare resource response
nodes.rationale: Matches pure REST textbooks and OpenAPI components cleanly; no wrapper nesting.

nodes.label: Envelope response
nodes.rationale: Envelopes extend with pagination meta without breaking clients; they add nesting noise.

nodes.label: JSON.stringify omits undefined
nodes.rationale: An envelope field set to undefined disappears from the response rather than appearing as null. Make absent-vs-null an explicit decision.

nodes.label: Response shapes
nodes.rationale: Pick envelope vs bare resource and keep it consistent. Mixing both is worse than either choice. Express has no opinion; res.json just JSON.stringifies what you hand it.

nodes.label: Stable error JSON shape
nodes.rationale: Clients parse one schema; you can add code without breaking UIs. Shape is { error: { code, message } }.

nodes.label: OpenAPI contract
nodes.rationale: The contract is part of the product. Write or generate OpenAPI 3.x for public routes. Swagger UI is optional sugar — the artifact is the spec. Even internal APIs gain onboarding, client generation, contract tests, and explicit breaking-change review.

nodes.label: Everything returns 200
nodes.rationale: Envelope-only APIs hide status. Use real statuses; body for details.

nodes.label: OpenAPI and handler drift
nodes.rationale: Drift between OpenAPI and handlers is a bug. CI should fail on breaking changes or route/doc mismatch. Use the same schemas as Zod when possible to avoid double sources of truth.

nodes.label: Static cache headers
nodes.rationale: Long maxAge for hashed filenames; short/none for HTML. Fingerprinted assets can be immutable; HTML points at changing hashes. Default weak ETags are fine for many apps.

nodes.label: Idempotency keys
nodes.rationale: Clients retry POSTs. Without an idempotency key you double-charge. Store the first response and replay it. Needed most on POST and some PATCH; GET/PUT are already idempotent when implemented correctly.

nodes.label: Idempotency payload mismatch 409
nodes.rationale: Same key, different body is a client bug or attack. Reject with 409 if payload hash mismatches stored request.

nodes.label: Replay stored idempotent response
nodes.rationale: Client sends Idempotency-Key on unsafe requests. Server stores key → response (status + body) under a TTL. Replay returns the same result without re-executing side effects.

nodes.label: ETag
nodes.rationale: Conditional requests avoid useless transfers. Express can generate weak ETags; for APIs, explicit version fields or hashes are often clearer.

nodes.label: If-Match lost-update 412
nodes.rationale: If-Match: v2 → 412 if current is v3. Detects lost updates.

nodes.label: If-None-Match 304
nodes.rationale: If-None-Match matching the current ETag yields 304 Not Modified when the client already has the current representation.

nodes.label: Cache-Control private no-store
nodes.rationale: Authenticated JSON is usually Cache-Control: private, no-store. Public catalog may use public, max-age carefully. Static hashed assets use long max-age + immutable.

nodes.label: process.env values are strings
nodes.rationale: DEBUG=false is the truthy string 'false'. Convert at the edge.

nodes.label: Isomorphic / universal code
nodes.rationale: Code written only against the shared standard surface so one module works in both hosts.

nodes.label: setTimeout return type differs
nodes.rationale: Browser returns a number; Node returns a Timeout with ref/unref/refresh.

nodes.label: node --env-file
nodes.rationale: Real environment wins; no variable expansion; missing file is a hard error unless --env-file-if-exists.

nodes.label: C++ bindings
nodes.rationale: Glue so fs.readFile in JavaScript calls read() in the OS.

nodes.label: libuv
nodes.rationale: C library for async I/O: event loop and waiting for files and sockets. The hands.

nodes.label: V8
nodes.rationale: Google's JavaScript engine: parses, compiles, garbage-collects. The brain.

nodes.label: Graceful worker shutdown
nodes.rationale: SIGTERM finished the job in 2125 ms; SIGKILL left it active with nobody working it.

nodes.label: __dirname vs process.cwd()
nodes.rationale: __dirname is where the file lives and never changes; cwd is where node was started.

nodes.label: process.exit vs exitCode
nodes.rationale: exit() abandons pending work including buffered stdout; exitCode lets the loop drain.

nodes.label: CORS is a browser policy
nodes.rationale: CORS is enforced by the browser, not HTTP. Node and curl ignore it.

nodes.label: Event loop is the program
nodes.rationale: Your file is the setup for the program. The event loop is the program.

nodes.label: Array.isArray
nodes.rationale: instanceof Array fails across realms because each iframe or vm has its own Array constructor.

nodes.label: JavaScript eight types
nodes.rationale: Seven primitives plus object. Arrays, dates, regexes, Map and class instances are objects. typeof function is a convenience, not a ninth type.

nodes.label: typeof null === object
nodes.rationale: Historic type-tag bug: objects used tag 000 and null was the all-zero pointer. A fix was rejected. Detect null with v === null.

nodes.label: null == undefined only
nodes.rationale: The one defensible == use: value == null tests null or undefined and nothing else. eqeqeq smart permits it.

nodes.label: null >= 0 is true
nodes.rationale: Relational operators ToNumber both sides; Number(null) is 0. == never numeric-compares null. A null stock silently passes >= 0.

nodes.label: Defaults fire only on undefined
nodes.rationale: f(undefined) and f() get the default; f(null) and f(0) do not. Same rule for destructuring, so API null bypasses defaults.

nodes.label: JSON.stringify drops undefined
nodes.rationale: undefined omits the field; null keeps it. In a PATCH, that is leave-alone versus set-to-empty.

nodes.label: null versus undefined
nodes.rationale: undefined is absence the engine produced; null is absence you chose. Prefer undefined by omission; use null to signal cleared in a payload.

nodes.label: No integer division
nodes.rationale: / always yields a double. trunc vs floor differ on negatives (-3 vs -4 for -7/2). Page count is Math.ceil(total/perPage).

nodes.label: Remainder % not modulo
nodes.rationale: Result takes the sign of the dividend (C). -7%3 is -1. Breaks wrap-around indices going backwards.

nodes.label: True modulo idiom
nodes.rationale: ((a%b)+b)%b is always non-negative for a positive divisor. Measured ((-7%3)+3)%3 is 2.

nodes.label: ?.() does not test callability
nodes.rationale: Guards only null/undefined. A present non-function still throws TypeError. Also does not catch undeclared variables.

nodes.label: Bitwise ToInt32 coercion
nodes.rationale: Every bitwise operator converts to 32-bit signed first. 2**31|0 is -2147483648; 2**32|0 is 0. Only 31 usable flags; 1<<31 is negative.

nodes.label: ~~ is not Math.trunc
nodes.rationale: ~~1e10 is 1410065408. Valid only below 2^31. Same for x|0, x>>0, x<<0. Use Math.trunc.

nodes.label: >> vs >>>
nodes.rationale: >> keeps the sign (-5>>1 is -3). >>> fills with zeros (-5>>>1 is 2147483645). Only unsigned 32-bit result.

nodes.label: Phase 2 — Operators, expressions and control flow
nodes.rationale: Fifteen high-frequency topics. Invisible-on-review bugs: precedence (?? with ||, right-assoc **) and ASI.
nodes.norm_label: phase 2 — operators, expressions and control flow

nodes.label: Circular ESM import TDZ
nodes.rationale: Module evaluation is depth-first. A top-level read of a not-yet-initialised import throws Cannot access before initialization. Defer the read inside an exported function. A cycle is not automatically a bug.

nodes.label: CommonJS circular require
nodes.rationale: require has no dead zone. A circular require returns a partially populated module.exports, typically undefined properties, with no error.

nodes.label: Array holes three states
nodes.rationale: Present, present holding undefined, and a hole. Reading the last two is undefined. map/forEach skip holes; spread/for...of visit them as undefined. Never create holes deliberately.

nodes.label: ?? versus ||
nodes.rationale: ?? falls back only on null/undefined; || falls back on every falsy value. Mixing ?? with || or && is a SyntaxError without parentheses.

nodes.label: undefined versus missing key
nodes.rationale: in and Object.hasOwn treat a key holding undefined as present. !== undefined, ?. and ?? cannot tell that from absence. Matters in PATCH and options objects.

nodes.label: delete on an array leaves a hole
nodes.rationale: length is unchanged. Use splice, filter or toSpliced. V8 notes array functions are considerably slower on objects with slow elements.
nodes.norm_label: delete on an array leaves a hole

nodes.label: DataCloneError
nodes.rationale: Functions and DOM nodes throw DataCloneError. Throwing at the clone is better than JSON silently dropping functions.

nodes.label: JSON.stringify seven losses
nodes.rationale: undefined/functions/symbols dropped in objects and nulled in arrays; NaN/Infinity become null; Date becomes a string; Map/Set become {}; BigInt and cycles throw; symbol keys and non-enumerable properties ignored.

nodes.label: Computed property names
nodes.rationale: Square-bracket expressions become keys, evaluated in source order while the object is built. A symbol key has no other literal form.

nodes.label: Duplicate keys last wins
nodes.rationale: After ES2015 duplicate names are legal even in strict mode because computed keys cannot be checked at parse time. A spread after an explicit key is almost always a bug. Private elements must still be unique.

nodes.label: __proto__ colon form prototype setter
nodes.rationale: Only the literal colon form sets [[Prototype]]. A non-object non-null value does nothing at all. Shorthand and computed forms create ordinary properties. Duplicate colon forms are a SyntaxError.

nodes.label: delete operator
