nodes.rationale: Removes an own property only. Does not free memory, remove variables, touch the prototype chain, or change array length. true does not mean anything was deleted.

nodes.label: V8 HiddenClass and dictionary mode
nodes.rationale: Frequent add/delete can generate HiddenClass overhead. Dictionary-mode properties are typically slower because inline caches do not work. No documented multiplier; one delete is not stated to demote.

nodes.label: Object.setPrototypeOf deoptimization
nodes.rationale: Engines optimise the chain at creation time. Changing it causes recompile for de-optimization. Set the chain at creation with { __proto__: proto } or Object.create.

nodes.label: Conditional key spread idiom
nodes.rationale: ...(cond && { k }) keeps the object one expression. Spreading a falsy non-object is a no-op. Prefer this over delete.

nodes.label: Rest destructuring instead of delete
nodes.rationale: const { password, ...safeUser } = user builds a fresh stable-shape object. If you are calling delete in a loop, you wanted a Map.

nodes.label: Call stack
nodes.rationale: LIFO execution contexts. Finite; V8 does not implement proper tail calls. An async continuation starts a fresh stack.

nodes.label: Event loop
nodes.rationale: An agent has a heap of objects, a LIFO stack of execution contexts, and a FIFO queue of jobs. The loop pulls one job, runs until the stack is empty, then pulls the next.

nodes.label: Heap
nodes.rationale: Large unstructured memory region populated as objects are created. No order.

nodes.label: Job queue
nodes.rationale: FIFO jobs from platform completions and from .then, queueMicrotask and await. Enables async while remaining single-threaded.

nodes.label: No tail-call optimisation in V8
nodes.rationale: The spec defines proper tail calls; V8 does not implement them. Deep recursion overflows regardless of how it is written.

nodes.label: Node vs browser event loops
nodes.rationale: libuv phases plus process.nextTick versus the HTML loop with rendering. Only 'microtasks before tasks' is asserted for both.

nodes.label: process.nextTick
nodes.rationale: Node-only queue drained before the promise microtask queue. setImmediate is a check-phase task.

nodes.label: Top-level await
nodes.rationale: A module that awaits at the top level delays evaluation of every module that imports it. Not available in CommonJS because require is synchronous.

nodes.label: Dynamic import()
nodes.rationale: Returns a promise for the module namespace. The module is still evaluated once no matter how many times you import it.

nodes.label: ESM import extension is required
nodes.rationale: ESM does not guess .js or /index.js. That is what makes resolution fast and cacheable.

nodes.label: Imports are hoisted and run first
nodes.norm_label: imports are hoisted and run first

nodes.label: ESM live read-only bindings
nodes.rationale: An import is a view onto the exporting module's variable, not a copy. CommonJS destructure copies the number once and never sees the update.

nodes.label: Named versus default exports
nodes.rationale: The default export is just a named export whose name happens to be default. Prefer named exports so grep and refactors work.

nodes.label: ESM top-level await
nodes.rationale: Every importer waits for it, transitively, and the module cannot be require()d from CommonJS (ERR_REQUIRE_ASYNC_MODULE).

nodes.label: cluster module vs platform replicas
nodes.rationale: cluster multiplies processes on one machine; replicas multiply machines. Prefer replicas in K8s.

nodes.label: Horizontal replicas
nodes.rationale: Need stateless handling or a shared session store; connection pools multiply with replica count.

nodes.label: node:cluster on one machine
nodes.rationale: Prefer when packing cores on a single VM without an orchestrator; not usually inside each pod.

nodes.label: Connection pool multiplication
nodes.rationale: Ten pods times pool size can knock over Postgres; right-size pools or use PgBouncer.

nodes.label: Module-scope connection reuse
nodes.rationale: Warm reuse is good; hundreds of isolates times pool size exhausts Postgres — cap pool at 1 or use a proxy.

nodes.label: Autoscale on lag and saturation
nodes.rationale: CPU-only HPA misses I/O-bound APIs that are slow but idle on CPU.

nodes.label: Poll blocking vs blocked event loop
nodes.rationale: Poll blocking is sleeping in a kernel call at ~0% CPU; a blocked loop is JS hogging the thread at 100% of one core.
nodes.norm_label: poll blocking vs blocked event loop

nodes.label: Hoisting makes undeclared dependencies work
nodes.rationale: npm flattens the tree so a transitive lodash sits in root node_modules. It breaks the day that dependency drops it.

nodes.label: node_modules walk
nodes.rationale: For a bare specifier Node looks in node_modules in the importing file's directory, then parents to the filesystem root. First match wins.

nodes.label: Corepack
nodes.rationale: Pins the package manager per project via packageManager. Ships with Node but is not enabled by default.

nodes.label: Hoisted node_modules
nodes.rationale: npm and yarn flatten transitive dependencies into top-level node_modules so duplicates collapse.

nodes.label: npm, pnpm, yarn
nodes.rationale: All three install packages. The difference that matters is the shape of node_modules and whether an undeclared dependency can accidentally work.

nodes.label: Phantom dependencies
nodes.rationale: A package your code imports without declaring it, because a hoisted transitive sat at the top level. It breaks when the real dependent drops it.

nodes.label: pnpm content-addressable store
nodes.rationale: One copy of each version on disk; node_modules is symlinks exposing only declared dependencies. Undeclared imports fail immediately.

nodes.label: Workspaces
nodes.rationale: One repo, several packages, one install, one lockfile. Siblings are symlinked. They do not give you build orchestration.

nodes.label: Timeout.unref
nodes.rationale: Removes a timer from the handles keeping the process alive without cancelling it. Use for background metrics, cache sweeps, heartbeats. process.getActiveResourcesInfo names leftover handles.

nodes.label: Process crash handler
nodes.rationale: Log first, stop accepting, drain in-flight, hard-cap with unrefed setTimeout, be idempotent. Pair with SIGTERM. Set exitCode rather than immediate process.exit so stdout drains.

nodes.label: rejectionHandled
nodes.rationale: A handler attached on a later tick fires this after Node already reported unhandled. Attach handlers at creation time.

nodes.label: uncaughtException
nodes.rationale: Synchronous throw escaped every try/catch. State afterwards is unknown, likely corrupt. Definitely not safe to continue.

nodes.label: isOperational flag
nodes.rationale: Boundary returns statusCode and code for operational errors; programmer errors shut the process down.

nodes.label: Operational vs programmer errors
nodes.rationale: Operational (timeout, 404, disk full) is expected — handle it. Programmer (TypeError, typo) is a bug — crash. Retrying TypeError loops forever; crashing on 404 is absurd.

nodes.label: Log and continue is wrong
nodes.rationale: After an uncaught exception a function stopped partway — lock, transaction, counter, half-written file. Restart into a known state.

nodes.label: Sequential independent awaits
nodes.rationale: Three independent awaits sum their latencies. Test: does this line need the previous line's value? If not, start together with Promise.all.

nodes.label: async function*
nodes.rationale: await inside, yield out. Consumer pulls one value at a time so the producer does no work in advance and only one item is in memory.

nodes.label: for await...of
nodes.rationale: Awaits each value so it can iterate sequences that arrive over time. Strictly sequential — never parallel. Use a pool for independent items.

nodes.label: Generator finally cleanup on break
nodes.rationale: break, return and throw call iterator.return(), resuming the generator at finally. That is where to close a file handle or connection.

nodes.label: Symbol.asyncIterator
nodes.rationale: for await looks for a next() that returns a promise of {value, done}. Async generators produce this protocol.

nodes.label: When sequential is right
nodes.rationale: Dependency chains, rate limits, ordered writes, and memory. Parallel is useless for CPU-bound work on one thread.

nodes.label: Pull-based backpressure
nodes.rationale: The generator suspends at yield until the consumer asks for the next value. A slow consumer automatically slows the producer.

nodes.label: Inject database handle
nodes.rationale: Caller hands a pool normally or a checked-out client inside a transaction, so one transaction can span repositories.

nodes.label: PostgreSQL client/server model
nodes.rationale: One OS process per connection — why connections are expensive enough to pool.

nodes.label: psql
nodes.rationale: The verification tool for the rest of the syllabus. Master the shell before racing ahead to SQL text.

nodes.label: Backpressure
nodes.rationale: write() returns false when the destination queue hits highWaterMark. Ignoring it moves data into an unbounded in-memory queue.

nodes.label: drain event
nodes.rationale: Fires when the queue falls below the high water mark. Use once, not on — on inside a loop leaks listeners and trips MaxListenersExceededWarning.

nodes.label: writableLength
nodes.rationale: Queued byte (or object) count. Direct measure of backpressure; legitimate disconnect threshold for a slow consumer.

nodes.label: write() returns false
nodes.rationale: Does not mean the write failed — the chunk was queued. Means stop until drain. 4000×64KB ignored: 250 MB queued vs 0 KB respected.

nodes.label: High water mark throughput curve
nodes.rationale: 4 KB is 10× slower than 64 KB on a 216 MB file; 1 MB is no faster than 256 KB. Default sits where the curve flattens.

nodes.label: highWaterMark
nodes.rationale: How much a stream buffers before backpressure. Node 24 defaults: 65536 bytes, 16 object-mode items. Raised from 16 KiB in Node 22.

nodes.label: Fan-out without per-client backpressure
nodes.rationale: One slow client queues at the full production rate and can OOM the server. Check write() per destination; drop, throttle, or disconnect laggards.

nodes.label: When to raise or lower highWaterMark
nodes.rationale: Raise for sequential bulk reads (ceiling ~256 KB). Lower for heavy objects, many concurrent sockets, or latency-sensitive SSE. Peak ≈ sum of stage marks × connections.
nodes.norm_label: when to raise or lower highwatermark

nodes.label: pipeline AbortSignal
nodes.rationale: Pass { signal } so client disconnect tears the chain down with AbortError ABORT_ERR. { end: false } keeps the destination open.

nodes.label: .pipe()
nodes.rationale: Does not forward errors or clean up. A mid-chain failure leaves handles open (EMFILE) or an unhandled error event kills the process.

nodes.label: stream.pipeline
nodes.rationale: Errors from any stage in one place; every stream destroyed on any outcome; backpressure wired between stages. Import from node:stream/promises.

nodes.label: Stream events end finish close
nodes.rationale: end is readable exhausted and only fires if consumed. finish is writable flushed after end(). close is last and the only event guaranteed after error.

nodes.label: _destroy resource cleanup
nodes.rationale: Runs exactly once on success and failure. Only correct place to release a connection or delete a temp file. pipeline calls destroy on every stream.

nodes.label: stream.finished
nodes.rationale: One promise for end, finish, error and close. Fires on every path unlike end. { cleanup: true } removes listeners; { signal } cancels.

nodes.label: Never .pipe() in a server
nodes.rationale: Every .pipe() in a request handler is a latent descriptor leak. After a Transform error, src.destroyed and dst.destroyed were both false.

nodes.label: Cleanup on close not end
nodes.rationale: destroy(err) emits error then close, never end. Cleanup in end leaks on every failure. Prefer finished() or pipeline.

nodes.label: Exponential backoff with full jitter
nodes.rationale: Math.random() * backoff spreads correlated failures. Without jitter every instance retries in a synchronised wave.

nodes.label: Visibility timeout / lockDuration
nodes.rationale: Set above p99 duration and renew. On a DB queue attempts increment at claim time, which is how a poison job is spotted.

nodes.label: Job idempotency
nodes.rationale: Every job will eventually run twice because at-least-once is the only guarantee.

nodes.label: Split queues by latency expectation
nodes.rationale: A video-encoding backlog starves receipts if they share one worker. Alert on oldest-job age, not just error rate.

nodes.label: Stalled vs failed jobs
nodes.rationale: Failed threw and counted an attempt. SIGKILL left active:1 with no error. Visibility timeout recovers stalls. attempts:1 still double-sends if the lease expires.

nodes.label: Catch up from state not the clock
nodes.rationale: where processed_at is null, not where created_at::date = today. Missed 2 a.m. is then self-healing.
nodes.norm_label: catch up from state not the clock

nodes.label: Authentication
nodes.rationale: Who you are. One chokepoint at the edge. 401 means I do not know who you are.

nodes.label: Authorization
nodes.rationale: What that identity may do. A decision at every object, always server-side. Hidden buttons and JWT role claims are not enforcement.

nodes.label: Broken object-level authorization
nodes.rationale: Authenticated, never checks the record is yours. Put the owner in the WHERE so the unscoped fetch is unreachable. Near the top of the OWASP API list.

nodes.label: Deny by default at the router
nodes.rationale: A route with no declared permission should throw at startup. A Friday endpoint with no check is the common regression; enumerate routes in a test.
nodes.norm_label: deny by default at the router

nodes.label: RBAC and ABAC
nodes.rationale: Start with ownership. RBAC when permissions are not 'is this mine' — name actions, not screens. ABAC is more expressive and harder to audit; do not start there.

nodes.label: Opaque generated storage key
nodes.rationale: User names a record; you look it up scoped to them and derive the path from a UUID you generated. Traversal then has no input.

nodes.label: Return 404 not 403 for foreign objects
nodes.rationale: A 403 confirms the record exists and leaks invoice numbering, user counts, registered emails. Reserve 403 for actions where existence is not a secret.

nodes.label: TOTP drift window
nodes.rationale: Adjacent steps produce unrelated codes. ±1 accepts a 90-second span. Wider gets sloppy; narrower generates support tickets.

nodes.label: HOTP
nodes.rationale: HMAC-SHA1 over an 8-byte counter with dynamic truncation. TOTP is HOTP of floor(unix/step).

nodes.label: Hashed MFA recovery codes
nodes.rationale: Ten single-use codes hashed like passwords. Without them, support becomes the recovery path — a social-engineering surface weaker than the password you just strengthened.

nodes.label: RFC 6238
nodes.rationale: Implementation reproduced SHA-1 and SHA-256 test vectors. HMAC-SHA1 is not weakened by SHA-1 collision attacks and is what authenticator apps implement.

nodes.label: Record accepted TOTP step
nodes.rationale: Without storing the last accepted step, TOTP is not single-use. A code observed in transit can be replayed for the rest of the step.

nodes.label: TOTP
nodes.rationale: HMAC of the current 30-second time step with a shared secret, dynamically truncated to six digits. A second factor turns a stolen password into a failed login.

nodes.label: WebAuthn / passkeys
nodes.rationale: Credential bound to origin; the browser will not sign for a lookalike. TOTP is a shared secret and can be relayed in real time. Passkeys are phishing-resistant; TOTP is the pragmatic fallback.

nodes.label: Phase 0 gate
nodes.rationale: Explain why a 3-second for loop stalls every request but a 3-second database query does not.

nodes.label: Phase 0 — The runtime model
nodes.rationale: V8 + libuv + C++ bindings + stdlib. Single-threaded execution vs multi-threaded I/O. Every Node is weird complaint traces here.

nodes.label: Phase 1 — Modules and packages
nodes.rationale: ESM, CJS, node: prefix, package.json, semver, CJS↔ESM interop, exports map. Type stripping stable as of v24.12.0 on the Node 24 LTS target.

nodes.label: Phase 2 — Async and the event loop
nodes.rationale: Loop phases, poll, microtasks vs macrotasks, nextTick starvation, combinators, AbortController, AsyncLocalStorage. Worth more than any framework.
nodes.norm_label: phase 2 — async and the event loop

nodes.label: Phase 2 gate
nodes.rationale: Hand-predict output order of nextTick, queueMicrotask, a resolved promise, setTimeout(0) and setImmediate.

nodes.label: Phase 10 — Observability and performance
nodes.rationale: Structured logging, request IDs via AsyncLocalStorage, OpenTelemetry, event loop lag, liveness vs readiness, caching, memory leaks, benchmarking.

nodes.label: Load testing
nodes.rationale: Verified 2026-08 on Node 24.19.0. Testing-phase view of what a load test is for and how it lies. Methodology lives in Phase 10 page 20.

nodes.label: Contract testing and consumer-driven contracts
nodes.rationale: Verified 2026-08 on Node 24.19.0 with zod 4.4.3. Where a green unit suite still ships a broken frontend.

nodes.label: LOGIN user vs NOLOGIN group
nodes.rationale: A user is a role with LOGIN. A group is usually a role without LOGIN used for membership. GRANT group TO login.

nodes.label: Role
nodes.rationale: The real catalog object (CREATE ROLE). User and group are both roles wearing different habits.

nodes.label: session_user vs current_user
nodes.rationale: session_user is who authenticated; current_user can change after SET ROLE. Node uses the connection-string role unless SET ROLE is used.

nodes.label: pg_hba.conf
nodes.rationale: Decides who may connect how (trust, scram-sha-256, peer) from which addresses. Missing entry yields no pg_hba.conf entry for host.

nodes.label: SQLSTATE 28P01
nodes.rationale: invalid_password / authentication failure. Measured from Node as err.code 28P01 on a wrong DATABASE_URL password.

nodes.label: \conninfo
nodes.rationale: First thing to run when something is confusing. Backend PID matches pg_stat_activity. Superuser explains works-in-psql-not-in-app.

nodes.label: Four connection failure messages
nodes.rationale: Connection refused never reached a server. database does not exist proves host/port/user/password. Wrong user and wrong password both say password authentication failed, deliberately.

nodes.label: Least-privilege app role
nodes.rationale: Container bootstrap user is a superuser — fine for local learning, wrong as the production app role. App should do DML on app tables, not drop the database or bypass RLS.

nodes.label: MySQL implicit commit on DDL
nodes.rationale: CREATE TABLE ends the transaction before the statement runs, so a later failure leaves the schema half-migrated. Why MySQL tools ship down scripts.

nodes.label: Transactional DDL
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL and SQLite can roll back CREATE TABLE. MySQL cannot. Inverts the usual the-embedded-one-is-limited assumption. Measured on PG 18.4, MySQL 8.4.11, SQLite 3.53.3.

nodes.label: CREATE DATABASE
nodes.rationale: Copies an existing database as a template (default template1). Only superusers or CREATEDB roles. App runtime roles must not. Cannot run inside a transaction.

nodes.label: template0
nodes.rationale: Pristine factory image. datallowconn is usually false. Use TEMPLATE template0 when template1 was customized.

nodes.label: template1
nodes.rationale: Default source for CREATE DATABASE. May hold encodings/extensions you want on every new DB. A dirty template1 puts unexpected objects in every new database.

nodes.label: psql exit codes
nodes.rationale: 0 success, 1 psql fatal, 2 connection lost, 3 SQL error with ON_ERROR_STOP. Code 3 never appears without the flag.

nodes.label: ON_ERROR_STOP
nodes.rationale: Default prints the error, continues, and exits 0. -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 stops and exits 3. Put on every non-interactive invocation.

nodes.label: --single-transaction
nodes.rationale: Wraps the whole file so a failing later statement rolls back earlier ones. Measured 0 leftover rows. Cannot wrap CREATE DATABASE, VACUUM, CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY, ALTER SYSTEM. Holds every lock until the end.

nodes.label: Function around the column
nodes.rationale: lower(email) is a different value from email; measured 0.139 ms to 105 ms, 755× slower.

nodes.label: Partial index
nodes.rationale: Indexes only matching rows: 8792 kB full versus 104 kB partial for 4000 live rows of 400000. The planner uses it only when it can prove implication.

nodes.label: Expression index
nodes.rationale: A second physical copy of a derived value that only serves the exact expression it stores. lower(email) went from 97.2 ms to 0.083 ms.

nodes.label: Expression-index statistics
nodes.rationale: ANALYZE gathers stats for the expression under the index name; creating one purely to give the planner statistics is a legitimate move.

nodes.label: Partial-index predicate implication
nodes.rationale: Write the query predicate as a literal matching the index; a generic plan planned without $1 may not prove implication.

nodes.label: IMMUTABLE index expressions
nodes.rationale: timestamptz::date depends on session TimeZone so it is STABLE and raises 42P17. Name the zone: date_trunc('day', created_at, 'UTC').

nodes.label: Partial UNIQUE index
nodes.rationale: The one thing a table constraint cannot express: uniqueness among live rows. Violations still raise 23505.

nodes.label: CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY
nodes.rationale: Avoids the ShareLock that blocks writers; costs two table passes plus a wait for every pre-existing transaction, including idle-in-transaction elsewhere.

nodes.label: indisvalid
nodes.rationale: A failed CONCURRENTLY leaves an index with indisvalid=false: unusable by queries but still maintained by writes. There is no resume.

nodes.label: CREATE INDEX ShareLock
nodes.rationale: Conflicts with RowExclusiveLock; reads continue, writes queue. On a minutes-long build that is an outage.

nodes.label: SQLSTATE 25001
nodes.rationale: CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY cannot run inside a transaction block; mark the migration non-transactional.

nodes.label: pg error object mapping
nodes.rationale: SQLSTATE is err.code, CONSTRAINT NAME is err.constraint; two unique constraints both raise 23505 and only the constraint name distinguishes them.

nodes.label: SQLSTATE
nodes.rationale: Five-character standard code, stable across versions and locales; the only safe thing to branch on.

nodes.label: SQLSTATE classes 23 and 40
nodes.rationale: Class 23 maps to user-facing validation; class 40 means retry. Class 42 is a SQL bug and should never be caught.

nodes.label: createRoot
nodes.rationale: The only client entry in React 19. From react-dom/client. Two methods: render and unmount.

nodes.label: createRoot error options
nodes.rationale: onUncaughtError, onCaughtError, onRecoverableError — the hook for reporting a whole tree.

nodes.label: hydrateRoot
nodes.rationale: Expects server-rendered HTML and attaches handlers. Argument order is container first, opposite of render.

nodes.label: Unmounted root cannot be reused
nodes.rationale: unmount() runs cleanups and empties the container. Further render throws Cannot update an unmounted root.

nodes.label: Commit phase
nodes.rationale: Applies DOM operations, then refs, layout effects, passive effects. Cannot be thrown away.

nodes.label: Render phase
nodes.rationale: React calls component functions to get elements. Repeatable and discardable. DOM still shows previous UI.

nodes.label: useEffect after paint
nodes.rationale: Default place for fetching, subscriptions, logging, timers.

nodes.label: useLayoutEffect before paint
nodes.rationale: Measure or mutate DOM before the user sees the frame. Blocks painting.

nodes.label: StrictMode double-mount
nodes.rationale: setup → cleanup → setup asserts cleanup fully undoes setup. Measured: 2 renders, 2 setups, 1 cleanup in dev.

nodes.label: StrictMode
nodes.rationale: Development-only detector. Doubles components, lazy initialisers, and initial effect mount. No production cost.

nodes.label: useLayoutEffect
nodes.rationale: After DOM mutation, before paint — and it blocks painting.

nodes.label: One root per container
nodes.rationale: Second createRoot warns; two roots then throw NotFoundError: Node.removeChild on unmount. Cache the root for HMR.

nodes.label: Children commit before parents
nodes.rationale: Refs and layout effects run bottom-up so a parent can assume children's DOM exists.

nodes.label: Render must be pure
nodes.rationale: React may call it more than once and throw the result away. Observable work in the body happens an uncontrolled number of times.

nodes.label: root.render() schedules work
nodes.rationale: DOM is still null on the line immediately after the call.

nodes.label: didInit ref is the wrong fix
nodes.rationale: Silences the symptom; the effect still cannot re-run. Breaks on Back, Fast Refresh, or Activity.
nodes.norm_label: didinit ref is the wrong fix

nodes.label: Cleanup contract
nodes.rationale: setup → cleanup → setup must be indistinguishable from setup alone. Cleanup runs with old values, tied to deps not lifetime.

nodes.label: READ COMMITTED
nodes.rationale: A fresh snapshot per statement. Allows non-repeatable reads and phantoms; never dirty reads. No 40001, so no retry loop — silent wrong data instead of errors.

nodes.label: UPDATE re-evaluates WHERE after wait
nodes.rationale: After a row-lock wait the UPDATE re-reads the newest committed version. Put the condition in WHERE and trust rowCount.

nodes.label: Lost update
nodes.rationale: Read-modify-write under READ COMMITTED: last writer wins with a stale value. 20 concurrent increments produced qty=2. No error, no deadlock.

nodes.label: SELECT FOR UPDATE then UPDATE
nodes.rationale: Serialises the read-modify-write so application logic can live in JS. 58.0 ms. Lock held until COMMIT.

nodes.label: SQL arithmetic UPDATE
nodes.rationale: SET qty = qty + 1 is atomic in one statement. Fastest of the four (37.9 ms, 20/20). Limited to values expressible in SQL.

nodes.label: jsonb -> vs ->>
nodes.rationale: -> returns jsonb and chains; ->> returns text and terminates. One character decides type.

nodes.label: Missing key vs JSON null
nodes.rationale: ->> returns SQL NULL for both a missing key and JSON null; use ? or jsonb_typeof to tell them apart.

nodes.label: jsonb containment @>
nodes.rationale: Asks whether the document contains a fragment; GIN can serve it. ->> equality cannot.

nodes.label: jsonpath @? and @@
nodes.rationale: Comparisons and wildcards that @> cannot express; GIN can serve both opclasses.

nodes.label: jsonb expression index
nodes.rationale: Index (doc->>'tag') for a hot key: 0.9 ms and 1352 kB. Expression must match the query exactly, including casts.

nodes.label: GIN jsonb_ops
nodes.rationale: Default GIN: indexes keys and values separately. Serves @> and ?; 17 MB here; cannot serve ->>.

nodes.label: GIN jsonb_path_ops
nodes.rationale: One hash per path-plus-value. Smaller/faster for @> (1.1 ms, 13 MB) but cannot serve ?.

nodes.label: jsonb accessor vs predicate families
nodes.rationale: Accessors dig a value out; predicates ask a question. The family you pick decides whether an index can help.

nodes.label: tsvector lexemes
nodes.rationale: Sorted set of lexemes with positions. english stems and drops stop words; simple does neither.

nodes.label: websearch_to_tsquery
nodes.rationale: Search-engine syntax; never raises. to_tsquery parses tsquery language and raises 42601 on ordinary user text.

nodes.label: Generated tsvector column
nodes.rationale: Same speed as an expression index (~17 ms). Chosen to merge columns, carry setweight, and keep queries as tsv @@ q.

nodes.label: to_tsvector IMMUTABLE config
nodes.rationale: One-arg to_tsvector(body) is rejected in an index (42P17) because it reads a session GUC. Name the config.

nodes.label: ts_headline after LIMIT
nodes.rationale: Re-tokenises original text and cannot use the index. Apply after LIMIT so it runs for the page, not every match.

nodes.label: gin_trgm_ops vs gist_trgm_ops
nodes.rationale: GIN for ILIKE/%/<%; GiST required for ORDER BY <-> nearest neighbour. GIN 9 MB vs GiST 22 MB here.

nodes.label: pg_trgm % vs <%
nodes.rationale: % compares whole strings (0.273 on a long title). <% / word_similarity scores the best substring (1.000).

nodes.label: FTS and trigram are complements
nodes.rationale: FTS stems grammar but misses typos; trigram finds typos but cannot stem. Production: FTS first, trigram fallback.

nodes.label: The Node side, observing, and alternatives
nodes.norm_label: the node side, observing, and alternatives

nodes.label: temp_bytes spill signal
nodes.rationale: Sorts or hashes exceeded work_mem. Gather this trend before raising work_mem.

nodes.label: hash_mem_multiplier
nodes.rationale: Default 2.0: hash nodes may use work_mem × multiplier. Hashes degrade worse on spill than sorts.

nodes.label: work_mem per sort or hash operation
nodes.rationale: Worst case ≈ work_mem × operations × concurrent queries. Raising globally is the classic OOM path. SET LOCAL or ALTER ROLE, never plain SET on a pool.
nodes.norm_label: work_mem per sort or hash operation

nodes.label: log_temp_files
nodes.rationale: Default -1. Set 0 to log every spill past work_mem, naming the statement behind rising temp_bytes.

nodes.label: set_config is_local for parameterized identity
nodes.rationale: SET LOCAL name = $1 is 42601. set_config(name, value, true) accepts parameters. current_setting(name, true) returns NULL if unset.

nodes.label: SET LOCAL for RLS identity
nodes.rationale: Plain SET persists on a pooled backend into the next tenant's request — measured ex54. This is a cross-tenant leak, not a style issue.

nodes.label: current_setting is STABLE
nodes.rationale: May be evaluated once per statement. Helper functions must be STABLE, not IMMUTABLE (wrong cache) or VOLATILE (per-row).

nodes.label: max_connections forces work_mem down
nodes.rationale: Each backend can allocate work_mem several times. Higher max_connections lowers the safe work_mem. Strongest argument for a pooler.

nodes.label: lock_timeout
nodes.rationale: Default 0 (wait forever). Essential for safe DDL. User context; set per role so migrations are not killed by web limits.

nodes.label: statement_timeout
nodes.rationale: Bounds a single statement. Default 0. Set per role, not globally. Not a substitute for lock_timeout.

nodes.label: log_lock_waits
nodes.rationale: Default off. Logs waits longer than deadlock_timeout. Best diagnostic for a freeze that then recovered — invisible to pg_stat_activity afterwards.

nodes.label: ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock queue
nodes.rationale: Default ALTER TABLE lock conflicts with every mode including SELECT's ACCESS SHARE. Blast radius is the longest transaction on the table, not DDL duration.

nodes.label: lock_timeout plus retry on 55P03
nodes.rationale: SET LOCAL lock_timeout, retry lock_not_available with backoff. statement_timeout does not reliably bound lock wait. Cancel the blocker, not the migration.

nodes.label: Invalid indexes after CONCURRENTLY failure
nodes.rationale: indisvalid=false: ignored for queries, still maintained on every write. Drop and retry or REINDEX INDEX CONCURRENTLY. Check post-migration.

nodes.label: Zero-downtime migration checklist
nodes.rationale: lock_timeout, no ACCESS EXCLUSIVE scans, NOT VALID constraints, CONCURRENTLY indexes, batched backfills, both-code compatibility, rollback without restore.

nodes.label: Waiting ACCESS EXCLUSIVE blocks the queue
nodes.rationale: New queries do not jump the queue. A DDL blocked by one slow reader makes the table unavailable before it has run. lock_timeout is not optional.
nodes.norm_label: waiting access exclusive blocks the queue

nodes.label: GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY
nodes.rationale: Standard SQL preferred over serial/bigserial, which expand to column plus sequence plus default. ALWAYS prevents explicit inserts from desynchronising the sequence.

nodes.label: B-tree locality for sequential keys
nodes.rationale: Sequential keys append to the rightmost leaf, stay in cache, and fill completely. Random keys split pages half-empty and make the working set the entire index.

nodes.label: uuid v4 versus uuid v7
nodes.rationale: 200k inserts: bigint 947 ms / 4408 kB index; v4 1727 ms / 8552 kB; v7 1356 ms / 6184 kB. Random keys scatter B-tree writes. uuidv7 first 48 bits are a millisecond timestamp.

nodes.label: uuidv7() built-in
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL 18 built-in, no extension. uuid_extract_timestamp recovers creation time — a free created_at and a leak of when the row was created. Use v4 for public ids when timing is sensitive.

nodes.label: Cast the literal, never the column
nodes.rationale: acct = '12345' index-only 0.199 ms vs acct::bigint = 12345 seq scan 47.9 ms (241×). created::date = current_date 65.4 ms vs a range on the bare column 1.2 ms. The index stores the column, not the cast.
nodes.norm_label: cast the literal, never the column

nodes.label: PostgreSQL 42883 type mismatch
nodes.rationale: No text = integer operator. Treat 42883 as a type-mismatch bug, not an inconvenience to cast away. pg sends untyped text so a JS number against a text column still uses the index; hand-written :: on the column is the danger.

nodes.label: bigint for surrogate primary keys
nodes.rationale: Measured 17 MB vs 21 MB and same PK index on 500k two-column rows. Exhausting an int sequence is 2200H and a full ACCESS EXCLUSIVE rewrite. Foreign keys must match referenced width or a cast kills the index.

nodes.label: Never store a UUID as text
nodes.rationale: 16 bytes as uuid, 40 as text, plus string comparison and no format validation. Common middle path: bigint PK for joins, uuid unique column for public ids.
nodes.norm_label: never store a uuid as text

nodes.label: numeric rounds half away from zero
nodes.rationale: 2.5::numeric(2,0) is 3. Float-to-int uses half-to-even (2.5 → 2). numeric NaN compares equal to itself so it can be sorted and indexed.
nodes.norm_label: numeric rounds half away from zero

nodes.label: char(n) padding semantics
nodes.rationale: Comparison ignores trailing spaces; concatenation after implicit text cast does not. Acceptable only for genuinely fixed-width codes.

nodes.label: text vs varchar vs char
nodes.rationale: Same implementation for text and varchar. Measured identical 13 MB and ~26 ms on 300k rows. char(50) pads: 51 bytes vs 4 for the same three characters, 24 MB vs 13 MB.

nodes.label: varchar cast truncates silently
nodes.rationale: INSERT into varchar(50) raises 22001. Explicit ::varchar(50) truncates with no warning. A CHECK cannot be cast away.

nodes.label: Implicit, assignment, and explicit casts
nodes.rationale: Implicit only where lossless (int + numeric). Assignment on store. Explicit ::, CAST, and type-named functions are equivalent. '42.7'::int is 22P02; 42.7::int rounds to 43. Invalid dates are 22008.

nodes.label: Largest-remainder allocation
nodes.rationale: 100/3 → 33.33×3 = 99.99. No rounding rule fixes indivisibility. Floor each share in minor units, then give leftover units to the largest remainders (33.34, 33.33, 33.33). Assert parts sum to the whole.

nodes.label: Round once at the charging boundary
nodes.rationale: Rounding at each step discards fractions that compound. Carry full precision through; store both inputs and the rounded charge so a historical invoice can be reproduced and explained. Implement jurisdiction-specific rules explicitly.
nodes.norm_label: round once at the charging boundary

nodes.label: Use text by default
nodes.rationale: varchar(n) bakes a guessed number into physical structure. Widening is 2.4 ms metadata; narrowing rewrites under ACCESS EXCLUSIVE (305 ms / 200k rows). Prefer text plus CHECK (length(col) <= n).

nodes.label: GIN index on jsonb
nodes.rationale: 200k rows: jsonb ->> 33.6 ms vs json 98.7 ms unindexed; @> with GIN 9.4 ms. json cannot be GIN-indexed (42704). ->> equality does not use default GIN; use @> or a B-tree expression index.

nodes.label: jsonb vs json
nodes.rationale: json stores exact text. jsonb parses to binary: keys sorted, last duplicate wins, whitespace dropped. json has no equality operator (42883). jsonb was larger on a small object (112 vs 56 bytes).

nodes.label: GIN @> not ANY for array membership
nodes.rationale: 200k rows: @> 73.2 ms seq scan → 4.8 ms with GIN. 't42' = ANY(tags) is not GIN-indexable (41.8 ms parallel seq scan). Write tags @> ARRAY['t42']. Scalar id = ANY($1) is a different, indexable IN-list idiom.
nodes.norm_label: gin @> not any for array membership

nodes.label: PostgreSQL arrays
nodes.rationale: Any type can be an array. 1-based; out-of-range subscript is NULL, not an error. Prefer cardinality() (0 for empty) over array_length() (NULL for empty). pg maps JS arrays natively.

nodes.label: Composite type
nodes.rationale: A row shape used as a column. No per-field constraints, FKs, or cheap indexes. ADD ATTRIBUTE rewrites every using table. pg returns the raw literal ("1 High St",London,"E1 6AN"). Appropriate as a function return type; every table has an implicit composite.

nodes.label: Promote queried jsonb keys to columns
nodes.rationale: A jsonb key has no CHECK, FK, statistics, or cheap B-tree. Use jsonb for schemaless payloads; promote keys you filter or join. A generated column is the migration-free middle step. Pass objects to pg; JSON.stringify double-encodes.
nodes.norm_label: promote queried jsonb keys to columns

nodes.label: Array versus child table
nodes.rationale: No FK from array elements (42804). No per-element constraints or extra columns. Any element change rewrites the whole MVCC row. Arrays for values that travel with the row; child tables for entities.

nodes.label: Avoid composites for storage
nodes.rationale: Use prefixed columns with real constraints, a child table for one-to-many, or jsonb if the shape is unknown. Unpack with (addr).city or to_jsonb(addr).

nodes.label: CHECK constraint
nodes.rationale: Rejects only when the expression is false. SQLSTATE 23514. Pair with NOT NULL or write CHECK (col IS NULL OR …).

nodes.label: CHECK passes on NULL
nodes.rationale: NULL >= 18 is unknown, not false. Measured: CHECK (age >= 18) accepted a NULL age.

nodes.label: NOT NULL
nodes.rationale: Column property, not DEFERRABLE. Default to NOT NULL. WHERE status != 'archived' silently excludes NULL rows.

nodes.label: NULLS NOT DISTINCT
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL 15+. Treats NULLs as equal so only one is allowed (23505). Works on constraint and index forms.

nodes.label: UNIQUE accepts unlimited NULLs
nodes.rationale: Two NULLs are not equal under three-valued logic. Measured: three NULLs inserted into a unique column.

nodes.label: text plus CHECK not varchar or enum
nodes.rationale: text and varchar(n) have identical performance; narrowing varchar rewrites (433 ms / 200k). Enums cannot drop or reorder values.
nodes.norm_label: text plus check not varchar or enum

nodes.label: Application cannot enforce referential integrity
nodes.rationale: Between findParent and insertChild another transaction can delete the parent. Only the database evaluates the constraint as part of the write.

nodes.label: Application validation vs constraints
nodes.rationale: Application validation is UX and can collect all errors. Constraints are correctness. 20 concurrent check-then-insert workers produced 20 duplicates and zero errors.

nodes.label: req.ip and req.ips
nodes.rationale: Derived from the left-most X-Forwarded-For entry whenever trust proxy is not false; otherwise ips is an empty array. Wrong behind a proxy until trust proxy is set.

nodes.label: req.originalUrl
nodes.rationale: Full original path including mount and query — useful behind routers.

nodes.label: qs vs simple docs contradiction
nodes.rationale: req.query reference still says the parser by default uses qs — stale Express 4 text. Settings table and migration guide agree on simple.

nodes.label: query parser simple
nodes.rationale: Express 5 default. Node querystring: repeated keys become arrays and bracket syntax is never interpreted. Safer default; breaks old nested-query clients.

nodes.label: express.text
nodes.rationale: Parses into a string. Default type text/plain. Still set limits.

nodes.label: req.accepts, req.is, req.get, req.range
nodes.rationale: req.is returns the matching content type or false. req.accepts returns the best Accept match or false. req.get is case-insensitive with Referrer/Referer interchangeable.

nodes.label: Phase 3 — Requests and body parsing
nodes.rationale: Target Express 5.2.1 on Node 24.19.0. Everything clients send — and the limits that keep one request from taking the process down.

nodes.label: Nested Loop Hash Join Merge Join
nodes.rationale: Equijoin unlocks all three. Non-equality leaves only nested loop. Planner picks by cost from statistics and indexes.
nodes.norm_label: nested loop hash join merge join

nodes.label: NOT NULL FK makes child-to-parent count knowable
nodes.rationale: Child JOIN parent via NOT NULL FK yields one row per child. Parent JOIN child drops parents with no children.
nodes.norm_label: not null fk makes child-to-parent count knowable

nodes.label: EXCLUDE USING gist no-overlap
nodes.rationale: Overlapping validity periods become a silent fan-out on only the affected SKUs.

nodes.label: Expression index pays only when selective
nodes.rationale: 200k×200k lower() join 211.5 then 212.6 ms — no change. Same index 59× faster with a 50-row driving side (65.2 → 1.1 ms).
nodes.norm_label: expression index pays only when selective

nodes.label: Non-equality ON leaves nested loop only
nodes.norm_label: non-equality on leaves nested loop only

nodes.label: Range join with tstzrange @>
nodes.rationale: Price at time of sale. Default [) makes the 2026-06-01 changeover unambiguous. Index the range with GiST.

nodes.label: GROUP BY omits missing combinations
nodes.rationale: No (IN, paid) row showing 0. A grid UI goes ragged. Manufacture the spine with a cross join of the dimensions and LEFT JOIN the aggregate.

nodes.label: EXISTS instead of HAVING count > 0
nodes.rationale: count(…)>0 forces a full count of every group. EXISTS stops at the first match and can use an index. Does not apply when the threshold is genuinely >1.

nodes.label: FILTER pivot
nodes.rationale: GROUP BY dimension with one FILTER count per category. Counts come back 0 for empty cells; sums come back NULL and need coalesce. Columns are fixed at query-writing time.

nodes.label: FILTER (WHERE …)
nodes.rationale: Goes after the aggregate's closing parenthesis and before OVER. Takes a full WHERE-style predicate. MySQL and SQL Server do not have it.

nodes.label: 42809 FILTER on a non-aggregate
nodes.rationale: wrong_object_type. Also what you get from a misspelled aggregate name rather than 'does not exist'.

nodes.label: FILTER is not a scan filter
nodes.rationale: No index can serve a FILTER predicate. One aggregate should use WHERE. FILTER pays from the second aggregate onwards.
nodes.norm_label: filter is not a scan filter

nodes.label: FILTER on aggregate window functions
nodes.rationale: Clause order is aggregate(...) FILTER (WHERE …) OVER (…). row_number/rank/lag are not aggregates and reject FILTER.

nodes.label: FILTER vs GROUP BY shape
nodes.rationale: Neither is faster (65 vs 72 ms). FILTER: one row, N columns, zeros for absent categories, frozen set. GROUP BY: N rows, omits empty categories, discovers new ones.

nodes.label: 42P20 windowing_error
nodes.rationale: WHERE or HAVING on a window is circular: WHERE decides which rows exist and the window value depends on those rows. Compute the window in a subquery or CTE and filter outside.

nodes.label: Named WINDOW clause
nodes.rationale: Naming convenience between HAVING and ORDER BY. Planner already merges identical definitions. Can extend with ORDER BY and a frame; cannot change PARTITION BY or override an existing ORDER BY.

nodes.label: Index matching PARTITION BY then ORDER BY
nodes.rationale: (user_id, amount DESC) turned 530 ms external merge into 283 ms index-only scan, 3783 → 575 buffers. Incremental Sort appears when the index supplies only a prefix.
nodes.norm_label: index matching partition by then order by

nodes.label: WindowAgg is not parallel-aware
nodes.rationale: No Gather in the plan. Extra cores do not help. Reduce input, share partitions, or provide an ordered index.

nodes.label: Run Condition
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL 15+ pushes outer WHERE rn <= N into WindowAgg for monotonic functions (row_number, rank, dense_rank, count). Emitted 15000 instead of 500000; the Sort still processes all rows.

nodes.label: What windows cost
nodes.rationale: Every window needs input sorted by PARTITION BY then ORDER BY. One window over 500000 rows took 530 ms; two sharing a sort 999 ms; two that cannot 1518 ms.

nodes.label: Compatible windows share one sort
nodes.rationale: If one partition/order spec is a prefix of the other, one Sort serves both WindowAgg nodes. Different partitions re-sort the whole intermediate (temp blocks 1070 → 3671).

nodes.label: Non-covering window index made top-N slower
nodes.rationale: Index Scan (not Index Only Scan) because id was not in the index: 434.74 ms / 3783 buffers → 533.67 ms / 500574 buffers. INCLUDE selected columns, or keep the sequential scan. Compare Buffers, not just milliseconds.
nodes.norm_label: non-covering window index made top-n slower

nodes.label: Omit WHERE when there are no filters
nodes.rationale: Emit the keyword only if where.length > 0. WHERE 1=1 works but leaves a permanently true predicate in every plan and log.
nodes.norm_label: omit where when there are no filters

nodes.label: One-pass WHERE fragment builder
nodes.rationale: Push value then fragment in one loop. Numbering follows push order, not request order. Test numeric/boolean filters with != null so 0 is not dropped.

nodes.label: Placeholder from params.length
nodes.rationale: $n is 1-based; params.length after the push is the number. A separate i++ drifts when a branch increments without pushing.

nodes.label: listItems composes WHERE sort LIMIT
nodes.rationale: buildList supplies WHERE params; orderClause is vetted literal text; limit/offset are pushed last so numbering stays intact.

nodes.label: Direction is a ternary never interpolated
nodes.rationale: dir === 'desc' ? 'DESC' : 'ASC' yields one of two literals. Interpolating ${dir} after a looks-like-direction check is the same class of bug.
nodes.norm_label: direction is a ternary never interpolated

nodes.label: orderClause
nodes.rationale: Looks up SORTABLE[sortKey], ternaries direction, appends id ASC as a stable tiebreaker so pagination does not duplicate or drop rows.

nodes.label: ORDER BY must be total
nodes.rationale: created_at alone tied 100 rows per timestamp. Without unique id, the same row can appear on two pages. WHERE must use the same columns in the same order.

nodes.label: Hand-built predicates versus a query builder
nodes.rationale: Explicit SQL is pasteable into EXPLAIN. A builder removes boilerplate; every knex.raw/sql.raw reopens the hole this page closes.
nodes.norm_label: hand-built predicates versus a query builder

nodes.label: Partial unique index for live emails
nodes.rationale: A full unique index blocks re-registration with 23505. CREATE UNIQUE INDEX ... WHERE deleted_at IS NULL. The partial index is unusable if the query omits that predicate.
nodes.norm_label: partial unique index for live emails

nodes.label: Soft delete as UPDATE
nodes.rationale: SET deleted_at = now() WHERE deleted_at IS NULL. Foreign keys do not cascade. Every query must filter forever.

nodes.label: ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING RETURNING trap
nodes.rationale: Conflict path writes nothing so RETURNING is empty. Retry cannot answer with the resource.
nodes.norm_label: on conflict do nothing returning trap

nodes.label: DO UPDATE RETURNING xmax
nodes.rationale: SET key = EXCLUDED.key makes RETURNING fire. (xmax = 0) AS was_inserted distinguishes 201 from 200.

nodes.label: Idempotency-Key unique constraint
nodes.rationale: The unique index is correctness. Ten racing inserts without ON CONFLICT produced 1 row and 9 23505s. Key must come from the client.

nodes.label: Idempotency-key response table
nodes.rationale: Store status, response jsonb, request_hash. In-flight is 409. Hash mismatch is 422. Scope PRIMARY KEY (user_id, key).

nodes.label: Soft delete is not an audit log
nodes.rationale: It records that a row is currently deleted, not who or previous values. Later UPDATE overwrites in place.
nodes.norm_label: soft delete is not an audit log

nodes.label: Naturally idempotent operations
nodes.rationale: PUT, DELETE, absolute SET are idempotent. Relative SET balance = balance + 10 and POST that creates a resource are not.

nodes.label: 228 topics in 14 phases
nodes.rationale: 60 Master (26%), 124 Understand, 35 Know, 9 When Needed. Master-only path: schema, every CRUD query, drive from Node, read EXPLAIN.

nodes.label: False Verified stamps on 210 pages
nodes.rationale: 210 pages claim Verified 2026-08 on PostgreSQL 18.4 attached to code that cannot have produced the topic. Strip 210→12 before any rewrite.

nodes.label: Five stamped page variants
nodes.rationale: psql/ops 83, SQL 49, Node 48, DDL 19, Types 16 — identified by Why it matters. Five shared code blocks; 168 pages share the same two gotchas.

nodes.label: 216 of 228 pages are template stamps
nodes.rationale: 94.7% carry Hold the model in your head before memorizing syntax. How it works and the first interview answer reprint the one-liner. Average 77 lines versus Node 198–267.

nodes.label: Twelve genuinely hand-written pages
nodes.rationale: Phase 0 architecture pages plus phase-10-indexes/18-fk-indexes.md. 05-wal.md is the model. vs-other-databases was a stamp then rewritten 2026-08-13.

nodes.label: Proposed PostgreSQL syllabus (2026-08-11)
nodes.rationale: Row-level inventory for review, excluded from the build until approved. Target PostgreSQL 18.4 from Node 24 with pg. No explanation pages until approval.

nodes.label: Every page carries SQL and Node pg
nodes.rationale: Runnable SQL, the pg call with $1 placeholders, actual output, and the Node-side failure (SQLSTATE, error.code, constraint). A psql-only page is incomplete.
nodes.norm_label: every page carries sql and node pg

nodes.label: Rewrite against the Node corpus standard
nodes.rationale: Keep syllabus and phase indexes. Sequence Phase 8 → 9 → 3 → 4. Do not review stamps one at a time. progress.js must stop counting stamps as finished.
nodes.norm_label: rewrite against the node corpus standard

nodes.label: Function-as-children
nodes.rationale: Same inversion as a render prop with children as the function, which JSX can nest inside the element.

nodes.label: Children namespace
nodes.rationale: Traverses the opaque children structure. Fragments are not traversed; arrays are flattened; elements are not rendered.

nodes.label: children is source structure not rendered output
nodes.rationale: There is no way to see what an inner component will render. One wrapper component is one child.
nodes.norm_label: children is source structure not rendered output

nodes.label: Children.toArray key rewriting
nodes.rationale: Drops empty nodes and prefixes keys with nesting and position so flattening cannot collide keys from different branches.

nodes.label: Slots, children and the context hole
nodes.norm_label: slots, children and the context hole

nodes.label: Slots pattern
nodes.rationale: Named element props for fixed regions. Community name, not a React API. Do not slice children by index.

nodes.label: Render prop
nodes.rationale: A function prop a component calls to decide what to render. The owner keeps state and behaviour; the caller keeps markup. The prop need not be named render — children is the same pattern.

nodes.label: When render props still win
nodes.rationale: Hooks cannot render. Render props remain right when the component controls placement, values are per-item, or rendering must run inside a boundary it owns.

nodes.label: Four things that stop render descent
nodes.norm_label: four things that stop render descent

nodes.label: cleanup(old) then setup(new)
nodes.rationale: Cleanup closes over the render that created it, so it disconnects the old room. At unmount it runs one final time.

nodes.label: Idempotent setup needs no cleanup
nodes.rationale: map.setZoomLevel(12) twice leaves the map at 12. Setters are usually idempotent; anything that opens, pushes or begins usually is not.

nodes.label: Move 1 — static object outside the component
nodes.rationale: If it involves no props or state it is not reactive. Module scope makes [] genuinely correct.
nodes.norm_label: move 1 — static object outside the component

nodes.label: All cleanups then all setups
nodes.rationale: When any setup runs, everything being torn down in that pass is already gone, including other components. Exclusive resources can transfer safely.

nodes.label: useInsertionEffect interleaves cleanup and setup
nodes.rationale: One component at a time, unlike other Effects. Refs are not attached yet and you cannot update state. Exists for CSS-in-JS.

nodes.label: StrictMode double-invocation
nodes.rationale: One extra setup+cleanup cycle in development before the first real setup. It tests the mount path only.

nodes.label: setup → cleanup → setup must match setup once
nodes.rationale: If the screen, network or outside world looks different after the extra cycle, the cleanup is incomplete.
nodes.norm_label: setup → cleanup → setup must match setup once

nodes.label: Start and stop, not mount and unmount
nodes.rationale: Ask what start means and what stop means. If both have clean answers the effect is resilient to being started and stopped as many times as needed.
nodes.norm_label: start and stop, not mount and unmount

nodes.label: Fiber
nodes.rationale: Unit of work and linked tree that made the render phase interruptible (work loop, double buffering, alternate).

nodes.label: Render, reconcile, commit
nodes.rationale: Render is pure and can be thrown away; commit touches the DOM and cannot be undone. Almost every React rule follows from this split.

nodes.label: useSyncExternalStore
nodes.rationale: Subscribe to an external mutable store without tearing under concurrent rendering.

nodes.label: Concurrent rendering
nodes.rationale: React can start rendering, stop, do something more urgent, and throw unfinished work away. Purity becomes a correctness requirement.

nodes.label: Part 3 — Concurrent React and the server
nodes.norm_label: part 3 — concurrent react and the server

nodes.label: Array constructor arity trap
nodes.rationale: new Array(3) is length 3 with holes; new Array(1,2) is [1,2]. One numeric argument is a length. Hazard when argument count is dynamic.

nodes.label: Array.from
nodes.rationale: Creates a shallow-copied Array from an iterable or array-like. Only built-in that accepts both protocols. Spread requires Symbol.iterator.

nodes.label: Array.from mapFn
nodes.rationale: Maps during construction: no intermediate array. Callback gets (element, index) only — no third array argument because the array is still being built.

nodes.label: Array.of
nodes.rationale: Always treats arguments as elements. Array.of(3) is [3]. Exists because Array() changes meaning by argument count.

nodes.label: Four ways to create holes
nodes.rationale: new Array(n); elision [1,,3]; arr.length = larger; delete arr[i] (length unchanged). All avoidable.

nodes.label: Methods that skip holes
nodes.rationale: Skip: forEach, map, filter, some, every, reduce, reduceRight. Treat as undefined: for...of, spread, Array.from, find, findIndex, includes, join, sort, fill, entries.

nodes.label: includes vs indexOf on holes
nodes.rationale: includes treats holes as undefined (true); indexOf skips holes (-1). Sharpest form of the hole-behaviour split.

nodes.label: length is not a count of elements
nodes.rationale: length is one more than the highest index. a[99]='x' makes length 100 with one value. Object.keys(a).length is the real count.
nodes.norm_label: length is not a count of elements

nodes.label: Three states of an array index
nodes.rationale: Present with a value; present holding undefined; a hole (property absent). Reading gives undefined for the last two; only in/hasOwn distinguish them.
nodes.norm_label: three states of an array index

nodes.label: Array length is writable
nodes.rationale: Writable nonnegative integer < 2^32. Shrinking truncates; growing appends holes. arr.length=0 empties in place. Invalid lengths throw RangeError.

nodes.label: Array creation and shape
nodes.rationale: new Array(n) creates holes so .map() does nothing. length is writable and is one more than the highest index.

nodes.label: splice vs delete on arrays
nodes.rationale: delete leaves a hole and length unchanged. splice removes the element, closes the gap, decrements length.

nodes.label: reduce skips holes not undefined
nodes.rationale: [1,2,,4] sums to 7; [1,2,undefined,4] is NaN. Clearest demonstration that a hole is not undefined.

nodes.label: Phase 5 — The built-in library
nodes.rationale: 26 topics grouped by object. Master-first: 01, 02, 04, 05, 06, 07, 09, 10 complete. Documentation-validated; no new sandboxes.

nodes.label: {length: n} range idiom
nodes.rationale: Array.from({length:n}, (_,i)=>...) never creates a sparse array. new Array(n).map skips holes. Standard way to build a range.

nodes.label: Never create holes
nodes.rationale: If you never create holes the hole-behaviour table stops mattering. Use splice to remove, Array.from({length:n}, fn) to allocate, Array.of when arity is dynamic.

nodes.label: Index signature and Record
nodes.rationale: Every key is assumed to exist unless noUncheckedIndexedAccess. Record with a union key produces required properties. Prefer Map when keys are runtime data.

nodes.label: Narrowing lost inside a callback
nodes.rationale: Measured on 7.0.2: narrowing of a property survives await in the same function and is discarded inside forEach, which could run later. Copy to a const first.

nodes.label: strictNullChecks
nodes.rationale: Without it, null and undefined belong to every type and | null is decoration. With it they are ordinary union members (TS18047). Defaults true via strict in TypeScript 7.

nodes.label: Empty object type {}
nodes.rationale: Not an empty object: any value with at least zero members, i.e. everything except null and undefined. Legitimate as T extends {} meaning defined.

nodes.label: object (lowercase)
nodes.rationale: Any non-primitive. Excludes strings and numbers. Exposes no members, so you cannot read properties from it.

nodes.label: Object wrapper interface
nodes.rationale: Members of Object.prototype. Primitives satisfy it by autoboxing. Same trap as String, Number, Boolean — lowercase primitives only.

nodes.label: Record<string, unknown>
nodes.rationale: What to write for any object whose properties you will read. unknown plus narrowing if you will prove the shape first.

nodes.label: typeof object includes null
nodes.rationale: typeof null === 'object' is a 1995 JavaScript bug that TypeScript models. Measured: string | number | null | undefined | string[] narrows to string[] | null. Pair with !== null.

nodes.label: assertNever exhaustiveness
nodes.rationale: After every case, the value is never. A missing case names itself (Type '"cancelled"' is not assignable to type '1'). A default fallback hides new variants.

nodes.label: Discriminated union
nodes.rationale: Shared property with a distinct literal in each member. Makes illegal combinations unrepresentable, unlike { ok: boolean; data?; error? }.

nodes.label: never
nodes.rationale: Empty type. Return of a function that always throws or loops; assignable to everything vacuously; result of narrowing everything away. Unexpected never means a branch is unreachable.

nodes.label: Intersection conflicting members become never
nodes.rationale: No error at the declaration. First assignment is Type 'string' is not assignable to type 'never'. interface extends reports TS2430 instead.

nodes.label: Intersection distributes over union
nodes.rationale: (A | B) & C becomes (A & C) | (B & C). Adds a shared field to every branch of a discriminated union without breaking the discriminant.

nodes.label: Intersection types
nodes.rationale: A & B means both at once. Unions widen values and narrow usable members; intersections do the reverse. Mixin pattern for composing named fragments.

nodes.label: Equality narrowing
nodes.rationale: Comparing against a literal removes everything else. Narrows both operands when they are both unions. Mechanism behind discriminated unions and switch exhaustiveness.

nodes.label: extends vs intersection on conflict
nodes.rationale: interface extends reports the conflict at the declaration. An intersection silently produces string & number, i.e. never, discovered at the call site.

nodes.label: Engine versus host
nodes.rationale: V8/SpiderMonkey/JSC execute the language; window, document and process come from the host, not from JavaScript.

nodes.label: Phase 2 — Operators, expressions and control flow
nodes.norm_label: phase 2 — operators, expressions and control flow

nodes.label: Phase 8 — Modules, errors, memory and the toolchain
nodes.norm_label: phase 8 — modules, errors, memory and the toolchain

nodes.label: Phase 13 — Complexity and JavaScript's real costs
nodes.norm_label: phase 13 — complexity and javascript's real costs

nodes.label: Phase 14 — Core data structures in JavaScript
nodes.norm_label: phase 14 — core data structures in javascript

nodes.label: Phase 16 — Dynamic programming and the harder set
nodes.norm_label: phase 16 — dynamic programming and the harder set

nodes.label: Phase 17 — Machine coding: implement it yourself
nodes.rationale: The brief's custom functions requirement: writing map, bind, debounce, Promise.all and an LRU from an empty file.
nodes.norm_label: phase 17 — machine coding: implement it yourself

nodes.label: Database-per-tenant
nodes.rationale: Rare: a small number of large tenants needing strict isolation, per-tenant restore and resource limits. Connection pooling multiplies per database; onboarding is provisioning.

nodes.label: Shared-to-separated migration asymmetry
nodes.rationale: Shared to separated is filter-and-copy. Separated to shared remaps colliding identity values everywhere they are referenced.

nodes.label: Schema-per-tenant
nodes.rationale: Right when isolation is contractual or regulatory, schemas genuinely differ, or per-tenant restore is routine. Cost: migrations run N times, cross-tenant queries become UNION over N, catalog grows, search_path is safety-critical.

nodes.label: SET LOCAL mandatory for tenant context
nodes.rationale: Plain SET persists on a pooled connection into the next request. With RLS keyed on app.tenant_id this is a concurrency-only leak. Use set_config(..., true).
nodes.norm_label: set local mandatory for tenant context

nodes.label: Shared schema with RLS
nodes.rationale: Default: cheapest operations, weakest structural isolation, most isolation bought back with RESTRICTIVE RLS plus FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY. Only reversible starting point.

nodes.label: Tenancy decision order
nodes.rationale: Contract or regulation first; then tenant count (thousands force shared); then cross-tenant query frequency; then genuine schema variation. Do not choose for hypothetical isolation.

nodes.label: tenant_id leads every index
nodes.rationale: Every query is tenant-scoped in application code and via the RLS predicate, so an index that does not lead with tenant_id cannot serve the filter on every query.

nodes.label: BYPASSRLS analytics role
nodes.rationale: Global billing and admin queries must bypass RLS via a dedicated named role, not the table owner, so unrestricted access is explicit.

nodes.label: Hybrid tenancy
nodes.rationale: Long tail on shared schema, dedicated databases for the largest or contractually separated few. Arriving from shared is the reversible direction.

nodes.label: Noisy neighbours
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL offers no intra-database isolation. Mitigate with per-role statement_timeout and work_mem, separate pools per tier, app rate limits, a reporting replica, or move a large tenant out.

nodes.label: Shared schema shards later
nodes.rationale: tenant_id is already the natural partition key. Keep it on every table and avoid cross-tenant foreign keys so splitting clusters later is routing.

nodes.label: Deleting a tenant completely
nodes.rationale: Separated models DROP SCHEMA CASCADE or DROP DATABASE. Shared schema DELETEs every table in FK order, ideally ON DELETE CASCADE plus information_schema-generated lists. Backups still hold data for the retention window.

nodes.label: Tenant isolation tests
nodes.rationale: Run as the application role. The forgotten case is two sequential requests for different tenants on one pooled connection, which catches SET versus SET LOCAL.

nodes.label: Tenant onboarding
nodes.rationale: Shared schema is an INSERT; schema-per-tenant is CREATE SCHEMA plus migrations; database-per-tenant is provisioning. Must be idempotent and transactional.

nodes.label: ON DELETE RESTRICT NO ACTION CASCADE SET NULL
nodes.rationale: RESTRICT raises 23001 immediately and cannot defer. NO ACTION raises 23503 and can be DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED. CASCADE is transitive. Unindexed FKs scan the child table.
nodes.norm_label: on delete restrict no action cascade set null

nodes.label: timestamptz for instants
nodes.rationale: Stores UTC, renders in session TimeZone. timestamp without zone is a wall-clock reading with no recoverable instant. SET TIME ZONE on a pool leaks.

nodes.label: Default to shared schema with RLS
nodes.rationale: Choose separation only when isolation is contractual or regulatory. Schema-per-tenant chosen for safety buys a permanent migration tax for a property FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY already provides.
nodes.norm_label: default to shared schema with rls

nodes.label: Phase 8 — Validation and authorization at the edge
nodes.norm_label: phase 8 — validation and authorization at the edge

nodes.label: App boot order
nodes.rationale: validate env → connect pool → createApp(deps) → server.listen → signal ready.

nodes.label: Close http.Server not Express app
nodes.rationale: Call close on the http.Server returned by listen, not the Express app.

nodes.label: SIGTERM graceful shutdown
nodes.rationale: Keep server from listen. On SIGTERM: stop accepting, drain, close pools.

nodes.label: App then router then route middleware
nodes.rationale: Application middleware runs before router middleware for that mount. Route-level middleware runs only for that route.
nodes.norm_label: app then router then route middleware

nodes.label: First registered middleware runs first
nodes.rationale: Express does not sort middleware by specificity. Registration order on app is absolute.

nodes.label: Liveness vs readiness probes
nodes.rationale: Liveness is cheap. Readiness checks pool/redis. Failing readiness stops new traffic; failing liveness restarts the process — conflating them causes restart storms.

nodes.label: Scope middleware off hot paths
nodes.rationale: Global middleware is easy and expensive — it runs for health checks and static. Scope auth and loggers to routers that need them.

nodes.label: Idempotency-Key
nodes.rationale: Clients retry POSTs. Without a key you double-charge. POST and some PATCH need keys; GET/PUT are already idempotent when implemented correctly.

nodes.label: Idempotency payload hash 409
nodes.rationale: Same key, different body is a client bug or attack. Reject with 409 if payload hash mismatches stored request.

nodes.label: Idempotency replay store
nodes.rationale: Store key → response (status + body) under a TTL. Replay returns the same result without re-executing side effects.

nodes.label: Inbound webhook verification
nodes.rationale: raw body + signature + timestamp skew. Persist event id for dedupe. Enqueue work; respond quickly.

nodes.label: Outbound webhook 202 enqueue
nodes.rationale: Fire-and-forget from the route is a bug under load. Express only accepts the command and returns 202.

nodes.label: express.raw for webhook signature
nodes.rationale: Signature is over exact bytes, not re-serialized JSON.

nodes.label: pg_advisory_xact_lock around migrate
nodes.rationale: Taken inside the same transaction that reads the tracking table and applies files. Five concurrent runners: one applied, four no-ops.

nodes.label: Migrations
nodes.rationale: A numbered file that runs exactly once, inside a transaction, with the fact that it ran recorded in the database.

nodes.label: Identity consumed on skipped conflict
nodes.rationale: ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING draws the identity before detecting conflict. Two rows, three runs, sequence at 6. Sequences are not gapless.

nodes.label: ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING
nodes.rationale: Requires a unique constraint. Idempotency is enforced by the database. SELECT-then-INSERT is not safe under concurrency.

nodes.label: ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE
nodes.rationale: Reassert reference data the code depends on. EXCLUDED is the row that would have been inserted. Use DO NOTHING when a human may edit the row.

nodes.label: Seeding
nodes.rationale: A seed runs more than once. If twice is not identical to once, it is a data-corruption script.

nodes.label: Transactional DDL
nodes.rationale: Failed migration leaves nothing behind, including the tracking row. Makes forward-only practical. MySQL/Oracle need manual cleanup.

nodes.label: ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS type trap
nodes.rationale: Matches column name only. Existing integer vs expected text is a silent no-op. CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS compares name, not definition.
nodes.norm_label: add column if not exists type trap

nodes.label: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS
nodes.rationale: Makes a statement idempotent. Not concurrency-safe, not a migration, does not compare definitions. Three gaps the syntax hides.

nodes.label: IF NOT EXISTS is not concurrency-safe
nodes.rationale: Catalog check and insert are not one atomic step. 228 of 500 concurrent attempts failed with 23505 on pg_type_typname_nsp_index.
nodes.norm_label: if not exists is not concurrency-safe

nodes.label: Connect on 127.0.0.1 never localhost
nodes.rationale: Node DNS verbatim order resolves localhost to ::1 first. A container published on IPv4 only yields connection refused.

nodes.label: alpine musl vs debian glibc collation
nodes.rationale: Same PostgreSQL 18.4 and en_US.utf8, different ORDER BY. musl locale is a stub and falls back to byte order. Match base image or pin ICU.
nodes.norm_label: alpine musl vs debian glibc collation

nodes.label: Local development database
nodes.rationale: Disposable, version-matched to production, on a non-colliding port. postgres:18-alpine on 55432.

nodes.label: pg_isready readiness loop
nodes.rationale: Container running is not accepting TCP. First init starts the server twice. sleep 5 is flaky or slow; poll pg_isready or compose healthcheck.

nodes.label: Migrations as a deploy step
nodes.rationale: Not at app boot. A failed migration should stop the deploy. App role should not have CREATE/ALTER. Long ACCESS EXCLUSIVE must not block old instances.

nodes.label: Forward-only migrations
nodes.rationale: Down migrations are untested, run months later, and cannot restore DROP COLUMN data. Recovery is a new forward file plus backup.

nodes.label: Deterministic fixtures
nodes.rationale: Math.random, Date.now, or unseeded faker make tests unreproducible. Pin emails and timestamps. Volume via generate_series.

nodes.label: IF NOT EXISTS is a name check
nodes.rationale: Editing CREATE to add a column is a silent no-op where the table exists. Migrations express change; IF NOT EXISTS expresses absence.
nodes.norm_label: if not exists is a name check

nodes.label: UNLOGGED all-text staging table
nodes.rationale: COPY is all-or-nothing. Stage as text, then INSERT SELECT with validation to restore ON CONFLICT and inspect rejects. UNLOGGED skips WAL.

nodes.label: tmpfs disposable data directory
nodes.rationale: With working migrations and seeds, rebuild in seconds. Faster (no disk sync) and cannot drift. Never mistake it for a real deployment.

nodes.label: Date overrides default ToPrimitive hint
nodes.rationale: Date makes hint default behave as string, so date + '' is a date string while date * 1 is a timestamp.

nodes.label: ToPrimitive
nodes.rationale: Hint string tries toString then valueOf. Hint number or default tries valueOf then toString. + uses default; templates use string; arithmetic uses number.

nodes.label: Four equality algorithms
nodes.rationale: == and === treat NaN as unequal and 0 equal to -0. SameValueZero (includes, Map/Set) equates NaN. SameValue (Object.is) also distinguishes -0.

nodes.label: value == null
nodes.rationale: The one defensible == use: tests null or undefined and nothing else. ESLint eqeqeq smart allows it.

nodes.label: null >= 0 is true
nodes.rationale: Relational operators ToNumber; Number(null) is 0. == never numeric-compares null. A null stock level silently passes a bounds check.

nodes.label: == vs ===
nodes.rationale: === compares without converting. == converts: null/undefined only each other; string to number; boolean to number first; object via ToPrimitive.

nodes.label: UTF-16 code units
nodes.rationale: .length, charAt and slice count UTF-16 code units. Code points above U+FFFF are surrogate pairs, so '🛒'.length is 2. Naive slice can emit a lone high surrogate.

nodes.label: Relational comparison algorithm
nodes.rationale: ToPrimitive hint number, then lexicographic if both strings else ToNumber. No null special case: null >= 0 is true while null == 0 is false. NaN makes every relation false so !(a<b) is not a>=b.

nodes.label: Private brand check
nodes.rationale: #x in obj is legal only inside the declaring class. Stronger than instanceof because privates cannot be forged or added later.

nodes.label: Private elements
nodes.rationale: No desugaring. # prefix; parser-enforced. Fields, methods, statics, and accessors. Cannot be deleted or created by assignment.

nodes.label: Private access SyntaxError
nodes.rationale: obj.#field outside the declaring class is a parse-time SyntaxError. The file never runs.

nodes.label: Accessor recursion trap
nodes.rationale: get name() { return this.name; } calls itself until the stack blows. Back with #name.

nodes.label: JSON round-trip clone
nodes.rationale: Deep but loses seven documented things and cannot handle cycles. Fine only for already JSON-shaped data.

nodes.label: structuredClone
nodes.rationale: Deep clone that rebuilds cycles. Silently drops prototypes and private elements; throws DataCloneError on some types.

nodes.label: Private is encapsulation not secrecy
nodes.rationale: A debugger shows them. JSON.stringify and structuredClone drop them. Maintenance property, not a security boundary.

nodes.label: Reflect.ownKeys
nodes.rationale: Only one-call way to get every own key — enumerable or not, strings and symbols. Use with getOwnPropertyDescriptor for a faithful clone.

nodes.label: Hand-written deep clone
nodes.rationale: Interview answer, not production. Still drops prototype, descriptors, accessors, and private fields. Ship structuredClone.

nodes.label: DataCloneError
nodes.rationale: DOMException when any part is not serialisable — functions, DOM nodes, Promise, WeakMap, Symbol. Better than JSON silently dropping functions.

nodes.label: structuredClone
nodes.rationale: Language deep clone via the structured clone algorithm. Rebuilds cycles, preserves Map/Set/Date/RegExp/typed arrays. Loses prototype, descriptors, private fields, RegExp.lastIndex. Clones data, not types.

nodes.label: structuredClone transfer option
nodes.rationale: Moves transferable buffers instead of copying; original is detached (byteLength 0). Only when finished with the source.

nodes.label: WeakMap
nodes.rationale: Required when keys must not keep objects alive (visited-set in a clone, per-object metadata). Not iterable and not serialisable.

nodes.label: Visited WeakMap before recurse
nodes.rationale: Register the empty clone in a WeakMap before walking children so cycles terminate and shared identity is preserved. After the loop never terminates. WeakMap so bookkeeping does not pin every visited object.

nodes.label: Parentheses for object assignment
nodes.rationale: A statement starting with { is a block. Assigning without declaring needs ({ a, b } = obj). Arrays have no such problem.

nodes.label: Destructuring null or undefined throws
nodes.rationale: Throws even with empty patterns. Guard with ?? {} or a = {} parameter default. Other values coerce to objects.

nodes.label: Destructuring
nodes.rationale: Pattern-matching on the left-hand side of an assignment: the shape of the expected value becomes bindings.

nodes.label: Destructuring defaults apply to undefined only
nodes.rationale: Defaults fire only when the value is undefined, not null. JSON payloads use null for missing, so defaults are routinely bypassed.
nodes.norm_label: destructuring defaults apply to undefined only

nodes.label: Nested destructuring
nodes.rationale: Intermediate names are paths, not bindings. Nesting throws when an intermediate is missing; default each risky level or use optional chaining.

nodes.label: Destructuring swap idiom
nodes.rationale: The RHS array is fully evaluated before assignment, so [a, b] = [b, a] needs no temporary.

nodes.label: Array vs object destructuring
nodes.rationale: Array destructuring matches by position; object destructuring matches by name. Array elements cannot be renamed; object properties can.

nodes.label: Resolved
nodes.rationale: Resolved describes the decision, not the outcome. resolve(anotherPromise) locks onto the inner promise immediately while leaving the outer pending.

nodes.label: async function adoption
nodes.rationale: return somePromise from an async function does not produce a nested promise. return await p and return p usually behave identically.

nodes.label: Promise adoption / flattening
nodes.rationale: Return a plain value and it is wrapped. Return a promise or thenable and it is adopted, never nested as Promise<Promise<T>>.

nodes.label: Hoisted undeclared dependencies
nodes.rationale: npm flattens so require('lodash') can find a transitive copy until that dependent drops it.

nodes.label: npx
nodes.rationale: Local .bin first, else download and execute. A typo'd name is an attack vector.

nodes.label: Pin Node in the repo
nodes.rationale: .nvmrc, engines, pinned Dockerfile tag, CI node-version-file. npm engines is advisory unless engine-strict.

nodes.label: dependencies vs devDependencies
nodes.rationale: Does the running application import it? Production uses --omit=dev.

nodes.label: V8 generational GC
nodes.rationale: New objects start young and cheap to scavenge; survivors age into old space where major GC pauses are costlier and show up as loop lag.

nodes.label: --max-old-space-size
nodes.rationale: Old-space budget, not a cgroup RSS limit. Measured 256 MB flag produced ~448 MB heap_size_limit. Too high and the kernel OOMKiller fires first.

nodes.label: performance marks and measures
