nodes.rationale: Named timestamps and the duration between them. Clear entries in long-lived processes or the buffer grows.

nodes.label: performance.now
nodes.rationale: Monotonic high-resolution clock inside the process. Prefer over Date.now() which can step on NTP and produce negative or wild durations.

nodes.label: PerformanceObserver
nodes.rationale: Observe entryTypes including gc. Histogram duration and watch multi-ms spikes; do not alert on individual GC entries.

nodes.label: HTTP server.close drain
nodes.rationale: Keep-alive can hold server.close open; track sockets and destroy idle ones after timeout.

nodes.label: Shutdown is the reverse of boot
nodes.rationale: SIGTERM → fail readiness → drain → close server → close pools → exit.
nodes.norm_label: shutdown is the reverse of boot

nodes.label: Serverless isolate freeze model
nodes.rationale: Process may freeze or die without SIGTERM; setInterval is not a background worker.

nodes.label: Readiness vs liveness
nodes.rationale: Failing readiness removes traffic without killing the pod mid-drain; liveness restarts.

nodes.label: Scaling — vertical vs horizontal, cluster vs replicas
nodes.norm_label: scaling — vertical vs horizontal, cluster vs replicas

nodes.label: Promote image digest
nodes.rationale: Production must run the exact bits that passed staging, not a hopeful rebuild on the deploy agent.

nodes.label: Multi-stage Node Dockerfile
nodes.rationale: Copy lockfile and package.json before source so code edits do not invalidate the dependency layer.

nodes.label: Container PID 1
nodes.rationale: PID 1 must reap zombies and forward signals; make Node PID 1 with exec-form CMD.

nodes.label: Dockerizing Node — multi-stage, non-root, layer cache
nodes.norm_label: dockerizing node — multi-stage, non-root, layer cache

nodes.label: npm start swallows SIGTERM
nodes.rationale: npm as PID 1 often does not forward SIGTERM to Node, so graceful handlers never run and the orchestrator SIGKILLs after grace.

nodes.label: Alpine musl vs glibc
nodes.rationale: Native addon prebuilds often target glibc first; Alpine can fail at runtime without a musl build.

nodes.label: node:24-bookworm-slim
nodes.rationale: Default for most fullstack APIs: glibc, good addon compatibility, still slim.

nodes.label: C++ addon
nodes.rationale: Crashes inside the addon take down the whole Node process; try/catch cannot catch a segfault.

nodes.label: Node embedder API
nodes.rationale: Your C++ binary hosts Node; typical HTTP services consume Node as host, they do not embed.

nodes.label: Node-API
nodes.rationale: Preferred stable ABI for new addons versus raw V8 or NAN.

nodes.label: Image size and hardening — distroless, alpine, slim
nodes.norm_label: image size and hardening — distroless, alpine, slim

nodes.label: async_hooks
nodes.rationale: Experimental lifecycle hooks (init/before/after/destroy) that track the async context tree. For APM vendors, not app code.

nodes.label: AsyncResource.bind
nodes.rationale: Captures the current async context and restores it when a callback later runs — the fix for EventEmitter and queue context loss.

nodes.label: node:diagnostics_channel
nodes.rationale: Supported instrumentation: named channels with near-zero cost when nobody is subscribed. Prefer over createHook.

nodes.label: executionAsyncId and triggerAsyncId
nodes.rationale: Id of the executing async context and the id that created it. The tree AsyncLocalStorage walks.

nodes.label: AsyncLocalStorage
nodes.rationale: Per-request ambient context (request id, tenant) that survives await without adding a parameter to every signature.

nodes.label: Do not use createHook in application code
nodes.rationale: Experimental, fires on every async op, and console.log inside a hook recurses. Use AsyncLocalStorage and diagnostics_channel.
nodes.norm_label: do not use createhook in application code

nodes.label: run() versus enterWith()
nodes.rationale: run(store, fn) scopes the store to fn and descendants. enterWith leaks into the rest of the current async context; prefer run().

nodes.label: writeFile is not atomic
nodes.rationale: Opens with 'w', truncates immediately, then writes. Crash, ENOSPC, or a concurrent reader sees a truncated file.

nodes.label: createWriteStream truncates
nodes.rationale: Default flags 'w' empties an existing file as soon as the stream is created, even if nothing is written. Use 'a' to append.

nodes.label: chokidar
nodes.rationale: Debounces, distinguishes add/change/unlink, awaitWriteFinish, auto-polls for network mounts, handles editor atomic-save.

nodes.label: fs.watch
nodes.rationale: OS events (inotify/FSEvents/ReadDirectoryChangesW). Fast, inconsistent. One writeFile produced two change events. Often silent on Docker mounts.

nodes.label: fs.watchFile
nodes.rationale: Polls with stat (default 5007 ms). Reliable on network/Docker mounts; expensive at scale. Deletion is curr.mtimeMs===0. Must unwatchFile.

nodes.label: inotify ENOSPC
nodes.rationale: Per-user watch limit, not disk space. One watch per directory; recursive watch over node_modules exhausts max_user_watches.

nodes.label: Do not watch files in production
nodes.rationale: Containers are immutable, events fail on production volumes, a partial write can be loaded, and the reload path is under-tested. Prefer restart or SIGHUP.
nodes.norm_label: do not watch files in production

nodes.label: HttpOnly Secure SameSite
nodes.rationale: HttpOnly blocks XSS exfiltration, Secure blocks plaintext HTTP, SameSite is the CSRF defence. A session cookie wants all three.

nodes.label: Set-Cookie array header
nodes.rationale: Node has no cookie API. Cookie request headers join with '; '. Set-Cookie must be an array so each cookie is its own header line.

nodes.label: Opaque session id vs JWT cookie
nodes.norm_label: opaque session id vs jwt cookie

nodes.label: URLSearchParams is the wrong cookie parser
nodes.norm_label: urlsearchparams is the wrong cookie parser

nodes.label: TLS certificate chain
nodes.rationale: Node uses a compiled Mozilla trust store, not the OS store. A missing intermediate is the common works-in-browser fails-in-Node bug.

nodes.label: mTLS
nodes.rationale: Rejection happens in the handshake, so failures are socket errors with nothing in HTTP logs.

nodes.label: rejectUnauthorized false
nodes.rationale: Disables chain and hostname verification. Encryption remains; authentication is gone.

nodes.label: SIGKILL leaves job active
nodes.rationale: SIGKILL mid-job leaves active:1 with no error. Recovered only when the visibility timeout expires.

nodes.label: Stalled job
nodes.rationale: The worker vanished. Nothing is reported; attemptsMade does not increase. Only the expiring lease recovers it.

nodes.label: Visibility timeout
nodes.rationale: BullMQ lockDuration or locked_until. Set above p99 duration. A job that outlives it is claimed twice.

nodes.label: Oldest-job age alert
nodes.rationale: A stopped worker produces no errors. Alert on oldest waiting job age and completion rate.

nodes.label: Acknowledge last
nodes.rationale: Ack after the durable effect. Ack first plus crash is silent loss; ack last plus crash is a duplicate.

nodes.label: Graceful worker shutdown
nodes.rationale: On SIGTERM stop claiming, finish in-flight jobs, then close pool and Redis. Close worker first.

nodes.label: Throw and let the queue retry
nodes.rationale: An inner retry loop multiplies attempts and holds the worker slot while sleeping.
nodes.norm_label: throw and let the queue retry

nodes.label: Domain-derived idempotency key
nodes.rationale: order-paid-email:${orderId} is stable across attempts. crypto.randomUUID() inside the job deduplicates nothing.

nodes.label: Outbound job four properties
nodes.rationale: Idempotent on a domain key, bounded by a timeout, classified 4xx vs 5xx/429, recorded locally.

nodes.label: UnrecoverableError
nodes.rationale: 4xx except 429 fail permanently. Retrying a 422 turns a clear error into a slow mystery.

nodes.label: fetch has no default timeout
nodes.rationale: Node fetch waits as long as the socket stays open. AbortSignal.timeout(ms) is the built-in bound.

nodes.label: Job idempotency
nodes.rationale: Every job will run twice because delivery is at-least-once. A non-repeatable handler is a pending incident.

nodes.label: Ledger-guarded balance update
nodes.rationale: Insert a ledger row on conflict do nothing, then apply the delta only if rowCount is 1, in one transaction.

nodes.label: Retry only transient and safe
nodes.rationale: Both questions must be yes. A timeout is transient but retrying an unguarded POST /charge duplicates money.

nodes.label: exec vs execFile
nodes.rationale: exec runs a shell. execFile with an args array treats report.txt; id as one filename. shell:true is DEP0190.

nodes.label: NoSQL operator injection
nodes.rationale: {"password":{"$ne":null}} logged in as admin. Coerce to string/$eq and validate body shape.

nodes.label: SQL $1 placeholders
nodes.rationale: A parameter can never become a statement. Identifiers cannot be placeholders; allowlist column names.

nodes.label: Boundary check order
nodes.rationale: Content-type, size cap, JSON.parse, schema. A 20 MB body blocked the loop 40.7 ms before any schema ran.

nodes.label: z.coerce pitfalls
nodes.rationale: Number("")/[]/null become 0. z.coerce.boolean maps "false" to true. Repeated query keys arrive as arrays.

nodes.label: Injection shape
nodes.rationale: Untrusted data concatenated into a string an interpreter reads as instructions. Fix: separate channels, not escaping.

nodes.label: Parse don't validate
nodes.rationale: A parser returns a new typed value. The raw body stops existing, so added fields cannot leak through.

nodes.label: FOR UPDATE NOWAIT
nodes.rationale: Fail immediately with 55P03 if any selected row is locked. For 'someone else is editing this'.

nodes.label: At-least-once job delivery
nodes.rationale: Committing the claim early leaves crashed workers' rows in running. A reaper plus idempotent handlers is the guarantee; exactly-once is not configurable.

nodes.label: SKIP LOCKED
nodes.rationale: Omit locked rows instead of waiting. Turns a table into a concurrent work queue; trades FIFO for parallelism.

nodes.label: LISTEN/NOTIFY
nodes.rationale: Transactional wake-up with no extra broker. At-most-once, 8000-byte payload, dedicated listener connection. Use as a hint beside durable state.

nodes.label: Notification queue
nodes.rationale: Shared 8 GB queue until every listener has read. A stuck listener is a database-wide problem.

nodes.label: SKIP LOCKED job queue
nodes.rationale: SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED then commit the claim before work. 8 workers, 200 jobs: 168.6 ms, 0 duplicates vs 593 without locking.

nodes.label: NOTIFY at-most-once
nodes.rationale: A notification sent while nobody is listening is discarded. Combine with a transactional outbox if the event must not be lost.

nodes.label: Audit trigger
nodes.rationale: AFTER ROW trigger writing to_jsonb(OLD/NEW). Attached to the table so migrations and psql cannot bypass it. Measured ~1.24× write cost.

nodes.label: DEFAULT partition
nodes.rationale: Catches keys outside every range; without it INSERT is 23514. Keep it empty by creating future partitions ahead of time.

nodes.label: Partitioning
nodes.rationale: Payoff is dropping a month in milliseconds, not query speed. RANGE for time series, LIST for enums, HASH to spread writes.

nodes.label: Partition pruning
nodes.rationale: Skips partitions that cannot match. 15.6 ms with the key vs 32.9 ms Parallel Append across five partitions — about 2×, not 5×.

nodes.label: AFTER versus BEFORE triggers
nodes.rationale: BEFORE to change the row, AFTER to react. NEW assignment in AFTER is silently discarded; RETURN NULL in BEFORE silently drops the row.

nodes.label: WHEN IS DISTINCT FROM
nodes.rationale: Evaluated before entering plpgsql so no-op updates skip the call (0.86×). <> is NULL when either side is NULL.

nodes.label: Partition key in primary key
nodes.rationale: Every unique constraint must include the partition key. No global index, so uniqueness on any other column cannot be enforced across partitions.

nodes.label: Full-text search
nodes.rationale: Documents become tsvector, queries become tsquery, @@ matches them. Good enough that most apps never need a separate search server.

nodes.label: tsquery
nodes.rationale: to_tsquery must never see raw user input; use the query parsers instead.

nodes.label: gin_trgm_ops
nodes.rationale: Makes ILIKE '%x%' a Bitmap Heap Scan: 87.0 ms → 1.13 ms. Cannot serve ORDER BY <->.

nodes.label: gist_trgm_ops
nodes.rationale: Serves ORDER BY <-> nearest-neighbour. Larger (22 MB vs 9 MB GIN).

nodes.label: pg_trgm
nodes.rationale: Compares overlapping three-character sequences. Finds typos FTS cannot; has no stemming. Also makes ILIKE '%x%' indexable.

nodes.label: word_similarity <%
nodes.rationale: % compares whole strings (0.273 vs a long title). <% scores the query against the best word (1.000). Query goes on the left.

nodes.label: RLS policy as query predicate
nodes.rationale: Index policy columns as the leading composite key; every query is tenant-scoped whether the app wrote it that way.

nodes.label: USING versus WITH CHECK
nodes.rationale: USING guards the row you started with; WITH CHECK guards the row you end up with. An UPDATE needs both.

nodes.label: RLS as authorization backstop
nodes.rationale: Filter in the application because it is clear and fast; enable RLS underneath because people are fallible. On Supabase, RLS is the whole mechanism.

nodes.label: citext
nodes.rationale: Case-insensitive text plus case-insensitive UNIQUE (23505 on a case variant). Folds case via collation, not Unicode composition; extension required.

nodes.label: lower() unique expression index
nodes.rationale: No-extension fallback for case-insensitive uniqueness; every query must use lower() or it silently misses rows.

nodes.label: UNIQUE NULLS NOT DISTINCT
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL 15+ option that treats NULLs as equal for uniqueness, raising 23505 on a second NULL.

nodes.label: UNIQUE allows many NULLs
nodes.rationale: NULLs are not equal so they do not conflict; three NULLs accepted. PostgreSQL 15+ UNIQUE NULLS NOT DISTINCT allows at most one.

nodes.label: Declarative partitioning
nodes.rationale: Enforces the key across partitions (23505). Unmatched partition key → 23514. Every unique constraint must include the partition key.

nodes.label: ONLY keyword
nodes.rationale: Without ONLY, SELECT/UPDATE/DELETE on a parent include children. DELETE FROM parent can wipe child rows.

nodes.label: Table inheritance
nodes.rationale: NOT NULL and CHECK inherit; PK, UNIQUE and FK do not. Two child rows can share id 1. Parent FKs do not see child rows. Avoid for new work.

nodes.label: Multirange types
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL 14+. Plain range union of gapped ranges raises 22000; int4multirange holds {[1,5),[10,15)} as one value.

nodes.label: PostgreSQL range types
nodes.rationale: First-class intervals (int4range, tstzrange, daterange, …) with @>, &&, <<, -|-. pg returns the text form '[1,10)'.

nodes.label: timestamp without time zone
nodes.rationale: Stores the digits and discards the offset. Same value means different instants to every reader. Only for floating wall-clock values with a stored zone name.

nodes.label: timestamptz
nodes.rationale: 8-byte UTC instant. Does not store a zone; converts on input/output. Same instant displays as 04:30+00, 10:00+05:30, 00:30-04.

nodes.label: CREATE TABLE as the client contract
nodes.rationale: Identity, FKs, CHECKs, money type, timestamptz and FK indexes are decisions every client must obey. DDL via pg returns command CREATE and null rowCount.
nodes.norm_label: create table as the client contract

nodes.label: Index every FK referencing column
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL indexes the referenced PK, not the child column. Unindexed parent DELETE scanned 300k children in 33.6 ms vs 8.7 ms indexed.

nodes.label: Types are expensive to reverse
nodes.rationale: Be liberal with constraints, conservative with types. Constraints relax with NOT VALID; type representation changes rewrite under ACCESS EXCLUSIVE.

nodes.label: Deliberate denormalization
nodes.rationale: Trade write complexity for read speed: counters, generated columns, materialized views. Measure first; prefer forms the database maintains.

nodes.label: Historical snapshot vs denormalization
nodes.rationale: unit_cents on an order line is a different fact from products.price_cents. Copying price at sale time is required; joining would rewrite past invoices.

nodes.label: One-to-many relationship
nodes.rationale: FK on the many side. NOT NULL makes it mandatory; ON DELETE CASCADE or RESTRICT; always index the referencing column (measured 4× slower unindexed).

nodes.label: One-to-one via unique FK
nodes.rationale: Make the FK the primary key of the child. Without uniqueness it is one-to-many wearing a one-to-one name (second profile → 23505).

nodes.label: Self-referencing tree
nodes.rationale: parent_id nullable marks a root. ON DELETE CASCADE deletes whole subtrees. Arbitrary depth needs a recursive CTE.

nodes.label: ON DELETE RESTRICT vs NO ACTION
nodes.rationale: Both refuse; 23001 vs 23503. NO ACTION is deferrable to commit (default). RESTRICT checks immediately and cannot be deferred. CASCADE is transitive and silent.
nodes.norm_label: on delete restrict vs no action

nodes.label: Normalize by default
nodes.rationale: A slow read is measurable and fixable later; inconsistent data is often unfixable and erodes trust. Denormalize against EXPLAIN, not a hunch.

nodes.label: CONCURRENTLY cannot run in a transaction
nodes.rationale: CREATE/DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY, VACUUM, CREATE/DROP DATABASE fail with 25001. A failed CONCURRENTLY build leaves an INVALID index still maintained on writes.
nodes.norm_label: concurrently cannot run in a transaction

nodes.label: Transactional DDL
nodes.rationale: CREATE/ALTER/DROP roll back like DML. A later failure vanished a successfully created table. Most engines commit DDL implicitly; PostgreSQL does not.

nodes.label: Batched DELETE on live tables
nodes.rationale: One 100k DELETE 115 ms vs 10 batches 484 ms (4.2× slower). Batching releases locks, stays interruptible, does not pin VACUUM, bounds WAL/replication lag.

nodes.label: DELETE leaves dead tuples
nodes.rationale: 47 MB table stayed 47 MB after deleting half and after VACUUM. VACUUM FULL rewrote to 24 MB under ACCESS EXCLUSIVE. VACUUM truncates only trailing empty pages.

nodes.label: DELETE takes no LIMIT
nodes.rationale: DELETE … LIMIT is 42601. Batch via ctid IN (SELECT ctid … LIMIT n). Never store ctid; it changes on update.

nodes.label: DELETE with no WHERE
nodes.rationale: WHERE is optional. Measured: DELETE FROM d_all removed 10 rows with no warning. Wrap in BEGIN and check the count. To empty a table, prefer TRUNCATE.

nodes.label: Keep DDL transactions short
nodes.rationale: ACCESS EXCLUSIVE is held until commit; an open transaction pins VACUUM's cleanup horizon database-wide. Atomicity is free; duration is not.

nodes.label: NOT MATERIALIZED
nodes.rationale: Forces inlining even with multiple references, which can double the work; ignored for volatile CTEs.

nodes.label: OFFSET 0 optimization fence
nodes.rationale: OFFSET 0 is an older fence that blocks pull-up when MATERIALIZED is not available.

nodes.label: Two references compute once
nodes.rationale: Two reads of the same CTE compute the body once and reuse the result.

nodes.label: MATERIALIZED fence
nodes.rationale: MATERIALIZED forces the CTE to be computed once and stored; measured about 6.1× the inlined cost when that fence is unnecessary.

nodes.label: PostgreSQL 12+ CTE inlining
nodes.rationale: A CTE is inlined unless it is referenced more than once, marked MATERIALIZED, recursive, volatile, or a data-modifying statement.

nodes.label: NULL keys group together
nodes.rationale: GROUP BY treats all NULLs as one key even though NULL = NULL is unknown.

nodes.label: GROUPING()
nodes.rationale: GROUPING(col) is 1 when that column is aggregated away, so a super-aggregate NULL is not confused with a data NULL.

nodes.label: CUBE
nodes.rationale: Every subset of the key list — 2^n grouping sets.

nodes.label: GROUPING SETS
nodes.rationale: One scan produces several GROUP BY combinations listed explicitly.

nodes.label: ROLLUP
nodes.rationale: Hierarchical subtotals from the full key list down to the grand total.

nodes.label: Aggregates skip NULL inputs
nodes.rationale: sum/avg/min/max skip NULL rows while count(*) counts them. An all-NULL group returns NULL, not 0. 0 and NULL are deliberately different on cancelled vs unfinished orders.

nodes.label: array_agg and string_agg
nodes.rationale: string_agg skips NULL inputs; array_agg keeps them as elements. That inconsistency is the source of most surprises in this family.

nodes.label: Empty-array [null] trap
nodes.rationale: A parent with no children yields NULL or [null], not []. FILTER alone is not the fix; the two-level payload needs coalesce around an inner aggregate that already excluded the NULL row.

nodes.label: json_agg and jsonb_agg
nodes.rationale: Nest children into a parent row for a one-query API payload. Do not skip NULL inputs, so LEFT JOIN NULLs become [null] instead of [].

nodes.label: mode and bool_and empty-set surprises
nodes.rationale: mode() hides ties by the WITHIN GROUP ordering. bool_and returns NULL for all-of-nothing, the same empty-set NULL rule as other aggregates.

nodes.label: percentile_cont and percentile_disc
nodes.rationale: cont interpolates at fraction f; disc returns the first actual value at or past f. Several percentiles can share one sort.

nodes.label: Ordered-set aggregates
nodes.rationale: Need input in order first, via WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY …). Percentiles are the usual meeting point. Cost 3.1× an avg() because sorting is unavoidable.

nodes.label: Supporting controlled and uncontrolled
nodes.rationale: Decide with !== undefined, write internal state only when uncontrolled, always fire the callback.

nodes.label: Controlled is per piece of state
nodes.rationale: Informal terms. A DataTable can mix controlled sort with uncontrolled column width.
nodes.norm_label: controlled is per piece of state

nodes.label: Closest common parent owns the state
nodes.rationale: Count components that render based on the value, not pass-throughs. Invent a component solely to own state if needed.
nodes.norm_label: closest common parent owns the state

nodes.label: Single source of truth
nodes.rationale: One owner per piece, not all state in one store. The same information in two places is the forbidden case.

nodes.label: Remove, hardcode, then add state
nodes.rationale: Hardcoding first separates data-flow bugs from state-update bugs.

nodes.label: getDerivedStateFromProps usually should not translate
nodes.rationale: Copying a prop into state is duplicated state. Derive during render instead.

nodes.label: Never sync a prop into state with an effect
nodes.rationale: Creates a second copy, a race, and a first render with the wrong value.
nodes.norm_label: never sync a prop into state with an effect

nodes.label: You Might Not Need an Effect (react.dev)
nodes.norm_label: you might not need an effect (react.dev)

nodes.label: Fetching data in an effect
nodes.rationale: A legitimate effect that react.dev still recommends replacing. Four downsides: no server fetch, waterfalls, no cache, and race-condition boilerplate.

nodes.label: ignore-flag race guard
nodes.rationale: Network responses may arrive out of order. Cleanup flips ignore so a stale response cannot set state. Pair with clearing state before the new fetch.

nodes.label: Network waterfall
nodes.rationale: A child cannot render — and so cannot fetch — until its parent has. Nested mount-time fetches serialise even when independent.

nodes.label: useData custom hook
nodes.rationale: Extracting the race guard is valuable. It does not add cache, deduplication, or pre-mount fetch. Framework loaders or TanStack Query / useSWR do.

nodes.label: never empty type
nodes.rationale: No value has it. Return type of functions that throw or loop; assignable to everything vacuously; result of narrowing everything away (exhaustiveness).

nodes.label: Branded type via intersection
nodes.rationale: string & { readonly __brand: 'UserId' } — a string no ordinary string has. Created at a validated boundary; exists only in the type system.

nodes.label: Conflicting intersection members become never
nodes.rationale: type TB = {x:string} & {x:number} is silent. TB['x'] is never. Failure appears at assignment: Type 'string' is not assignable to type 'never'.

nodes.label: Intersections distribute over unions
nodes.rationale: (A | B) & C becomes (A & C) | (B & C). Adds a shared field to every branch of a discriminated union without breaking the discriminant.

nodes.label: Intersection types A & B
nodes.rationale: Both at once. Every member of every operand is required. Mixin pattern for composing named fragments.

nodes.label: Union widens values, intersection widens members
nodes.rationale: | widens the set of values and narrows usable members; & does the reverse. Or feels permissive for values but makes the type less useful until narrowed.
nodes.norm_label: union widens values, intersection widens members

nodes.label: interface extends vs intersection
nodes.rationale: extends reports TS2430 at the declaration. & produces an unsatisfiable type silently. Prefer extends for layered domain shapes.

nodes.label: app is a request listener
nodes.rationale: express() returns a function. Pass it to http.createServer(app) or call app.listen. Express fills the function Node already expects. Sandbox-measured: typeof app === 'function' and app.handle exists.

nodes.label: Express app
nodes.rationale: express() result: settings, top-level middleware, mounts. Itself a request listener. Only app owns application settings.

nodes.label: Application settings (app.set / app.get)
nodes.rationale: App-wide defaults. Do not confuse app.get('etag') (setting) with app.get('/etag', handler) (route).

nodes.label: etag default weak
nodes.rationale: Measured etag = "weak". Affects automatic ETag generation for some responses.

nodes.label: trust proxy
nodes.rationale: Default false. Without it, req.ip is the proxy. Affects IP, protocol from X-Forwarded-*, secure cookies, and rate-limit keys. Never true blindly.

nodes.label: strict and case-sensitive routing unset
nodes.rationale: Measured undefined, not false. Express never assigns them until you app.set. Unset behaves as off. app.get('strict routing') === false never runs on a fresh app.

nodes.label: Host-based routing
nodes.rationale: Branch on req.hostname via vhost-style middleware. For most JSON APIs, path prefixes beat multi-host apps. Multi-host usually belongs on Nginx.

nodes.label: Express built-in middleware
nodes.rationale: express.json, urlencoded, raw, text (based on body-parser), express.static (serve-static), express.Router. Application settings are not middleware.

nodes.label: No built-in multipart parser
nodes.rationale: Built-in list is json, urlencoded, raw, text, static, Router. multipart/form-data is not JSON.

nodes.label: Third-party middleware checklist
nodes.rationale: Check Express 5 support, maintenance, whether middleware is the right shape, what it mutates, and whether it calls next(err) or throws.

nodes.label: Middleware supply-chain surface
nodes.rationale: A battle-tested package saves time; every dependency is supply-chain surface. Prefer fewer, better mounts. Defaults are not a security review.

nodes.label: Allow-list filter and sort fields
nodes.rationale: Never pass raw req.query into Mongo or SQL builders. Allow-list fields and operators. Prevents sorting on unindexed or sensitive columns and injection-style operators.

nodes.label: Mongo operator injection via query
nodes.rationale: ?filter[$gt]=… injects operators when query objects are merged blindly. Fix with allow-list plus parameterized queries.

nodes.label: Header versioning
nodes.rationale: Accept-Version: 1. Cleaner URLs, harder to explore.

nodes.label: Media-type versioning
nodes.rationale: Accept: application/vnd.app.v1+json. Strict, heavy.

nodes.label: URL prefix versioning
nodes.rationale: Most common style for REST JSON APIs: /api/v1/users. Visible, cache-friendly, easy routers. Clearest default for this stack.

nodes.label: Bounded full-text search
nodes.rationale: Search endpoints that hit full-text indexes belong behind explicit q params and timeouts. Do not run unbounded scans on the request thread.

nodes.label: Deprecate with sunset headers
nodes.rationale: Deprecate with docs + sunset headers; do not break v1 silently.

nodes.label: Git ref
nodes.rationale: A ref is a file containing a hash. Namespaces: refs/heads, refs/tags, refs/remotes, refs/stash. Inspectable as text, but a bad hash write is not prevented.

nodes.label: git update-ref
nodes.rationale: Prefer update-ref over editing ref files: it writes the reflog entry recovery depends on.

nodes.label: Delta compression
nodes.rationale: Deltas are chosen by similarity across the repository, not by commit adjacency. Hashes are over content, never the stored form.

nodes.label: Git is not a large-file store
nodes.norm_label: git is not a large-file store

nodes.label: Packing is below the object model
nodes.rationale: 'Git stores diffs' is false of the model and true of bytes on disk. cat-file still returns whole objects.
nodes.norm_label: packing is below the object model

nodes.label: Console API beyond log
nodes.rationale: table, dir({depth:null}), group, time, count, assert, error/warn (stderr). Node log truncates nested objects at depth 2.

nodes.label: DevTools lazy object expansion
nodes.rationale: A logged object is expanded later by reference. structuredClone at log time captures the instant.

nodes.label: node --inspect-brk
nodes.rationale: Breaks on the first line so breakpoints can be set before anything runs. debugger; is a no-op unless a debugger is attached.

nodes.label: Cold versus warm micro-benchmark
nodes.rationale: Same function, same input: cold 0.21ms vs warm 0.0074ms, about 28x. Single-shot timings measure compilation state.

nodes.label: Deoptimisation
nodes.rationale: Optimised code is discarded when a later call violates observed types. Measured: add(a,b) lost optimisation after strings and objects.

nodes.label: V8 compilation tiers
nodes.rationale: Ignition interprets bytecode; Sparkplug is a fast baseline; Maglev mid-tier; TurboFan fully optimises hot type-stable functions.

nodes.label: Keep data shapes stable
nodes.rationale: Do not tune for the JIT. Normalise payloads at the boundary so functions see consistent types and objects share keys in the same order.

nodes.label: Unpolyfillable engine features
nodes.rationale: Proxy, WeakRef, BigInt and real #private fields need engine capabilities that cannot be reconstructed in JavaScript.

nodes.label: Numbers are IEEE-754 doubles
nodes.rationale: One numeric type. 0.1 + 0.2 is 0.30000000000000004 because 0.1 is a repeating binary fraction. Not JS-specific.

nodes.label: JSON.parse corrupts large integer IDs
nodes.rationale: JSON.parse turns numbers into doubles. Send IDs as strings, or recover digits via the reviver ctx.source and BigInt.

nodes.label: Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER
nodes.rationale: 2^53-1 = 9007199254740991. Beyond it distinct integers collapse: MSI+1 === MSI+2.

nodes.label: toFixed is not a rounding function
nodes.rationale: (1.005).toFixed(2) is '1.00' because 1.005 is stored slightly low. It also returns a string.
nodes.norm_label: tofixed is not a rounding function

nodes.label: BigInt
nodes.rationale: Arbitrary-precision integers past 2^53-1. Create from a string for large values; a number literal is already rounded. Division truncates.

nodes.label: Money as integer minor units
nodes.rationale: Store paise or cents. Arithmetic in integers. Round once explicitly. Divide by 100 only when formatting with Intl.NumberFormat.

nodes.label: Signed zero -0
nodes.rationale: IEEE-754 signed zero from underflow, 0*-1, -1/Infinity, Math.round(-0.2). Invisible to ===, includes, String, JSON.stringify. Detect with Object.is(x,-0) or 1/x===-Infinity. Matters for atan2 and Object.is deep-equal.

nodes.label: Object.is (SameValue)
nodes.rationale: Fourth equality algorithm: === with NaN and -0 fixed. Use inside comparison helpers (React, shallowEqual) so NaN fields do not retrigger; keep === for everyday code.

nodes.label: SameValueZero
nodes.rationale: NaN equals NaN; 0 equals -0. Used by includes and Map/Set keys.

nodes.label: Literal rounding above MAX_SAFE_INTEGER
nodes.rationale: Any-base literals above 2^53-1 are rounded at parse time. Use BigInt literals such as 0xffffffffffffffffn.

nodes.label: Literal bases are notation only
nodes.rationale: 0b, 0o, 0x, decimal, and exponent forms all produce number. Only the n suffix changes the type to bigint.

nodes.label: Phase 1 — Values, types and coercion
nodes.rationale: Seventeen topics. Disproportionate bugs come from references vs copies, coercion, and floating point (cart totals).

nodes.label: Phase 1 gate
nodes.rationale: Predict []==false, ''==0, null==undefined from the algorithm, and never store a cart total as 19.99.

nodes.label: JSX {count && <X/>} zero trap
nodes.rationale: 0&&anything is 0 and React renders 0 as text. Force a boolean: count>0&&….

nodes.label: ?? default-value idiom
nodes.rationale: Default to ??. || replaces legitimate 0, '', false. 0??'f' is 0.

nodes.label: Logical operators return operands
nodes.rationale: 'a'&&'b' is 'b'; 0&&'b' is 0. Only ! returns a boolean. Cannot be replaced by a function because that would evaluate both arguments.

nodes.label: ?. with ?? default
nodes.rationale: cart?.items?.[0]?.qty??1 preserves a legitimate 0 unlike ||.

nodes.label: if uses ToBoolean
nodes.rationale: if(stock) treats 0 as absent. Compare explicitly: stock>0 or stock!=null.

nodes.label: Only undefined triggers a default
nodes.rationale: null is a value: greet(null) is 'hi null'. Missing key vs DB NULL are not interchangeable. Use ?? in the body if null should fall back.

nodes.label: Guard clauses
nodes.rationale: Early returns for failures so the happy path is last and unindented. Highest-value refactor for nested ifs.

nodes.label: Keys are string or symbol only
nodes.rationale: Anything else is coerced to a string. o[1] and o['1'] are the same property; two plain objects collide on [object Object]. Map is the answer for identity or non-string keys.
nodes.norm_label: keys are string or symbol only

nodes.label: JSON __proto__ is an ordinary key
nodes.rationale: JSON.parse is safe: __proto__ becomes a plain own property. Pollution happens in a later recursive merge that assigns through Object.prototype's accessor.

nodes.label: Object.create(null) dictionary
nodes.rationale: No inherited keys and no __proto__ accessor. Cost: no toString or hasOwnProperty; string conversion throws. Prefer Map unless you need a plain-object shape.

nodes.label: Prototype pollution
nodes.rationale: Assigning target['__proto__'] from untrusted JSON pollutes Object.prototype for every object, including ones created earlier. Defend with Object.create(null), skip dangerous keys, or defineProperty.

nodes.label: hasOwnProperty
nodes.rationale: Broken on Object.create(null) and on objects that shadow the method. MDN prefers Object.hasOwn. Fallback is Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call.

nodes.label: Object.hasOwn
nodes.rationale: Modern default for data. Own-only, works on null-prototype objects, immune to shadowing, coerces primitives. ES2022 static method.

nodes.label: Map for identity and ordered keys
nodes.rationale: The moment keys are not naturally strings — objects, or numbers you care about as numbers — use a Map. Map is insertion-ordered for every key type.
nodes.norm_label: map for identity and ordered keys

nodes.label: await does not block the thread
nodes.rationale: await suspends the async function, not the thread. It cannot slice a long synchronous computation.
nodes.norm_label: await does not block the thread

nodes.label: await is microtask scheduling
nodes.rationale: Code before the first await is synchronous. await on a non-promise still yields a microtask, never a task, so an await loop still starves rendering.

nodes.label: async function always returns a promise
nodes.rationale: No path out is not a promise. return wraps or adopts; throw becomes a rejection.
nodes.norm_label: async function always returns a promise

nodes.label: async function never throws synchronously
nodes.rationale: try { asyncFn() } without await catches nothing. Synchronous argument checks must live in a non-async wrapper.

nodes.label: return p vs Promise.resolve(p) identity
nodes.rationale: Promise.resolve(p) returns the same native promise; an async function must create its own. Breaks caches keyed by promise reference.

nodes.label: async/await like generators plus promises
nodes.rationale: The function suspends and resumes; the awaited promise decides when. Gain is real try/catch, ordinary loops, and locals instead of threaded handler arguments.

nodes.label: Concurrency vs parallelism
nodes.rationale: Concurrency is several operations in progress; parallelism is simultaneous execution. Promise.all is concurrency; workers are parallelism.

nodes.label: Never-blocking exceptions
nodes.rationale: Atomics.wait over SharedArrayBuffer can halt an agent (dedicated/shared workers only). Sync APIs — readFileSync, execSync, alert, localStorage — stop the world.

nodes.label: Run-to-completion
nodes.rationale: A function cannot be preempted. Buys no locks; costs a frozen UI for any long synchronous job.

nodes.label: Single-threaded JavaScript
nodes.rationale: True of your code, false of the platform. Network, timers, disk, crypto and rendering run elsewhere.

nodes.label: Worker as separate agent
nodes.rationale: Own thread, heap and event loop. Communication is structured-cloned message passing; isolation preserves run-to-completion.

nodes.label: A promise chain is sequential
nodes.rationale: Each link waits for the previous to settle. Chaining independent fetches is an accidental waterfall; Promise.all is the composition tool.

nodes.label: Phase 7 — Asynchronous JavaScript
nodes.rationale: Syllabus centre of gravity: eleven Master topics; if only one phase is finished to Master depth, finish this one.

nodes.label: catch is then(undefined, onRejected)
nodes.rationale: No separate error channel. A rejection is the second argument's turn. catch internally calls then.

nodes.label: catch restores the chain
nodes.rationale: A catch that returns normally fulfils, so later then handlers run. Re-throw to keep failing. A log-only catch swallows the error as undefined.

nodes.label: finally transparency
nodes.rationale: onFinally receives no argument; a return is ignored and the original outcome passes through. A throw or rejected return replaces the outcome, destroying the original error.

nodes.label: then(f, g) is not then(f).catch(g)
nodes.rationale: Two-argument then handles only upstream rejections. A throw inside f rejects the next promise. Trailing catch handles both.

nodes.label: finally is a link, not a clause
nodes.rationale: It runs when the promise it attaches to settles, not at the end of the chain. Transparency means it does not mark a rejection handled.
nodes.norm_label: finally is a link, not a clause

nodes.label: Identity and thrower default handlers
nodes.rationale: Missing onFulfilled is (x) => x; missing onRejected is (x) => { throw x; }. Error propagation is the default thrower firing per link.

nodes.label: Chain error propagation modeled after try
nodes.rationale: Promises catch all errors, even thrown exceptions and programming errors. A TypeError in a handler lands in the same catch as a network failure.
nodes.norm_label: chain error propagation modeled after try

nodes.label: Cart as a state machine
nodes.rationale: Immutable updates, derived totals; the total is computed rather than stored.

nodes.label: Idempotency from the client
nodes.rationale: Disabling the button is not a fix for a double-submitted checkout.

nodes.label: Phase 18 — Building the store front end
nodes.rationale: Framework-free on purpose. When React's version breaks at 2 a.m., you know what it was doing.
nodes.norm_label: phase 18 — building the store front end

nodes.label: URL as the single source of truth
nodes.norm_label: url as the single source of truth

nodes.label: Odd/even LTS rule ends at v27
nodes.norm_label: odd/even lts rule ends at v27

nodes.label: v27 one major per year, every release LTS
nodes.rationale: The odd/even unstable vs stable rule ends with v27. October 2026 is when the v27 alpha opens, not when v27 ships.
nodes.norm_label: v27 one major per year, every release lts

nodes.label: Arrow this is a free variable
nodes.rationale: Lookup finds the nearest ordinary function; object literals are not scopes so method arrows see module undefined.
nodes.norm_label: arrow this is a free variable

nodes.label: Function declaration hoisting
nodes.rationale: Name and body exist from the top of the scope, even after return.

nodes.label: Function expression TDZ vs var TypeError
nodes.rationale: const/let throw Cannot access before initialization; var f is undefined so the call is TypeError.
nodes.norm_label: function expression tdz vs var typeerror

nodes.label: Inferred function .name
nodes.rationale: Assignment targets name the function; only an unbound expression has name === "".

nodes.label: Named function expression inner binding
nodes.rationale: inner is visible only inside the body, giving a recursion handle that survives reassignment.

nodes.label: Block-level function declarations
nodes.rationale: Strict: block-scoped and hoisted in the block. Sloppy: Annex B, engine-dependent, even if (false).

nodes.label: Parameter list TDZ
nodes.rationale: Defaults initialise left to right; a = b, b = 2 throws Cannot access 'b' before initialization.

nodes.label: Parameter scope is parent of body
nodes.rationale: Defaults cannot see body functions or var; a default closure captures the parameter, not a shadowed body var.
nodes.norm_label: parameter scope is parent of body

nodes.label: Scope-entry bindings
nodes.rationale: function starts callable; var starts undefined; let/const/class start empty; import is usable after side effects.

nodes.label: Temporal dead zone
nodes.rationale: A stretch of time after the binding exists and before initialisation; not a region of source.

nodes.label: Lexical scoping
nodes.rationale: Lookup walks outward at write time; this is what makes closures possible.

nodes.label: Closures
nodes.rationale: A function plus the variables it still sees; captures the variable, not the value.

nodes.label: Declarations, expressions and arrow functions
nodes.rationale: Three forms hoist, name, and construct differently; the error string identifies the form.

nodes.label: Block functions and the parameter list
nodes.rationale: Hoisting errors that do not look like hoisting: block-level functions and parameter-list TDZ.
nodes.norm_label: block functions and the parameter list

nodes.label: Hoisting and the temporal dead zone
nodes.rationale: Nothing moves; entering a scope creates every binding. What fills the slot differs by declaration kind.
nodes.norm_label: hoisting and the temporal dead zone

nodes.label: Lexical scope and the scope chain
nodes.rationale: Scope is decided by where code is written, not where it is called.
nodes.norm_label: lexical scope and the scope chain

nodes.label: Parameters
nodes.rationale: The parameter list is its own language: own scope, TDZ, evaluation order, and simple vs non-simple.

nodes.label: Lag is not downstream I/O wait
nodes.rationale: A slow downstream API is I/O wait, not lag. Sync bcrypt, image resize, GC thrash, and stdout backpressure do show up as lag.
nodes.norm_label: lag is not downstream i/o wait

nodes.label: High lag plus high CPU
nodes.rationale: Sync JS, crypto, or JSON on the loop. Profile and move work off the request path.

nodes.label: Low lag plus high p99
nodes.rationale: Waiting on I/O or a queue, not blocking the event loop. Look at downstream and pool wait times. CPU profiles show idle.

nodes.label: --cpu-prof
nodes.rationale: Samples during the run and writes .cpuprofile on exit. Hard kill (-9) skips flush. Wrong tool when lag is low and you are I/O bound.

nodes.label: Node Inspector --inspect
nodes.rationale: Live CPU/Memory session without waiting for exit. Exposing --inspect on a public IP is a remote code surface — treat like a root shell.

nodes.label: 0x flame graphs
nodes.rationale: Low-ceremony capture plus interactive HTML. Same family of data as --cpu-prof; automates visualization.

nodes.label: Flame graph width is sample time
nodes.rationale: Width is portion of samples in that stack frame subtree. Thin towers or empty app frames often mean I/O wait.
nodes.norm_label: flame graph width is sample time

nodes.label: Startup probe
nodes.rationale: Optional. Has boot finished? Wait; do not kill yet. Same checks as readiness, but only during boot.

nodes.label: module.enableCompileCache
nodes.rationale: Persists compilation artifacts. Measured status 1 under /tmp/node-compile-cache. Ephemeral /tmp in Kubernetes gives no cross-restart benefit.

nodes.label: Lazy imports
nodes.rationale: Eager slows boot, speeds first request. Lazy speeds boot, moves cost to first use. Eager-import the hot path.

nodes.label: Time to readiness
nodes.rationale: Measure the full ready path — load config, import routes, connect DB, listen — not only import time. DNS to Postgres can be 80% of the wait.

nodes.label: Parallel independent connects
nodes.rationale: Promise.all for Redis and Postgres is fine if both are required before ready. Optional deps can degrade without blocking ready.

nodes.label: Validate, connect, listen, ready
nodes.rationale: Validate env, connect dependencies, start listening, then report ready. Listening early is the bug.

nodes.label: Health checks — liveness vs readiness
nodes.rationale: Conflating liveness and readiness is how a temporary dependency blip becomes a restart storm.

nodes.label: heapUsed
nodes.rationale: V8 heap currently live. Climbing over hours with flat traffic is the leak signal. heapTotal growth then plateau is reservation, not a leak.

nodes.label: RSS resident set
nodes.rationale: Pages in RAM including heap, stacks, code, native addons. Alert on RSS and cgroup memory for Kubernetes OOM risk, not V8's opinion.

nodes.label: v8.getHeapStatistics
nodes.rationale: Default heap_size_limit ~4288 MB here. With --max-old-space-size=256 the reported limit was 448 MB, not 256.

nodes.label: Rising heapUsed under stable load
nodes.rationale: Live set not returning after GC. Growth that tracks traffic may be a working set or a poorly intended unbounded cache.

nodes.label: cgroup OOM vs V8 heap OOM
nodes.rationale: Kernel kills on container RSS including off-heap. Align the flag and container limits; watch RSS.
nodes.norm_label: cgroup oom vs v8 heap oom

nodes.label: heap_size_limit vs flag value
nodes.rationale: Default limit ~4288 MB; --max-old-space-size=256 produced ~448 MB. The limit includes more than old space.

nodes.label: --max-old-space-size
nodes.rationale: Roughly the old-space heap budget. Hitting it yields heap OOM; it is not a cgroup RSS limit. Too high on a small container lets the kernel OOMKiller fire first.

nodes.label: In-process vs Redis cache
nodes.rationale: In-process is fastest and per pod; after scale-out you have N independent caches. Redis is shared, networked, operational.

nodes.label: Heap snapshot
nodes.rationale: v8.writeHeapSnapshot returns a string path. Take two snapshots minutes apart under the same load and diff retained size.

nodes.label: Retainer path
nodes.rationale: The reference chain to a GC root. That path is the bug: something pushed and never removed.

nodes.label: Unbounded cache leak
nodes.rationale: Module-level Map with no max or TTL. Bound by count and bytes; LRU or Redis maxmemory.

nodes.label: --heap-prof
nodes.rationale: Allocation timeline-style profile. For what is retained right now, prefer heap snapshots.

nodes.label: Clinic.js suite
nodes.rationale: Doctor for triage (CPU vs I/O vs memory), Flame for CPU, Bubbleprof for async delay, Heapprofiler for allocation views. On-demand or canary, not every prod pod.

nodes.label: Flame graphs
nodes.rationale: Stacked picture of where CPU samples landed. Use when a CPU profile's call table is hard to see.

nodes.label: Microtask queue
nodes.rationale: Promise.then, await resumptions and queueMicrotask. Drains after nextTick at a checkpoint, but once inside a microtask the microtask queue keeps draining first.

nodes.label: await is a microtask yield
nodes.rationale: Body runs synchronously until the first await; resumption is a microtask. Does not yield to timers or I/O. await setImmediate() is the real phase yield.

nodes.label: CPU-bound work
nodes.rationale: Busy work (JSON.parse of 50MB, image resize, bcrypt sync, ReDoS) holds the single thread. Waiting I/O is fine. Node's genuine weakness; the fix is never async.

nodes.label: await yields to the microtask queue
nodes.rationale: await does not give the event loop a turn. An await-heavy loop over in-memory values never runs timers or I/O; CPU-bound work needs setImmediate, a real phase.
nodes.norm_label: await yields to the microtask queue

nodes.label: Event loop delay cannot detect starvation
nodes.rationale: The metric is sampled by a timer, and timers never run while starved. Use --cpu-prof or attach the inspector instead.
nodes.norm_label: event loop delay cannot detect starvation

nodes.label: async does not stop blocking
nodes.rationale: async changes the return value, not whether the body blocks. There is no await that makes a for loop yield.

nodes.label: Event loop delay misses a fully blocked loop
nodes.rationale: Sampled by a timer that cannot fire while blocked. A 1.2s block reported worst gap 0ms because it recorded no samples. Missing data is the signal.
nodes.norm_label: event loop delay misses a fully blocked loop

nodes.label: util.callbackify
nodes.rationale: Hands an async function to a callback consumer. Rare in apps; for libraries keeping a callback API over promises.

nodes.label: Error-first callback convention
nodes.rationale: cb(err) or cb(null, value), exactly once, always asynchronously. Mixed sync/async firing is why you defer early returns with process.nextTick.

nodes.label: util.promisify
nodes.rationale: Assumes last argument is error-first (err, value) called once. Multiple success values, wrong this, or non-standard shape need a manual wrapper or promisify.custom.

nodes.label: util.promisify.custom
nodes.rationale: Author-defined promise form when the mechanical translation is wrong. promisify checks that symbol first.

nodes.label: Explicit construction antipattern
nodes.rationale: Wrapping an already-promise API in new Promise adds a forgotten-reject path and a never-settling promise. new Promise belongs only around callback or event APIs.

nodes.label: new Promise only wraps callback APIs
nodes.rationale: The one legitimate use of the Promise constructor. Prefer built-in fs/promises, dns/promises, timers/promises, stream/promises over promisify.
nodes.norm_label: new promise only wraps callback apis

nodes.label: Readable stream
nodes.rationale: Source: for await, pipe/pipeline, or events. Mixing consumers loses data. Paused mode is pull — backpressure comes free.

nodes.label: Readable.from
nodes.rationale: Turns an array, iterable, or async generator into a stream. Replaces most custom Readables.

nodes.label: Async generator pipeline stage
nodes.rationale: Same backpressure and error propagation with no callback contract. Write a class when you need a reusable object, _writev, _destroy, or custom hwm.

nodes.label: Readable.from high water mark 1
nodes.rationale: Object mode on, hwm 1 so a generator wrapping a paged API does not prefetch.

nodes.label: Custom Readable _read
nodes.rationale: _read is a request: eventually push or push(null). push() false means stop. Never throw — this.destroy(err). Never call _read yourself.

nodes.label: Readable.from string special case
nodes.rationale: Strings and Buffers emit as one chunk, not per character. Other iterables emit one chunk per element.

nodes.label: Prefer Readable.from over a class
nodes.rationale: Write the class only for pull control, _writev batching, or _destroy cleanup. Generators have no _read/callback contract.

nodes.label: for await of Readable
nodes.rationale: Default way to read a stream: backpressure, try/catch errors, automatic cleanup. Next chunk is requested only when the loop body finishes.

nodes.label: Readable iterator helpers
nodes.rationale: map, filter, take, reduce, toArray and more since v17. Stability 1 Experimental in Node 24. map/filter accept { concurrency }.

nodes.label: stream/consumers
nodes.rationale: text, json, buffer, arrayBuffer, blob collect a whole stream. No size limit of their own — never point at unbounded input.

nodes.label: Transform is sequential
nodes.rationale: One chunk at a time preserves order and forbids parallelism. Concurrent work belongs on readable.map({ concurrency }) or a bounded pool.

nodes.label: break destroys the stream
nodes.rationale: break, return and throw call the iterator return(), which destroys the stream. It cannot be resumed.

nodes.label: on data async has no backpressure
nodes.rationale: .on() ignores the returned promise, so the source keeps emitting while every handler runs concurrently.
nodes.norm_label: on data async has no backpressure

nodes.label: consumers impose no size limit
nodes.rationale: await json(req) will buffer a 2 GB body. Size-limit first, then collect.

nodes.label: Mongo session.withTransaction
nodes.rationale: Retries the callback on transient errors, so it must be idempotent. Omitting {session} commits outside the transaction with no warning.

nodes.label: Migration system four parts
nodes.rationale: Ordered files, schema_migrations ledger, advisory lock before reading the ledger, one transaction per file, plus checksums.

nodes.label: pg_advisory_lock
nodes.rationale: Session lock on a fixed key. Second deploy waited 1306 ms then found nothing to do. Must be taken before reading the ledger.

nodes.label: Advisory lock for clustered schedules
nodes.rationale: pg_try_advisory_lock on a checked-out client. pool.query can hand the same session so both instances report true.

nodes.label: pool.query BEGIN bug
nodes.rationale: Each pool.query takes a free connection. Concurrent flows scatter; one flow's ROLLBACK can run on another's connection. Quiet processes hide it.

nodes.label: One tool owns schema and pool
nodes.rationale: Do not mix three layers. A second tool for reports means two migration histories and two pools against the same connection budget.
nodes.norm_label: one tool owns schema and pool

nodes.label: PostgreSQL transactional DDL
nodes.rationale: A failed second ALTER rolled back the first. MySQL and Mongo leave half-applied schema; write those migrations idempotent.

nodes.label: One delivery job per webhook subscriber
nodes.rationale: A dispatcher enqueues N jobs. One job looping over subscribers fails as a unit and re-delivers to those that already succeeded.
nodes.norm_label: one delivery job per webhook subscriber

nodes.label: Honour Retry-After
nodes.rationale: If the server tells you when to come back, obey it rather than your own schedule.

nodes.label: Backpressure vs concurrency limiting
nodes.rationale: Limiting bounds work you initiate; backpressure bounds work pushed at you. A job queue is backpressure — backlog sits in Redis/Postgres, not the process.

nodes.label: Count the product of limits
nodes.rationale: Limit 10 inside concurrency 5 across 4 processes is 200 against one database. Match the scarcest resource, usually below pool.max.

nodes.label: mapLimit worker pool
nodes.rationale: N runners pull a shared cursor. next++ must be synchronous or two runners claim the same index. Measured peak 8 vs 200.

nodes.label: Unbounded Promise.all
nodes.rationale: map starts everything; all only waits. 200 items peaked at 200 in-flight. Exhausts the pool, overruns APIs, and holds every pending result.

nodes.label: Why an index is not used
nodes.norm_label: why an index is not used

nodes.label: Phase 10 — Indexes and the query planner
nodes.norm_label: phase 10 — indexes and the query planner

nodes.label: Fake
nodes.rationale: Working simplified implementation. Best when several tests need the collaborator to actually work. Drift risk — back with one integration test against the real thing.

nodes.label: Transaction per test rollback
nodes.rationale: BEGIN in beforeEach, ROLLBACK in afterEach, pass the checked-out client. Faster than truncate-and-reseed. Fails for code that manages its own transactions.

nodes.label: Testcontainers — real database integration tests
nodes.rationale: Verified 2026-08: testcontainers 12.1.0, pg 8.23.0, postgres:18-alpine, rootless podman 5.8.4.

nodes.label: Runner flags worth knowing
nodes.rationale: Verified 2026-08 on Node 24.19.0. Several flags find bugs in the suite; two can make a broken suite report green.

nodes.label: Snapshot testing
nodes.rationale: Verified 2026-08 on Node 24.19.0. t.assert.snapshot() needs no flag on this version.

nodes.label: ESLint flat config, Prettier, or Biome
nodes.rationale: Verified 2026-08: eslint 10.8.1, prettier 3.9.6, @biomejs/biome 2.5.8 on Node 24.19.0.
nodes.norm_label: eslint flat config, prettier, or biome

nodes.label: Property-based and mutation testing
nodes.rationale: Verified 2026-08: fast-check 4.9.0, @stryker-mutator/core 9.6.1 on Node 24.19.0.

nodes.label: pool.query BEGIN bug
nodes.rationale: Idle pool luck: all three statements share one connection. Under load BEGIN, UPDATE and ROLLBACK hit backends 1055/1056/1056 — the update autocommits and a stray open transaction remains.

nodes.label: withTransaction helper
nodes.rationale: One client from pool.connect(); ROLLBACK.catch to avoid masking; release() in finally. Isolation goes on BEGIN, not SET after the first query (25001).

nodes.label: Bounded retry with jitter
nodes.rationale: Unbounded retry is livelock; no jitter collides in lockstep. Cap attempts; backoff with jitter. Retry 40001 and 40P01 only.

nodes.label: Optimistic version column
nodes.rationale: WHERE version = $2; rowCount 0 means retry. Right for think-time / cross-request edits. Worst under single-row contention: 170 retries, 337.4 ms.

nodes.label: withSerializable retry loop
nodes.rationale: Re-run the whole transaction; retry 40001/40P01 only; bound attempts; jitter; no external side effects. Sleep after release, never inside catch before finally.

nodes.label: Transaction cost is connection-seconds
nodes.rationale: A transaction holds a connection for its entire duration. Do not open it across HTTP calls; that exhausts the pool and stalls VACUUM.

nodes.label: Never await while holding a pooled client
nodes.rationale: Sleeping in catch before finally pins a connection while idle and turns a retry storm into a pool shortage.
nodes.norm_label: never await while holding a pooled client

nodes.label: Automatically updatable view
nodes.rationale: One table, no aggregate, DISTINCT, GROUP BY, window, or set operation. Otherwise 55000 and an INSTEAD OF trigger is required.

nodes.label: WITH CHECK OPTION
nodes.rationale: Without it a write can insert a row that immediately vanishes from the view. With it the insert raises 44000.

nodes.label: Matview staleness is yours to manage
nodes.rationale: Nothing refreshes it. Prefer a scheduled refresh. A trigger-driven full recompute inside a write is almost always wrong.
nodes.norm_label: matview staleness is yours to manage

nodes.label: Triggers maintain data not behaviour
nodes.rationale: Invisible from the application: right for updated_at and audit, wrong for business rules or external side effects inside the transaction.

nodes.label: Dead tuples vs autovacuum pace
nodes.rationale: Rising n_dead_tup with recent last_autovacuum means not keeping pace (tune per-table scale_factor). Old or NULL last_autovacuum means blocked by a long-open transaction.

nodes.label: VACUUM silent skip without MAINTAIN
nodes.rationale: Missing MAINTAIN privilege: VACUUM warns, skips the table, and exits successfully. Nightly jobs that lost their grant never fail.

nodes.label: pg_stat_user_tables
nodes.rationale: One row per table: seq_scan, idx_scan, n_live_tup, n_dead_tup, last_autovacuum, write mix. Cheap, approximate, for trends and triage.

nodes.label: Unused indexes via idx_scan = 0
nodes.rationale: Exclude unique/PK. Check stats_reset, replica stats, and idx_scan lag before DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY.

nodes.label: Batched backfill with SKIP LOCKED
nodes.rationale: LIMIT + ORDER BY + FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, commit per batch, pause so autovacuum keeps up. One huge UPDATE bloats and loses work on failure.

nodes.label: Table health
nodes.rationale: Views that tell you something is wrong before anyone notices: dead tuples, unused indexes, whether autovacuum is keeping up.

nodes.label: High seq_scan is a hint not a verdict
nodes.rationale: Sequential scans are often optimal for small tables or queries that touch most rows. Treat them as EXPLAIN candidates; adding an index can make a query slower.
nodes.norm_label: high seq_scan is a hint not a verdict

nodes.label: Three questions three views
nodes.rationale: Now = pg_stat_activity/pg_locks; aggregate cost = pg_stat_statements; quietly worse = pg_stat_user_tables/pg_stat_database.

nodes.label: log_min_duration_statement
nodes.rationale: Default -1 disabled. 1000 ms is a web starting point. Sample the merely-slow band with log_min_duration_sample + log_statement_sample_rate.

nodes.label: auto_explain
nodes.rationale: Logs the plan at the moment a query was slow. Load via shared_preload_libraries (restart), session_preload_libraries, or LOAD.

nodes.label: Monitoring three-legged stool
nodes.rationale: pg_stat_activity (now), pg_stat_statements (aggregate), the log (which execution was slow). Production wants all three.

nodes.label: Monitoring views
nodes.rationale: Three questions, three views: live activity, aggregate cost, and quiet deterioration. Using the wrong view spends an outage reading averages.

nodes.label: Logging slow queries
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL logs almost nothing useful by default, and the one setting people turn on leaks secrets.

nodes.label: auto_explain.log_analyze instruments every statement
nodes.rationale: Docs warn of extremely negative impact: per-node timing applies to all statements, not only logged ones. Mitigate with log_timing=off or sample_rate; enable only while investigating.

nodes.label: ADD COLUMN constant default is catalog-only
nodes.rationale: Since PG 11 a non-volatile default is stored in metadata. Volatile defaults, identity, stored generated, and constrained domains still rewrite.
nodes.norm_label: add column constant default is catalog-only

nodes.label: VALIDATE CONSTRAINT uses SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE
nodes.rationale: Does not block reads or writes. ADD FOREIGN KEY is SHARE ROW EXCLUSIVE and still blocks writes on both tables.
nodes.norm_label: validate constraint uses share update exclusive

nodes.label: Expand and contract
nodes.rationale: Expand additively, migrate data and dual-write, contract later. Every deploy compatible with schema before and after; every migration compatible with code before and after.

nodes.label: SET NOT NULL via validated CHECK
nodes.rationale: CHECK (col IS NOT NULL) NOT VALID → VALIDATE → SET NOT NULL. Since PG 12 the validated check lets SET NOT NULL skip its ACCESS EXCLUSIVE scan.
nodes.norm_label: set not null via validated check

nodes.label: NOT VALID then VALIDATE CONSTRAINT
nodes.rationale: Skips the lengthy scan; new rows are enforced immediately. Do not leave convalidated=false indefinitely.

nodes.label: Never rename a column in one step
nodes.rationale: No instant when old and new code agree on the name. Add, dual-write, backfill, switch reads, drop later. Same for int→bigint.
nodes.norm_label: never rename a column in one step

nodes.label: Schema change and code deploy are never simultaneous
nodes.rationale: During a rolling deploy old and new code share one schema. Never remove in the same step that adds a replacement.
nodes.norm_label: schema change and code deploy are never simultaneous

nodes.label: Transactional DDL holds locks until commit
nodes.rationale: One transaction wrapping five ALTERs holds the first ACCESS EXCLUSIVE for all five. Split scans/rewrites. CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY cannot run in a transaction.
nodes.norm_label: transactional ddl holds locks until commit

nodes.label: CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY
nodes.rationale: No write-blocking lock. Cannot run in a transaction. Scans twice and waits for existing transactions. Slower than a regular build.

nodes.label: Direct vs pooled endpoints
nodes.rationale: Wrong endpoint fails only under load. Serverless uses pooled; migrations, LISTEN/NOTIFY and admin use direct.

nodes.label: Neon pooled endpoint via PgBouncer
nodes.rationale: Hostname token -pooler. transaction pool_mode, up to 10k clients. Protocol-level prepared statements supported (PgBouncer 1.21+).

nodes.label: Serverless connection pattern
nodes.rationale: Always pooled endpoint; module-scope pool; max 1–2 per instance; connectionTimeoutMillis set. Optional HTTP driver for one-shot queries.

nodes.label: Supabase Supavisor ports
nodes.rationale: 5432 direct/session, 6543 transaction. Transaction mode does not support prepared statements. Direct is IPv6 by default.

nodes.label: Migrations must use the direct endpoint
nodes.rationale: Need session semantics, advisory locks, and CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY. Transaction-mode poolers produce intermittent failures.
nodes.norm_label: migrations must use the direct endpoint

nodes.label: Provider backups do not make restore yours
nodes.rationale: Provider guarantees a backup exists, not a practised restore, adequate retention, or coverage of a correct-but-wrong-rows migration. Keep pg_dump.
nodes.norm_label: provider backups do not make restore yours

nodes.label: archive_timeout
nodes.rationale: Default 0. Quiet databases may not fill a WAL segment for hours, so last hours are unarchived. Forces a switch and bounds RPO.

nodes.label: Logical vs physical backups
nodes.rationale: Logical: portable, per-table, no PITR, slow restore. Physical: whole cluster, same major/arch, PITR, fast restore. Production wants both.

nodes.label: pg_basebackup -X stream
nodes.rationale: Streams WAL generated during the backup so it is restorable standalone. PG 18 incremental backups recombine with pg_combinebackup.

nodes.label: Point-in-time recovery
nodes.rationale: Restore base backup, replay archived WAL to any later second. Base need not be a consistent snapshot; log replay repairs it like crash recovery.

nodes.label: Base backups and WAL archiving
nodes.rationale: Managed providers do this; you still decide RPO/RTO. Logical restore measured 4× dump because indexes rebuild.

nodes.label: Illusion of delegation
nodes.rationale: Automated backups, failover and instance tuning do not imply durability, availability or performance are handled. Most managed incidents are application-side.

nodes.label: \pset null
nodes.rationale: By default NULL and empty string render identically as blank. Highest-value single .psqlrc line: \pset null '(null)'.

nodes.label: \o and \g redirect
nodes.rationale: \o file is a persistent output mode; \g file is one-shot; \g | cmd pipes. Both write rendered output.

nodes.label: \x expanded output
nodes.rationale: One column per line. \x auto switches only when the row does not fit — the setting to keep in .psqlrc.

nodes.label: psql query buffer
nodes.rationale: SQL is sent only when terminated. Meta-commands execute immediately. A missing semicolon looks like a hang.

nodes.label: \e editor
nodes.rationale: Opens $EDITOR on the buffer. Trailing semicolon executes on save. \ef/\ev fetch a function or view as CREATE OR REPLACE.

nodes.label: \g family
nodes.rationale: ; and \g send the buffer. \gx forces expanded. \gexec executes each returned value as SQL. \gdesc describes columns without running.

nodes.label: psql prompt suffixes
nodes.rationale: =# ready, -# mid-statement, '# unterminated string, (# unbalanced parentheses. Ctrl-C clears the buffer.

nodes.label: UPDATE FROM duplicate-source trap
nodes.rationale: Three candidate prices, rowCount 1, one value chosen arbitrarily. MERGE rejects the same input with 21000. Deduplicate with DISTINCT ON if staying on UPDATE FROM.

nodes.label: DISTINCT ON
nodes.rationale: Keeps the first row per group as ORDER BY produced them, whole row included. PostgreSQL-specific. Index (group, sort) removes the Sort.

nodes.label: DISTINCT ON ORDER BY rule
nodes.rationale: DISTINCT ON expressions must be the leading ORDER BY expressions or 42P10. Omitting ORDER BY is legal and returns an arbitrary row per group.

nodes.label: WITH ORDINALITY
nodes.rationale: Adds a position column to any set-returning function so client array order survives a join.

nodes.label: unnest parallel arrays
nodes.rationale: Column-wise not a cross join. Mismatched lengths pad the short array with NULL, no error. Always cast $1::text[]. Prefer FROM unnest over select-list SRFs.

nodes.label: VALUES as a table expression
nodes.rationale: Needs AS t(cols). Types inferred from the first row. Join a client list without a temp table. Each batch size is a different statement for the plan cache.

nodes.label: Missing FK index audit
nodes.rationale: Query pg_constraint contype='f' for FKs whose leading index columns do not match conkey, requiring indisvalid so a failed CONCURRENTLY build does not count.

nodes.label: Referencing-side FK index
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL indexes the referenced PK/UNIQUE side automatically but never the referencing column. Without that index every parent DELETE scans the child table.

nodes.label: PostgreSQL 18 skip scan
nodes.rationale: Can probe once per distinct leading value when that column has few distincts (Index Searches: 7). Not chosen for 5000-value leading columns.

nodes.label: pg_stat_statements.max dealloc
nodes.rationale: Default 5000 distinct normalised statements. Overflow evicts least-executed; growing dealloc means raise max or stop unparameterised IN-list churn.

nodes.label: pg_stat_statements
nodes.rationale: Ranks statements by total time after normalising literals to $n. Requires shared_preload_libraries and a restart.

nodes.label: shared_preload_libraries
nodes.rationale: pg_stat_statements hooks the executor and must be preloaded. CREATE EXTENSION alone leaves an empty view.

nodes.label: Duplicate indexes
nodes.rationale: Group pg_index by indrelid, indkey, indclass, indexprs, indpred, indisunique. A PRIMARY KEY or UNIQUE already is an index; adding another on the same column is dead weight.

nodes.label: idx_scan
nodes.rationale: How many times the planner chose the index. Zero after a full business cycle is a drop candidate, but exclude UNIQUE, check stats_reset, replicas, and quarterly jobs.

nodes.label: Index
nodes.rationale: A second sorted copy of some columns maintained on every write so some SELECTs can stop scanning. A PRIMARY KEY is already a unique index.

nodes.label: Equality then range column order
nodes.rationale: Put equality predicates first, then the range/sort column. (user_id, created_at) used 23 buffers vs 396 for the reverse order.

nodes.label: Leftmost-prefix rule
nodes.rationale: Index on (a,b,c) serves (a), (a,b), (a,b,c) but not b or c alone. Phone-book order: surname then first name.

nodes.label: total_exec_time ranking
nodes.rationale: Order by total, not mean. A 18 ms query run 500 times (9240 ms) outranks an 87 ms query run twice (173 ms).

nodes.label: stats_fetch_consistency cache
nodes.rationale: idx_scan lags: backends flush on a timer and the reader caches a snapshot. pg_stat_clear_snapshot() plus a wait; never judge unused from seconds-old reads.

nodes.label: Index write cost
nodes.rationale: One index nearly doubled a 200000-row insert (1239→2266 ms); three tripled it (4035 ms) with 36 MB of indexes vs 15 MB heap. Key width, not column count, drives size.

nodes.label: WHEN NOT MATCHED BY SOURCE
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL 17 delete half of a reconcile: target rows the source no longer has. Before 17 this was DELETE WHERE NOT EXISTS.

nodes.label: count(*) vs count(col) after LEFT JOIN
nodes.rationale: count(*) counts the NULL-extended row (5 vs 4). Per group it turns no orders into a count of 1.
nodes.norm_label: count(*) vs count(col) after left join

nodes.label: LEFT JOIN IS NULL anti-join
nodes.rationale: Works if the tested column is NOT NULL. Prefer NOT EXISTS in new code for a dedicated Hash Anti Join.

nodes.label: Manufactured NULLs indistinguishable from stored
nodes.rationale: Test a NOT NULL right-hand column, normally the primary key, to detect unmatched rows.

nodes.label: EXCEPT
nodes.rationale: Compares whole rows, not a key. Prefer anti-join when the question is which entities are missing.

nodes.label: count(*) arrives as a string from pg
nodes.rationale: bigint exceeds JS safe integers. Cast ::int or register a type parser.
nodes.norm_label: count(*) arrives as a string from pg

nodes.label: Emulate FULL OUTER with LEFT plus anti-join UNION ALL
nodes.norm_label: emulate full outer with left plus anti-join union all

nodes.label: FULL OUTER JOIN
nodes.rationale: Keeps unmatched rows from both sides. The reconciliation, migration-verify, and snapshot-diff tool.

nodes.label: FULL JOIN only merge or hash joinable
nodes.rationale: Must track unmatched rows on both sides. Nested loop has no cheap bookkeeping, so inequality FULL JOIN is rejected.
nodes.norm_label: full join only merge or hash joinable

nodes.label: IS DISTINCT FROM for snapshot diffs
nodes.rationale: <> yields NULL when either side is NULL and silently drops the differing row.
nodes.norm_label: is distinct from for snapshot diffs

nodes.label: USING on FULL JOIN coalesces the key
nodes.rationale: Merged column is coalesce(left, right), never NULL for a row present on either side.
nodes.norm_label: using on full join coalesces the key

nodes.label: USING merged join column
nodes.rationale: Requires identical names. SELECT * emits one merged column. On outer joins that column is coalesced.

nodes.label: pg SELECT * duplicate names last-wins
nodes.rationale: Server sent six columns; JS object had four keys. Alias columns or use rowMode array.

nodes.label: 42702 ambiguous column
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL refuses rather than guessing. The dangerous case is an unambiguous column rebound after a later migration.

nodes.label: Output alias usable in ORDER BY and GROUP BY not WHERE
nodes.rationale: WHERE and HAVING run before SELECT so the alias does not exist (42703). GROUP BY accepting it is a PostgreSQL extension.
nodes.norm_label: output alias usable in order by and group by not where

nodes.label: Alias every table and qualify every column
nodes.norm_label: alias every table and qualify every column

nodes.label: DISTINCT runs after windows
nodes.rationale: A window value such as row_number makes every row unique, so SELECT DISTINCT stops de-duplicating. De-duplicate at an inner level first.

nodes.label: dense_rank
nodes.rationale: Ties share a place with no gap (1, 1, 2). Use for distinct score levels rather than sporting position.

nodes.label: ntile
nodes.rationale: Divides into n buckets; remainder goes to earliest buckets (7 into 3 → 3,2,2). Splits ties across boundaries, so unsuitable for grading. Prefer percentile_cont thresholds.

nodes.label: percent_rank
nodes.rationale: (rank - 1) / (rows - 1), always 0 to 1. Sibling cume_dist is the proportion of rows at or before this one.

nodes.label: rank
nodes.rationale: Ties share a place; next value skips the gap (1, 1, 3). max(rank) equals row count, not distinct values. Ranking functions ignore the frame clause.

nodes.label: row_number
nodes.rationale: Consecutive integers; ties broken arbitrarily. Non-deterministic unless ORDER BY is unique. Always add a unique tiebreaker before WHERE rn = 1.

nodes.label: The four ranking functions
nodes.rationale: row_number, rank, dense_rank and percent_rank take no arguments and differ only in tie behaviour.

nodes.label: DISTINCT ON top-1
nodes.rationale: Shortest PostgreSQL-only top-1 per key. Cannot return N > 1. Measured 546.62 ms without index on this table.

nodes.label: LATERAL top-N per group
nodes.rationale: Wins when the driving set is small and each probe is indexed. Timed out at 30s without an index (5000 full scans); 906.59 ms with one. Only form that takes OFFSET per group.

nodes.label: count() is 0, sum() is NULL over empty
nodes.rationale: No rows, a zero total, and a NULL total collapse into two outputs. coalesce when the API wants a number. LEFT JOIN rewrite of count() needs coalesce(o.n, 0) to keep zeros.
nodes.norm_label: count() is 0, sum() is null over empty

nodes.label: SubPlan loops per outer row
nodes.rationale: SubPlan plus loops=5000 is the diagnosis. Rewrite as GROUP BY plus LEFT JOIN unless the outer set is small by construction or the planner already un-correlated it.

nodes.label: Top-N per group
nodes.rationale: Three shapes: row_number + filter, DISTINCT ON (top-1), LATERAL LIMIT. Winner depends on group count versus table size.

nodes.label: Correlated subquery
nodes.rationale: References an outer column, so it cannot be computed once. An N+1 written inside one statement: no round trips, same shape of work.

nodes.label: Correlated cost coupled to visibility map
nodes.rationale: Best case 145 ms vs GROUP BY 65 ms (2.2×). After stale visibility map 414 ms vs 90 ms (4.6×); Heap Fetches 0 → 133359. Do not benchmark on a freshly vacuumed table.
nodes.norm_label: correlated cost coupled to visibility map

nodes.label: Archive pattern
nodes.rationale: WITH moved AS (DELETE … RETURNING *) INSERT INTO archive SELECT * FROM moved. No moment the row exists in neither table or both. Also upsert-plus-audit via xmax = 0.

nodes.label: Unreferenced write CTE still runs
nodes.rationale: A SELECT CTE nobody references can be discarded; a write is a promised side effect and executes exactly once. Delete the CTE, not just the reference.

nodes.label: Sibling SELECT cannot see the write
nodes.rationale: Measured visible_to_sibling 0, visible_via_returning 1, and 1 row present afterwards. Re-read the table and you get the world before the statement started.
nodes.norm_label: sibling select cannot see the write

nodes.label: Two CTEs writing the same row
nodes.rationale: No error: a reported 1, b reported 0, final value 1. SERIALIZABLE does not help — one transaction. Merge into one UPDATE, disjoint WHERE, or separate statements. MERGE would raise 21000 for the analogous mistake.
nodes.norm_label: two ctes writing the same row

nodes.label: One statement, several writes
nodes.rationale: A CTE may contain INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE or MERGE. With RETURNING feeding the next step, a move-then-record is one atomic statement and one round trip.

nodes.label: The snapshot rule
nodes.rationale: Every part of one statement sees the same pre-statement snapshot. Sibling writes are invisible except via RETURNING. Makes the result independent of unspecified CTE order.

nodes.label: When a transaction beats one multi-CTE write
