nodes.rationale: Use BEGIN when a later step must read an earlier write, the branch is in application code, the same rows are written twice, or the work should be batched. Constraints still fail the whole statement.
nodes.norm_label: when a transaction beats one multi-cte write

nodes.label: count(*) OVER ()
nodes.rationale: One-query total. Measured 152.77 ms — three times a separate count(*). WindowAgg must see every matching row before emitting the first, so LIMIT cannot stop early.

nodes.label: Exact count(*)
nodes.rationale: A second query returning the exact total. Measured 48.83 ms vs 2.11 ms for the page (~23×) over 125000 matching rows. Scales with matches; the page stays bounded by LIMIT. Required only for a numbered pager.

nodes.label: Planner row estimate
nodes.rationale: EXPLAIN (FORMAT JSON) Plan Rows is free and was 125833 vs actual 125000 (0.7% high) here. Accuracy is not guaranteed: multi-column filters, correlated columns, and stale statistics can miss by orders of magnitude. Label it approximate.

nodes.label: reltuples
nodes.rationale: Approximate whole-table row count in pg_class, maintained by VACUUM/ANALYZE. Good for order of magnitude; stale between maintenance; never for a user-reconciled total.

nodes.label: Counting for pagination
nodes.rationale: The page is cheap; the total is not. Decide which question the list endpoint is actually being asked. Work down the four-answer list, not up it.

nodes.label: limit + 1 has-more
nodes.rationale: Fetch pageSize+1; if the extra row arrives there is another page, then slice it off. Measured 2.10 ms vs 2.11 ms for the plain page — free and exact. Cannot render Page 1 of N. Classic bug: forgetting to slice so the last page returns 21 items.

nodes.label: WindowAgg defeats LIMIT
nodes.rationale: count(*) OVER () is unknown until the last matching row. Plan showed WindowAgg actual rows=125000 feeding a Limit of 20. You pay a full scan and carry the total on every returned row.

nodes.label: idle_in_transaction_session_timeout
nodes.rationale: Kills a session that is open but idle. Protects VACUUM xmin and locks. Arrives as a Client error event, not a rejected query.

nodes.label: pool.on error handler
nodes.rationale: FATAL with no in-flight query emits an unhandled error event and kills Node. Mandatory for idle-in-transaction termination.

nodes.label: pg-cursor streaming
nodes.rationale: Fetches in batches so memory stops depending on row count. Needs a checked-out client, read(n) until empty, close then release.

nodes.label: pool.query buffers the whole result
nodes.rationale: Heap grew +101 MB for 300000 rows, linear in result size. First row waits for the last.

nodes.label: DECLARE cursor dies on COMMIT
nodes.rationale: FETCH after COMMIT is 34000. WITH HOLD materialises the whole result at commit. pg-cursor uses a protocol portal with the same binding.

nodes.label: Long cursor snapshot pins xmin
nodes.rationale: A twenty-minute export is twenty minutes of no VACUUM database-wide. Hidden cost of streaming.

nodes.label: Keyset batching instead of a cursor
nodes.rationale: Each LIMIT chunk is its own short transaction on a pooled connection. Interruptible, no long snapshot. Sees rows committed during the run.
nodes.norm_label: keyset batching instead of a cursor

nodes.label: ADD COLUMN DEFAULT no rewrite
nodes.rationale: Since PostgreSQL 11, ADD COLUMN NOT NULL DEFAULT is O(1); relfilenode unchanged. Changing a column type usually rewrites.

nodes.label: ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock
nodes.rationale: ALTER TABLE takes ACCESS EXCLUSIVE, which conflicts with every mode including ACCESS SHARE from SELECT.

nodes.label: DDL lock queue pile-up
nodes.rationale: A 12 ms ALTER queued behind a long read blocked later SELECTs for 2.4 s because locks are granted in request order.

nodes.label: lock_timeout for migrations
nodes.rationale: SET lock_timeout fails with 55P03 instead of stalling the table. statement_timeout is not a substitute because a lock wait is not executing.

nodes.label: NOWAIT vs SKIP LOCKED
nodes.rationale: NOWAIT raises 55P03. SKIP LOCKED omits locked rows and is wrong for a point lookup. lock_timeout also raises 55P03 with a different message.

nodes.label: Where DDL belongs
nodes.rationale: Numbered recorded migrations are the normal way. ensureSchema at startup races and is unversioned. DDL in a request handler takes ACCESS EXCLUSIVE on a live table.

nodes.label: Phase 8 gate
nodes.rationale: Move on when you can migrate forward-only and seed idempotently without runtime DDL in requests.

nodes.label: Unreleased client leak
nodes.rationale: With max 2, the third call timed out after 1501 ms. pool.end() never resolves while a client is stranded. release() belongs in finally.

nodes.label: Executor contract
nodes.rationale: Every repository function takes db as first argument. Never import the pool. BoundPool and Client are interchangeable at the .query() surface.

nodes.label: pool.query vs held client
nodes.rationale: pool.query checks out, runs one statement, releases. Consecutive calls may be different sessions. A client shares a transaction.

nodes.label: AsyncLocalStorage ambient client
nodes.rationale: Removes the argument so forgetting db is impossible. ?? pool silently autocommits when async context is lost; missing store should throw.

nodes.label: Pass db through every layer
nodes.rationale: Only the outermost layer names pool. A service that opens its own transaction cannot be composed.

nodes.label: Pool handed instead of client
nodes.rationale: After ROLLBACK, orders=0 items=1. Different backend pids, no PostgreSQL error. Half the request committed.

nodes.label: Tests must inject the executor
nodes.rationale: Code using pool.query cannot see uncommitted fixtures. The harness enforces the executor contract.

nodes.label: innerHTML XSS surface (img onerror, iframe srcdoc)
nodes.norm_label: innerhtml xss surface (img onerror, iframe srcdoc)

nodes.label: null/undefined/true/false render nothing; 0 and NaN render
nodes.norm_label: null/undefined/true/false render nothing; 0 and nan render

nodes.label: Objects are not valid as a React child (#31)
nodes.norm_label: objects are not valid as a react child (#31)

nodes.label: who owns the value (props vs local state)
nodes.norm_label: who owns the value (props vs local state)

nodes.label: react package
nodes.rationale: Knows components, elements, state and hooks; document.createElement does not occur in the package.

nodes.label: React Native
nodes.rationale: Learn once, write anywhere — not write once, run anywhere. Hooks transfer; host elements and styling do not.

nodes.label: react / react-dom version-match rule
nodes.rationale: The packages share private internals that are not a stable API; mismatch is undefined behaviour.

nodes.label: Renderer host config
nodes.rationale: react never learns what a node is; a renderer supplies createInstance, appendChild, commitUpdate and about thirty more.

nodes.label: Four disguises of unstable identity
nodes.rationale: Local arrows, HOCs in render, and memo or lazy called during render. A map of module-level components is safe.

nodes.label: Wrapper hell
nodes.rationale: Composing several render-prop components nests JSX and closures until the code is unreadable. Custom hooks were introduced to solve this.

nodes.label: Never apply a HOC during render
nodes.rationale: A new enhanced type each render makes React unmount and remount the subtree, losing all state. Same nesting-rule bug.
nodes.norm_label: never apply a hoc during render

nodes.label: HOC prop collisions are silent
nodes.rationale: Injected names collide by spread order with no warning. Wrapper stacks hide where a prop came from.

nodes.label: HOC refs and React 19
nodes.rationale: Before 19, ref was not a prop so spreads dropped it. Function-component HOCs that spread props now forward ref automatically. Class instance refs and React 18 still need forwardRef.

nodes.label: Hooks replaced render props
nodes.rationale: Hooks share logic without extra tree nodes, make values usable anywhere in the component, and compose linearly instead of nesting.

nodes.label: Higher-order component
nodes.rationale: A function that takes a component and returns a new one by wrapping, not mutating. Apply at module level, once.

nodes.label: Synchronize with an external system
nodes.rationale: If you are not synchronizing with a browser API, widget, network, or non-React component, you probably do not need an Effect.

nodes.label: Effect Events are non-reactive
nodes.rationale: They always see the latest values, but their execution does not re-run the surrounding Effect. Theme can style a notification without reconnecting chat.

nodes.label: Move 6 — extract an Effect Event
nodes.rationale: Read isMuted or an inline callback prop without reacting to it. Muting should not reconnect the chat.

nodes.label: Effects versus events
nodes.rationale: Effects are caused by rendering itself. Events are caused by a particular interaction. If why names a user action, it is a handler.

nodes.label: Share handler logic with a plain function
nodes.rationale: Hoisting shared follow-up into an effect fires it on mount and every product change, so a user already in-cart sees Added on page load.
nodes.norm_label: share handler logic with a plain function

nodes.label: Displayed versus interaction test
nodes.rationale: Code that runs because a component was displayed belongs in Effects; the rest belongs in events.

nodes.label: Effect Event identity is intentionally unstable
nodes.rationale: A runtime assertion: put it in a dependency array and the effect re-runs every render. Never wrap it in useCallback.
nodes.norm_label: effect event identity is intentionally unstable

nodes.label: Actions
nodes.rationale: A function passed to form action. React calls it with FormData, wraps it in a transition, tracks pending state, and resets on success.

nodes.label: Server Components
nodes.rationale: Runs only on the server; code never reaches the browser. No state, effects, event handlers, or browser APIs — and it can be async.

nodes.label: Suspense
nodes.rationale: A component threw a promise React knows about. A plain fetch inside useEffect cannot suspend no matter how many boundaries wrap it.

nodes.label: 'use client' directive
nodes.rationale: Marks an entry point into the client graph, not 'this file is a component'. Everything it imports goes to the browser too.

nodes.label: 'use server' directive
nodes.rationale: Marks a Server Function and has nothing to do with Server Components. Every Server Function is a public HTTP endpoint.

nodes.label: Error boundaries
nodes.rationale: Still class-only in 19.2.8 via getDerivedStateFromError and componentDidCatch. Do not catch event handlers, timeouts, or SSR errors.

nodes.label: Session advisory lock pool leak
nodes.rationale: pg_try_advisory_lock on a pooled client plus client.release() without destroy returns a connection that still holds the lock.

nodes.label: Merge join needs equality
nodes.rationale: A pure range ON clause is nested loop only. Merge join requires mergejoinable btree equality operators.

nodes.label: SET cannot take bind parameters
nodes.rationale: SET LOCAL TIME ZONE $1 fails 42601. Replacement is SELECT set_config($1, $2, true).

nodes.label: XID wraparound warning threshold
nodes.rationale: Warning is near 2.13 billion, not 1 billion. Page on autovacuum_freeze_max_age (200 million), not the wrap warning.

nodes.label: Review work order
nodes.rationale: The work-order table is the point: executable top to bottom by someone who has not read the pages.

nodes.label: checkJs project-wide
nodes.rationale: "checkJs": true checks every .js in the project. Inverse // @ts-nocheck opts one file out. Needs allowJs.

nodes.label: JSDoc type annotations
nodes.rationale: @param, @returns, @type, @typedef, @template, and import('./x.js').T cover ordinary application code. Conditional, mapped, and satisfies types get unreadable.

nodes.label: // @ts-check
nodes.rationale: First comment at the top of a .js file turns the checker on for that file. Types come from JSDoc. Same TS2345 as TypeScript; Node still runs the file unchanged.

nodes.label: Phase 0 How TypeScript runs
nodes.rationale: 13 pages before syntax: what the tool is, what it leaves behind, and which of the three programs that accept .ts actually reads the types.

nodes.label: strict defaults to true in TypeScript 7
nodes.rationale: Measured: no-flag was not a loose baseline. esModuleInterop and moduleResolution changed defaults too.
nodes.norm_label: strict defaults to true in typescript 7

nodes.label: tsc emits broken JavaScript by default
nodes.rationale: tsc emits rejected JS and exits 2. --noEmitOnError and --noEmit exit 1. Ignoring the exit code ships output the compiler already rejected.
nodes.norm_label: tsc emits broken javascript by default

nodes.label: JSDoc checking vs converting to .ts
nodes.rationale: JSDoc costs no build or rename; converting gives the full language. If types get hard to write in JSDoc, that file wants to be TypeScript.

nodes.label: TypeScript Playground
nodes.rationale: Isolation: reproduce without local tsconfig/@types/editor version, toggle one option, compare compiler versions, inspect emitted JS, share a runnable link.

nodes.label: readonly T[]
nodes.rationale: Removes mutating methods from the type; does not freeze at runtime. T[] assigns to readonly T[], not the reverse. Better parameter type for non-mutating functions.

nodes.label: Object.freeze
nodes.rationale: The only runtime guarantee. Also shallow. Most codebases rely on readonly for intent; freeze when a runtime write must throw.

nodes.label: readonly
nodes.rationale: Compile-time promise only. Stops assignments the checker can see. Erased at runtime and bypassed by as. readonly items: T[] blocks replacement; items: readonly T[] blocks mutation.

nodes.label: readonly is shallow
nodes.rationale: Readonly<T> maps top-level properties only. c.db.host still mutates. Deep immutability needs a recursive type and costs compile time and error quality.

nodes.label: Erasure as the foundation fact
nodes.rationale: Types are deleted and never checked at runtime. Once internalised, enum reputation, erasableSyntaxOnly, runtime validation, and why a green bundler proves nothing stop being separate facts.

nodes.label: readonly T[] parameter
nodes.rationale: T[] assigns to readonly T[] but not the reverse. Declaring readonly accepts both kinds and documents that the function does not mutate.

nodes.label: The six Map vs object differences
nodes.norm_label: the six map vs object differences

nodes.label: Control flow and choosing a loop
nodes.norm_label: control flow and choosing a loop

nodes.label: CSS debugging order
nodes.rationale: In order: is the element in the DOM, did the rule parse, did it match ($0.matches), did it win (strike-through/Computed), is the box where you think (Layout).

nodes.label: DevTools as the CSS error console
nodes.rationale: Because CSS reports nothing, the Styles pane is the error console the language lacks. Inspect first: which rules match, which declarations lost.
nodes.norm_label: devtools as the css error console

nodes.label: Struck-through declaration: two causes
nodes.rationale: Cascade loss (winner in Computed) versus parse failure (warning triangle, property missing from Computed). Opposite fixes: specificity/layer vs syntax.

nodes.label: CSSOM
nodes.rationale: The live object model a stylesheet is parsed into (document.styleSheets / cssRules). The engine consults this, not the authored text; malformed rules silently vanish from the count.

nodes.label: CSS as a declarative constraint language
nodes.rationale: CSS states claims about elements; the engine finds the one winning value per property. There is no execution order or call stack, so you debug by asking which rules matched and which won.
nodes.norm_label: css as a declarative constraint language

nodes.label: Parse-time value normalization
nodes.rationale: Authored text is not retained: #ff0000 becomes rgb(), padding/border shorthands expand to longhands, and unspecified longhands get defaults such as currentcolor.

nodes.label: @import serializes stylesheet requests
nodes.rationale: The imported file is undiscoverable until the importer is parsed. Measured at 500 ms delay: chained @import FCP 1076 ms vs parallel links 636 ms.

nodes.label: Four ways CSS reaches the page
nodes.rationale: link (default, cacheable, parallel), style (critical CSS, cached with HTML), inline style (script-computed values), and @import (avoid in delivered CSS).
nodes.norm_label: four ways css reaches the page

nodes.label: CSS at-rule map
nodes.rationale: About a dozen at-rules worth knowing: @media/@container, @supports, @layer, @scope, @property, @font-face, @keyframes, @starting-style, @page, @counter-style, @import.

nodes.label: Block vs statement at-rules
nodes.rationale: Block forms wrap rules and nest; statement forms end at a semicolon. @layer has both: @layer a, b; declares order, @layer a { } fills a layer. First mention sets order.

nodes.label: Unknown at-rule drops its whole block
nodes.rationale: An unrecognized at-rule is discarded silently with every rule inside it. Base styling must live outside recent at-rules; enhancement only goes inside.
nodes.norm_label: unknown at-rule drops its whole block

nodes.label: Inline style as a cascade decision
nodes.rationale: A normal inline declaration beats every author rule except author !important. Prefer setting a custom property inline and consuming it from a stylesheet.
nodes.norm_label: inline style as a cascade decision

nodes.label: JavaScript host
nodes.rationale: A language feature works everywhere the engine is new enough. A host feature works only where that host provides it.

nodes.label: ECMA-262 spec
nodes.rationale: The spec has no I/O. A conforming engine can compute a value but cannot show it.

nodes.label: Hoisting
nodes.rationale: Not code moving. Bindings are registered in the compile pass; values arrive in execute.

nodes.label: Temporal dead zone
nodes.rationale: A TDZ binding exists but has no value. typeof on it throws; typeof on a never-declared name returns undefined.

nodes.label: await tears down the stack frame
nodes.norm_label: await tears down the stack frame

nodes.label: V8 does not implement tail-call optimisation
nodes.norm_label: v8 does not implement tail-call optimisation

nodes.label: Stack limit is bytes not calls
nodes.rationale: Measured 12524 frames with no locals versus 5442 with six args plus an array local on Node 24.
nodes.norm_label: stack limit is bytes not calls

nodes.label: Strict mode rules
nodes.rationale: Turns silent sloppy failures into errors. ES modules and class bodies are strict always.

nodes.label: this is undefined in a strict plain call
nodes.rationale: undefined this fails at the mistake. sloppy this === globalThis silently corrupts globals.
nodes.norm_label: this is undefined in a strict plain call

nodes.label: TC39 stage process
nodes.rationale: Stage 3 is when engines ship and risk remains. Stage 4 is two implementations plus tests. Never build on Stage 2 or below.

nodes.label: Capability detection
nodes.rationale: Test the capability with a real operation. Safari private mode defines localStorage then throws on setItem.

nodes.label: The engine, the runtime and the spec
nodes.norm_label: the engine, the runtime and the spec

nodes.label: Execution contexts and the call stack
nodes.norm_label: execution contexts and the call stack

nodes.label: Engines implement proposals not editions
nodes.rationale: The useful question is the runtime floor, not ES6. Editions are yearly snapshots of already-finished proposals.

nodes.label: 300-line cap is file size not content budget
nodes.rationale: Write the explanation first, then split on a concept boundary. A Master topic may run 900–1400 lines across chunks.
nodes.norm_label: 300-line cap is file size not content budget

nodes.label: Event loop split language vs Node
nodes.rationale: Job queue, microtasks and promise resolution live in JS Phase 7. libuv phases, setImmediate and process.nextTick belong to Node Phase 2.
nodes.norm_label: event loop split language vs node

nodes.label: Network split at the wire
nodes.rationale: fetch, AbortController, FormData and console CORS failures are JS Phase 11. Status-code design and server headers belong to Express.

nodes.label: __dirname versus process.cwd
nodes.rationale: Relative paths resolve against the current working directory, not the file that contains them. Use __dirname or import.meta.dirname for files that ship with the code.

nodes.label: process.exit versus process.exitCode
nodes.rationale: process.exit is immediate and abandons pending work. Set exitCode and let the event loop drain.

nodes.label: process.env values are always strings
nodes.rationale: DEBUG=false is the truthy string 'false'. Convert at the edge, once, and validate at startup.

nodes.label: SIGTERM graceful shutdown
nodes.rationale: SIGTERM is what Docker and Kubernetes send before they kill you. Without a handler, in-flight requests are dropped on every deploy.

nodes.label: Pin the version in the repo
nodes.rationale: .nvmrc, engines, a pinned Dockerfile tag, and CI reading the same file. Anything relying on a person remembering will drift.
nodes.norm_label: pin the version in the repo

nodes.label: --env-file
nodes.rationale: A variable already in the environment wins. No variable expansion. A missing file is a hard error unless --env-file-if-exists is used.

nodes.label: Node flags must come before the script name
nodes.rationale: A misplaced flag is silently ignored rather than rejected. Confirm with process.execArgv.
nodes.norm_label: node flags must come before the script name

nodes.label: NODE_OPTIONS
nodes.rationale: Flags that decide what to run (--eval, --print, --test, --env-file) are rejected so an inherited variable cannot hijack every Node process.

nodes.label: Node.js 24 Active LTS
nodes.rationale: Build on Node 24 LTS in production; Node 26 to learn what's next. Maintained through 30 Apr 2028.

nodes.label: Run the Active LTS in production
nodes.rationale: The rule is whatever is Active LTS, not whatever is newest. Feature set is frozen and it receives backported fixes for 30 months from release.
nodes.norm_label: run the active lts in production

nodes.label: Four CSS combinators
nodes.rationale: Descendant (any depth), child >, next sibling +, subsequent sibling ~. Descendant leaks into nested components; child breaks on extra wrappers.

nodes.label: Owl selector * + *
nodes.rationale: .flow > * + * applies spacing to every child except the first because + requires a preceding sibling. Vertical rhythm without a :first-child exception.

nodes.label: Selectors evaluate right-to-left
nodes.rationale: The engine finds the key (rightmost) selector then walks left. main * is heavier than main > .thing because the candidate set is every element.

nodes.label: :has() parent and previous-sibling selector
nodes.rationale: Styles an element from descendants or later siblings. Baseline Widely since 2023-12-19. p:has(+ p) is a previous-sibling selector CSS could not express before.

nodes.label: :has() restrictions and cost
nodes.rationale: No :has() inside :has(); no pseudo-elements in the argument; unforgiving. Upward invalidation: 8× a class at 5000 rows (1.25 ms) — still cheaper than the JS it replaces except on huge subjects that change every frame.

nodes.label: :empty whitespace trap
nodes.rationale: Requires no child nodes at all. A space or newline is a text node so pretty-printed HTML rarely matches. Comments do not count. Prefer :not(:has(*)) when it fails.

nodes.label: Custom properties cross shadow
nodes.rationale: Inherited properties including all custom properties pass the boundary — the primary theming API.

nodes.label: :host and :host-context()
nodes.rationale: :host styles the component element; :host-context() matches when an ancestor matches, for theme adaptation.

nodes.label: Page beats :host
nodes.rationale: A page rule on the host element wins over the shadow stylesheet's :host regardless of specificity; shadow :host is a default.

nodes.label: ::part()
nodes.rationale: Component opts an element in for outside styling; descendants stay private — ::part(header) .title does not work.

nodes.label: ::slotted()
nodes.rationale: Styles top-level light-DOM slotted nodes only; page rules win because those nodes belong to the light tree.

nodes.label: Shadow DOM style boundary
nodes.rationale: Selectors do not cross a shadow root in either direction; that is real encapsulation unlike CSS Modules or @scope.

nodes.label: Built-in Express middleware
nodes.rationale: Express ships json, urlencoded, static, raw/text, and Router. Application settings are not middleware.

nodes.label: Content-Type gates parsers
nodes.rationale: Parsers skip bodies they do not claim. Per-route parsers avoid parsing huge bodies on routes that never need them.

nodes.label: express.json()
nodes.rationale: Populates req.body only when Content-Type is JSON it understands. Wrong type skips the parser; body stays undefined, not automatic 415.

nodes.label: express.urlencoded()
nodes.rationale: HTML form posts. extended:false uses querystring; true uses qs for nested objects. Mount only what clients send.

nodes.label: express.raw() for webhooks
nodes.rationale: JSON parsing destroys exact bytes. HMAC webhooks need express.raw so signatures verify over the original Buffer.

nodes.label: First body consumer wins the stream
nodes.rationale: Global express.json() before a route-level raw parser leaves the hook with an empty or re-serialized body. Mount raw on /webhooks/* first.
nodes.norm_label: first body consumer wins the stream

nodes.label: query parser extended
nodes.rationale: app.set('query parser', 'extended') restores qs nested objects. Nested parsing plus object merge historically enabled prototype-pollution payloads.

nodes.label: Express 5 query parser simple
nodes.rationale: Express 5 defaults query parser to simple. Nested bracket queries stay literal keys, not objects.

nodes.label: req.body needs a parser
nodes.rationale: No parser → no body. No cookie-parser → no cookies object. Writing cookies still uses res.cookie.

nodes.label: req.originalUrl
nodes.rationale: Full original path including mount and query — useful behind routers.

nodes.label: req anatomy
nodes.rationale: req is Node IncomingMessage plus Express fields. method, url, path, params, query, headers are routing-time; body/cookies/user need middleware.

nodes.label: Prefer flat public query params
nodes.rationale: simple is the safer default. Never pass raw req.query into Mongo/SQL builders even if extended is on.

nodes.label: Controller layer
nodes.rationale: Parse/validate input already on req, call service, map status. Does not own SQL or business rules.

nodes.label: Repository layer
nodes.rationale: Queries/commands via drivers. Does not decide HTTP status. Driver types do not leak upward.

nodes.label: Service layer
nodes.rationale: Owns invariants and orchestration. No res.json, no Express types.

nodes.label: createApp(deps)
nodes.rationale: Phase 10 completes composition with createApp(deps). Tests substitute fakes; boot order stays explicit.

nodes.label: Router factory DI
nodes.rationale: Pass dependencies into router factories. Do not import a global db singleton from every file if you care about tests.

nodes.label: Keep Express types out of services
nodes.rationale: Services stay testable without spinning an HTTP server. Express owns where the HTTP layer stops.
nodes.norm_label: keep express types out of services

nodes.label: A branch is 41 bytes and zero new objects
nodes.rationale: Measured with wc -c and an unchanged object count — the concrete reason branching is free.
nodes.norm_label: a branch is 41 bytes and zero new objects

nodes.label: Detached HEAD
nodes.rationale: HEAD holds a raw hash. New commits advance HEAD only. Switching away abandons them unless you branch first.

nodes.label: Ref
nodes.rationale: A file containing a hash. refs/heads/* move on commit; refs/tags/* never move; refs/remotes/* move on fetch.

nodes.label: reftable backend
nodes.rationale: Opt-in at git init --ref-format=reftable. Default is files plus packed-refs. cat .git/refs/heads/main can fail; rev-parse always works.

nodes.label: HEAD is a symbolic ref
nodes.rationale: Usually contains ref: refs/heads/<branch>. git rev-parse follows HEAD → branch file → commit.

nodes.label: HEAD snapshot
nodes.rationale: The snapshot of the last commit on the current branch, reached via .git/HEAD.

nodes.label: Reflog
nodes.rationale: logs/ records every ref movement. Local, not pushed, expires 90/30 days. Enabled by logallrefupdates = true.

nodes.label: reset --soft --mixed --hard
nodes.rationale: All move HEAD. --mixed also resets the index. --hard also overwrites the working tree and is the only variant that can lose uncommitted work.

nodes.label: Part 2 — Working with other people
nodes.rationale: Phases 4–6 · 47 topics · 15 Master. Exists because someone else has commits you do not.

nodes.label: Phase 4 — Remotes and syncing
nodes.rationale: origin is a named URL; fetch vs pull; divergence refuses to guess; --force-with-lease and --force-if-includes.

nodes.label: Phase 5 — Undo, recover and rewrite
nodes.rationale: Framing question: has anyone else seen these commits? reset vs revert vs reflog.

nodes.label: Phase 6 — Team workflow and code review
nodes.rationale: None of this is enforced by Git. Merge, squash, or rebase-merge is a one-time team decision.
nodes.norm_label: phase 6 — team workflow and code review

nodes.label: fetch is a host API
nodes.rationale: Not in ECMA-262. Node 18 shipped it via undici for portability. An older Node lacking it is a host-version problem.

nodes.label: setTimeout is a host API
nodes.rationale: Not in ECMA-262. HTML spec in browsers, separately by Node. A bare engine has no timers.

nodes.label: Spec, engine and host
nodes.rationale: ECMA-262 has no I/O. A language feature works wherever the engine is new enough; a host feature works only where that host provides it.

nodes.label: Shared web-platform surface
nodes.rationale: fetch, URL, AbortController, structuredClone, Intl, crypto, TextEncoder work in browser, worker, Node 24 and edge. Shared modules must stay on this list.

nodes.label: Default Array.sort string compare
nodes.rationale: [10, 9, 1].sort() is [1, 10, 9] because SortCompare stringifies. Specified, not a quirk.

nodes.label: ECMA-262 living standard
nodes.rationale: Read tc39.es/ecma262, not a numbered edition PDF. Host APIs are in WHATWG and Node docs, not ECMA-262.

nodes.label: The process object and exit codes
nodes.norm_label: the process object and exit codes

nodes.label: for...in walks the prototype chain
nodes.rationale: for...in walks the prototype chain and yields string indices on arrays.

nodes.label: class desugaring
nodes.rationale: class is not magic; it desugars onto the prototype chain.

nodes.label: The prototype chain
nodes.rationale: Phase gate: draw the prototype chain for a subclass instance and explain what super.method() looks up.

nodes.label: The iteration protocols
nodes.rationale: Symbol.iterator is a well-known-symbol-keyed method. Phase gate: write a generator that yields pages and consume it with for await...of.

nodes.label: __proto__ colon form
nodes.rationale: Dedicated creation-time syntax that sets [[Prototype]] and creates no property. Shorthand {__proto__} and computed {["__proto__"]:v} are ordinary properties. Non-object/non-null x is a silent no-op.

nodes.label: Prototype pollution
nodes.rationale: JSON.parse is not the hole — "__proto__" is a normal own key in JSON. Recursive merge that assigns target["__proto__"] hits Object.prototype's accessor and pollutes every object, including ones created earlier.

nodes.label: [[Prototype]] internal slot
nodes.rationale: Not a property. Read with Object.getPrototypeOf. obj.__proto__ is a deprecated accessor inherited from Object.prototype, so it is absent on null-prototype objects.

nodes.label: Object.create
nodes.rationale: Sets [[Prototype]] with no constructor call. Second-argument descriptors default every flag to false — silent read-only unless stated.

nodes.label: Object.setPrototypeOf
nodes.rationale: Engines specialise access on the creation-time chain; changing it de-optimises compiled code. Prefer {__proto__: proto} or Object.create at creation. Deep chains tax every miss.

nodes.label: JSON.parse
nodes.rationale: SyntaxError on trailing commas, single quotes, empty bodies. The parse itself is safe from prototype pollution; the merge afterwards is not.

nodes.label: Blue/green deploy
nodes.rationale: Two full environments; rollback is a second flip if sessions and schemas allow.

nodes.label: Canary deploy
nodes.rationale: Needs real golden-signal metrics, not only pods ready; include write paths in the canary mix.

nodes.label: Serverless Node — cold starts, connection reuse
nodes.norm_label: serverless node — cold starts, connection reuse

nodes.label: Expand/contract migrations
nodes.rationale: Old and new code run together in canary/rolling; incompatible schema breaks one colour.

nodes.label: FileHandle.stat
nodes.rationale: Stats the open descriptor, not the path, so it cannot race with a rename. Closes the Content-Length race.

nodes.label: Hard link
nodes.rationale: Second name for the same inode; one filesystem only. nlink>1 means delete may not free space until the last name and last fd are gone.

nodes.label: ino + dev identity
nodes.rationale: How you tell two paths are the same file. Path strings cannot see hard links, bind mounts, or case-insensitive filesystems.

nodes.label: lstat
nodes.rationale: Does not follow. Identifies links and is the only one that works on a broken symlink. Use it before deletion.

nodes.label: stat
nodes.rationale: Follows symlinks and describes the target. Never reports isSymbolicLink()===true; throws ENOENT on a broken link.

nodes.label: Serve file over HTTP
nodes.rationale: stat first (404 before headers), Content-Length from stat().size, pipeline with AbortSignal, treat ERR_STREAM_PREMATURE_CLOSE as normal.

nodes.label: util.parseArgs
nodes.rationale: Core CLI parser. No number type, no generated help, no subcommands. Strict mode throws on unknown options.

nodes.label: Content-Security-Policy
nodes.rationale: A CSP with unsafe-inline in script-src is not a CSP. Roll out via Report-Only first.

nodes.label: JSON in a script tag breakout
nodes.norm_label: json in a script tag breakout

nodes.label: Cross-site scripting
nodes.rationale: An encoding bug, not a filtering bug. Encode on output for the known context.

nodes.label: Mutation score
nodes.rationale: Not a target to chase. Equivalent mutants and log-message mutations are not worth killing. 100% is as suspect as 100% coverage.

nodes.label: Mutation testing
nodes.rationale: Asks whether tests actually check anything. Surviving mutants at a >= boundary showed 100% line coverage still missed the comparison.

nodes.label: Property-based testing
nodes.rationale: Asks whether there are inputs you did not think of. If a property finds nothing, question the generator before concluding the code is correct.

nodes.label: inet_server_port vs published port
nodes.rationale: inet_server_port() is the listen port inside the container (5432), not the host-published port (55432).

nodes.label: 127.0.0.1 and published port 55432
nodes.rationale: Node resolves localhost to ::1 first; IPv4 publishes fail. Non-default 55432:5432 avoids colliding with a host Postgres on 5432.

nodes.label: Five-year major support
nodes.rationale: A new major roughly once a year; each major is supported about five years. Upgrade minors promptly; treat majors as a project.

nodes.label: Major vs minor version
nodes.rationale: 17→18 needs pg_upgrade, dump/restore, or logical replication. 18.3→18.4 is the same on-disk major: install and restart.

nodes.label: server_version_num 180004
nodes.rationale: 180004 means major 18, minor 4. Gate multi-major app code with version_num; pin postgres:18-alpine.

nodes.label: Container-first local Postgres
nodes.rationale: Pin major (postgres:18-alpine), reset in one command, match CI. Prefer that over a host distro package until you need native.

nodes.label: BRIN index
nodes.rationale: Stores min/max per 128-page range; 24 kB vs 64 MB B-tree on 3 M ordered rows. A filter not a lookup — always a bitmap scan with recheck. Useless when physical correlation is near 0.

nodes.label: GiST index
nodes.rationale: A framework for predicates with no total order: overlap, containment, distance. Backs exclusion constraints; serves <-> ordering that GIN cannot.

nodes.label: Hash index
nodes.rationale: Equality only; 16 MB vs 28 MB B-tree here. Cannot UNIQUE (0A000), ranges, INCLUDE, or index-only scans. WAL-logged and crash-safe since PostgreSQL 10.

nodes.label: pg_stats.correlation
nodes.rationale: Check before creating BRIN. Near 1 or −1 is excellent; measured 0.0119 on shuffled data and the planner ignored the index.

nodes.label: ANALYZE
nodes.rationale: The planner looks at a sample, not the data. A table analyzed at 2000 rows and grown to 402000 estimated 1 row of 400001 and took 157 ms instead of 58 ms. Last statement of every bulk load.

nodes.label: Autoanalyze threshold
nodes.rationale: Fires at threshold + scale_factor × reltuples — 50 + 10% by default. On a 10-million-row table that is a million modifications; lower scale_factor to 0.01 on large tables.

nodes.label: default_statistics_target
nodes.rationale: Histogram buckets and most-common-values. Raise per column, not globally: 101 buckets at 100, 1001 at 1000, ANALYZE 1309 ms.

nodes.label: Extended statistics
nodes.rationale: Per-column stats assume independence and multiply selectivities. CREATE STATISTICS (dependencies, ndistinct) moved 33607 → 100990 against an actual 100000. Must be created by hand and take effect only after ANALYZE.

nodes.label: Autovacuum threshold
nodes.rationale: 50 + 0.2 × live_rows. 90000 live → 18050 dead. A 10-million-row table waits for two million dead rows. Override per table, not globally.

nodes.label: Phase 10 — Indexes and the query planner
nodes.norm_label: phase 10 — indexes and the query planner

nodes.label: Specialist indexes vs default B-tree
nodes.rationale: If unsure which applies, the answer is B-tree. BRIN, hash and GiST exist only when you know exactly why the B-tree is wrong.

nodes.label: lock_timeout
nodes.rationale: Bounds wait for a lock without killing a slow-but-progressing query. Prefer SET LOCAL so it does not leak on pooled connections.

nodes.label: ACCESS EXCLUSIVE
nodes.rationale: Most DDL takes this lock; it conflicts with everything including SELECT.

nodes.label: Metadata-only DDL
nodes.rationale: ADD COLUMN with a constant default is catalog-only since PG 11 (2.0 ms on 200k rows). Volatile defaults and non-coercible type changes rewrite the table.

nodes.label: VACUUM FULL
nodes.rationale: Rewrites the table under ACCESS EXCLUSIVE and returns space. Use only after a permanent shrink; pg_repack is the live-table answer.

nodes.label: DDL lock queue
nodes.rationale: A waiting ALTER blocks later SELECTs even though ACCESS SHARE is compatible with the current holder. How a 2 ms ADD COLUMN takes a site down.

nodes.label: Safe DDL migration pattern
nodes.rationale: SET lock_timeout then retry. Split rewrites into a short lock plus unlocked backfill (NOT VALID then VALIDATE, CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY).

nodes.label: pg_stat_replication LSN stages
nodes.rationale: flush_lsn is durability; replay_lsn is visibility. Replication separates the two.

nodes.label: Read-your-writes
nodes.rationale: Async replicas do not provide the guarantee that a client sees its own committed writes.

nodes.label: Replica read routing hierarchy
nodes.rationale: Reads that feed writes belong on the primary; a stale replica read of a balance before a debit is a correctness bug.

nodes.label: bigint identity primary key
nodes.rationale: Sequential appends stay on the rightmost leaf. Smaller, faster, readable. Common pattern: bigint PK plus a uuid unique column for public ids.

nodes.label: uuid v4 (random)
nodes.rationale: Random PK: 1727 ms / 8552 kB index vs bigint 947 ms / 4408 kB on 200k inserts. Scatters B-tree writes and splits pages half-empty.

nodes.label: uuidv7() time-ordered
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL 18 built-in. First 48 bits are a millisecond timestamp, recovering locality (1356 ms / 6184 kB) but leaking creation time via uuid_extract_timestamp().

nodes.label: Volatile DEFAULT rewrites the table
nodes.rationale: gen_random_uuid() needs a distinct value per row — 902 ms rewrite. Add nullable, batch-backfill, then set default and NOT NULL.

nodes.label: GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY vs serial
nodes.rationale: ALWAYS rejects a manual id with 428C9, preventing the sequence from drifting out of step.
nodes.norm_label: generated always as identity vs serial

nodes.label: Never store UUID as text
nodes.rationale: 16 bytes as uuid vs 40 as text, plus string comparison and no format validation. pg sends uuid as a string; invalid values fail with 22P02.

nodes.label: Batched backfill
nodes.rationale: One UPDATE over millions holds row locks, huge WAL, and VACUUM's horizon. Batches of a few thousand commit separately.

nodes.label: Constant DEFAULT add is catalog-only
nodes.rationale: Since PostgreSQL 11 a constant default is stored once and applied on read — 4 ms at 200k rows. Old three-step dance is obsolete for constants.

nodes.label: NOT VALID then VALIDATE CONSTRAINT
nodes.rationale: CHECK (col IS NOT NULL) NOT VALID is 3 ms ACCESS EXCLUSIVE; VALIDATE is 25 ms under SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE so reads/writes continue. Then SET NOT NULL can use the CHECK as proof (PG 12+).

nodes.label: ALTER TABLE ACCESS EXCLUSIVE
nodes.rationale: Every ALTER takes ACCESS EXCLUSIVE. A 3 ms change can outage if it queues behind a long read; later queries queue behind it. Use SET LOCAL lock_timeout.

nodes.label: Add-backfill-swap type change
nodes.rationale: Add new column, batch-backfill, keep current with a trigger, then drop/rename in a short lock_timeout transaction. Interruptible unlike one ALTER TYPE.

nodes.label: ALTER TABLE rewrite vs catalog-only
nodes.rationale: relfilenode change means rewrite. int→bigint, narrowing varchar, volatile DEFAULT, SET LOGGED/UNLOGGED rewrite; widening varchar, DROP COLUMN, varchar→text do not.

nodes.label: Database-per-tenant
nodes.rationale: Rare: tens of large tenants needing strict isolation and resource limits. Pooling multiplies; onboarding is provisioning; no cross-tenant SQL.

nodes.label: Schema-per-tenant
nodes.rationale: Right when isolation is contractual, schemas genuinely differ, or per-tenant restore is routine. Cost: N migrations, UNION reports, growing catalog, safety-critical search_path.

nodes.label: Tenancy decision order
nodes.rationale: Contractual isolation first, then tenant count (thousands force shared), then cross-tenant query frequency, then genuine schema variation. Default shared + RLS.

nodes.label: Tenant deletion and erasure
nodes.rationale: Separated: DROP SCHEMA/DATABASE CASCADE. Shared: DELETE in FK order, generate table list from information_schema, or ON DELETE CASCADE. Backups retain data for the retention window.

nodes.label: Tenant onboarding
nodes.rationale: Shared: INSERT (ms). Schema: CREATE SCHEMA + N migrations (seconds–minutes). Database: provision + pool. Self-serve signup makes the latter a product constraint.

nodes.label: Shared → separated is reversible
nodes.rationale: Filter by tenant_id and copy out. Separated → shared remaps colliding identities everywhere. Start shared when the requirement is uncertain.

nodes.label: col = ANY($1::type[])
nodes.rationale: One array parameter replaces a generated IN list and avoids the NOT IN NULL trap.

nodes.label: NOT IN with NULL
nodes.rationale: One NULL in the list makes every row unknown. Prefer NOT EXISTS for subqueries.

nodes.label: join_collapse_limit
nodes.rationale: Default 8. Past that the planner stops enumerating orders and written join order starts to matter.

nodes.label: Multi-table joins
nodes.rationale: Joins chain left to right. Inner joins may be reordered; an outer join is not, so a later INNER JOIN cancels a LEFT JOIN.

nodes.label: Junction table
nodes.rationale: Composite PK (a_id, b_id) enforces pair uniqueness and indexes the first column. Index the second FK for the reverse lookup.

nodes.label: Has-all-tags relational division
nodes.rationale: IN is has-any. Restrict, GROUP BY parent, HAVING count(DISTINCT tag_id) = cardinality($1).

nodes.label: LEFT JOIN guarantee
nodes.rationale: Every left row appears at least once, not exactly once. Unmatched left rows are emitted with manufactured right-side NULLs. Fan-out still applies.

nodes.label: ON vs WHERE on outer joins
nodes.rationale: For inner joins interchangeable. For outer joins, a right-table predicate in WHERE silently converts the join back to inner. Measured 2 rows vs 4.
nodes.norm_label: on vs where on outer joins

nodes.label: Planner rewrites LEFT to Hash Join
nodes.rationale: EXPLAIN showing Hash Join where the query says LEFT JOIN means a WHERE predicate made NULL-extended rows unreachable. The node name is the diagnosis.
nodes.norm_label: planner rewrites left to hash join

nodes.label: RIGHT JOIN
nodes.rationale: RIGHT JOIN is LEFT JOIN with the operands swapped. Prefer LEFT so the preserved table is read first. RIGHT earns its keep only when FROM order is fixed by a generated query, view, or join chain.

nodes.label: Outer-join predicate classification
nodes.rationale: Right-table filters belong in ON; left-table filters belong in WHERE (in ON they do not filter); the join key belongs in ON. A later INNER JOIN or HAVING on the right side also cancels the outer join.

nodes.label: LEFT JOIN IS NULL anti-join idiom
nodes.rationale: WHERE right.pk IS NULL keeps unmatched left rows. Correct if the tested column is NOT NULL; still materialises matching pairs. Prefer NOT EXISTS in new code.
nodes.norm_label: left join is null anti-join idiom

nodes.label: Four anti-join spellings
nodes.rationale: NOT EXISTS (default), LEFT JOIN … WHERE pk IS NULL (older, fragile), EXCEPT (different whole-row semantics), NOT IN (avoid for subqueries).

nodes.label: NOT EXISTS anti join
nodes.rationale: Keeps left rows with no match. Plans as Hash Anti Join. Correct with NULLs because a NULL row simply fails to match.

nodes.label: NOT IN NULL trap
nodes.rationale: x NOT IN (a,b,NULL) expands to x <> a AND x <> b AND x <> NULL. The last conjunct is NULL for any x, so WHERE keeps nothing. One NULL customer_id turned Dee into [].

nodes.label: IN as semi join
nodes.rationale: Positive IN and EXISTS both plan as Parallel Hash Semi Join. Prefer EXISTS when correlated, IN or = ANY($1::int[]) for an independent list.

nodes.label: EXCEPT
nodes.rationale: Whole-row set difference. Answers which rows differ, not which entities are missing. EXCEPT ALL keeps count_left − count_right.

nodes.label: count(DISTINCT)
nodes.rationale: Counts unique non-NULL values; a different question, not a faster count.

nodes.label: DISTINCT subquery rewrite
nodes.rationale: SELECT count(*) FROM (SELECT DISTINCT col …) can unlock a cheaper plan than count(DISTINCT col).

nodes.label: Index-only scan flip
nodes.rationale: A covering index can turn a heap scan count into an index-only scan.

nodes.label: count(DISTINCT) is not parallel
nodes.rationale: The distinct aggregate cannot be parallelized the way a plain count can.

nodes.label: Partial and Finalize Aggregate
nodes.rationale: Parallel plans compute Partial aggregates per worker and Finalize them in the leader.

nodes.label: psql \copy
nodes.rationale: Default to \copy: it trades throughput for reach, needs no server privileges, and is the only option against a managed or containerised database.

nodes.label: \copy TO STDOUT
nodes.rationale: Streams row by row rather than buffering the full result, so it is the right tool for exports larger than memory.

nodes.label: SQL COPY
nodes.rationale: COPY is SQL executed by the server and reads the server filesystem; it needs superuser or pg_read_server_files / pg_write_server_files.

nodes.label: \watch
nodes.rationale: Polls, and polling costs; keep watched queries cheap and prefer count= limits so a forgotten watch cannot poll forever.

nodes.label: \i include
nodes.rationale: Resolves paths against the current working directory; fails when CI runs from the repository root.

nodes.label: \ir include
nodes.rationale: Use \ir for anything a file includes; it nests correctly so a tree of seed scripts can be reorganised without rewriting paths.

nodes.label: psql -At
nodes.rationale: -A drops padding, -t drops header and footer; what remains is exactly the data a Unix filter expects.

nodes.label: \gexec
nodes.rationale: Executes each returned value as SQL; always run the SELECT alone first so a DROP does not reach more tables than intended.

nodes.label: Phase 1 — psql, mastered
nodes.rationale: psql is the verification tool for the rest of the syllabus; master the shell before racing ahead to SQL text.

nodes.label: COPY is one transaction
nodes.rationale: One malformed value rolls back the entire load; a three-row file with one bad value loaded zero rows.

nodes.label: All-text staging table for untrusted CSV
nodes.rationale: Load into text columns then INSERT … SELECT with casts and a filter; there is no skip-bad-rows option except ON_ERROR ignore on PostgreSQL 17+.
nodes.norm_label: all-text staging table for untrusted csv

nodes.label: Seed includes vs migration runner
nodes.rationale: If losing the database is an inconvenience, psql includes are enough; if it is an incident, use a migration runner that records applied versions.

nodes.label: FILTER clause
nodes.rationale: Restricts which rows enter one aggregate without a second scan or a CASE wrapper.

nodes.label: FILTER equals CASE speed
nodes.rationale: FILTER is not faster than the equivalent CASE aggregate; both are one scan.

nodes.label: FILTER vs CASE
nodes.rationale: FILTER and CASE express the same pivot; FILTER is clearer and does not invent zeros the way COALESCE(sum(CASE…),0) can.

nodes.label: FILTER is not a scan filter
nodes.rationale: FILTER does not reduce the scan; WHERE does. FILTER only chooses which already-read rows enter the aggregate.
nodes.norm_label: filter is not a scan filter

nodes.label: client.release()
nodes.rationale: Returns the connection for reuse. Does not close it or roll anything back. Always call it in finally.

nodes.label: pool.connect checkout
nodes.rationale: Takes a connection out of the pool until release(). A fourth request against max 3 queues; leaks present as latency, not exceptions.

nodes.label: Pool totalCount idleCount waitingCount
nodes.rationale: Sustained waitingCount > 0 means undersized pool, slow queries, or a leak. A leak also pins idleCount at 0 with totalCount at max.

nodes.label: password as a function
nodes.rationale: Evaluated when a connection opens, not per query. Pair with idleTimeoutMillis shorter than an IAM token TTL.

nodes.label: client.end() vs release()
nodes.rationale: end() closes a standalone Client. A pooled client from pool.connect() gets release(). Calling end() on a pooled client is a bug.

nodes.label: connectionTimeoutMillis and idleTimeoutMillis
nodes.rationale: connectionTimeoutMillis covers socket open and waiting for a free pooled connection. idleTimeoutMillis should sit below intermediary idle TCP drops.

nodes.label: Long cursor pins xmin horizon
nodes.rationale: A twenty-minute stream is twenty minutes of no VACUUM database-wide. Hidden cost of streaming a large result.

nodes.label: FATAL errors arrive as events
nodes.rationale: When the server terminates a connection with no in-flight query, pg emits 'error' instead of rejecting a promise.

nodes.label: Lazy pool connection
nodes.rationale: new Pool() performs no I/O. A bad host surfaces as ECONNREFUSED on the first query, so boot with SELECT 1.

nodes.label: Module-scope pg.Pool
nodes.rationale: Create one Pool at module scope and share it. Construction opens nothing; the first query opens the first connection.

nodes.label: idle_in_transaction_session_timeout
nodes.rationale: Kills a session that issued BEGIN then waited. Pins xmin and blocks VACUUM. Delivered as an 'error' event, not a rejected query.

nodes.label: pool.on('error') is mandatory
nodes.rationale: An idle connection killed by the server emits 'error' on the pool. Unhandled, that is an uncaught exception that kills the process.

nodes.label: key compiles to a third argument
nodes.norm_label: key compiles to a third argument

nodes.label: index keys keep slots not items
nodes.norm_label: index keys keep slots not items

nodes.label: JSX prop spread is object-literal spread
nodes.norm_label: jsx prop spread is object-literal spread

nodes.label: Named splat /*splat
nodes.rationale: SPA fallbacks that used app.get('*') must move to /*splat or /{*splat} to match the root. req.params.splat is an array of segments, not a string.

nodes.label: Express 5 path-to-regexp rewrite
nodes.rationale: Illegal patterns throw at registration — process fails before any request. Sandbox-measured: app.get('*') Missing parameter name; /user/:id? Unexpected ?; /*splat accepted.

nodes.label: Illegal paths throw at registration
nodes.rationale: Upgrade pain is front-loaded. Broken deploys beat intermittent routing bugs. Not the same as middleware order bugs, which fail at request time.

nodes.label: Express 5 path migration map
nodes.rationale: '*' → /*splat or /{*splat}; /:file.:ext? → /:file{.:ext}; regex alternation → array of paths. Named wildcard yields an array of segments.

nodes.label: Named splat params are arrays
nodes.rationale: Migration guide: {splat: ['foo','bar']}. Request reference: /files/images/image.png → req.params.file = ['images','image.png'].

nodes.label: Static root isolation
nodes.rationale: A static root too high exposes node_modules or .env. Root only the build output directory. Express 5 dotfiles defaults should not serve secrets.

nodes.label: res.attachment
nodes.rationale: Sets Content-Disposition and infers Content-Type from the extension. Must run before the body is sent.

nodes.label: res.download
nodes.rationale: res.sendFile plus Content-Disposition: attachment. Transfers the file as an attachment with a filename you choose.

nodes.label: res.sendFile
nodes.rationale: Serves one file inline on a route. Use when the file is chosen by logic — auth, tenancy, a lookup. Path must be absolute unless root is set. Errors arrive in the callback, not as thrown exceptions.

nodes.label: sendFile root option
nodes.rationale: When root is set, Express validates the relative path resolves within that root — the documented traversal guard. Without it, path.join of client input can escape to ../../etc/passwd.

nodes.label: Signed URL offload
nodes.rationale: When files are large or private, issue a signed URL to object storage. Node then spends no bandwidth, memory, or event-loop time on the transfer.

nodes.label: Commit DAG
nodes.rationale: Directed because parents point one way; acyclic because a commit hash includes its parents; a graph because merges have multiple parents.

nodes.label: Commit dates are metadata not structure
nodes.rationale: A commit dated 2030 can sit under one dated 2026. Never build logic on dates; use ancestry via merge-base --is-ancestor.
nodes.norm_label: commit dates are metadata not structure

nodes.label: Rebase versus merge trade-off
nodes.rationale: A DAG records parallel work honestly. Rebase flattens for readability by rewriting what happened; merge keeps truth at the cost of a harder history.

nodes.label: Author identity required to commit
nodes.rationale: Author and committer are fields inside the commit object, so there is nothing to hash without them. Hard failure, not a warning.

nodes.label: Object hash framing
nodes.rationale: Git hashes type, space, length, NUL, then content. A generic SHA-1 collision is not directly usable as a Git object swap.

nodes.label: Identity is asserted not authenticated
nodes.rationale: user.email is free text. Audit value is the host's push auth; cryptographic proof needs signed commits.

nodes.label: MERGE rowCount is total across branches
nodes.rationale: command is MERGE and rowCount is 3 with no insert/update/delete split. Breakdown needs RETURNING merge_action().
nodes.norm_label: merge rowcount is total across branches

nodes.label: MERGE USING source
nodes.rationale: Source may be a table, subquery, or VALUES. Application rows usually arrive via unnest of array parameters.

nodes.label: WHEN first matching branch wins
nodes.rationale: Order decides the action. A bare WHEN MATCHED before a conditional DELETE swallows every matched row.

nodes.label: merge_action()
nodes.rationale: Returns INSERT, UPDATE or DELETE per row. Legal only in a MERGE RETURNING list; elsewhere raises 42601.

nodes.label: old. and new. in MERGE RETURNING
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL 18 aliases. old.qty is null on INSERT, but a stored NULL looks the same — use merge_action() for the branch.
nodes.norm_label: old. and new. in merge returning

nodes.label: MERGE RETURNING since PostgreSQL 17
nodes.rationale: Widely-repeated advice said MERGE has no RETURNING. Support arrived in 17; this page repeated the false claim until measured.

nodes.label: 21000 MERGE cannot affect row a second time
nodes.rationale: Two source rows match one target. Deduplicate the source first, typically DISTINCT ON (key).
nodes.norm_label: 21000 merge cannot affect row a second time

nodes.label: MERGE availability 15 / 17 / 18
nodes.rationale: MERGE arrived in 15. 17 added RETURNING, merge_action() and WHEN NOT MATCHED BY SOURCE. 18 added old./new. aliases.

nodes.label: MERGE concurrent 23505 or silent duplicate
nodes.rationale: Two transactions can both take NOT MATCHED. Isolation below SERIALIZABLE does not fix it; no unique constraint yields a silent duplicate.

nodes.label: ON CONFLICT is index-arbitrated
nodes.rationale: A unique index is the arbiter so concurrent upserts resolve. MERGE evaluates ON against its snapshot and is not index-arbitrated.

nodes.label: MERGE SQL-standard table sync
nodes.rationale: MERGE inserts, updates and deletes in one pass. It is not a drop-in replacement for ON CONFLICT and is the wrong tool for concurrent upsert.

nodes.label: Phase 4 gate: INSERT RETURNING, UPDATE WHERE, parameterize
nodes.norm_label: phase 4 gate: insert returning, update where, parameterize

nodes.label: ON CONFLICT in request handlers, MERGE in batch jobs
nodes.rationale: Concurrency is the dividing line, not RETURNING. MERGE wins for controlled ETL, DELETE-in-pass, complex WHEN, or portability.
nodes.norm_label: on conflict in request handlers, merge in batch jobs

nodes.label: Syllabus Phase 12 — When Git goes wrong
nodes.norm_label: syllabus phase 12 — when git goes wrong

nodes.label: SHA-1 and SHA-256 do not interoperate
nodes.rationale: No in-place conversion; hosts and tooling assume 40-character hashes. Cryptography is better; ecosystem cost is prohibitive.
nodes.norm_label: sha-1 and sha-256 do not interoperate

nodes.label: Destructuring assignment parentheses
nodes.rationale: ({x,y}=obj) needs parens because a leading { starts a block. Array destructuring needs none.

nodes.label: {} block vs object literal
nodes.rationale: {}+[] as a statement is 0 (empty block then +[]); as an expression is '[object Object]'. Same reason destructuring and arrow object returns need parens.

nodes.label: Expression vs statement
nodes.rationale: Expressions produce a value; statements perform an action. Only expressions are legal where a value is expected.

nodes.label: IIFE needs parentheses
nodes.rationale: function at statement start is a declaration and requires a name. Parens force expression position. Remaining uses: top-level await in non-modules, multi-statement const.

nodes.label: JSX interpolation is expression-only
nodes.rationale: if is a statement, so JSX uses && and ternaries. Arrow ()=>{id:1} parses id: as a label and returns undefined.

nodes.label: Accidental label in arrow body
nodes.rationale: ()=>{id:1} parses id: as a label; no return so undefined. Fix: ()=>({id:1}).

nodes.label: for…of default loop
nodes.rationale: Works on every iterable, supports break/continue/return and await. Get the index via entries().

nodes.label: forEach cannot break or await
nodes.rationale: return exits the callback only. Async forEach ignores the returned promise — silent race. Use for…of or Promise.all(map).

nodes.label: switch fallthrough
nodes.rationale: Without break/return/throw, execution continues. Stacked empty cases are idiomatic. Prefer return over break. Comment non-empty fallthrough.

nodes.label: Labelled break and continue
nodes.rationale: One good use: exit nested loops. Prefer extract-and-return. Second use: break a loop from inside a switch.

nodes.label: Labels are not goto
nodes.rationale: A label can only be targeted by break/continue inside the labelled statement. Cannot jump backwards, into a block, or out of a function.

nodes.label: Exhaustive default that throws
nodes.rationale: Omitted default is a silent no-op. Throw so new statuses are loud; TypeScript never checks pair with this.

nodes.label: Array spread vs object spread
nodes.rationale: [...x] uses Symbol.iterator; {...x} copies own enumerable properties. [...{}] throws; {...['x','y']} yields {"0":"x","1":"y"}.

nodes.label: Spread copies are shallow
nodes.rationale: Nested values stay the same references. Spread each changed level for structural sharing, or structuredClone for a deep copy.

nodes.label: Spread vs rest
nodes.rationale: Same ... syntax, opposite direction. Rest collects on the left of = or in a parameter list; spread expands everywhere else.

nodes.label: delete creates array holes
nodes.rationale: delete arr[1] leaves length 3 and 1 in arr false. map preserves holes. Use splice/filter/toSpliced. Returns true even if the key never existed.

nodes.label: Arrow closes over outer arguments
nodes.rationale: Module-scope arrow: ReferenceError. Nested arrow silently reports the enclosing call's arguments (4 args in, length 2). Use rest.

nodes.label: Arrow functions lack function machinery
nodes.rationale: No own this, arguments, prototype, super, or new.target. new A() is TypeError: A is not a constructor. prototype is undefined.

nodes.label: setTimeout delay is a minimum
nodes.rationale: The callback also waits for the current job, every job queued ahead, and the entire microtask queue. A floor, not a schedule.

nodes.label: Releasing Zalgo (sometimes-async)
nodes.rationale: A function should be always-async or never-async. Cache-hit sync vs miss async fires events before listeners attach. Defer the fast path with queueMicrotask.

nodes.label: Error-first callback convention
nodes.rationale: An async callback cannot throw — the stack is gone — so the error travels as data in position zero. On success the first argument is null, not omitted.

nodes.label: Missing return after if (err)
nodes.rationale: Unlike catch, an if does not end the block. Fall-through starts the success path with undefined and points the stack trace at the wrong function.

nodes.label: A job is complete when the stack is empty
nodes.rationale: MDN definition of run-to-completion. Nothing else — timer, event, rendering — runs until the call stack fully unwinds.
nodes.norm_label: a job is complete when the stack is empty

nodes.label: Promise state is not readable
nodes.rationale: No promise.state or promise.value. A synchronous isSettled() would reintroduce Zalgo. The only read is attaching a handler.

nodes.label: fetch does not reject on 404 or 500
nodes.norm_label: fetch does not reject on 404 or 500

nodes.label: Phase 11 — Network, storage and data transfer
nodes.norm_label: phase 11 — network, storage and data transfer

nodes.label: CORS is a browser policy
nodes.rationale: Node has no origin and no cookies to protect, so it never enforces CORS. A successful Node request proves nothing about whether the browser will be allowed to read it.

nodes.label: fetch relative URL throws in Node
nodes.norm_label: fetch relative url throws in node

nodes.label: Cold start
nodes.rationale: New isolate pays runtime init, module graph import, and first DB connect before the first request.

nodes.label: V8/Node startup snapshot
nodes.rationale: Freezes initialized heap after bootstrap so the next launch skips re-parse; specialist lever for CLIs.

nodes.label: Serverless freeze model
nodes.rationale: Process may freeze without a SIGTERM you control; setInterval may pause; disk and global cache are per-isolate.

nodes.label: When serverless is the wrong default
nodes.rationale: Long-lived WebSockets, heavy steady CPU, or DB-heavy work without a pool proxy.
nodes.norm_label: when serverless is the wrong default

nodes.label: Compile cache vs startup snapshot
nodes.rationale: Compile cache stores compilation artifacts; snapshots store initialized heap state. Cache is the practical win for many apps.

nodes.label: Snapshots are tied to the Node/V8 build
nodes.rationale: Rebuild in CI per runtime artifact; native addons and listen() during bootstrap are not snapshot-safe.
nodes.norm_label: snapshots are tied to the node/v8 build

nodes.label: createRequire
nodes.rationale: Build a working require inside ESM via createRequire(import.meta.url). Escape hatch that reintroduces synchronous loading.

nodes.label: Subpath imports (#internal)
nodes.rationale: Private aliases inside the package. Keys must start with #. Node resolves them natively with no build step, and they accept conditions.

nodes.label: enableCompileCache
nodes.rationale: Persists V8 compilation output to disk. Call before heavy imports, or set NODE_COMPILE_CACHE. Keyed by Node version and architecture.

nodes.label: Loader hooks run on a separate thread
nodes.rationale: Stops a loader from deadlocking the main thread. No shared memory; communicate through register() data and a MessagePort.
nodes.norm_label: loader hooks run on a separate thread

nodes.label: module.register()
nodes.rationale: Registers resolve and load customization hooks. Still experimental in Node 24. Register before the modules they affect via --import.

nodes.label: node:module API
nodes.rationale: The programmable side of the module system. You go years without needing it, then need it for a loader, a test double, or a startup-time win.

nodes.label: CORS preflight
nodes.rationale: Non-simple requests (JSON, custom headers, PATCH/DELETE) send OPTIONS. * and credentials are mutually exclusive.

nodes.label: Vary header
nodes.rationale: Any response that varies by a request header must say so or shared caches poison representations.

nodes.label: __Host- cookie prefix
nodes.rationale: Browser refuses unless Secure, Path=/, and no Domain. Hardening unforgeable by a subdomain.

nodes.label: HttpOnly Secure SameSite
nodes.rationale: HttpOnly blocks document.cookie XSS theft; Secure blocks plaintext; SameSite blunts CSRF. Session cookies want all three.

nodes.label: CORS is a browser rule not authorization
nodes.rationale: Node fetch with a spoofed Origin read the whole response with no CORS headers. Protects the browser user only.
nodes.norm_label: cors is a browser rule not authorization

nodes.label: Opaque session id vs JWT cookie
nodes.rationale: Opaque id keeps authority server-side so revocation is a delete. JWT needs a denylist, reintroducing the store.
nodes.norm_label: opaque session id vs jwt cookie

nodes.label: A signal listener replaces default terminate
nodes.norm_label: a signal listener replaces default terminate

nodes.label: value attribute vs value property
nodes.rationale: The attribute stays at the initial value; the property holds what the user typed. Assert on element.value, not markup.

nodes.label: File inputs are always uncontrolled
nodes.rationale: The picker sets the value; JS cannot assign it. Read via ref or FormData.

nodes.label: React onChange is the DOM input event
nodes.rationale: Fires every keystroke with the value after the stroke. Native change afterwards fires nothing. No built-in 'finished' event — use onBlur or debounce.
nodes.norm_label: react onchange is the dom input event

nodes.label: Controlled vs uncontrolled
nodes.rationale: Controlled: React state is the value (value + onChange). Uncontrolled: the DOM owns it (defaultValue). Pick once per field for its lifetime.

nodes.label: File input FileList and clear
nodes.rationale: e.target.files is a FileList. Clear with node.value = ''. Same file twice does not fire onChange unless reset.

nodes.label: Read a form with FormData
nodes.rationale: name is the key; e.currentTarget is the form; preventDefault stops navigation. Unchecked checkboxes are absent; repeated names need getAll.

nodes.label: select takes value, not option selected
nodes.rationale: selected on option is stripped and warned. multiple takes an array; read selectedOptions, not e.target.value.
nodes.norm_label: select takes value, not option selected

nodes.label: textarea takes value, not children
nodes.rationale: Children warn; children plus defaultValue throws. Rendered markup still puts text between the tags.

nodes.label: Strings in braces are literal
nodes.rationale: Compile-time whitespace rules apply only to JSX text. Template literals keep newlines; CSS still has to not collapse them.

nodes.label: JSX whitespace rules
nodes.rationale: Newline-adjacent whitespace is stripped at compile time. Newline between elements is removed; between words becomes one space. Within a line, spaces are kept.

nodes.label: Disappearing space between elements
nodes.rationale: Breaking Hello world across lines deletes the space. {' '} is an expression and survives Prettier.

nodes.label: {' '} vs
nodes.rationale: U+0020 collapses and may break. U+00A0 does neither. Entities work in JSX text, not inside {}.

nodes.label: Store the raw string, convert at the edge
nodes.rationale: Number() on each keystroke destroys intermediate states (1., -, 1.0) and jumps the caret. Initialise to '' / false / [], never undefined.
nodes.norm_label: store the raw string, convert at the edge

nodes.label: Start uncontrolled, upgrade fields that need it
nodes.rationale: Most forms need per-keystroke state for none of their fields. Controlled when you validate as they type or fields constrain each other.
nodes.norm_label: start uncontrolled, upgrade fields that need it

nodes.label: Form elements are where the DOM already holds state
nodes.rationale: React either takes that state over or leaves it alone. Every warning in the topic exists because the two got mixed.
nodes.norm_label: form elements are where the dom already holds state

nodes.label: SQLSTATE error codes
nodes.rationale: Match err.code not err.message. 23505 unique, 23503 FK, 25P02 aborted tx, 57014 timeout, 53300 too many clients.

nodes.label: Translate 23505 to domain errors
nodes.rationale: catch (e) { if (e.code === '23505') } in a service couples the domain to PostgreSQL.

nodes.label: UnrecoverableError
nodes.rationale: 4xx except 429 should fail permanently. Retrying a 422 five times turns a clear error into a slow mystery.

nodes.label: Poison message
nodes.rationale: Fails every time. Without a DLQ it retries forever or piles into an unread failed set.

nodes.label: Transient vs permanent errors
nodes.rationale: Retry ECONNREFUSED, 57P01, 40001, 40P01. Never retry 23505, 42601, 28P01. A timeout is not knowing whether the write committed.

nodes.label: BullMQ has no built-in DLQ
nodes.rationale: Exhausted jobs stay in failed, mixing today's blips with last month's poison. Move on failed when attemptsMade reaches attempts.

nodes.label: Calendar arithmetic vs elapsed milliseconds
nodes.rationale: Adding 7*24*3600*1000 across DST moved 7:00 a.m. New York to 8:00 a.m. Use Temporal, date-fns-tz, Luxon, or PostgreSQL interval in a named zone.

nodes.label: Instant vs calendar date
nodes.rationale: toISOString().slice(0,10) is always the UTC day. 2026-08-10T18:45Z is the 10th in UTC and the 11th in IST. Format with an explicit timeZone.

nodes.label: Do not trust a scheduled job's clock
nodes.rationale: Jobs run late, twice, or in another zone. Pass the window in and select on state (processed_at is null) so a 2:47 run matches a 2:00 run.
nodes.norm_label: do not trust a scheduled job's clock

nodes.label: timestamptz not timestamp
nodes.rationale: timestamptz stores an instant. timestamp stores a wall-clock reading with no zone and silently means different moments after a region change.

nodes.label: Store UTC, convert at the edge
nodes.rationale: An instant is unambiguous; a calendar date depends on who is looking. User timezone is data you must store — it cannot be recovered from an instant.
nodes.norm_label: store utc, convert at the edge

nodes.label: --experimental-test-module-mocks
nodes.rationale: Without the flag mock.module is not a function — TypeError, not a helpful message. Put it on the test script.

nodes.label: mock.module()
nodes.rationale: Replaces a module in the loader so importers get the test version. Escape hatch for a dependency you cannot inject.

nodes.label: t.mock.module scoped restore
nodes.rationale: t.mock.module is undone when the test ends; top-level mock.module is not. Default process-per-file isolation prevents leaks between files; --test-isolation=none can leak.

nodes.label: vi.mock hoisting
nodes.rationale: Vitest's transform hoists vi.mock above imports, so it avoids the import-order trap that mock.module suffers. Bought with a transform step.

nodes.label: Mock-first then dynamic import
nodes.rationale: A static import evaluates the module under test before the mock exists. Even a later await import() returns the cached module. Mock first, then dynamic-import.

nodes.label: Prefer dependency injection over mock.module
nodes.rationale: Use mock.module only for third-party import-time side effects, uninjectable builtins, or legacy code. Injection has no flag, no import-order rule, and a visible signature.

nodes.label: --test-rerun-failures
nodes.rationale: State file records passes and replays them without executing. A test edited to throw still printed ✔ (passed on attempt 0) and exited 0. Local iteration only; never CI.

nodes.label: --experimental-test-tag-filter
nodes.rationale: Key is tags, plural, array. Singular tag: is silently ignored — a filtered CI job can run zero tests and exit 0. Filename globs are safer until this leaves experimental.

nodes.label: --test-randomize
nodes.rationale: Not --test-random-order, which does not exist. Shared-state three-test suite: seeds 1/2/3/7/11 gave 2/1/1/0/3 failures. Seed 7 passed entirely.

nodes.label: --test-shard
nodes.rationale: Cheapest honest CI speed-up. Unlike rerun-failures or tag filtering it cannot make a broken suite look green.

nodes.label: Phase 9 measurement corrections
nodes.rationale: Forgotten await is not silent (file fails). Directory positional fails MODULE_NOT_FOUND. rerun-failures can go green. tags must be plural array. Flag is --test-randomize.

nodes.label: Syllabus flag names predating page 14 measurements
nodes.rationale: Part 3 still lists --test-random-order and --test-name-tag. Phase 9 pages measured those names do not exist on Node 24.19.0.
nodes.norm_label: syllabus flag names predating page 14 measurements

nodes.label: Part 1 — Foundations
nodes.rationale: Phases 0–2. The part that makes you actually good at Node and most courses skip.

nodes.label: Part 2 — Core I/O
nodes.rationale: Phases 3–5. Node exists to do I/O well.

nodes.label: Part 3 — Application Layer
nodes.rationale: Phases 6–9. Data access, background work, security, testing. Parallelizable alongside building.

nodes.label: Part 4 — Production
nodes.rationale: Phases 10–12. The difference between it works on my machine and it works at 3 a.m.

nodes.label: postgresql:// connection URI
nodes.rationale: postgresql://USER:PASSWORD@HOST:PORT/DATABASE. Sandbox example: postgresql://devbible:devbible@127.0.0.1:55432/devbible. Easy to pass around and easy to log by accident.

nodes.label: DATABASE_URL
nodes.rationale: Common app convention; not read by psql by default. Never print it in error handlers or APM breadcrumbs.

nodes.label: PG* environment variables
nodes.rationale: PGHOST, PGPORT, PGUSER, PGPASSWORD, PGDATABASE. PGPASSWORD is convenient and easy to leak in process lists.

nodes.label: .pgpass
nodes.rationale: hostname:port:database:username:password file for psql. Permissions must be tight (0600) or psql silently ignores it.

nodes.label: ex31-psql-basics.sh
nodes.rationale: sandbox/pg-api measurement script for Phase 1 psql pages. Verified 2026-08 on PostgreSQL 18.4 and psql 18.4.

nodes.label: Three psql connection forms
nodes.rationale: Flags (-h -p -U -d), postgresql:// URI, or PG* environment. Mixable; omitted values fall back to env then OS username. URI is the same DATABASE_URL the app uses.

nodes.label: LISTEN/NOTIFY is at-most-once
nodes.rationale: A notification sent while nobody is listening is discarded. Fine as a hint; unacceptable for exactly-once. Combine with an outbox.

nodes.label: Outbox is at-least-once
nodes.rationale: Relay can publish then crash before setting published_at. Exactly-once effect needs an idempotent consumer.

nodes.label: Dual write bug
nodes.rationale: No transaction spans database and queue. Measured: order committed, enqueue failed, jobs = 0. Reversing order just moves the failure.

nodes.label: Idempotent consumer ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING
nodes.rationale: Unique idempotency key; rowCount 0 means already handled. Naive job sent 2 emails, idempotent sent 1.
nodes.norm_label: idempotent consumer on conflict do nothing

nodes.label: SKIP LOCKED relay claim
nodes.rationale: Three workers, 20 rows: 20 unique claims, 94 ms. Without SKIP LOCKED: 189 ms serialised behind one row.

nodes.label: Outbox table in the same transaction
nodes.rationale: Business row and event row commit or neither does. Partial index on published_at IS NULL keeps the relay query small.
nodes.norm_label: outbox table in the same transaction

nodes.label: EXECUTE to PUBLIC on new functions
nodes.rationale: proacl NULL means the built-in default, not no access. Combined with SECURITY DEFINER this is the classic privilege-escalation shape. There is no DENY; revoke from PUBLIC and re-grant.
nodes.norm_label: execute to public on new functions

nodes.label: relacl privilege string
nodes.rationale: grantee=privileges/grantor. rwadDxtm map to SELECT UPDATE INSERT DELETE TRUNCATE REFERENCES TRIGGER MAINTAIN. relacl NULL is the built-in default, not locked down. Empty grantee is PUBLIC.

nodes.label: has_*_privilege boot assertion
nodes.rationale: These functions resolve group membership and inheritance, which reading relacl does not. Assert the app can SELECT and cannot TRUNCATE, CREATE or be superuser, at boot.

nodes.label: Pool object connectionString leak
nodes.rationale: pool.options.password is undefined but connectionString still holds the credential. JSON.stringify and util.inspect reproduce it. pg error objects carry no password.

nodes.label: Safe connection identity readout
nodes.rationale: Log current_user, current_database(), inet_server_addr() and is_superuser instead of the connection string. is_superuser=on is an alert.

nodes.label: URL password encoding
