nodes.rationale: / and # in a password throw ERR_INVALID_URL with *****REDACTED*****. @ : and space parse. encodeURIComponent or pass discrete host/user/password fields.

nodes.label: Custom dump format -Fc
nodes.rationale: Default choice: compressed, indexed, selective and parallel restore, one file. Same size as gzipped plain text; unlike -Fp the format cannot be changed after the dump.

nodes.label: pg_restore table of contents
nodes.rationale: pg_restore -l lists restorable items. TABLE vs TABLE DATA enables schema-only or data-only. SEQUENCE SET captures identity positions; skip them and the first insert duplicates keys.

nodes.label: pg_restore -j parallelises across items
nodes.rationale: One dominant table cannot be split. -j 4 was 10.06 s vs 10.29 s serial. Parallel dump requires -Fd; -Fc -j is a hard error.

nodes.label: Restore costs far more than dump
nodes.rationale: Measured 2.55 s dump vs 10.29 s restore. Restore inserts rows, rebuilds every index, revalidates constraints and writes WAL.
nodes.norm_label: restore costs far more than dump

nodes.label: Selective restore leaves indexes behind
nodes.rationale: pg_restore -t restores the table item, not separate index and constraint items. The table accepts duplicates with no error.

nodes.label: Logical backup
nodes.rationale: SQL that recreates one database from a consistent snapshot. Portable and selective, and about four times slower to restore than to take.

nodes.label: Three dependency-array forms
nodes.rationale: No array: after every commit. Empty: after the initial commit only. Populated: initial commit and when a dependency changes by Object.is.

nodes.label: Object and function identity re-runs the Effect
nodes.rationale: Object.is fails every render for a new object or function. Depend on primitives, move inside, extract an Effect Event, or useMemo/useCallback last.
nodes.norm_label: object and function identity re-runs the effect

nodes.label: What an effect is for
nodes.rationale: An effect synchronizes a component with a system outside React. It is not run-after-render, not componentDidMount, and not where you respond to a click.

nodes.label: useEffect anatomy
nodes.rationale: Three parts: setup after commit, optional cleanup that undoes it, and a dependency array with three distinct forms.

nodes.label: The dependency array is not a preference
nodes.rationale: The array declares what the effect reads. It is true or false. Lying produces an effect that reads one render's values forever.
nodes.norm_label: the dependency array is not a preference

nodes.label: The cleanup contract
nodes.rationale: Cleanup is the stop half of a start/stop pair. React will call that pair as many times as it needs to.

nodes.label: Cleanup recipes
nodes.rationale: The contract resolves differently depending on what the effect touches. Two of react.dev's cases need no cleanup.

nodes.label: When cleanup is not the answer
nodes.rationale: Some effects fire twice because the code was never an effect. No cleanup will fix them.
nodes.norm_label: when cleanup is not the answer

nodes.label: Cleanup
nodes.rationale: The only correct effect is one where setup → cleanup → setup is indistinguishable from setup alone.

nodes.label: Race conditions
nodes.rationale: The screen shows the answer to a question the user has already moved on from. No error, no failed request — just the wrong data, sometimes.

nodes.label: An effect has its own lifecycle
nodes.rationale: Components mount, update and unmount. Effects only start and stop synchronizing. One mount can contain many start/stop cycles.
nodes.norm_label: an effect has its own lifecycle

nodes.label: Objects and functions as dependencies
nodes.rationale: Objects and functions created at different times are different. Avoid object and function dependencies.

nodes.label: Effect ordering
nodes.rationale: Three kinds of effect in three passes, and inside each pass every cleanup before any setup.

nodes.label: Phase 4 — Effects and synchronization
nodes.rationale: useEffect is misused as run-after-render. The phase follows two ideas: an effect is caused by rendering, and setup and cleanup are a pair React may run any number of times.

nodes.label: componentDidMount is the wrong model
nodes.rationale: useEffect(fn, []) stays connected to the first room forever. Synchronization with real deps and cleanup handles mount, update and unmount.

nodes.label: Cleanup is not unmount code
nodes.rationale: It runs on dependency change with old values, on unmount, and once extra under StrictMode. Tied to dependencies, not the component lifetime.

nodes.label: Cache hit ratio understates OS cache
nodes.rationale: blks_read counts shared-buffer misses, many served from the OS page cache. A sharp drop matters; 97% is not a RAM purchase.
nodes.norm_label: cache hit ratio understates os cache

nodes.label: pg_stat_database
nodes.rationale: One row per database: cache hit, temp spills, deadlocks, rollback ratio, stats_reset. Read stats_reset first.

nodes.label: shared_buffers
nodes.rationale: Allocated once at startup (postmaster, restart). Default 128 MB. Dedicated server guidance ~25% of RAM because OS page cache is the second tier.

nodes.label: Database health and alerting
nodes.rationale: Database-level statistics plus the 3am alert list: disk, connections, oldest xact, idle-in-transaction, lag, dead tuples, deadlocks, temp_bytes.

nodes.label: Statistics counters are estimates
nodes.rationale: n_live_tup and n_dead_tup are approximate; stats report after statements complete. Exact counters would need sync on every row operation.

nodes.label: Database statistics are approximate by design
nodes.rationale: Cumulative, approximate, reported after statements complete, reset with stats_reset. For trends and triage, not accounting.
nodes.norm_label: database statistics are approximate by design

nodes.label: Composite primary key
nodes.rationale: Natural fit for a join table. The pair is the uniqueness rule. Index serves the leading column only.

nodes.label: Join table trailing-column index
nodes.rationale: PK (post_id, tag_id) serves WHERE post_id. WHERE tag_id is a Seq Scan on 20k rows until a second index exists.

nodes.label: Many-to-many join table
nodes.rationale: PRIMARY KEY (a_id, b_id) is the uniqueness rule. A surrogate id permits the duplicate you meant to forbid. Name it from the domain once it carries attributes.

nodes.label: First normal form
nodes.rationale: One value per column. Comma-separated product_names cannot be joined, indexed, or counted without parsing strings.

nodes.label: Second normal form
nodes.rationale: No partial dependency on part of a composite key. product_name depends only on product_id, not (order_id, product_id).

nodes.label: Depend on the key the whole key and nothing but the key
nodes.rationale: Plain-language test that replaces formal 1NF/2NF/3NF. Duplication permits contradiction two concurrent writers cannot prevent.
nodes.norm_label: depend on the key the whole key and nothing but the key

nodes.label: Row constructor comparison
nodes.rationale: (a, b) > (1, 5) is lexicographic: a > 1 or (a = 1 and b > 5). Correct spelling for keyset pagination. Any NULL component yields NULL, same three-valued logic as NOT IN.

nodes.label: = ANY($1::int[]) list parameter
nodes.rationale: One parameter regardless of list length; empty array matches nothing. Empty IN () is a syntax error. Never interpolate a NOT IN list — a null turns the predicate into no rows.

nodes.label: NOT EXISTS anti join
nodes.rationale: Never compares a value to NULL; a NULL join key simply does not match. Default for every subquery negation. LEFT JOIN … WHERE right.id IS NULL is the older null-safe spelling.

nodes.label: NOT IN NULL trap
nodes.rationale: x NOT IN (a, NULL) is x <> a AND x <> NULL. Comparison to NULL is unknown; WHERE unknown drops every row. Measured 1 → 0 after one NULL elsewhere. NOT EXISTS still returned 1.

nodes.label: IN / = ANY / EXISTS as semi join
nodes.rationale: IN is defined as = ANY. All three plan as a semi join that stops at the first match. Choice is readability, not speed. EXISTS SELECT 1 vs SELECT * is identical.
nodes.norm_label: in / = any / exists as semi join

nodes.label: IN, EXISTS and the NOT IN trap
nodes.rationale: IN, = ANY and EXISTS agree. Their negations do not: NOT IN against one NULL returns no rows. The most expensive NULL behaviour in SQL.
nodes.norm_label: in, exists and the not in trap

nodes.label: hydrateRoot
nodes.rationale: Expects server-rendered HTML and attaches handlers; argument order is container first, unlike createRoot().render.

nodes.label: use
nodes.rationale: The only React API allowed inside a condition; reads a promise or a context during render.

nodes.label: One root per container
nodes.rationale: A second createRoot on the same element produces NotFoundError: Node.removeChild on unmount.

nodes.label: Must be {__html: ...} and exclusive of children
nodes.rationale: Wrong shape throws #61. children plus innerHTML throws #60. Nested key prevents an accidental server object from matching.
nodes.norm_label: must be {__html: ...} and exclusive of children

nodes.label: React escapes text and attributes by default
nodes.rationale: Ordinary XSS vectors are closed unless you opt in. The name and nested __html key are deliberate speed bumps.
nodes.norm_label: react escapes text and attributes by default

nodes.label: React 19 rewrites javascript: URLs
nodes.rationale: Rewritten to throw on click, but the href still appears in markup — scanners flag a finding that is already mitigated.

nodes.label: Sanitize with a real library or do not inject
nodes.rationale: Safe only if HTML is entirely yours, or DOMPurify (allowlist attributes, not just tags) as close to render as possible.
nodes.norm_label: sanitize with a real library or do not inject

nodes.label: script tags do not run; img onerror does
nodes.rationale: innerHTML never executes script elements. Measured: img onerror and iframe srcdoc ran. Filtering <script> is not a sanitizer.
nodes.norm_label: script tags do not run; img onerror does

nodes.label: Effect Event call-site rules
nodes.rationale: Top-level Hook. Call only from Effects or other Effect Events. Never during render, never from a handler, never pass to another component or Hook.

nodes.label: Logic that belongs to an event
nodes.rationale: Logic triggered by a user action ended up in an effect, where the information about what the user did no longer exists.
nodes.norm_label: logic that belongs to an event

nodes.label: Chains of effects
nodes.rationale: Each effect sets the state that wakes the next. One card costs four renders. The cascade is only visible when you read all four together.

nodes.label: State that belongs elsewhere
nodes.rationale: The effect papers over a state-location problem. The fix moves the state and the effect disappears.

nodes.label: You might not need an effect
nodes.rationale: Effects are an escape hatch. If there is no external system, you should not need an Effect.
nodes.norm_label: you might not need an effect

nodes.label: Cleanup without setup is a code smell
nodes.rationale: Usually reaching for when this unmounts. Cleanup also runs on every dependency change. If there is no external system, remove the Effect.
nodes.norm_label: cleanup without setup is a code smell

nodes.label: 81 pages clustered 169–269 lines
nodes.rationale: All 81 rewritten pages in phases 1, 2, 5, 10, 11 fall inside 169–269. Not one exceeds 270. Clustering tell: YES.

nodes.label: Item 14 re-split queue
nodes.rationale: 20 Master-tier single-file pages still inside the clustering band. Write to deserved depth, then chunk on concept boundaries.

nodes.label: D1–D5 review scoring rubric
nodes.rationale: Weighted composite: D1 explanation 35%, D2 examples 20%, D3 gotchas 15%, D4 interview 15%, D5 provenance 15%. Invented output forces WRONG.

nodes.label: Clustering tell
nodes.rationale: Files bunched in a narrow band just under the 300-line cap evidence writing to a budget rather than to the topic.

nodes.label: Review evidence rule
nodes.rationale: Every dimension below 8 needs location, quote, gap, and add. Vague 'needs more depth' is not a finding.

nodes.label: No new sandboxes
nodes.rationale: CLAUDE.md rule 8: validate against official docs; no run means no output block. Unvalidated pages are listed here, not flagged on the page.

nodes.label: tsc emit-on-error default
nodes.rationale: tsc reports errors and emits JavaScript anyway, exit 2. --noEmitOnError stops output. A build that ignores the exit code ships broken output.

nodes.label: The language server is not the build
nodes.norm_label: the language server is not the build

nodes.label: Type inference
nodes.rationale: Most types are written by nobody. The compiler infers differently for let vs const. Read inferred types from emitted .d.ts, not tooltips.

nodes.label: noUncheckedIndexedAccess
nodes.rationale: Same first<T>(items: T[]) source emits T or T | undefined depending on the flag, because indexing can miss.

nodes.label: Literal widening let vs const
nodes.rationale: let x = 'Hyderabad' infers string because it can be reassigned. const keeps "Hyderabad". Object properties widen even under const because contents stay mutable.

nodes.label: Array type T[]
nodes.rationale: T[] and Array<T> are the same. Inference unions elements and forgets length and position. mixed[99] type-checks.

nodes.label: unique symbol
nodes.rationale: Type of one specific symbol. Two Symbol('key') values are different types. Symbol.for is typed symbol because it is not unique.

nodes.label: Computed key unique symbol folklore
nodes.rationale: Older TypeScript required unique symbol (TS1170). On 7.0.2 both an interface and a type alias accepted a let symbol as a computed key. Still prefer const so the binding cannot be reassigned.

nodes.label: Delete unused CSS
nodes.rationale: The one selector-performance win that reliably pays: fewer bytes, less parse, fewer rules to bucket.

nodes.label: :has() matching cost
nodes.rationale: Relational matching is slower than a class (1.25 ms vs 0.15 ms on 5000 nodes) but only hurts when the subject is huge and the argument changes every frame.

nodes.label: Key selector bucketing
nodes.rationale: An element is only tested against rules whose rightmost part could match it.

nodes.label: Right-to-left selector matching
nodes.rationale: Engines start from the rightmost compound so the candidate set is small and failed ancestors prune fast.

nodes.label: Style invalidation breadth
nodes.rationale: Matching cost is rarely the bottleneck; jank comes from how much of the tree must restyle when state changes.

nodes.label: :focus vs :focus-visible
nodes.rationale: :focus matches any focus including mouse click; :focus-visible is the keyboard/AT ring so outline:none on :focus is no longer needed.

nodes.label: :focus-within
nodes.rationale: Parent selector for focus containment that predates :has(); highlight a field or keep a menu open.

nodes.label: Never style on data-testid
nodes.rationale: A test id must stay stable and meaningless; CSS on it makes renaming a visual regression.

nodes.label: :has() removes state hooks
nodes.rationale: body:has(dialog[open]) and .field:has(:user-invalid) delete the JS that used to sync a class.

nodes.label: js- prefix convention
nodes.rationale: js-submit is queried, never styled; btn--primary is styled, never queried.

nodes.label: State on attributes
nodes.rationale: A single data-state value cannot accumulate stale classes; styling aria-* keeps visual and announced state the same. Specificity stays 0,1,0.

nodes.label: Selector case sensitivity
nodes.rationale: Types are case-insensitive in HTML; class/id are sensitive; attribute values need the i flag to ignore case.

nodes.label: Five selector families
nodes.rationale: Type, class, id, universal, attribute — each couples CSS to a different contract. Class is the default.

nodes.label: Prose type-selector pattern
nodes.rationale: Scope type selectors under .prose for CMS/Markdown you cannot class; bare h2 leaks into components.

nodes.label: CSS fails silently
nodes.rationale: Invalid declaration dropped alone; invalid selector discards the whole rule; unclosed brace eats the next. Nothing is reported.

nodes.label: :has() parent selector
nodes.rationale: Parent and previous-sibling selector that replaces whole categories of state-toggling JavaScript.

nodes.label: Three consumers, three hooks
nodes.rationale: Style on class, state on data-*/aria-*, tests on data-testid, script on data-* or js-; one consumer per hook so a rename stays local.

nodes.label: CSS cascade layers
nodes.rationale: Native cascade control. Unlayered acts as an implicit final layer; !important inverts layer order.

nodes.label: Anonymous cascade layers
nodes.rationale: Unnamed @layer {} takes position from appearance and cannot be appended to. Prefer names.

nodes.label: @import layer()
nodes.rationale: Assign a whole vendor stylesheet to a named layer. @import must precede every rule except @charset and @layer statements.

nodes.label: Nested layers and dot notation
nodes.rationale: framework.layout is ordered only inside framework. A nested layer can never escape its parent's position.

nodes.label: @layer statement form
nodes.rationale: @layer reset, base, layout, components, utilities; writes no rules. First declared is weakest. Prevents first-block appearance from silently reordering.

nodes.label: !important inverts layer order
nodes.rationale: Foundational layers hold the most binding constraints. A utility layer must not !important past a reset or design-system invariant.

nodes.label: Recommended layer order
nodes.rationale: reset, vendor, base, layout, components, utilities — utilities always win with one class.

nodes.label: revert-layer
nodes.rationale: Rolls a property back to the previous layer in the same origin, not to initial or the previous origin (that is revert).

nodes.label: Swallow a vendor stylesheet
nodes.rationale: @import vendor into an early layer so a later one-class rule wins without !important. Vendor !important still beats you via inversion.

nodes.label: Author cascade ladder
nodes.rationale: Weakest: normal first layer → later layers → unlayered → normal inline → animations → important unlayered → important later layers → important first layer → important inline.

nodes.label: Inline styles are criterion 3
nodes.rationale: Not 'specificity 1000'. A normal inline beats every normal author rule; it loses to author !important because importance already separated them.

nodes.label: Origin and importance ladder
nodes.rationale: Eight levels: transitions, important UA/user/author, animations, then normal author/user/UA. Important reverses origin order for accessibility.

nodes.label: Cascade sorting order
nodes.rationale: Origin+importance, context, inline styles, layers, specificity, appearance. First distinguishing criterion wins; the rest are never consulted.

nodes.label: Transitions vs animations
nodes.rationale: Transitions sit above everything. Animations sit below important author, so !important is how you defeat a @keyframes value.

nodes.label: Phase 2 cascade gate
nodes.rationale: Design a layer order that imports third-party CSS and needs no !important.

nodes.label: @layer
nodes.rationale: Declare precedence once up front. Layers sit above specificity so a later-layer class beats an earlier-layer id.

nodes.label: Unlayered implicit final layer
nodes.rationale: Unlayered declarations behave as if they were in an implicit final layer. Last wins for normal, first wins for important — so unlayered wins all normal and loses all important.

nodes.label: async never throws synchronously
nodes.rationale: A throw anywhere, including before the first await, becomes a rejection. try { asyncFn() } without await catches nothing.

nodes.label: Callback
nodes.rationale: A function passed into another function as an argument, invoked to complete a routine. Says nothing about timing.

nodes.label: Callback hell
nodes.rationale: Nesting is forced because a callback has no return value to sequence on. The real cost is per-level error handling, not indentation.

nodes.label: Error-first callback convention
nodes.rationale: An async callback cannot throw — the stack is gone — so the error travels as data in argument zero. On success the first argument is null, not omitted.

nodes.label: Missing return after if (err)
nodes.rationale: An if does not end the block the way catch does. Fall-through starts the success path with undefined and the stack points at the wrong function.

nodes.label: try/catch cannot reach an async callback
nodes.rationale: The try finishes when the callee returns. The callback runs later on a fresh stack. Put try inside the callback and route errors as cb(err).
nodes.norm_label: try/catch cannot reach an async callback

nodes.label: Zalgo sometimes-async callback
nodes.rationale: A function that calls its callback synchronously on some paths and asynchronously on others. Defer the fast path with queueMicrotask.

nodes.label: Callback trust-table failures
nodes.rationale: Too early (Zalgo), too late, never, twice, wrong arguments, swallowed throw. None produce an exception.

nodes.label: Inversion of control
nodes.rationale: You hand the rest of your program to someone else's function. They decide when, how often, and with what arguments it runs. Failures are silent.

nodes.label: MDN three promise guarantees
nodes.rationale: Never invoked before the current event-loop run completes; invoked even if attached after settling; multiple then handlers in insertion order.

nodes.label: Floating promise
nodes.rationale: A started promise that was not returned. Sequencing breaks (next handler gets undefined immediately) and its rejection cannot reach the chain catch.

nodes.label: Job complete when stack empty
nodes.rationale: MDN: a job is considered completed when the stack is empty. Explains why try/catch cannot reach a later callback.

nodes.label: Named functions do not fix callback hell
nodes.rationale: Hoisting removes indentation and nothing else: sequence becomes invisible, closures are lost, per-level if(err) remains, trust bugs remain.
nodes.norm_label: named functions do not fix callback hell

nodes.label: Call the callback exactly once
nodes.rationale: Every exit path must invoke the callback once. A guard that returns without calling back hangs forever with no object left behind.

nodes.label: Callbacks are not inherently async
nodes.rationale: map's callback and readFile's callback are the same construct. Only the callee's documentation tells you the timing.

nodes.label: When a callback is still the right tool
nodes.rationale: Synchronous work, many-shot events, and pure scheduling. Promises are one-shot and cannot model a stream of events.
nodes.norm_label: when a callback is still the right tool

nodes.label: Chains catch programming errors
nodes.rationale: A TypeError in a handler lands in the same catch as a network failure. In the callback pyramid it would escape to uncaughtException.

nodes.label: Always return the promise
nodes.rationale: MDN's most consequential chaining rule. Prefer concise arrow bodies so a missing return is impossible.

nodes.label: fs callback, sync, and promise flavors
nodes.rationale: Import from node:fs/promises by default; node:fs callbacks are error-first; *Sync blocks the whole process.
nodes.norm_label: fs callback, sync, and promise flavors

nodes.label: path.join
nodes.rationale: Concatenates and normalises; an absolute later argument is treated as a relative segment.

nodes.label: path.resolve
nodes.rationale: Always absolute; restarts at any absolute argument, discarding earlier segments.

nodes.label: Root plus separator containment check
nodes.rationale: After path.resolve, require equality with ROOT or startsWith(ROOT + path.sep). startsWith(ROOT) alone lets uploads-evil through.

nodes.label: Path traversal attack
nodes.rationale: ../, absolute paths, encoded separators, and symlinks turn a file-serving endpoint into read-any-file.

nodes.label: realpath then re-check containment
nodes.rationale: A path inside the root can still be a symlink to ../secret.txt. String checks cannot see through links.

nodes.label: Zip-slip
nodes.rationale: Archive entries named ../../etc/cron.d/x write outside the extract directory unless each entry is containment-checked.

nodes.label: stat vs lstat
nodes.rationale: stat follows links and never reports isSymbolicLink; lstat describes the link and works on broken links.

nodes.label: Mid-stream upload size limit
nodes.rationale: Content-Length is client-supplied and absent under chunked encoding. Count bytes as they arrive.

nodes.label: mkdtemp
nodes.rationale: Atomically creates a directory with a random six-character suffix. Argument is a prefix, not a directory.

nodes.label: readlink vs realpath
nodes.rationale: readlink is the literal maybe-relative target. realpath follows the whole chain to an absolute path.

nodes.label: symlink
nodes.rationale: symlink(target, path) like ln -s. Relative targets resolve against the link's directory, not cwd.

nodes.label: Mid-stream request body limit
nodes.rationale: Content-Length is a claim. Count bytes, reply 413, then destroy. stream/consumers json is unbounded.

nodes.label: Drain or destroy unread bodies
nodes.rationale: Unread bytes sit in the socket buffer and block keep-alive reuse. req.resume() or destroy.

nodes.label: Safe vs idempotent methods
nodes.rationale: Safe means no state change. Idempotent means n identical requests leave the same state as one. POST retries need a key.

nodes.label: TypeError fetch failed cause
nodes.rationale: Every transport failure is the same TypeError. Diagnosis is err.cause.code: ECONNREFUSED, ENOTFOUND, UND_ERR_SOCKET.

nodes.label: fetch does not throw on 4xx or 5xx
nodes.rationale: A rejected promise means the exchange failed. Check res.ok (200-299) before treating the body as data.
nodes.norm_label: fetch does not throw on 4xx or 5xx

nodes.label: Response body is single-use
nodes.rationale: json/text/arrayBuffer consume a ReadableStream. Second read is Body is unusable. clone buffers.

nodes.label: undici
nodes.rationale: Implementation of Node fetch. Pool, keep-alive and retries live on an undici Dispatcher, not on fetch itself.

nodes.label: Unread fetch body holds the connection
nodes.rationale: With connections:1 the second request never starts. Consume or res.body.cancel() including on error paths.
nodes.norm_label: unread fetch body holds the connection

nodes.label: AbortSignal.timeout
nodes.rationale: Covers the whole exchange including a dribbling body. Unref'd so a pending timeout does not keep the process alive.

nodes.label: fetch has no default timeout
nodes.rationale: TCP connect may give up around 130s on Linux. Once connected, a silent server never times out.

nodes.label: One deadline for the whole handler
nodes.rationale: Three sequential 5s timeouts are a 15s worst case. Share AbortSignal.timeout and combine with AbortSignal.any.
nodes.norm_label: one deadline for the whole handler

nodes.label: Built-in fetch rejects npm undici Agent
nodes.rationale: UND_ERR_INVALID_ARG: bundled and npm copies are different classes. Use setGlobalDispatcher or undici.fetch.
nodes.norm_label: built-in fetch rejects npm undici agent

nodes.label: http.Agent
nodes.rationale: keepAlive default true since Node 19. maxSockets is a per-origin concurrency cap that queues overflow.

nodes.label: undici Agent dispatcher
nodes.rationale: Default dispatcher opens a connection per parallel request. Bound with Agent({connections}). Bundled undici is not importable.

nodes.label: Exponential backoff with jitter
nodes.rationale: Without jitter every instance retries together and the recovering upstream meets a thundering herd.

nodes.label: Idempotency-Key
nodes.rationale: Generate once per logical operation and reuse across retries. A new key per attempt creates a second charge.

nodes.label: Retry-After
nodes.rationale: Authoritative over computed backoff. Seconds or an HTTP date. Ignoring it turns a rate limit into a ban.

nodes.label: Retry only what is safe
nodes.rationale: Transport-before-bytes, 502/503/504, 429 after Retry-After, and GETs. Timed-out writes only with a key. Never 4xx besides 429.

nodes.label: The three flavors
nodes.rationale: Every fs operation exists as promise, callback, and sync. Promise is the default after listen.

nodes.label: node:path
nodes.rationale: Never build paths with + or templates. join vs resolve is a security boundary.

nodes.label: Path traversal
nodes.rationale: Any filesystem path from user input is a security boundary.

nodes.label: Atomic writes and temp files
nodes.rationale: writeFile is not atomic. Write a same-directory temp, fsync, then rename.

nodes.label: Virtual filesystems
nodes.rationale: An object implementing the fs interface without a disk: tests and single-executable assets.

nodes.label: Phase 4 — Filesystem, paths, and URLs
nodes.rationale: Complete 14-page phase on Node 24.19.0. Difficulty is failure modes: races, traversal, partial writes, leaked descriptors.

nodes.label: Sync fs blocks the event loop
nodes.rationale: 200 readFileSync calls blocked a 1 ms timer for 86 ms with zero ticks; one thread owns JS until the syscall returns.
nodes.norm_label: sync fs blocks the event loop

nodes.label: Sync fs only at startup, CLI, workers, crash handlers
nodes.rationale: Before server.listen there is no concurrency to protect. After listen, request paths use fs/promises.
nodes.norm_label: sync fs only at startup, cli, workers, crash handlers

nodes.label: join vs resolve is a security boundary
nodes.rationale: resolve gives the true final path to validate against a root; join can look contained after an absolute input.
nodes.norm_label: join vs resolve is a security boundary

nodes.label: Decode user paths once before validating
nodes.rationale: ..%2f is a literal until something decodes it. Decode once, then validate; never after.
nodes.norm_label: decode user paths once before validating

nodes.label: Store files under generated IDs
nodes.rationale: Best defence is not accepting paths: UUID storageKey plus metadata filename and ownership checks.

nodes.label: Phase 4 upload phase gate
nodes.rationale: A correct upload mid-stream limits, realpath-checks the destination, renames on one filesystem, and cleans up in finally.

nodes.label: Respond 413 before req.destroy
nodes.rationale: Destroy first and the client sees UND_ERR_SOCKET, which looks retryable. 413 is not.

nodes.label: Slow dependency worse than dead
nodes.rationale: Down fails in microseconds with ECONNREFUSED. Slow holds pooled connections and handlers until the pool and health checks collapse.

nodes.label: A timed-out write is unknown not failed
nodes.rationale: Abort does not undo server work. Retrying POST /charge without an idempotency key charges twice.
nodes.norm_label: a timed-out write is unknown not failed

nodes.label: One client per dependency
nodes.rationale: Shared module owns the pool bound, auth header, default deadline and metrics so payment bursts cannot starve email.

nodes.label: os.availableParallelism
nodes.rationale: Respects cgroup CPU limits and affinity. cpus().length reports the host and over-forks in a constrained container.

nodes.label: node:cluster
nodes.rationale: One Node process uses one core. cluster forks a worker per core sharing one listening port. On Kubernetes prefer replicas; cluster is for a single VM and zero-downtime reload.

nodes.label: Sticky sessions
nodes.rationale: Pinning clients to a worker hides in-memory state. Prefer Redis sessions, rate limits, and pub/sub so workers stay stateless.

nodes.label: process.exitCode vs process.exit
nodes.rationale: process.exit terminates immediately and can truncate a large pending pipe write to one buffer (65536 bytes).

nodes.label: PID 1 exec-form CMD
nodes.rationale: CMD npm start makes /bin/sh PID 1 and does not forward SIGTERM. Node is SIGKILLed after the grace period (exit 137).

nodes.label: SIGTERM
nodes.rationale: Installing a listener replaces default terminate. A handler that forgets to exit hangs until SIGKILL.

nodes.label: The process object and exit codes
nodes.norm_label: the process object and exit codes

nodes.label: Non-matching media does not block paint
nodes.rationale: media=print or a non-matching query is still fetched at low priority but does not wait. Basis of the print+onload non-critical CSS trick; styles land after first paint.
nodes.norm_label: non-matching media does not block paint

nodes.label: Render-blocking CSS
nodes.rationale: The browser will not paint until matching stylesheets arrive, choosing a blank frame over FOUC. Measured: no CSS FCP 47 ms vs delayed matching sheet 671 ms.

nodes.label: Composite-only properties
nodes.rationale: transform and opacity run after layout and paint. Neighbours do not reflow around a transformed box, so they can overlap.

nodes.label: Layout-invalidating properties
nodes.rationale: width, height, padding, margin, inset, font-size, display, flex/grid tracks. Never animate these; left and transformX can land in the same place but only left recomputes geometry.

nodes.label: Rendering pipeline stages
nodes.rationale: Style → layout (reflow) → paint (repaint) → composite. A change at one stage forces every later stage, never earlier ones.

nodes.label: :root for global custom properties
nodes.rationale: Matches html in HTML documents but at class specificity 0,1,0. Top of the inheritance chain; properties on body never reach anything above body.

nodes.label: @scope donut scoping
nodes.rationale: @scope (.root) to (.limit) styles inside the root and stops at the limit inclusive. No combinator/:not() chain expresses a hole. Baseline Newly available 2025-12-12.

nodes.label: @scope does not add specificity
nodes.rationale: @scope (.card) { .title } stays 0,1,0; .card .title would be 0,2,0. Containment equivalent of :where().

nodes.label: @scope proximity cascade
nodes.rationale: When two scoped rules match, the nearer scoping root wins before specificity. The only place DOM distance participates in the cascade; enables nearest-ancestor theming.

nodes.label: :where() for overridable defaults
nodes.rationale: Resets, library base styles, and .prose rules should weigh nothing so a consumer class always wins. Zero specificity does not mean no effect — anything else wins.

nodes.label: pg_advisory_xact_lock
nodes.rationale: Transaction-scoped lock on a chosen bigint. 500/500 succeeded. Session-scoped pg_advisory_lock can wedge after a crash. Same mechanism real tools use.

nodes.label: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS race
nodes.rationale: Catalog check and insert are not atomic. 228/500 failed with 23505 on pg_type_typname_nsp_index.
nodes.norm_label: create table if not exists race

nodes.label: Silent startup seed race
nodes.rationale: 20 workers, 20 duplicate admin rows, zero errors. Worse than CREATE race because it is silent data corruption.

nodes.label: drizzle-kit
nodes.rationale: v0.31.10. TypeScript schema objects; SQL generated by diff. Same derived-schema trade-off as Prisma.

nodes.label: The four migration models
nodes.rationale: node-pg-migrate and graphile-migrate: you write SQL. Prisma Migrate and drizzle-kit: the tool diffs a schema file. Split: do you write the schema, or does the tool derive it?

nodes.label: graphile-migrate
nodes.rationale: v1.4.1. One idempotent current.sql re-run on save, then committed as a numbered file. Fits functions/triggers/views/RLS; poor fit for incremental ALTER TABLE.

nodes.label: node-pg-migrate
nodes.rationale: v9.0.0. SQL or JS files, optional down. You own the schema; SQL is source of truth. Natural next step from a hand-written runner.

nodes.label: Prisma Migrate
nodes.rationale: v7.9.1. schema.prisma is source of truth; migrations are generated by diff. Do not use without Prisma Client.

nodes.label: Migration checksum
nodes.rationale: Never edit a shipped file. Runner re-hashes and fails if checksum changes, so two environments cannot share a version with different schemas.

nodes.label: schema_migrations tracking table
nodes.rationale: version PK, applied_at, checksum. The database records its own version. version PK answers 'has this run?' by constraint, not app logic.

nodes.label: Lock before reading tracking table
nodes.rationale: pg_advisory_xact_lock immediately after BEGIN, before SELECT from schema_migrations. Locking after the read leaves a window both runners see empty.

nodes.label: migrate()
nodes.rationale: Creates schema_migrations, checks out one client, BEGIN, pg_advisory_xact_lock, lexical .sql sort, sha256 checksum, apply+INSERT, COMMIT.

nodes.label: checkSchema() boot check
nodes.rationale: Compare EXPECTED columns against information_schema.columns; process.exit(1) on mismatch. A container that will not start is rollback-able.

nodes.label: What a naive drift check misses
nodes.rationale: numeric(p,s) reports as numeric; varchar length in character_maximum_length; identity is is_identity not column_default; indexes and constraints live in other catalogs.
nodes.norm_label: what a naive drift check misses

nodes.label: ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING
nodes.rationale: Requires a unique constraint. Measured rowCount 2, 0, 0. Bare INSERT raises 23505. SELECT-then-INSERT is not idempotent under concurrency.

nodes.label: DO UPDATE so RETURNING fires
nodes.rationale: DO NOTHING RETURNING gives rowCount 0 on replay. SET key = EXCLUDED.key is a no-op UPDATE so RETURNING returns the original row. (xmax = 0) AS was_inserted distinguishes 201 from 200.

nodes.label: Idempotency-Key unique constraint
nodes.rationale: Client UUID in a header. Unique index is correctness: 10 racing INSERTs → 1 success, 9× 23505. ON CONFLICT only shapes the response.

nodes.label: DO NOTHING versus DO UPDATE
nodes.rationale: DO NOTHING for rows a human may edit. DO UPDATE SET col = EXCLUDED.col for reference data the code depends on.

nodes.label: border resets border-image
nodes.rationale: border sets border-image to none even though the name does not imply it. Declare border first, then border-image.

nodes.label: font resets line-height
nodes.rationale: font resets line-height to normal unless the size/line-height form is used, collapsing vertical rhythm.

nodes.label: grid vs grid-template
nodes.rationale: grid resets implicit-grid longhands including grid-auto-flow; grid-template is the narrower shorthand.

nodes.label: Shorthand writes all longhands
nodes.rationale: A shorthand is a complete statement of a concept, not a patch. Omitted sub-values reset to initial, so they override earlier longhands you never named.

nodes.label: Supertest integration tests
nodes.rationale: Hit the real Express stack with mocked services. Do not mock Express itself.

nodes.label: Safe req attachments
nodes.rationale: Attach requestId, ctx, user, validated on req. Prefer namespaced objects when many features share the request.

nodes.label: app.js factory vs server.js listen
nodes.rationale: server.js listens; app.js exports the factory so tests can createApp without binding a port.

nodes.label: Mock outbound dependencies
nodes.rationale: In route tests mock outbound dependencies (DB, mail), not req/res plumbing.

nodes.label: Do not clobber Express core properties
nodes.rationale: Do not overwrite req.url/method/headers or wrap res.end/json casually. Inject DB via factory deps, not req.
nodes.norm_label: do not clobber express core properties

nodes.label: cookie-parser
nodes.rationale: Mount cookieParser() for req.cookies; cookieParser('secret') fills req.signedCookies. Session middleware typically depends on it.

nodes.label: Cookie read/write asymmetry
nodes.rationale: Writing cookies is built in via res.cookie. Reading them needs cookie-parser or a manual Cookie header parse.

nodes.label: httpOnly, secure, SameSite cookie flags
nodes.rationale: httpOnly blocks document.cookie for session tokens. secure is HTTPS-only and required with SameSite=None. sameSite sets CSRF posture.

nodes.label: res.cookie
nodes.rationale: res.cookie is built in. Flags decide whether browser JS can read the cookie and when it is sent.

nodes.label: Signed cookies are not encryption
nodes.rationale: Signed cookies detect tampering; they are not encryption. Secrets still need HTTPS and careful res.cookie flags.

nodes.label: Static cache headers
nodes.rationale: Long maxAge for hashed filenames; short/none for HTML. Fingerprinted assets can be immutable; HTML points at changing hashes.

nodes.label: API Cache-Control
nodes.rationale: Authenticated JSON is usually Cache-Control: private, no-store. Public catalogs may use public, max-age carefully.

nodes.label: ETag
nodes.rationale: Express can generate weak ETags. For APIs, explicit version fields or hashes are often clearer.

nodes.label: If-Match 412 lost update
nodes.rationale: If-Match: v2 → 412 if current is v3 (lost update).

nodes.label: If-None-Match 304
nodes.rationale: 304 Not Modified when the client already has the current representation.

nodes.label: Phase 0 — How Git stores things
nodes.rationale: Only completed Git phase: 14 topics / 14 pages.

nodes.label: sandbox/git-p0
nodes.rationale: Command blocks come from sandbox/git-* scripts run in a throwaway repo with neutralized global config.

nodes.label: Never invent output
nodes.rationale: git-filter-repo and git-lfs are not installed. Those pages will be measured after install or cite upstream docs — the never-invent-output rule does not bend.

nodes.label: Compressed binaries do not delta
nodes.rationale: JPEGs, zips, and compiled artefacts neither delta nor compress. Each version is stored near full size forever.

nodes.label: Cruft pack
nodes.rationale: Unreachable objects held with .mtimes for a two-week grace period. Why gc does not shrink a rewritten repo immediately.

nodes.label: Loose objects
nodes.rationale: One zlib-compressed file per object, written on commit. Path is first two hash characters plus the rest.

nodes.label: Packfile
nodes.rationale: .pack holds delta-compressed objects; .idx is hash→offset; .rev is reverse index. Measured 51 objects 204K packed to 6.03 KiB.

nodes.label: Git is not a large-file store
nodes.rationale: Already-compressed binaries get almost none of packfile savings. git-lfs is not installed on this machine.
nodes.norm_label: git is not a large-file store

nodes.label: await does not consume stack
nodes.rationale: 200000-deep async recursion succeeded. Every await returns to the event loop; the continuation is a microtask on a fresh stack.

nodes.label: Microtasks vs macrotasks
nodes.rationale: Assert only what Node and the browser agree on: microtasks drain before tasks. Name the runtime for anything narrower.

nodes.label: Documentation-validated pages
nodes.rationale: No new measurement sandboxes. No run means no console block. Verified lines name MDN and spec sections.

nodes.label: No run means no console block
nodes.rationale: Ordering claims are held to documentation. No page prints an interleaving nobody produced.
nodes.norm_label: no run means no console block

nodes.label: navigator exists on Node 21+
nodes.rationale: typeof navigator !== 'undefined' is true on Node 24. It never tested for a browser, only a name.

nodes.label: Safari private mode localStorage probe
nodes.rationale: Safari private browsing defines localStorage then throws QuotaExceededError on write. Probe with a real setItem.

nodes.label: Four JavaScript hosts
nodes.rationale: Browser main thread, Web Worker, Node, and edge runtimes offer different globals. Workers have no DOM, window, or localStorage.

nodes.label: Test the capability, not the environment
nodes.rationale: Every user-agent check eventually misidentifies something. Ask for the capability with a real operation.
nodes.norm_label: test the capability, not the environment

nodes.label: Progressive enhancement
nodes.rationale: Ship a version that works everywhere, then add capability-gated improvements. Infinite scroll or a Load more button; both load products.

nodes.label: {} + [] parse vs coerce
nodes.rationale: As a statement {} is an empty block and +[] is ToNumber('') = 0. In expression position it is concatenation to '[object Object]'.

nodes.label: Expression vs statement
nodes.rationale: Expressions produce a value; statements perform an action. Only expressions are legal where a value is expected — JSX, arrow implicit return.

nodes.label: IIFE parentheses
nodes.rationale: function at statement start is a declaration and requires a name. Parentheses force expression position. Remaining uses: const that needs several statements.

nodes.label: Fiber double buffering
nodes.rationale: current and work-in-progress trees point at each other via alternate. DOM node's __reactFiber$ may be last render.

nodes.label: Fiber
nodes.rationale: Internal record of one tree node. Linked list of child/sibling/parent replaced recursion so rendering is interruptible.

nodes.label: HostComponent vs FunctionComponent
nodes.rationale: tag 5 type is a string (li); tag 0 type is your function. Host belongs to the renderer.

nodes.label: Host config
nodes.rationale: createInstance, appendChild, commitUpdate, … ~30 functions. react never learns what a node is.

nodes.label: ink
nodes.rationale: Terminal renderer. latest=7.1.1.

nodes.label: @react-three/fiber
nodes.rationale: Declarative WebGL — 3D scenes as components. latest=9.7.0 as of 2026-07-31.

nodes.label: React Native
nodes.rationale: Same React, different renderer. Learn once, write anywhere — not write once, run anywhere.

nodes.label: react-reconciler
nodes.rationale: Build a custom renderer. 0.33.0, no stability guarantee. Almost never appropriate.

nodes.label: react-test-renderer deprecated
nodes.rationale: Still published 19.2.8 but deprecated. Asserted against internals. Use React Testing Library.

nodes.label: Duplicate React hook error
nodes.rationale: Two copies of react: hooks live in module-level internals so copy A calling copy B finds nothing.

nodes.label: react-dom package
nodes.rationale: 7148 KB vs react 168 KB (42.7×). Events, hydration, streaming, DOM property tables.

nodes.label: react package
nodes.rationale: 42 public exports. No render, no createRoot, no document.createElement anywhere in source.

nodes.label: Hook records on the fiber
nodes.rationale: Function components have no instance. useState lives in a linked list of hook records keyed by call order.

nodes.label: Fiber does not make React faster
nodes.rationale: It makes rendering schedulable. A slow render is still slow.
nodes.norm_label: fiber does not make react faster

nodes.label: react / react-dom version-match rule
nodes.rationale: They share private internals. A mismatch is undefined behaviour, usually a crash inside the renderer.

nodes.label: % is remainder not modulo
nodes.rationale: Result takes the sign of the dividend. -7 % 3 is -1. True modulo for wrap-around: ((a % b) + b) % b.

nodes.label: Bitwise permission flags
nodes.rationale: & is looser than !== so (flags & MASK) !== 0 needs parentheses. For app-scale domain flags a Set of strings is usually clearer.

nodes.label: Bitwise ToInt32 wrap
nodes.rationale: Every bitwise operator converts to 32-bit signed first. ~~1e10 is 1410065408. Use Math.trunc. Only 31 usable flags; 1 << 31 is negative.

nodes.label: break in switch inside a loop
nodes.norm_label: break in switch inside a loop

nodes.label: Labelled break and continue
nodes.rationale: One good use: exit nested loops. Prefer extracting a function and return. Labels are not goto — they cannot jump backwards or leave a function.

nodes.label: Ternary vs if
nodes.rationale: Ternary chooses a value; if chooses an action. One level inline; two or more align as a decision table or extract a function.

nodes.label: Guard clauses
nodes.rationale: Early returns for failures so the happy path is last and unindented. Highest-value refactor for nested conditionals.

nodes.label: Detached method
nodes.rationale: Assigning, destructuring, or passing obj.method as a callback drops the receiver. Strict (modules/classes) gives undefined and TypeError; sloppy substitutes globalThis and silently creates globals.

nodes.label: Arrow class field
nodes.rationale: Field initialiser runs with this already the instance; the arrow captures it. One function per instance, not on the prototype — subclasses cannot override normally and super cannot reach it.

nodes.label: Function.prototype.bind
nodes.rationale: Returns a new function whose this is permanent — bind only works once; call/apply cannot override. Constructor bind installs an own property that shadows the prototype method.

nodes.label: Call-site arrow wrapper
nodes.rationale: Best default: explicit, free, method stays on the prototype and overridable. Wrong for removable listeners because each arrow is a new function.

nodes.label: removeEventListener identity match
nodes.rationale: Removal matches by function identity. An inline arrow cannot be removed. Store one bound function or arrow field and pass it to both add and remove.

nodes.label: Array.prototype.toSpliced
nodes.rationale: ES2023 non-mutating counterpart; returns the new dense array, not the removed items.

nodes.label: ES2023 non-mutating array family
nodes.rationale: toSorted, toReversed, toSpliced, with. All return a new dense array and leave the original alone.

nodes.label: sort mutates in place
nodes.rationale: sort returns the same array reference. const sorted = arr.sort() is not a copy.

nodes.label: Array.prototype.toSorted
nodes.rationale: ES2023 non-mutating sort; returns a shallow-copied dense sorted array.

nodes.label: Non-mutating end equivalents
nodes.rationale: Spread or slice instead of push/pop/shift/unshift when the array is shared or is React state.

nodes.label: cache stampede
nodes.rationale: Many concurrent misses on one expired hot key overload the origin. Mitigate with single-flight, distributed locks, jittered TTLs, or stale-while-revalidate.

nodes.label: in-process vs Redis cache
nodes.rationale: In-process is fastest and per pod; after scale-out you have N independent caches. Redis is shared, networked, operational. Choose by coherence needs.

nodes.label: single-flight cache fill
nodes.rationale: In-process Map of inflight promises collapses concurrent misses. Does not protect a multi-pod fleet — that needs a distributed lock or soft TTL.

nodes.label: TTL and write-path invalidation
nodes.rationale: TTL bounds how wrong you can be; it is not the only invalidation. Delete or overwrite on write when updates must show sooner. Pick TTLs from product tolerance and origin load.

nodes.label: Custom module loaders
nodes.rationale: Intercept resolve/load for transpile, mock, or policy. Power tools for tooling authors, not app servers.

nodes.label: node --import loader registration
nodes.rationale: Modern Node registers loaders via --import a registration module; pin Node 24 docs.

nodes.label: Loader load hook
nodes.rationale: Returns source for a URL so a loader can transpile or substitute modules.

nodes.label: Loader resolve hook
nodes.rationale: Maps a specifier to a URL; chain with next() to defer to default resolution.

nodes.label: Prefer compiled JS over production loaders
nodes.rationale: On-the-fly transforms hurt startup, complicate debugging, and drift from the CI artifact.
nodes.norm_label: prefer compiled js over production loaders

nodes.label: host vs hostname
nodes.rationale: host includes the port; hostname does not. An allowlist on host fails the moment a port appears.

nodes.label: url.parse deprecated
nodes.rationale: DEP0169. Known parsing differences from the standard have caused SSRF bypasses. Use new URL().

nodes.label: URLSearchParams
nodes.rationale: Decodes on read, encodes on write. get returns only the first repeated key — a real authorisation-bypass shape. Use getAll.

nodes.label: WHATWG URL
nodes.rationale: URL and URLSearchParams are globals implementing the same standard as the browser. Handle encoding and relative resolution string concat gets wrong.

nodes.label: SSRF URL check
nodes.rationale: Check protocol and hostname on the parsed object, never a regex on the raw string. Incomplete without pinning the resolved IP.

nodes.label: Idempotency-Key
nodes.rationale: Generate once per logical operation and reuse across retries. A key regenerated inside the retry loop defeats deduplication.

nodes.label: child_process.exec
nodes.rationale: Hands the string to /bin/sh. Quoted interpolation was defeated by closing quotes and by $(...) inside double quotes.

nodes.label: child_process.execFile
nodes.rationale: Passes arguments to execve. Removes shell injection, not argument injection or path traversal. shell:true restores the shell.

nodes.label: Quoting is not a shell defence
nodes.norm_label: quoting is not a shell defence

nodes.label: Node SEA
nodes.rationale: The Node binary with a CommonJS blob injected by postject. 121 MB for a trivial script. CLI distribution, not server deploy.

nodes.label: Calendar vs elapsed arithmetic
nodes.rationale: Adding 7*24h across DST moved 7:00 a.m. New York to 8:00 a.m. Use calendar arithmetic in a named zone.

nodes.label: timestamptz not timestamp
nodes.rationale: timestamptz stores an instant. timestamp is a wall-clock reading with no zone.

nodes.label: Catch up from state not clock
nodes.rationale: Process where processed_at is null, not where created_at::date = today. A late run then self-heals.
nodes.norm_label: catch up from state not clock

nodes.label: Midnight stored as an instant
nodes.rationale: Compute the deadline once in the zone that owns the rule. Then expires_at <= now() is zone-independent.

nodes.label: Store UTC convert at the edge
nodes.rationale: An instant is unambiguous. A calendar date depends on who is looking. Store the user's timezone.
nodes.norm_label: store utc convert at the edge

nodes.label: Custom lookup skips literal IPs
nodes.rationale: http.request lookup is never called for a literal IP. Parse-time net.isIP is required alongside connect-time checks.

nodes.label: Server-side request forgery
nodes.rationale: The server fetches a user URL from inside the network: cloud metadata 169.254.169.254, loopback admin ports, private ranges.

nodes.label: Adding an enum value to a response
nodes.rationale: Breaking: exhaustive switches and TypeScript unions meet a value they have no branch for. Ship handling first, then emit.
nodes.norm_label: adding an enum value to a response

nodes.label: Request vs response compatibility direction
nodes.rationale: Response: adding is safe, removing or narrowing is not. Request: relaxing is safe, tightening is not. Same verb, opposite answers.

nodes.label: Expand-migrate-contract
nodes.rationale: A rename is a removal plus an addition. Add the new field, migrate consumers, remove the old only after telemetry shows zero usage.

nodes.label: ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES
nodes.rationale: Defaults are keyed on the creating role, not the schema. Omit FOR ROLE and a DBA records a rule for postgres while migration tables stay ungranted.

nodes.label: IS DISTINCT FROM
nodes.rationale: Null-safe comparison; WHERE v IS DISTINCT FROM 30 includes NULLs that v <> 30 drops.

nodes.label: NOT EXISTS anti-join
nodes.rationale: Handles NULL correctly and usually plans as an anti-join rather than a hashed subplan.

nodes.label: NOT IN with NULL drops all rows
nodes.rationale: 2 NOT IN (1, NULL) expands to true AND unknown → NULL, so the row is dropped. Prefer NOT EXISTS.
nodes.norm_label: not in with null drops all rows

nodes.label: SQL three-valued logic
nodes.rationale: NULL is absence; comparisons yield unknown. WHERE keeps only true, so col = NULL matches nothing. Use IS NULL or IS NOT DISTINCT FROM.

nodes.label: CHECK does not reject NULL
nodes.rationale: NULL >= 18 is unknown; CHECK rejects only false. Pair CHECK with NOT NULL, or write CHECK (col IS NULL OR …).

nodes.label: now() vs clock_timestamp()
nodes.rationale: now() is transaction start and stays constant; clock_timestamp() is wall clock per call.

nodes.label: DEFAULT now() is transaction start
nodes.rationale: Two inserts 150 ms apart in one transaction got identical timestamps. Use clock_timestamp() for wall-clock per row.

nodes.label: Generated expression must be IMMUTABLE
nodes.rationale: now(), random(), nextval(), other tables, STABLE locale functions → 42P17. Falsely marking IMMUTABLE silently freezes a wrong stored value.

nodes.label: No VIRTUAL generated columns in PG 18
nodes.rationale: STORED only. For compute-on-read use a view or expression index. Changing the expression is drop + re-add and rewrites the table.
nodes.norm_label: no virtual generated columns in pg 18

nodes.label: GENERATED ALWAYS AS STORED
nodes.rationale: Computed on write from same-row IMMUTABLE inputs and stored. Cannot drift because writes raise 428C9.

nodes.label: DISTINCT ON
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL-only: keep the first row per group as ORDER BY produced them. DISTINCT ON (user_id) … ORDER BY user_id, at DESC is latest event per user, whole row.

nodes.label: DISTINCT ON vs row_number vs LATERAL
nodes.rationale: DISTINCT ON for top-1 over a whole table; row_number() for top-N or the rank; LATERAL when the outer set is small and indexed, and to keep groups with no rows.
nodes.norm_label: distinct on vs row_number vs lateral

nodes.label: Plain DISTINCT
nodes.rationale: Deduplicates the entire computed select list. A unique column in the list makes every row distinct. Treats NULLs as equal. Do not use it to mask join fan-out.

nodes.label: MERGE is not concurrency-safe for upsert
nodes.rationale: MERGE can still raise a unique violation under concurrent inserts because it does not use the unique index as an arbiter the same way ON CONFLICT does.
nodes.norm_label: merge is not concurrency-safe for upsert

nodes.label: MERGE
nodes.rationale: SQL-standard insert/update/delete in one pass from a source. Not a drop-in ON CONFLICT replacement; wrong tool for concurrent upsert. Does support RETURNING and merge_action().

nodes.label: TRUNCATE CASCADE vs named tables
nodes.rationale: Inbound FKs raise 0A000. CASCADE empties referencing tables transitively, unlike DROP CASCADE which removes objects not data.

nodes.label: TRUNCATE skips row triggers
nodes.rationale: AFTER DELETE FOR EACH ROW never fires. Audit and counter side effects silently vanish. Use AFTER TRUNCATE FOR EACH STATEMENT.

nodes.label: TRUNCATE RESTART IDENTITY
nodes.rationale: Plain TRUNCATE leaves sequences alone. After 10000 rows the next id was 10001.

nodes.label: TRUNCATE is transactional
nodes.rationale: Unlike MySQL and Oracle, PostgreSQL TRUNCATE rolls back. It takes ACCESS EXCLUSIVE until commit.

nodes.label: TRUNCATE vs DELETE
nodes.rationale: DELETE is O(rows) and fires triggers. TRUNCATE is near O(1), reclaims space immediately, and has different semantics.

nodes.label: Archive with DELETE RETURNING then INSERT
nodes.rationale: WITH moved AS (DELETE … RETURNING *) INSERT INTO archive SELECT * FROM moved. No window where the row is in neither table or both. Measured: 6 orders → 5, 1 archived.
nodes.norm_label: archive with delete returning then insert

nodes.label: Data-modifying CTE
nodes.rationale: INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/MERGE inside WITH, chained by RETURNING. One statement is already atomic — no BEGIN needed. Always MATERIALIZED; NOT MATERIALIZED cannot inline a write.

nodes.label: Unreferenced write CTE still runs
nodes.rationale: A SELECT CTE nobody references can be discarded; a write is a promised side effect and executes once regardless. Deleting the reference but not the CTE leaves a write running.

nodes.label: Two write CTEs on the same row
nodes.rationale: One update is silently lost — a: 1, b: 0, no error. SERIALIZABLE does not help: there is only one transaction. Merge into one UPDATE, make sets disjoint, or use separate statements.
nodes.norm_label: two write ctes on the same row

nodes.label: The snapshot rule
nodes.rationale: Every part of one statement shares one snapshot taken before it began. Sibling SELECT on the table cannot see a CTE write (visible_to_sibling: 0, visible_via_returning: 1). CTE execution order is unspecified; one snapshot makes the result deterministic.

nodes.label: this is decided by the call site
nodes.rationale: MDN: if the call is obj.f(), this refers to obj. Same function object, different this depending on the receiver. Nothing travels when extracted.
nodes.norm_label: this is decided by the call site

nodes.label: this in a class field initialiser
nodes.rationale: Already bound — to the instance for an instance field, to the class for a static one. Why an arrow field captures the instance permanently.
nodes.norm_label: this in a class field initialiser

nodes.label: Four ways a method loses this
nodes.rationale: Assign to a variable; pass as a callback; destructure it out; re-attach to a different object. Callbacks are the most common form.
nodes.norm_label: four ways a method loses this

nodes.label: Method borrowing
nodes.rationale: Assigning bird.sayHi = car.sayHi and calling it gives this === bird. A feature of the same rule that makes extracting a method dangerous.

nodes.label: Sloppy-mode this substitution
nodes.rationale: In non-strict mode undefined/null this is replaced with globalThis. Writes silently create globals. Strict (modules, classes) throws TypeError instead.

nodes.label: thisArg on iteration methods
nodes.rationale: forEach, map, filter, some, every, find, findIndex, flatMap take optional thisArg. reduce, reduceRight and sort do not. Arrows sidestep it.

nodes.label: bind only works once
nodes.rationale: A bound function's this is permanent. Re-binding does nothing; call/apply cannot override it.

nodes.label: removeEventListener identity trap
nodes.rationale: Removal matches by function identity. An inline arrow is a new function each time, so removeEventListener silently does nothing.

nodes.label: this inside methods
nodes.rationale: A method is not attached to its object. this is decided by how it is called — the binding is created by the dot.

nodes.label: Iteration callback (element, index, array)
nodes.rationale: Every iteration method passes three arguments. Passing a named function whose later params mean something misfires.

nodes.label: 07.2 · The fixes, and which to choose
nodes.norm_label: 07.2 · the fixes, and which to choose

nodes.label: Arrow class field
nodes.rationale: Field initialiser runs with this bound to the instance; the arrow captures it lexically. Own property per instance; not overridable; no super.

nodes.label: bind in the constructor
nodes.rationale: Creates a new function with this fixed and stores it as an own property that shadows the prototype method. Binding is permanent.

nodes.label: call / apply / thisArg for one call
nodes.rationale: Sets this for one call, not permanently. Not a fix for the detached-method problem if you are already at the call site.
nodes.norm_label: call / apply / thisarg for one call

nodes.label: Per-instance cost of bound or arrow methods
nodes.rationale: bind-in-constructor and arrow fields create one function object per instance and take the method off the prototype, blocking override and super.
nodes.norm_label: per-instance cost of bound or arrow methods

nodes.label: Wrap at the call site
nodes.rationale: () => this.m() leaves the method a plain prototype method, costs nothing, stays overridable. Best default except removable listeners.

nodes.label: CYCLE clause
nodes.rationale: PG 14+. CYCLE id SET is_cycle USING path flags the row where the loop closed and stops. Only option that reports the cycle. A self-referencing FK does not prevent cycles.

nodes.label: Recursive depth guard
nodes.rationale: WHERE t.d < N bounds work unconditionally. Cannot tell a legitimately deep tree from a loop. Measured: 8-row table produced 107 rows before d < 40 stopped it. UNION instead of UNION ALL dedups but fails if rows carry a depth/path column.

nodes.label: SEARCH DEPTH/BREADTH FIRST
nodes.rationale: Creates a sortable ord column; you must still ORDER BY ord. DEPTH FIRST follows each branch to its end — what a rendered tree needs.

nodes.label: WITH RECURSIVE
nodes.rationale: Anchor UNION ALL recursive term joining the table to the CTE. Missing RECURSIVE is 42P01 (ordinary missing-table). Carry depth and path in the term. Reverse the join to climb. Index the join column or cost is depth × full scan.

nodes.label: WorkTable Scan / Recursive Union
nodes.rationale: Each round reads only the previous iteration's rows, not everything found so far. loops= on the recursive term is iteration count (depth). Aggregates are forbidden in the recursive term (42P19) because they would summarise a fragment.

nodes.label: release(true) destroys the connection
nodes.rationale: Use after FATAL, client-side query_timeout, or unknown session state. Cheaper than poisoning later borrowers.

nodes.label: pool.end()
nodes.rationale: Waits for in-flight queries then permanently retires the pool. A 300 ms query held end() 319 ms. A second end() throws.

nodes.label: query_timeout
nodes.rationale: Client-side give-up; the server keeps executing. Users retry and the server accumulates work nobody is waiting for. Set slightly above statement_timeout.

nodes.label: statement_timeout
nodes.rationale: Server-side cancel; SQLSTATE 57014; connection stays usable. The only timeout that actually stops the database doing work.

nodes.label: Shutdown order: server then pool
nodes.rationale: server.close() first, then wait for in-flight requests, then pool.end(). Reversed, deploys burst 500s.

nodes.label: alpine vs debian collation
nodes.rationale: Same PostgreSQL 18.4 and en_US.utf8: musl sorts by byte value, glibc applies locale rules. ORDER BY changes if the base image does not match production.

nodes.label: Wait on pg_isready not sleep
nodes.rationale: The container reports running before TCP accepts. First-time init starts the server twice. A fixed sleep is flaky or slow.

nodes.label: Local PostgreSQL in Podman/Docker
nodes.rationale: Pin postgres:18-alpine on host port 55432. POSTGRES_* vars apply only on first data-directory init.

nodes.label: Prefer 127.0.0.1 over localhost
nodes.rationale: localhost can resolve to ::1 first; a container published only on IPv4 refuses it. Node 24 autoSelectFamily hides this; the literal address does not depend on it.

nodes.label: Connect on 127.0.0.1 never localhost
nodes.rationale: Node resolves localhost to ::1 first. A container published on IPv4 only is not listening there.

nodes.label: SELECT ... FOR UPDATE
nodes.rationale: Locks returned rows until commit. Two concurrent adds produced 130 with no retries. Readers still see the old MVCC version.

nodes.label: Lost update
nodes.rationale: Two requests both read 100, wrote 110 and 120; both reported ok; expected 130. No error.

nodes.label: version column
nodes.rationale: UPDATE … SET balance, version = version + 1 WHERE id AND version = $n. Increment in the same statement. Stale write is rowCount 0 → 409. updated_at fails when now() is shared in one transaction.

nodes.label: Do slow work first, lock last
nodes.rationale: Eight 100 ms requests: 863 ms with work inside the lock vs 143 ms with lock only to write. Re-read the locked row before writing.
nodes.norm_label: do slow work first, lock last

nodes.label: Retry only relative operations
nodes.rationale: Add-N can retry. Absolute 'set to what the user saw' is a 409. Cap attempts and back off. ETag/If-Match is the HTTP spelling (412).

nodes.label: Phase 2 — Data types and the relational model
nodes.norm_label: phase 2 — data types and the relational model

nodes.label: Phase 3 — DDL tables constraints schema design
nodes.norm_label: phase 3 — ddl tables constraints schema design

nodes.label: JSX braces take expressions not statements
nodes.norm_label: jsx braces take expressions not statements

nodes.label: style prop takes a camelCased object
nodes.norm_label: style prop takes a camelcased object

nodes.label: four conditional forms (&&, ternary, early return, lookup)
nodes.norm_label: four conditional forms (&&, ternary, early return, lookup)

nodes.label: Error boundaries require a class
nodes.rationale: No function equivalent for getDerivedStateFromError or componentDidCatch in React 19.

nodes.label: getDerivedStateFromError vs componentDidCatch
nodes.rationale: Static method is render-phase and must be pure. Instance method is commit-phase logging with the component stack.

nodes.label: memo compares props only
nodes.rationale: useState already bails out on the same state. PureComponent also compared state.

nodes.label: Component, PureComponent, shouldComponentUpdate
nodes.rationale: Always render, shallow compare, or write the comparison. Function equivalents: plain, memo, memo with compare.

nodes.label: HOCs wrap around a component
nodes.rationale: A hook cannot wrap from the outside. memo, forwardRef, error boundaries, instrumentation stay HOC-shaped.

nodes.label: RSC composition via children
nodes.rationale: A Client Component can receive a Server Component as children but cannot import one. Composition keeps server code out of the bundle.

nodes.label: Elements are ordinary values
nodes.rationale: JSX builds a descriptor; creating an element does not render it.

nodes.label: Pass expensive subtrees as children
nodes.rationale: The element object is created outside the stateful wrapper, so React skips that subtree without memo.

nodes.label: The context hole
nodes.rationale: Create the element where the value lives and pass the finished element down. Intermediates never mention the value.

nodes.label: Lift vs composition vs context vs store
nodes.rationale: Server data is a cache, not lifted UI state. Props first, composition next, context when props become unwieldy.
nodes.norm_label: lift vs composition vs context vs store

nodes.label: Props immutable by contract not enforcement
nodes.rationale: React does not freeze props or nested objects. Ask the parent for a new object instead of mutating.
nodes.norm_label: props immutable by contract not enforcement

nodes.label: Mind your own business
nodes.rationale: Do not change objects or variables that existed before the call: props, state, context, refs, module variables.

nodes.label: Local mutation
nodes.rationale: Objects created during this render are yours. Did this object exist before the render started?

nodes.label: Side effects belong in event handlers
nodes.rationale: Handlers run later, outside the rule. useEffect is the fallback after handlers are exhausted.
nodes.norm_label: side effects belong in event handlers

nodes.label: The purity rule is smaller than people think
nodes.rationale: React requires not mutating shared data, not unconditional immutability. Handlers and effects can do anything.
nodes.norm_label: the purity rule is smaller than people think

nodes.label: Extra setup+cleanup cycle
nodes.rationale: Development-only cycle before the first real setup: setup → cleanup → setup. Asserts mount-path symmetry.

nodes.label: Cleanup is not unmount code
nodes.rationale: Cleanup runs on dependency change, unmount, and the StrictMode extra cycle. It is tied to the effect's dependencies, not the component's lifetime.

nodes.label: setup → cleanup → setup must be indistinguishable
nodes.rationale: The user should not be able to tell production's single setup from development's extra cycle. Incomplete cleanup fails that invariant.
nodes.norm_label: setup → cleanup → setup must be indistinguishable

nodes.label: Remount principle
nodes.rationale: Visiting a page should not differ from visiting it, clicking a link, then pressing Back. StrictMode remounts once in development to verify that.

nodes.label: StrictMode only doubles the mount
nodes.rationale: The extra cycle is attached to mounting, not every re-run. Dependency-change leaks pass a green StrictMode.

nodes.label: Array.prototype.every
nodes.rationale: true if all match; stops on first false. Empty array returns true (vacuous). Gates need length > 0 &&.

nodes.label: every is vacuously true on []
nodes.rationale: MDN: for-all over the empty set. cart.every(inStock) passes for an empty cart.

nodes.label: Array.prototype.filter
nodes.rationale: New array of matches; visits every element. filter(...)[0] is a common misuse of find.

nodes.label: Array.prototype.find
nodes.rationale: First matching element or undefined; stops at the match. findLast searches from the end.

nodes.label: Array.prototype.findIndex
nodes.rationale: Index of first match, or -1. if (i) is inverted: 0 is falsy and -1 is truthy. Always compare !== -1.

nodes.label: Array.prototype.forEach
nodes.rationale: Always returns undefined and is not chainable. No way to stop other than throwing. Wrong tool if you need break/await.

nodes.label: Array.prototype.map
nodes.rationale: New array, same length, callback return values. Misused as a loop it allocates an array of undefined.

nodes.label: Array.prototype.some
nodes.rationale: true if any element matches; stops on first true. Empty array → false.

nodes.label: async forEach discards promises
nodes.rationale: forEach expects a synchronous function and does not wait for promises. MDN example prints 0 instead of 14. filter(async) filters nothing because every promise is truthy.

nodes.label: find visits holes; forEach skips them
nodes.rationale: MDN: find is invoked for every index, treating holes as undefined. forEach skips empty slots. Same sparse array: 7 visits vs 3.
nodes.norm_label: find visits holes; foreach skips them

nodes.label: map(parseInt) radix bug
nodes.rationale: ["1","2","3"].map(parseInt) is [1, NaN, NaN] because index arrives as parseInt radix.

nodes.label: Array iteration methods
nodes.rationale: Eight methods; pick by what you want back. They differ in return value, early stop, and whether they visit holes.

nodes.label: for...of for control flow
nodes.rationale: break, continue, return, and await work in for...of and none of them work in forEach. Use the loop when the body is control flow.

nodes.label: Mutating an array while iterating
nodes.rationale: Range is fixed before the first callback. Appended elements are not visited; removals cause skips. Build a new array.

nodes.label: for...of await vs Promise.all(map)
nodes.rationale: for...of + await is sequential. Promise.all over map is concurrent. Pick by independence and load.

nodes.label: Editor vs CI compiler version drift
nodes.rationale: Same loose.ts: 7.0.2 four errors, 5.9.3 exit 0, because the strict default changed. Fix: Use Workspace Version and typescript.tsdk.
nodes.norm_label: editor vs ci compiler version drift

nodes.label: lib.d.ts updates break untouched files
nodes.rationale: TS ships updated DOM and ES declarations. A lib change produces errors in code you did not write. Read breaking changes and lib.d.ts updates.

nodes.label: TypeScript minors can break builds
nodes.rationale: Minors add checks. A caret range lets a colleague's npm install produce errors yours does not. Pin the exact compiler and upgrade in its own PR.

nodes.label: strict defaults to true in TypeScript 7
nodes.rationale: tsc --help --all reports default: true on 7.0.2 and false on 5.9.3. Unflagged loose.ts reports TS7006, TS18047, TS2564, TS18046.
nodes.norm_label: strict defaults to true in typescript 7

nodes.label: TypeScript 7 changed option defaults
nodes.rationale: strict, esModuleInterop true; moduleResolution bundler or node16/nodenext following module. Unset projects behave differently on 7.

nodes.label: Styling hooks that are not classes
nodes.norm_label: styling hooks that are not classes

nodes.label: query parser default simple
nodes.rationale: Express 5 default is simple (was extended in 4). Nested a[b]=1 is not an object. Measured on 5.2.1: query parser = "simple".

nodes.label: Express docs qs vs simple contradiction
nodes.rationale: req.query reference still says default uses qs (Express 4 leftover). Settings table and migration guide say simple. Read back app.get('query parser').
nodes.norm_label: express docs qs vs simple contradiction

nodes.label: req.params
nodes.rationale: Come from the path pattern. Always strings. Coerce and validate at the edge; never trust req.params.id as a number.

nodes.label: req.query
nodes.rationale: Query strings are not part of the route pattern. They land after the path matches. Duplicate keys become arrays under simple.

nodes.label: simple vs extended query parser
nodes.rationale: simple (Node querystring): a[b]=1 stays a literal key. Express 4 extended (qs) produced nested objects. Upgrades break req.query.filter.status.

nodes.label: Primitive versus object
nodes.rationale: Primitives copy on assignment, compare by value, and are immutable. Objects share by reference, compare by identity, and are mutable.

nodes.label: JSON.stringify throws on BigInt
nodes.rationale: JSON has no BigInt type. Use a replacer to string; do not patch BigInt.prototype.toJSON.

nodes.label: Autoboxing
nodes.rationale: Property access on a primitive wraps it, reads the method from String/Number/Boolean.prototype, then discards the wrapper. Assignments do not persist.

nodes.label: Number literal method-dot trap
nodes.rationale: 5.toFixed(2) is a SyntaxError because 5. starts a decimal. Write (5).toFixed(2).

nodes.label: Ponyfill
nodes.rationale: Exports the implementation instead of patching the global. Prefer in libraries; reserve true polyfills for an app entry you control.

nodes.label: Array sort default string compare
nodes.rationale: [10,9,1].sort() is [1,10,9] because SortCompare converts to strings. Specified, not a quirk.

nodes.label: ECMA-262 living standard
nodes.rationale: Read tc39.es/ecma262, not a numbered-edition PDF. Host APIs like fetch and document live in WHATWG, not ECMA-262.

nodes.label: Strings are UTF-16 code units
nodes.rationale: .length, charAt and slice count 16-bit units. Code points above U+FFFF are surrogate pairs. slice(0,1) on an emoji can yield a lone \ud83d.

nodes.label: Intl.Segmenter graphemes
nodes.rationale: 👨‍👩‍👧 is 8 code units, 5 code points, 1 grapheme. Truncate and reverse at grapheme level. Word granularity is locale-aware.

nodes.label: Unicode NFC versus NFD
nodes.rationale: é can be U+00E9 or e plus combining acute. They render the same and are not ===. Normalise NFC at the boundary. Sort with Intl.Collator, not default sort.

nodes.label: Infinity and -Infinity
nodes.rationale: Division by zero does not throw. Propagates silently. JSON.stringify turns Infinity and NaN into null.

nodes.label: Math.max empty identity
nodes.rationale: Math.max() and Math.max(...[]) return -Infinity, the identity for max — not 0 and not an error.

nodes.label: Number.isFinite validation
nodes.rationale: Rejects NaN and both infinities. Number.isNaN(Infinity) is false so overflow passes a NaN-only check.

nodes.label: Math.max(...arr) argument cap
nodes.rationale: Very large spreads throw RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded. Use reduce. Empty spread is -Infinity.

nodes.label: NaN poisons every relational
nodes.rationale: !(a<b) is not equivalent to a>=b when NaN is possible. Guard with Number.isFinite.

nodes.label: Rest excluded from fn.length
nodes.rationale: Rest must be last. ((a,...r)=>0).length is 1. Libraries that inspect arity see only fixed parameters.

nodes.label: Defaults evaluated at call time
nodes.rationale: Stored unevaluated; run left to right only for omitted arguments. order(1,undefined,3) evaluates only b.

nodes.label: fn.length stops at first default
