nodes.rationale: (a=1,b)=>0 reports 0. Express error handlers (length===4) silently stop routing if a default is added. Default in the body instead.

nodes.label: Shared-default myth
nodes.rationale: list=[] is fresh each call. list=shared mutates one outer array. Constructing defaults are safe; referencing defaults are not.

nodes.label: Parameter scope vs body scope
nodes.rationale: Any default creates two scopes. A default closure keeps the parameter x; var x in the body is a different binding. scopes('param') is ['body','param'].

nodes.label: Default this binding
nodes.rationale: Bare fn() is undefined in strict and globalThis in sloppy. Strict turns a silent global write into TypeError.

nodes.label: Module top-level this
nodes.rationale: ES module top-level this is undefined. CommonJS top-level this is module.exports. Use globalThis for the global object.

nodes.label: Accidental global
nodes.rationale: Assigning to an undeclared name creates a global in sloppy mode and throws ReferenceError in strict/modules.

nodes.label: Module top level is not global
nodes.rationale: Top-level var is a global only in a classic script. ES modules and CommonJS keep it off globalThis. let/const never create global properties.
nodes.norm_label: module top level is not global

nodes.label: Script top-level var as non-configurable global
nodes.rationale: In a classic script, top-level var is a non-configurable global property and cannot be deleted. Modules do not do this.
nodes.norm_label: script top-level var as non-configurable global

nodes.label: Property shadowing
nodes.rationale: The first match wins and own properties are always first. The prototype's value is untouched and still reachable via Object.getPrototypeOf.

nodes.label: Shared mutable prototype state
nodes.rationale: Fn.prototype.items = [] is one array shared by every instance. push is a read then a mutation, so no shadowing own property is created. Create per-instance fields instead.

nodes.label: A write creates an own property
nodes.rationale: Reads walk the chain; writes do not. Assignment shadows a prototype data property. The prototype and other inheritors are untouched.
nodes.norm_label: a write creates an own property

nodes.label: Derived class field initialisation order
nodes.rationale: Base fields run at the start of the constructor. Derived fields run immediately before super() returns, so an overridden method called from the parent constructor sees them still undefined.

nodes.label: Instance field versus prototype method
nodes.rationale: A field is an own enumerable property per instance. A method is one shared non-enumerable function on Ctor.prototype. items = [] must be a field.

nodes.label: Intl.Segmenter
nodes.rationale: Code points are not graphemes; skin-tone and family emoji are several code points that display as one character.

nodes.label: Array.prototype.join
nodes.rationale: null and undefined become empty strings, so missing values silently become empty CSV fields.

nodes.label: String.prototype.split
nodes.rationale: No separator returns [whole string]. limit truncates and discards the remainder. Capture groups in a regex separator are included.

nodes.label: split("") splits UTF-16 code units
nodes.rationale: Emoji and other non-BMP characters become surrogate halves. [...str] and Array.from yield code points.

nodes.label: empty string split is [""]
nodes.rationale: "".split(",") is [""] not [], so field counts are 1 for empty CSV input.

nodes.label: Node.js is a runtime, not a language
nodes.rationale: A program that runs JavaScript outside the browser and gives it access to your computer. Same language. Different powers.
nodes.norm_label: node.js is a runtime, not a language

nodes.label: V8
nodes.rationale: V8 is the brain: parses, compiles and garbage-collects JavaScript and only does one thing at a time.

nodes.label: Bun on JavaScriptCore
nodes.rationale: Startup difference is real and matters for serverless and CLI. Throughput usually does not, because the bottleneck is almost never the runtime.

nodes.label: Deno permission model
nodes.rationale: No file, network or env access unless granted. Deno 2 added npm, package.json and node_modules while keeping the sandbox.

nodes.label: Deoptimization
nodes.rationale: A function that keeps flipping between optimised and interpreter — a deopt loop — can be slower than one that was never optimised.

nodes.label: Hidden classes
nodes.rationale: Give objects all their properties at construction and do not delete properties from hot objects. Do not restructure for shape stability until a profiler points here.

nodes.label: The event loop is the program
nodes.rationale: Your file is the setup for the program. The process does not exit when the file ends; the loop keeps running as long as work is pending.
nodes.norm_label: the event loop is the program

nodes.label: Same language, different host
nodes.rationale: The browser supplies the DOM and a strict sandbox; Node supplies filesystem, sockets, processes and no sandbox at all.

nodes.label: Build on Node for production fullstack work
nodes.rationale: Not because it is the fastest, but because compatibility gaps are the expensive kind of problem and most apps are bound by the database anyway.
nodes.norm_label: build on node for production fullstack work

nodes.label: Date.toJSON ISO string
nodes.rationale: The most common JSON bug: a parsed clone holds a string, so .getTime() throws far from the serialisation.

nodes.label: toJSON hook
nodes.rationale: The return value is serialised instead of the object. Lives with the type, unlike a per-call-site replacer.

nodes.label: Reviver is innermost-first
nodes.rationale: Depth-first: children are transformed before parents. Root is called last with key "".

nodes.label: Reviving Date from JSON
nodes.rationale: Match ISO strings or key.endsWith("At"). A loose pattern turns version strings into dates.

nodes.label: Reviver must return value
nodes.rationale: Returning undefined deletes the property. Doing so for the root deletes the entire result.

nodes.label: PerformanceObserver GC entries
nodes.rationale: Observe entryTypes gc; histogram duration and watch multi-ms spikes. kind maps through NODE_PERFORMANCE_GC_* constants.

nodes.label: Process metrics — RSS, heap, handles
nodes.rationale: RSS, heap used, and active handles together debug 'memory is high' without guessing.

nodes.label: Memory leaks
nodes.rationale: Almost always a growing set of objects still reachable from a root — a Map, a closure, a listener list — not malloc forgot free.

nodes.label: Common leak sources
nodes.rationale: Most Node leaks are unbounded caches, never-removed listeners, closures over large objects, or uncleared timers/sockets.

nodes.label: GC basics
nodes.rationale: V8 frees memory you can no longer reach. You control heap size, allocation rate, and whether GC pauses show up as event-loop lag.

nodes.label: Conventional commits
nodes.rationale: feat/fix/feat! machine-map to MINOR/PATCH/MAJOR and generate changelogs.

nodes.label: False patch
nodes.rationale: A PATCH-labeled release that changes behaviour consumers relied on — a SemVer violation.

nodes.label: semantic-release automation
nodes.rationale: Optional automation of SemVer policy; still needs least-privilege write tokens in CI.

nodes.label: Semantic Versioning
nodes.rationale: MAJOR breaking, MINOR compatible feature, PATCH compatible fix — a promise to consumers.

nodes.label: Node core SemVer compatibility culture
nodes.rationale: Millions of dependents; breaking changes are rare and deliberate. Features that belong in userland get closed.

nodes.label: Log and exit from crash handlers
nodes.norm_label: log and exit from crash handlers

nodes.label: Catastrophic backtracking
nodes.rationale: Nested quantifiers, overlapping alternation, or a quantified group that can fail. The failing near-match is the expensive case; valid inputs short-circuit.

nodes.label: Regular expression denial of service
nodes.rationale: A slow regex is a security problem because Node matches synchronously on the only request thread. Node 24 has no engine-level regex timeout.

nodes.label: Worker-thread regex timeout
nodes.rationale: AbortSignal and setTimeout cannot interrupt a synchronous match. A worker_threads worker can be terminate()d; re2 is the linear-engine alternative.

nodes.label: ReDoS
nodes.rationale: One backtracking regex on the event loop stalls the whole Node process. Verified Node 24.19.0: 28 chars → 3.6 s CPU, 10 ms interval fired zero times.

nodes.label: ReDoS input length cap
nodes.rationale: Input length is the exponent. Cap then reject — do not truncate, which can turn a hostile non-match into an accidental match. Cheapest mitigation.

nodes.label: Dummy password hash
nodes.rationale: Verify against a boot-time dummy with the same algorithm parameters when the user is missing. Measured 71.2 vs 69.5 ms. Random delay is not a fix.

nodes.label: Timing attack
nodes.rationale: A first-mismatch loop leaks the matching prefix. Remote byte-level attacks need thousands of samples; endpoint-level millisecond leaks survive jitter.

nodes.label: crypto.timingSafeEqual
nodes.rationale: Compares every byte. Throws ERR_CRYPTO_TIMING_SAFE_EQUAL_LENGTH on unequal lengths. Takes Buffer/TypedArray, not strings. ~0.2 µs per call.

nodes.label: Login user enumeration
nodes.rationale: Skipping the password hash for unknown emails is an 83 ms oracle. Same error text, status, and signup/reset behaviour are also required.

nodes.label: Timing attacks
nodes.rationale: How long code takes is data. Naive compare staircase 5.4→141.2 ms; the exploited leak is 83 ms user enumeration on login.

nodes.label: Module mocking with mock.module()
nodes.rationale: Verified 2026-08 on Node 24.19.0. Experimental, Stability 1.0 Early development.

nodes.label: Test doubles — stub, spy, mock, fake
nodes.rationale: Verified 2026-08 on Node 24.19.0. The four are distinguished by what they replace and what you assert on.
nodes.norm_label: test doubles — stub, spy, mock, fake

nodes.label: Fixtures, factories, and test data
nodes.rationale: Verified 2026-08 on Node 24.19.0. Test data rots when written once, shared everywhere, and then nobody dares change it.

nodes.label: Coverage — why 100% is a bad target
nodes.rationale: Verified 2026-08 on Node 24.19.0. Coverage measures which lines executed, not whether anything was checked.
nodes.norm_label: coverage — why 100% is a bad target

nodes.label: Vitest and Jest — when they earn their place
nodes.rationale: Verified 2026-08: node:test 0.22s, Vitest 4.1.10 1.43s, Jest 30.4.2 1.52s on the same 50-test suite.
nodes.norm_label: vitest and jest — when they earn their place

nodes.label: Biome
nodes.rationale: Measured 0.09s vs 0.75s for ESLint plus Prettier, doing lint, format and import organisation. No JS plugin API and no type-aware rules.

nodes.label: ESLint flat config
nodes.rationale: eslint.config.mjs is the only format in ESLint 9+. No extends (spread objects), no env (globals package), no nested-file cascade — one file scoped by files globs.

nodes.label: Linter vs formatter
nodes.rationale: A formatter rewrites layout and has no opinion about correctness; a linter finds legal code that is probably wrong. You need both, from two tools or one.

nodes.label: Prettier
nodes.rationale: Formatting only, almost unconfigurable. Pair with eslint-config-prettier so ESLint stylistic rules do not fight it on save.

nodes.label: Type-aware lint rules
nodes.rationale: no-floating-promises needs the type checker. Biome cannot replace typescript-eslint. Highest-value Node rule: catches a missing await at write time.

nodes.label: Phase 6 — Data access
nodes.rationale: Node-side only: pooling, parameterized queries, pg and Mongo drivers, transactions, N+1, repository pattern. Databases live in their own sections.

nodes.label: Phase 9 — Testing (syllabus)
nodes.rationale: node:test, assert, unit/integration/e2e, DI, API and async testing, mock.module (Stability 1.0), doubles, coverage, Vitest/Jest, Testcontainers, contracts.

nodes.label: Phase 9 — Testing
nodes.rationale: Complete — 20 pages on Node 24.19.0. Built on node:test; Vitest or Jest only where they earn it. Measurements are the point.

nodes.label: Linting as cheapest testing layer
nodes.rationale: A type-aware linter catches a floating promise, unused variable and == in milliseconds on every file. Wire it into CI via verify, not just the editor.

nodes.label: Recap rule with Node Phase 6
nodes.rationale: Pool sizing, transaction propagation, N+1, repository rationale, ORM comparison belong to Node 6. PG Part 3 recaps ≤40 lines and links; it does not re-own those pages.

nodes.label: Pact consumer-driven contracts
nodes.rationale: Consumer publishes a pact file to a broker; provider replays it in its CI; can-i-deploy gates release. Worth it with several independent teams; one team should share a schema package.

nodes.label: Shared Zod UserResponse schema
nodes.rationale: Provider validates the real handler; consumer validates the mock. Both sides fail on a breaking change; neither can change it alone.

nodes.label: Phase 8 — Security
nodes.rationale: argon2/scrypt/bcrypt, sessions vs JWT, injection/XSS/CSRF/SSRF/prototype pollution/ReDoS, zod at the boundary, secrets, Permission Model.

nodes.label: Contract written independently of the model
nodes.rationale: A schema generated from the model cannot fail: both sides agree on the new shape while the frontend still breaks. Independence is the entire mechanism.
nodes.norm_label: contract written independently of the model

nodes.label: Changing a field's meaning, same type
nodes.rationale: Worst change on the table: amount in euros becoming cents validates perfectly and is off by a hundred. Never redefine a field — add a new one and deprecate the old.
nodes.norm_label: changing a field's meaning, same type

nodes.label: Deprecation and Sunset headers
nodes.rationale: Standard headers a client can log. Pair with a usage metric so the contract step is a decision from data, not an announcement.

nodes.label: Adding a response enum value is breaking
nodes.rationale: A consumer with an exhaustive switch or TypeScript union meets a value it has no branch for. Ship handling first, wait for deploy, then emit.
nodes.norm_label: adding a response enum value is breaking

nodes.label: Expand, migrate, contract
nodes.rationale: Add the new field alongside the old, let consumers move, remove the old when telemetry shows zero usage. Version only for restructures that cannot expand.

nodes.label: Rename is removal plus addition
nodes.rationale: Consumer error is identical to a deletion: createdAt expected string, received undefined. There is no just renaming a field across an API boundary.

nodes.label: Response add-safe, request tighten-unsafe
nodes.rationale: Response: adding is safe, removing or narrowing is not. Request: relaxing is safe, tightening is not. Adding a required request field is breaking; adding a response field is not.

nodes.label: Graceful shutdown
nodes.rationale: Stop accepting, drain in-flight, close pools, exit. The thing that makes deploys stop dropping requests. Gate includes surviving SIGTERM mid-request.

nodes.label: Phase 5 — Networking, HTTP, and processes
nodes.rationale: node:http, bodies as streams, fetch, AbortSignal.timeout, graceful SIGTERM shutdown, child_process, cluster, worker_threads.

nodes.label: Phase 11 — Deployment and operations
nodes.rationale: 12-factor config, boot sequence, Dockerize Node, PID 1 and SIGTERM, trust proxy, zero-downtime deploys.

nodes.label: API design belongs to Express
nodes.rationale: Nobody builds an API on raw node:http. Node teaches it so Express is not magic. REST, middleware, pagination, versioning, OpenAPI, RBAC stay in Express.

nodes.label: EXCLUDE USING gist
nodes.rationale: No two bookings for the same room may overlap. Cannot be expressed with UNIQUE or CHECK; app-level checks race. Use '[)' bounds so back-to-back bookings do not overlap.

nodes.label: Consistency as constraints
nodes.rationale: Consistency is whatever constraints say. UNIQUE, PRIMARY KEY, EXCLUDE and foreign keys can be DEFERRABLE; CHECK and NOT NULL are always immediate.

nodes.label: FK-without-index audit query
nodes.rationale: pg_constraint contype=f vs a valid index whose leading columns match the FK columns. Composite counts if leftmost prefix and order match; indisvalid required.

nodes.label: ON DELETE CASCADE needs child FK index
nodes.norm_label: on delete cascade needs child fk index

nodes.label: Referencing-side FK index
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL indexes the referenced PK/UNIQUE side automatically and never the referencing column. Without that index every parent DELETE scans the child — 33.2 ms vs 6.2 ms on 300000 children.

nodes.label: FOR KEY SHARE
nodes.rationale: What an FK insert takes on the parent. Conflicts only with FOR UPDATE, so a child insert does not block a non-key parent update.

nodes.label: autovacuum_freeze_max_age
nodes.rationale: Anti-wraparound autovacuum at 200 million, under 10% of the 2^31 budget. Runs even if autovacuum is off.

nodes.label: Row freezing
nodes.rationale: VACUUM marks old rows frozen: visible to everyone, no id comparison. relfrozenxid tracks progress; age(relfrozenxid) grows with every database transaction, even on idle tables.

nodes.label: xidWarnLimit and xidStopLimit
nodes.rationale: WARNING at ≈2.134 billion (10 million before stop). Writes refused at ≈2.144 billion. Ten million XIDs is minutes at a few thousand writes/s.

nodes.label: XID wraparound
nodes.rationale: 32-bit XIDs; visibility is modular comparison. If the counter advanced 2^31 past a row's xmin the row would appear future-dated and vanish.

nodes.label: Alert at 500 million not the WARNING
nodes.rationale: The WARNING is the you-already-lost line. Alert at 500 million; treat 200 million as the number that matters. Age past 200 million means the anti-wraparound vacuum cannot advance a pinned horizon.
nodes.norm_label: alert at 500 million not the warning

nodes.label: security_invoker views
nodes.rationale: Views run with the owner's privileges by default, bypassing caller RLS. PostgreSQL 15+ security_invoker = true uses the caller's privileges.

nodes.label: DDL is an ownership right
nodes.rationale: No GRANT DROP or GRANT ALTER. App role with DML still gets 42501 on DROP TABLE. Does not protect rows; TRUNCATE is grantable and should be withheld.

nodes.label: ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES FOR ROLE owner
nodes.rationale: Stops a manual grant on every new table. A hand-created table with a different owner never receives those defaults.
nodes.norm_label: alter default privileges for role owner

nodes.label: GRANT USAGE not CREATE on schema
nodes.rationale: CREATE is grantable; objects the app creates are then owned by the app and the boundary erodes.
nodes.norm_label: grant usage not create on schema

nodes.label: Two connection strings owner vs app
nodes.rationale: Migrations connect as owner; the service must not be able to read MIGRATION_DATABASE_URL. Two variables in one .env is the pattern without the protection.
nodes.norm_label: two connection strings owner vs app

nodes.label: Identity vs serial sequence grant
nodes.rationale: An identity sequence is owned by the column so INSERT needs no USAGE on the sequence. A serial DEFAULT nextval() is an ordinary sequence call and needs GRANT USAGE ON SEQUENCE.

nodes.label: Column grants are additive
nodes.rationale: A column grant adds access; table-wide SELECT from any inherited role makes the column list irrelevant. SELECT * and predicates on ungranted columns fail; count(*) needs no column privilege.

nodes.label: ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES
nodes.rationale: Stores a rule applied when new objects are created; not retroactive. Keyed on the creating role (defaclrole). Omit FOR ROLE and a DBA records a rule for postgres, not the migration role.

nodes.label: GRANT ON ALL TABLES is a snapshot
nodes.rationale: It expands to the tables that exist at execution and stores one ACL each. A table created afterwards is 42501. You also need ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES for future objects.
nodes.norm_label: grant on all tables is a snapshot

nodes.label: View as a column boundary
nodes.rationale: Column grants only widen. A view exposes named columns and cannot be widened by an unrelated group membership.

nodes.label: pg_dump ACCESS SHARE lock
nodes.rationale: Reads and writes proceed; ALTER/DROP/TRUNCATE/VACUUM FULL wait. A waiting ALTER then blocks everything queued behind it. Do not run migrations and dumps in the same window.

nodes.label: pg_dump REPEATABLE READ snapshot
nodes.rationale: 1000 rows inserted during the dump appeared in the source and zero in the restore. Parallel workers share the leader snapshot via pg_export_snapshot. The long transaction holds the xmin horizon.

nodes.label: Physical streaming replica
nodes.rationale: A byte-identical whole-cluster copy permanently in recovery. Writes return 25006. It replays VACUUM and DDL. pg_is_in_recovery() is true on a standby.

nodes.label: hot_standby_feedback
nodes.rationale: Default off. The standby reports its oldest snapshot so primary VACUUM defers cleanup. Cost is table bloat on the primary — the same xmin-horizon problem as a long transaction. vacuum_defer_cleanup_age was removed in PG16.

nodes.label: Recovery conflict 40001
nodes.rationale: Replay of primary VACUUM would remove row versions a standby query still needs. Default max_standby_streaming_delay is 30 s then canceling statement due to conflict with recovery. SQLSTATE 40001 is retryable. Some conflicts terminate the session.

nodes.label: \gset
nodes.rationale: Stores each column of exactly one result row into a psql variable. Prefix avoids collisions. Together with \if, scripts can branch on data.

nodes.label: Bare :var is injectable
nodes.rationale: \set danger '1; DROP TABLE something; --' becomes two statements. Mitigate with :'var' / :"var". Untrusted input belongs in app parameterized queries.

nodes.label: Three interpolation forms
nodes.rationale: :var raw text for names/numbers/fragments. :'var' quoted escaped string literal. :"var" quoted escaped identifier. Same value status produced literal status vs column value paid.

nodes.label: Unset variable left as text
nodes.rationale: No error for an undefined name. Guard with \if :{?name} and \q 1.

nodes.label: Variables are textual substitution
nodes.rationale: Client-side paste before SQL is sent. Not parameters, no binding, no type checking. Acceptable for scripts you control; untrusted input belongs in application code with real placeholders.

nodes.label: Declarative partitioning
nodes.rationale: Enforces the key across partitions (duplicate 23505). No matching partition → 23514. Worth it for detach-drop or partition-key pruning; not below tens of millions of rows.

nodes.label: ONLY excludes children
nodes.rationale: DELETE FROM parent includes children unless ONLY. pg_inherits also backs partitioning; check relkind = 'p' for a partitioned parent.

nodes.label: Unique constraint must include partition key
nodes.rationale: Global uniqueness on id alone is not enforceable without checking every partition. Generate ids centrally and accept uniqueness on trust, or add the partition key.
nodes.norm_label: unique constraint must include partition key

nodes.label: Primary keys are not inherited
nodes.rationale: NOT NULL and CHECK inherit. PK, UNIQUE, and FK do not. A FK pointing at the parent misses child rows. SELECT on parent sees children.

nodes.label: Table inheritance
nodes.rationale: Predates declarative partitioning. Parent PK is not inherited: two child rows with id 1 accepted. Use essentially never for new work.

nodes.label: Bulk insert speed ladder
nodes.rationale: 10000 rows: autocommit 19551 ms, one transaction 2262 ms, multi-row VALUES 148 ms, unnest 81 ms, COPY 243 ms. WAL flush plus round trips dominate.

nodes.label: 65535 parameter ceiling
nodes.rationale: Protocol stores the count in 16 bits. 21845 rows times 3 columns succeeded; one more failed with 08P01 about parameter formats. Chunk or unnest one array per column.

nodes.label: Extended query protocol
nodes.rationale: Not escaping. Statement is parsed then values are bound. Multi-statement text with parameters fails 42601. Concatenated payload executed two statements and dropped a table.

nodes.label: unnest N rows through one parameter per column
nodes.rationale: 5000 rows through 3 parameters. Multi-row VALUES would need 15000 and hit 65535 at 21845 rows. One statement shape so the plan cache stays warm. 81 ms versus COPY 243 ms at 10000 rows.
nodes.norm_label: unnest n rows through one parameter per column

nodes.label: Identity consumed before conflict
nodes.rationale: Sequences are non-transactional. Three runs of a two-row idempotent seed left last_value at 6. Gaps are expected.

nodes.label: Conflict target needs a unique index
nodes.rationale: 42P10 without a matching unique or exclusion constraint. Partial indexes need a matching WHERE. Deferrable unique constraints cannot be the arbiter.
nodes.norm_label: conflict target needs a unique index

nodes.label: EXCLUDED proposed row
nodes.rationale: EXCLUDED is the row that would have been inserted. table.qty + EXCLUDED.qty accumulates; SET qty = EXCLUDED.qty overwrites. WHERE on DO UPDATE skips no-op writes.

nodes.label: Atomic upsert
nodes.rationale: Only correct insert-if-absent. Check-then-insert raced: 20 workers produced 20 duplicates and zero errors. MERGE can still raise unique_violation under concurrent inserts.

nodes.label: TRUNCATE RESTART IDENTITY
nodes.rationale: Plain TRUNCATE left next id at 10001. Sequences are separate objects. Tests asserting id === 1 fail on the second run without RESTART IDENTITY.

nodes.label: UPDATE writes a new tuple version
nodes.rationale: Never in-place. Dead versions await VACUUM. Non-HOT updates also add index entries. SET x = x is not free.
nodes.norm_label: update writes a new tuple version

nodes.label: DELETE does not shrink the table
nodes.rationale: 47 MB before and after deleting half the rows, still 47 MB after VACUUM, 24 MB after VACUUM FULL. VACUUM truncates only trailing empty pages.
nodes.norm_label: delete does not shrink the table

nodes.label: TRUNCATE
nodes.rationale: Near O(1) new empty files. 4.4 ms versus DELETE 12.7 ms on 10000 rows. No WHERE, no RETURNING, ACCESS EXCLUSIVE, own privilege, blocked by inbound FKs.

nodes.label: WHERE on right table cancels LEFT JOIN
nodes.rationale: ON is the match rule; WHERE runs after NULL extension. NULL = 'paid' is unknown and discarded. Measured 4 rows vs 2.
nodes.norm_label: where on right table cancels left join

nodes.label: Downstream INNER JOIN cancels LEFT JOIN
nodes.rationale: NULL-extended rows fail the later equijoin. Continue LEFT, or parenthesise the inner pair — those are different queries.
nodes.norm_label: downstream inner join cancels left join

nodes.label: Outer-join predicate classification
nodes.rationale: Right-table predicates belong in ON; left-table predicates in WHERE; the join key in ON. A left filter in ON does not filter.

nodes.label: LATERAL LIMIT 1 when columns are needed
nodes.rationale: A semi join exposes no right-hand columns. Need the matched row? Rewrite as LEFT JOIN LATERAL … LIMIT 1, not by adding columns to EXISTS.
nodes.norm_label: lateral limit 1 when columns are needed

nodes.label: count(DISTINCT) survives fan-out
nodes.rationale: De-duplicating ids is idempotent under row duplication; addition is not. Diagnose fan-out by comparing count(*) to count(DISTINCT parent pk).

nodes.label: Join fan-out inflates sum
nodes.rationale: Order 10 has two items, so its 100 is added twice. Measured 650 against true 550. Two child joins multiply.

nodes.label: LATERAL pre-aggregation
nodes.rationale: Aggregate the child before joining so no duplication reaches parent columns. Measured 6 orders, 550 revenue, 5 item rows. LEFT JOIN LATERAL … ON true keeps childless parents.

nodes.label: sum(DISTINCT) is not a fan-out fix
nodes.rationale: It de-duplicates values, not rows. Two different 200s collapse. Measured 350 — a third wrong answer. There is no DISTINCT-shaped fix for sum.
nodes.norm_label: sum(distinct) is not a fan-out fix

nodes.label: sum(count(*)) OVER ()
nodes.rationale: count(*) is computed per GROUP BY group; then the window sums those group rows. Standard percentage-of-total on a grouped report without a self-join.

nodes.label: 21000 more than one row returned
nodes.rationale: Planner cannot know the row count, so the query is accepted and the executor discovers the problem. LIMIT 1 without ORDER BY converts a loud error into a plan-dependent answer.

nodes.label: Scalar subquery
nodes.rationale: Uncorrelated form is evaluated once and attached to every row. More than one row is 21000; zero rows is NULL, not an error. Prefer an aggregate or unique key over LIMIT 1.

nodes.label: Where windows run
nodes.rationale: Windows run after GROUP BY and HAVING, before DISTINCT and ORDER BY. Cannot filter a window in the same query level; can window over an aggregate.

nodes.label: Scalar and row subqueries
nodes.rationale: A subquery in an expression position must produce one row and one column. Enforced at runtime, so today's one-row table is tomorrow's 21000.

nodes.label: Safe dynamic WHERE
nodes.rationale: Build predicate strings and the parameter array in the same loop so $n cannot drift. Separate construction is a runtime error or an injection hole.

nodes.label: Sort and filter allowlists
nodes.rationale: ?sort=price reintroduces SQL injection to a codebase that parameterizes everything else. Values can be parameters; column names and ASC/DESC cannot.

nodes.label: Phase 9 CRUD patterns for a real API
nodes.rationale: 18 topics: repository, list, safe dynamic WHERE, allowlists, request transactions, keyset, optimistic concurrency. Where injection re-enters a parameterized codebase.
nodes.norm_label: phase 9 crud patterns for a real api

nodes.label: Critical Phase 8–9 topics were stamps
nodes.rationale: DDL-from-Node showed INSERT. Soft delete never mentioned deleted_at. list/WHERE/allowlists were byte-identical and had no predicate-building code.

nodes.label: Sorting cannot use parameter machinery
nodes.rationale: ORDER BY needs an identifier. ORDER BY $1 silently sorts by a constant. Identifiers need an allowlist of authored SQL.

nodes.label: Commit phase
nodes.rationale: Applies DOM operations then runs refs and effects. Cannot be thrown away; children commit before parents.

nodes.label: useLayoutEffect
nodes.rationale: Runs after DOM mutation but before paint; blocks painting. Use only to avoid flicker.

nodes.label: useEffectEvent
nodes.rationale: Read latest props/state inside an effect without adding them as dependencies.

nodes.label: Cleanup must fully undo setup
nodes.rationale: A didInit ref silences the symptom; a re-runnable effect with abort in cleanup is the real fix.

nodes.label: Three tiers of impurity cost
nodes.rationale: Visible in StrictMode today; wrong UI when Compiler or memoization changes call count; un-undoable side effects from abandoned concurrent renders.

nodes.label: What StrictMode cannot catch
nodes.rationale: Production-only paths, unrun branches, idempotent writes, event handlers, and effects after the first mount. A clean dev run is not proof.

nodes.label: useRef guard is the wrong StrictMode fix
nodes.rationale: It hides the symptom. The effect still cannot be re-run on remount, Fast Refresh or Activity restore.
nodes.norm_label: useref guard is the wrong strictmode fix

nodes.label: StrictMode, the Compiler and how purity is enforced
nodes.norm_label: strictmode, the compiler and how purity is enforced

nodes.label: StrictMode doubling is the test
nodes.rationale: React cannot inspect purity, so it runs the function twice in development. The second call is the detector, not overhead.

nodes.label: Cannot update a different component during render
nodes.norm_label: cannot update a different component during render

nodes.label: Props changing is not a render trigger
nodes.norm_label: props changing is not a render trigger

nodes.label: Four state buckets
nodes.rationale: Server state, URL state, form state and UI state. Wrong bucket is the source of most global-state complexity.

nodes.label: Four type sources
nodes.rationale: Inference, bundled .d.ts, DefinitelyTyped @types/*, or a local ambient declaration. Missing all four is TS7016.

nodes.label: Server state is a cache
nodes.rationale: Data owned by the API is borrowed, may be stale, and needs invalidation rather than mutation. Deletes half of a typical Redux store.

nodes.label: A declaration is a promise, not a check
nodes.rationale: The compiler enforces your .d.ts across the codebase without ever verifying it matches the JavaScript.
nodes.norm_label: a declaration is a promise, not a check
